+  have hDTIME : (fun p : α × List Bool => (g₁ p.1, p.2)) ⁻¹' B ∈
+      DTIME (encPair enc encBits) fun N => 2 ^ (2 * (d + 1) * F N) := by
+    refine preimage_mem_DTIME (C := C₀ + 6 + 5 ^ d) hd (.of_tidy hg) fun p => ?_
+    have hN_eq : 2 * n + 1 + p.2.length = N := by
+    have hnN : n ≤ N := by omega
+    have hyN : p.2.length ≤ N := by omega
+    have hfn_F : f n ≤ F N := by
+    have hN_F : N ≤ F N := Nat.le_add_right _ _
+    have h₁ : 2 ^ N ≤ 2 ^ F N := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hN_F
+    have h₂ : 2 ^ f n ≤ 2 ^ F N := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hfn_F
+    have h₃ : 2 * N + 3 ≤ 3 * 2 ^ N := by have := @Nat.lt_two_pow_self N; omega
+    have h₄ : F N + 1 ≤ 2 ^ F N := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
+    have h₅ : 2 ^ F N ≤ 2 ^ (2 * F N) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
+    have h₆ : (f n + 1) * 2 ^ f n ≤ 2 ^ (2 * F N) := by
+          ≤ (F N + 1) * 2 ^ F N := Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) h₂
+        _ ≤ 2 ^ F N * 2 ^ F N := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h₄
+        _ = 2 ^ (2 * F N) := by rw [← pow_add, ← two_mul]
+    have h₇ : (n + 1) ^ d₀ ≤ C₀ * 2 ^ (2 * F N) := by
+        _ ≤ C₀ * 2 ^ (2 * F N) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left C₀ (h₁.trans h₅)
+    have hT_le : N + (n + (n + (n + 1) ^ d₀ + (f n + 1) * 2 ^ f n)) + N ≤
+    have hlen_g : (encPair encBits encBits (g₁ p.1, p.2)).length ≤ 5 * 2 ^ (2 * F N) := by
+      have hlen_eq : (encPair encBits encBits (g₁ p.1, p.2)).length =
+    have hpow_g : (encPair encBits encBits (g₁ p.1, p.2)).length ^ d ≤
+      calc (encPair encBits encBits (g₁ p.1, p.2)).length ^ d
+          ≤ (5 * 2 ^ (2 * F N)) ^ d := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hlen_g d
+        _ = 5 ^ d * 2 ^ (2 * d * F N) := by rw [Nat.mul_pow, ← Nat.pow_mul]; ring_nf
+    have hT_le' : N + (n + (n + (n + 1) ^ d₀ + (f n + 1) * 2 ^ f n)) + N ≤
+  have hN1 : N + 1 ≤ 2 * N := by omega
+  have hFN : F N ≤ (c_f + 1) * (2 ^ (d_f + 1) * N ^ (d_f + 1)) := by
+    have : F N ≤ (c_f + 1) * (N + 1) ^ (d_f + 1) := by simp only [F]; nlinarith
+/-- Pulling back `B ∈ P (encPair encBits encUnary)` along
+`a ↦ (frame (enc a) ++ List.replicate (2 ^ f (enc a).length) true, 2 ^ g (enc a).length)`, where
+`f` and `g` are polynomial-time in unary with `n ≤ f n`, gives a problem in `EXP enc`. -/
+    (hB : B ∈ P (encPair encBits encUnary)) {f g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    (hf : Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime f encUnary encUnary) (hnf : ∀ n, n ≤ f n)
+        2 ^ g (enc a).length)) ⁻¹' B ∈ EXP enc := by
+  have hpad_f' : ComputableTidilyInO (fun x : List Bool => 2 ^ f x.length) encBits encUnary
+      (fun x => x.length + (x.length + 1) ^ d₀ + (f x.length + 1) * 2 ^ f x.length)
+    hpad_f.mono_le (fun x => by simp [encUnary_apply]) fun x => by simp [encUnary_apply]
+  have hpad_g' : ComputableTidilyInO (fun x : List Bool => 2 ^ g x.length) encBits encUnary
+      (fun x => x.length + (x.length + 1) ^ d₁ + (g x.length + 1) * 2 ^ g x.length)
+    hpad_g.mono_le (fun x => by simp [encUnary_apply]) fun x => by simp [encUnary_apply]
+  let g₁ (a : α) : List Bool := frame (enc a) ++ List.replicate (2 ^ f (enc a).length) true
+  have hg₁ : ComputableTidilyInO g₁ enc encBits
+  obtain ⟨C₀, hC₀⟩ := (PolynomiallyBounded.of_forall_le 1 (max d₀ d₁) fun m => by
+    simp only [one_mul]; exact le_rfl).exists_le_mul_two_pow (p := fun m => (m + 1) ^ max d₀ d₁)
+  simp only [encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate] at hf_le hg_le
+  let H (n : ℕ) : ℕ := f n + g n
+  have hDTIME : (fun a : α => (g₁ a, 2 ^ g (enc a).length)) ⁻¹' B ∈
+      DTIME enc fun n => 2 ^ (2 * (d + 1) * H n) := by
+    refine preimage_mem_DTIME (C := 2 * C₀ + 6 + 7 ^ d) hd (.of_tidy hφ) fun a => ?_
+    have hnH : n ≤ H n := (hnf n).trans (Nat.le_add_right _ _)
+    have hfH : f n ≤ H n := Nat.le_add_right _ _
+    have hgH : g n ≤ H n := Nat.le_add_left _ _
+    have h₁ : 2 ^ n ≤ 2 ^ H n := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hnH
+    have h₂ : 2 ^ f n ≤ 2 ^ H n := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hfH
+    have h₃ : 2 ^ g n ≤ 2 ^ H n := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hgH
+    have h₄ : 3 * n + 3 ≤ 3 * 2 ^ n := by have := @Nat.lt_two_pow_self n; omega
+    have h₅ : H n + 1 ≤ 2 ^ H n := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
+    have h₆ : 2 ^ H n ≤ 2 ^ (2 * H n) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
+    have h₇ : (f n + 1) * 2 ^ f n ≤ 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by
+          ≤ (H n + 1) * 2 ^ H n := Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) h₂
+        _ ≤ 2 ^ H n * 2 ^ H n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h₅
+        _ = 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by rw [← pow_add, ← two_mul]
+    have h₈ : (g n + 1) * 2 ^ g n ≤ 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by
+          ≤ (H n + 1) * 2 ^ H n := Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) h₃
+        _ ≤ 2 ^ H n * 2 ^ H n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h₅
+        _ = 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by rw [← pow_add, ← two_mul]
+    have h₉ : (n + 1) ^ d₀ ≤ C₀ * 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by
+        _ ≤ C₀ * 2 ^ (2 * H n) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left C₀ (h₁.trans h₆)
+    have h₁₀ : (n + 1) ^ d₁ ≤ C₀ * 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by
+        _ ≤ C₀ * 2 ^ (2 * H n) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left C₀ (h₁.trans h₆)
+    have hT_le : n + (n + (n + 1) ^ d₀ + (f n + 1) * 2 ^ f n) +
+          (n + (n + 1) ^ d₁ + (g n + 1) * 2 ^ g n) ≤ (2 * C₀ + 6) * 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by nlinarith
+    have hlen_φ : (encPair encBits encUnary (g₁ a, 2 ^ g n)).length ≤ 7 * 2 ^ (2 * H n) := by
+      have hlen_eq : (encPair encBits encUnary (g₁ a, 2 ^ g n)).length =
+    have hpow_φ : (encPair encBits encUnary (g₁ a, 2 ^ g n)).length ^ d ≤
+      calc (encPair encBits encUnary (g₁ a, 2 ^ g n)).length ^ d
+          ≤ (7 * 2 ^ (2 * H n)) ^ d := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hlen_φ d
+        _ = 7 ^ d * 2 ^ (2 * d * H n) := by rw [Nat.mul_pow, ← Nat.pow_mul]; ring_nf
+    calc n + (n + (n + 1) ^ d₀ + (f n + 1) * 2 ^ f n) +
+          (encPair encBits encUnary (g₁ a, 2 ^ g n)).length ^ d
+  have hn1 : n + 1 ≤ 2 * n := by omega
+  have hpow_n1 : (n + 1) ^ D_fg ≤ 2 ^ D_fg * n ^ D_fg := by
+    calc (n + 1) ^ D_fg ≤ (2 * n) ^ D_fg := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hn1 D_fg
+      _ = 2 ^ D_fg * n ^ D_fg := Nat.mul_pow 2 n D_fg
+  have hHn : H n ≤ (c_f + c_g) * (2 ^ D_fg * n ^ D_fg) := by
+    have h₁ : f n ≤ c_f * (n + 1) ^ D_fg :=
+    have h₂ : g n ≤ c_g * (n + 1) ^ D_fg :=
+    have h₃ : H n ≤ (c_f + c_g) * (n + 1) ^ D_fg := by simp only [H]; nlinarith
+    _ = (2 * (d + 1) * (c_f + c_g) * 2 ^ D_fg) * n ^ D_fg := by ring
+    _ ≤ n * n ^ D_fg := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (n ^ D_fg) (by omega)

+# Structural consequences of the NP-hardness of MCSP
+If the Minimum Circuit Size Problem (`Cslib.MCSP`) is `NP`-hard under polynomial-time many-one
+reductions (`Cslib.Complexity.NPHard`), several structural collapses and class separations follow
+   Murray and Williams state Theorem 4.1 as:
+   > "If every sparse language in `NP` has a polynomial-time reduction to `MCSP`, then
+   The Lean theorems here assume full `NPHard MCSP.encInstance MCSP` (which implies the hypothesis
+   for every language in `NP`, and in particular every tally/sparse language in `NP`), so they
+   formalize the full-`NPHard` specialization of Theorem 4.1. For any problem `A ∈ NEXP`, its
+   exponentially padded version `ntm.padded c` lies in `NP`, and the `NP`-hardness reduction `R`
+   (applied only to `ntm.padded c`) maps padded instances `z (enc a)` of length `2 ^ poly(|enc a|)`
+   to `MCSP` instances `R (z (enc a))`. Reading the `(R (z (enc a))).table` bit at position `y`
+   defines a problem in `EXP` on pairs `(enc a, y)`, hence in `P/poly` when `EXP ⊆ P/poly`.
+   Hardwiring `enc a` into the `P/poly` circuits bounds the circuit complexity of
+   `(R (z (enc a))).function` by a fixed polynomial `s_bound |enc a|` on arity `m_bound |enc a|`.
+   Consequently, membership of `R (z (enc a))` in `MCSP` depends only on the capped threshold
+   `min (s_bound |enc a|) (R (z (enc a))).threshold`, and brute-force enumeration of all circuit
+   certificates of that size (`Cslib.MCSP.boundedMCSPSearch`) takes time `2 ^ poly(|enc a|)` and
+   Murray and Williams state Theorem 1.6 as:
+   > "If `MCSP` is `NP`-hard under polynomial-time reductions, then `EXP ≠ NP ∩ P/poly`.
+   Combining Theorem 4.1 with `NEXP ⊈ NP` (`Cslib.Complexity.not_NEXP_subset_NP`, proved in
+   padding from the deterministic time hierarchy) shows that `EXP ⊆ NP ∩ P/poly` (equivalently
+   `EXP = NP ∩ P/poly`, since `NP ∩ P/poly ⊆ NP ⊆ EXP`) is impossible if `MCSP` is `NP`-hard.
+   As an immediate corollary via `ZPP ⊆ RP ⊆ NP ∩ P/poly` (`RP_subset_NP`, `RP_subset_PPolyOn`),
+   `NP`-hardness of `MCSP` under arbitrary polynomial-time many-one reductions implies `EXP ⊈ RP`
+   If `MCSP` is both `NP`-hard and in `P/poly`, then `NP ⊆ P/poly` and the polynomial hierarchy
+* `Cslib.MCSP.boundedMCSPSearch`: brute-force circuit search up to a unary gate budget `S` and
+  of Murray–Williams Theorem 4.1 (`EXP ⊆ P/poly ⟹ EXP = NEXP`).
+* [C. D. Murray, R. R. Williams, *On the (non) NP-hardness of computing circuit
+/-! ### Pair decoding and lifting `EXP ⊆ P/poly` to pairs of bitstrings -/
+/-- Decode an encoded pair of bitstrings `frame u ++ v` into `(unframe w, dropFrame w)`. -/
+private def decodePair (w : List Bool) : List Bool × List Bool :=
+/-- `decodePair` is a left inverse of `encPair encBits encBits`. -/
+private theorem decodePair_encPair (p : List Bool × List Bool) :
+/-- Re-encoding `decodePair w` increases the word length by at most `1`. -/
+    ∀ w : List Bool, (encPair encBits encBits (decodePair w)).length ≤ w.length + 1
+  | false :: b :: v => by simp [decodePair, unframe, dropFrame]
+    simp only [decodePair, unframe, dropFrame, length_encPair, encBits_apply,
+/-- If `EXP encBits ⊆ PPolyOn encBits`, then `EXP` on paired bitstrings `encPair encBits encBits`
+    EXP (encPair encBits encBits) ⊆ PPolyOn (encPair encBits encBits) := by
+  have hk' : L ∈ DTIME (encPair encBits encBits) fun m => 2 ^ m ^ (k + 1) :=
+  have hdecO : ComputableTidilyInO decodePair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)
+      (fun w => w.length + w.length) (fun w => w.length + w.length) :=
+  have hpre : decodePair ⁻¹' L ∈ DTIME encBits fun n => 2 ^ (n + 1) ^ (k + 1) := by
+    refine preimage_mem_DTIME (C := 3) hk' (.of_tidy hdecO) fun w => ?_
+    change n + n + 2 ^ (encPair encBits encBits (decodePair w)).length ^ (k + 1) ≤
+  have hpre_EXP : decodePair ⁻¹' L ∈ EXP encBits := by
+      (eventually_atTop.mpr ⟨2, fun n hn => Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) ?_⟩) hpre⟩
+    have hn2 : n + 1 ≤ n ^ 2 := by nlinarith
+  have hpre_PPoly : decodePair ⁻¹' L ∈ PPolyOn encBits := hEXP hpre_EXP
+  have hred : PolyTimeReducible (encPair encBits encBits) encBits L (decodePair ⁻¹' L) :=
+    ⟨encPair encBits encBits, .of_tidy (.of_eq fun _ => rfl), fun p => by
+      change p ∈ L ↔ decodePair (encPair encBits encBits p) ∈ L
+/-! ### Bounded brute-force certificate search for MCSP -/
+/-- Certificate length is monotone in both the input arity and the gate budget. -/
+private theorem certLength_mono {m₁ m₂ s₁ s₂ : ℕ} (hm : m₁ ≤ m₂) (hs : s₁ ≤ s₂) :
+    certLength m₁ s₁ ≤ certLength m₂ s₂ := by
+/-- Check whether a truth table `T` (of arity `m = Nat.log 2 T.length`) has a circuit of size at
+most `S` by enumerating all certificates of length `min (certLength m S) (Nat.log 2 K)`. Because
+the certificate length is capped at `Nat.log 2 K`, at most `K + 1` certificates are enumerated, so
+the search runs in time polynomial in `T.length`, `S`, and `K` when `S` and `K` are given in
+def boundedMCSPSearch (T : List Bool) (S K : ℕ) : Bool :=
+  let cLen := min (certLength m S) (Nat.log 2 K)
+    checkCertificate (fun y out => out == tableValue T y) m S u
+/-- `boundedMCSPSearch` is computable in polynomial time when the truth table `T` is given as bits
+and the gate budget `S` and enumeration budget `K` are given in unary. -/
+    {T : γ → List Bool} {S K : γ → ℕ}
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => boundedMCSPSearch (T a) (S a) (K a)) encIn encBool := by
+  let m (a : γ) : ℕ := Nat.log 2 (T a).length
+  let cLen (a : γ) : ℕ := min (certLength (m a) (S a)) (Nat.log 2 (K a))
+  have hm : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime m encIn encUnary :=
+  have hcLen : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime cLen encIn encUnary := by
+      (fun a => min (certLength (m a) (S a)) (Nat.log 2 (K a))) encIn encUnary
+    have hcert : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => certLength (m a) (S a)) encIn encUnary := by
+    have hlogK : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Nat.log 2 (K a)) encIn encUnary :=
+      2 ^ cLen a * (2 * cLen a + 1) ≤ size_enum (encIn a).length := by
+    have hc_le_log : cLen a ≤ Nat.log 2 (K a) := Nat.min_le_right _ _
+    have hlog_le : Nat.log 2 (K a) ≤ K a := Nat.log_le_self 2 (K a)
+    have hpow_le : 2 ^ cLen a ≤ K a + 1 := by
+          rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (K a) with h0 | hpos
+    have hlin_le : 2 * cLen a + 1 ≤ 2 * (K a + 1) := by omega
+    have hKa : K a + 1 ≤ c_K * ((encIn a).length + 1) ^ d_K + 1 :=
+  have henum : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => BitString.enumList (cLen a))
+      2 ^ m p.1 * (2 * m p.1 + 1) ≤ size_T (encPair encIn encBits p).length := by
+    have hpow : 2 ^ m p.1 ≤ lenT + 1 := by
+      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos lenT with h0 | hpos
+      have : m p.1 ≤ lenT := Nat.log_le_self 2 lenT
+    have hlen_p : (encIn p.1).length ≤ (encPair encIn encBits p).length :=
+    have hlenT_le : lenT + 1 ≤ c_T * ((encPair encIn encBits p).length + 1) ^ d_T + 1 := by
+      (fun q : ((γ × List Bool) × List Bool) × Bool =>
+      (encPair (encPair (encPair encIn encBits) encBits) encBool) encBool := by
+        (fun q : ((γ × List Bool) × List Bool) × Bool => tableValue (T q.1.1.1) q.1.2)
+        checkCertificate (fun y out => out == tableValue (T p.1) y) (m p.1) (S p.1) p.2)
+/-- When `T` has length `2 ^ m` and the enumeration budget satisfies
+`certLength m S ≤ Nat.log 2 K`, `boundedMCSPSearch T S K` returns `true` if and only if the
+Boolean function represented by `T` has circuit complexity at most `S`. -/
+theorem boundedMCSPSearch_eq_true_iff {m S K : ℕ} {T : List Bool} (hT : T.length = 2 ^ m)
+      complexity interpretation (single (tableFunction m T)) ≤ S := by
+  have hm : Nat.log 2 T.length = m := by rw [hT, Nat.log_pow Nat.one_lt_two]
+    refine complexity_le_iff.2 ⟨c, Circuit.computes_single_iff.2 fun y => ?_, hcS⟩
+    have hcS : c.size ≤ S := hsize ▸ hcomp
+      (accept := fun y out => out == tableValue T y) hcS fun y => by
+    exact ⟨u, hu_len, by simpa using hV []⟩
+/-- On the truth table `List.ofFn x.table` of an `MCSP.Instance` `x`, when
+`certLength x.arity S ≤ Nat.log 2 K`, `boundedMCSPSearch` decides whether `x.function` has
+  have hfun : tableFunction x.arity (List.ofFn x.table) = x.function := by
+/-! ### Murray–Williams Theorem 4.1, Theorem 1.6, and Karp–Lipton consequences -/
+> "If every sparse language in `NP` has a polynomial-time reduction to `MCSP`, then
+This theorem assumes full `NPHard MCSP.encInstance MCSP` (which implies the hypothesis for every
+language in `NP`, and in particular every tally/sparse language in `NP`; the proof applies `hHard`
+only to the unary-padded language `ntm.padded c`), and shows that if `EXP encBits ⊆ PPolyOn encBits`
+then `NEXP enc ⊆ EXP enc` for every encoding `enc` of instances. -/
+    (hHard : NPHard MCSP.encInstance MCSP) (hEXP : EXP encBits ⊆ PPolyOn encBits)
+  obtain ⟨c₁, c₂, k_tapes, State, hfinite, ntm, hdec⟩ := hk
+  set c := Nat.card (Turing.Action k_tapes Bool State) * (c₁ + c₂)
+  obtain ⟨R, hR, hR_iff⟩ := hHard encBits (ntm.padded c) (ntm.padded_mem_NP c)
+  have hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encUnary encUnary := by
+  have hnf (n : ℕ) : n ≤ f n :=
+  let z (x : List Bool) : List Bool := frame x ++ List.replicate (2 ^ f x.length) true
+  have hR_table : ComputableInPolyTime (fun w : List Bool => List.ofFn (R w).table)
+  have hR_thresh : ComputableInPolyTime (fun w : List Bool => (R w).threshold)
+  let B_bit : Set (List Bool × List Bool) :=
+    {q : List Bool × List Bool | tableValue (List.ofFn (R q.1).table) q.2 = true}
+  have hB_bit : B_bit ∈ P (encPair encBits encBits) :=
+  let L_pad : Set (List Bool × List Bool) :=
+    (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => (z p.1, p.2)) ⁻¹' B_bit
+  have hL_pad_EXP : L_pad ∈ EXP (encPair encBits encBits) :=
+  let m_bound (n : ℕ) : ℕ := c_R + (f n + 2) * d_R
+  let s_bound (n : ℕ) : ℕ := c_M * (2 * n + 1 + m_bound n + 1) ^ d_M + 2
+  let g (n : ℕ) : ℕ := certLength (m_bound n) (s_bound n) + n
+  have harity (x : List Bool) : (R (z x)).arity ≤ m_bound x.length := by
+      simp only [z, List.length_append, length_frame, List.length_replicate, pow_add]
+      change 2 * n + 1 + 2 ^ f n + 1 ≤ 2 ^ f n * 4
+    have hpow_le : 2 ^ (R (z x)).arity ≤ 2 ^ m_bound n := by
+        _ = 2 ^ m_bound n := by simp only [m_bound, ← pow_mul, ← pow_add]
+      complexity interpretation (single (R (z x)).function) ≤ s_bound x.length := by
+    let a_frame : Fin (frame x).length → Bool := fun j => (frame x)[j]
+    have ha_frame : List.ofFn a_frame = frame x := List.ofFn_getElem
+  -- Compose the unary bounds explicitly: one `fun_prop` over the unfolded nest is too slow.
+  have hid : ComputableInPolyTime (fun n : ℕ => n) encUnary encUnary := .id'
+  have hc (a : ℕ) : ComputableInPolyTime (fun _ : ℕ => a) encUnary encUnary := .const a
+  have hadd {u v : ℕ → ℕ} (hu : ComputableInPolyTime u encUnary encUnary)
+      ComputableInPolyTime (fun n => u n + v n) encUnary encUnary :=
+  have hmul {u v : ℕ → ℕ} (hu : ComputableInPolyTime u encUnary encUnary)
+      ComputableInPolyTime (fun n => u n * v n) encUnary encUnary :=
+  have hm_bound : ComputableInPolyTime m_bound encUnary encUnary :=
+  have hs_bound : ComputableInPolyTime s_bound encUnary encUnary :=
+  have hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encUnary encUnary := by
+    exact hadd (hadd (hadd hs_bound hns) (hmul hs_bound (hadd (hc 3) (hmul (hc 2) hns)))) hid
+  have hB_search : B_search ∈ P (encPair encBits encUnary) := by
+    have hunframe_len : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × ℕ => (unframe p.1).length)
+        (fun p : List Bool × ℕ => s_bound (unframe p.1).length) encIn encUnary :=
+        (fun p : List Bool × ℕ => min (s_bound (unframe p.1).length) (R p.1).threshold)
+      (fun a : α => (z (enc a), 2 ^ g (enc a).length)) ⁻¹' B_search ∈ EXP enc :=
+  have hA_eq : A = (fun a : α => (z (enc a), 2 ^ g (enc a).length)) ⁻¹' B_search := by
+        (z x, 2 ^ g n) ∈ B_search ↔ R (z x) ∈ MCSP := by
+      exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hcomp_le x, h⟩⟩
+    have hpad_iff : a ∈ A ↔ z x ∈ ntm.padded c := by
+      change Nat.card (Turing.Action k_tapes Bool State) * (c₁ * 2 ^ n ^ k + c₂) ≤
+        c * (frame x ++ List.replicate (2 ^ f n) true).length
+      have hpow_le : 2 ^ n ^ k ≤ 2 ^ f n := by
+        rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with h0 | hpos
+        · rcases k with _ | k <;> simp [f, h0]

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Direct consequences of charged asymptotic bounds
+Time, workspace and encoded output are separate obligations. These rules package or forget the
+actual realizing machine; they do not normalize it or import a higher construction calculus.
+variable {α β : Type*} {f : α → β} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encOut : β ↪ List Bool}
+/-- Exact plain machine bounds and an explicit output charge supply asymptotic bounds. -/
+    (hf : ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t s) (k : ℕ)
+    (ht : ∀ a, t a ≤ k * (T a + 1)) (hs : ∀ a, s a ≤ k * (S a + 1))
+    ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S :=
+/-- Weaken both bounds by independent pointwise estimates and a common constant. -/
+theorem mono {T' S' : α → ℕ} (h : ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S) (k : ℕ)
+    ComputableInO f encIn encOut T' S' :=
+  of_bounds hc (c * (k + 1)) (fun a => by nlinarith [hT a])
+    (fun a => by nlinarith [hS a]) (fun a => by nlinarith [hS a, hl a])
+/-- Pointwise larger bounds retain the same encoded-output charge. -/
+theorem mono_le {T' S' : α → ℕ} (h : ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S)
+    (hT : ∀ a, T a ≤ T' a) (hS : ∀ a, S a ≤ S' a) :
+    ComputableInO f encIn encOut T' S' :=
+  h.mono 1 (fun a => by have := hT a; omega) (fun a => by have := hS a; omega)
+/-- Weaken independent time and charged workspace bounds up to constants. -/
+theorem weaken {T' S' : α → ℕ} (h : ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S)
+    (hT : T ≼ T') (hS : S ≼ S') : ComputableInO f encIn encOut T' S' :=
+/-- An equal encoded output reuses the same machine and both resource budgets. -/
+theorem of_enc_eq {γ : Type*} {encC : γ ↪ List Bool} {g : α → γ}
+    (h : ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S) (hg : ∀ a, encC (g a) = encOut (f a)) :
+    ComputableInO g encIn encC T S := by
+  obtain ⟨c, ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, htm⟩, hl⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨c, ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, fun a => hg a ▸ htm a⟩,
+    fun a => by rw [hg a]; exact hl a⟩
+/-- Pull back along an input map preserving the complete encoded word. No algorithm for the
+semantic map is assumed: the realizing machine receives exactly the same word. -/
+    (h : ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S) (g : δ → α)
+    ComputableInO (f ∘ g) encD encOut (T ∘ g) (S ∘ g) := by
+  obtain ⟨c, ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, htm⟩, hl⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨c, ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, fun a => hg a ▸ htm (g a)⟩, fun a => hl (g a)⟩
+/-- Polynomial bounds on both resource functions give a plain polynomial-time certificate. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime (h : ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S)
+    fun n => c * (cs * (n + 1) ^ ds + 1), by fun_prop, by fun_prop, h.mono ?_ ?_⟩
+variable {α β : Type*} {f : α → β} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encOut : β ↪ List Bool}
+  {T S T' S' t s : α → ℕ}
+public theorem ComputableInBigO.of_bounds (h : ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t s)
+    (ht : t ≼ T) (hs : s ≼ S) : ComputableInBigO f encIn encOut T S :=
+/-- Weakening the bounds, up to constant factors. -/
+public theorem ComputableInBigO.weaken (h : ComputableInBigO f encIn encOut T S)
+    (hT : T ≼ T') (hS : S ≼ S') : ComputableInBigO f encIn encOut T' S' :=
+  .of_bounds hc ((BigOLe.const_mul c (u := fun a => T a + 1)
+    ((BigOLe.const_mul c (u := fun a => S a + 1) (.of_le_linear 1 1 fun _ => by omega)).trans hS)

+  have hB : B ≤ B * (n + 1) := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right B (Nat.succ_pos n)
+  have : A * (n + 1) + B ≤ (A + B) * (n + 1) := by rw [Nat.add_mul]; omega

+    ComputableInO (f ∘ g) encIn encOut (fun a => T₁ a + T₂ (g a))

+  obtain ⟨c₂, ⟨k₂, Q₂, _, tm₂, h₂⟩, l₂⟩ := Internal.NormalForm.inO hf
+  refine ⟨6 * c₁ + c₂ + (6 * max k₁ k₂ + 20), ⟨_, _, inferInstance, tm₂.comp tm₁ true,
+    fun a => (((h₁ a).comp (h₂ (g a)) true).mono ?_ ?_).computesInTimeAndSpace⟩, fun a => ?_⟩
+  · -- the intermediate word is no longer than the time of `g`
+    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c₁ (by omega : T₁ a + 1 ≤ T₁ a + T₂ (g a) + 1)
+    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c₂ (by omega : T₂ (g a) + 1 ≤ T₁ a + T₂ (g a) + 1)
+    have e : (6 * c₁ + c₂) * (T₁ a + T₂ (g a) + 1) =
+        6 * (c₁ * (T₁ a + T₂ (g a) + 1)) + c₂ * (T₁ a + T₂ (g a) + 1) := by ring
+    exact le_mul_succ (A := 6 * c₁ + c₂) (B := 6 * max k₁ k₂ + 20) (by omega) le_rfl
+  · -- the intermediate word is within the space bound of `g`
+    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c₁ (by omega : S₁ a + 1 ≤ S₁ a + S₂ (g a) + 1)
+    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c₂ (by omega : S₂ (g a) + 1 ≤ S₁ a + S₂ (g a) + 1)
+    have e : (6 * c₁ + c₂) * (S₁ a + S₂ (g a) + 1) =
+        6 * (c₁ * (S₁ a + S₂ (g a) + 1)) + c₂ * (S₁ a + S₂ (g a) + 1) := by ring
+    exact le_mul_succ (A := 6 * c₁ + c₂) (B := 6 * max k₁ k₂ + 20) (by omega) le_rfl
+  · have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c₂ (by omega : S₂ (g a) + 1 ≤ S₁ a + S₂ (g a) + 1)
+/-- **Case distinction** within the bounds of the test plus those of the branch taken, through the
+theorem ite {encC : Bool ↪ List Bool} {c : α → Bool} {f g : α → β}
+    {Tc Tf Tg Sc Sf Sg : α → ℕ} (hc : ComputableInO c encIn encC Tc Sc)
+    (hf : ComputableInO f encIn encMid Tf Sf) (hg : ComputableInO g encIn encMid Tg Sg) :
+    ComputableInO (fun x => if c x then f x else g x) encIn encMid
+      (fun x => Tc x + if c x then Tf x else Tg x)
+      (fun x => Sc x + if c x then Sf x else Sg x) := by
+  obtain ⟨c₀, ⟨k₀, Q₀, _, tm₀, h₀⟩, -⟩ := Internal.NormalForm.inO hc
+  obtain ⟨c₁, ⟨k₁, Q₁, _, tm₁, h₁⟩, l₁⟩ := Internal.NormalForm.inO hf
+  obtain ⟨c₂, ⟨k₂, Q₂, _, tm₂, h₂⟩, l₂⟩ := Internal.NormalForm.inO hg
+  obtain ⟨k, K, Q, _, tm, h⟩ := ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace.ite (encOut := encMid)
+    (tc := fun a => c₀ * (Tc a + 1)) (sc := fun a => c₀ * (Sc a + 1))
+    (tf := fun a => c₁ * (Tf a + 1)) (sf := fun a => c₁ * (Sf a + 1))
+    (tg := fun a => c₂ * (Tg a + 1)) (sg := fun a => c₂ * (Sg a + 1))
+    ⟨k₀, Q₀, inferInstance, tm₀, h₀⟩ ⟨k₁, Q₁, inferInstance, tm₁, fun x => h₁ x.1⟩
+    ⟨k₂, Q₂, inferInstance, tm₂, fun x => h₂ x.1⟩

+    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c' (by omega : Y + 1 ≤ X + Y + 1)
+    have e : (c₀ + c') * (X + Y + 1) = c₀ * (X + Y + 1) + c' * (X + Y + 1) := by ring
+    exact le_mul_succ (A := c₀ + c') (B := d') (by omega) (by omega)
+  refine ⟨c₀ + c₁ + c₂ + k, ⟨K, Q, inferInstance, tm,
+    · exact key c₁ k _ _ _ le_rfl (by omega)
+    · exact key c₂ k _ _ _ le_rfl (by omega)
+    · exact key c₁ k _ _ _ le_rfl (by omega)
+    · exact key c₂ k _ _ _ le_rfl (by omega)
+    · exact key c₁ 0 _ _ _ (by have := l₁ x; omega) (by omega)
+    · exact key c₂ 0 _ _ _ (by have := l₂ x; omega) (by omega)

+# Direct plain list lookup at a binary index
+Lookup in a computed list at a computed index encoded in binary. The index is first capped at the
+length of the list by the saturating fold `Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue`, which reads the
+binary digits most significant first and caps every partial value. An index far beyond the list
+therefore costs only its encoded length and is never expanded to unary; beyond the list every
+The capped-binary fold is the one used by the binary lookup rule of the raw calculus in
+certified directly, with the plain fold, the unary list length, unary subtraction and lookup at a
+unary index. The saturating step `min cap (2 * v + b)` is computed as `cap - (cap - v - v - b)`.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.listGetD_binary`: lookup with a fixed default at a
+  binary index, in any sized list encoding.
+/-- Lookup in a computed list at a computed binary index, with a fixed default, in any sized list
+encoding. The index is first capped at the length of the list, reading its binary digits most
+significant first and capping every partial value, so an index far beyond the list costs only its
+encoded length; beyond the list every lookup returns the default. -/
+theorem listGetD_binary {α γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {encL : List α ↪ List Bool} [ListEncoding encA encL] [SizedListEncoding encA encL]
+    {l : γ → List α} {i : γ → ℕ} (d : α)
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (l x).getD (i x) d) encIn encA := by
+  have hlen : ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (l x).length) encIn encUnary := by
+    have h := foldl' (encA := encA) (encL := encL) (encB := encUnary) (list := l)
+      (fun p : (ℕ × ℕ) × Bool => min p.1.1 (2 * p.1.2 + p.2.toNat))
+    have hq := fst (encPair encUnary encUnary) encBool
+    have hb : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : (ℕ × ℕ) × Bool => p.2.toNat)
+    have heq : (fun p : (ℕ × ℕ) × Bool => min p.1.1 (2 * p.1.2 + p.2.toNat)) =
+      (par := fun x => (l x).length) (list := fun x => (encNat (i x)).reverse)
+      (step := fun cap value bit => min cap (2 * value + bit.toNat))
+  have heq : (fun x => (l x).getD (i x) d) = fun x =>
+    rcases le_total (i x) (l x).length with h | h
+    · rw [Nat.min_eq_left h, List.getD_eq_default _ _ h, List.getD_eq_default _ _ le_rfl]

+/-! # Direct mapping with the complete original input
+The existing captured fold retains the original input while appending each callback result.
+Its prefix bound follows from the list's encoded length and the callback machine's own clock.
+/-- Map with the complete original input captured uniformly by one joint callback machine.
+The list certificate fixes its element encoding before the callback is checked. -/
+theorem mapWithInput {α β γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {f : γ → α → β} {list : γ → List α}
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : γ × α => f p.1 p.2) (encPair encIn encA) encB) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (list x).map (f x)) encIn (encList encB) := by
+  let L := fun n : ℕ => n + cl * (n + 1) ^ dl
+  let bound := fun n : ℕ => L n * (2 * (c * (3 * L n + 3) ^ d) + 1)
+  have hb : PolynomiallyBounded bound := by dsimp [bound, L]; fun_prop
+  have houter := fst (encPair encIn (encList encB)) encA
+  have hvalue := snd (encPair encIn (encList encB)) encA
+  have hfold := foldlWith (encA := encA) (encL := encList encA) (encP := encIn)
+    (step := fun x mapped value => mapped ++ [f x value]) id' hlist (const []) hstep
+      have hlistBound : (encList encA (list x)).length ≤ L (encIn x).length :=
+      have heach : ∀ b ∈ ((list x).take i).map (f x),
+          (encB b).length ≤ c * (3 * L (encIn x).length + 3) ^ d := by
+          (encA := encA) (encL := encList encA) (list x) a hain).trans hlistBound
+        have hx : (encIn x).length ≤ L (encIn x).length := by dsimp [L]; omega
+  simpa only [foldlMap, List.nil_append, id_eq] using hfold

+  simpa only [foldlMap, List.nil_append, id_eq] using hfold
+/-- Reverse a computed word, fixing its raw intermediate encoding before proof search.

+theorem bitsReverseWithInput {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {word : γ → List Bool}

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Encrypt-then-MAC Authenticated Encryption and PRF-Based Instantiation
+This module formalizes the generic **Encrypt-then-MAC** composition (`encryptThenMAC`) and its
+security reductions ([Boneh and Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*, Version 0.6,
+Section 9.4.1 and Theorem 9.2][BonehShoup2023], printed pp. 367–368), together with a concrete
+and Theorem 5.2, printed pp. 183–189) that witnesses joint non-vacuity of all hypotheses:
+   ([BonehShoup2023], Section 9.4.1, Theorem 9.2, printed pp. 367–368): given a symmetric cipher
+   `E : SymmetricCipher` whose ciphertexts on `n`-bit plaintexts under supported keys at security
+   parameter `n` have length `M.msgLen n`, and a message authentication code `M : MACScheme`
+   * `keyGen n` samples independent keys `ke ← E.keyGen n` and `km ← M.keyGen n` and encodes the
+   * `encrypt n k msg` encrypts `c ← E.encrypt n (unframe k) msg`, signs
+     `tag ← M.sign (dropFrame k) c`, and returns `encPair encBits encBits (c, tag)`.
+   * `decrypt n k ct` checks canonical pair framing
+     `encPair encBits encBits (unframe ct, dropFrame ct) == ct`, checks
+     `(unframe ct).length == M.msgLen n`, and verifies `M.verify (dropFrame k) (unframe ct)
+     (dropFrame ct)`; if all three hold, it returns `E.decrypt n (unframe k) (unframe ct)`, and
+   Because `encPair encBits encBits` is injective, ciphertext freshness in `ciGame` coincides with
+   message-tag pair freshness in `M.sufCmaGame`, yielding exact per-parameter equalities for both

+    (hlen : ∀ key query, query.length = key.length → (family key query).length = key.length) :

+    have htake : (r ++ List.zipWith xor (family k r) msg).take n = r := by
+    have hdrop : (r ++ List.zipWith xor (family k r) msg).drop n =

+An indexed signature scheme ([BonehShoup2023], Definition 14.6) signs pairs `(u, msg)` of an index
+`u < q` and a message. Its security game lets the adversary choose the indices of its signing
+queries, but never the same index twice; it wins with a valid signature on any pair `(u, msg)` it
+never had signed. An indexed scheme is what a stateful signer that never reuses an index needs:
+Merkle's tree signature uses the index of the next unused leaf ([Merkle1989], Section 6;
+[BonehShoup2023], Section 14.6.4, where the index is a nonce). The index is an explicit input, so
+the syntax is stateless; the state is the signer's obligation never to repeat an index, which the
+The definition here differs from [BonehShoup2023], Definition 14.6, in four labelled ways.
+* Signing may be randomized; the source requires deterministic signing.
+* Messages are arbitrary bit strings, with no length restriction.
+* Instead of forbidding the adversary to repeat an index, the signing oracle refuses a repeated
+  index, and an index `u ≥ q`, by returning the empty word and recording nothing. Every oracle
+* A forgery may name any index, whereas the source's message space is `{1, …, q} × M`. The
+  structure does not require verification to reject an index `u ≥ q`; the game does. The oracle
+  never signs at such an index, so a forger that finds a valid signature there wins. This
+A request to the signing oracle is the word `encPair encUnary encBits (u, msg)`. The oracle reads
+* `Cslib.Crypto.IndexedForger`: adaptive oracle adversary outputting `(u, msg, sig)`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.IndexedSignatureScheme.requestDecoder`: the index and message of a request word.
+  running an oracle-PPT forger against the signing oracle, and for the whole game.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023],
+* [R. C. Merkle, *A Certified Digital Signature*][Merkle1989], Section 6.
+/-- An adaptive indexed forger receives a unary security parameter and a public key, queries a
+signing oracle on request words `encPair encUnary encBits (u, msg)`, and outputs a candidate
+abbrev IndexedForger := ℕ → List Bool → WordOracleComp Unit (ℕ × List Bool × List Bool)
+/-- An indexed signature scheme ([BonehShoup2023], Definition 14.6, with randomized signing and
+arbitrary-length messages): at security parameter `n` it signs pairs `(u, msg)` with
+`u < capacity n`, each index at most once. Key generation and signing are strict PPT, verification
+is deterministic polynomial time, and every honest signature verifies. -/
+  /-- The number `q(n)` of indices available at security parameter `n`. -/
+  /-- Sample a public key and secret key `(pk, sk)` at unary parameter `n`. -/
+  keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)
+  /-- Sign the message `msg` at index `u` with the secret key `sk`. -/
+  sign : List Bool → ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)
+  /-- Verify a candidate signature `sig` on the message `msg` at index `u` under `pk`. -/
+  verify : List Bool → ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → Bool
+  /-- The capacity is computable in polynomial time, so it is polynomially bounded. -/

+Merkle's tree signature ([Merkle1989], Section 6) authenticates `2 ^ d` one-time verification
+keys by the root of a Merkle tree, which is the public key. The signature at leaf `u` is the
+one-time key of leaf `u`, its one-time signature and its authentication path. Each leaf may be used
+once, so the scheme is an indexed signature scheme (`IndexedSignatureScheme`) whose index is the
+`MerkleSignature.scheme S H depth` builds it from any signature scheme `S`, used as a one-time
+scheme on `n`-bit messages, and a keyed hash `H` with `n`-bit digests under `n`-bit keys:
+* key generation samples a hash key `k ← {0, 1}^n` and `2 ^ depth n` key pairs of `S`, and
+  publishes `k` and the Merkle root of the one-time verification keys;
+* signing `msg` at leaf `u` signs the digest `H k msg` with the one-time key of leaf `u`
+  (hash-and-sign, [BonehShoup2023], Section 13.2), and attaches the verification key and the
+* verification checks the opening of leaf `u` with `merkleVerify`, which fixes the path length to
+  `depth n` and checks `u < 2 ^ depth n`, and then the one-time signature on `H k msg`.
+The capacity is `2 ^ depth n`, required to be computable in unary in polynomial time, hence
+The scheme is stateful in use: the signer must sign at most once per leaf, for instance with a
+counter. `IndexedSignatureScheme` makes the leaf an explicit input, and its security game refuses

+/-- Computing the public key from the hash key and the one-time key pairs takes polynomial
+      (fun p : List Bool × List (List Bool × List Bool) => publicKey H p.1 p.2)
+/-- Merkle key generation is uniformly strict PPT. -/

+        (fun q : (ℕ × List Bool) × List (List Bool × List Bool) => q.1.2)
+/-- Merkle signing is uniformly strict PPT. -/
+      (fun p => sign S H p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) := by
+  let E := encPair encBits (encPair encUnary encBits)
+  have hdec : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × ℕ × List Bool =>

+  have hu : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × ℕ × List Bool => p.2.1) E encUnary :=

+  have hsign : IsPPTOn E encBits (fun p : List Bool × ℕ × List Bool =>
+  have hpath : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × ℕ × List Bool =>
+  have hpost : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun q : (List Bool × ℕ × List Bool) × List Bool =>

+is a one-time forgery against `S` at the leaf it names. Two reductions turn this into a bound with

+  honestly, and extracts a collision from the forgery. If the forged verification key differs from
+  the one at the named leaf, both open the same position of the tree, and
+  `extractMerkleCollision` finds a collision in the tree. Otherwise, if the leaf already signed
+  another message with the same digest, those two messages collide.
+* `MerkleSignature.oneTimeForger` plants its challenge key at a uniform leaf `i`, generates the
+  other keys itself, and answers the query at leaf `i` with its one-time signing oracle. Because
+  the indexed game never signs twice at one leaf, it makes at most one query, and its simulation of
+  the signing oracle is exact. A forgery at leaf `i` that is not a collision is a one-time forgery
+  on a new digest. The factor `2 ^ depth n` is exact: the leaf is drawn from exactly
+Merkle ([Merkle1989], Section 6) gives the construction with an informal argument. The bound is
+the composition, original to this library, of the plug-and-pray argument for indexed signatures
+from one-time signatures ([BonehShoup2023], Section 14.6.1, referring to Exercise 13.2), the
+collision extraction behind [BonehShoup2023], Theorem 8.8, for the shrunken public key, and the
+hash-and-sign bound of [BonehShoup2023], Theorem 13.1, for the digest.

+Merkle signatures over Lamport's one-time scheme on the identity function, with a toy truncating
+hash and two leaves: an honest signature at each leaf verifies, and changing the message, the
+leaf, or naming an index outside the tree is rejected. The indexed signing oracle signs at a fresh
+leaf and refuses a repeated leaf or one outside the tree. The capacity hypothesis holds for constant
+depth and for depth `Nat.clog 2 (n + 1)`, whose capacity grows linearly.
+/-- A toy keyed hash: the first `k.length` bits of the input, padded with `false`. -/

+theorem length_truncHash (k x : List Bool) : (truncHash k x).length = k.length := by
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => truncHash p.1 p.2)
+/-- Lamport's scheme on the identity function, a concrete (insecure) one-time scheme. -/

+/-! ### A run with explicit keys at `n = 4` -/

+/-- Lamport secret words for two leaves; the identity makes them the public words too. -/

+def sk₁ : List (List Bool) := (List.range 8).map fun j => [true, j % 2 == 0, true, false]
+  [(encList encBits sk₀, encList encBits sk₀), (encList encBits sk₁, encList encBits sk₁)]
+def msg : List Bool := [true, false, true, true, false]
+/-- The Lamport signature on the digest of `m` with the secret words `sk`. -/
+def otsOn (sk : List (List Bool)) (m : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+    sk.getD (2 * i + ((truncHash key m).getD i false).toNat) [])
+def sigAt (u : ℕ) (sk : List (List Bool)) : List Bool :=
+-- Honest signatures at both leaves verify.
+example : verify lamportId truncHash (fun _ => 1) (publicKey truncHash key keys) 0 msg
+example : verify lamportId truncHash (fun _ => 1) (publicKey truncHash key keys) 1 msg
+-- A message with another digest is rejected.
+example : verify lamportId truncHash (fun _ => 1) (publicKey truncHash key keys) 0
+    [false, false, true, true, false] (sigAt 0 sk₀) = false := by
+-- A message with the same digest under the toy hash verifies: a collision of `truncHash`, which
+-- the reduction to collision finding would output.
+example : verify lamportId truncHash (fun _ => 1) (publicKey truncHash key keys) 0
+    [true, false, true, true, true] (sigAt 0 sk₀) = true := by
+-- The signature of leaf `0` is rejected at leaf `1`.

+-- At the index `0 + 2` outside the tree the same opening recomputes the root, and only the range

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+GSW circuit evaluation is run on noiseless constants, on actual noisy encryptions under a key
+with a nonzero error, on a depth-zero circuit and on malformed words. The scheme at the
+logarithmic-depth family is then used as the base of Gentry's generic refresh, and its
+native evaluator is composed with varying dimensions.
+-- At `n = 1` and `w = 2` the constant one is the identity matrix `I_4`, row by row.
+    [true, false, false, false, false, true, false, false,
+      false, false, true, false, false, false, false, true] ∧
+    constSerialized 1 2 false = List.replicate 16 false := by decide +kernel
+-- Noiseless constants decrypt correctly under every secret word of the declared width.
+      decryptSerialized 1 2 secret (constSerialized 1 2 false) = false := by decide +kernel
+-- The compiled NAND circuit (an AND gate and a NOT gate, four NAND layers) maps noiseless
+-- constants to the noiseless constant of their NAND, for all four input pairs.
+    [constSerialized 1 2 a, constSerialized 1 2 b] = constSerialized 1 2 (!(a && b)) := by
+/-- Key inputs with secret `5`, public rows `9` and `22`, and the nonzero error vector `(1, 0)`,
+private def publicWord : List Bool := publicMatrixSerialized 1 2 6 keyInputs
+private def secretWord : List Bool := secretSerialized 1 6 keyInputs.1

+# Merkle trees as authenticated data structures: verification and position binding
+`Cslib.Crypto.merkleRoot` hashes a list of leaves and `Cslib.Crypto.merklePath` opens one position.
+This module adds the verifier and the security notion of an authenticated data structure scheme
+([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.9.1): a verifier `merkleVerify` with completeness, binding and a
+polynomial-time certificate, the game of Attack Game 8.2, and the security of Theorem 8.8,
+reduced to collision resistance with no loss.
+* **The verifier.** `merkleVerify H k d root i leaf path` accepts when `path` has `d` labels,
+  `i < 2 ^ d`, and the root recomputed from `leaf` at position `i` along `path` is `root`
+  (the `V` of [BonehShoup2023], Definition 8.3). These are the checks that the module
+  documentation of `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MerkleTree` requires of a verifier, under
+  "What a verifier must check"; without them binding fails. Honest openings are accepted
+  of Definition 8.3. An opening has one label per level, each of at most `k.length` bits when
+* **Binding of the verifier.** Two openings of one position to different leaves, both accepted at
+  the same depth, give a collision of `H k`, found by `extractMerkleCollision`
+* **The game.** In `merkleBindingGame` the adversary receives the security parameter and a uniform
+  key `k`, and outputs a root, a position and two openings. It wins when both openings are
+  accepted at the depth of the first path and their leaves differ (`merkleBreaksBinding`).
+  `MerklePositionBinding H` asks that every uniform strict PPT adversary win with negligible
+* **The reduction.** `merkleCollisionFinder` runs the adversary and applies
+  `extractMerkleCollision` to its two openings. Every win yields a collision, so the binding
+  advantage is at most the collision advantage at every parameter
+  (`succProbability_merkleBindingGame_le`), and the reduction is strict PPT
+**Differences from [BonehShoup2023].** Attack Game 8.2 is stated for a scheme over `(X^n, Y)`
+with a fixed number `n` of items; here:
+* the hash is a keyed family with a uniform `n`-bit key, and adversaries are uniform strict PPT
+* the adversary chooses the depth `d`, the length of its first path, and must open both leaves at
+  that depth, which makes the game stronger than one with a fixed depth;
+* positions are `0 ≤ i < 2 ^ d`, the padding positions included, rather than `1 ≤ i ≤ n`;
+* the adversary writes its position in unary (`encMerkleBindingOutput`), so the game covers
+  polynomially bounded positions: enough for trees with polynomially many leaves, but not for
+  trees whose leaves are indexed by superpolynomially many positions.
+**Kilian's construction.** Kilian's succinct arguments commit to a PCP proof with a hash tree and
+open the queried positions ([Barak and Goldreich][BarakGoldreich2001], Construction 3.4, steps
+P1.3 and V3). That tree differs from this one, which is [BonehShoup2023]'s Figure 8.12: its leaf
+labels are the proof bits themselves, not their hashes, and an internal label hashes the plain
+concatenation `ℓ_γ0 ℓ_γ1` of its children's labels, not their `encPair` pairing. Its prover sends
+both child labels at every level of a path rather than only the siblings, and the verifier checks
+the same hash equations along the path. Barak and Goldreich's hashing family resists non-uniform

+        ∀ a ∈ X.yes, s a ≤ ((Cslib.ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal :=
+example {X : PromiseProblem α} : PromiseProblem.RPReducible encA encA X X :=

+    (hXY : PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₁ X Y)
+    (hYZ : PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError encB encC (fun _ => s₂) Y Z) :
+    PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError encA encC (fun a => s₁ a + s₂ - 1) X Z :=
+example {X : PromiseProblem α} {Y : PromiseProblem β} {Z : PromiseProblem γ}
+    {s : β → ℝ} {f : α → β} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encA encB)

+/-- A concrete `PromiseRP` solver using a real 1-bit coin flip: on `true`,
+`V (b, r) = b && r.headD false` accepts `[true]` and rejects `[false]` (acceptance probability
+`1 / 2`); on `false`, it rejects both coins (acceptance probability `0`). -/
+example : PromiseProblem.ofSet ({true} : Set Bool) ∈ PromiseRP encBool := by
+  refine ⟨1, fun p : Bool × List Bool => p.1 && p.2.headD false, by fun_prop,

+    generalize hk : (1 : Polynomial ℕ).eval (encBool true).length = k
+/-- A concrete randomized `RPReducible` reduction whose soundness on the no-instance `false` is
+`f (b, r) = b || (r.headD false && r.tail.headD false)` maps `true` exclusively to `true` (all 4
+seeds) and maps `false` to `false` on 3 out of 4 seeds (soundness `3 / 4 ∈ (2 / 3, 1)`). -/

+    generalize hk : (2 : Polynomial ℕ).eval (encBool false).length = k
+/-- Edge case `s ≤ 0`: when `s a = 0`, even the constant yes-map `fun _ => pure true` (which maps

+    fun a _ b hb => ?_, fun _ _ => ENNReal.toReal_nonneg⟩

title: feat(Crypto): Merkle trees with authentication paths and collision extraction (#1023)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A Merkle tree hashes a list of leaves to a single root so that each leaf can later be opened
+against the root with a short authentication path ([Merkle1989], Section 6; [BonehShoup2023],
+Section 8.9). Here the hash is a keyed function `H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, as in
+`CollisionResistant`. As in both sources, a leaf `x` becomes the node `H k x`, and the parent of
+nodes `l` and `r` is `H k (encPair encBits encBits (l, r))`. The pairing `encPair` is injective,
+so nodes of any length can be paired without ambiguity.
+The tree over `leaves` has depth `Nat.clog 2 leaves.length`, the least `d` with
+`leaves.length ≤ 2 ^ d`. Missing leaves read as the empty word, padding the tree to `2 ^ d` leaves
+as [BonehShoup2023] suggests. For `2 ^ d` leaves this is Merkle's `H(1, 2 ^ d, Y)`, with his
+`Y_i` as `leaves.getD (i - 1) []`. For other leaf counts it differs from Merkle's recursion, which
+An authentication path for position `i` lists the sibling of each node on the way from leaf `i`
+to the root. `merkleRootOfPath` recomputes a root from a leaf, a position and a path. Its
+openings of the same position to different leaves, along paths of equal length and with the same
+recomputed root, contain a collision of `H k`, found deterministically by
+`extractMerkleCollision`. This is the reduction behind [BonehShoup2023], Theorem 8.8.
+**What a verifier must check.** Leaves and internal nodes are hashed with the same `H k`, with no
+domain separation, so a recomputed root alone binds nothing. A verifier must fix the path length
+* with a shorter path, an internal node's hash input opens as a leaf; for leaves `[a, b]`, the
+  "leaf" `encPair encBits encBits (H k a, H k b)` at position `0` with path `[]` recomputes the
+* `merkleRootOfPath` reads only the low `path.length` bits of `i`, so positions wrap modulo
+* the root does not fix the number of leaves: `[a, b, c]` and `[a, b, c, []]` have the same root.
+The root, the path, root recomputation and extraction have plain polynomial-time certificates for
+hash families whose digests have the length of the key. Positions are unary in these
+certificates, which suits trees with polynomially many leaves.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleParents`, `Cslib.Crypto.merkleLevel`: one level of the tree from the one
+  below, and level `j` counted from the hashed leaves.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleRoot`, `Cslib.Crypto.merklePath`: the root and the authentication path of
+  recomputing a root from an opening, and the recomputed root.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.extractMerkleCollision`: the first differing pair of hash inputs of two openings.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleRootOfPath_merklePath`: an honest opening recomputes the root.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractMerkleCollision`: a second opening of a position yields a
+* [R. C. Merkle, *A Certified Digital Signature*][Merkle1989], Section 6.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023], Section 8.9,
+variable (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool) (k : List Bool)
+/-- The hashed leaves of the tree over `leaves`, padded with the empty word to `2 ^ d` leaves for
+  (List.range (2 ^ Nat.clog 2 leaves.length)).map fun i => H k (leaves.getD i [])
+/-- The parents of a level: node `i` hashes the pair of nodes `2 * i` and `2 * i + 1`. -/
+    H k (encPair encBits encBits (level.getD (2 * i) [], level.getD (2 * i + 1) []))
+/-- Level `j` of the tree over `leaves`, counted from the hashed leaves at level `0`. -/
+def merkleLevel (leaves : List (List Bool)) (j : ℕ) : List (List Bool) :=
+/-- The root of the Merkle tree over `leaves` ([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.9). -/
+/-- The position of the sibling of node `p` within its level. -/
+  if p % 2 = 0 then p + 1 else p - 1
+/-- One step of `merklePath`: record the sibling of the current node, then move to the parent

+/-- The authentication path of position `i`: the sibling of each node on the way from leaf `i` up
+to the root, starting at the leaves ([BonehShoup2023], Figure 8.12). -/
+def merklePath (leaves : List (List Bool)) (i : ℕ) : List (List Bool) :=
+  ((merklePathStep H k)^[Nat.clog 2 leaves.length] (merkleLeafLevel H k leaves, i, [])).2.2
+/-! ### Recomputing a root from an opening -/
+/-- One step of `merkleInputs`: hash the current input to a node and pair it with `sibling`,
+putting the node on the left when the current position is even. -/
+def merkleInputsStep (state : List (List Bool) × ℕ) (sibling : List Bool) :
+  ((if state.2 % 2 = 0 then encPair encBits encBits (node, sibling)
+    else encPair encBits encBits (sibling, node)) :: state.1, state.2 / 2)

+Concrete runs of `merkleRoot`, `merklePath` and `merkleRootOfPath` on a three-leaf tree, padded to
+four leaves, under a truncating keyed hash; the two openings a verifier must reject by checking the
+path length and the position range; and collision extraction from two forged openings of one
+position, at the leaf level and one level up.
+/-- A toy keyed hash: the first `k.length` bits of the input, padded with `false`. It has many
+collisions, which the extraction tests below use. -/
+def truncHash (k x : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+theorem length_truncHash (k x : List Bool) : (truncHash k x).length = k.length := by
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => truncHash p.1 p.2)
+/-- The certificates apply to the toy hash. -/
+example : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List (List Bool) × ℕ =>
+    merklePath truncHash p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) (encPair encBits (encPair (encList encBits) encUnary))
+/-- A three-leaf tree has depth two; the missing fourth leaf reads as `[]`. -/
+def leaves : List (List Bool) := [[true], [false, true], [true, true, false]]
+    [[true, false, false], [false, true, false], [true, true, false], [false, false, false]] := by
+-- Every position, including the padding position `3`, opens to the root.
+    merkleRootOfPath truncHash key (leaves.getD i []) i (merklePath truncHash key leaves i) =
+-- Without a fixed path length, the hash input of an internal node opens as a leaf: here the
+-- root's own input at position `0` with the empty path.
+      (merkleLevel truncHash key leaves 1).getD 1 [])) 0 [] = merkleRoot truncHash key leaves := by
+-- Without a range check, position `1 + 4` reuses the opening of position `1`.
+    (merklePath truncHash key leaves 1) = merkleRoot truncHash key leaves := by
+-- Two leaves that agree on their first two bits collide under `truncHash` with a two-bit key.
+example : extractMerkleCollision truncHash [false, false] [true, true, false] [true, true, true] 0
+    [[false, true]] [[false, true]] = ([true, true, false], [true, true, true]) := by
+-- Different leaf nodes `[true, false]` and `[true, true]` whose paired inputs collide one level up:
+-- the extracted pair is the two level-one inputs.
+    merkleRootOfPath truncHash [false, false] [true, true] 0 [[false, false]] := by

+# Authenticated Encryption and Adaptive Chosen-Ciphertext Security
+This module formalizes symmetric authenticated encryption (`AuthenticatedEncryption`) and adaptive
+[Boneh and Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*, Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023],
+   Definition 5.2, and Example 5.1, printed pp. 181–182; Exercise 5.10(a), printed p. 211):
+   a uniform symmetric cipher on `n`-bit messages at security parameter `n` consists of strict PPT
+   key generation `keyGen`, strict PPT encryption `encrypt`, and deterministic polynomial-time
+   decryption `decrypt` returning `Option (List Bool)` (encoded via `encOption encBits`). In
+   `cpaGame`, an adaptive `OracleDistinguisher` submits left-or-right pairs `(m0, m1)` of `n`-bit
+   messages and receives `encrypt n k (if bit then m1 else m0)`. We also formalize Example 5.1 and
+   Exercise 5.10(a) (`not_indcpa_of_ciphertext_length_eq`): if every supported ciphertext of an
+   `n`-bit message has length `n`, decryption completeness forces `encrypt` to be a deterministic
+   permutation on `n`-bit strings, which a 2-query CPA adversary (`detCPAAdversary`) breaks with
+   Definitions 9.1–9.2, printed pp. 358–359): in `ciGame`, an adaptive `CIAdversary` queries an
+   encryption oracle on `n`-bit messages (logging returned ciphertexts in `queriedCiphertexts`) and
+   wins by outputting a candidate ciphertext `ct` such that `!queriedCiphertexts.contains ct` and
+   `(decrypt n k ct).isSome`. A cipher provides `AuthenticatedEncryption` when it satisfies both
+   ([BonehShoup2023], Sections 9.2.2–9.2.3, Attack Game 9.2, Definition 9.5, and Theorem 9.1,

+   interleave left-or-right encryption queries (`false`, recording challenge ciphertexts) with
+   decryption queries (`true`, rejecting recorded challenge ciphertexts and returning

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) samples a public/secret key pair `(pk, sk) ← keyGen n` and
+encapsulates a symmetric key `(k, ctKem) ← encaps n pk` ([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 11.9). Its
+chosen-plaintext / semantic security (`KEMINDCPA`, Exercise 11.9) asks that replacing the
+encapsulated key `k` with an independent uniform `n`-bit key `BitString.sampleList n` is
+computationally indistinguishable to every uniform strict PPT distinguisher receiving
+A Data Encapsulation Mechanism (DEM) for bit messages encrypts a single challenge bit under a
+fresh uniform `n`-bit key (`demGame`, [BonehShoup2023], Section 2.2, Attack Game 2.1 and
+Combining `encaps` with `encryptSym` produces the hybrid public-key encryption scheme
+`hybridEncrypt encaps encryptSym` (`hybridDecrypt decaps decryptSym`, Exercise 11.9(a)). By
+Boneh and Shoup's Exercise 11.9(b), if the KEM is IND-CPA secure and the DEM is one-time IND-CPA
+secure, then `hybridEncrypt encaps encryptSym` is IND-CPA secure (`KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa`).
+We formalize both the single hidden-bit KEM distinguisher bound of Exercise 11.9(b)
+(`advantage_hybridGame_le`), together with a non-vacuous one-time pad DEM instantiation
+Relative to [Boneh and Shoup, Exercise 11.9][BonehShoup2023], this development is specialized as
+* Plaintext messages are single bits (`Bool`), matching `Encryption.game` and `Encryption.INDCPA`
+* Both the ideal KEM key distribution and the one-time DEM key distribution at security parameter
+  `n` are fixed to uniform `n`-bit strings (`BitString.sampleList n`). Because `encaps` returns
+  arbitrary bit lists and `KEMINDCPA` requires only negligible distinguishing advantage, finitely
+  many or negligibly probable length deviations remain compatible with `KEMINDCPA`, whereas
+  non-negligible length deviations are detectable (as in `not_kemINDCPA_leaking`).
+* Decapsulation `decaps` and hybrid decryption `hybridDecrypt` are total deterministic functions
+  without a separate `reject` symbol; `hybridDecrypt_hybridEncrypt` states exact recovery on
+  supported ciphertexts when `decaps` and `decryptSym` are correct on supported outputs.
+* In `kemRealGame` and `kemIdealGame`, the KEM distinguisher receives the public key `pk`
+  explicitly alongside `(k, ctKem)` (encoded as `(pk, (k, ctKem))`). Although the prose of
+  Exercise 11.9 writes that the challenger sends `(k_b, c_kem)`, the public key `pk` is public in a
+  public-key KEM experiment and is required by the reduction distinguisher to run
+  `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.KEMINDCPA`: real and ideal KEM IND-CPA experiments and security.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.hybridIdealGame`: intermediate game replacing the encapsulated key
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+/-- The real KEM IND-CPA experiment ([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 11.9, Experiment `0`):
+sample `(pk, sk) ← keyGen n` and `(k, ctKem) ← encaps n pk`, and pass the encoded triple
+def kemRealGame (keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
+    (encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
+  distinguisher n (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits) (keys.1, encapsulated))
+/-- The ideal KEM IND-CPA experiment ([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 11.9, Experiment `1`):
+sample `(pk, sk) ← keyGen n`, `(k, ctKem) ← encaps n pk`, and an independent uniform `n`-bit key
+`kIdeal ← BitString.sampleList n`, and pass `(pk, (kIdeal, ctKem))` to `distinguisher n`. -/

+    (encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
+/-- The real KEM IND-CPA experiment is uniform strict PPT when key generation, encapsulation, and
+theorem isPPTOn_kemRealGame {keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)}
+    {encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)}
+    {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {n : α → ℕ}

+  let E1 := encPair input (encPair encBits encBits)
+  let E2 := encPair E1 (encPair encBits encBits)
+      (fun p : α × List Bool × List Bool => (n p.1, p.2.1))
+      (fun p : (α × List Bool × List Bool) × List Bool × List Bool =>
+/-- The ideal KEM IND-CPA experiment is uniform strict PPT when key generation, encapsulation, and
+theorem isPPTOn_kemIdealGame {keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)}
+    {encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)}

+# Converse of Liu–Pass: Average-Case Hardness of $K^t$ Implies One-Way Functions
+This module formalizes the Section 4 converse construction of
+[Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020]
+if $t$-time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity $K^t$ is mildly hard on average against uniform strict
+PPT heuristics for some polynomial-time computable time bound $t(n) \ge n + 1$, then there exists a
+weak one-way function (`Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWay`), and therefore by Yao's hardness amplification
+(`Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWay.exists_oneWay`) there exists a strong one-way function
+**Model note ($t(n) \ge n + 1$ sufficient clock hypothesis vs. $t(n) > 0$):**
+In [Liu and Pass, Fact 2.1, §2.2, p. 8; Theorem 3.1 (b), §3, p. 9; Theorem 4.1, §4, p. 10 of
+`arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020], the time bound is stated as $t(n) > 0$ under a machine model in
+which outputting an $n$-bit string takes at least $1$ step. Under `complexitylib`'s multi-tape
+Turing machine output convention (`DescriptionMethod.universalTM`), the literal/copy program bound
+supplies a program that prints each $n$-bit string within $n + 1$ steps
+(`Kolmogorov.timeBoundedNat_le_length_add`). This module assumes `∀ n, n + 1 ≤ t n` so that bound
+ensures finite $K^t$ for every input; this is a sufficient clock hypothesis in the native model,
+rather than a lower bound on every program or an equivalence with the source's $t(n) > 0$
+## Construction Overview ([Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 4.1, §4, p. 10][LiuPass2020])
+   At parameter $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every string $y \in \{0, 1\}^n$ has time-bounded Kolmogorov

+2. **Preimage soundness and shared-coin PPT heuristic reduction:**
+   Any preimage of `targetImage i y = (i, some y)` under `liuPassCore t n` yields a program of
+   length at most $i$ that outputs $y$ within $t(n)$ steps, certifying $K^t(y) \le i$
+   (`timeBoundedNat_le_of_liuPassCore_eq_targetImage`). Whereas Liu and Pass (§4, p. 10) fix a
+   "good" random tape by an averaging argument and union bound (obtaining weak-OWF polynomial
+   $q(n) = 2^{2c+3} n p(n)^2$), our proof shares a single polynomial coin tape across all
+   over $i \in \{0, \dots, \mathrm{maxComplexity}(n)\}$ to define a uniform strict PPT heuristic

+/-- Decode the program-length prefix $i \in \{0, \dots, \mathrm{maxComplexity}(n)\}$ from the first

+/-- Extract the candidate program of length at most `decodeLen n x` after the `lenWidth n`-bit

+parse $x$ into a length $i := \mathrm{decodeLen}\ n\ x \le n + \mathrm{copyOverhead}$ and a program

title: feat(Crypto/OneWay): add WeakOneWay, output normalization, and schedule reindexing (#992)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Weak One-Way Functions, Output Normalization, and Schedule Reindexing
+This module defines $\alpha$-weak one-way functions (`Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWayAt`) and weak one-way
+functions (`Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWay`) against uniform strict PPT inverters following
+[Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020] (Definition 2.2,
+§2.1, p. 7 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`; FOCS 2020, p. 1246), originally due to [A. C. Yao][Yao1982] and
+In addition to basic monotonicity, `<` vs. `≤` equivalence bridges, strong-implies-weak
+(`Cslib.Crypto.not_weakOneWay_const`), this module provides two structural transformations reused
+by Yao's direct-product hardness amplification and the Liu–Pass Section 4 converse construction:
+   Every weak one-way function yields a weak one-way function whose output length depends only on
+   the input length, reusing self-delimiting padding from
+   Given an input-length schedule `m : ℕ → ℕ` with `m n ≥ n + 1` computable in unary polynomial
+   time and a parameter-indexed family `core : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool` defined on inputs of
+   length `m n`, `OneWayReindex.reindex m core` extends the family to all input lengths
+   $M \in \mathbb{N}$ by finding the greatest parameter $n$ with $m(n) \le M$
+   (`GeneratorReindex.parameter`), evaluating `core n` on the $m(n)$-bit prefix, and pairing the
+   core output with the parameter $n$ in unary (`wrappedImage`). This is a library variant and
+   generalization of the input-truncation padding trick in
+   [Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 4.1, §4, p. 10 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020] (cf. the
+   with the parameter $n$ appended to the output so images from distinct parameters are disjoint
+   and the reduction is lossless even for nonmonotone schedules. Both weak one-wayness
+   (`OneWayReindex.weakOneWay`) and strong one-wayness (`OneWayReindex.oneWay`) transfer from the
+   parameter-indexed game `familyInversionGame` to all input lengths.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWayAt`: $\alpha$-weak one-way function against uniform strict PPT inverters
+* `Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWay`: weak one-way function ($\frac{1}{q(\cdot)}$-weak OWF for some positive
+  polynomial $q$, [Liu and Pass, Definition 2.2, §2.1, p. 7 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayReindex.reindex`: extend a parameter-indexed family on input lengths `m n` to
+* `Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWay.exists_monotone_poly`: every weak OWF admits a monotone polynomial bound
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWay.weakOneWay`: every strong one-way function is a weak one-way function.
+  right-inverses and constant functions refute weak one-wayness.
+  `reindex m core` at length `M ≥ m 0` reduces without probability loss to a uniform PPT inverter in
+  one-wayness transfer from `familyInversionGame` on `m n` to `reindex m core` on all input lengths.
+* [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],
+  full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1` (Section 2.1, Definition 2.2 and Section 4, Theorem 4.1).
+* [A. C. Yao, *Theory and Application of Trapdoor Functions*][Yao1982].
+A polynomial-time computable function $f : \{0, 1\}^* \to \{0, 1\}^*$ is an $\alpha$-weak one-way
+function if for every uniform strict PPT inverter $\mathcal{A}$, for all sufficiently large
+structure WeakOneWayAt (f : List Bool → List Bool) (α : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop where
+  /-- A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm evaluates the function. -/
+  /-- Every uniform strict PPT inverter succeeds with probability `< 1 - α n` eventually. -/
+  weak : ∀ adversary : Inverter, IsPPT encBits adversary →
+      (Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval (inversionGame f adversary n)) : ℝ) < 1 - α n

+# One-Way Functions Imply Average-Case Hardness of Time-Bounded Kolmogorov Complexity
+This module proves the **M2a polynomial-overhead form** of the forward direction of the main
+theorem of [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020]:
+if one-way functions exist, then for every constant $d \in \mathbb{N}$ there exists a polynomial
+$p(n) > 0$ such that for every time bound $t(n) \ge p(n)$, $t$-time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity
+$K^t$ is mildly hard on average against uniform strict PPT heuristics, and mildly hard on average
+to approximate within the symmetric error windows $d (\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$,
+$d \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$, $d \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, and the real-valued window $d \log_2 n$.
+All section, theorem, definition, lemma, and page locators follow the full version
+In [Liu and Pass, Theorem 3.1 (b)–(c), §3, p. 9 and Theorem 5.2, §5.2, p. 11 of
+arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020], the universal Turing machine is assumed to simulate any fixed
+machine with constant multiplicative time overhead (rate-$1$ universal simulation), which yields
+hardness for all polynomial $t(n) \ge (1 + \varepsilon) n$ once the PRG evaluation is optimized to
+near-linear time. Because `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded` is defined over the library's polynomial-
+evaluating the truncated generator takes a fixed polynomial $p(n)$ steps on the universal machine,
+giving the M2a polynomial-threshold form $\exists p,\ \forall t \ge p$.
+[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020] defines
+$g$-approximation via the symmetric error bound $|v - f(x)| \le g(|x|)$, formalized on $\mathbb{N}$
+by `Cslib.Complexity.MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` (`Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g n`). The threshold
+distinguisher of Theorem 5.2 directly establishes one-sided underestimation hardness
+(`Cslib.Complexity.MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`) for the upper-rounded integer log window
+$g(n) = d (\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$ (`d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`). Applying the PPT shift and
+heuristic's output down by $g(|x|)$ and doubling the PRG stretch parameter from $2 d + 3$ to
+$4 d + 3$) yields symmetric `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` for `d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`. Since
+for all $n \ge 1$, monotonicity immediately yields symmetric approximation hardness for
+`d * Nat.clog 2 n`, `d * Nat.log 2 n`, and the real-valued $|(v : \mathbb{R}) - K^t(x)| \le
+  a $(1 / n^2, \gamma)$-condEP-PRG with $\gamma \ge 2 d + 3$ implies one-sided
+  $d (\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$-approximation hardness of $K^t$ for all $t \ge p_G$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 5.2, §5.2, p. 11 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020], M2a
+  a $(1 / n^2, \gamma)$-condEP-PRG with $\gamma \ge 4 d + 3$ implies symmetric PPT approximation
+  hardness of $K^t$ for all $t \ge p_G$ under $d (\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$,
+  ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 5.2, §5.2, p. 11 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020], M2a
+  exact average-case PPT hardness specialization of Theorem 5.2 ($\gamma \ge 3$, M2a
+  every one-way function implies the existence of a polynomial $p$ such that for all $t \ge p$,
+  $K^t$ is mildly hard on average to approximate within $d (\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$,
+  $d \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$, $d \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, and real $d \log_2 n$ against uniform
+  ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 3.1 (a) $\Rightarrow$ (c), §3, p. 9 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020],
+  every one-way function implies the existence of a polynomial $p$ such that for all $t \ge p$,
+  $K^t$ is mildly hard on average against uniform strict PPT heuristics
+  ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 3.1 (a) $\Rightarrow$ (b), §3, p. 9 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020],
+  existential M2a polynomial-overhead forms of [Liu and Pass, Theorem 3.1 (a) $\Rightarrow$ (c) and
+* [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],
+open Cslib.Complexity Probability Probability.PMF BitString Filter Kolmogorov Turing.MultiTapeTM
+private def stretchLen (γ n : ℕ) : ℕ := n + γ * Nat.log 2 n
+    stretchLen γ (n + 1) ≤ stretchLen γ n + γ + 1 := by
+  Nat.findGreatest (fun k => stretchLen γ k ≤ m) m + 1
+    m < stretchLen γ (seedLen γ m) ∧ stretchLen γ (seedLen γ m) ≤ m + γ + 1 := by
+  let n₀ := Nat.findGreatest (fun k => stretchLen γ k ≤ m) m
+  have hn₀_le_m : n₀ ≤ m := Nat.findGreatest_le m
+  have hn₀_spec : stretchLen γ n₀ ≤ m :=
+    Nat.findGreatest_spec (P := fun k => stretchLen γ k ≤ m) (Nat.zero_le m) (by simp [stretchLen])
+  have hgt : m < stretchLen γ (n₀ + 1) := by
+        (P := fun k => stretchLen γ k ≤ m) (Nat.lt_succ_self n₀) (by omega))
+    · have heq : n₀ = m := by omega
+  have hle : stretchLen γ (n₀ + 1) ≤ m + γ + 1 :=
+private theorem seedLen_bound (γ m : ℕ) : m < (γ + 1) * seedLen γ m := by
+  have hlog : Nat.log 2 (seedLen γ m) ≤ seedLen γ m := Nat.log_le_self 2 _
+private theorem tendsto_seedLen (γ : ℕ) : Tendsto (seedLen γ) atTop atTop := by
+  have : (γ + 1) * seedLen γ m ≤ (γ + 1) * N := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (γ + 1) hlt.le
+/-! ### Truncated generator and threshold distinguisher for Theorem 5.2 -/
+private def truncGen (G : List Bool → List Bool) (p : ℕ × List Bool) : List Bool :=
+private theorem computableInPolyTime_truncGen {G : List Bool → List Bool}
+    ComputableInPolyTime (truncGen G) (encPair encUnary encBits) encBits := by
+private def thresholdValue (γ d c n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  let m := n + γ * Nat.log 2 n - c
+    ComputableInPolyTime (thresholdValue γ d c) encUnary encUnary := by
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => d * (Nat.log 2 x.length + 1)) encBits encNat := by
+      ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => d * (Nat.log 2 x.length + 1))
+private noncomputable def thresholdDistinguisher (γ d c : ℕ) (H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ) :
+  (fun v => decide (thresholdValue γ d c n ≤ v)) <$>
+private theorem isPPT_thresholdDistinguisher (γ d c : ℕ) {H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ}
+    IsPPT encBool (thresholdDistinguisher γ d c H) := by
+      (fun v => decide (thresholdValue γ d c p.1 ≤ v)) <$>
+      (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => p.2.take (p.1 + γ * Nat.log 2 p.1 - c))
+      (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ℕ => decide (thresholdValue γ d c pair.1.1 ≤ pair.2))
+        (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ℕ => thresholdValue γ d c pair.1.1)
+        (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ℕ => min (thresholdValue γ d c pair.1.1) pair.2)
+        (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ℕ => decide (thresholdValue γ d c pair.1.1 ≤ pair.2)) =
+          decide (thresholdValue γ d c pair.1.1 ≤ min (thresholdValue γ d c pair.1.1) pair.2)) := by
+/-! ### Theorem 5.2: Conditional EP-PRGs imply $K^t$ is mildly hard on average
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Theorem 5.2, §5.2, p. 11 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020] (M2a
+If $G$ is a $(1 / n^2, \gamma)$-condEP-PRG with entropy-loss constant $\alpha$ and stretch factor
+$\gamma \ge 2 d + 3$, then there exists a polynomial $p_G$ (with $n + 1 \le p_G(n)$ for all $n$)
+such that for every time bound $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ dominating $p_G$,
+`Kolmogorov.timeBoundedNat t` is mildly hard on average to one-sidedly approximate within the
+    {G : List Bool → List Bool} {γ α : ℕ} (d : ℕ) (hγ : 2 * d + 3 ≤ γ)
+    (hG : CondEPPRG G (fun n => 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) γ α) :

+      ∀ {t : ℕ → ℕ}, (∀ n, pG.eval n ≤ t n) →

+  have hq_eval (m : ℕ) : q.eval m = 16 * (m + 1) ^ (γ + α + 2) := by
+  have hq_pos (m : ℕ) : 0 < q.eval m := by
+  have hall_sec : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ c : Fin (γ + 2),
+          fun y => ProbComp.eval (thresholdDistinguisher γ d c.val H n y))
+          fun y => ProbComp.eval (thresholdDistinguisher γ d c.val H n y)) : ℝ) ≤
+    Filter.eventually_all.mpr fun c => hG_sec (thresholdDistinguisher γ d c.val H)
+  set C₀ := 2 * γ + 3 + c_sim with hC₀_def
+  have h_ev_n : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ (c : Fin (γ + 2)) (m : ℕ),
+      m = n + γ * Nat.log 2 n - c.val →
+          decide (timeBoundedNat t x - d * (Nat.log 2 m + 1) ≤ v ∧
+      n hn_sec hn_ent hn_4γ hlog_n_ge hlog_bound c m hm_def
+    set m₀ := n + γ * Nat.log 2 n with hm₀_def
+    have hc_le : c.val ≤ γ + 1 := Nat.le_of_lt_succ c.isLt

+    have hm_ge_n : n ≤ m := by omega
+    have hm_le_m₀ : m ≤ m₀ := by omega
+    have hlog_m_le : Nat.log 2 m ≤ 2 * Nat.log 2 n + 1 := by
+      have hlog_le : Nat.log 2 n ≤ n := Nat.log_le_self 2 n
+      have hm_le_sq : m ≤ n * n := by

+      simp only [PMF.bind_map, thresholdDistinguisher, ProbComp.eval_map, ← hm₀_def, ← hm_def,
+    set B : ℝ := (n : ℝ) - (α : ℝ) * (Nat.log 2 n : ℝ) - (c.val : ℝ) with hB_def

title: feat(Computability/Complexity): add average-case hardness definitions and PPT shift bridge (#733) (#986)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Mild Average-Case Hardness of Functions Against Efficient Heuristics
+This module formalizes generic mild average-case hardness definitions for functions
+`f : List Bool → ℕ` (and `f : List Bool → ℕ∞`) over the uniform distribution on `{0, 1}^n`
+following [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],
+together with monotonicity, one-sided-to-symmetric shifting bridges, rounded-logarithm comparison
+lemmas, and negative nonvacuity witnesses on the constant zero function. All section, definition,
+theorem, lemma, and page locators follow the full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1` (and ECCC TR20-052).
+* `Cslib.Complexity.MildlyHardOnAverage`: mild average-case hardness of exact computation for
+  `List Bool → ℕ` against uniform strict PPT heuristics
+  ([Liu and Pass, Definition 2.4, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+  $g(n)$-approximation (`Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g n`, i.e., $|v - f(x)| \le g(|x|)$) for
+  `List Bool → ℕ` against uniform strict PPT heuristics
+  ([Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+  underestimation error (`f x - g n ≤ v ∧ v ≤ f x`) against uniform strict PPT heuristics.
+  library specializations to deterministic polynomial-time heuristics.
+  library infinitely-often (`∃ᶠ n in atTop`) deterministic companions.
+  monotonicity in the approximation error bound `g`.
+  shift + gap-scaling bridge converting one-sided $(2 g)$-approximation hardness into symmetric
+  $g$-approximation hardness whenever `fun x => g x.length` is computable in polynomial time.
+  upper-rounded integer log window `d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)` implies the real-valued symmetric window
+  negative nonvacuity lemmas showing the constant zero function is not mildly hard on average.
+* [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],
+([Liu and Pass, Definitions 2.4 and 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]) -/
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.4, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]:
+A function $f : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathbb{N}$ is mildly hard on average if there exists a positive
+polynomial $p$ such that for every uniform strict PPT heuristic
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ, IsPPTOn encBits encNat H →
+          (ProbComp.eval (H x)).map fun v => decide (v = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]:
+A function $f : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathbb{N}$ is mildly hard on average to $g$-approximate if there
+exists a positive polynomial $p$ such that for every uniform strict PPT heuristic
+where $|v - f(x)|$ is formalized on $\mathbb{N}$ by the symmetric distance `Nat.dist v (f x)`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ, IsPPTOn encBits encNat H →
+            decide (Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g n)) true).toReal ≤
+approximation hardness against uniform strict PPT heuristics, requiring
+(`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f`) whenever `fun x => g x.length` is computable in polynomial time
+by shifting any heuristic output down by $g(|x|)$. -/

+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧

+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (H x = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+          decide (Nat.dist (H x) (f x) ≤ g n)) true).toReal ≤

+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+          decide (f x - g n ≤ H x ∧ H x ≤ f x)) true).toReal ≤
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧

+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (H x = f x)) true).toReal ≤

+private theorem bind_map_decide_le_of_imp {n : ℕ} (q : List Bool → PMF ℕ)
+    (P Q : List Bool → ℕ → Prop) [∀ x v, Decidable (P x v)] [∀ x v, Decidable (Q x v)]

+  · have hq := himp x hx v hp
