lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Correctness of the AKS primality test
+**Theorem** [Agrawal, Kayal, Saxena, Theorem 4.1][AKS2004]: if `n ≥ 2` passes the tests of the
+AKS algorithm for an `r` such that the multiplicative order of `n` modulo `r` exceeds `log₂² n`,
+If `n ≤ r`, every `a < n` is coprime to `n` by step 3. Otherwise suppose `n` is composite with
+least prime factor `p`. Step 3 forces `p > r`. Let `ζ` be a primitive `r`-th root of unity in a
+* Every `m = (n/p)^i p^j` is introspective for every product of the polynomials `X + a`,
+* Let `t` be the number of residues of these `m` modulo `r`; `log₂² n < ord_r(n) ≤ t ≤ φ(r)`. Put
+  `B = ⌊√t log₂ n⌋`, so `B < t` and `B ≤ ⌊√φ(r) log₂ n⌋`.
+* **Lower bound.** The products of `B` factors `X + a` with `0 ≤ a ≤ B` take `C(2B, B)` distinct
+  values at `ζ`: two products agreeing at `ζ` agree at the `t` distinct roots `ζ^m`, and have
+* **Upper bound.** Since `n` is not a power of `p`, the numbers `(n/p)^i p^j` with
+  `i, j ≤ ⌊√t⌋` are distinct; there are more than `t` of them, so two, `m₁ ≠ m₂`, agree modulo
+  `r`. Every value above is then a root of `Y^{m₁} - Y^{m₂}`, so there are at most `n^{⌊√t⌋}`.
+* Finally `n^{⌊√t⌋} ≤ n^{√t} < 2^{B + 1} ≤ C(2B, B)`, a contradiction.
+This follows [Agrawal, Kayal, Saxena, Section 4][AKS2004], with two simplifications: the field is
+generated by a primitive root of unity rather than by an irreducible factor of the cyclotomic
+polynomial, and the lower bound counts only products of exactly `B` factors.
+* `Cslib.AKS.prime_iff_passes`: the AKS tests characterize the primes.
+* [M. Agrawal, N. Kayal, N. Saxena, *PRIMES is in P*][AKS2004]
+/-- **Step 4.** If `n ≤ r` and no `a ≤ r` has `1 < gcd(a, n) < n`, then `n` is prime. -/
+    (hgcd : ∀ a, 1 ≤ a → a ≤ r → a.gcd n = 1 ∨ a.gcd n = n) (hnr : n ≤ r) : n.Prime := by
+  have hlt : n.minFac < n := (Nat.not_prime_iff_minFac_lt hn).mp hnp
+  have hg : n.minFac.gcd n = n.minFac := Nat.gcd_eq_left (Nat.minFac_dvd n)
+  rcases hgcd n.minFac hq.one_lt.le (hlt.le.trans hnr) with h | h
+/-- If `n` has positive multiplicative order modulo `r`, then `n` is coprime to `r`. -/
+theorem coprime_of_orderOf_pos {n r : ℕ} (h : 0 < orderOf (n : ZMod r)) : n.Coprime r :=
+/-- If `q^i p^j = q^{i'} p^{j'}` for distinct exponent pairs and a prime `p`, then `q` is a power
+theorem exists_eq_pow_of_pow_mul_pow_eq {p q i j i' j' : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q ≠ 0)
+    (hne : (i, j) ≠ (i', j')) (h : q ^ i * p ^ j = q ^ i' * p ^ j') : ∃ s, q = p ^ s := by
+  wlog hii : i ≤ i' generalizing i j i' j'
+  · exact this (fun e => hne (by simp_all)) h.symm (by omega)
+    rw [pow_add, pow_add, mul_assoc, mul_assoc] at h
+    have h' := Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left (pow_pos (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hq) i) h
+    have hdvd : q ∣ p ^ j := ⟨q ^ d * p ^ j', by rw [h']; ring⟩
+  · have hj : p ^ j = p ^ j' :=
+  induction B, hB using Nat.le_induction with
+variable {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
+/-- The product `∏_{a ∈ s} (X + a)` over `ℤ / p` of a multiset `s` of `B` numbers in `[0, B]`. -/
+  ((s : Multiset (Fin (B + 1))).map fun a : Fin (B + 1) => X + C ((a : ℕ) : ZMod p)).prod
+    linProd p s = (((s : Multiset (Fin (B + 1))).map fun a : Fin (B + 1) => -((a : ℕ) : ZMod p)).map
+      fun c => X - C c).prod := by
+theorem natDegree_linProd (s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B) : (linProd p s).natDegree = B := by
+/-- Distinct multisets give distinct products when `B < p`: the product determines its roots. -/
+theorem linProd_injective (hB : B < p) : Function.Injective (linProd (B := B) p) := by
+  rw [linProd_eq, linProd_eq, roots_multiset_prod_X_sub_C, roots_multiset_prod_X_sub_C] at hroots
+  have hinj : Function.Injective fun a : Fin (B + 1) => -((a : ℕ) : ZMod p) := by
+    have ha : (a : ℕ) < p := by omega
+    have hb : (b : ℕ) < p := by omega
+    rw [ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff', Nat.mod_eq_of_lt ha, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hb] at hab
+/-- Powers of a primitive `r`-th root of unity only depend on the exponent modulo `r`. -/
+    {m₁ m₂ : ℕ} (h : (m₁ : ZMod r) = m₂) : ζ ^ m₁ = ζ ^ m₂ := by
+  rw [← pow_mod_orderOf, ← pow_mod_orderOf ζ m₂, ← hζ.eq_orderOf, h]
+/-- **The lower bound.** Let `S` be a set of more than `B` residues modulo `r`, each the residue
+of a number introspective for every product `∏_{a ∈ s} (X + a)`. If `B < p`, these `C(2B, B)`
+products take distinct values at a primitive `r`-th root of unity `ζ`: two products agreeing at `ζ`
+agree at the `|S|` distinct roots `ζ^m`, and have degree `B`. -/
+theorem card_image_aeval_linProd [NeZero r] {ζ : K} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ r) (hB : B < p)
+    (hS : ∀ x ∈ S, ∃ m : ℕ, (m : ZMod r) = x ∧
+      ∀ s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B, Introspective K r m (linProd p s)) :
+    (univ.image fun s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B => aeval ζ (linProd p s)).card = B.centralBinom := by
+    show B + 1 + B - 1 = 2 * B by omega, Nat.centralBinom_eq_two_mul_choose]
+  have hdiff : linProd p s - linProd p s' ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr fun h => hne
+  have hF : (linProd p s - linProd p s').map (algebraMap (ZMod p) K) ≠ 0 :=
+  -- The `|S|` distinct powers `ζ^m` are roots of `F`.
+  have hsub : (S.image fun x => ζ ^ x.val).val ⊆
+      ((linProd p s - linProd p s').map (algebraMap (ZMod p) K)).roots := by
+    obtain ⟨m, rfl, hm⟩ := hS x hx
+    rw [mem_roots hF, IsRoot, eval_map_algebraMap, map_sub, sub_eq_zero,
+      hζ.pow_eq_pow_of_natCast_eq (ZMod.natCast_zmod_val _), ← hm s ζ hζr, ← hm s' ζ hζr, hss']
+  have hcard : (S.image fun x => ζ ^ x.val).card = S.card := by
+    refine card_image_of_injOn fun x _ y _ hxy => ZMod.val_injective r ?_
+  have : ((linProd p s - linProd p s').map (algebraMap (ZMod p) K)).natDegree ≤ B := by
+/-- **The upper bound.** If distinct `m₁ ≡ m₂ (mod r)` are both introspective for every product
+`∏_{a ∈ s} (X + a)`, then every value of these products at a primitive `r`-th root of unity is a
+root of `Y^{m₁} - Y^{m₂}`, so there are at most `max m₁ m₂` such values. -/
+theorem card_image_aeval_linProd_le {ζ : K} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ r) {m₁ m₂ : ℕ}
+    (h₁ : ∀ s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B, Introspective K r m₁ (linProd p s))
+    (h₂ : ∀ s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B, Introspective K r m₂ (linProd p s)) :
+    (univ.image fun s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B => aeval ζ (linProd p s)).card ≤ max m₁ m₂ := by
+  set Q : K[X] := X ^ m₁ - X ^ m₂
+  have hsub : (univ.image fun s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B => aeval ζ (linProd p s)).val ⊆
+    rw [mem_roots hQ, IsRoot, eval_sub, eval_pow, eval_X, eval_pow, eval_X, sub_eq_zero,
+      h₁ s ζ hζr, h₂ s ζ hζr, hζ.pow_eq_pow_of_natCast_eq hmod]
+/-- If `m` is coprime to `r`, so is its residue `m % r`. -/
+private theorem coprime_mod_of_coprime {m r : ℕ} (h : m.Coprime r) : (m % r).Coprime r := by
+/-- **Correctness of the AKS tests** [Agrawal, Kayal, Saxena, Theorem 4.1][AKS2004]: if `n ≥ 2`
+passes the tests of the AKS algorithm for an `r` such that the multiplicative order of `n` modulo
+    (hr : Real.logb 2 n ^ 2 < orderOf (n : ZMod r)) (h : Passes n r) : n.Prime := by
+  have hord_pos : 0 < orderOf (n : ZMod r) := by
+    have : (0 : ℝ) < orderOf (n : ZMod r) := lt_of_le_of_lt (by positivity) hr
+  have hcop : n.Coprime r := coprime_of_orderOf_pos hord_pos
+  -- The least prime factor `p` of `n` exceeds `r`.
+  have hpn : p ∣ n := Nat.minFac_dvd n
+  have hplt : p < n := (Nat.not_prime_iff_minFac_lt hn).mp hnp
+    have hg : p.gcd n = p := Nat.gcd_eq_left hpn
+    rcases hgcd p hp.one_lt.le hle with h | h
+  have hqp : q * p = n := Nat.div_mul_cancel hpn
+  have hcopq : q.Coprime r := Nat.Coprime.coprime_dvd_left (Nat.div_dvd_of_dvd hpn) hcop
+  have hcopp : p.Coprime r := Nat.Coprime.coprime_dvd_left hpn hcop
+  -- The residues of the introspective numbers `q^i p^j`.
+  set S : Finset (ZMod r) := univ.filter fun x => ∃ i j : ℕ, x = ((q ^ i * p ^ j : ℕ) : ZMod r)
+  have hord_t : orderOf (n : ZMod r) ≤ t := by
+    have hsub : ((range (orderOf (n : ZMod r))).image fun i => (n : ZMod r) ^ i) ⊆ S := by
+      exact ⟨i, i, by rw [← hqp]; push_cast; ring⟩
+          ((range (orderOf (n : ZMod r))).image fun i => (n : ZMod r) ^ i).card := by
+        intro i hi j hj hij
+        exact pow_injOn_Iio_orderOf (by simpa using hi) (by simpa using hj) hij
+    refine card_le_card_of_injOn (fun x => x.val) ?_ (fun x _ y _ hxy => ZMod.val_injective r hxy)
+    simp only [S, coe_filter, mem_univ, true_and, Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hx
+  have htot_lt : r.totient < r := Nat.totient_lt r (by omega)
+  have hlogt : Real.logb 2 n < Real.sqrt t := by
+  have hBreal : (B : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt t * Real.logb 2 n := Nat.floor_le (by positivity)
+        (B : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt t * Real.logb 2 n := hBreal
+        _ < Real.sqrt t * Real.sqrt t := by gcongr
+  have hBℓ : B ≤ numTests n r :=
+  have hBp : B < p := by omega
+    have : (2 : ℝ) < Real.sqrt t := by linarith
+  -- A primitive `r`-th root of unity in characteristic `p`.
+  have hζ := IsCyclotomicExtension.zeta_spec r (ZMod p) K
+  set ζ := IsCyclotomicExtension.zeta r (ZMod p) K
+  -- Every `q^i p^j` is introspective for every product of the `X + a`, `a ≤ B`.
+  have hintro : ∀ i j : ℕ, ∀ s : Sym (Fin (B + 1)) B,
+      Introspective K r (q ^ i * p ^ j) (linProd p s) := by
+    have hn' : Introspective K r n (X + C ((a : ℕ) : ZMod p)) := by
+      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (a : ℕ) with ha | ha
+      · exact introspective_of_congruence hpn (hcong a ha (by have := a.isLt; omega))
+  have hlow := card_image_aeval_linProd (K := K) hζ hBp (S := S) hBt (fun x hx => by
+    simp only [S, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at hx
+  -- Two of the numbers `q^i p^j`, `i, j ≤ ⌊√t⌋`, agree modulo `r`.
+  obtain ⟨⟨i, j⟩, hij, ⟨i', j'⟩, hij', hne, heq⟩ :=
+      (f := fun ij => ((q ^ ij.1 * p ^ ij.2 : ℕ) : ZMod r))
+      (fun ij _ => by simp only [S, coe_filter, mem_univ, true_and, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
+  simp only [mem_product, mem_range] at hij hij'
+  -- They are distinct as numbers, since `n` is not a power of `p`.
+  have hm_ne : q ^ i * p ^ j ≠ q ^ i' * p ^ j' := by
+    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := exists_eq_pow_of_pow_mul_pow_eq hp hq0 hne hm
+    have hns : n = p ^ (s + 1) := by rw [← hqp, hs, pow_succ]
+    · exact hnp (by rw [hns, zero_add, pow_one]; exact hp)
+    · exact hpow ⟨p, s + 1 + 1, by omega, hns.symm⟩
+  have hup := card_image_aeval_linProd_le (K := K) hζ hm_ne heq (hintro i j) (hintro i' j')
+  have hmk : ∀ i j, i ≤ k → j ≤ k → q ^ i * p ^ j ≤ n ^ k := by

+      _ = n ^ k := by rw [← mul_pow, hqp]
+  have hcard : B.centralBinom ≤ n ^ k := by

+/-- **The AKS tests characterize the primes**: for `n ≥ 2` and `r` such that the multiplicative

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Fix a prime `p`, a number `r`, and a field `K` that is an algebra over `ℤ / p`. A number `m` is
+*introspective* for a polynomial `f` over `ℤ / p` if `f(η)^m = f(η^m)` for every `r`-th root of
+unity `η` of `K` (`Cslib.AKS.Introspective`). This is the form of Agrawal, Kayal and Saxena's
+introspection `f(X)^m ≡ f(X^m) (mod X^r - 1, p)` that their proof uses, evaluated at roots of unity
+as in Lenstra's exposition [Agrawal, Kayal, Saxena, Section 4][AKS2004].
+* `p` is introspective for every `f`, by the Frobenius map (`introspective_prime`).
+* Introspective numbers are closed under products, and introspective polynomials under products
+* If `p ∣ n` and the AKS congruence `(X + a)^n ≡ X^n + a (mod X^r - 1, n)` holds, then `n` is
+* If `n` is introspective for `f` and `p ∣ n`, so is `n / p`, because the Frobenius map of a field
+* `Cslib.AKS.Introspective`: `f(η)^m = f(η^m)` at every `r`-th root of unity `η`.
+* [M. Agrawal, N. Kayal, N. Saxena, *PRIMES is in P*][AKS2004]
+/-- `m` is **introspective** for `f` (with respect to `r`): `f(η)^m = f(η^m)` for every `r`-th root
+  ∀ η : K, η ^ r = 1 → aeval η f ^ m = aeval (η ^ m) f
+/-- **The prime is introspective** for every polynomial: `f(η)^p = f(η^p)` by the Frobenius map,
+since the coefficients of `f` lie in `ℤ / p`. -/
+    Introspective K r p f := fun η _ => by
+theorem Introspective.mul (hm : Introspective K r m f) (hm' : Introspective K r m' f) :
+    Introspective K r (m * m') f := fun η hη => by
+  have hηm : (η ^ m) ^ r = 1 := by rw [← pow_mul, mul_comm, pow_mul, hη, one_pow]
+  rw [pow_mul, hm η hη, hm' _ hηm, ← pow_mul]
+theorem Introspective.mul_poly (hf : Introspective K r m f) (hg : Introspective K r m g) :
+    Introspective K r m (f * g) := fun η hη => by
+  rw [map_mul, map_mul, mul_pow, hf η hη, hg η hη]
+/-- Every number is introspective for the constant `1`. -/
+theorem introspective_one (r m : ℕ) : Introspective K r m (1 : (ZMod p)[X]) := fun η _ => by
+theorem introspective_X (r m : ℕ) : Introspective K r m (X : (ZMod p)[X]) := fun η _ => by
+/-- Products of introspective polynomials are introspective. -/
+    (hs : ∀ f ∈ s, Introspective K r m f) : Introspective K r m s.prod := by
+  | empty => simpa using introspective_one r m
+      (ih fun g hg => hs g (Multiset.mem_cons_of_mem hg))
+/-- Every power of `m` is introspective when `m` is. -/
+theorem Introspective.pow (hm : Introspective K r m f) (k : ℕ) : Introspective K r (m ^ k) f := by
+  | zero => exact fun η _ => by simp
+  | succ k ih => rw [pow_succ]; exact ih.mul hm
+/-- **The AKS congruence gives introspection.** If `p ∣ n` and
+`(X + a)^n ≡ X^n + a (mod X^r - 1, n)`, then `n` is introspective for `X + a`. -/
+theorem introspective_of_congruence {n a : ℕ} (hpn : p ∣ n) (h : Congruence n r a) :
+    Introspective K r n (X + C (a : ZMod p)) := fun η hη => by
+  let ψ : ZMod n →+* K := (algebraMap (ZMod p) K).comp (ZMod.castHom hpn (ZMod p))

+Directed `s`–`t` connectivity on adjacency matrices (`Cslib.Complexity.STCON`, encoded by
+`Cslib.Complexity.encSTCON`) is complete for nondeterministic logarithmic space under logspace
+The classes are the library's native ones: `NL` is decided by one finite-state nondeterministic
+machine within work space `c * (Nat.log2 n + 1)`, every branch halting, and the reductions are
+computed by deterministic machines within such space (`Cslib.Complexity.LogSpaceReducible`).
+  nondeterministic counter program walks from `s`, guessing one vertex at a time and giving up
+* **Hardness** (`Cslib.Complexity.STCON.logSpaceHard`): a problem decided by a machine within
+  space `c * (Nat.log2 n + 1)` reduces to `STCON` by mapping an instance to the configuration graph
+  of the machine on its encoding, with a sink after the accepting vertices
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.STCON.configurationInstance`), computed in logarithmic space by a counter
+The complement of `STCON` is in `NL` too (`Cslib.Complexity.STCON.compl_mem_NL`) by the
+proved for these native classes by Erik Demaine's inductive-counting construction. Consequently
+form in which the hardness of 2SAT is usually derived. Finally `STCON` is in `L` exactly when
+  every problem in `NL` reduces to `STCON` in logarithmic space.
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, Example 8.19, Corollary 8.24,
+* [N. Immerman, *Nondeterministic Space Is Closed under Complementation*][Immerman1988]

+  refine ⟨fun a => configurationInstance ntm c (enc a),

+its complement in `NL`, which reduces to `STCON`. This combines Theorem 8.25 of Sipser with

+# The Computational and Decisional Diffie–Hellman assumptions
+([BonehShoup2023], Attack Game 10.5) draws a group description `d` from a setup law and two
+independent uniform exponents `α, β : ZMod (F.order d)`, gives the adversary `(d, encode (α • g),
+encode (β • g))`, and accepts when the adversary outputs `encode ((α * β) • g)`.
+The Decisional Diffie–Hellman (DDH) experiment ([BonehShoup2023], Attack Game 10.6) compares the
+real tuple `(d, encode (α • g), encode (β • g), encode ((α * β) • g))` against the ideal tuple
+`(d, encode (α • g), encode (β • g), encode (γ • g))` with an independent uniform `γ`.
+We prove the implications `DDH ⇒ CDH ⇒ DiscreteLog` between the assumptions, and the
+distributional rerandomisation lemma underlying the random self-reducibility of DDH
+rerandomising maps any fixed real DDH tuple to the uniform real DDH distribution and any fixed
+non-DDH tuple to the uniform ideal DDH distribution. The rerandomisation acts on group elements with
+exact uniform exponents; the efficient worst-case-to-average-case algorithm (Exercise 10.10) is not
+formalized. The Diffie–Hellman assumptions are hypotheses, not theorems.
+  the Computational Diffie–Hellman experiment and assumption.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.dlToCDHAdversary`: the reduction from discrete logarithm to
+  the real and ideal Decisional Diffie–Hellman experiments and assumption.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.cdhToDDHDistinguisher`: the reduction from CDH to DDH.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+/-- The Computational Diffie–Hellman experiment ([BonehShoup2023], Attack Game 10.5): draw a
+description `d` and independent uniform `α, β : ZMod (F.order d)`, give the adversary the
+description and the encodings of `α • g` and `β • g`, and accept when it outputs the encoding of
+    (adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)) (n : ℕ) : Game := do
+    (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d), F.encode d (β • F.generator d)))
+  return decide (guess = F.encode d ((α * β) • F.generator d))
+/-- The Computational Diffie–Hellman assumption for a family and a setup law: every uniform strict
+PPT adversary computes `encode ((α * β) • g)` from `(d, encode (α • g), encode (β • g))` with
+  ∀ adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool),
+    IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encBits encBits))) encBits
+    Negligible fun n => Game.succProbability (F.cdhGame setup adversary n)
+/-- Turn a discrete-logarithm adversary into a CDH adversary by running it on `(d, encode (α • g))`
+to obtain a candidate exponent `a` and multiplying `encode (β • g)` by `a`. -/
+def dlToCDHAdversary (adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+    (n : ℕ) (input : F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool) : ProbComp (List Bool) := do
+/-- Whenever the discrete-logarithm adversary recovers `α`, `dlToCDHAdversary` outputs the valid
+    (adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)) (n : ℕ) :
+  simp only [discreteLogGame, cdhGame, dlToCDHAdversary, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure,
+  refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun d => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ zero_le
+  refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun α => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ zero_le
+  refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun β => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ zero_le
+  refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun guess => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ zero_le
+  by_cases hα : (ofBits guess : ZMod (F.order d)) = α
+  · simp only [hα, F.smul_encode, smul_smul, decide_true, le_rfl]
+  · simp only [hα, decide_false, PMF.pure_apply, Bool.true_eq_false, ↓reduceIte, zero_le]
+/-- The discrete-logarithm-to-CDH reduction is uniform strict PPT when the discrete-logarithm
+    {adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)}
+    IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encBits encBits))) encBits
+      (fun input => F.dlToCDHAdversary adversary input.1 input.2) := by
+    (prepare := fun input : ℕ × F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool =>
+theorem CDH.discreteLog {F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily} {setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc} (h : F.CDH setup) :
+/-- The real Decisional Diffie–Hellman experiment ([BonehShoup2023], Attack Game 10.6): draw `d`
+and independent uniform `α, β : ZMod (F.order d)`, and give the distinguisher
+`(d, encode (α • g), encode (β • g), encode ((α * β) • g))`. -/
+    (distinguisher : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp Bool)
+    (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d), F.encode d (β • F.generator d),
+/-- The ideal Decisional Diffie–Hellman experiment ([BonehShoup2023], Attack Game 10.6): draw `d`
+and independent uniform `α, β, γ : ZMod (F.order d)`, and give the distinguisher
+`(d, encode (α • g), encode (β • g), encode (γ • g))`. -/
+    (distinguisher : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp Bool)
+    (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d), F.encode d (β • F.generator d),
+/-- The Decisional Diffie–Hellman assumption for a family and a setup law: every uniform strict PPT
+      IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))))
+/-- Turn a CDH adversary into a DDH distinguisher by testing whether its candidate shared element
+    (adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+    (n : ℕ) (input : F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) : ProbComp Bool := do
+  let guess ← adversary n (input.1, input.2.1, input.2.2.1)
+/-- In the real DDH game, `cdhToDDHDistinguisher` simulates the CDH game exactly. -/
+    (adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)) (n : ℕ) :
+    F.ddhRealGame setup (F.cdhToDDHDistinguisher adversary) n = F.cdhGame setup adversary n := by
+  simp only [ddhRealGame, cdhToDDHDistinguisher, cdhGame, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure,
+/-- A fixed candidate word matches a uniformly chosen encoded group element with probability at
+      (fun γ => PMF.pure (decide (guess = F.encode d (γ • F.generator d))))) true ≤
+  simp only [PMF.uniformOfFintype_apply, ZMod.card, PMF.pure_apply, eq_comm (a := true),
+        (fun γ : ZMod (F.order d) => guess = F.encode d (γ • F.generator d))).card ≤ 1 := by
+    refine Finset.card_le_one_iff.mpr fun {γ₁ γ₂} h₁ h₂ => ?_
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at h₁ h₂
+          (if guess = F.encode d (x • F.generator d) then 1 else 0)
+            guess = F.encode d (γ • F.generator d))).card : ℝ≥0∞) *
+/-- In the ideal DDH game, `cdhToDDHDistinguisher` succeeds with probability at most `1 / m`
+whenever every supported group order is at least `m`. -/
+    (adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)) (n m : ℕ)
+    (F.ddhIdealGame setup (F.cdhToDDHDistinguisher adversary) n) true ≤ (m : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := by
+  calc ∑' d, setup n d * ∑' α, PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d)) α *
+              (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d), F.encode d (β • F.generator d)))).bind
+                PMF.pure (decide (guess = F.encode d (γ • F.generator d)))) true
+      ≤ ∑' d, setup n d * (m : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := by
+                        F.encode d (β • F.generator d)))).bind fun guess =>
+                      PMF.pure (decide (guess = F.encode d (γ • F.generator d)))) true
+                  ∑' β, PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d)) β * (m : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := by
+                refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun α => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ zero_le
+                refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun β => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ zero_le
+                        (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d), F.encode d (β • F.generator d))) guess *
+                        PMF.pure (decide (guess = F.encode d (γ • F.generator d)))) true
+                        (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d), F.encode d (β • F.generator d))) guess *
+        · have hd0 : setup n d = 0 := by rwa [PMF.mem_support_iff, not_not] at hd
+/-- **Quantitative reduction from CDH to DDH**: when every supported group at parameter `n` has
+order at least `m > 0`, any CDH adversary's success probability is at most the DDH distinguishing
+    (adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)) (n m : ℕ)
+    (hm0 : 0 < m) (hm : ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, m ≤ F.order d) :
+/-- The CDH-to-DDH reduction is uniform strict PPT when the CDH adversary is. -/
+    {adversary : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)}
+    (hA : IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encBits encBits))) encBits
+    IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))))
+      encBool (fun input => F.cdhToDDHDistinguisher adversary input.1 input.2) := by
+    (prepare := fun input : ℕ × F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool =>
+      (fun p : (ℕ × F.Desc × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) × List Bool =>
+/-- **DDH implies CDH** when every supported group at parameter `n` has order at least `m n > 0`
+theorem DDH.cdh {F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily} {setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc} (hDDH : F.DDH setup)
+    {m : ℕ → ℕ} (hm0 : ∀ n, 0 < m n) (hm : ∀ n, ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, m n ≤ F.order d)
+    (hinv : Negligible fun n => (1 / m n : ℝ≥0)) : F.CDH setup := by
+    fun n => F.succProbability_cdhGame_le_advantage_ddh_add setup adversary n (m n) (hm0 n) (hm n)
+/-- **DDH implies the discrete-logarithm assumption** when every supported group at parameter `n`
+has order at least `m n > 0` and `1 / m n` is negligible. -/
+theorem DDH.discreteLog {F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily} {setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc} (hDDH : F.DDH setup)
+    {m : ℕ → ℕ} (hm0 : ∀ n, 0 < m n) (hm : ∀ n, ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, m n ≤ F.order d)
+    (hinv : Negligible fun n => (1 / m n : ℝ≥0)) : F.DiscreteLog setup :=
+/-- Re-randomize a candidate DDH triple `(u, v, w)` in `F.Carrier d` using exponents
+def ddhRerandomize (d : F.Desc) (u v w : F.Carrier d)
+    (r s₁ s₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d :=
+    r • w + (r * s₂) • u + s₁ • v + (s₁ * s₂) • F.generator d)
+/-- Algebraic action of `ddhRerandomize` on multiples of the generator: a tuple error
+`γ - α * β` is scaled by `r` and added to the new Diffie–Hellman product
+theorem ddhRerandomize_smul_generator (d : F.Desc) (α β γ r s₁ s₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+    F.ddhRerandomize d (α • F.generator d) (β • F.generator d) (γ • F.generator d) r s₁ s₂ =
+        ((r * α + s₁) * (β + s₂) + r * (γ - α * β)) • F.generator d) := by
+  refine Prod.ext rfl (Prod.ext rfl (congrArg (· • F.generator d) (by ring)))
+/-- The re-randomized triple distribution obtained by drawing `r, s₁, s₂ : ZMod (F.order d)`
+noncomputable def ddhRerandomizeLaw (d : F.Desc) (u v w : F.Carrier d) :
+    PMF (F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) := do
+  return F.ddhRerandomize d u v w r s₁ s₂
+/-- The real DDH tuple distribution on `F.Carrier d`. -/
+    PMF (F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) := do
+  return (α • F.generator d, β • F.generator d, (α * β) • F.generator d)
+/-- The ideal DDH tuple distribution on `F.Carrier d`. -/
+    PMF (F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) := do
+  return (α • F.generator d, β • F.generator d, γ • F.generator d)
+private theorem uniformOfFintype_bind_equiv {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α]
+    (PMF.uniformOfFintype α).bind (fun a => f (e a)) = (PMF.uniformOfFintype α).bind f := by
+/-- **Random self-reducibility of DDH (real case)**: re-randomizing any fixed real DDH tuple
+`(α • g, β • g, (α * β) • g)` yields the exact uniform real DDH tuple distribution. -/
+    F.ddhRerandomizeLaw d (α • F.generator d) (β • F.generator d) ((α * β) • F.generator d) =
+  simp only [ddhRerandomizeLaw, ddhRealTupleLaw, ddhRerandomize_smul_generator, sub_self, mul_zero,
+        PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, (β + s₂) • F.generator d,
+        PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d, (α' * β') • F.generator d)) :=
+      (fun β' => PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d, (α' * β') • F.generator d))
+          PMF.pure ((r * α + s₁) • F.generator d, (β + s₂) • F.generator d,
+          PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d, (α' * β') • F.generator d)) := by
+        PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d, (α' * β') • F.generator d))
+/-- **Random self-reducibility of DDH (ideal case)**: re-randomizing any fixed non-DDH tuple
+`(α • g, β • g, γ • g)` with `γ ≠ α * β` yields the exact uniform ideal DDH tuple distribution. -/
+theorem ddhRerandomizeLaw_ideal (d : F.Desc) {α β γ : ZMod (F.order d)} (hγ : γ ≠ α * β) :
+    F.ddhRerandomizeLaw d (α • F.generator d) (β • F.generator d) (γ • F.generator d) =
+        PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, (β + s₂) • F.generator d,
+          (α' * (β + s₂) + r * (γ - α * β)) • F.generator d)) =
+        PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d,
+          (α' * β' + r * (γ - α * β)) • F.generator d)) :=
+      (fun β' => PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d,
+        (α' * β' + r * (γ - α * β)) • F.generator d))
+          PMF.pure ((r * α + s₁) • F.generator d, (β + s₂) • F.generator d,
+            ((r * α + s₁) * (β + s₂) + r * (γ - α * β)) • F.generator d)) =
+          PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d,
+            (α' * β' + r * (γ - α * β)) • F.generator d)) := by
+        PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d,
+          (α' * β' + r * (γ - α * β)) • F.generator d))
+    (fun γ' => PMF.pure (α' • F.generator d, β' • F.generator d, γ' • F.generator d))

+# ElGamal encryption and IND-CPA security under DDH
+uses a group description `d`, a secret exponent `α : ZMod (F.order d)`, and the public key
+To encrypt a group element `m : F.Carrier d` with randomness `β : ZMod (F.order d)`, the sender
+forms the ciphertext `(v, e) = (β • g, β • u + m) = (β • g, (α * β) • g + m)`. Decryption recovers
+`e - α • v = m`, and encoded decryption (`decodeElGamal`) computes this in polynomial time from
+`(d, a, encode v, encode e)` using `F.order`, `F.smul`, and `F.add`.
+For bit encryption, `false` and `true` are embedded as the distinct group elements `0` and `g`
+(`bitElement`, encoded in polynomial time by `encodeBit`). In the chosen-plaintext experiment
+(`elGamalCPAGame`), an `Encryption.Adversary` receives the encoded public key `(d, encode (α • g))`,
+chooses two challenge bits with a saved state word, and receives an ElGamal encryption of the
+selected challenge bit. Replacing the Diffie–Hellman mask `(α * β) • g` with an independent uniform
+`γ • g` masks the message perfectly (`uniform_smul_generator_add`), reducing IND-CPA security of
+ElGamal encryption directly to the Decisional Diffie–Hellman assumption (`DDH.elGamalINDCPA`,
+Security is proved for one-bit messages `{0, g}` through the library's bit-message
+`Encryption.Adversary`, not for adversarially chosen group-element messages. The experiment is a
+hand-written game whose key generation and encryption sample exact uniform exponents in
+`ZMod (F.order d)`; only decryption (`decodeElGamal`) is certified polynomial time, and the scheme
+is not an instance of `Encryption.INDCPA` with efficient honest algorithms. The Diffie–Hellman
+  embedding and polynomial-time encoding of message bits as group elements.
+  `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.elGamalINDCPA`: the IND-CPA experiment and security property
+  `γ • g + m` is uniformly distributed over `F.Carrier d`.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+/-- Algebraic ElGamal encryption of a group element `m : F.Carrier d` under public key
+`u : F.Carrier d` with randomness `β : ZMod (F.order d)`. -/
+def elGamalEncrypt (d : F.Desc) (u m : F.Carrier d) (β : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+/-- Under a genuine public key `u = α • g`, the second ciphertext component is
+theorem elGamalEncrypt_smul_generator (d : F.Desc) (α β : ZMod (F.order d)) (m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.elGamalEncrypt d (α • F.generator d) m β =
+      (β • F.generator d, (α * β) • F.generator d + m) := by
+  simp only [elGamalEncrypt, smul_smul, mul_comm β α]
+/-- Algebraic ElGamal decryption of a ciphertext pair `(v, e)` using secret key
+def elGamalDecrypt (d : F.Desc) (α : ZMod (F.order d)) (ct : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) :
+/-- **ElGamal decryption correctness**: decrypting an encryption under `u = α • g` with secret key
+@[simp] theorem elGamalDecrypt_elGamalEncrypt (d : F.Desc) (α β : ZMod (F.order d))
+    F.elGamalDecrypt d α (F.elGamalEncrypt d (α • F.generator d) m β) = m := by
+  simp only [elGamalDecrypt, elGamalEncrypt, smul_smul, mul_comm β α, add_sub_cancel_left]
+/-- Decryption on encoded group elements: given `(d, a, encode v, encode e)`, compute
+`encode (e - a • v)` as `F.add (d, encode e, F.smul (d, F.order d - a % F.order d, encode v))`. -/
+def decodeElGamal (input : F.Desc × ℕ × List Bool × List Bool) : List Bool :=
+    F.smul (input.1, F.order input.1 - input.2.1 % F.order input.1, input.2.2.1))
+/-- `decodeElGamal` computes `encode (elGamalDecrypt d a (v, e))` on encoded group elements. -/
+theorem decodeElGamal_encode (d : F.Desc) (a : ℕ) (v e : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.decodeElGamal (d, a, F.encode d v, F.encode d e) =
+      F.encode d (F.elGamalDecrypt d (a : ZMod (F.order d)) (v, e)) := by
+  have hneg : ((F.order d - a % F.order d : ℕ) : ZMod (F.order d)) = -(a : ZMod (F.order d)) := by
+  simp only [decodeElGamal, F.smul_encode, hneg, neg_smul, F.add_encode, elGamalDecrypt,
+/-- Encoded ElGamal decryption of an honest encryption recovers the encoded message. -/
+@[simp] theorem decodeElGamal_elGamalEncrypt (d : F.Desc) (a : ℕ) (β : ZMod (F.order d))
+      F.encode d (F.elGamalEncrypt d ((a : ZMod (F.order d)) • F.generator d) m β).1,
+      F.encode d (F.elGamalEncrypt d ((a : ZMod (F.order d)) • F.generator d) m β).2) =
+/-- Encoded ElGamal decryption is computable in polynomial time. -/
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encNat (encPair encBits encBits))) encBits := by
+      (fun input : F.Desc × ℕ × List Bool × List Bool => input.1)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encNat (encPair encBits encBits))) F.encDesc := by fun_prop
+      (fun input : F.Desc × ℕ × List Bool × List Bool => input.2.1)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encNat (encPair encBits encBits))) encNat := by fun_prop
+      (fun input : F.Desc × ℕ × List Bool × List Bool => input.2.2.1)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encNat (encPair encBits encBits))) encBits := by fun_prop
+      (fun input : F.Desc × ℕ × List Bool × List Bool => input.2.2.2)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encNat (encPair encBits encBits))) encBits := by fun_prop
+      (fun input : F.Desc × ℕ × List Bool × List Bool => F.order input.1)
+      (fun input : F.Desc × ℕ × List Bool × List Bool =>
+/-! ### Surjectivity of the generator map and the one-time group mask -/
+/-- Every element of `F.Carrier d` is a scalar multiple of the generator: `α ↦ α • g` is
+    Function.Surjective fun α : ZMod (F.order d) => α • F.generator d := by
+/-- **One-time group mask**: for any group element `m : F.Carrier d`, masking `m` by `γ • g` for a
+uniform `γ : ZMod (F.order d)` has the same distribution as `γ • g` itself. -/
+    ((PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun γ => f (γ • F.generator d + m)) =
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun γ => f (γ • F.generator d) := by
+      ((fun γ => f (γ • F.generator d)) ∘ Equiv.addRight μ) =
+/-! ### Bit encryption and IND-CPA security under DDH -/
+/-- Embed a message bit `b : Bool` into `F.Carrier d` as `0` (for `false`) or `g` (for `true`). -/
+  if b then F.generator d else 0
+/-- Distinct message bits map to distinct group elements. -/
+/-- Encode a message bit `b : Bool` as an encoded element of `F.Carrier d` using `F.smul`. -/
+  F.smul (d, if b then 1 else 0, F.encode d (F.generator d))
+    F.encodeBit d b = F.encode d (F.bitElement d b) := by
+/-- `encodeBit` is computable in polynomial time from the group description and the bit. -/
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : F.Desc × Bool => F.encodeBit p.1 p.2)

+   $[n] \times [n]$. It is a yes-instance (`G ∈ BipartitePermutationIndependentSet`) when there
+   exist two permutations $\pi_1, \pi_2 \in S_n$ (`Equiv.Perm (Fin G.1)`) such that for no edge
+   $((u_1, u_2), (v_1, v_2)) \in G.2$ do we simultaneously have $\pi_1(u_1) = u_2$ and
+   $\pi \in S_{2n}$ (`Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * G.1))`) preserves the two blocks $[0, n)$ and

title: feat(crypto): certify the uniform serialized Lyubashevsky extractor (#745)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The extractor needs only runtime dimensions `m,k`, two bit challenges and two optional integer
+responses. It computes the response difference followed by the signed reversed challenge
+difference. Dimensions are unary resources; integer magnitudes are binary. Every input word has
+a total interpretation: missing vector entries are zero, missing challenge bits are false, and
+surplus coordinates are ignored. The optional-vector default is the zero vector.
+The same word program handles all dimensions; no parameter-family claim is inferred from a
+certificate for one fixed finite vector type. This is a deterministic operation certificate,
+not a rewinding, knowledge-soundness or cryptographic security theorem.
+  arithmetic, framing and output costs in one uniform plain certificate.
+  the typed protocol extractor for all dimensions, statements and commitments.
+/-- Dimensions followed by two challenge/optional-response pairs. -/
+  (ℕ × ℕ) × ((List Bool × Option (List ℤ)) × (List Bool × Option (List ℤ)))
+/-- Unary dimensions, raw challenges and framed optional lists of binary signed integers. -/
+/-- Parse every input word with the existing framing conventions; malformed fields have total
+  let response (w : List Bool) : Option (List ℤ) :=
+    if w.isEmpty then none else some ((frames w.tail).map decodeIntBin)
+  let row (w : List Bool) := (unframe w, response (dropFrame w))
+    ∃ D : Decoder encLyubashevskyExtractInput, D.decode = decodeLyubashevskyExtractInput := by
+  let decoder := Decoder.pair (Decoder.pair Decoder.unary Decoder.unary) (Decoder.pair row row)
+/-- Parsing inverts the complete canonical input encoding. -/
+/-- The total input parser has a plain polynomial-time certificate, including malformed words. -/
+/-- Compute `z-z′` first, then the SIGNED challenge difference `c′-c`. The unary dimensions
+control both output segments; optional responses default to zero coordinatewise. -/
+    (if input.2.2.1.getD i false then (1 : ℤ) else 0) -
+      (if input.2.1.1.getD i false then (1 : ℤ) else 0))
+/-- Extraction always writes the two declared segments, even on malformed-length inputs. -/
+/-- One native extractor handles runtime dimensions and all binary integer magnitudes. -/
+private theorem getD_optional_ofFn {m : ℕ} (z : Option (Fin m → ℤ)) (i : Fin m) :
+private theorem map_range_eq_ofFn {α : Type} (n : ℕ) (f : ℕ → α) (g : Fin n → α)
+    (h : ∀ i : Fin n, f i.val = g i) : (List.range n).map f = List.ofFn g := by
+  exact List.map_congr_left fun i _ => h i
+/-- Canonical typed vectors give exactly the ordered response difference and signed reversed
+challenge difference. This formula is independent of statement matrices and the modulus. -/
+theorem lyubashevskyExtractList_ofFn {m k : ℕ} (c : Fin k → Bool) (z : Option (Fin m → ℤ))
+    (c' : Fin k → Bool) (z' : Option (Fin m → ℤ)) :
+      ((List.ofFn c, z.map List.ofFn), (List.ofFn c', z'.map List.ofFn))) =
+        (fun i => (if c' i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) - (if c i then (1 : ℤ) else 0))) := by
+/-- The complete serialized program: parse, extract, and frame every signed output coordinate. -/
+/-- The complete extractor is one plain polynomial-time word function, not a separate machine
+/-- The word program exactly implements the integer-list extractor on canonical encoded data. -/
+/-- Canonical vectors realize the actual typed extractor for every statement and commitment.
+The ignored statement dimensions and modulus do not need to be supplied to the word program. -/
+    (y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) (ZMod q) × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) (ZMod q))
+    (w : Fin n → ZMod q) (c : BitString k) (z : Option (Fin m → ℤ))
+      ((List.ofFn c, z.map List.ofFn), (List.ofFn c', z'.map List.ofFn))) =
+        lyubashevskyExtract n m k q y w c z c' z' (finSumFinEquiv.symm i)) := by
+  cases i using Fin.addCases <;> simp [lyubashevskyExtract, lyubashevskyChallenge]
+/-- The complete word program agrees exactly with the named typed extractor, including absent
+responses and zero dimensions, without assuming acceptance of either conversation. -/
+    (y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) (ZMod q) × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) (ZMod q))
+    (w : Fin n → ZMod q) (c : BitString k) (z : Option (Fin m → ℤ))
+      ((List.ofFn c, z.map List.ofFn), (List.ofFn c', z'.map List.ofFn)))) =
+        lyubashevskyExtract n m k q y w c z c' z' (finSumFinEquiv.symm i))) := by
+  rw [lyubashevskyExtractWord_enc, lyubashevskyExtractList_eq_extract n m k q y w]

+    (∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly) ↔

+/-- **The Karp–Lipton theorem, `NP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ PH = Σ₂`** (from the language-level `NP`

+# Removing the stack-machine bridge's word recoding

+The list interface parses the frames; only the two Boolean symbols need a finite conversion.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.bits_encList_polyTime`: raw and framed binary words are equivalent.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.trans_encList_polyTime`: the equivalence after any binary embedding.

+    word.foldl (fun acc bit => acc ++ [bit]) acc = acc ++ word := by

+/-- Framing a fixed Boolean encoding, or parsing its frames and converting each symbol, takes
+polynomial time. The encodings of `false` and `true` can be arbitrary fixed words. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Polynomial degree bounds in an arbitrary size measure
+These bounds and their arithmetic are independent of machine computability.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.DegreeBounded`: a bound by a constant times `(size + 1) ^ d`.
+/-- `u` is bounded by a polynomial of degree `d` in `size`. -/
+@[expose] public def DegreeBounded {α : Type*} (size u : α → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ c, ∀ a, u a ≤ c * (size a + 1) ^ d
+variable {α β : Type*} {size : α → ℕ} {u v : α → ℕ} {d d₁ d₂ : ℕ}
+public theorem mono (h : DegreeBounded size v d) (huv : ∀ a, u a ≤ v a) :
+public theorem mono_deg (h : DegreeBounded size u d₁) (hd : d₁ ≤ d₂) : DegreeBounded size u d₂ :=
+public theorem const (k : ℕ) : DegreeBounded size (fun _ => k) d :=
+public theorem add (hu : DegreeBounded size u d) (hv : DegreeBounded size v d) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => u a + v a) d :=
+/-- Adding bounds of different degrees gives a bound of their maximum degree. -/
+public theorem add_max (hu : DegreeBounded size u d₁) (hv : DegreeBounded size v d₂) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => u a + v a) (max d₁ d₂) :=
+public theorem smul (k : ℕ) (hu : DegreeBounded size u d) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => k * u a) d :=
+public theorem add_const (k : ℕ) (hu : DegreeBounded size u d) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => u a + k) d :=
+public theorem mul (hu : DegreeBounded size u d₁) (hv : DegreeBounded size v d₂) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => u a * v a) (d₁ + d₂) :=
+  ⟨c₁ * c₂, fun a => (Nat.mul_le_mul (h₁ a) (h₂ a)).trans_eq (by rw [Nat.pow_add]; ring)⟩
+/-- Substitution: if `v` has degree `d₂` in `size'` and `size' ∘ g` has degree `d₁` in `size`,
+public theorem comp {size' : β → ℕ} {v : β → ℕ} {g : α → β} (hv : DegreeBounded size' v d₂)
+    (hg : DegreeBounded size (fun a => size' (g a)) d₁) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => v (g a)) (d₁ * d₂) :=

title: feat(complexity): prove NP ∩ coNP and UP ∩ coUP oracle lowness and Low₁ = NP ∩ coNP (#719) (#721)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Oracle lowness of `NP ∩ coNP` and `UP ∩ coUP`
+An oracle language `A ∈ NP ∩ coNP` adds nothing to nondeterministic polynomial time:
+`NP^A = NP` and `P^A ⊆ NP ∩ coNP`, and conversely any language `A` with `NP^A = NP` lies in
+`NP ∩ coNP` [Schöning][Schoening1989] [Arora and Barak, Chapter 3][AroraBarak09]. When `A` is in
+`UP ∩ coUP`, every `P^A` predicate has at most one accepting replay certificate, giving
+The proof combines deterministic instruction-indexed oracle replay
+`Turing.MultiTapePTM.oracleReplies`) with uniform `#P` products and Boolean sums
+1. Given `#P` functions `fYes` and `fNo` whose supports are `A` and `Aᶜ`, each replayed step `i`
+   contributes `fYes q_i` when step `i` submits query `q_i` and the guessed reply bit is `true`,
+   `fNo q_i` when step `i` submits `q_i` and the guessed reply bit is `false`, and `1` (for bit
+   `false`) or `0` (for bit `true`) at local and halted instructions.
+2. Multiplying these step factors over `i < |answers|` produces a `#P` path count that is positive
+   if and only if `answers` equals the canonical transcript `machine.oracleReplies`. When `fYes`
+   and `fNo` are bounded by `1` (`A ∈ UP ∩ coUP`), the path count is `1` on the canonical
+   transcript and `0` on every other transcript.
+3. Summing over all transcript words of the polynomial clock length therefore certifies any
+   polynomial-time predicate of `(a, output (f a))` in `NP` (or `UP`). Applying this to the output
+   bits of a `P^A` decider yields `P^A ⊆ NP ∩ coNP` (and `P^A ⊆ UP ∩ coUP`), and applying it to an
+   `NP^A` verifier on `encPair enc encBits` yields `NP^A = NP`.
+  functions lie in `NP` (for `A ∈ NP ∩ coNP`) and `UP` (for `A ∈ UP ∩ coUP`).
+  `NP^A = NP` if and only if `A ∈ NP ∩ coNP`, and `NP = coNP` if and only if `NP^NP = NP`.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]

+/-- **`P` relative to an oracle is closed under complement**: negate the Boolean decider. -/

+  refine ⟨fun a => !f a, hf.map (by fun_prop), fun a => ?_⟩
+/-- **`P` relative to an oracle is closed under intersection.** -/
+theorem inter_mem_PWithOracle {L₁ L₂ : Set α} (h₁ : L₁ ∈ PWithOracle A enc)
+    (h₂ : L₂ ∈ PWithOracle A enc) : L₁ ∩ L₂ ∈ PWithOracle A enc := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => f₁ a && f₂ a, (hf₁.prod hf₂).map (g := fun p => p.1 && p.2) (by fun_prop),
+  rw [Set.mem_inter_iff, hL₁ a, hL₂ a, Bool.and_eq_true]
+/-- **`P` relative to an oracle is closed under union.** -/

+    (h₂ : L₂ ∈ PWithOracle A enc) : L₁ ∪ L₂ ∈ PWithOracle A enc := by

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.

+# Interpolation bounds the number of points
+If a space of functions `α → K` interpolates every function on a finite set `G`, restricting to
+`G` maps it onto `G → K`, so its dimension is at least `|G|`. For the span of finitely many
+(`Cslib.LinearAlgebra.card_le_of_forall_exists_mem_span_eq`). This is the dimension count of the
+polynomial method: if every function agrees on `G` with a combination of few functions, `G` is
+* `Cslib.LinearAlgebra.card_le_of_forall_exists_mem_span_eq`: if every function agrees on `G` with
+  a combination of the functions `v a` for `a ∈ s`, then `#G ≤ #s`.
+/-- If every function agrees on `G` with a combination of the functions `v a` for `a ∈ s`, then `G`
+has at most `#s` points: restricting the span to `G` is onto `G → K`. -/
+    (G : Finset α) (s : Finset ι) (v : ι → α → K)
+    (h : ∀ f : α → K, ∃ g ∈ Submodule.span K (v '' s), ∀ x ∈ G, g x = f x) : #G ≤ #s := by
+  let restrict := (LinearMap.funLeft K K ((↑) : G → α)).comp
+  have hsurj : Function.Surjective restrict := fun g => by
+    obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := h fun x => if hx : x ∈ G then g ⟨x, hx⟩ else 0
+    exact ⟨⟨p, hp⟩, funext fun x => (by simpa using hpx x.1 x.2 : p x.1 = g x)⟩

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+If the Boolean hierarchy over `NP` collapses at any finite level `k` (`coBH k ⊆ BH k`, or
+equivalently `BH (k + 1) = BH k`), then the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its third level
+`Σ₃ᴾ ∩ Π₃ᴾ` (`PH = Σ₃ᴾ`) [Kadin][Kadin1988]. In particular, if `DP = coDP` (or `SATUNSAT ∈ coDP`),
+To place a language `A ∈ Π₃ᴾ` in `Σ₃ᴾ`, peel off its first two quantifier blocks of lengths `p₁`
+and `p₂`; the negated inner quantifier defines a language `E ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)` such that
+`a ∈ A ↔ ∀ u₁ (|u₁| = p₁(n)), ∃ u₂ (|u₂| = p₂(n)), (a, u₁ ++ u₂) ∉ E`, where every queried word
+For each `r ≤ k`, an `r`-tuple of words of length `m(n)` is represented as a single concatenated
+bit string `s` of length `r * m(n)` paired with `a` under `encPair enc encBits`. The canonical
+alternating languages `kadinChain enc m E r ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) r` satisfy
+`(a, s ++ y) ∈ kadinChain enc m E (r + 1) ↔ (a, y) ∈ E ∧ (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r` whenever
+`|s| = r * m(n)`. Assuming `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k`, the
+complement `(kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ` lies in `BH (encPair enc encBits) k`. Stepping down the nested
+difference representation of `(kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ` from `r = k` to `r = 0` yields at each level
+either a hard prefix `s` of length `r * m(n)` that reduces `(a, y) ∉ E` on words of length `m(n)`
+to an existential check over `NP`, or completeness for the next level down. Taking the union of
+* `Cslib.Complexity.kadinChain`: the canonical `BH r` language on concatenated `r`-tuples of fixed
+* `Cslib.Complexity.allWordsIn`: the `NP` language checking that `d` concatenated words of fixed
+  polynomial length all belong to a given language.
+  polynomial-time many-one reduces to a language in `BH encBits r`.
+  bit-string encoding `encBits` transfers to every instance encoding `enc`.
+  `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k → PiP 3 enc ⊆ SigmaP 3 enc`.
+  `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k → SigmaP 3 enc = PiP 3 enc`.
+* [J. Kadin, *The Polynomial Time Hierarchy Collapses if the Boolean Hierarchy
+* [J.-Y. Cai et al., *The Boolean Hierarchy I: Structural Properties*][CaiEtAl1988]
+/-! ### Alternating verifiers on fixed-length bit-string slices -/
+/-- The encoded length of `(a, s)` under `encPair enc encBits` when `s` has length `q |enc a|`. -/
+private noncomputable def pairPoly (q : Polynomial ℕ) : Polynomial ℕ := 2 * X + 1 + q
+private theorem length_encPair_eq_eval_pairPoly {q : Polynomial ℕ} {a : α} {s : List Bool}
+    (encPair enc encBits (a, s)).length = (pairPoly q).eval (enc a).length := by
+/-- Shift the first `p |enc a|` certificate bits from the quantifier stream onto the accumulated
+private def shiftVerifier (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool) (x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool) : Bool :=
+private theorem shiftVerifier_append {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool}
+    {a : α} {s u v : List Bool} (hu : u.length = p.eval (enc a).length) :
+    shiftVerifier enc p V ((a, s), u ++ v) = V ((a, s ++ u), v) := by
+    (hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encBool) :
+      (fun x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool => p.eval (enc x.1.1).length)
+    {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} (ps : List (Polynomial ℕ × Polynomial ℕ)) {N : γ → ℕ}
+    (hN : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime N encIn encUnary) {W : γ → List Bool}
+      (fun x => splitAlternatingBlocks (ps.map fun pq => (pq.1.eval (N x), pq.2.eval (N x)))
+/-- `R : α → List Bool → Prop` is verified at `(b, k)` on prefixes `s` of length `q |enc a|` by a
+polynomial-time alternating verifier whose certificate block lengths are polynomials in
+private def OnSliceAlt (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (b : Bool) (k : ℕ) (q : Polynomial ℕ)
+  ∃ (ps : List (Polynomial ℕ)) (V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool),
+    ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encBool ∧
+    ∀ a : α, ∀ s : List Bool, s.length = q.eval (enc a).length →
+      (R a s ↔ Alternation b (ps.map fun p => p.eval (enc a).length) fun v => V ((a, s), v) = true)
+variable {b : Bool} {k : ℕ} {p q : Polynomial ℕ} {R R₁ R₂ : α → List Bool → Prop}
+private theorem congr (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₁)
+    (hR : ∀ a s, s.length = q.eval (enc a).length → (R₁ a s ↔ R₂ a s)) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂ := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, fun a s hs => (hR a s hs).symm.trans (hA a s hs)⟩
+private theorem congr_poly (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) {q' : Polynomial ℕ}
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q' R := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, fun a s hs => hA a s (hs.trans (hq _).symm)⟩
+/-- At slice length `0`, an existential `OnSliceAlt` relation defines a `SigmaP k` language on
+private theorem mem_SigmaP (h : OnSliceAlt enc true k 0 R) : {a | R a []} ∈ SigmaP k enc := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine mem_SigmaP_iff_tidy.mpr ⟨ps, fun x => V ((x.1, []), x.2), hk, ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+  · exact hV.tidy.comp (((fst enc encBits).prod (.const [])).prod (snd enc encBits))
+/-- Negating the verifier swaps quantifier polarities. -/
+private theorem not (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) : OnSliceAlt enc (!b) k q (fun a s => ¬R a s) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨ps, fun x => !V x, hk, by fun_prop, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  exact alternation_congr fun v => by simp
+/-- Prepending a length-zero block flips the leading quantifier polarity and increments the
+private theorem zero_cons (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) : OnSliceAlt enc (!b) (k + 1) q R := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨0 :: ps, V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  rw [hR a s hs, List.map_cons, Polynomial.eval_zero, alternation_zero_cons, Bool.not_not]
+/-- Appending a length-zero block increments the level without changing the leading polarity. -/
+private theorem append_zero (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) : OnSliceAlt enc b (k + 1) q R := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨ps ++ [0], V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  rw [hR a s hs, List.map_append, List.map_singleton, Polynomial.eval_zero, alternation_append_zero]
+/-- Conjoining two `OnSliceAlt` relations at the same polarity and level. -/
+private theorem and (h₁ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₁) (h₂ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => R₁ a s ∧ R₂ a s) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hp, hV, hR₁⟩ := h₁
+  obtain ⟨qs, W, hq, hW, hR₂⟩ := h₂
+  have hlen : ps.length = qs.length := hp.trans hq.symm
+        (pqs.map fun pq => (pq.1.eval (enc x.1.1).length, pq.2.eval (enc x.1.1).length)) x.2
+    by simp [pqs, hp, hq], ?_, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+        (fun x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool => (enc x.1.1).length)
+    rw [hR₁ a s hs, hR₂ a s hs]
+    have hfst : pqs.map Prod.fst = ps := List.map_fst_zip hlen.le
+    have hsnd : pqs.map Prod.snd = qs := List.map_snd_zip hlen.ge
+      (pqs.map fun pq => (pq.1.eval (enc a).length, pq.2.eval (enc a).length)) b
+      (fun v => V ((a, s), v) = true) (fun v => W ((a, s), v) = true)).symm
+/-- Disjoining two `OnSliceAlt` relations at the same polarity and level. -/
+private theorem or (h₁ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₁) (h₂ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => R₁ a s ∨ R₂ a s) := by
+  have h : OnSliceAlt enc (!!b) k q (fun a s => ¬(¬R₁ a s ∧ ¬R₂ a s)) := (h₁.not.and h₂.not).not
+  exact h.congr fun a s _ => by tauto
+/-- Implication from a negated `OnSliceAlt` relation to a positive one at the same polarity. -/
+private theorem imp (h₁ : OnSliceAlt enc (!b) k q R₁) (h₂ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => R₁ a s → R₂ a s) := by
+  have h₁' : OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => ¬R₁ a s) := by
+/-- Embed a `SigmaP k (encPair enc encBits)` language at any slice polynomial `q`. -/
+private theorem of_mem_SigmaP {C : Set (α × List Bool)} (hC : C ∈ SigmaP k (encPair enc encBits))
+    OnSliceAlt enc true k q (fun a s => (a, s) ∈ C) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := hC
+  refine ⟨ps.map fun p => p.comp (pairPoly q), V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+/-- Embed a `PiP k (encPair enc encBits)` language at any slice polynomial `q`. -/
+private theorem of_mem_PiP {C : Set (α × List Bool)} (hC : C ∈ PiP k (encPair enc encBits))
+    OnSliceAlt enc false k q (fun a s => (a, s) ∈ C) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := hC
+  refine ⟨ps.map fun p => p.comp (pairPoly q), V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+/-- Drop the first `p |enc a|` bits of the slice prefix before evaluating `R`. -/
+private theorem drop (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k (p + q) (fun a s => R a (s.drop (p.eval (enc a).length))) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨ps, fun x => V ((x.1.1, x.1.2.drop (p.eval (enc x.1.1).length)), x.2), hk, ?_,
+        (fun x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool => p.eval (enc x.1.1).length)
+/-- Prepend an existential quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` to a universal relation. -/
+private theorem exists_append_flip (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc false k (q + p) R) :
+      (fun a s => ∃ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ R a (s ++ u)) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p :: ps, shiftVerifier enc p V, by simp [hk],
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_shiftVerifier p hV.tidy), fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  refine exists_congr fun u => and_congr_right fun hu => ?_
+  have hsu : (s ++ u).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by
+  exact alternation_congr fun v => by rw [shiftVerifier_append hu]
+/-- Prepend a universal quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` to an existential relation. -/
+private theorem forall_append_flip (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc true k (q + p) R) :
+      (fun a s => ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length → R a (s ++ u)) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p :: ps, shiftVerifier enc p V, by simp [hk],
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_shiftVerifier p hV.tidy), fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  refine forall_congr' fun u => imp_congr_right fun hu => ?_
+  have hsu : (s ++ u).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by
+  exact alternation_congr fun v => by rw [shiftVerifier_append hu]
+/-- Merge an existential quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` into the leading existential
+private theorem exists_append_same (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc true (k + 1) (q + p) R) :
+      (fun a s => ∃ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ R a (s ++ u)) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨(p + p₁) :: ps, shiftVerifier enc p V, by simpa using hk,
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_shiftVerifier p hV.tidy), fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+    have hsu : (s ++ u).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by simp [hs, hu]
+    obtain ⟨w₁, hw₁, hA⟩ := (hR a (s ++ u) hsu).1 hRu
+    simpa only [List.append_assoc, shiftVerifier_append hu] using hv
+    have hu : (w.take n).length = n := by simp [n, hw]
+    have hw₁ : (w.drop n).length = p₁.eval (enc a).length := by simp [n, hw]
+    have hsu : (s ++ w.take n).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by simp [hs, hu, n]
+    refine ⟨w.take n, hu, (hR a (s ++ w.take n) hsu).2 ⟨w.drop n, hw₁, ?_⟩⟩

+/-- Merge a universal quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` into the leading universal
+private theorem forall_append_same (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc false (k + 1) (q + p) R) :
+      (fun a s => ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length → R a (s ++ u)) := by
+      (fun a s => ¬∃ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ ¬R a (s ++ u)) :=
+  exact hnot.congr fun a s _ => by simp
+/-! ### Kadin's alternating tuple chain and word-tuple predicates -/
+/-- The canonical `BH r` language on concatenated `r`-tuples of words of length `m |enc a|`:
+`(a, s ++ y)` belongs to `kadinChain enc m E (r + 1)` when `(a, y) ∈ E` and
+`(a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r`. -/
+def kadinChain (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+    {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} \
+      {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.take ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ kadinChain enc m E r}
+theorem kadinChain_zero (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+theorem mem_kadinChain_succ_append {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)} {r : ℕ}
+    {a : α} {s y : List Bool} (hs : s.length = (r • m).eval (enc a).length) :
+    (a, s ++ y) ∈ kadinChain enc m E (r + 1) ↔
+      (a, y) ∈ E ∧ (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r := by
+  have hs' : s.length = r * m.eval (enc a).length := by simpa using hs
+theorem kadinChain_mem_BH {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)}
+    kadinChain enc m E r ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) r := by
+        (fun x : α × List Bool => (r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)
+    have hdrop : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+        {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} E :=
+    have htake : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+          (x.1, x.2.take ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ kadinChain enc m E r}
+    exact ⟨_, hdrop.mem_NP hE, _, htake.mem_BH ih, rfl⟩
+/-- The `NP` language checking that each of the first `d` consecutive blocks of length `m |enc a|`
+def allWordsIn (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+    {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.take (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} ∩
+      {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d}
+theorem allWordsIn_zero (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+    allWordsIn enc m E 0 = Set.univ := rfl
+theorem mem_allWordsIn_succ_append {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)} {d : ℕ}
+    {a : α} {y z : List Bool} (hy : y.length = m.eval (enc a).length) :
+    (a, y ++ z) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E (d + 1) ↔
+      (a, y) ∈ E ∧ (a, z) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d := by
+theorem allWordsIn_mem_NP {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)}
+    allWordsIn enc m E d ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits) := by
+  | zero => exact ⟨0, fun _ => true, .const _, by simp [IsVerifier]⟩
+        (fun x : α × List Bool => m.eval (enc x.1).length)
+    have htake : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+        {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.take (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} E :=
+    have hdrop : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+        {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d}
+/-- Unpack a `BH (r + 1)` language `D ⊆ U` (where `U ∈ NP`) into `D = B \ D₁` with
+`D₁ ⊆ B ⊆ U`, so that `D₁ = B \ D ⊆ U \ D`. -/
+private theorem mem_BH_succ_subset {γ : Type} {encγ : γ ↪ List Bool} {r : ℕ}
+    {U D : Set γ} (hU : U ∈ NP encγ) (hD : D ∈ BH encγ (r + 1)) (hDU : D ⊆ U) :
+    ∃ B ∈ NP encγ, ∃ D₁ ∈ BH encγ r,
+      B ⊆ U ∧ D₁ ⊆ B ∧ D = B \ D₁ ∧ D₁ ⊆ U \ D := by
+  obtain ⟨B', hB', D', hD', rfl⟩ := hD
+  refine ⟨B' ∩ U, inter_mem_NP hB' hU, D' ∩ (B' ∩ U),
+    have hxU : x ∈ B' \ D' → x ∈ U := fun h => hDU h

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A problem `A` in `Σₖ₊₁` is the projection of a problem `B` in `Πₖ` on pairs of an instance and a
+first certificate (`Cslib.Complexity.exists_mem_PiP_of_mem_SigmaP_succ`), the first step of the
+collapse of the hierarchy [Arora and Barak, Theorem 5.4][AroraBarak09]. `B` contains the pairs
+`(a, w₁)` from which the remaining `k` alternating quantifiers accept, with respect to the encoding
+`encPair enc encBits` of pairs. Its blocks of certificates have lengths given by polynomials in the
+length of `enc a`, while `Πₖ` asks for polynomials in the length of the encoded pair. The verifier
+of `B` therefore reads longer blocks and cuts each to its first bits
+(`Cslib.Complexity.truncateBlocks`), which does not change the quantifiers
+* `Cslib.Complexity.truncateBlocks`: cut blocks of certificates to shorter blocks.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.alternation_truncateBlocks`: cutting longer blocks does not change
+* `Cslib.Complexity.exists_mem_PiP_of_mem_SigmaP_succ`: a problem in `Σₖ₊₁` is the projection of
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The blocks of `w` of lengths `p.eval m`, for the polynomials `p` of `ps` in order, each cut to
+def truncateBlocks : List (Polynomial ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ → List Bool → List Bool
+  | p :: ps, n, m, w => w.take (p.eval n) ++ truncateBlocks ps n m (w.drop (p.eval m))
+/-- **Cutting longer blocks does not change alternating quantifiers**: quantifying over blocks of
+lengths `p.eval m` and cutting each to `p.eval n ≤ p.eval m` bits quantifies over all blocks of
+theorem alternation_truncateBlocks {ps : List (Polynomial ℕ)} {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) {q : Bool}
+    Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval m) (fun w => P (truncateBlocks ps n m w)) ↔
+      Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval n) P := by
+  induction ps generalizing q P with
+    -- a long block, appended to anything, cuts to its first `p.eval n` bits
+    have hcut (w v : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval m) :
+        truncateBlocks (p :: ps) n m (w ++ v) = w.take (p.eval n) ++ truncateBlocks ps n m v := by
+    have key (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval m) {q : Bool} :
+        Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval m)
+          (fun v => P (truncateBlocks (p :: ps) n m (w ++ v))) ↔
+        Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval n) fun v => P (w.take (p.eval n) ++ v) :=
+      (alternation_congr fun v => by rw [hcut w v hw]).trans
+    -- a short block is the cut of its padding
+    have hpad (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval n) :
+        (w ++ List.replicate (p.eval m - p.eval n) false).length = p.eval m := by
+    have htake (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval n) :
+        (w ++ List.replicate (p.eval m - p.eval n) false).take (p.eval n) = w := by
+    have hlen (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval m) : (w.take (p.eval n)).length = p.eval n :=
+        exact ⟨_, hlen w hw, (key w hw).mp hP⟩
+        refine ⟨_, hpad w hw, (key _ (hpad w hw)).mpr ?_⟩
+/-- Cutting blocks is polynomial-time, for a fixed list of polynomials and lengths `n`, `m` computed
+    (hM : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime M encIn encUnary) {W : γ → List Bool}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => truncateBlocks ps (N x) (M x) (W x)) encIn encBits := by
+/-- **A problem in `Σₖ₊₁` is the projection of a problem in `Πₖ`**, as in the proof of
+[Arora and Barak, Theorem 5.4][AroraBarak09]: there are a polynomial `p` and a problem `B` in `Πₖ`
+on pairs of an instance and a word, encoded by `encPair enc encBits`, such that `a ∈ A` iff some
+word `w` of length `p (enc a).length` has `(a, w) ∈ B`. -/
+theorem exists_mem_PiP_of_mem_SigmaP_succ {k : ℕ} {A : Set α} (hA : A ∈ SigmaP (k + 1) enc) :
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (B : Set (α × List Bool)), B ∈ PiP k (encPair enc encBits) ∧
+      ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ (a, w) ∈ B := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hlen, hV, hA⟩ := hA
+  have hlen' : ps.length = k := by simpa using hlen
+  -- the pairs `(a, w₁)` from which the last `k` quantifiers accept
+  let B : Set (α × List Bool) := {y | Alternation false
+    (ps.map fun r => r.eval (enc y.1).length) fun w => V (y.1, y.2 ++ w) = true}
+  have hle (y : α × List Bool) : (enc y.1).length ≤ (encPair enc encBits y).length := by
+  refine ⟨p, B, ⟨ps, fun z => V (z.1.1, z.1.2 ++ truncateBlocks ps (enc z.1.1).length
+      (encPair enc encBits z.1).length z.2), hlen', ?_, fun y => ?_⟩, hA⟩
+  · exact (alternation_truncateBlocks (hle y) (P := fun w => V (y.1, y.2 ++ w) = true)).symm

title: doc(guide): add the NP-completeness chapter (#629)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+This chapter states and proves NP-completeness results the way the library does: problems with
+explicit encodings, polynomial time on multi-tape Turing machines, verifiers, polynomial-time
+reductions and the Cook–Levin theorem. It ends by proving that `Clique` is NP-complete, step by
+step, which is the outline every new NP-completeness proof follows.
+Each problem lives in its own module under `Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Problems`, so a
+development imports the problems it uses. The first examples need only these:
+A decision problem is a set of instances, `A : Set α`. Complexity is measured on words, so a problem
+comes with an encoding of its instances as bit strings, `enc : α ↪ List Bool`. The encoding is
+part of every statement: whether a problem is in {name}`P` can depend on it, as it does for
+numbers written in unary rather than binary.
+Encodings are built from a few combinators: {name}`encBool` and {name}`encNat` (binary) for
+atoms, {name}`encPair` and {name}`encList` for pairs and lists, and {name}`encBits` for bit
+strings, which encode themselves. Encodings are ordinary functions, so you can look at them:
+[true, true, true, false, true, true, false, true]
+Problems fix their encodings next to their definitions. Satisfiability of CNF formulas over
+variables numbered by natural numbers is {name}`SAT`, encoded by {name}`encCNF`:
+A graph is a list of vertices and a list of edges ({name}`Graph`), encoded by {name}`encGraph`.
+{name}`Clique` asks whether a graph has a clique of a given size, so its instances are pairs,
+{name}`ComputableInPolyTime` `f encIn encOut` says that some multi-tape Turing machine with a
+binary alphabet and finitely many states computes `f`, reading `encIn a` and writing
+`encOut (f a)`, within time and space bounded by polynomials in the length of `encIn a`. This is
+the notion that definitions and theorems use.
+You rarely build machines. Closure rules for the usual operations are registered with
+`fun_prop`, so a function written with certified operations gets its certificate automatically:
+example : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 * p.2 + 1)
+Loops whose body depends on the rest of the input, such as a filter that compares each element
+with another part of the input, need the `polytime` tactic, which chooses loop rules and composes
+certificates. Membership tests and their negations are certified too:
+example : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1.filter (· ≤ p.2))
+    (fun p : List ℕ × List ℕ => p.1.filter fun x => x ∉ p.2)
+Both tactics prove only the cost. That `f` computes what you intend is a separate proof.
+A problem is in {name}`P` when a Boolean function deciding it is computable in polynomial time
+  ⟨fun l => decide (0 ∈ l), by polytime, fun l => by simp⟩
+{name}`NP` is defined by verifiers. A verifier `V : α × List Bool → Bool` reads an instance
+together with a certificate. {name}`IsVerifier` `enc p V A` says that `a ∈ A` exactly when some
+certificate of length `p.eval (enc a).length` makes `V` accept, so certificates are polynomially
+long in the encoded instance. A problem is in {name}`NP` when it has a verifier that is
+computable in polynomial time on the encoded pair ({name}`mem_NP`):
+example {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (A : Set α) :
+    A ∈ NP enc ↔ ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+Certificates have exactly the prescribed length. When the natural certificate is shorter, pad it
+with `false` and use {name}`IsVerifier.of_padding`. Every problem in {name}`P` is in {name}`NP`,
+with a verifier that ignores its certificate ({name}`P_subset_NP`), and {name}`coNP` consists of
+{name}`PolyTimeReducible` `encA encB A B` holds when a function `f`, computable in polynomial time
+from `encA` to `encB`, satisfies `a ∈ A ↔ f a ∈ B`. A reduction is built as a triple: the map, its
+Reductions compose ({name}`PolyTimeReducible.trans`), and {name}`P` is closed under them
+state deciders, verifiers and reductions in the same plain form.
+{name}`NPHard` `encB B` says that every problem in {name}`NP`, over any type of instances and with
+any encoding of them, reduces to `B`; {name}`NPComplete` adds that `B` is itself in {name}`NP`.
+Hardness transfers along reductions ({name}`NPHard.trans`), which is how almost every hardness
+proof goes. An NP-complete problem is in {name}`P` exactly when {name}`P` and {name}`NP` coincide
+({name}`NPComplete.mem_P_iff`), so two NP-complete problems are both in {name}`P` or both outside
+example : Clique ∈ P (encPair encGraph encNat) ↔ SAT ∈ P encCNF :=
+Its hardness half ({name}`CookLevin.SAT_npHard`) encodes the computation of any polynomial-time
+verifier as a formula. Unsatisfiability, its complement, is coNP-complete
+restates the theorem together with every definition it depends on.
+Every other NP-completeness proof in the library starts from Cook–Levin and follows reductions.
+Here is the tree, with the reduction for each edge and the completeness theorem for each problem:
+* SAT reduces to directed Hamiltonian paths and cycles ({name}`polyTimeReducible_SAT_DirHamPath`,
+  {name}`DirHamCycle_npComplete`), these reduce to their undirected versions
+  cycles reduce to the traveling salesperson problem ({name}`polyTimeReducible_HamCycle_TSP`,
+Chaining reductions with {name}`NPHard.trans` gives the hardness of any problem in the tree
+The module documentation of `Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Reduction` indexes the same
+results by problem, with the module to import for each.
