lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Keyed collision-resistant hash families and compression functions
+In the uniform PPT model, an unkeyed deterministic function `H : List Bool → List Bool` cannot be
+collision-resistant against a family of PPT adversaries unless a collision can never be hardcoded:
+a fixed collision `(m₁, m₂)` exists whenever the domain is larger than the range, and a uniform
+algorithm could find it in constant time at any fixed input length or carry it as a constant.
+Standard uniform formulations therefore index a hash family `H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`
+by a public key `k ← {0, 1}^n` sampled uniformly at security parameter `n`; the adversary receives
+`(1^n, k)` and wins by outputting a pair `(m₁, m₂)` of valid inputs with `m₁ ≠ m₂` and
+`H k m₁ = H k m₂` ([BonehShoup2023], Sections 8.1–8.2; [KatzLindell2020], Section 5.1).
+Parameterizing the experiment by a validity predicate `valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool` accommodates
+both fixed-input-length compression families (`validCompressionInput n x := (x.length == 2 * n)`,
+mapping `2n`-bit inputs to `n`-bit outputs under an `n`-bit key) and arbitrary-input-length hash
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CollisionFinder`: uniform adversary taking `(n, k)` and outputting candidate
+  probability against every uniform strict PPT adversary.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.HashFamily`: unrestricted collision-resistant hash families on arbitrary bit
+  extraction transfers collision resistance between hash families.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CollisionResistantOn.mono`: restricting the valid input domain preserves collision
+  probability bounded away from zero refutes collision resistance.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023],
+* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020], Section 5.1.
+/-- A collision finder receives the unary security parameter `n` and public hash key `k` and
+outputs a pair `(m₁, m₂)` of candidate colliding messages. -/
+abbrev CollisionFinder := ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)
+/-- Test whether `(m₁, m₂)` is a valid collision for `H k` at security parameter `n` under the
+def isCollision (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool) (valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool)
+    (n : ℕ) (k m₁ m₂ : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  valid n m₁ && valid n m₂ && (m₁ != m₂) && (H k m₁ == H k m₂)
+theorem isCollision_eq_true_iff {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool}
+    {valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool} {n : ℕ} {k m₁ m₂ : List Bool} :
+    isCollision H valid n k m₁ m₂ = true ↔
+      valid n m₁ = true ∧ valid n m₂ = true ∧ m₁ ≠ m₂ ∧ H k m₁ = H k m₂ := by
+  simp only [isCollision, Bool.and_eq_true, bne_iff_ne, beq_iff_eq, and_assoc]
+/-- Collision testing is symmetric in the two candidate messages. -/
+theorem isCollision_comm (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool)
+    (valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool) (n : ℕ) (k m₁ m₂ : List Bool) :
+    isCollision H valid n k m₁ m₂ = isCollision H valid n k m₂ m₁ := by
+theorem isCollision_self (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool)
+    (valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool) (n : ℕ) (k m : List Bool) :
+    isCollision H valid n k m m = false := by
+    {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool} {valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => H p.1 p.2)
+    (hvalid : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => valid p.1 p.2)
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {n : γ → ℕ} {k m₁ m₂ : γ → List Bool}
+      (fun a => isCollision H valid (n a) (k a) (m₁ a) (m₂ a)) encIn encBool := by
+  have hv₁ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => valid (n a) (m₁ a)) encIn encBool :=
+  have hv₂ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => valid (n a) (m₂ a)) encIn encBool :=
+  have hH₁ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => H (k a) (m₁ a)) encIn encBits :=
+  have hH₂ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => H (k a) (m₂ a)) encIn encBits :=
+/-- Testing whether `(m₁, m₂)` is a valid collision is polynomial-time when `H` and `valid` are
+    {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool} {valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => H p.1 p.2)
+    (hvalid : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => valid p.1 p.2)
+      (fun p : ℕ × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool =>
+        isCollision H valid p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2.1 p.2.2.2)
+      (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))) encBool := by
+/-- The keyed collision-finding experiment: sample a uniform `n`-bit key `k`, run `adversary n k`
+to obtain a candidate pair `(m₁, m₂)`, and accept when `isCollision H valid n k m₁ m₂` holds. -/
+noncomputable def collisionGame (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool)
+    (valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool) (adversary : CollisionFinder) (n : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool := do
+  return isCollision H valid n k pair.1 pair.2
+/-- Run the complete collision experiment on its unary security parameter. -/
+theorem isPPTOn_collisionGame {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => H p.1 p.2)
+    (hvalid : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => valid p.1 p.2)
+    IsPPTOn encUnary encBool (collisionGame H valid adversary) := by
+/-- The collision experiment is uniformly strict PPT, independently of unused auxiliary input. -/
+theorem isPPT_collisionGame {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => H p.1 p.2)
+    (hvalid : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => valid p.1 p.2)
+    IsPPT encBool (fun n _ => collisionGame H valid adversary n) :=
+/-- Collision resistance of a keyed hash family `H` on the valid input domain `valid`: every
+uniform strict PPT collision finder has negligible success probability. -/
+def CollisionResistantOn (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool)
+    (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (collisionGame H valid adversary n))
+/-- Unrestricted collision resistance on all bit strings `List Bool`. -/
+abbrev CollisionResistant (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool) : Prop :=
+/-- Collision resistance gives negligible collision-finding probability for every strict PPT
+theorem CollisionResistantOn.negligible {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool}
+    {valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool} (h : CollisionResistantOn H valid)
+      (fun n => Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval (collisionGame H valid adversary n))) := by
+  simpa only [Game.advantage_pure_false] using h adversary hPPT
+/-- Establish collision resistance by bounding every strict PPT adversary's success probability. -/
+theorem CollisionResistantOn.of_negligible {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool}
+    (h : ∀ adversary : CollisionFinder, IsPPT (encPair encBits encBits) adversary →
+        (fun n => Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval (collisionGame H valid adversary n)))) :
+  simpa only [Game.advantage_pure_false] using h adversary hPPT
+/-- If a deterministic map `extract` turns every valid `H₁`-collision under an `n`-bit key `k`
+into a valid `H₂`-collision under `k`, then postprocessing `adversary` by `extract` at parameter `n`
+    {H₁ H₂ : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool} {valid₁ valid₂ : ℕ → List Bool → Bool}
+    (extract : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool × List Bool)
+      isCollision H₁ valid₁ n k m₁ m₂ = true →
+      isCollision H₂ valid₂ n k (extract n k m₁ m₂).1 (extract n k m₁ m₂).2 = true) :
+            return extract m k pair.1 pair.2) n)) := by
+  simp only [collisionGame, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.bind_bind, PMF.pure_bind]
+  cases hcol : isCollision H₁ valid₁ n k pair.1 pair.2
+  · rw [himp k hklen pair.1 pair.2 hcol]
+/-- **Deterministic collision-extraction reduction**: if a polynomial-time function `extract`
+turns every `H₁`-collision at parameter `n` (for all sufficiently large `n` and `n`-bit keys `k`)
+into an `H₂`-collision under the same key `k`, then collision resistance of `H₂` implies collision
+    {H₁ H₂ : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool} {valid₁ valid₂ : ℕ → List Bool → Bool}
+    (extract : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool × List Bool)
+      (fun p : ℕ × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool => extract p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2.1 p.2.2.2)
+    (himp : ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ k, k.length = n → ∀ m₁ m₂,
+      isCollision H₁ valid₁ n k m₁ m₂ = true →
+      isCollision H₂ valid₂ n k (extract n k m₁ m₂).1 (extract n k m₁ m₂).2 = true) :
+  let redAdversary : CollisionFinder := fun n k => do
+    return extract n k pair.1 pair.2
+      (fun p : (ℕ × List Bool) × (List Bool × List Bool) =>
+  have hredPPT : IsPPT (encPair encBits encBits) redAdversary := by
+    change IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encBits) (encPair encBits encBits)
+/-- Restricting the valid input domain preserves collision resistance. -/
+    {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool} {valid₁ valid₂ : ℕ → List Bool → Bool}
+    (hsub : ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ m, valid₁ n m = true → valid₂ n m = true) :
+  refine hCR.of_extract (fun _ _ m₁ m₂ => (m₁, m₂)) (by polytime) ?_

+  exact ⟨hn m₁ hcol.1, hn m₂ hcol.2.1, hcol.2.2.1, hcol.2.2.2⟩
+/-- **Finding collisions with probability bounded away from zero refutes collision resistance**:
+a strict PPT adversary whose success probability is at least a fixed `c > 0` at every security
+    {H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool} {valid : ℕ → List Bool → Bool}
+    (h : ∀ n, c ≤ Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval (collisionGame H valid adversary n))) :
+  fun hCR => not_negligible_const hc (negligible_of_le (hCR.negligible adversary hPPT) h)
+/-- Validity predicate for a fixed-input-length `2n → n` compression family: at security parameter
+    validCompressionInput n x = true ↔ x.length = 2 * n :=
+      (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => validCompressionInput p.1 p.2)
+/-- Testing whether an input has length `2 * n` is computable in plain polynomial time. -/
+      (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => validCompressionInput p.1 p.2)
+/-- A keyed `2n → n` collision-resistant compression family ([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.2):
+computable in deterministic polynomial time, mapping `2n`-bit inputs under an `n`-bit key to
+structure CompressionFamily (h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool) : Prop where
+  /-- Deterministic polynomial-time evaluation of `(k, x) ↦ h k x`. -/
+  polyTime : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => h p.1 p.2)
+  /-- Compressing a `2n`-bit input under an `n`-bit key produces an `n`-bit digest. -/
+  length_eq : ∀ k x, x.length = 2 * k.length → (h k x).length = k.length
+  /-- Finding two distinct `2n`-bit inputs with the same digest under a uniform `n`-bit key is
+  hard for every uniform strict PPT adversary. -/
+/-- A keyed collision-resistant hash family on arbitrary-length bit strings (`List Bool`), mapping
+every message under an `n`-bit key to an `n`-bit digest. -/
+structure HashFamily (H : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool) : Prop where
+  /-- Deterministic polynomial-time evaluation of `(k, msg) ↦ H k msg`. -/

+  /-- Hashing any message under an `n`-bit key produces an `n`-bit digest. -/

IsAffine (fun _ : α => c) := fun _ _ _ => by rw [h, zero_add]

+# Reduced monomials over a finite field are independent

+are distinct as functions on `σ → K` when their exponent vectors are distinct, and in fact linearly
+independent (`FiniteField.linearIndependent_prod_pow`), by the combinatorial Nullstellensatz. So a
+combination of such monomials that vanishes at every point has zero coefficients

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+`PP` contains `NP` [Gill][Gill1977]: on random strings `b :: w`, accept when `b = false` and run the
+verifier on `w` when `b = true`, so the majority accepts exactly when some certificate does. `PP` is
+closed under complement [Gill][Gill1977]: with two more random bits, accept on a quarter of the
+random strings and one more, and on half of them reject what the verifier accepts; the majority
+accepts exactly when the verifier accepts at most half of its random strings. Hence also
+* [J. Gill, *Computational complexity of probabilistic Turing machines*][Gill1977]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- Counting the words of length `n + 1` by their first bit. -/
+private theorem card_filter_ofFn_succ (n : ℕ) (P : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
+    (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (n + 1) → Bool => P (List.ofFn r)).card =
+      (Finset.univ.filter fun w : Fin n → Bool => P (false :: List.ofFn w)).card +
+        (Finset.univ.filter fun w : Fin n → Bool => P (true :: List.ofFn w)).card := by
+/-- **`NP ⊆ PP`** [Gill][Gill1977]: on random strings `b :: w`, accept when `b = false` and run
+the verifier on `w` when `b = true`. The majority accepts exactly when the verifier accepts some
+theorem NP_subset_PP : NP enc ⊆ PP enc := by
+  let V' (x : α × List Bool) : Bool := !(x.2.headD false) || V (x.1, x.2.tail)
+  have hV' : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V' (encPair enc encBits) encBool :=
+  have hcount (m : ℕ) : acceptCount V' a (m + 1) = 2 ^ m + acceptCount V a m := by
+    rw [acceptCount, card_filter_ofFn_succ m fun l => V' (a, l) = true]
+  have heval : (p + 1).eval (enc a).length = p.eval (enc a).length + 1 := by simp
+  rw [heval, hcount, hA a, ← acceptCount_pos_iff, pow_succ]
+/-- **`PP` is closed under complement** [Gill][Gill1977]. On random strings `b₁ :: b₂ :: w`,
+accept when `b₁ = b₂ = false` and on `b₁ = false, b₂ = true` only for `w` all zeros, and reject
+what the verifier accepts on `w` when `b₁ = true`. With `acc` accepted and `rej` rejected strings
+of length `m`, this accepts `2 ^ m + 1 + 2 * rej` of the `4 * 2 ^ m` strings, more than half
+theorem compl_mem_PP (hA : A ∈ PP enc) : Aᶜ ∈ PP enc := by
+  let V' (x : α × List Bool) : Bool :=
+  have hV' : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V' (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+    have hw : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => x.2.tail.tail)
+  -- exactly one word of length `m` is all zeros
+  have hzero (m : ℕ) : (Finset.univ.filter fun w : Fin m → Bool =>
+      ((List.ofFn w).any fun b => b) = false).card = 1 := by
+    refine Finset.card_eq_one.mpr ⟨fun _ => false, Finset.ext fun w => ?_⟩
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, List.any_eq_false, List.mem_ofFn,
+    exact ⟨fun h => funext h, fun h i => by rw [h]⟩
+  have hcount (m : ℕ) : acceptCount V' a (m + 1 + 1) = 2 ^ m + 1 +
+      2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun w : Fin m → Bool => V (a, List.ofFn w) = false).card := by
+    rw [acceptCount, card_filter_ofFn_succ (m + 1) fun l => V' (a, l) = true,
+      card_filter_ofFn_succ m fun l => V' (a, false :: l) = true,
+      card_filter_ofFn_succ m fun l => V' (a, true :: l) = true]
+    simp only [V', List.headD_cons, List.tail_cons, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, Bool.not_false,
+  have heval : (p + 2).eval (enc a).length = p.eval (enc a).length + 1 + 1 := by simp
+  have hsum := acceptCount_add_card_filter_eq_false (V := V) (a := a) (n := p.eval (enc a).length)
+  rw [heval, hcount, Set.mem_compl_iff, hA a, pow_succ, pow_succ]
+theorem PP_eq_preimage_compl_PP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : PP enc = compl ⁻¹' PP enc := by
+/-- **`coNP ⊆ PP`**: `NP ⊆ PP` and `PP` is closed under complement. -/
+theorem coNP_subset_PP : coNP enc ⊆ PP enc := fun _ hA => by

+A problem is in `PSPACE` exactly when a Boolean function deciding it is tidily computable within
+some time and space polynomial in the length of the encoded instance
+complement, under polynomial-time reductions, and under polynomially bounded existential
+quantification [Arora and Barak, Chapter 4][AroraBarak09]. The existential quantifier over the
+words `w` of length `ℓ` is reachability within two steps from the all-zero word to the all-one word
+of width `ℓ + 1`, along edges to `true :: w` for the accepted `w` and from every word starting with
+`true` to the all-one word; Savitch's algorithm decides it at depth `1`, enumerating the candidates
+in place and reusing the space of the decider for each.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*][Sipser2013]
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- **`PSPACE` in the quantitative calculus**: a problem is in `PSPACE` exactly when a Boolean
+function deciding it is tidily computable within some time and within space polynomial in the
+theorem mem_PSPACE_iff_computableTidilyInO : A ∈ PSPACE enc ↔ ∃ (f : α → Bool) (T S : α → ℕ),
+    ComputableTidilyInO f enc encBool T S ∧ PolyBounded (fun a => (enc a).length) S ∧
+      ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a = true := by
+    exact ⟨f, fun a => 2 * t a + 3 * s a + c, s, .of_bounds hc (c + 1) (fun a => by nlinarith)
+      (fun a => by nlinarith) fun a => by
+  · rintro ⟨f, T, S, ⟨c, hc, -⟩, hS, hA⟩
+/-- **`PSPACE` within polynomial space**: a problem is in `PSPACE` exactly when a Boolean function
+deciding it is tidily computable within space polynomial in the length of the encoded instance
+    ∃ f : α → Bool, ComputableTidilyInPolySpace f enc encBool ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a = true := by
+  · rintro ⟨f, T, S, hf, hS, hA⟩
+    exact ⟨f, T, S, hf, hS, hA⟩
+/-- A Boolean function computable within polynomial space decides a problem in `PSPACE`. -/
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolySpace f enc encBool) (hA : ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a = true) :
+/-- **`PSPACE` is closed under complement**: negate the answer. -/
+theorem compl_mem_PSPACE (hA : A ∈ PSPACE enc) : Aᶜ ∈ PSPACE enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f, T, S, hf, hS, hA⟩ := mem_PSPACE_iff_computableTidilyInO.mp hA
+  refine mem_PSPACE_iff_computableTidilyInO.mpr ⟨_, T, S, hnot, hS, fun a => ?_⟩
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PSPACE {β : Type} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {B : Set β}
+    (h : PolyTimeReducible enc encB A B) (hB : B ∈ PSPACE encB) : A ∈ PSPACE enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f, T, S, hf, hS, hB⟩ := mem_PSPACE_iff_computableTidilyInO.mp hB
+  obtain ⟨Tg, Sg, hSg, hgO⟩ := ComputableTidilyInPolySpace.of_polyTime hg.tidy
+    hSg.add (hS.comp hg.polyBounded_length), fun a => (hAB a).trans (hB (g a))⟩
+/-- The edges of the graph on words of width `n + 1` whose reachability within two steps from the
+all-zero word to the all-one word is a bounded existential over `f`: an edge from the all-zero word
+to `true :: w` when `f (x, w)`, and from every word starting with `true` to the all-one word. -/
+private def existsEdge {β : Type} (f : β × List Bool → Bool) (x : β) (u v : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  if !(u.any fun b => b) && v.headD false then f (x, v.tail)
+/-- Savitch's algorithm at depth `1` on the edges of `existsEdge` decides the bounded
+private theorem savitch_existsEdge {β : Type} (f : β × List Bool → Bool) (x : β) (n : ℕ) :
+      (List.replicate (n + 1) true) = true ↔ ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = n ∧ f (x, w) = true := by
+  · rintro ⟨m, hm, h₁ | h₁, h₂ | h₂⟩
+    refine ⟨true :: w, by simp [hw], Or.inr ?_, Or.inr ?_⟩
+/-- **`PSPACE` is closed under polynomially bounded existential quantification**: if `B ⊆ β × List
+Bool` is in `PSPACE` and `ℓ` is polynomial-time, then so is the set of the `x` for which some word
+`w` of length `ℓ x` has `(x, w) ∈ B`. The candidates are enumerated in place: this is reachability
+within two steps between two words of width `ℓ x + 1` (`existsEdge`), which Savitch's algorithm
+decides at depth `1`, reusing the space of the decider of `B` for every candidate
+theorem setOf_exists_mem_PSPACE {β : Type} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {B : Set (β × List Bool)}
+    {ℓ : β → ℕ} (hB : B ∈ PSPACE (encPair encB encBits))

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Fix a prime `q`. Boneh and Shoup's Schnorr, Okamoto, Chaum–Pedersen and generic linear
+protocols ([BonehShoup2023], Sections 19.1 and 19.5.1–19.5.4) are one protocol, for the
+preimage of a `ZMod q`-linear map. Groups are written additively: a group of prime order `q`
+is a `ZMod q`-module, and the book's `g ^ α` is `α • g`. A multiplicative group of exponent `q`
+In `linear ψ u ι`, a statement `y` determines a linear map `ψ y : M →ₗ[ZMod q] N` and a target
+`u y : N`; a witness is a preimage `x` with `ψ y x = u y`. The prover commits to `ψ y r` for a
+uniform `r : M` and answers the challenge `c` with `r + c • x`. Challenges come from any type `C`
+with an injection `ι : C ↪ ZMod q`, which covers a subset of `ZMod q` as well as bit strings
+Completeness and special honest-verifier zero knowledge hold for every modulus. Special
+soundness, which divides by a difference of distinct challenges, uses that `q` is prime. The
+instances need no hypothesis that the group is cyclic or that the given elements generate it.
+* `SigmaProtocol.linear`: the protocol for preimages of statement-dependent linear maps.
+* `SigmaProtocol.okamoto`: knowledge of `(α, β)` with `α • g + β • h = u` (Section 19.5.1).
+* `SigmaProtocol.chaumPedersen`: `(u, v, w)` is a Diffie–Hellman triple (Section 19.5.2).
+* `SigmaProtocol.linearSystem`: a solution of `∑ j, α j • g i j = u i` for all `i`
+  `SigmaProtocol.linear_specialHVZK`: Theorem 19.12 for groups of prime order `q`.
+* The same three properties for each instance, with the instance's own relation
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+* [C.-P. Schnorr, *Efficient Signature Generation by Smart Cards*][Schnorr1991]
+variable {q : ℕ} {M N Y C : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module (ZMod q) M] [Fintype M]
+/-- The Sigma protocol for a preimage of the linear map `ψ y` at `u y`
+([BonehShoup2023], Figures 19.8 and 19.9). The prover commits to `ψ y r` for a uniform `r` and
+answers the challenge `c` with `r + ι c • x`; the verifier checks `ψ y z = t + ι c • u y`. -/
+noncomputable def linear (ψ : Y → M →ₗ[ZMod q] N) (u : Y → N) (ι : C ↪ ZMod q) :
+    SigmaProtocol M Y N C M where
+  commit _ y := (PMF.uniformOfFintype M).map fun r => (ψ y r, r)
+  respond x _ r c := r + ι c • x
+  verify y t c z := decide (ψ y z = t + ι c • u y)
+/-- The extractor divides the difference of the responses by the difference of the
+def linearExtract (ι : C ↪ ZMod q) (_ : Y) (_ : N) (c : C) (z : M) (c' : C) (z' : M) : M :=
+/-- The simulator samples a uniform response and solves the verification equation for the
+noncomputable def linearSimulate (ψ : Y → M →ₗ[ZMod q] N) (u : Y → N) (ι : C ↪ ZMod q)
+  (PMF.uniformOfFintype M).map fun z => (ψ y z - ι c • u y, z)
+variable (ψ : Y → M →ₗ[ZMod q] N) (u : Y → N) (ι : C ↪ ZMod q)
+@[simp] theorem linear_accepts_iff {y : Y} {t : N} {c : C} {z : M} :
+    (linear ψ u ι).Accepts y t c z ↔ ψ y z = t + ι c • u y := by
+/-- An honest transcript is `(ψ y r, r + ι c • x)` for a uniform `r`. -/
+    (linear ψ u ι).transcript x y c =
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype M).map fun r => (ψ y r, r + ι c • x) := by
+theorem linear_complete : (linear ψ u ι).Complete fun x y => ψ y x = u y := by
+  intro x y hxy c tz htz
+/-- `linearExtract` is a witness extractor when `q` is prime ([BonehShoup2023], Theorem 19.12). -/
+    (linear ψ u ι).SpecialSoundness (fun x y => ψ y x = u y) (linearExtract ι) := by
+  intro y t c z c' z' hc hz hz'
+  have hne : ι c - ι c' ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (ι.injective.ne hc)
+  simp only [linearExtract, map_smul, map_sub, hz, hz', add_sub_add_left_eq_sub, ← sub_smul,
+/-- `linearSimulate` is a perfect simulator at every challenge ([BonehShoup2023],
+    (linear ψ u ι).SpecialHVZK (fun x y => ψ y x = u y) (linearSimulate ψ u ι) where
+  accepts y c tz htz := by
+  transcript_eq x y hxy c := by
+    simp only [Function.comp_apply, Equiv.coe_addRight, map_add, map_smul, hxy,
+variable {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] {G C : Type} [AddCommGroup G] [Module (ZMod q) G] [DecidableEq G]
+/-- Schnorr's Sigma protocol for knowledge of `α` with `α • g = u`
+noncomputable def schnorr (g : G) : SigmaProtocol (ZMod q) G G C (ZMod q) :=
+  linear (fun _ => LinearMap.toSpanSingleton (ZMod q) G g) id ι
+@[simp] theorem schnorr_accepts_iff {u t : G} {c : C} {z : ZMod q} :
+    (schnorr ι g).Accepts u t c z ↔ z • g = t + ι c • u := by
+theorem schnorr_complete : (schnorr ι g).Complete fun α u => α • g = u :=
+  (linear_complete _ _ ι).mono fun _ _ h => by simpa using h
+    (schnorr ι g).SpecialSoundness (fun α u => α • g = u) (linearExtract ι) :=
+  (linear_specialSoundness _ _ ι).mono fun _ _ h => by simpa using h
+    (schnorr ι g).SpecialHVZK (fun α u => α • g = u)
+      (linearSimulate (fun _ => LinearMap.toSpanSingleton (ZMod q) G g) id ι) :=
+  (linear_specialHVZK _ _ ι).mono fun _ _ h => by simpa using h
+/-- Okamoto's Sigma protocol for knowledge of a representation `(α, β)` of `u`, meaning
+noncomputable def okamoto (g h : G) : SigmaProtocol (ZMod q × ZMod q) G G C (ZMod q × ZMod q) :=
+@[simp] theorem okamoto_accepts_iff {u t : G} {c : C} {z : ZMod q × ZMod q} :
+    (okamoto ι g h).Accepts u t c z ↔ z.1 • g + z.2 • h = t + ι c • u := by

+# Native codes for the existing half-split balanced circuit
+The constructor keeps the exact `Circuit.balanced` topology, including the order of gate blocks.
+Its private dynamic program fills contiguous-interval rows in increasing interval length.
+The loop count is the length of the complete leaf-code list, never a binary arity parameter.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.balancedCode`: the complete raw code of a balanced circuit.
+  binary input arity and native generators of the complete operator, fallback and leaf codes.
+The resource proof counts all gates, gate arguments and outputs, including dead gates, and
+controls the binary lengths of wire references. Thus an arbitrarily large unused input arity
+does not become a unary resource bound. Every stored interval, invalid-interval fallback, row
+and table frame is charged; the captured input is charged by the native loop combinator.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Section 6.1][AroraBarak09]

+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut`: some machine with a binary alphabet and
+finitely many states computes `f` in the sense of `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInTimeAndSpace`,
+within time and space bounded by polynomially bounded functions of the length of the encoded input
+[Arora and Barak, Chapter 1][AroraBarak09]. Time and space are independent bounds, as in
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength`; that a polynomial time bound already bounds
+the space is a lemma about machines, not part of the definition.
+The predicate is registered with `fun_prop`. This file proves the closure rules that need no
+machine construction beyond upstream's: the identity, constants, functions on finite types and
+  functions that do not change the encoded word.
+  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.of_finite`: constant functions and functions on finite
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- `f` is computable in polynomial time: some machine with a binary alphabet and finitely many
+states computes `f`, relative to the encodings `encIn` and `encOut`, within time and space
+bounded by polynomially bounded functions of the length of the encoded input. -/
+def ComputableInPolyTime {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (encIn : α ↪ List Bool)
+  ∃ t s : ℕ → ℕ, PolynomiallyBounded t ∧ PolynomiallyBounded s ∧
+    ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength f encIn encOut t s
+variable {α β : Type*} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encOut : β ↪ List Bool}
+/-- A function whose encoded values are its encoded arguments is computable in polynomial time:

+  obtain ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, htm⟩ := computableInTimeAndSpace_id (enc := encIn)

+/-- Every function on a finite type is computable in polynomial time, by a lookup machine. -/

+  let ⟨c, h⟩ := computableInTimeAndSpace_of_finite (encIn := encIn) (encOut := encOut) f

+# Carry lookahead by parallel prefix doubling
+A carry summary `(g, p)` acts on a carry `c` by `g || (p && c)`. Summaries are composed in
+significance order. Each round doubles the interval summarized by each cell; cells without a
+neighbour retain their summary. The initial carry is an additional cell, so width zero still
+The construction uses the associative carry-transfer operation underlying parallel-prefix
+addition [Ladner and Fischer, Section 4][LadnerFischer1980]. OR-propagate summaries represent
+the same carry functions. It uses the simple doubling network, rather than their optimized
+linear-size prefix network. All gates, including constants and negations, count.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.CarryLookahead.scan`: the prefix circuit after a specified number
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.carryLookahead`: full addition with carry-in and carry-out.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.carryLookaheadAdd`: modular addition of two unsigned words.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.carryLookaheadFinish`: finish a carry-save pair in logarithmic depth.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.val_eval_carryLookahead`: exact unsigned addition at every width.
+Native polynomial-time generation of the complete codes is proved in `CarryLookahead.PolyTime`.
+* [R. E. Ladner, M. J. Fischer, *Parallel Prefix Computation*][LadnerFischer1980]
+/-- Compose the high-significance summary with the low-significance summary. -/

+private theorem combine_assoc (a b c : Bool × Bool) :

+  rcases a with ⟨a, a'⟩; rcases b with ⟨b, b'⟩; rcases c with ⟨c, c'⟩
+  cases a <;> cases a' <;> cases b <;> cases b' <;> cases c <;> cases c' <;> rfl

+@[simp] theorem combine_unit_right (a : Bool × Bool) : combine a (false, true) = a := by
+@[simp] theorem combine_self (a : Bool × Bool) : combine a a = a := by
+  rcases a with ⟨a, b⟩; cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
+/-- Consecutive carry summaries, with the most significant one first. -/
+def rangeSummary (row : ℕ → Bool × Bool) (start : ℕ) : ℕ → Bool × Bool

+    rw [show m + 1 + n = (m + n) + 1 by omega, rangeSummary, ih, rangeSummary,
+private theorem rangeSummary_eq_unit (row : ℕ → Bool × Bool) {start : ℕ}
+    (h : ∀ i, start ≤ i → row i = (false, true)) (count : ℕ) :
+    rangeSummary row start count = (false, true) := by
+    rw [rangeSummary, h start le_rfl, combine_unit_left, ih]
+/-- Read one summary from two equal-width rows, using the identity after the row ends. -/
+def readRow {k : ℕ} (row : BitString (k + k)) (i : ℕ) : Bool × Bool :=

+/-- The neighbour at the given distance, or the cell itself if the neighbour is absent. -/

+  if h : i.val + distance < k then ⟨i.val + distance, h⟩ else i
+/-- The generate output of one prefix cell. Inactive cells use idempotence to retain their value,
+so the scalar circuit has exactly two gates in either branch. -/

+    ((Formula.input (Fin.natAdd k i)).and (Formula.input (Fin.castAdd k (neighbour k distance i))))
+/-- The propagate output of one prefix cell. -/

+  (Formula.input (Fin.natAdd k i)).and (Formula.input (Fin.natAdd k (neighbour k distance i)))
+/-- One round of parallel carry composition, with all generate bits before all propagate bits. -/

+/-- The doubling network on an existing row of carry summaries. -/

+/-- Propagate one reversed input summary; the incoming carry is a constant transfer. -/

+/-- Carry summaries in descending significance, followed by the incoming carry. -/

+/-- The carry network; `w - i` is the generate-wire index of the carry into bit `i`. -/
+/-- One sum bit, reading the original inputs followed by the carry network. -/
+/-- Convert carry summaries to sum bits and retain the final carry as the last output. -/
+    (Circuit.wiring signature fun _ : Fin 1 => Fin.natAdd (w + w + 1) ⟨0, by omega⟩)
+@[simp] theorem size_sumFormula (w : ℕ) (i : Fin w) : (sumFormula w i).size = 15 := by
+@[simp] theorem size_finish (w : ℕ) : (finish w).size = 15 * w := by
+/-- The arithmetic carry into bit `i`, used only as the specification. -/
+def inputCarry {w : ℕ} (u : BitString (w + w + 1)) (i : ℕ) : Bool :=
+  BitVec.carry i (word (u ∘ leftInput w)) (word (u ∘ rightInput w)) (u (Fin.last (w + w)))
+private theorem readRow_initial {w : ℕ} (u : BitString (w + w + 1)) (i : Fin (w + 1)) :
+  simp only [readRow, i.isLt, ↓reduceDIte, initial, Circuit.eval_append, Fin.append_left,
+private theorem rangeSummary_initial {w : ℕ} (u : BitString (w + w + 1)) (i : ℕ)
+    have hs : w - (i + 1) + 1 = w - i := by omega
+    have hr := readRow_initial u ⟨w - (i + 1), by omega⟩
+    have hj : w - (i + 1) < w := by omega

+      getLsbD_word (u ∘ rightInput w) ⟨i, by omega⟩, Function.comp_apply]
+      cases BitVec.carry i (word (u ∘ leftInput w)) (word (u ∘ rightInput w))
+/-- The generate output at reversed index `w-i` is exactly carry `i`, including both endpoints. -/
+    (carries w).eval interpretation u ⟨w - i.val, by omega⟩ = inputCarry u i.val := by
+  have hpow : w + 1 ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 (w + 1) := Nat.le_pow_clog (by decide) _
+  have h := readRow_scan ((initial w).eval interpretation u) (Nat.clog 2 (w + 1)) (w - i.val)
+  rw [he, rangeSummary_add, rangeSummary_initial u i.val (by omega)] at h
+  have hz : rangeSummary (readRow ((initial w).eval interpretation u))
+  simpa [readRow, show w - i.val < w + 1 by omega, carries, Circuit.eval_comp] using hg
+/-- Add two unsigned words and an input carry. Inputs are the first word, the second word, then
+one carry bit. Outputs are the low `w` sum bits followed by the output carry. -/
+/-- The exact number of gates in the doubling adder. -/
+/-- Every gate has fan-in at most two, and the adder has logarithmic depth. -/
+  have h₁ := Circuit.depth_append_le (Circuit.wiring signature id) (CarryLookahead.carries w)
+/-- An explicit absolute-constant logarithmic depth bound, including width zero. -/
+/-- A coarse polynomial bound on the complete adder's number of gates. -/
+/-- Each low output bit is the sum bit with the specified incoming carry. -/
+theorem eval_carryLookahead_sum {w : ℕ} (u : BitString (w + w + 1)) (i : Fin w) :
+    show i.castSucc = Fin.castAdd 1 i from rfl, Fin.append_left, Circuit.eval_pi,
+/-- The last output is the final carry, also at width zero. -/
+    (carryLookahead w).eval interpretation u (Fin.last w) = CarryLookahead.inputCarry u w := by
+/-- Exact unsigned addition, including the output carry. -/
+theorem val_eval_carryLookahead {w : ℕ} (a b : BitString w) (c : Bool) :
+      ((carryLookahead w).eval interpretation (Fin.append (Fin.append a b) (fun _ => c))) : ℕ) =
+        (BitString.equivFin w a : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w b : ℕ) + c.toNat := by
+  let u := Fin.append (Fin.append a b) (fun _ : Fin 1 => c)
+  have hl : u ∘ CarryLookahead.leftInput w = a := by
+  have hr : u ∘ CarryLookahead.rightInput w = b := by
+    simp only [u, Function.comp_apply, CarryLookahead.rightInput, Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right]
+  have hc : u (Fin.last (w + w)) = c := Fin.append_right _ _ 0
+  have hs : word (Fin.init ((carryLookahead w).eval interpretation u)) =
+      word a + word b + BitVec.setWidth w (BitVec.ofBool c) := by
+    simpa only [Fin.init, hl, hr, hc] using eval_carryLookahead_sum u ⟨i, hi⟩
+  simp only [CarryLookahead.inputCarry, hl, hr, hc, BitVec.carry_width] at hout
+  by_cases h : (BitString.equivFin w a : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w b : ℕ) + c.toNat ≥ 2 ^ w
+  · simp only [h, decide_false, Bool.toNat_false, zero_mul, Nat.add_zero]
+/-- Discard the final carry and hardwire a false incoming carry. -/
+def carryLookaheadAdd (w : ℕ) : Circuit signature (w + w) w :=
+/-- The modular result used to collapse a carry-save pair. -/
+    (BitString.equivFin w ((carryLookaheadAdd w).eval interpretation (Fin.append a b)) : ℕ) =
+      ((BitString.equivFin w a : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w b : ℕ)) % 2 ^ w := by
+  have h := val_eval_carryLookahead a b false
+  have he : (carryLookaheadAdd w).eval interpretation (Fin.append a b) =
+  simp only [Circuit.depth_wiring, Circuit.depth_oneGate, zero_max] at h₂
+/-- An explicit absolute-constant depth bound for modular addition. -/
+/-- Polynomial size after fixing the incoming carry and selecting the modular result. -/
+/-- A drop-in carry-save finisher: the first word is the modular sum and the second is zero. -/
+def carryLookaheadFinish (w : ℕ) : Circuit signature (w + w) (w + w) :=
+/-- Only one extra constant gate is needed to clear the second carry-save word. -/
+/-- The carry-save finisher has logarithmic depth in the word width. -/
+/-- A polynomial gate bound for the drop-in carry-save finisher. -/
+/-- The replacement finishing stage preserves every carry-save value modulo `2^w`. -/

+/-- A 4-to-2 carry-save reduction followed by the new finisher computes the same modular sum.

+/-- Finishing a 4-to-2 reduction adds only a constant to the logarithmic depth bound. -/

+# Native generation of carry-lookahead circuit codes
+All constructors return the actual binary gate-and-output encoding. Widths and loop counts are
+unary; distances and wire references are binary. The prefix loop carries its already generated
+code and appends one fixed-width round at a time. Bounds on the complete intermediate encoding
+justify the loop, including tags, delimiters and output references.
+  the complete adder code from unary width.
+  `computableTidilyInPolyTime_carryLookaheadFinish`: the modular and carry-save finishing codes.
+/-- The total raw neighbour rule used by the doubling layer. -/
+def neighbourIndex (k distance i : ℕ) : ℕ := if i + distance < k then i + distance else i
+/-- The generate cell's full code, also defined on out-of-range raw coordinates. -/
+def generateCode (k distance i : ℕ) : List (Op × List ℕ) × List ℕ :=
+    ![i, k + i, neighbourIndex k distance i]
+def propagateCode (k distance i : ℕ) : List (Op × List ℕ) × List ℕ :=
+    ![k + i, k + neighbourIndex k distance i]
+private theorem generateCode_eq (k distance : ℕ) (i : Fin k) :
+    generateCode k distance i.val = (generateFormula k distance i).toCircuit.code := by
+    ![Fin.castAdd k i, Fin.natAdd k i, Fin.castAdd k (neighbour k distance i)]
+  have hw : (fun j => (wires j).val) = ![i.val, k + i.val, neighbourIndex k distance i.val] := by
+      fin_cases j <;> simp [wires, neighbour, neighbourIndex, h, Nat.add_comm]
+private theorem propagateCode_eq (k distance : ℕ) (i : Fin k) :
+    propagateCode k distance i.val = (propagateFormula k distance i).toCircuit.code := by
+  let wires : Fin 2 → Fin (k + k) := ![Fin.natAdd k i, Fin.natAdd k (neighbour k distance i)]
+  have hw : (fun j => (wires j).val) = ![k + i.val, k + neighbourIndex k distance i.val] := by
+      fin_cases j <;> simp [wires, neighbour, neighbourIndex, h, Nat.add_comm]
+private theorem generateCode_polyTime {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {k distance i : α → ℕ} (hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encNat)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => generateCode (k a) (distance a) (i a)) enc encCode := by
+  · change ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => k a + i a) enc encNat
+  · change ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => neighbourIndex (k a) (distance a) (i a)) enc encNat
+private theorem propagateCode_polyTime {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {k distance i : α → ℕ} (hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encNat)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => propagateCode (k a) (distance a) (i a)) enc encCode := by
+  · change ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => k a + i a) enc encNat
+      (fun a => k a + neighbourIndex (k a) (distance a) (i a)) enc encNat
+/-- Bundle the fixed-size generate and propagate blocks of one doubling round. -/
+def stepCode (k distance : ℕ) : List (Op × List ℕ) × List ℕ :=
+/-- The raw round is exactly the typed circuit's code, with no malformed-input assumption. -/
+theorem stepCode_eq (k distance : ℕ) : stepCode k distance = (step k distance).code := by
+      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => (generateFormula k distance i).toCircuit.code) := by
+    simpa using generateCode_eq k distance ⟨i, by simpa using hi⟩
+      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => (propagateFormula k distance i).toCircuit.code) := by
+    simpa using propagateCode_eq k distance ⟨i, by simpa using hi⟩
+  rw [stepCode, hg, hp, bundleCode_code _ _ (by intro i; simp [generateFormula]),
+/-- A doubling round is generated uniformly from a unary width and a binary distance. -/
+    {k distance : α → ℕ} (hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encUnary)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => stepCode (k a) (distance a)) enc encCode := by
+  have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => k a + k a) enc encNat := by fun_prop
+      (fun p : α × ℕ => generateCode (k p.1) (distance p.1) p.2)
+      (fun p : α × ℕ => propagateCode (k p.1) (distance p.1) p.2)
+    (Circuit.wiring signature (id : Fin k → Fin k)).code = ([], List.range k) := by
+  change List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => i.val) = List.range k
+/-- Generate any number of doubling rounds from unary width and round count. The native loop
+keeps the accumulated code and unary round counter, with polynomial intermediate encoded length. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (scan p.1 p.2).code)

+        (fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × (List (Op × List ℕ) × List ℕ)) => p.2.1 + 1)

+      (range.comp (show ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 + p.1)
+        (encPair encUnary encUnary) encUnary from by fun_prop))
+    simpa only [Function.comp_def, List.map_id_fun', id_eq, init] using
+  have heq (k t : ℕ) : (next k)^[t] (init k) = (t, (scan k t).code) := by
+  have hb : PolyBounded (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (encPair encUnary encUnary p).length) bound :=
+  have h := iterateWith (par := Prod.fst) (count := Prod.snd) (init := fun p => init p.1)
+    (step := next) (fst _ _) (snd _ _) hi hn hb (fun p i hit => by
+      have hsize : (scan p.1 i).size ≤ 3 * p.1 * p.2 := by
+/-- The generate gate of an initial cell, expressed as raw circuit data. -/
+def initialGenerateCode (w i : ℕ) : List (Op × List ℕ) × List ℕ :=
+/-- The propagate gate of an initial cell, expressed as raw circuit data. -/
+def initialPropagateCode (w i : ℕ) : List (Op × List ℕ) × List ℕ :=
+    initialGenerateCode w i.val = (initialGenerate w i).code := by
+    initialPropagateCode w i.val = (initialPropagate w i).code := by
+/-- The whole initial row, with one gate per generate or propagate cell. -/
+def initialCode (w : ℕ) : List (Op × List ℕ) × List ℕ :=
+private theorem initialCode_eq (w : ℕ) : initialCode w = (initial w).code := by
+      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (w + 1) => (initialGenerate w i).code) := by
+      initialGenerateCode_eq w ⟨i, by simpa using hi⟩
+      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (w + 1) => (initialPropagate w i).code) := by
+      initialPropagateCode_eq w ⟨i, by simpa using hi⟩
+/-- Native generation of the complete initial carry row from unary width. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun w => (initial w).code) encUnary encCode := by
+  have hw : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1)
+  have hi : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.2)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Sign-pattern counts from integer product queries
+A quadratic polynomial on `{-1, 0, 1}` gives twice the indicator of a requested sign.
+Multiplying these indicators expresses `2 ^ k` times a sign-pattern count as an integer
+combination of `3 ^ k` product-sign queries. No division or selection of matrix rows is needed.
+For a polynomial's roots, the queries and counts use `roots.toFinset`, so each distinct real
+root contributes once, independently of its multiplicity. Mathlib assigns the zero polynomial
+an empty root multiset. The equivalence with existence of a real root therefore requires a
+This is a counting identity. It does not supply an algorithm for evaluating a sign query or a
+time or space bound for sign determination.
+* `Cslib.SignQueries.signCount`: the number of points realizing a sign pattern.
+* `Cslib.SignQueries.tarskiQuery`: the sum of signs at distinct real roots.
+* `Cslib.SignQueries.scaledRootCount`: the integer combination of root sign queries.
+* `Cslib.SignQueries.scaledRootCount_eq`: its specialization to distinct real roots.
+* `Cslib.SignQueries.scaledRootCount_pos_iff`: for a nonzero polynomial, a positive scaled
+  count is equivalent to existence of a root realizing the requested sign pattern.

+/-- Evaluating a sign's quadratic at another sign gives twice the equality indicator. -/

+/-- Expanding the product of the sign quadratics gives the scaled pattern indicator. -/
+theorem product_indicator {J : Type*} [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] (σ t : J → SignType) :
+    (∑ e : J → Fin 3, patternWeight σ e * ∏ i, (t i : ℤ) ^ (e i).val) =
+      if t = σ then 2 ^ Fintype.card J else 0 := by

+      (Fintype.prod_sum (fun (i : J) (e : Fin 3) => weight (σ i) e * (t i : ℤ) ^ e.val)).symm

+original input, current index and accumulator. Its native computation may use arbitrary time in
+polynomial space. A polynomial bound on all encoded accumulator prefixes suffices for the fold;
+the count itself need not be polynomially bounded.

+variable {α β : Type} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encState : β ↪ List Bool}

+private theorem iterate_advance (step : α → ℕ → β → β) (x : α) (init : β) (k : ℕ) :
+    (advance step)^[k] (x, 0, init) = (x, k, k.fold (fun i _ a => step x i a) init) := by
+  | succ k ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, Nat.fold_succ]; rfl
+/-- A fold over a binary count is polynomial-space when its step and seed are polynomial-space
+and every accumulator prefix has polynomially bounded encoded length. -/
+    {step : α → ℕ → β → β} {init : α → β} {count bound : α → ℕ}
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInPolySpace (fun p : α × ℕ × β => step p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)

+      (fun x => (count x).fold (fun i _ a => step x i a) (init x)) encIn encState := by
+  have hinput := of_polyTime (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst encIn (encPair encNat encState))
+  have hrest := of_polyTime (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.snd encIn (encPair encNat encState))
+      (encPair encIn (encPair encNat encState)) (encPair encIn (encPair encNat encState)) :=
+  have hstart : ComputableTidilyInPolySpace (fun x => (x, 0, init x))

+    have ha := hstates x k hk
+  exact hout.congr fun x => by rw [iterate_advance]
+/-- A prefix invariant proves the fold's polynomial-space certificate and its final
+postcondition. The invariant and bound are proof data; only the count, seed and step run. -/
+    {step : α → ℕ → β → β} {init : α → β} {count bound : α → ℕ}
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInPolySpace (fun p : α × ℕ × β => step p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Replacing the public-key distribution in chosen-message security
+One uniform distinguisher samples a hidden fair challenge bit after the adversary has chosen its
+messages and saved state. It runs the actual encryption and guessing stages, then returns the
+guess XOR the hidden bit. Comparing this same distinguisher on two public-key distributions
+controls the change in their chosen-message gaps, with an exact factor of two.
+* `publicKeyGame`: the chosen-message experiment for a specified public-key law.
+* `keyDistinguisher`: the single reduction, preserving the adversary's saved state.
+* `eval_game_eq_publicKeyGame`: the actual encryption game uses its public-key marginal.
+* `isPPT_keyDistinguisher`: native strict PPT composition of the actual reduction.
+* `probability_keyDistinguisher`: the exact affine identity for the signed chosen-message gap.
+* `advantage_publicKeyGame_le`: quantitative public-key replacement with loss two.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023],
+  Section 11.2, for the chosen-message experiment and game-reduction method.
+/-- Run the chosen-message experiment with a specified public-key distribution. The complete
+state returned by message selection is passed unchanged to guessing. -/
+    (encrypt : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+    (encrypt security pk (if bit then choice.1.2 else choice.1.1))
+/-- An honest key generator contributes precisely its public-key marginal. -/
+theorem eval_game_eq_publicKeyGame (keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
+    (encrypt : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+    ProbComp.eval (game keyGen encrypt adversary bit security) =
+        encrypt adversary bit security := eval_game keyGen encrypt adversary bit security
+/-- A single uniform distinguisher with its own hidden fair challenge bit. The adversary sees
+only the supplied public key and the actual challenge ciphertext, with its saved state retained. -/
+    (encrypt : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+    (adversary : Adversary) : Distinguisher := fun security pk => do
+  let ciphertext ← encrypt security pk (if bit then choice.1.2 else choice.1.1)
+  let guess ← adversary.guess security choice.2 ciphertext
+/-- The reduction is one uniform strict PPT program when encryption and both adversary stages
+    {encrypt : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)} {adversary : Adversary}
+    (hadversary : adversary.IsPPT) : IsPPT encBool (keyDistinguisher encrypt adversary) := by
+/-- The hidden-bit experiment averages the two chosen-message games, complementing the second.
+No finiteness or independence assumption is imposed on the saved state. -/
+    (encrypt : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+      (publicKeyGame keys encrypt adversary bit security).map (fun guess => guess ^^ bit)) := by
+/-- Acceptance is one half plus half the signed chosen-message gap. -/
+    (encrypt : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+      (1 + (Game.succProbability (publicKeyGame keys encrypt adversary false security) : ℝ) -
+        Game.succProbability (publicKeyGame keys encrypt adversary true security)) / 2 := by
+/-- Replacing the public-key law costs at most twice the advantage of one uniform hidden-bit
+distinguisher, plus the chosen-message advantage under the replacement law. -/
+    (encrypt : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
+    Game.advantage (publicKeyGame real encrypt adversary false security)
+            Game.advantage (publicKeyGame ideal encrypt adversary false security)
+              (publicKeyGame ideal encrypt adversary true security) := by
+    ((Game.succProbability (publicKeyGame real encrypt adversary false security) : ℝ) -
+      Game.succProbability (publicKeyGame real encrypt adversary true security))
+    ((Game.succProbability (publicKeyGame ideal encrypt adversary false security) : ℝ) -
+      Game.succProbability (publicKeyGame ideal encrypt adversary true security)) 0
+  have hscale (a b c d : ℝ) :
+      _ = |2 * ((1 + a - b) / 2 - (1 + c - d) / 2)| := by rw [abs_mul]; norm_num

+/-- Self-delimiting framing: double each bit `b` to `[true,b]` and terminate with `[false]`. -/

+-- including the three depths above. Fresh inputs use the initial false mask of this real key.
+    (bits : List Bool) (hbits : bits.length = arity) (output : List Bool)
+    ⟨arity, c⟩ hdepth bits (bits.map (fun bit => [false, bit, false])) hbits ?_ output houtput
+-- The concrete base scheme inhabits the whole scheme and fixed-width interfaces at any budget.
+  Leveled.correct decryptionCircuits tagged_correct tagged_width tagged_bootstrappable budget
+  Leveled.fixedWidth decryptionCircuits tagged_correct tagged_width tagged_bootstrappable budget
+-- Total decoding and circuit-based decryption cover malformed keys and truncated ciphertexts.
+-- All four native algorithm certificates accept their full inputs, including arbitrary key
+-- serializations, malformed ciphertexts and circuits outside the budget. No validity is assumed.
+    (fun p => Leveled.keyGen tagged p.1 p.2) := by
+    (fun p => Leveled.encrypt tagged p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) := by
+    (fun p : ℕ × List Bool × List Bool => Leveled.decrypt decryptionCircuits p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+    (fun p => Leveled.evaluate decryptionCircuits p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2.1 p.2.2.2.1 p.2.2.2.2) := by
+  apply Leveled.isPPTOn_evaluate encrypt_ppt decryptionCircuits circuits_poly evaluate_ppt
+-- A nonconstant budget family instantiates the actual Scheme fields with one uniform clock.
+  exact Leveled.isPPTOn_scheme_evaluate encrypt_ppt decryptionCircuits circuits_poly evaluate_ppt
+-- The same generated decryption circuits supply the compact widths' polynomial bounds.

+The raw depth computation uses binary wire indices, unary input count, and unary computed
+depths. A prefix of `k` gates has `n + k` depth entries, all at most `k`, so its full framed
+encoding has length at most `(n + k) * (2 * k + 1)`. This bound also holds on malformed code:
+missing arguments and unavailable wires read zero. Binary lookups cap the index before
+converting it to unary, so a large invalid index is charged only its binary encoded length.
+  the designated outputs, including their binary lookups.

+      (encPair encOp (encPair encUnary encUnary)) encUnary := by fun_prop
+  have hab : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : Op × ℕ × ℕ => max p.2.1 p.2.2 + 1)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The certificates follow the actual raw compiler: compute the depth table and selected-output
+maximum, then generate both microlevels at each depth. The input count and internal enumeration
+counters are unary; source wire references and emitted node references are binary. Every layer,
+node, delimiter and output selector is included in the output encoding.
+The construction is uniform in the input count, gate count and number of designated outputs.
+It is polynomial-time on all raw code, without a well-formedness or promised-depth hypothesis.
+  `computableTidilyInPolyTime_finishLayer`: generate the two microlevels of a depth.
+  the complete schedule and output selectors.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Section 6.1][AroraBarak09]
+/-- Decide whether a unary-numbered wire is already available, then emit its binary copy index. -/
+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_carry {depths : α → List ℕ} {level wire : α → ℕ}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => carry (depths a) (level a) (wire a)) input encNode :=
+/-- Prepare the first intermediate, retaining binary source references. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => prepareFirst (gate a)) input encNode := by
+  have harg (i : ℕ) : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (gate a).2.getD i 0)
+  apply finite_cases (branch := fun op a => prepareFirst (op, (gate a).2)) hgate.fst'
+/-- Prepare the second intermediate, retaining the binary source reference. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => prepareSecond (gate a)) input encNode := by
+  have harg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (gate a).2.getD 1 0) input encNat :=
+  apply finite_cases (branch := fun op a => prepareSecond (op, (gate a).2)) hgate.fst'
+  | const _ | not | and => exact const (Node.const false)
+/-- Finish a gate, computing scratch positions in unary before emitting binary indices. -/
+    {op : α → Op} (hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime inputCount input encUnary)
+      (fun a => finish (inputCount a) (gateCount a) (gateIndex a) (op a)) input encNode := by
+      (fun a => inputCount a + gateCount a + gateIndex a) input encNat :=
+      (fun a => inputCount a + 2 * gateCount a + gateIndex a) input encNat :=
+    (branch := fun op a => finish (inputCount a) (gateCount a) (gateIndex a) op) hop
+    simpa only [finish, Function.comp_def] using computableTidilyInPolyTime_nodeCopy.comp hfirst
+/-- Generate a preparation layer, charging the complete framed node list. -/
+    {gates : α → List (Op × List ℕ)} {depths : α → List ℕ}
+      (fun a => prepareLayer (inputCount a) (gates a) (depths a) (level a))
+      (fun p : α × ℕ => (gates p.1).getD p.2 (.const false, []))
+      (fun p : α × ℕ => decide ((depths p.1).getD (inputCount p.1 + p.2) 0 = level p.1))

+def frame (w : List Bool) : List Bool := w.flatMap (fun b => [true, b]) ++ [false]

+  fun _ _ h => by simpa only [List.length_replicate] using congrArg List.length h⟩

+A verifier with prover index type `ι` is a program `α → WordOracleComp ι Bool`, realized with a

-In Gentry's work, a public-key bit encryption scheme is **bootstrappable** when its homomorphic
-evaluation algorithm can evaluate the scheme's own augmented decryption circuits
-`Dec(·, c₁) op Dec(·, c₂)` (for each De Morgan gate `op`) on an encrypted secret key, producing
-refreshed ciphertexts whose length is bounded by a polynomial in the security parameter
-independently of the evaluated circuit's size and depth [Gentry2009].
-This module does **not** construct such a homomorphic evaluation of the decryption circuit, nor
-does it prove that any concrete scheme is bootstrappable. Instead, `Bootstrappable` is an
-**assumed interface**: an opaque deterministic polynomial-time gate-plus-key-switch operation
-`evalAugDecrypt op pk₂ ek c₁ c₂`, whose recryption/gate correctness and compactness are taken as
-fields of the class. From this interface (together with semantic or circular security, also
-assumed as hypotheses) this module and its submodules `KeyEncryption`, `KeyChain`, and
-`HomomorphicEval` prove Gentry's bootstrapping *composition*: chaining the assumed gate operations
-yields leveled, respectively fixed-key, fully homomorphic encryption.

+# Naor's bit commitment scheme from pseudorandom generators
+Naor's statistically binding, computationally hiding bit commitment scheme [Naor1991] commits to a
+bit `b : Bool` under a receiver string `r : List Bool` and a uniform seed `seed : List Bool` of
+`naorCommit generator r b seed` outputs `generator seed` when `b = false`, and
+* `Cslib.Crypto.naorCommit`: commit to a single bit using a generator, receiver string, and seed.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.naorCommitEnsemble`: the commitment distribution for a family of receiver strings
+* `Cslib.Crypto.NaorBinding`: statistical binding at seed length `n` for receiver string `r`,
+  requiring that no two seeds of length `n` open to `false` and `true` with the same commitment.
+  receiver string `r` of length `length n` that `NaorBinding generator n r` fails.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.BitCommitmentScheme`: a two-message statistically binding, computationally hiding
+  pseudorandom generator with expansion `fun n => 3 * n + 1`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.uniformList_map_naorCommit_id`: replacing the generator output with a uniform
+  word of length `m` makes the commitment distribution exactly `BitString.uniformList m` for
+  every receiver string `r` and committed bit `b`.
+  for deterministic polynomial-time families of receiver strings `r : ℕ → List Bool` and bit
+  families `b₀ b₁ : ℕ → Bool` (rather than a stateful randomized PPT malicious receiver whose
+  internal state passes to the distinguisher).
+  `Cslib.Crypto.negligible_naorBindingError`: statistical binding when `3 * n ≤ length n`.
+  `Cslib.Crypto.OneWay.exists_bitCommitmentScheme`: packaged Naor bit commitment scheme from a
+* [O. Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography: Volume 1, Basic Tools*][Goldreich2001],
+/-! ### Stretching a one-way function to `3 * n + 1` bits -/
+/-- Any one-way function yields a pseudorandom generator stretching `n` bits to `3 * n + 1` bits. -/
+  have htarget : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun n => 3 * n + 1) encUnary encUnary := by fun_prop
+  exact ⟨_, hg.amplify (fun n => 3 * n + 1) htarget (fun n => by lia)⟩
+/-- Naor's bit commitment: evaluate `generator seed`, and XOR with `r` when `b = true`. -/
+def naorCommit (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (r : List Bool) (b : Bool)
+  if b then BitString.listXor y.length [y, r] else y
+@[simp] theorem naorCommit_false (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (r seed : List Bool) :
+    naorCommit generator r false seed = generator seed := rfl
+@[simp] theorem naorCommit_true (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (r seed : List Bool) :
+/-- `naorCommit` factors through the identity generator `naorCommit id r b`. -/
+theorem naorCommit_eq_comp_id (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (r : List Bool) (b : Bool)
+    naorCommit generator r b seed = naorCommit id r b (generator seed) := rfl
+@[simp] theorem length_naorCommit (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (r : List Bool)
+    (naorCommit generator r b seed).length = (generator seed).length := by
+/-- Naor commitment is computable in polynomial time when its inputs are. -/
+    {generator : List Bool → List Bool} {r : α → List Bool} {b : α → Bool} {seed : α → List Bool}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => naorCommit generator (r a) (b a) (seed a))
+/-- Applying `naorCommit id r b` to a uniform `m`-bit word yields a uniform `m`-bit word for
+@[simp] theorem uniformList_map_naorCommit_id (m : ℕ) (r : List Bool) (b : Bool) :
+    (BitString.uniformList m).map (naorCommit id r b) = BitString.uniformList m := by
+      (fun y => BitString.listXor m [y, r]) ?_).trans (BitString.uniformList_map_listXor m r)
+/-- The commitment ensemble on a uniform `n`-bit seed for receiver string `r n` and bit `b n`. -/
+noncomputable def naorCommitEnsemble (generator : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (r : ℕ → List Bool) (b : ℕ → Bool) (n : ℕ) : PMF (List Bool) :=
+    (r : ℕ → List Bool) (b : ℕ → Bool) (n : ℕ) :
+      (generatorEnsemble generator n).map (naorCommit id (r n) (b n)) := by
+/-- For any polynomial-time receiver family `r` and bit family `b`, the Naor commitment ensemble
+is computationally indistinguishable from uniform words of length `length n`. -/
+    {generator : List Bool → List Bool} {length : ℕ → ℕ}
+      (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => naorCommit id (r p.1) (b p.1) p.2)
+  have hind := hG.indistinguishable.map (f := fun n y => naorCommit id (r n) (b n) y) hmap
+  simpa only [← naorCommitEnsemble_eq_map, uniformList_map_naorCommit_id] using hind
+/-- **Computational hiding of Naor bit commitment.** Commitments to any two deterministic
+polynomial-time bit families `b₀` and `b₁` under any deterministic polynomial-time receiver string
+family `r : ℕ → List Bool` are computationally indistinguishable against uniform strict PPT
+distinguishers (formulated over deterministic polynomial-time families `r, b₀, b₁`, rather than a
+stateful randomized PPT malicious receiver whose internal state passes to the distinguisher). -/
+    {generator : List Bool → List Bool} {length : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {r : ℕ → List Bool} {b₀ b₁ : ℕ → Bool}
+/-- A receiver string `r` is binding for seed length `n` if no two seeds of length `n` produce
+def NaorBinding (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (n : ℕ) (r : List Bool) : Prop :=
+  ∀ s₀ s₁ : List Bool, s₀.length = n → s₁.length = n →
+    naorCommit generator r false s₀ ≠ naorCommit generator r true s₁
+/-- Equivalence between `NaorBinding` on lists of length `n` and on `BitString n`. -/
+theorem naorBinding_iff_bitString (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (n : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
+          naorCommit generator r true (List.ofFn s₁) := by
+    exact h (List.ofFn s₀) (List.ofFn s₁) (by simp) (by simp)
+  · intro h s₀ s₁ hs₀ hs₁
+instance decidablePredNaorBinding (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (n : ℕ) :
+  fun r => decidable_of_iff' _ (naorBinding_iff_bitString generator n r)
+/-- If a commitment opened as `false` with `s₀` equals a commitment opened as `true` with `s₁`,
+then `s₀` and `s₁` must open to the same bit whenever `NaorBinding` holds. -/
+theorem NaorBinding.eq_of_naorCommit_eq {generator : List Bool → List Bool} {n : ℕ} {r : List Bool}
+    (hbind : NaorBinding generator n r) {b₀ b₁ : Bool} {s₀ s₁ : List Bool}
+    (heq : naorCommit generator r b₀ s₀ = naorCommit generator r b₁ s₁) : b₀ = b₁ := by
+  · exact False.elim (hbind s₀ s₁ hs₀ hs₁ heq)
+  · exact False.elim (hbind s₁ s₀ hs₁ hs₀ heq.symm)
+/-- The bad receiver string determined by a pair of seeds `(s₀, s₁)`. -/
+def naorBadShift (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (m n : ℕ)
+    (pair : BitString n × BitString n) : BitString m :=
+/-- If `NaorBinding generator n r` fails, then `ofList (length n) r` is the XOR of two generator
+    {length : ℕ → ℕ} (hlen : ∀ s, (generator s).length = length s.length)

+/-! ### PPT certificates for `runTwoRound` and honest interaction -/

+/-- Sample the GMW simulator's random strings and commitment seeds for a guessed challenge

+# Zero-knowledge simulation for the 3-copy GMW protocol
+This module proves that for any uniform strict oracle PPT malicious verifier `Vstar` and any
+deterministic polynomial-time families of instances `a : ℕ → α`, valid `ThreeSAT` witnesses
+`w : ℕ → List Bool` (`∀ n, ThreeSAT.verifier (f (a n), w n) = true`), and auxiliary inputs
+`z : ℕ → List Bool`, the output ensemble of `Vstar` interacting with the honest prover `gmwProver`
+is computationally indistinguishable from the output ensemble of the witness-free simulator
+The proof proceeds through four hybrids on `n + 1` independent challenge-guessing attempts:
+   Each attempt of `game0` guesses a uniform 3-bit challenge `ch_guess` in advance, answers the
+   second round using `ch_guess`, and outputs `true :: out` if the verifier's actual challenge
+   equals `ch_guess` (occurring with probability `1 / 8` independent of `out`), or `[]` otherwise.
+   Repeating `n + 1` times and taking `gmwFirstSuccess` differs from the real view with statistical
+   distance at most `(7 / 8) ^ (n + 1)`, which is negligible.
+   Using `eval_replicate_naorSelectPads`, we factor the `totalLen (f (a n))` commitment seeds into
+   independent active seeds and pseudorandom unopened pads without changing the distribution of each
+3. **Replacing pseudorandom unopened pads with uniform pads (`game0_indistinguishable_game1`).**
+   By `ComputationallyIndistinguishable.replicate_bind` applied to the shifted PRG ensemble
+   `hG.indistinguishable.shift 7`, replacing the `totalLen (f (a n))` pseudorandom unopened pads in
+   `game0Pads` by uniform `(length (n + 7))`-bit strings in `game1` is computationally
+   Once unopened commitment positions use uniform pads (`eval_replicate_map_naorCommitSplit`), the
+   commitment transcript depends on the committed bits only through `naorMaskBits openFlags bits`,
+   and for any satisfying witness `w n` (`naorMaskBits_realBits`) and uniform masks `m₀, m₁, m₂`
+   (`uniformList_bind_ite_listXor_three`), each attempt of `game1` is identically distributed to the
+  between the real interaction view of `Vstar` with `gmwProver` and `gmwSimulator`.
+* [O. Goldreich, S. Micali, A. Wigderson, *Proofs that Yield Nothing But Their Validity, or All
+  Languages in NP Have Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems*][GoldreichMicaliWigderson1991]
+* [O. Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography: Volume 1, Basic Tools*][Goldreich2001], Chapter 4.
+/-! ### Step 1: Replacing the verifier's challenge in `runTwoRound` by a random guess -/
+private theorem runTwoRound_query_inl {α β : Type} (reply1 reply2 : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (n : ℕ) (k : Fin (n + 1) → WordOracleComp Unit α) (s : ℕ × List Bool)
+    f <$> runTwoRound reply1 reply2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) s =
+      (ProbComp.unifFin n >>= fun u => f <$> runTwoRound reply1 reply2 (k u) s) := by
+    ProbOracleComp.handler, StateT.run_bind, StateT.run_lift, bind_assoc, pure_bind, map_bind]
+private theorem runTwoRound_query_inr {α β : Type} (reply1 reply2 : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (q : Unit × List Bool) (k : List Bool → WordOracleComp Unit α) (s : ℕ × List Bool)
+    f <$> runTwoRound reply1 reply2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) s =
+      let step := twoRoundStep reply1 reply2 q.2 s
+      f <$> runTwoRound reply1 reply2 (k step.1) step.2 := by
+private theorem length_snd_mem_support_runTwoRound {α : Type} (r1 r2 : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (prog : WordOracleComp Unit α) {s : ℕ × List Bool} (hs : s.2.length = 3)
+  induction prog using PFunctor.FreeM.induction generalizing s with
+    simp only [runTwoRound_pure, ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.support_pure, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp
+      have hq := runTwoRound_query_inl r1 r2 n k s id
+      change p ∈ (ProbComp.eval (runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) s)).support
+      have hq := runTwoRound_query_inr r1 r2 q k s id
+      change p ∈ (ProbComp.eval (runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) s)).support
+      have hstep : (twoRoundStep r1 r2 q.2 s).2.2.length = 3 := by
+private theorem runTwoRound_congr_reply1_of_one_le {α : Type} (r1 r1' r2 : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (prog : WordOracleComp Unit α) {s : ℕ × List Bool} (hs : 1 ≤ s.1) :
+    runTwoRound r1 r2 prog s = runTwoRound r1' r2 prog s := by
+  induction prog using PFunctor.FreeM.induction generalizing s with
+      have h1 := runTwoRound_query_inl r1 r2 n k s id
+      have h2 := runTwoRound_query_inl r1' r2 n k s id
+      change runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) s =
+        runTwoRound r1' r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) s
+      rw [h1, h2]; congr 1; funext u; exact ih u hs
+      have h1 := runTwoRound_query_inr r1 r2 q k s id
+      have h2 := runTwoRound_query_inr r1' r2 q k s id
+      change runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) s =
+        runTwoRound r1' r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) s
+      have hstep : twoRoundStep r1 r2 q.2 s = twoRoundStep r1' r2 q.2 s := by
+      have hs' : 1 ≤ (twoRoundStep r1' r2 q.2 s).2.1 := by
+private theorem eval_bind_runTwoRound_reply1 {α β : Type} (μ : ProbComp β)
+    (f₁ f₂ : β → List Bool → List Bool) (r2 : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (hf : ∀ r, ProbComp.eval ((fun b => f₁ b r) <$> μ) =
+      ProbComp.eval ((fun b => f₂ b r) <$> μ))
+    ProbComp.eval (μ >>= fun b => runTwoRound (f₁ b) r2 prog (0, ch₀)) =
+      ProbComp.eval (μ >>= fun b => runTwoRound (f₂ b) r2 prog (0, ch₀)) := by
+      have h1 (b : β) := runTwoRound_query_inl (f₁ b) r2 n k (0, ch₀) id
+      have h2 (b : β) := runTwoRound_query_inl (f₂ b) r2 n k (0, ch₀) id
+          runTwoRound (f₁ b) r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) (0, ch₀)) =
+          runTwoRound (f₂ b) r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) (0, ch₀))
+      have h1 (b : β) := runTwoRound_query_inr (f₁ b) r2 q k (0, ch₀) id
+      have h2 (b : β) := runTwoRound_query_inr (f₂ b) r2 q k (0, ch₀) id
+      simp only [id_map, twoRoundStep, beq_self_eq_true, ↓reduceIte] at h1 h2
+          runTwoRound (f₁ b) r2 (k (f₁ b q.2)) (1, ch₀) =
+          runTwoRound (f₂ b) r2 (k (f₂ b q.2)) (1, ch₀) =
+          runTwoRound (f₁ b) r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) (0, ch₀)) =
+          runTwoRound (f₂ b) r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) (0, ch₀))
+        (fun d => d.bind (fun ans => ProbComp.eval (runTwoRound (fun _ => []) r2 (k ans) (1, ch₀))))
+private theorem eval_runTwoRound_of_two_le (r1 r2 : List Bool → List Bool) (ch_guess : List Bool)
+    (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) {s : ℕ × List Bool}
+    ProbComp.eval ((fun p => if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []) <$>
+      runTwoRound r1 r2 prog s) = PMF.pure [] := by
+  induction prog using PFunctor.FreeM.induction generalizing s with
+      change ProbComp.eval (_ <$> runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) s) = _
+          ((fun p => if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []) <$>
+            runTwoRound r1 r2 (k u) s)) = fun _ => PMF.pure [] := by
+      change ProbComp.eval (_ <$> runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) s) = _
+      have hstep : twoRoundStep r1 r2 q.2 s = ([], s) := by
+private theorem eval_runTwoRound_guess (r1 r2 : List Bool → List Bool) (ch_guess : List Bool)
+    (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) (s : ℕ × List Bool) :
+    ProbComp.eval ((fun p => if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []) <$>
+    ProbComp.eval ((fun p => if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []) <$>
+      runTwoRound r1 (fun _ => r2 ch_guess) prog s) := by
+  induction prog using PFunctor.FreeM.induction generalizing s with
+      change ProbComp.eval (_ <$> runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) s) =
+        ProbComp.eval (_ <$> runTwoRound r1 _ (OracleComp.query (Sum.inl n) >>= k) s)
+      change ProbComp.eval (_ <$> runTwoRound r1 r2 (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) s) =
+        ProbComp.eval (_ <$> runTwoRound r1 _ (OracleComp.query (Sum.inr q) >>= k) s)
+        · have heq : BitString.listRow 3 0 q.2 = ch_guess := beq_iff_eq.mp hch
+            eval_runTwoRound_of_two_le r1 (fun _ => r2 ch_guess) ch_guess (k (r2 ch_guess))
+    (BitString.uniformList 3).map (fun ch_guess => if ch₀ == ch_guess then true :: out else []) =
+        (fun ch_guess => if [false, false, false] == ch_guess then true :: out else []) := by
+  have hzero : BitString.ofList 3 [false, false, false] = 0 := by
+  have hiff : (ch₀ = BitString.listXor 3 [u, ch₀]) ↔ ([false, false, false] = u) := by
+      have h1 := congrArg (fun l => BitString.ofList 3 l + BitString.ofList 3 ch₀) h
+      simp only [BitString.ofList_listXor_pair 3 u ch₀, add_assoc, BitString.add_self,
+      rw [← hzero, BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp), BitString.ofFn_ofList hu_len] at h2
+      have h1 : BitString.ofList 3 (BitString.listXor 3 [[false, false, false], ch₀]) =
+      rw [BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp), BitString.ofFn_ofList hch₀] at h2
+private theorem gmwFirstSuccess_cons (x : List Bool) (xs : List (List Bool)) :
+    gmwFirstSuccess (x :: xs) = if x.headD false then x.tail else gmwFirstSuccess xs := by
+/-- Single-attempt hybrid 0: guess a 3-bit challenge `ch_guess`, sample honest prover coins
+`(bits, seeds)`, run `prog` against `honestReply1` and `fun _ => honestReply2 ... ch_guess`, and
+return `true :: out` when the verifier's challenge equals `ch_guess`, or `[]` otherwise. -/
+private noncomputable def game0 (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (s m : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ)
+    (w : List Bool) (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) : ProbComp (List Bool) := do
+  let coins ← sampleHonestCoins s φ w
+  return if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []
+/-- Tag `out` with `true :: out` when a uniform 3-bit challenge equals `[false, false, false]`,
+private noncomputable def bernoulliAttempt (out : List Bool) : PMF (List Bool) :=
+    (fun ch_guess => if [false, false, false] == ch_guess then true :: out else [])
+/-- Choose `p` when a uniform 3-bit challenge equals `[false, false, false]`, and `q` otherwise. -/
+private noncomputable def mixThree {α : Type} (p q : PMF α) : PMF α :=
+    (fun ch_guess => if [false, false, false] == ch_guess then p else q)
+/-- Distribution of `gmwFirstSuccess` after `k` independent attempts from
+private noncomputable def repeatAttempt (μ : PMF (List Bool)) : ℕ → PMF (List Bool)
+private theorem eval_game0_eq_bind_bernoulliAttempt (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (s m : ℕ)
+    (φ : CNF ℕ) (w : List Bool) (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) :
+    ProbComp.eval (game0 generator s m φ w prog) =
+      (((gmwProver generator s m φ w).run prog
+        (gmwProver generator s m φ w).init).map Prod.fst).bind bernoulliAttempt := by
+  have hguess (ch_guess : List Bool) (coins : List Bool × List (List Bool)) :
+        return if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []) =
+        return if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []) := by
+  have hlen : p.2.2.length = 3 := length_snd_mem_support_runTwoRound _ _ prog rfl hp
+      (fun x => if x.headD false then PMF.pure x.tail else ν) = mixThree μ ν := by
+  simp only [bernoulliAttempt, mixThree, PMF.bind_bind, PMF.bind_map, Function.comp_def]
+  by_cases h : ([false, false, false] == ch_guess) = true
+  · have hfalse : ([false, false, false] == ch_guess) = false := Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr h
+    {μ : PMF (List Bool)} (hg : ProbComp.eval g = μ.bind bernoulliAttempt) (k : ℕ) :
+    ProbComp.eval (gmwFirstSuccess <$> OracleComp.replicate k g) = repeatAttempt μ k := by
+          (fun xs => if x.headD false then x.tail else gmwFirstSuccess xs) =
+        if x.headD false then PMF.pure x.tail else repeatAttempt μ k := by
+      mixThree (distinguishingGame p adv) (distinguishingGame q adv) := by
+    Game.advantage (mixThree g1 g2) g1 = (7 / 8 : ℝ≥0) * Game.advantage g2 g1 := by
+        (fun v => if v = 0 then g1 else g2) := by
+      have hi := congrArg (fun l => l.getD i.val false) h.symm
+  have hsucc : (Game.succProbability (mixThree g1 g2) : ℝ) - Game.succProbability g1 =
+      (7 / 8 : ℝ) * ((Game.succProbability g2 : ℝ) - Game.succProbability g1) := by
+        (Game.succProbability (if v = 0 then g1 else g2) : ℝ) =
+            if v = 0 then (Game.succProbability g1 : ℝ) - Game.succProbability g2 else 0 := by
+private theorem advantage_repeatAttempt_le (μ : PMF (List Bool)) (adv : List Bool → ProbComp Bool)
+    Game.advantage (distinguishingGame (repeatAttempt μ k) adv) (distinguishingGame μ adv) ≤
+    (s m : ℕ → ℕ) (φ : ℕ → CNF ℕ) (w : ℕ → List Bool)
+      (fun n => ((gmwProver generator (s n) (m n) (φ n) (w n)).run (prog n)
+        (gmwProver generator (s n) (m n) (φ n) (w n)).init).map Prod.fst)
+          (game0 generator (s n) (m n) (φ n) (w n) (prog n)))) := by
+    (eval_game0_eq_bind_bernoulliAttempt generator (s n) (m n) (φ n) (w n) (prog n)) (n + 1)]
+/-- Run one attempt with pre-sampled unopened pads `pads` and active flags
+private noncomputable def gameWithPads (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (s m : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ)
+    (w : List Bool) (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) (pads : List (List Bool)) :
+  let bits := realBits φ w m₀ m₁ m₂

+    (fun _ => proverReply2 s φ ch_guess bits seeds)
+  return if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []
+/-- Single-attempt hybrid with pseudorandom unopened pads. -/
+private noncomputable def game0Pads (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (s m : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ)
+    (w : List Bool) (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) : ProbComp (List Bool) :=
+    gameWithPads generator s m φ w prog
+/-- Single-attempt hybrid with uniform unopened pads. -/
+private noncomputable def game1 (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (s m : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ)
+    (w : List Bool) (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) : ProbComp (List Bool) :=
+    gameWithPads generator s m φ w prog
+    (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (s m : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) (w : List Bool)
+    ProbComp.eval (d_pads >>= gameWithPads generator s m φ w prog) =
+        let bits := realBits φ w m₀ m₁ m₂

+          (fun _ => proverReply2 s φ ch_guess bits seeds)
+        return if p.2.2 == ch_guess then true :: p.1 else []) := by
+private theorem proverReply1_eq_naorSelectPads (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (m : ℕ)
+    (r openFlags bits : List Bool) (seeds pads : List (List Bool)) :
+    proverReply1 generator m r openFlags bits seeds pads =
+      proverReply1 id m r (List.replicate bits.length false) bits []
+        (naorSelectPads generator openFlags bits seeds pads) := by
+private theorem eval_game0Pads_eq_eval_game0 (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (s m : ℕ)
+    (φ : CNF ℕ) (w : List Bool) (prog : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool)) :
+    ProbComp.eval (game0Pads generator s m φ w prog) =
+      ProbComp.eval (game0 generator s m φ w prog) := by

+      honestReply1 generator m φ (realBits φ w m₀ m₁ m₂, seeds) =
+        fun r => proverReply1 generator m r (List.replicate (totalLen φ) true)
+          (realBits φ w m₀ m₁ m₂) seeds [] := rfl
+/-! ### Step 3: Pseudorandom unopened pads to uniform unopened pads -/

+private theorem eval_game1_eq_eval_gmwSimAttempt (generator : List Bool → List Bool) {s m : ℕ}
+    {φ : CNF ℕ} {w : List Bool} (hw : ThreeSAT.verifier (φ, w) = true)

+  let simCont (ch_guess r₀ r₁ r₂ : List Bool) : PMF (List Bool) :=

+    dsimp only [simCont]; simp only [ProbComp.eval_bind]; congr 1; funext seeds

+            (fun r => proverReply1 generator m r openFlags (naorMaskBits openFlags bits) seeds pads)
