+# Computational zero-knowledge interactive proofs for NP
+Goldreich, Micali, and Wigderson [GoldreichMicaliWigderson1991] proved that if one-way functions
+exist, then every language in `NP` has a computational zero-knowledge interactive proof system.
+This module defines computational zero-knowledge interactive proofs (`ZeroKnowledgeProof`) and
+constructs such a proof system for `ThreeSAT` and hence for every language in `NP` via
+While the theorem that every language in `NP` has a computational zero-knowledge interactive proof
+system from one-way functions is due to Goldreich, Micali, and Wigderson
+[GoldreichMicaliWigderson1991] using Naor's commitment scheme [Naor1991], the concrete underlying
+`ThreeSAT` protocol formalized in `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.GMW` is a direct **3-copy
+masked-3SAT truth-table commitment protocol** rather than GMW's original 3-coloring protocol:
+each of 3 parallel copies commits to a random variable mask, the XOR-masked assignment, and the
+8-entry masked truth table of each clause, and a random 3-bit challenge selects for each copy
+whether to open the mask and full truth tables or the masked assignment and the active truth-table
+  quantifies over uniform strict oracle PPT malicious verifiers `Vstar` and deterministic
+  polynomial-time-generable families of instances `a : ℕ → α`, valid witnesses
+  `w : ℕ → List Bool` (`∀ n, isWitness (a n) (w n) = true`), and auxiliary inputs
+  `z : ℕ → List Bool` (`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime · encUnary _`), rather than non-uniformly over
+  arbitrary sequences `(x, w) ∈ R_L` and `z ∈ {0, 1}^*`. Fixed-instance zero-knowledge
+  (`ZeroKnowledgeProof.zero_knowledge_const`) is an immediate corollary for constant families
+  own polynomial-time witness predicate `isWitness : α → List Bool → Bool` characterizing `A`
+  (`mem_iff_exists_witness`). No witness-length bound is imposed, so `isWitness` by itself need not
+  be an `NP` relation; membership in `IP` (`mem_IP`) does not need one, and in `zero_knowledge`
+  the witness family `w : ℕ → List Bool` is polynomial-time-generable in `1^n`. In
+  `isWitness a w := ThreeSAT.verifier (f a, w)` checks a `ThreeSAT` witness for the Karp-reduced
+  formula `f a` rather than a witness for the original `NP` verifier of `A`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.ZeroKnowledgeProof`: a computational zero-knowledge interactive proof system for a
+  language `A`, bundling a uniform strict oracle PPT verifier, an honest prover with a uniform
+  strict PPT interaction realization, perfect completeness, soundness `1 / 3` against unbounded
+  provers, and uniform zero-knowledge with poly-time-generable auxiliary input.
+  systems for any language Karp-reducible to `ThreeSAT` and for `ThreeSAT` itself.
+  every language with a `ZeroKnowledgeProof` belongs to `IP`.
+  zero-knowledge for any fixed instance and valid witness.
+  generator with stretch at least `3 * k + 1` yields a computational zero-knowledge proof system
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWay.exists_zeroKnowledgeProof_of_mem_NP`: if a one-way function exists, every
+  language in `NP` has a computational zero-knowledge proof system.
+* [O. Goldreich, S. Micali, A. Wigderson, *Proofs that Yield Nothing But Their Validity, or All
+  Languages in NP Have Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems*][GoldreichMicaliWigderson1991]
+* [O. Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography: Volume 1, Basic Tools*][Goldreich2001], Chapter 4.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09], Chapter 9.
+/-- A computational zero-knowledge interactive proof system for a language `A : Set α` (with
+instance encoding `enc : α ↪ List Bool`), indexed by a security parameter `n : ℕ` [Goldreich,
+* `verifier n a`: the honest verifier's interactive program on security parameter `n` and
+  instance `a`, certified uniform strict oracle PPT in `(1^n, a)` by `isOraclePPT_verifier`.
+* `prover n a w`: the honest prover strategy on security parameter `n`, instance `a`, and
+* `isWitness a w`: the bundled polynomial-time witness predicate characterizing membership in `A`
+  (`mem_iff_exists_witness`). No witness-length bound is imposed, so `isWitness` by itself need
+  not be an `NP` relation (in `zero_knowledge`, `w` is polynomial-time-generable in `1^n`). When
+  constructed via a Karp reduction `f : α → CNF ℕ` to `ThreeSAT`
+  `isWitness a w` is `ThreeSAT.verifier (f a, w)`, checking a `ThreeSAT` witness for `f a`.
+* `complete` and `sound`: completeness `1` for valid witnesses and soundness error at most `1 / 3`
+  against all computationally unbounded stateful provers `P : Prover Unit`.
+* `zero_knowledge`: **uniform zero-knowledge with poly-time-generable auxiliary input**. For every
+  uniform strict oracle PPT malicious verifier `Vstar` (taking security parameter `n`, instance `a`,
+  and auxiliary input `z`), there is a uniform strict PPT simulator `S` (taking `(1^n, a, z)`
+  without any witness) whose output ensemble is computationally indistinguishable from the real
+  interaction output across all deterministic polynomial-time-generable families of instances
+  `a : ℕ → α`, valid witnesses `w : ℕ → List Bool`, and auxiliary inputs `z : ℕ → List Bool`
+structure ZeroKnowledgeProof {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (A : Set α) where
+  /-- The honest verifier, indexed by security parameter `n` and instance `a`. -/
+  verifier : ℕ → α → WordOracleComp Unit Bool
+  /-- The honest prover strategy, taking security parameter `n`, instance `a`, and witness `w`. -/
+  prover : ℕ → α → List Bool → Prover Unit
+  /-- The polynomial-time witness check used by the honest prover. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : α × List Bool => isWitness p.1 p.2)
+  /-- `a ∈ A` if and only if some witness `w` satisfies `isWitness a w = true`. -/
+  mem_iff_exists_witness : ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ ∃ w, isWitness a w = true
+  /-- The honest verifier is uniform strict oracle PPT in `(1^n, a)`. -/
+    IsOraclePPTOn (encPair encUnary enc) encBool (fun p : ℕ × α => verifier p.1 p.2)
+  /-- The PPT program realizing the honest prover's interaction with a verifier program. -/
+  interact : ℕ → α → List Bool → WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool) → ProbComp (List Bool)
+  /-- `interact` has the exact output distribution of `prover.run`. -/

+# Nonvacuity and axiom checks for PP truth-table and Boolean closure
+def headTrue : Set (List Bool) := {w | w.getD 0 false = true}
+def secondTrue : Set (List Bool) := {w | w.getD 1 false = true}
+  ⟨fun w => w.getD 0 false, by fun_prop, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+  ⟨fun w => w.getD 1 false, by fun_prop, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+def query (x : List Bool × ℕ) : List Bool := x.1.drop x.2
+def combine (x : List Bool × List Bool) : Bool :=
+theorem polyTime_count : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime count encBits encUnary := by
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime query (encPair encBits encUnary) encBits := by
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime combine (encPair encBits encBits) encBool := by
+  {w | combine (w, truthTableAnswers (query ⁻¹' headTrue) count w) = true}
+theorem reduction : PolyTimeTruthTableReducible encBits encBits language headTrue :=
+  ⟨count, query, combine, polyTime_count, polyTime_query, polyTime_combine, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+theorem joint_mem_PP : query ⁻¹' headTrue ∈ PP (encPair encBits encUnary) :=
+example : {w : List Bool | ∀ i < count w, (w, i) ∈ query ⁻¹' headTrue} ∈ PP encBits :=
+example : {w : List Bool | ∃ i < count w, (w, i) ∈ query ⁻¹' headTrue} ∈ PP encBits :=

+# Uniform AWPP weights for bounded oracle queries
+Amplify an AWPP numerator and pad its denominator to depend only on the original input.
+Truncating every query gives uniform bounds even on replay states containing longer words.

+  dyadic denominator and a polynomial-time unary denominator exponent.
+* [S. Fenner, *PP-Lowness and a Simple Definition of AWPP*][Fenner2003].
+/-- AWPP query numerators can have a common denominator depending only on the original input.
+Every query is truncated to the certified unary length cap, so the bounds hold for all words,
+including arbitrary words occurring in a replay state. The requested error exponent is also
+computed in unary and may be zero. -/

+    (hA : A ∈ AWPP encBits) {T e : α → ℕ}

+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime R enc encUnary ∧ ∀ a w,
+          (w.take (T a) ∈ A → (2 : ℤ) ^ e a * (D - H (a, w)) ≤ D) ∧
+          (w.take (T a) ∉ A → (2 : ℤ) ^ e a * H (a, w) ≤ D) := by
+  let query : α × List Bool → List Bool := fun x => x.2.take (T x.1)
+  have hquery : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime query (encPair enc encBits) encBits := by
+  have he' : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => e x.1)
+      (encPair enc encBits) encUnary := he.comp (.fst enc encBits)
+  let H₀ : α × List Bool → ℤ := fun x => AWPPAmplification.majorityPolynomial
+    (g (query x)) ((2 : ℤ) ^ p.eval (query x).length) (6 * e x.1)
+  have hH₀ : H₀ ∈ GapP (encPair enc encBits) := by
+  let padding : α × List Bool → ℕ := fun x =>
+  have hpadding : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime padding (encPair enc encBits) encUnary := by
+  have hpow : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => 2 ^ padding x)
+  let H : α × List Bool → ℤ := fun x => H₀ x * (2 : ℤ) ^ padding x
+  have hH : H ∈ GapP (encPair enc encBits) := by
+  refine ⟨H, hH, fun a => 12 * e a * p.eval (T a), by fun_prop, fun a w => ?_⟩
+  simp only [encBits_apply] at hb hy hn
+  let d : ℤ := 2 ^ (2 * (6 * e a) * p.eval (query (a, w)).length)

+  change (0 ≤ H₀ (a, w) * P ∧ H₀ (a, w) * P ≤ _) ∧ _

+          ((2 : ℤ) ^ e a * (d - H₀ (a, w))) * P := by ring
+    change (2 : ℤ) ^ e a * (H₀ (a, w) * P) ≤ d * P

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# GapP weights for finite oracle replay
+An instruction-indexed transcript supplies a Boolean reply at each machine instruction. Query
+instructions use a GapP numerator, while local instructions assign zero weight to `true`.
+Each pair of branch weights sums to `2 ^ R(a)`. Summing the accepting transcript products gives
+an ordinary GapP function by uniform indexed products and uniform Boolean sums.

+# Polynomial-space Mathlib stack machines decide problems in PSPACE
+The source certificate supplies termination and a Boolean answer. A polynomial bound on every
+reachable source stack gives a tidy polynomial-space computation, then membership in `PSPACE`.
+The source runtime need not be polynomially bounded. Input and output words use the bridge's
+standard finite-symbol encodings; the final Boolean answer is recoded to `encBool`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.mem_PSPACE_of_tm2`: a terminating Mathlib TM2 decider with polynomially
+  bounded stacks decides a problem in `PSPACE`.
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, Section 8.1][Sipser2013]
+/-- A terminating finite-alphabet Mathlib stack-machine decider with polynomially bounded
+stacks decides a problem in `PSPACE`, under the standard binary input-word encoding. -/

+    {ea : α → List αΓ} {eb : Bool → List βΓ} {f : α → Bool} {A : Set α}

+# From Mathlib TM2 computations to CSLib polynomial time
+Mathlib counts one fixed stack-machine statement per transition. The simulation certifies each
+statement using CSLib's list and finite-table calculus, then iterates it for the source polynomial
+clock. Encoded configurations have linear growth in source time. The resulting certificate is for
+an actual tidy binary multi-tape Turing machine, with polynomial time and space.
+Input and output words use `encList (encFinite _)`. Their alphabets may differ or be empty.
+Typed encoders must be injective, as required by CSLib. Every working alphabet must be finite;
+Mathlib's `FinTM2` alone only guarantees finiteness of the input alphabet.
+This is a polynomial-time bridge, not a space-preserving simulation or a converse equivalence.
+The source model and runtime convention are Mathlib's
+`Mathlib.Computability.TuringMachine.StackTuringMachine`. This is a direct proof through the
+tidy calculus, independent of the TM2-to-TM0 compiler in
+/-- A source clock may continue after halting without changing the result. -/
+theorem stepTotal_of_step {K : Type} [DecidableEq K] {Γ : K → Type} {Λ σ : Type}
+    (M : Λ → Stmt Γ Λ σ) (cfg : Cfg Γ Λ σ) :
+    stepTotal M cfg = (step M cfg).getD cfg := by
+  cases cfg with | mk label v store => cases label <;> rfl
+private theorem iterate_bind_none {α : Type} (f : α → Option α) (n : ℕ) :
+    (fun value : Option α => value.bind f)^[n] none = none := by
+  | succ n ih => simp only [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, Option.bind_none]
+private theorem iterate_getD_of_bind {α : Type} (f : α → Option α) (n : ℕ) (a b : α)
+    (h : (fun value : Option α => value.bind f)^[n] (some a) = some b) :
+    (fun value => (f value).getD value)^[n] a = b := by
+    | none => rw [hf, iterate_bind_none] at h; contradiction
+    | some c => simpa only [hf, Option.getD_some] using ih c (by simpa only [hf] using h)
+/-- Bounded partial execution to a halted configuration agrees with the padded total clock. -/
+    (stepTotal tm.m)^[time] (initList tm input) = haltList tm output := by
+  have hexact : (stepTotal tm.m)^[h.steps] (initList tm input) = haltList tm output := by
+    rw [show stepTotal tm.m = (fun cfg => (tm.step cfg).getD cfg) from
+  have hhalt : stepTotal tm.m (haltList tm output) = haltList tm output := rfl
+/-- Initialization copies the source input and supplies empty auxiliary stacks. -/
+/-- Polynomially many source steps have polynomially bounded encoded intermediate states. -/
+theorem run_polyTime (tm : FinTM2) [∀ k, Finite (tm.Γ k)] (p : Polynomial ℕ) :
+  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := length_encCfg_le (Γ := tm.Γ) (Λ := tm.Λ) (σ := tm.σ)

+    {ea : α → List αΓ} {eb : β → List βΓ} {f : α → β}
+    (h : TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea eb f) [∀ k, Finite (h.tm.Γ k)]

+  have hout := (dpi_apply (fun k => encList (encFinite (h.tm.Γ k))) h.tm.k₁).comp hstacks

+# Polynomial-time simulation of one Mathlib TM2 step
+The simulator operates on Mathlib's configurations themselves. Finite functions in a source
+statement are finite case analyses; stack operations reuse the certified list and table calculus.
+Halting configurations remain fixed, so a clock may safely run beyond the source's halting time.
+* `Turing.TM2.stepTotal`: a TM2 step that stays put after halting.
+* `Turing.TM2.stepTotal_polyTime`: one fixed source transition is polynomial-time in the complete
+* `Turing.TM2.stepTotal_stack_bound`: a fixed source transition adds at most a constant number

+    (fun cfg : Cfg Γ Λ σ => (cfg.l, cfg.var, cfg.stk)) encCfg
+/-- Reading the source label is efficient. -/
+    (Cfg.l (Γ := Γ) (Λ := Λ) (σ := σ)) encCfg (encFinite (Option Λ)) := cfg_parts.fst'
+/-- Reading the finite register state is efficient. -/
+    (Cfg.var (Γ := Γ) (Λ := Λ) (σ := σ)) encCfg (encFinite σ) := cfg_parts.snd'.fst'
+/-- Reading the complete stack family is efficient. -/
+/-- Construct a configuration while charging all retained storage. -/
+@[fun_prop] theorem cfg_mk {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {label : α → Option Λ} {state : α → σ} {store : α → ∀ k, List (Γ k)}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Cfg.mk (label a) (state a) (store a)) input encCfg :=
+private theorem map_head {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {state : α → σ} {store : α → ∀ k, List (Γ k)}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => f (state a) (store a k).head?) input (encFinite σ) := by
+  exact (of_finite (fun p : σ × Option (Γ k) => f p.1 p.2)).comp (hv.prod hhead)
+private theorem stepAux_with {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} (q : Stmt Γ Λ σ)
+    {state : α → σ} {store : α → ∀ k, List (Γ k)}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => stepAux q (state a) (store a)) input encCfg := by
+  induction q generalizing state store with
+    have hsymbol := (of_finite f (encB := encFinite (Γ k))).comp hv
+    have hstack := (dpi_apply (fun k => encList (encFinite (Γ k))) k).comp hs
+  | peek k f q ih => exact ih (map_head hv hs k f) hs
+    have hstack := (dpi_apply (fun k => encList (encFinite (Γ k))) k).comp hs
+    exact ih (map_head hv hs k f) (dpi_update hs ((listTail _).comp hstack))
+  | load f q ih => exact ih ((of_finite f).comp hv) hs
+  | branch f q₁ q₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
+    refine (((of_finite f).comp hv).cond (ih₁ hv hs) (ih₂ hv hs)).of_enc_eq ?_
+    cases hf : f (state a) <;> simp [stepAux, hf]
+  | goto f => exact cfg_mk ((of_finite (fun v => some (f v))).comp hv) hv hs
+  | halt => exact cfg_mk (const none) hv hs
+/-- Executing a fixed statement is efficient, including its straight-line continuations. -/
+theorem stepAux_polyTime (q : Stmt Γ Λ σ) : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun cfg : Cfg Γ Λ σ => stepAux q cfg.var cfg.stk) encCfg encCfg :=
+  stepAux_with q (cfg_var (Γ := Γ) (Λ := Λ)) (cfg_stacks (Γ := Γ) (Λ := Λ))
+/-- Execute one source step, keeping the last configuration after halting. -/
+def stepTotal (M : Λ → Stmt Γ Λ σ) (cfg : Cfg Γ Λ σ) : Cfg Γ Λ σ :=
+  cfg.l.elim cfg (fun l => stepAux (M l) cfg.var cfg.stk)
+/-- The finite label chooses a fixed certified statement. -/
+theorem stepTotal_polyTime (M : Λ → Stmt Γ Λ σ) :
+    (branch := fun label (cfg : Cfg Γ Λ σ) =>
+      label.elim cfg (fun l => stepAux (M l) cfg.var cfg.stk)) fun label => by
+/-- A syntactic bound on the number of pushes along any path through a statement. -/
+def pushBound : Stmt Γ Λ σ → ℕ
+omit [Fintype K] [Finite Λ] [Finite σ] [∀ k, Finite (Γ k)] in
+/-- Only pushes can increase stack lengths. -/
+theorem stepAux_stack_bound (q : Stmt Γ Λ σ) (v : σ) (store : ∀ k, List (Γ k))
+    ∀ k, ((stepAux q v store).stk k).length ≤ bound + pushBound q := by
+  induction q generalizing v store bound with
+    have hupdate (k : K) : (Function.update store j (f v :: store j) k).length ≤ bound + 1 := by
+      · subst k; simpa using Nat.add_le_add_right (h j) 1
+      · simpa only [Function.update_of_ne hk] using (h k).trans (Nat.le_add_right bound 1)
+    simpa only [stepAux, pushBound, Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm 1] using
+  | peek j f q ih => exact ih _ _ bound h
+    · simpa only [Function.update_of_ne hk] using h k
+  | load f q ih => exact ih _ _ bound h
+  | branch f q₁ q₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>

+        (ih₁ v store bound h k).trans (Nat.add_le_add_left (Nat.le_max_left _ _) bound)
+omit [Fintype K] [Finite σ] [∀ k, Finite (Γ k)] in
+/-- A fixed finite program has a uniform per-transition stack-growth constant. -/

+    ∀ (cfg : Cfg Γ Λ σ) (bound : ℕ), (∀ k, (cfg.stk k).length ≤ bound) →

+# Acyclic key-chain generation and leveled semantic security
+This module defines acyclic evaluation key chains (`Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.EvalChain`),
+leveled public keys (`Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.LeveledPK`), and leveled key generation
+(`Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.leveledKeyGen`), and proves that any semantically secure
+public-key bit encryption scheme `S` and any unary polynomial-time depth bound `D : ℕ → ℕ` yield a
+semantically secure leveled key chain of length `D n`
+  acyclic evaluation key chains and leveled public keys.
+  real and all-zero dummy evaluation key-chain generators.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.LeveledSemanticSecure`: semantic security in the presence of an
+  evaluation key chain of length `D n`.
+  `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.isPPTOn_leveledKeyGen`: uniform strict PPT certificates for real
+  replacing the real key chain with the all-dummy key chain.
+  acyclic key chain of length `D n` from base semantic security alone.
+* [C. Gentry, *Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices*][Gentry2009]
+/-! ### Acyclic key-chain generation and leveled semantic security -/

+/-- Framed encoding of a leveled public key. -/

+leveled public key, and a challenge ciphertext. -/

+/-- Uniform strict polynomial-time admissibility for leveled public-key distinguishers. -/

+/-- One step of real key-chain generation at security parameter `n`: sample a fresh key pair
+`(pk, sk)`, encrypt the current secret key (truncated to `skLength n` so that state growth is
+uniformly bounded on all inputs) under `pk`, and append `(pk, ek)` to the chain. -/

+/-- Generate `r` real evaluation-key levels starting from initial secret key `sk₀`. -/
+noncomputable def genRealChain (S : EncryptionScheme) (n r : ℕ) (sk₀ : List Bool) :
+    S.genRealChain n 0 sk₀ = pure ([], sk₀) := rfl
+theorem genRealChain_succ (S : EncryptionScheme) (n r : ℕ) (sk₀ : List Bool) :
+    S.genRealChain n (r + 1) sk₀ = S.genRealChain n r sk₀ >>= S.genRealStep n := rfl
+/-- Real key-chain generation is uniformly strict PPT in the security parameter, chain length,
+      (fun p => S.genRealChain p.1.1 p.1.2 p.2) := by
+    (count := fun p : (ℕ × ℕ) × List Bool => p.1.2)

+  simp only [encEvalChain, length_encPair, encBits_apply, encList_append, encList_cons,

+/-- Every supported result of `genRealChain n r keys₀.2` has a final secret key coming from a

+/-- Every supported result of `genRealChain n r keys₀.2` has final secret key length

+/-- One dummy evaluation-key level: sample `(pk, sk) ← S.keyGen n` and encrypt the all-zero

+/-- Semantic security of the leveled FHE scheme with depth bound `D : ℕ → ℕ`: no uniform strict PPT
+distinguisher can distinguish encryptions of `false` from encryptions of `true` even given the

+    (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (S.leveledEncryptGame (D n) true n >>= adversary n))
+/-- Hybrid distribution `k` (`0 ≤ k ≤ L`) for the leveled key chain: the first `L - k` evaluation

+noncomputable def leveledHybrid (S : EncryptionScheme) (L : ℕ) (b : Bool) (n k : ℕ) :
+  let res ← S.genRealChain n (L - k) keys₀.2

+/-- Prefix sampled at outer hybrid level `k < L`: samples `(pk_0, sk_0)` and the first `L - 1 - k`
+noncomputable def leveledPrefix (S : EncryptionScheme) (L n k : ℕ) :
+    ProbComp (List Bool × EvalChain × List Bool) := do

+    {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {L n k : γ → ℕ}

+/-- Suffix continuation at outer hybrid level `k < L`: given the prefix `(pk_0, realChain, sk_r)`
+and the critical level `(pk, ek)`, samples `k` dummy evaluation keys and the challenge ciphertext
+    (b : Bool) (n k : ℕ) (ctx : List Bool × EvalChain × List Bool)
+    (pk : List Bool) (ek : List (List Bool)) : ProbComp Bool := do
+  adversary n ((ctx.1, ctx.2.1 ++ (pk, ek) :: dummy), c)

+theorem eval_leveledPrefix_real (S : EncryptionScheme) (L : ℕ) (b : Bool) (n k : ℕ)
+      let ctx ← S.leveledPrefix L n k
+      S.leveledSuffix adversary b n k ctx keys.1 ek) =
+    ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid L b n k >>= adversary n) := by

+  simp [leveledPrefix, leveledSuffix, leveledHybrid, hsub, genRealChain_succ, genRealStep,
+theorem eval_leveledPrefix_dummy (S : EncryptionScheme) (L : ℕ) (b : Bool) (n k : ℕ)
+      let ctx ← S.leveledPrefix L n k
+      let ek ← S.encryptKey keys.1 (List.replicate (S.skLength n) false)
+      S.leveledSuffix adversary b n k ctx keys.1 ek) =
+    ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid L b n (k + 1) >>= adversary n) := by
+  have hsub : L - (k + 1) = L - 1 - k := by omega
+  simp [leveledPrefix, leveledSuffix, leveledHybrid, hsub, genDummyChain, OracleComp.replicate_succ,
+/-- Single-level test at outer hybrid index `k`: runs `encryptKeyTest` on `leveledPrefix` and
+    (L : ℕ) (b : Bool) (n k : ℕ) (challenge : List Bool × List Bool) : ProbComp Bool :=
+    (L : ℕ) (b : Bool) (n k : ℕ) (hk : k < L) :
+    (Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid L b n k >>= adversary n)) : ℝ) -
+      Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid L b n (k + 1) >>= adversary n)) =
+            S.leveledLevelTest adversary L b n k)) : ℝ) -
+            S.leveledLevelTest adversary L b n k))) := by
+  have h := S.encryptKeyTest_gap n (S.leveledPrefix L n k)
+  simpa only [S.eval_leveledPrefix_real L b n k hk adversary,
+    S.eval_leveledPrefix_dummy L b n k adversary] using h
+/-- Uniform two-level hybrid reduction replacing the real key chain of length `D n` with the
+all-dummy key chain: samples a level `k ← sampleDyadicIndex (D n)` and runs `leveledLevelTest`. -/
+noncomputable def leveledChainReduction (S : EncryptionScheme) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (b : Bool)
+    (adversary : LeveledDistinguisher) : PKDistinguisher := fun n challenge => do
+  if k < D n then S.leveledLevelTest adversary (D n) b n k challenge else pure false
+      IsPPTOn (encPair (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits encBits)) encUnary) encBool
+        (fun p => S.leveledLevelTest adversary (D p.1.1) b p.1.1 p.2 p.1.2) := by
+    exact S.isPPTOn_encryptKeyTest (by ppt) (by polytime) (by ppt) (by polytime) (by polytime)
+        (ProbComp.eval (S.leveledEncryptGame (D n) b n >>= adversary n)) : ℝ) -
+        (ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid (D n) b n (D n) >>= adversary n)) =
+            S.leveledChainReduction D b adversary n)) : ℝ) -
+            S.leveledChainReduction D b adversary n))) := by
+    (fun k => ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid (D n) b n k >>= adversary n))
+    (fun k => ProbComp.eval (S.encryptGame true n >>= S.leveledLevelTest adversary (D n) b n k))
+    (fun k => ProbComp.eval (S.encryptGame false n >>= S.leveledLevelTest adversary (D n) b n k))
+    (fun k hk => S.leveledLevelTest_gap adversary (D n) b n k hk)

+        ProbComp.eval (S.leveledEncryptGame (D n) b n >>= adversary n) := by

+/-- Reduction from the all-dummy hybrid game (`k = D n`) to single-bit semantic security on

+      ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid (D n) b n (D n) >>= adversary n) := by

+/-- **Leveled semantic security from base semantic security**: if `S` is semantically secure and

+        (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (S.leveledEncryptGame (D n) b n >>= adversary n))

+        (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (S.leveledHybrid (D n) true n (D n) >>= adversary n))

+# Public-key bit encryption and bit-by-bit key encryption
+This module defines uniform public-key bit encryption schemes (`Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme`),
+`isPPTOn_encryptKeyTest`) replacing an encrypted secret key with an encryption of `0^m`
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme`: uniform public-key bit encryption scheme with tidy efficiency
+  and correctness on the support of `keyGen`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.SemanticSecure`: semantic security against uniform strict PPT
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.encryptKey`: bit-by-bit encryption of a secret key word.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.encryptKeyTest`: single-challenge hybrid test for replacing an
+  encrypted secret key with an encryption of `0^m`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.encryptKeyTest_gap`: exact signed hybrid gap for replacing an
+  encrypted secret key with an encryption of `0^m`.
+* [C. Gentry, *Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices*][Gentry2009]
+/-- A distinguisher for a public-key bit encryption scheme receives the unary security parameter,
+a public key, and a challenge ciphertext. -/
+abbrev PKDistinguisher := ℕ → List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp Bool
+/-- Uniform strict polynomial-time admissibility for public-key distinguishers. -/
+  IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool (fun p => adversary p.1 p.2)
+/-- A uniform public-key bit encryption scheme with tidy polynomial-time key generation, encryption,
+and deterministic decryption, fixed secret-key bit length `skLength n` at security parameter `n`,
+and perfect decryption correctness on supported key pairs and ciphertexts. -/
+  /-- Sample a public/secret key pair `(pk, sk)` at unary security parameter `n`. -/
+  keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)
+  /-- Encrypt a single bit `b` under public key `pk`. -/
+  encrypt : List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)
+  /-- Deterministically decrypt a ciphertext `c` using secret key `sk`. -/
+  decrypt : List Bool → List Bool → Bool
+  /-- Bit length of secret keys generated at security parameter `n`. -/
+  /-- Key generation is uniformly strict PPT in the unary parameter. -/
+  keyGen_ppt : IsPPTOn encUnary (encPair encBits encBits) keyGen
+  /-- Encryption is uniformly strict PPT in the public key and plaintext bit. -/
+  encrypt_ppt : IsPPTOn (encPair encBits encBool) encBits (fun p => encrypt p.1 p.2)
+  /-- Decryption is computable tidily in polynomial time. -/
+    (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => decrypt p.1 p.2) (encPair encBits encBits) encBool
+  /-- The secret-key length function is computable tidily in polynomial time in unary. -/
+  /-- Every secret key sampled at parameter `n` has length `skLength n`. -/
+  length_sk : ∀ n keys, keys ∈ (ProbComp.eval (keyGen n)).support → keys.2.length = skLength n
+  /-- Decryption recovers the encrypted bit for every supported key pair and ciphertext. -/
+    ∀ b c, c ∈ (ProbComp.eval (encrypt keys.1 b)).support → decrypt keys.2 c = b
+theorem isPPTOn_keyGen_comp (S : EncryptionScheme) {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {n : γ → ℕ} (hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime n encIn encUnary) :
+    IsPPTOn encIn (encPair encBits encBits) (fun a => S.keyGen (n a)) :=
+theorem isPPTOn_encrypt_comp (S : EncryptionScheme) {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    IsPPTOn encIn encBits (fun a => S.encrypt (pk a) (b a)) :=
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {sk c : γ → List Bool}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => S.decrypt (sk a) (c a)) encIn encBool :=
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {n : γ → ℕ}

+/-- Sample a key pair and encrypt the challenge bit `b` under the public key. -/

+distinguisher can distinguish encryptions of `false` from encryptions of `true`. -/
+    (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (S.encryptGame false n >>= adversary n))
+    (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (S.encryptGame true n >>= adversary n))
+/-- Encrypt a bit string `msg` bit-by-bit under public key `pk`. Used to produce evaluation keys

+/-- Encrypting a concatenated bit string is equivalent in distribution to encrypting both halves
+independently and concatenating the resulting ciphertext lists. -/

+/-- Every ciphertext list in the support of `encryptKey pk msg` has the same length as `msg`. -/

+    simp only [encryptKey_nil, ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.support_pure, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hcs

+/-- Decrypting each ciphertext in `encryptKey keys.1 msg` under `keys.2` recovers `msg`. -/

+    simp [S.decrypt_encrypt n keys hkeys b c hc, ih hcs']
+/-- One step of iterative bit-by-bit encryption, consuming the head of the remaining plaintext bits
+and appending its encryption to the accumulated ciphertext list. -/
+    (state : List Bool × List (List Bool)) : ProbComp (List Bool × List (List Bool)) := do
+      (fun cs => acc ++ cs) <$> S.encryptKey pk msg := by
+      List.tail_cons, bind_assoc, pure_bind, map_bind, ih, encryptKey_cons]

+theorem encryptKey_eq_iterate (S : EncryptionScheme) (pk : List Bool) (msg : List Bool) :
+/-- Bit-by-bit key encryption is uniformly strict PPT in the public key and message bit string. -/
+    IsPPTOn (encPair encBits encBits) (encList encBits) (fun p => S.encryptKey p.1 p.2) := by
+  have heq : (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => S.encryptKey p.1 p.2) =
+      fun p => Prod.snd <$> OracleComp.iterate p.2.length (S.encryptKeyStep p.1) (p.2, []) := by
+  have hiter : IsPPTOn (encPair encBits encBits) (encPair encBits (encList encBits))
+      (count := fun p : List Bool × List Bool => p.2.length)
+      (initial := fun p : List Bool × List Bool => (p.2, []))
+      (step := fun (p : List Bool × List Bool) state => S.encryptKeyStep p.1 state)
+      (growth := fun p : List Bool × List Bool =>
+        (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => 2 * (k * (2 * p.1.length + 4) ^ d) + 2)
+    have hc_bound := hlen (p.1, state.1.headD false) c hc
+    have hpair_len : (encPair encBits encBool (p.1, state.1.headD false)).length + 1 ≤
+    have hc_le : c.length ≤ k * (2 * p.1.length + 4) ^ d := by
+    have htail : state.1.tail.length ≤ state.1.length := by simp

+1. `copyInputToWork`: copy the read-only input `x` onto work tape `0` and rewind work tape `0` to
+2. `runOnWork`: execute the single-tape transitions of `tm` directly on work tape `0`. By
+   `BiTape.Represents.step`, `n` steps of `tm` correspond to `n` steps of `runOnWork tm`.
+3. `emitWork`: starting from the final head position on work tape `0`, walk right and emit each

+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.copyInputToWork`: copy the input tape to work tape `0` and rewind to `0`.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.emitWork`: emit the word on work tape `0` to the output tape until blank.
+  `ofSingleTapeTM tm` computes `y` from `x` in `2 * x.length + 4 + (t + (y.length + 1))` steps
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]

+        ⟨none, p', fun _ => tapeOfList x, fun _ => 0, []⟩ := by
+    refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ rfl rfl
+  have hp₀ : ((1 : Fin (x.length + 2)) : ℕ) ≠ 0 := by omega
+  have happ := transformsTapesAt_appendRead (copyReader Symbol) (0 : Fin 1) x 1 hp₀ []
+  rcases happ with ⟨p', ws', e, hrun, ⟨-, hws', he⟩, -⟩
+    simp only [copyReader_q₀, Nat.sub_self, List.drop_zero, copyReader_read, List.length_nil,
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ rfl rfl

+# Polynomial identity testing, the Schwartz–Zippel lemma and Kabanets–Impagliazzo
+*Polynomial identity testing* (`PIT`) asks whether a given arithmetic circuit computes the zero
+formal polynomial. Over the integers, `Cslib.Circuits.Arithmetic.PITInt` is the set of pairs
+`⟨n, c⟩ : Σ n, Circuit (arithSignature ℤ) n 1` with `c.polynomial 0 = 0` in
+`MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ`, encoded as bit strings by `Cslib.Circuits.Arithmetic.encArithCircuitInt`
+(number of inputs in unary, gate operations with binary integer constants via `encIntBin`, and
+This file develops three components connecting polynomial identity testing, randomized zero testing
+   [DeMillo and Lipton][DeMilloLipton1978], [Arora and Barak, Lemma 7.22][AroraBarak09]: over any
+   integral domain `R`, a nonzero polynomial `P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R` of total degree `d` has
+   at most `d * #S ^ (n - 1)` roots in `S ^ n` (`MvPolynomial.card_roots_le`), and if `d < #S`
+   then `P` evaluates to a nonzero element at some point of `S ^ n`
+   bounds the zero set of any arithmetic circuit outside `PITInt`
+2. **Laplace cofactor expansion of the permanent and downward self-reducibility to `PITInt`**
+   [Arora and Barak, Theorem 20.16][AroraBarak09]: for any `(n + 1) × (n + 1)` matrix `A`,
+   (`Matrix.permanent_succ_row_zero`). On the generic matrix `genericMatrix R (m + 1)`, each minor
+   is a variable reindexing of `genericMatrix R m` (`permanent_genericMatrix_succ`). Using explicit
+   circuit `permBaseDiff` and the Laplace step test circuit `permStepDiff` with explicit polynomial
+   `C : ∀ m, Circuit (arithSignature ℤ) (m * m) 1` computes `(genericMatrix ℤ m).permanent` for all
+   `m ≤ n` if and only if `⟨0, permBaseDiff (C 0)⟩ ∈ PITInt` and
+   `⟨(m + 1) * (m + 1), permStepDiff m (C m) (C (m + 1))⟩ ∈ PITInt` for all `m < n`
+   integer permanent family `intPermFamily` lies in `VP ℤ`, a polynomial-time decider for `PITInt`
+   soundly and completely certifies permanent circuit chains
+3. **`NEXP` circuit lower bounds and the Kabanets–Impagliazzo theorem**
+   - Unconditionally, combining Kannan's theorem (`exists_mem_SigmaP_two_notMem_SIZE`) with the
+     inclusion `Σ₂ ⊆ PH ⊆ PSPACE ⊆ EXP ⊆ NEXP` (`SigmaP_subset_NEXP`) shows that for every fixed
+     degree `k`, `NEXP` contains a language outside `SIZE (c (n + 1) ^ k)`
+   - Conditionally on `PITInt ∈ P encArithCircuitInt` and the Impagliazzo–Kabanets–Wigderson /
+     Valiant–Toda collapse from a polynomial-time PIT-certified permanent circuit family under
+     `NEXP ⊆ P/poly`, either `NEXP ⊄ P/poly` or `intPermFamily ∉ VP ℤ`
+     (combining `#P`-completeness of the permanent with the easy-witness collapse
+     `NEXP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ NEXP = MA`) is taken as an explicit hypothesis.
+  injective bit-string encoding of single-output integer arithmetic circuits.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Arithmetic.PITInt`: the Polynomial Identity Testing problem over `ℤ`.
+  family `n ↦ (genericMatrix R n).permanent` and its integer specialization.
+  `IsLaplacePermChain`: the Laplace cofactor difference circuits, explicit recursive permanent
+  circuit family, and Laplace permanent chain predicate reducing permanent verification to `PITInt`.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Arithmetic.PermPITCertified`: existence of a polynomial-time `PITInt` decider and
+  a polynomially bounded arithmetic circuit family certified by it on all Laplace permanent
+  of the permanent along column 0 and row 0.
+  Lemma 4.2, characterizing permanent circuits up to dimension `n` via `n + 1` instances of
+  `PITInt ∈ P` and `intPermFamily ∈ VP ℤ` yield a `PermPITCertified` permanent tester.
+* [V. Kabanets, R. Impagliazzo, *Derandomizing polynomial identity tests means proving circuit
+* [J. T. Schwartz, *Fast probabilistic algorithms for verification of polynomial
+* [R. A. DeMillo, R. J. Lipton, *A probabilistic remark on algebraic program
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Lemma 7.22 and
+[Arora and Barak, Lemma 7.22][AroraBarak09]: for a nonzero polynomial `P` in `n` variables over an
+integral domain `R` and a finite subset `S ⊆ R`, the number of roots of `P` in `S ^ n` multiplied
+theorem card_mul_card_roots_le [DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R}
+    S.card * #(piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) |>.filter (fun x => eval x P = 0)) ≤
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos S.card with hcard | hcard
+    have hSpos : (0 : ℚ≥0) < S.card := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hcard
+    have hSnpos : (0 : ℚ≥0) < (S.card : ℚ≥0) ^ n := pow_pos hSpos n
+    rw [div_le_div_iff₀ hSnpos hSpos, mul_comm _ (S.card : ℚ≥0)] at hq
+[DeMillo and Lipton][DeMilloLipton1978], [Arora and Barak, Lemma 7.22][AroraBarak09]: a nonzero
+polynomial `P` in `n` variables over an integral domain `R` vanishes at at most
+theorem card_roots_le [DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R}
+    #(piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) |>.filter (fun x => eval x P = 0)) ≤
+    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos S.card with hcard | hcard
+/-- **Non-vanishing corollary of Schwartz–Zippel**: if `P ≠ 0` and `P.totalDegree < #S`, then `P`
+evaluates to a nonzero value at some point in `S ^ n`. -/
+    ∃ x : Fin n → R, (∀ i, x i ∈ S) ∧ eval x P ≠ 0 := by
+  have hSpos : 0 < S.card := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero fun h => by omega
+  have hSnpos : 0 < S.card ^ n := Nat.pow_pos hSpos
+  have hlt : P.totalDegree * S.card ^ n < S.card * S.card ^ n :=
+      #(piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) |>.filter (fun x => eval x P = 0)) <
+  have heq : (piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) |>.filter (fun x => eval x P = 0)) =
+    filter_eq_self.mpr fun x hx => hall x fun i => mem_piFinset.mp hx i
+/-- **Laplace expansion of the permanent along column 0.** -/
+    A.permanent = ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), A i 0 * (A.submatrix i.succAbove Fin.succ).permanent := by
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) i
+/-- **Laplace expansion of the permanent along row 0.** -/
+    A.permanent = ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), A 0 j * (A.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove).permanent := by
+/-- Evaluating the formal polynomial computed by an arithmetic circuit at `x : Fin n → K` agrees
+@[simp] theorem Circuit.eval_polynomial (c : Circuit (arithSignature K) n m) (x : Fin n → K)
+    MvPolynomial.eval x (c.polynomial j) = c.eval (arithInterpretation K) x j := by
+/-! #### Encoding of integer arithmetic circuits and `PITInt` -/
+/-- Encoding of an operation of `arithSignature ℤ`: `.add` is `[false, false]`, `.mul` is
+`[false, true]`, and `.const z` is `true :: encIntBin z`. -/
+def encArithOpInt : ArithOp ℤ ↪ List Bool where
+      simp only [List.cons.injEq, true_and, Bool.false_eq_true, Bool.true_eq_false, false_and] at h
+/-- Encoding of a gate of an integer arithmetic circuit: its operation paired with the list of its

+/-- Encoding of the code of an integer arithmetic circuit: the list of gates paired with the list
+def encArithCodeInt : List (ArithOp ℤ × List ℕ) × List ℕ ↪ List Bool :=
+/-- Encoding of a single-output integer arithmetic circuit bundled with its input arity: the input
+arity in unary paired with the circuit code. -/
+def encArithCircuitInt : (Σ n, Circuit (arithSignature ℤ) n 1) ↪ List Bool where

+    obtain ⟨rfl, hcode⟩ := Prod.mk.inj ((encPair encUnary encArithCodeInt).injective h)
+@[simp] theorem encArithCircuitInt_apply (c : Σ n, Circuit (arithSignature ℤ) n 1) :
+    encArithCircuitInt c = encPair encUnary encArithCodeInt (c.1, c.2.code) := rfl
+/-- The encoded length of a bundled integer arithmetic circuit is at least its number of input
+theorem le_length_encArithCircuitInt (c : Σ n, Circuit (arithSignature ℤ) n 1) :
+  simpa [encArithCircuitInt] using length_le_encPair_left encUnary encArithCodeInt (c.1, c.2.code)
+/-- **Polynomial Identity Testing (`PITInt`)**: the single-output arithmetic circuits over `ℤ` whose
+designated output computes the zero formal polynomial. -/
+def PITInt : Set (Σ n, Circuit (arithSignature ℤ) n 1) :=

+/-- **Schwartz–Zippel hitting property for arithmetic circuits**: if `⟨n, c⟩ ∉ PITInt` and
+`(c.polynomial 0).totalDegree < #S`, then `c` evaluates to a nonzero integer at some point of

+/-- The 1-gate arithmetic circuit computing the constant `a`. -/

+/-! #### The permanent family and Laplace self-reducibility via `PITInt` -/

+def minorVar {m : ℕ} (j : Fin (m + 1)) (idx : Fin (m * m)) : Fin ((m + 1) * (m + 1)) :=

+# Quantitative certificates for polynomial PRG stretch
+Keep a seed of the original length at the front of a word. Each iteration expands that seed by one
+bit and retains the previously emitted suffix. Efficiency (`polyTime_iterate`, `polyTime_stretch`)
+only needs a bounded seed prefix; the one-bit length promise is used separately to prove output
+Under the genuine one-bit length invariant (`(generator s).length = s.length + 1`), `iterate` and
+`stretch` also admit cumulative quantitative certificates (`ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace`) that
+stream the emitted bits in forward generation order followed by the reversed final seed
+(`forwardIterate`), charging `O(n + k + ∑_{i < k} (tGen(seed_i) + n + 1))` time and `O(Q + n + 1)`
+workspace during the streaming loop, and then apply one linear-time zero-workspace reversal
+`(n + k)`-bit reversal buffer to restore the exact original output order.
+  `Cslib.Crypto.PRGStretch.stretch`: repeatedly expand a fixed-width seed prefix and retain
+  forward-streamed intermediate representation before final reversal.
+  functional iteration and stretch have uniform polynomial-time TM certificates without a length
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PRGStretch.forwardIterate_eq`: the forward representation emits each round's bit in
+  generation order, then the reversed final seed.
+  expansions in forward order with cumulative time and `k`-independent workspace `O(Q + n + 1)`,
+  and degree certificates for `iterate` (unparameterized and with captured parameters) and
+  `stretch`, preserving the exact reverse-generation output order and recovering
+* [B. Barak, *Pseudorandomness*, CS 127][Barak2016PRG], length extension for PRGs.
+  We retain the final seed and reverse the order of the emitted bits.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A public-key bit encryption scheme is **bootstrappable** when it can homomorphically evaluate its
+own augmented decryption circuits `Dec(·, c₁) op Dec(·, c₂)` (for each De Morgan gate `op`) on an
+encrypted secret key, producing refreshed ciphertexts whose length is bounded by a polynomial in the
+security parameter independently of the evaluated circuit's size and depth [Gentry2009].
+   bootstrappable encryption scheme `S` and any unary polynomial-time depth bound `D : ℕ → ℕ` yield
+   a compact leveled fully homomorphic encryption scheme evaluating all De Morgan circuits (and
+   formulas) of depth at most `D n`. Key generation samples an acyclic chain of `D n + 1` key pairs
+   `(pk_0, sk_0), …, (pk_{D n}, sk_{D n})` and publishes the evaluation keys
+   `ek_ℓ ← S.encryptKey pk_{ℓ+1} sk_ℓ` for `0 ≤ ℓ < D n`. Semantic security follows by a uniform
+   two-level hybrid reduction (across the `D n` levels from top to bottom and across the
+   `S.skLength n` secret-key bits within each level) replacing each `ek_ℓ` with encryptions of
+2. **Fixed-key FHE under circular security (`fixedKeyFHE_of_circularSecure`)**: If publishing a
+   single self-encrypted evaluation key `ek ← S.encryptKey pk sk` preserves semantic security
+   (`CircularSecure`), the same homomorphic gate evaluation using the single key `(pk, ek)`
+   evaluates De Morgan circuits and formulas of **arbitrary** depth (with no depth bound fixed at
+   key generation), while maintaining polynomial-time evaluation and compactness.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme`: uniform public-key bit encryption scheme with tidy efficiency
+  and correctness on the support of `keyGen`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.SemanticSecure`: semantic security against uniform strict PPT
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.encryptKey`: bit-by-bit encryption of a secret key word.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Bootstrappable`: homomorphic evaluation of augmented De Morgan decryption gates
+  leveled key-chain generation and synchronous level-by-level homomorphic circuit evaluation.
+  fixed-key circular evaluation key generation and gate-by-gate homomorphic circuit evaluation.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.CircularSecure`: semantic security in the presence of a
+  self-encrypted secret key `ek ← S.encryptKey pk sk`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.EncryptionScheme.encryptKeyTest_gap`: exact signed hybrid gap for replacing an
+  encrypted secret key with an encryption of `0^m`.
+  acyclic key chain of length `D n`.
+  theorem (efficiency, correctness up to depth `D n`, compactness, and semantic security).
+  theorem under circular security for circuits of arbitrary depth.
+* [C. Gentry, *Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices*][Gentry2009]
+/-- A distinguisher for a public-key bit encryption scheme receives the unary security parameter,
+a public key, and a challenge ciphertext. -/

+/-- Uniform strict polynomial-time admissibility for public-key distinguishers. -/

+/-- A uniform public-key bit encryption scheme with tidy polynomial-time key generation, encryption,
+and deterministic decryption, fixed secret-key bit length `skLength n` at security parameter `n`,
+and perfect decryption correctness on supported key pairs and ciphertexts. -/
+  /-- Sample a public/secret key pair `(pk, sk)` at unary security parameter `n`. -/
+  keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)
+  /-- Encrypt a single bit `b` under public key `pk`. -/
+  encrypt : List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)
+  /-- Deterministically decrypt a ciphertext `c` using secret key `sk`. -/
+  decrypt : List Bool → List Bool → Bool
+  /-- Bit length of secret keys generated at security parameter `n`. -/
+  /-- Key generation is uniformly strict PPT in the unary parameter. -/

+# Fusion covers and De Morgan circuit size
+The Fusion bounds for Boolean functions are stated for monotone circuits that read positive
+and negative literals for free, charging only AND gates. This module transfers them to the
+ordinary size of circuits over the De Morgan basis, where negations may occur anywhere and every
+Let `ρ(f)` be the pair-cover complexity of the true set of `f` from the true sets of its `2 n`
+literals. For the lower bound, the dual-rail translation `Monotone.dualRail` turns a De Morgan
+circuit of size `s` into a monotone circuit of size `2 s` on the dual-rail inputs, and these are
+obtained from the literals by wiring and one free constant. Its AND gates give `ρ(f) ≤ 2 s`,
+for any admissible class of semifilters. For the upper bound, the quadratic compiler turns an
+unrestricted `t`-pair cover into a monotone circuit with at most `4 (t + 1)² (2 n + t + 1)` gates;
+adding `n` negations for the literals gives a De Morgan circuit. In the same terms, monotone AND
+The formalized upper bound is `O((t + 1)² (n + t))`, cubic in the cover size when `t ≥ n`
+rather than quadratic, because unions, free in the AND cost, are charged in size; this is a
+property of the construction, not a proven lower bound. The formalized size bound depends on
+`n` as well as on `ρ(f)`. These formalize known correspondences, not new bounds.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Monotone.railSelect`: the position of each dual-rail input among the literals.

+# Ordered interpretations with a domain formula
+An ordered interpretation of dimension `k` supplies a domain formula and formulas for the target
+input relations, all over the canonically ordered source language. In a source structure the
+universe of the image is the set of `k`-tuples satisfying the domain formula, ordered
+lexicographically with the first coordinate most significant. Up to the rank isomorphism, this is
+the image of [Immerman1999, Definition 1.26]: here the domain tuples are renumbered by rank onto
+`Fin m`, where `m` is their number, and the target relations are evaluated at the unranked tuples.
+The canonical numerics of the image are those of `Fin m`; nothing about their definability is
+assumed at this level. A first-order query on ordered structures must include first-order
+definitions of the target numerics [Immerman1999, Remark 1.32], and without the assumption that
+the domain formula is `true`, target `BIT` need not be first-order definable in the image
+[Immerman1999, the paragraph after Exercise 1.33]. These semantic maps are therefore more general
+than Immerman's first-order queries: his parity example shows that an image whose numerics are
+not certified need not be a first-order query. The example is cited, not formalized. His numeric
+definitions are the certificates of `Ordered.DomainInterpretation.Certificate`, which first-order
+An ordered target structure needs at least two elements [Immerman1999, Proviso 1.15]. An
+interpretation is *admissible* when its domain has at least two tuples in every source. This is the
+library's convention, motivated by that proviso; Immerman's definition does not discuss smaller

+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.DomainInterpretation.rank`: the rank of each domain tuple.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.DomainInterpretation.Admissible`: at least two domain tuples everywhere.

+An outer ordered interpretation `J` is composed with an inner interpretation `I` carrying a
+numeric certificate. The composite has dimension `l * k`, flattening the outer coordinate before
+the inner one. Its domain says that every block is a domain tuple of `I` and that the ranks of the
+blocks satisfy the pullback of the domain formula of `J`; its relation formulas are pullbacks of
+those of `J`. The inner certificate is what makes these pullbacks possible: the formulas of `J`
+mention the numeric symbols of the image of `I`.
+Flattened lexicographic order on the composite domain is lexicographic order on the ranks of the
+blocks, so the composite ranks are exactly the ranks of `J` in the image of `I`. Hence the image of
+the composite is the image of `J` in the image of `I`. Pulling back an outer certificate through
+the inner one certifies the composite. This is the substitution proof of
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.DomainInterpretation.map_comp`: the composite image is the iterated one.
+/-- Pull back a formula on blocks of `l` target variables along a certified interpretation, and
+flatten each block of blocks to `l * k` source variables. -/

+  domain := Formula.iInf (fun j : Fin l => I.domain.relabel fun i => finProdFinEquiv (j, i)) ⊓
+variable (J : DomainInterpretation L' L'' l) {I : DomainInterpretation L L' k}
+      (∀ j, I.domain.Realize fun i => x (finProdFinEquiv (j, i))) ∧
+        (C.onFormula J.domain).Realize fun p => x (finProdFinEquiv p) := by
+    ∃ h : (J.comp C).card M = J.card (I.map hI M), ∀ i, (J.comp C).unrank M i =
+      flattenTuple fun j => I.unrank M (J.unrank (I.map hI M) (Fin.cast h i) j) := by
+      (J.comp C).domain.Realize (flattenTuple fun j => I.unrank M (J.unrank (I.map hI M) i j)) := by
+      (C.realize_onFormula hI J.domain (J.unrank (I.map hI M) i)).mpr (realize_domain_unrank i)⟩
+  have hsurj (x : Fin (l * k) → Fin M.size) (hx : (J.comp C).domain.Realize x) :
+      ∃ i, (flattenTuple fun j => I.unrank M (J.unrank (I.map hI M) i j)) = x := by
+    let r : Fin l → I.map hI M := fun j => I.rank M _ (hb j)
+    have hr : (fun p : Fin l × Fin k => x (finProdFinEquiv p)) =
+        fun p => I.unrank M (r p.1) p.2 := by
+    rw [hr, C.realize_onFormula hI J.domain r] at hJ

+  have hmono : StrictMono fun i : Fin (J.card (I.map hI M)) =>
+      lexRank (flattenTuple fun j => I.unrank M (J.unrank (I.map hI M) i j)) := by
+/-- The composite image has one element per domain tuple of `J` in the image of `I`. -/
+/-- The composite ranks flatten the blocks of the ranks of `J` in the image of `I`. -/
+    (J.comp C).unrank M i = flattenTuple fun j =>
+      I.unrank M (J.unrank (I.map hI M) (Fin.cast (J.card_comp C hI M) i) j) :=
+/-- The composite of admissible interpretations is admissible. -/
+  fun M => (J.card_comp C hI M).symm ▸ hJ _
+/-- A pulled-back formula holds of composite ranks when it holds of the corresponding ranks of `J`

+An ordered query `K` first-order reduces to `K'`, written `K ≤_fo K'`, when some first-order query
+on ordered structures maps the members of `K` to members of `K'` and the other structures outside
+`K'` [Immerman1999, Definition 2.11]. A first-order query on ordered structures includes
+first-order definitions of the numeric relations and constants of its image [Immerman1999,
+Remark 1.32]; with a domain formula other than `true` these are a genuine obligation, since target
+`BIT` need not be definable [Immerman1999, the paragraph after Exercise 1.33]. Here the admissible
+maps are therefore the images `I.map hI` of admissible ordered interpretations `I` that have a
+numeric certificate, and `Ordered.Reduces` is the many-one reducibility by these maps.
+Reflexivity uses the identity interpretation of dimension one. Transitivity composes
+interpretations, substituting the inner numeric definitions into the outer formulas
+[Immerman1999, Proposition 1.28 and Exercise 2.15(1)]. Definability pulls back along reductions.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.IsFirstOrderMap`: the images of certified admissible interpretations.
+  Proposition 1.28, Remark 1.32, Exercise 1.33 and the paragraph after it, Definition 2.11 and

+    ∃ h : (id L).card M = M.size, ∀ i, (id L).unrank M i = fun _ => Fin.cast h i :=
+    (fun x _ => ⟨x 0, funext fun i => congrArg x (Subsingleton.elim 0 i)⟩)

+    (match c with | .zero => Ordered.zero L | .one => Ordered.one L | .max => Ordered.max L)

+    · change i.val = M.size - 1 ↔ i.val = (DomainInterpretation.id L).card M - 1
+/-- The identity interpretation maps every ordered structure to itself. -/

+/-- **First-order reducibility** of ordered queries, `K ≤_fo K'`: many-one reducibility by

+/-- **First-order definability pulls back along first-order reductions**, by the certified pullback

+# Clocked multi-step execution and whole-run native transport for generic RAMs
+Iterating `FiniteState.step` yields a clocked multi-step finite-state semantics `FiniteState.run`
+`WordRAM.Program.toGeneric`) `WordRAM.Executes`. Each continuing step adds at most one distinct
+On the native multitape Turing-machine side, `NativeCertificate.iterate` packages binary-counter
+* `NativeCertificate.iterate`: clocked iteration certificate with trajectory-maximum bounds.
+  `FiniteState.runSpace`: native clocked whole-run certificates and parameterized resource bounds.
+  transport of `Executes` certificates to native multitape Turing machines.
+* `Model.NativePrimitives.IsPolynomial`: polynomiality predicate for scalar primitive bundles.
+* `FiniteState.length_entries_run_le`: `n` steps add at most `n` stored sparse-memory cells.
+* `FiniteState.run_inO`, `FiniteState.eval_inO`: one finite native machine implements clocked
+  multi-step execution uniformly across runtime configurations, step budgets, and states.
+  per-step primitive and sparse-memory bounds along the run.

+/-- Extract the continuing finite state from a step outcome, if any. -/
+def continuing : Result M r → Option (FiniteState M r)
+@[simp] theorem continuing_none : continuing (M := M) (r := r) none = none := rfl

+    continuing res = res.elim none Sum.getLeft? := by
+/-- Extract the halting output value from a step outcome, if any. -/

+/-- Advance a continuing finite state by one step; halting and faulting outcomes are absorbing. -/
+def stepResult (k : M.Config) (p : Program M r) : Result M r → Result M r
+  | some (.inl s) => step k p s
+@[simp] theorem stepResult_none (k : M.Config) (p : Program M r) :
+    stepResult k p none = none := rfl
+@[simp] theorem stepResult_inl (k : M.Config) (p : Program M r) (s : FiniteState M r) :
+    stepResult k p (some (.inl s)) = step k p s := rfl
+@[simp] theorem stepResult_inr (k : M.Config) (p : Program M r) (v : M.Value) :
+    stepResult k p (some (.inr v)) = some (.inr v) := rfl

+This module assembles the polynomial-time rational hitting-list generator from the certified

+(`Runtime/Determinant.lean`), the integer lift tables (`Runtime/Lift.lean`), the reduced-rational

+Given parameters `(n, s)`, `gridPointWords` enumerates the three-dimensional grid
+`{1, …, H}³` in lexicographic order and collects the encoded normalized tuples emitted at all
+nonsingular points. `outputWord` prepends the self-delimiting binary encodings of the common
+matrix dimension `M * Dg` and the emitted tuple count `words.length`, and `hittingListWord n s`
+`CyclotomicRing.degree (Parameters.exponent n s)`, and `Parameters.gridSize n s`, agreeing with
+`encodeOutput (hittingList n s)` for all `n, s : ℕ` (`hittingListWord_eq`).
+For a standalone `List Bool → List Bool` generator, `inputWord n s` encodes `(n, s)` as the unary
+word `true ^ n ++ [false] ++ true ^ s`, `parseInput` recovers `some (n, s)` when `1 ≤ n`, `1 ≤ s`,
+and `w = inputWord n s` (and `none` otherwise), and `hittingGenerator` emits
+`encodeOutput (hittingList n s)` on valid inputs and `[]` on malformed inputs.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.gridPointWords`: list of encoded tuples emitted across the `{1, …, H}³`
+  encoding of the generator output for fixed parameters and for the selected parameter schedule.
+  `true ^ n ++ [false] ++ true ^ s` and its parser.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hittingGenerator`: the standalone `List Bool → List Bool` hitting-list
+  computable tidily in polynomial time from unary `(n, s)`.
+  dimension-bound, encoding-length, and hitting specification for `hittingGenerator`.

+/-! ### Grid enumeration and complete output encoding -/

+/-- Complete binary encoding of the generator output for parameters `(n, N, M, Dg, H)`: the

+/-- Complete binary encoding of the hitting list at the selected parameters for `(n, s)`. -/

+/-- Project the first field, absorbing linear work in the producer bounds. -/

+@[simp] theorem fst_space {f : α → β × γ} (c : NativeCertificate f ei (encPair em eo)) :
+/-- Project the second field, absorbing linear work in the producer bounds. -/

+@[simp] theorem snd_time {f : α → β × γ} (c : NativeCertificate f ei (encPair em eo)) :
+@[simp] theorem snd_space {f : α → β × γ} (c : NativeCertificate f ei (encPair em eo)) :
+/-- Add an option tag, absorbing linear work in the producer bounds. -/
+    NativeCertificate (fun a => Option.some (f a)) ei (encOption em) :=

+@[simp] theorem some_space (c : NativeCertificate f ei em) :
+/-- Add a left sum tag, absorbing linear work in the producer bounds. -/

+    NativeCertificate (fun a => Sum.inl (f a)) ei (encSum em right) :=
+@[simp] theorem inl_time (c : NativeCertificate f ei em) (right : γ ↪ List Bool) :
+@[simp] theorem inl_space (c : NativeCertificate f ei em) (right : γ ↪ List Bool) :
+/-- Add a right sum tag, absorbing linear work in the producer bounds. -/

+    NativeCertificate (fun a => Sum.inr (f a)) ei (encSum left em) :=
+@[simp] theorem inr_time (left : γ ↪ List Bool) (c : NativeCertificate f ei em) :
+@[simp] theorem inr_space (left : γ ↪ List Bool) (c : NativeCertificate f ei em) :
+/-- Transport along pointwise equality without changing bounds. -/

+/-- Retain a producer on the first component of an extended input. -/

+    (pull c other).space a = (encPair ei other a).length + c.space a.1 := rfl

+    NativeCertificate (fun a : α × β => a.2) (encPair input out) out :=

+@[simp] theorem payload_space (input : α ↪ List Bool) (out : β ↪ List Bool) (a : α × β) :
+    (payload input out).space a = (encPair input out a).length := rfl

+# Native implementation of fixed-program finite RAM steps
+The input contains configuration and the complete finite state, including the memory default.
+All encodings are injective representations of finite data, rather than of the denoted total
+memory function. Native certificates are assembled directly from arbitrary scalar time/space
+bounds, fixed tuple manipulation and parameterized sparse-memory scans. No polynomiality premise
+or selection of polynomial bounds is used.
+For each fixed program and register count, the resulting finite native machine works on every
+encoded input. Constants may depend on that fixed program; this is not an arbitrary-program
+interpreter. Initialization, iteration, output decoding and charged configuration selection
+* `FiniteState.encoding`: binary control label, complete register tuple, default and sparse store.
+  fixed-program step implementation and its parameterized time and space bounds.
+  component cost profiles decomposed across operations, instructions, and program dispatch.
+  formula and upper bound in terms of register count, register word bound, default length, and
+* `FiniteState.step_inO`: one finite native machine implements `FiniteState.step` for all runtime
+  configurations and finite states within `stepTime` and `stepSpace`.
+Reuses Christian Reitwiessner's native machine calculus and the certified scalar/sparse-memory
+/-- Encode all finite state components, including the default and distinct stored bindings. -/

+@[simp] theorem encoding_apply (enc : M.Encoding) (s : FiniteState M r) :
+    encoding enc s = encPair encNat (encPair (encPi enc.value)
+/-- Configuration is a runtime input, alongside the complete finite state. -/

+/-- Exact bit length of an encoded finite state in terms of its four encoded fields. -/
+/-- Bound the encoded finite state from the control label, register bound, default, and store. -/
+  have hr : (encPi enc.value s.regs).length ≤ r * (2 * bound + 1) := by
+    simpa [Fintype.card_fin] using length_encPi_le enc.value s.regs hregs

+/-- The nested tuple representation underlying the finite-state encoding. -/

+/-- Construct the state from its identically encoded field tuple. -/

+variable {α : Type} {ei : α ↪ List Bool} {s : α → FiniteState M r}

+@[simp] theorem fields_space (enc : M.Encoding) (c : NativeCertificate s ei (encoding enc)) :
+/-- Read a fixed register, using the complete tuple input-length guarantee. -/
+def register (enc : M.Encoding) (c : NativeCertificate s ei (encoding enc)) (i : Fin r) :

+@[simp] theorem register_time (enc : M.Encoding) (c : NativeCertificate s ei (encoding enc))

+@[simp] theorem register_space (enc : M.Encoding) (c : NativeCertificate s ei (encoding enc))

+/-- Gather a fixed tuple of operand registers, permitting repeated indices. -/

+/-- Update a fixed register and retain all other state fields. -/

+/-- Validate a moved value before updating a fixed register. -/

+      address.space x + c.space x + c.space x +
+        SparseMemory.readSpace enc.address enc.value ((a x, (s x).memory), (s x).default) := rfl

+def writeCertificate (enc : M.Encoding) (c : NativeCertificate s ei (encoding enc))

+    {a : α → M.Address} (address : NativeCertificate a ei enc.address)

+    {a : α → M.Address} (address : NativeCertificate a ei enc.address)
+      c.space x + (c.space x + (c.space x + (address.space x + value.space x + c.space x +
+        SparseMemory.writeSpace enc.address enc.value ((a x, v x), (s x).memory)))) := rfl
+/-- Implement one fixed operation from scalar, tuple and sparse-memory certificates. -/
+    (config : NativeCertificate k ei enc.config) (c : NativeCertificate s ei (encoding enc))

+      (some (setCertificate enc (pull c enc.value) d (payload ei enc.value))))

+/-- Validate a fixed continuing label and emit the updated state. -/

+    exact congr (option (evalOpCertificate enc N config c o) (const none)

+/-- A native finite machine for a fixed program, uniform in runtime configuration and state.

+# Linear resource bounds for tagged sum constructors
+Prepending the fixed Boolean tag bit to the payload encoding costs linear time and space in the
+encoded input length, without any finite-domain or inhabitance assumption on either summand.
+Uses Christian Reitwiessner's native tidy degree/resource calculus (`ComputableTidilyInO.append`).
+/-- A left sum tag has a direct native linear implementation. -/
+theorem inl (left : α ↪ List Bool) (right : β ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (Sum.inl (α := α) (β := β)) left (encSum left right)
+  have hid : ComputableTidilyInO (fun a : α => a) left left
+/-- A right sum tag has a direct native linear implementation. -/
+theorem inr (left : α ↪ List Bool) (right : β ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (Sum.inr (α := α) (β := β)) right (encSum left right)
+  have hid : ComputableTidilyInO (fun a : β => a) right right

+# Carry-save addition trees and logarithmic-depth bit counting
+A 3-to-2 carry-save adder (`csa3to2 w`) reduces three `w`-bit words `x`, `y`, `z` to a bitwise
+exclusive-or word `csaSum x y z` and a shifted carry word `csaCarry x y z` in constant depth (`≤ 6`)
+and linear size (`≤ 20 w`), preserving the sum of their unsigned values modulo `2 ^ w`
+(`val_csaSum_add_val_csaCarry_mod`). Two carry-save layers form a 4-to-2 reducer (`csa4to2 w`) that
+combines two redundant carry-save pairs `(a₁, b₁)` and `(a₂, b₂)` into one pair `(s, c)` in depth
+at most `12` and size at most `40 w`.
+Combining `k` one-bit inputs along a balanced binary tree (`Circuit.balanced`) of 4-to-2 reducers
+produces a carry-save pair whose sum modulo `2 ^ w` is the Hamming weight `BitString.weight x`, in
+depth `O(log k)` and size `O(k w)`. Iterating `csa3to2 w` with a zero third word `w` times
+(`finishCircuit w w`) clears a further carry bit at every step
+(`sndBits_eval_finishCircuit_eq_false`), collapsing the carry-save pair to a single `w`-bit binary
+Taking `w = ⌈log₂ (k + 1)⌉` gives a De Morgan circuit (`weightCircuit k`) of depth `O(log k)` and
+size `O(k log k)` that outputs the exact binary representation of `BitString.weight x`
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.finishCircuit`: carry-clearing iteration reducing a carry-save pair to a
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.weightCircuit`: De Morgan circuit computing the binary numeral of the
+  `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.depth_weightCircuit_le`: size `O(k log k)` and depth `O(log k)`.
+* [A. K. Chandra, L. Stockmeyer, U. Vishkin, *Constant depth reducibility*]
+/-! ### Unsigned word values and carry-save arithmetic -/
+/-- The sum of the unsigned values of a carry-save pair of `w`-bit words. -/
+  (BitString.equivFin w (fstBits p) : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w (sndBits p) : ℕ)
+    pairVal (Fin.append x y) = (BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w y : ℕ) := by
+/-- The carry of a 1-bit full adder: whether at least two of the three bits are true. -/
+    ((a ^^ b) ^^ c).toNat + 2 * (maj3 a b c).toNat = a.toNat + b.toNat + c.toNat := by
+  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
+/-- The bitwise exclusive-or word of a 3-to-2 carry-save adder on `w`-bit words. -/
+def csaSum (x y z : BitString w) : BitString w :=
+  fun i => (x i ^^ y i) ^^ z i
+/-- The shifted carry word of a 3-to-2 carry-save adder on `w`-bit words: bit `0` is `false` and
+bit `i + 1` is the full-adder carry from bit `i`. -/
+def csaCarry (x y z : BitString w) : BitString w :=
+  fun i => if h : 0 < (i : ℕ) then
+    maj3 (x ⟨(i : ℕ) - 1, by omega⟩) (y ⟨(i : ℕ) - 1, by omega⟩) (z ⟨(i : ℕ) - 1, by omega⟩)
+    ∑ i : Fin (w + 1), (maj3 (x i) (y i) (z i)).toNat * 2 ^ ((i : ℕ) + 1) := by
+  simp only [csaCarry, Fin.val_zero, lt_self_iff_false, ↓reduceDIte, Bool.toNat_false, zero_mul,
+    zero_add, Fin.val_succ, Nat.add_pos_right _ Nat.one_pos, Nat.add_sub_cancel, Fin.val_castSucc,
+/-- **Carry-save 3-to-2 invariant**: the sum and shifted carry words have the same sum of unsigned
+values modulo `2 ^ w` as the three input words. -/
+    ((BitString.equivFin w (csaSum x y z) : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w (csaCarry x y z) : ℕ)) %
+    ((BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w y : ℕ) +
+  · have hsum : (BitString.equivFin (w + 1) x : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin (w + 1) y : ℕ) +
+      rw [add_assoc (BitString.equivFin (w + 1) (csaSum x y z) : ℕ), val_csaCarry_add_top,
+        val_equivFin_eq_sum x, val_equivFin_eq_sum y, val_equivFin_eq_sum z,
+        val_equivFin_eq_sum (csaSum x y z), ← sum_add_distrib, ← sum_add_distrib,
+      calc (x i).toNat * 2 ^ (i : ℕ) + (y i).toNat * 2 ^ (i : ℕ) + (z i).toNat * 2 ^ (i : ℕ)
+        _ = ((x i).toNat + (y i).toNat + (z i).toNat) * 2 ^ (i : ℕ) := by ring
+        _ = ((csaSum x y z i).toNat + 2 * (maj3 (x i) (y i) (z i)).toNat) * 2 ^ (i : ℕ) := by
+/-- When the third word is zero and the first `t` bits of `y` are `false`, the first `t + 1` bits
+of the shifted carry word `csaCarry x y 0` are `false`. -/
+    (hy : ∀ i : Fin w, (i : ℕ) < t → y i = false) (i : Fin w) (hi : (i : ℕ) < t + 1) :
+    csaCarry x y (fun _ => false) i = false := by
+  · have hlt : (⟨(i : ℕ) - 1, by omega⟩ : Fin w).val < t := by dsimp; omega
+    cases x ⟨(i : ℕ) - 1, by omega⟩ <;> rfl
+/-- Formula for bit `i` of `csaSum` on three `w`-bit words. -/
+def csaSumFormula (w : ℕ) (i : Fin w) : Formula signature (w + (w + w)) :=
+@[simp] theorem eval_csaSumFormula (i : Fin w) (u : BitString (w + (w + w))) :
+      csaSum (fstBits u) (fstBits (sndBits u)) (sndBits (sndBits u)) i := by
+@[simp] theorem size_csaSumFormula (i : Fin w) : (csaSumFormula w i).size = 15 := by
+theorem depth_csaSumFormula_le (i : Fin w) : (csaSumFormula w i).depth ≤ 6 := by
+/-- Formula for `maj3` on three input coordinates. -/
+def maj3Formula (a b c : Fin n) : Formula signature n :=
+@[simp] theorem eval_maj3Formula (a b c : Fin n) (u : BitString n) :
+    (maj3Formula a b c).eval interpretation u = maj3 (u a) (u b) (u c) := by
+@[simp] theorem size_maj3Formula (a b c : Fin n) : (maj3Formula a b c).size = 5 :=
+theorem depth_maj3Formula_le (a b c : Fin n) : (maj3Formula a b c).depth ≤ 3 := by
+/-- Formula for bit `i` of `csaCarry` on three `w`-bit words. -/
+def csaCarryFormula (w : ℕ) (i : Fin w) : Formula signature (w + (w + w)) :=
+@[simp] theorem eval_csaCarryFormula (i : Fin w) (u : BitString (w + (w + w))) :
+      csaCarry (fstBits u) (fstBits (sndBits u)) (sndBits (sndBits u)) i := by
+theorem size_csaCarryFormula_le (i : Fin w) : (csaCarryFormula w i).size ≤ 5 := by
+theorem depth_csaCarryFormula_le (i : Fin w) : (csaCarryFormula w i).depth ≤ 3 := by
+/-- **3-to-2 carry-save adder**: reduces three `w`-bit words to two `w`-bit words `(sum, carry)`
+with the same sum modulo `2 ^ w`, using at most `20 w` gates and depth at most `6`. -/
+def csa3to2 (w : ℕ) : Circuit signature (w + (w + w)) (w + w) :=
+      ((BitString.equivFin w (fstBits u) : ℕ) + pairVal (sndBits u)) % 2 ^ w := by
+  have h1 : ∑ i : Fin w, (csaSumFormula w i).toCircuit.size = 15 * w := by
+  have h2 : ∑ i : Fin w, (csaCarryFormula w i).toCircuit.size ≤ 5 * w := by
+        (fun i => (csaCarryFormula w i).toCircuit.size) 5 fun i _ => by
+/-- Wiring selecting the first three `w`-bit words of two carry-save pairs. -/
+def csa4to2FirstIn (w : ℕ) : Fin (w + (w + w)) → Fin ((w + w) + (w + w)) :=
+    (Fin.append (Fin.castAdd (w + w) ∘ Fin.natAdd w) (Fin.natAdd (w + w) ∘ Fin.castAdd w))
+/-- **4-to-2 carry-save reducer**: combines two carry-save pairs `(a₁, b₁)` and `(a₂, b₂)` of
+`w`-bit words into a single carry-save pair in depth at most `12` and size at most `40 w`. -/
+def csa4to2 (w : ℕ) : Circuit signature ((w + w) + (w + w)) (w + w) :=
+    pairVal ((csa4to2 w).eval interpretation (Fin.append p₁ p₂)) % 2 ^ w =
+  have h1 : Fin.append p₁ p₂ ∘ (Fin.natAdd (w + w) ∘ Fin.natAdd w) = sndBits p₂ := by
+  have h2 : fstBits (Fin.append p₁ p₂ ∘ csa4to2FirstIn w) = fstBits p₁ := by
+  have h3 : sndBits (Fin.append p₁ p₂ ∘ csa4to2FirstIn w) =
+  have h' : ((Circuit.wiring signature (Fin.natAdd (w + w) ∘ Fin.natAdd w)).append
+/-- Wiring that appends `w` copies of a single constant wire to a `(w + w)`-bit carry-save pair. -/
+def finishStepIn (w : ℕ) : Fin (w + (w + w)) → Fin ((w + w) + 1) :=
+/-- One carry-clearing step: applies `csa3to2 w` to `(a, b, 0)`, clearing one more low carry bit. -/
+def finishStep (w : ℕ) : Circuit signature (w + w) (w + w) :=
+  have h1 : fstBits ((Circuit.wiring signature (finishStepIn w)).eval interpretation
+        (Circuit.oneGate (Op.const false) Fin.elim0)).eval interpretation p)) = fstBits p := by
+  have h2 : fstBits (sndBits ((Circuit.wiring signature (finishStepIn w)).eval interpretation
+        (Circuit.oneGate (Op.const false) Fin.elim0)).eval interpretation p))) = sndBits p := by
+  have h3 : sndBits (sndBits ((Circuit.wiring signature (finishStepIn w)).eval interpretation
+    pairVal ((finishStep w).eval interpretation p) % 2 ^ w = pairVal p % 2 ^ w := by
+/-- `t` steps of carry-clearing on a `(w + w)`-bit carry-save pair. -/
+def finishCircuit (w : ℕ) : ℕ → Circuit signature (w + w) (w + w)
+    pairVal ((finishCircuit w t).eval interpretation p) % 2 ^ w = pairVal p % 2 ^ w := by
+  | succ t ih => rw [finishCircuit, Circuit.eval_comp, pairVal_eval_finishStep_mod, ih]
+theorem sndBits_eval_finishCircuit_eq_false (t : ℕ) (p : BitString (w + w)) (i : Fin w)
+    sndBits ((finishCircuit w t).eval interpretation p) i = false := by
+    exact csaCarry_eq_false_of_lt _ _ (fun j hj => ih j hj) i hi
+    (BitString.equivFin w (fstBits ((finishCircuit w w).eval interpretation p)) : ℕ) % 2 ^ w =
+  have hsnd : sndBits ((finishCircuit w w).eval interpretation p) = fun _ => false :=
+    funext fun i => sndBits_eval_finishCircuit_eq_false w p i i.isLt
+theorem size_finishCircuit_le (w t : ℕ) : (finishCircuit w t).size ≤ t * (20 * w + 1) := by
+theorem depth_finishCircuit_le (w t : ℕ) : (finishCircuit w t).depth ≤ 7 * t := by
+/-! ### Balanced carry-save tree for Hamming weight -/
+/-- A carry-save pair of `w`-bit words all of whose bits are `false`, from one `const false`
+def zeroPairCircuit (k w : ℕ) : Circuit signature k (w + w) :=
+    (zeroPairCircuit k w).eval interpretation x = fun _ => false :=
+/-- Leaf circuit placing input bit `j : Fin k` into bit `0` of the first `w`-bit word, and `false`
+on all other wires of the `(w + w)`-bit carry-save pair, using one `const false` gate. -/
+def bitPairCircuit (k w : ℕ) (j : Fin k) : Circuit signature k (w + w) :=
+      (fun i : Fin w => if (i : ℕ) = 0 then Fin.castAdd 1 j else Fin.natAdd k 0)

+    have hsnd : sndBits ((bitPairCircuit k (w + 1) j).eval interpretation x) =
+    have h0 : fstBits ((bitPairCircuit k (w + 1) j).eval interpretation x) 0 = x j := by

+theorem depth_bitPairCircuit_le (j : Fin k) : (bitPairCircuit k w j).depth ≤ 1 :=
+/-- Balanced binary tree of `csa4to2 w` reducers over all `k` input bits. -/
