lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Search problems: FNP, FP and TFNP
+A *search problem* is a relation `R : α → List Bool → Prop` between instances and solutions; the
+task is to find, given `a`, some `w` with `R a w` [Papadimitriou, Section 10.3][Papadimitriou94],
+[Arora and Barak, Section 2.5][AroraBarak09]. Solutions are bit strings, so the length of a
+solution is the length of its description, as in Megiddo and Papadimitriou
+[MegiddoPapadimitriou1991]. Instances are encoded by `enc : α ↪ List Bool`, and a verifier reads
+the pair `encPair enc encBits (a, w) = frame (enc a) ++ w`, as for `Cslib.Complexity.NP`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.FNP`: relations that are *polynomially balanced* (every solution of `a` has
+  length at most `p (enc a).length` for a polynomial `p`) and *polynomial-time decidable*. These
+  are the two conditions of [Papadimitriou, Section 10.3][Papadimitriou94]. Balance is a property
+  of the relation itself: unlike the certificates of `NP`, solutions have no prescribed length.
+  `Cslib.Complexity.mem_FNP_iff_exists_bounded` gives the equivalent form in which the length bound
+  is part of the decided predicate.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SolvesSearch R f`: a function `f : α → Option (List Bool)` *solves* `R` if
+  `f a = some w` only for solutions `w` of `a`, and `f a = none` only when `a` has no solution.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.FPSearch`: the relations in `FNP` solved by a polynomial-time function, with
+  outputs encoded by `encOption encBits`. This is Papadimitriou's class `FP` of search problems
+  [Papadimitriou, Section 10.3][Papadimitriou94]; it is named `FPSearch` to distinguish it from
+  the class of polynomial-time computable functions.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.TFNP`: the *total* relations in `FNP`, those for which every instance has a
+`NP` is the class of domains of `FNP` relations (`Cslib.Complexity.mem_NP_iff_exists_FNP`), and
+the domain of a relation in `FPSearch` is in `P` (`Cslib.Complexity.searchDomain_mem_P`). Hence
+`FNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc` implies `NP enc ⊆ P enc`
+Total problems arise from `NP ∩ coNP`: if `A` and its complement are domains of the `FNP`
+relations `R` and `S`, then the disjoint sum `Cslib.Complexity.searchSum R S`, whose solutions are
+`true :: u` for a solution `u` of `R` and `false :: u` for a solution `u` of `S`, is in `TFNP`.
+Solving it in polynomial time decides `A`, so `TFNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc` implies
+and no relation is claimed to be hard here.
+A *polynomial-time search reduction* from `R` to `S` (`Cslib.Complexity.SearchReducible`) is a
+pair of polynomial-time functions: `f` maps instances of `R` to instances of `S`, and `g` maps a
+solution `w` of `f a` back to the solution `g (a, w)` of `a`. This is the reduction of Megiddo and
+Papadimitriou [MegiddoPapadimitriou1991] and of Johnson, Papadimitriou and Yannakakis
+[JohnsonPapadimitriouYannakakis1988] used for `TFNP` and its subclasses. For relations that need
+not be total, `f` must in addition map instances with a solution to instances with a solution (as
+in Levin reductions); otherwise a solver for `S` reporting that `f a` has no solution would say
+nothing about `a`. For a total target, this condition holds automatically
+(`Cslib.Complexity.SearchReducible.of_isTotalSearch`), so on `TFNP` the definition is exactly the
+one-way condition of the literature. A search reduction is in particular a polynomial-time
+* `Cslib.Complexity.verifierSearch`: the search problem of a verifier.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.searchSum`: the disjoint sum of two search problems.
+  `Cslib.Complexity.SearchReducible.mem_TFNP`: closure of `FPSearch` and transfer of totality.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SearchHard.subset_FPSearch`: if a problem hard for a subclass of `FNP` is in
+* [N. Megiddo, C. H. Papadimitriou, *On total functions, existence theorems and computational
+* [D. S. Johnson, C. H. Papadimitriou, M. Yannakakis, *How easy is local
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The instances of the search problem `R` that have a solution. -/
+def searchDomain (R : α → List Bool → Prop) : Set α := {a | ∃ w, R a w}
+theorem mem_searchDomain {a : α} : a ∈ searchDomain R ↔ ∃ w, R a w := Iff.rfl
+/-- The search problem `R` is *total*: every instance has a solution. -/
+def IsTotalSearch (R : α → List Bool → Prop) : Prop := ∀ a, ∃ w, R a w
+theorem isTotalSearch_iff_searchDomain_eq_univ : IsTotalSearch R ↔ searchDomain R = Set.univ :=
+/-- `f` *solves* the search problem `R`: it returns `some w` only for a solution `w`, and `none`
+def SolvesSearch (R : α → List Bool → Prop) (f : α → Option (List Bool)) : Prop :=
+  ∀ a, (∀ w, f a = some w → R a w) ∧ (f a = none → a ∉ searchDomain R)
+theorem SolvesSearch.rel (h : SolvesSearch R f) {a : α} {w : List Bool} (ha : f a = some w) :
+theorem SolvesSearch.not_mem (h : SolvesSearch R f) {a : α} (ha : f a = none) :
+/-- A solver finds a solution exactly on the instances that have one. -/
+  | some w => simpa using ⟨w, h.rel ha⟩
+/-- A function that always returns a solution solves the search problem. -/
+theorem solvesSearch_some {g : α → List Bool} (hg : ∀ a, R a (g a)) :
+    SolvesSearch R fun a => some (g a) :=
+  fun a => ⟨fun _ h => Option.some_injective _ h ▸ hg a, fun h => (Option.some_ne_none _ h).elim⟩
+/-- A solver of a total search problem never returns `none`. -/
+theorem SolvesSearch.rel_getD (h : SolvesSearch R f) (htot : IsTotalSearch R) (a : α)
+    (d : List Bool) : R a ((f a).getD d) := by
+/-- The search problems in `FNP` with respect to the encoding `enc` of instances: relations that
+are polynomially balanced, every solution of `a` having length at most `p (enc a).length` for a
+polynomial `p`, and decided by a polynomial-time function of the instance and the candidate
+def FNP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (α → List Bool → Prop) :=
+  {R | (∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ a w, R a w → w.length ≤ p.eval (enc a).length) ∧
+    ∃ V : α × List Bool → Bool, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      ∀ a w, R a w ↔ V (a, w) = true}
+/-- The search problems in `FNP` solved by a polynomial-time function, Papadimitriou's class `FP`
+def FPSearch (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (α → List Bool → Prop) :=
+  {R | R ∈ FNP enc ∧ ∃ f : α → Option (List Bool),
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc (encOption encBits) ∧ SolvesSearch R f}
+def TFNP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (α → List Bool → Prop) :=
+variable {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {R S : α → List Bool → Prop}
+    (∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ a w, R a w → w.length ≤ p.eval (enc a).length) ∧
+      ∃ V : α × List Bool → Bool, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+        ∀ a w, R a w ↔ V (a, w) = true :=
+theorem mem_FPSearch : R ∈ FPSearch enc ↔ R ∈ FNP enc ∧ ∃ f : α → Option (List Bool),
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc (encOption encBits) ∧ SolvesSearch R f :=
+theorem mem_TFNP : R ∈ TFNP enc ↔ R ∈ FNP enc ∧ IsTotalSearch R := Iff.rfl
+theorem FPSearch_subset_FNP : FPSearch enc ⊆ FNP enc := fun _ h => h.1
+theorem TFNP_subset_FNP : TFNP enc ⊆ FNP enc := fun _ h => h.1
+/-- **`FNP` with the length bound in the verifier.** A relation is in `FNP` exactly when it holds
+of the candidate solutions of length at most `p (enc a).length` accepted by a polynomial-time
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+        ∀ a w, R a w ↔ w.length ≤ p.eval (enc a).length ∧ V (a, w) = true := by
+    exact ⟨p, V, hV, fun a w => ⟨fun h => ⟨hp a w h, (hR a w).1 h⟩, fun h => (hR a w).2 h.2⟩⟩
+    refine ⟨⟨p, fun a w h => ((hR a w).1 h).1⟩,
+      fun x => decide (x.2.length ≤ p.eval (enc x.1).length) && V x, ?_, fun a w => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [hR a w, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
+/-- A polynomial-time solver of a total relation in `FNP` puts it in `FPSearch`. -/
+theorem mem_FPSearch_of_total (hR : R ∈ FNP enc) {g : α → List Bool}
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime g enc encBits) (h : ∀ a, R a (g a)) : R ∈ FPSearch enc :=
+/-- A total relation in `FPSearch` has a polynomial-time function returning a solution. -/
+theorem exists_total_of_mem_FPSearch (hR : R ∈ FPSearch enc) (htot : IsTotalSearch R) :
+    ∃ g : α → List Bool, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime g enc encBits ∧ ∀ a, R a (g a) :=
+  ⟨fun a => (f a).getD [], optionGetDWithInput hf (const []), fun a => hsolve.rel_getD htot a []⟩
+/-- **Domains of `FNP` relations are in `NP`**: a solution, framed and padded, is a certificate. -/
+theorem searchDomain_mem_NP (hR : R ∈ FNP enc) : searchDomain R ∈ NP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨p, hp⟩, V, hV, hR⟩ := hR
+  exact mem_NP_of_witness (encW := encBits) ⟨fun w => w, fun _ => rfl, id'.exists_degree⟩ hV
+    (fun a w => (hR a w).symm) fun a w h => ⟨w, h, hp a w h⟩
+/-- The search problem of a verifier: the certificates of the prescribed length that it accepts. -/
+def verifierSearch (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α)
+  w.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ V (a, w) = true
+/-- The search problem of a polynomial-time verifier is in `FNP`. -/
+theorem verifierSearch_mem_FNP {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    verifierSearch enc p V ∈ FNP enc := by
+  refine ⟨⟨p, fun a w h => h.1.le⟩,
+    fun x => decide (x.2.length = p.eval (enc x.1).length) && V x, ?_, fun a w => ?_⟩
+/-- A verifier verifies exactly the domain of its search problem. -/
+theorem IsVerifier.searchDomain_eq {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool} {A : Set α}
+    (h : IsVerifier enc p V A) : searchDomain (verifierSearch enc p V) = A :=
+/-- **`NP` is the class of domains of `FNP` relations.** -/
+theorem mem_NP_iff_exists_FNP {A : Set α} : A ∈ NP enc ↔ ∃ R ∈ FNP enc, searchDomain R = A :=
+    fun ⟨_, hR, hA⟩ => hA ▸ searchDomain_mem_NP hR⟩
+/-- **Domains of `FPSearch` relations are in `P`**: test whether the solver finds a solution. -/
+theorem searchDomain_mem_P (hR : R ∈ FPSearch enc) : searchDomain R ∈ P enc :=
+  ⟨fun a => (f a).isSome, optionIsSome hf, fun _ => hsolve.isSome_iff.symm⟩
+/-- **If every `FNP` relation is in `FPSearch`, then `NP ⊆ P`** for the encoding `enc`. -/
+theorem NP_subset_P_of_FNP_subset_FPSearch (h : FNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc) : NP enc ⊆ P enc :=
+/-- The disjoint sum of the search problems `R` and `S`: the solutions of `a` are `true :: u` for
+the solutions `u` of `a` in `R`, and `false :: u` for the solutions `u` of `a` in `S`. -/
+def searchSum (R S : α → List Bool → Prop) (a : α) : List Bool → Prop
+theorem searchSum_nil {a : α} : ¬searchSum R S a [] := id
+theorem searchSum_true_cons {a : α} {u : List Bool} : searchSum R S a (true :: u) ↔ R a u :=
+theorem searchSum_false_cons {a : α} {u : List Bool} : searchSum R S a (false :: u) ↔ S a u :=
+theorem searchDomain_searchSum : searchDomain (searchSum R S) = searchDomain R ∪ searchDomain S :=
+  Set.ext fun _ => ⟨fun ⟨w, hw⟩ => match w, hw with
+    fun h => h.elim (fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨true :: u, hu⟩) fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨false :: u, hu⟩⟩
+theorem searchSum_mem_FNP (hR : R ∈ FNP enc) (hS : S ∈ FNP enc) : searchSum R S ∈ FNP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨p, hp⟩, V, hV, hRV⟩ := hR
+  obtain ⟨⟨q, hq⟩, W, hW, hSW⟩ := hS
+  refine ⟨⟨p + q + 1, fun a w h => ?_⟩,
+    fun x => !x.2.isEmpty && if x.2.headD false then V (x.1, x.2.tail) else W (x.1, x.2.tail),
+  · have htail : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => (x.1, x.2.tail))
+/-- The disjoint sum of search problems whose domains cover all instances is total. -/
+theorem isTotalSearch_searchSum (h : ∀ a, a ∈ searchDomain R ∨ a ∈ searchDomain S) :
+    IsTotalSearch (searchSum R S) := fun a => by
+/-- The disjoint sum of `FNP` relations whose domains cover all instances is in `TFNP`. -/
+theorem searchSum_mem_TFNP (hR : R ∈ FNP enc) (hS : S ∈ FNP enc)
+    (h : ∀ a, a ∈ searchDomain R ∨ a ∈ searchDomain S) : searchSum R S ∈ TFNP enc :=
+/-- **Problems in `NP ∩ coNP` give total search problems**: if `A` and its complement are in `NP`,
+then `A` and `Aᶜ` are domains of `FNP` relations whose disjoint sum is in `TFNP`. -/
+theorem exists_searchSum_mem_TFNP {A : Set α} (hA : A ∈ NP enc) (hA' : A ∈ coNP enc) :
+    ∃ R S, searchDomain R = A ∧ searchDomain S = Aᶜ ∧ searchSum R S ∈ TFNP enc := by
+  refine ⟨R, S, rfl, hSA, searchSum_mem_TFNP hR hS fun a => ?_⟩
+/-- **Solving a disjoint sum decides the first domain.** If the domains of `R` and `S` are
+disjoint and `searchSum R S` is in `FPSearch`, the domain of `R` is in `P`: an instance is in it
+exactly when the solver returns a solution tagged `true`. -/
+    (hdisj : Disjoint (searchDomain R) (searchDomain S)) : searchDomain R ∈ P enc := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => ((f a).getD []).headD false, ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+      (const [] : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun _ : α => ([] : List Bool)) enc encBits)
+  · change a ∈ searchDomain R ↔ ((f a).getD []).headD false = true
+      exact ⟨fun h => (this (.inl h)).elim, fun h => by simp at h⟩
+      · exact ⟨fun h => (Set.disjoint_left.1 hdisj h ⟨u, hw⟩).elim, fun h => by simp at h⟩
+/-- **If every `TFNP` relation is in `FPSearch`, then `NP ∩ coNP ⊆ P`** for the encoding `enc`
+    NP enc ∩ coNP enc ⊆ P enc := fun A ⟨hA, hA'⟩ => by
+  obtain ⟨R, S, rfl, hS, hRS⟩ := exists_searchSum_mem_TFNP hA hA'
+/-- A **polynomial-time search reduction** from `R` to `S`: a polynomial-time map `f` of
+instances that maps instances with a solution to instances with a solution, and a
+polynomial-time map `g` taking a solution `w` of `f a` back to a solution `g (a, w)` of `a`. -/
+def SearchReducible (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (R : α → List Bool → Prop)
+  ∃ (f : α → β) (g : α × List Bool → List Bool), ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encA encB ∧
+      (∀ a, a ∈ searchDomain R → f a ∈ searchDomain S) ∧ ∀ a w, S (f a) w → R a (g (a, w))
+/-- `S` is hard for the class `𝒞` of search problems under search reductions: every problem in
+`𝒞`, with any encoding of its instances, reduces to `S`. -/
+def SearchHard (𝒞 : ∀ {α : Type}, (α ↪ List Bool) → Set (α → List Bool → Prop))
+    (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (S : β → List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
+  ∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (R : α → List Bool → Prop), R ∈ 𝒞 enc →
+/-- `S` is complete for the class `𝒞` of search problems: it is in `𝒞` and hard for it. -/
+def SearchComplete (𝒞 : ∀ {α : Type}, (α ↪ List Bool) → Set (α → List Bool → Prop))
+    (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (S : β → List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
+  S ∈ 𝒞 encB ∧ SearchHard 𝒞 encB S
+variable {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encC : γ ↪ List Bool}
+  {T : β → List Bool → Prop} {U : γ → List Bool → Prop}
+/-- For a total target, the one-way condition on solutions suffices for a search reduction. -/
+    {g : α × List Bool → List Bool} (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encA encB)
+    (h : ∀ a w, T (f a) w → R a (g (a, w))) : SearchReducible encA encB R T :=
+  ⟨f, g, hf, hg, fun a _ => hT (f a), h⟩
+/-- Every search problem reduces to itself. -/
+theorem SearchReducible.refl (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (R : α → List Bool → Prop) :
+  ⟨id, Prod.snd, id', snd encA encBits, fun _ h => h, fun _ _ h => h⟩
+theorem SearchReducible.trans (hRT : SearchReducible encA encB R T)
+    (hTU : SearchReducible encB encC T U) : SearchReducible encA encC R U :=
+  let ⟨f, g, hf, hg, hdom, hsol⟩ := hRT
+  let ⟨f', g', hf', hg', hdom', hsol'⟩ := hTU
+  ⟨f' ∘ f, fun x => g (x.1, g' (f x.1, x.2)), hf'.comp hf,
+    fun a ha => hdom' _ (hdom a ha), fun a w h => hsol a _ (hsol' (f a) w h)⟩
+/-- A search reduction is a polynomial-time many-one reduction between the domains. -/
+theorem SearchReducible.polyTimeReducible (h : SearchReducible encA encB R T) :
+  ⟨f, hf, fun a => ⟨hdom a, fun ⟨w, hw⟩ => ⟨_, hsol a w hw⟩⟩⟩
+theorem SearchReducible.isTotalSearch (h : SearchReducible encA encB R T)
+  fun a => let ⟨w, hw⟩ := hT (f a); ⟨_, hsol a w hw⟩
+/-- An `FNP` relation that reduces to a `TFNP` relation is in `TFNP`. -/
+theorem SearchReducible.mem_TFNP (h : SearchReducible encA encB R T) (hR : R ∈ FNP encA)
+    (hT : T ∈ TFNP encB) : R ∈ TFNP encA :=
+/-- **`FPSearch` is closed under search reductions**: an `FNP` relation that reduces to a relation
+theorem SearchReducible.mem_FPSearch (h : SearchReducible encA encB R T) (hR : R ∈ FNP encA)
+    (hT : T ∈ FPSearch encB) : R ∈ FPSearch encA := by
+  obtain ⟨f, g, hf, hg, hdom, hsol⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨hR, fun a => (s (f a)).elim none fun w => some (g (a, w)),
+    fun a => ⟨fun w ha => ?_, fun ha hR => ?_⟩⟩
+      simp only [hsa, Option.elim_some, Option.some.injEq] at ha
+      exact ha ▸ hsol a v (hsolve.rel hsa)
+    | none => exact hsolve.not_mem hsa (hdom a hR)
+variable {𝒞 : ∀ {α : Type}, (α ↪ List Bool) → Set (α → List Bool → Prop)}
+theorem SearchHard.trans (hT : SearchHard 𝒞 encB T) (hTU : SearchReducible encB encC T U) :
+  fun enc R hR => (hT enc R hR).trans hTU
+/-- **A hard problem in `FPSearch` collapses the class.** If every problem of `𝒞` is in `FNP` and
+a `𝒞`-hard problem is in `FPSearch`, then every problem of `𝒞` is in `FPSearch`. -/
+theorem SearchHard.subset_FPSearch (h𝒞 : ∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool), 𝒞 enc ⊆ FNP enc)
+    (hT : SearchHard 𝒞 encB T) (hT' : T ∈ FPSearch encB) (enc : α ↪ List Bool) :
+  fun R hR => (hT enc R hR).mem_FPSearch (h𝒞 enc hR) hT'
+/-- A `TFNP`-complete problem is in `FPSearch` exactly when all of `TFNP` is. -/
+    {T : β → List Bool → Prop} (hT : SearchComplete @TFNP encB T) :
+    T ∈ FPSearch encB ↔ ∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool), TFNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc :=
+  ⟨fun h _ enc => SearchHard.subset_FPSearch (fun _ => TFNP_subset_FNP) hT.2 h enc,

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Search to decision: `FPSearch = FNP` exactly when `P = NP`
+Every search problem in `FNP` reduces to a decision problem in `NP`
+*prefix problem* (`Cslib.Complexity.prefixSearch`) asks, given an instance `a` and a word `u`,
+whether some solution of `a` begins with `u`. A decision procedure `D` for it finds solutions bit
+by bit (`Cslib.Complexity.prefixSearchRun`): starting from the empty word, stop when the current
+word is a solution, and otherwise extend it by `false` when `D` says that a solution begins with
+the extension, and by `true` otherwise. As long as some solution begins with the current word,
+this stays true, and the word grows by one bit at every step until it is a solution; since
+solutions are no longer than `p (enc a).length`, that many steps suffice
+Hence if `NP ⊆ P` for the encoding of pairs of instances and words, every `FNP` relation is in
+when `NP ⊆ P` for every encoding (`Cslib.Complexity.FNP_subset_FPSearch_iff`). Through the
+Cook–Levin theorem this happens exactly when `SAT ∈ P`
+directly: the search problem `Cslib.Complexity.SAT.searchRel` of assignment certificates is in
+* `Cslib.Complexity.prefixSearch`: the prefix problem of a search problem.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SAT.searchRel`: the search problem of satisfying assignments.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.prefixSearch_mem_FNP`: the prefix problem of an `FNP` relation is in `FNP`, so
+* `Cslib.Complexity.rel_prefixSearchRun`: with a correct decision procedure for the prefix problem,
+  the search through prefixes finds a solution of every instance that has one.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {R : α → List Bool → Prop}
+/-- The prefix problem of `R`: the solutions of a pair `(a, u)` are the words `v` such that
+`u ++ v` is a solution of `a`. Its domain consists of the pairs `(a, u)` such that some solution of
+def prefixSearch (R : α → List Bool → Prop) (x : α × List Bool) (v : List Bool) : Prop :=
+/-- The prefix problem of an `FNP` relation is in `FNP`. -/
+theorem prefixSearch_mem_FNP (hR : R ∈ FNP enc) : prefixSearch R ∈ FNP (encPair enc encBits) := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨p, hp⟩, V, hV, hRV⟩ := hR
+  refine ⟨⟨p, fun x v h => ?_⟩, fun y => V (y.1.1, y.1.2 ++ y.2), ?_, fun x v => hRV _ _⟩
+    have h₂ := Polynomial.eval_mono p (length_le_encPair_left enc encBits x)
+      (bitsAppend (fst (encPair enc encBits) encBits).snd' (snd (encPair enc encBits) encBits)))
+/-- One step of the search through prefixes, with `V` deciding solutions and `D` deciding the
+prefix problem: keep a solution, and otherwise extend the word by `false` if `D` accepts the
+def prefixSearchStep (V D : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (u : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  if V (a, u) then u else if D (a, u ++ [false]) then u ++ [false] else u ++ [true]
+/-- The search through prefixes for `n a` steps, starting from the empty word. -/
+def prefixSearchRun (V D : α × List Bool → Bool) (n : α → ℕ) (a : α) : List Bool :=
+  (List.replicate (n a) false).foldl (fun u _ => prefixSearchStep V D a u) []
+variable {V D : α × List Bool → Bool} (hV : ∀ a w, R a w ↔ V (a, w) = true)
+  (hD : ∀ a u, D (a, u) = true ↔ ∃ v, R a (u ++ v))
+/-- A solution is kept by the search. -/
+theorem foldl_prefixSearchStep_of_rel {a : α} {u : List Bool} (hu : R a u) (l : List Bool) :
+    l.foldl (fun u _ => prefixSearchStep V D a u) u = u := by
+    rw [List.foldl_cons, prefixSearchStep, ite_eq_left ((hV a u).1 hu)]
+/-- A step from a word that some solution extends, but that is not a solution, adds one bit and
+theorem prefixSearchStep_spec {a : α} {u : List Bool} (hu : ∃ v, R a (u ++ v)) (hnot : ¬R a u) :
+    (∃ v, R a (prefixSearchStep V D a u ++ v)) ∧
+      (prefixSearchStep V D a u).length = u.length + 1 := by
+  have hVu : ¬V (a, u) = true := fun h => hnot ((hV a u).2 h)
+/-- The search through prefixes keeps a solution extending the word, and the word is a solution or
+has grown by one bit per step. -/
+theorem foldl_prefixSearchStep_spec {a : α} (l : List Bool) {u : List Bool}
+    (∃ v, R a (l.foldl (fun u _ => prefixSearchStep V D a u) u ++ v)) ∧
+      (R a (l.foldl (fun u _ => prefixSearchStep V D a u) u) ∨
+        u.length + l.length ≤ (l.foldl (fun u _ => prefixSearchStep V D a u) u).length) := by
+    · obtain ⟨hstep, hlen⟩ := prefixSearchStep_spec hV hD hu hRu
+/-- **Search through prefixes is correct.** If the solutions of `a` are no longer than `n a`, and
+`a` has a solution, the search through prefixes for `n a` steps finds one. -/
+theorem rel_prefixSearchRun {n : α → ℕ} (hn : ∀ a w, R a w → w.length ≤ n a) {a : α}
+    (ha : a ∈ searchDomain R) : R a (prefixSearchRun V D n a) := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨v, hv⟩, h⟩ := foldl_prefixSearchStep_spec hV hD (List.replicate (n a) false)
+    (u := []) (a := a) (let ⟨w, hw⟩ := ha; ⟨w, by simpa using hw⟩)
+    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_nil, List.length_replicate, zero_add] at hlen this
+/-- The search through prefixes is polynomial-time when `V`, `D` and the number of steps are. -/
+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_prefixSearchRun {V D : α × List Bool → Bool} {n : α → ℕ}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (prefixSearchRun V D n) enc encBits := by
+      (fun y : (α × List Bool) × Bool => prefixSearchStep V D y.1.1 y.1.2)
+    have hu : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun y : (α × List Bool) × Bool => y.1.2)
+    have ha : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun y : (α × List Bool) × Bool => y.1.1)
+        (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBool) encBits := bitsAppend hu (const [b])
+    inferInstance, inferInstance⟩ (growth := fun _ => 1) ⟨.const 1, fun a u _ _ => ?_⟩
+/-- **Search reduces to decision**: if the `NP` problems on pairs of instances and words are in
+`P`, every `FNP` relation is in `FPSearch`. The solver decides the prefix problem, searches through
+    (h : NP (encPair enc encBits) ⊆ P (encPair enc encBits)) : FNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨p, hp⟩, V, hV, hRV⟩ := hR
+  obtain ⟨D, hD, hDR⟩ := h (searchDomain_mem_NP (prefixSearch_mem_FNP ⟨⟨p, hp⟩, V, hV, hRV⟩))
+  let n : α → ℕ := fun a => p.eval (enc a).length
+  have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime n enc encUnary := (unary_eval p).comp (encoding_length enc)
+  refine ⟨⟨⟨p, hp⟩, V, hV, hRV⟩, fun a => if V (a, prefixSearchRun V D n a) then
+    some (prefixSearchRun V D n a) else none, ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+  · exact cond (hV.comp (id'.prod hrun)) ((optionSome encBits).comp hrun) (const none)
+  · have hcorrect := rel_prefixSearchRun hRV (fun a u => (hDR (a, u)).symm) hp (a := a)
+/-- **`FPSearch = FNP` exactly when `P = NP`**, both for every encoding of instances. -/
+    (∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool), FNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc) ↔
+      ∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool), NP enc ⊆ P enc :=
+    fun h _ enc => FNP_subset_FPSearch_of_NP_subset_P (h (encPair enc encBits))⟩
+/-- **`FPSearch = FNP` exactly when `SAT ∈ P`**, by the Cook–Levin theorem. -/
+    (∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool), FNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc) ↔ SAT ∈ P encCNF := by
+  exact ⟨fun h _ e => le_antisymm P_subset_NP (h e), fun h _ e => (h e).ge⟩
+/-- The search problem of `SAT`: certificates for `SAT.verifier`, listing the values of the
+variables in order of first occurrence, that are no longer than the encoded formula. -/
+def searchRel (φ : Logic.PL.CNF ℕ) (w : List Bool) : Prop :=
+/-- The formulas with a solution in `SAT.searchRel` are the satisfiable ones. -/
+/-- **Search to decision for `SAT`**: satisfying assignments are found in polynomial time exactly
+theorem searchRel_mem_FPSearch_iff : searchRel ∈ FPSearch encCNF ↔ SAT ∈ P encCNF := by
+  refine ⟨fun h => searchDomain_searchRel ▸ searchDomain_mem_P h, fun h => ?_⟩
+  have hsearch : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (search D) encCNF encBits :=
+  refine ⟨searchRel_mem_FNP, fun φ => if D φ then some (search D φ) else none,
+    cond hD ((optionSome encBits).comp hsearch) (const none), fun φ => ⟨fun w hw => ?_, ?_⟩⟩
+    exact fun hφ => hDφ ((hSAT φ).1 hφ)

+/-! Concrete clients for `FNP`, `FPSearch`, `TFNP`, disjoint sums and search reductions. -/
+/-! ### A total problem: the empty word solves every instance -/
+/-- Every instance has exactly the empty word as solution. -/
+private def emptyRel (_ : List Bool) (w : List Bool) : Prop := w = []
+  ⟨⟨0, fun _ w h => by simp [emptyRel] at h; simp [h]⟩, fun x => x.2.isEmpty, by fun_prop,
+/-! ### A partial problem: copy the instance, when it starts with `true` -/
+/-- The solution of an instance starting with `true` is the instance itself; other instances have
+private def copyRel (a : List Bool) (w : List Bool) : Prop := a.headD false = true ∧ w = a
+  mem_FNP_iff_exists_bounded.2 ⟨Polynomial.X, fun x => x.1.headD false && decide (x.2 = x.1),
+    by fun_prop, fun a w => by
+      exact ⟨fun ⟨h, hw⟩ => ⟨by simp [hw, encBits], h, hw⟩, fun ⟨_, h, hw⟩ => ⟨h, hw⟩⟩⟩
+/-- The solver of `copyRel` checks the first bit. -/
+private theorem copyRel_mem_FPSearch : copyRel ∈ FPSearch encBits := by
+  refine ⟨copyRel_mem_FNP, fun a => if a.headD false then some a else none, by fun_prop,
+    fun a => ⟨fun w hw => ?_, fun hw ⟨w, h, _⟩ => ?_⟩⟩
+example : searchDomain copyRel ∈ P encBits := searchDomain_mem_P copyRel_mem_FPSearch
+example : searchDomain copyRel ∈ NP encBits := searchDomain_mem_NP copyRel_mem_FNP
+/-- The empty word solves exactly the instances that do not start with `true`. -/
+private def notHeadRel (a : List Bool) (w : List Bool) : Prop := a.headD false = false ∧ w = []
+  ⟨⟨0, fun _ w h => by simp [h.2]⟩, fun x => !x.1.headD false && x.2.isEmpty, by fun_prop,
+    a ∈ searchDomain copyRel ∨ a ∈ searchDomain notHeadRel := by
+/-- The disjoint sum is solved in polynomial time, so the first domain is decided. -/
+    fun a => some (if a.headD false then true :: a else [false]), by fun_prop,
+/-- The total `emptyRel` reduces to the partial `copyRel`: map every instance to `[true]`, whose
+solution is `[true]`, and every solution back to the empty word. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.const _, fun _ _ => ⟨[true], rfl, rfl⟩, fun _ _ _ => rfl⟩
+/-- A reduction to the total `emptyRel` needs only the one-way condition on solutions. -/
+/-- **A complete problem.** `emptyRel` is complete for the total problems solvable in polynomial
+time: such a problem reduces to it by solving the instance in the map back. -/
+example : SearchComplete (fun {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) => TFNP enc ∩ FPSearch enc)
+  refine ⟨⟨emptyRel_mem_TFNP, emptyRel_mem_FPSearch⟩, fun enc R ⟨hR, hR'⟩ => ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgR⟩ := exists_total_of_mem_FPSearch hR' hR.2
+    (hg.comp (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst enc encBits)) fun a _ _ => hgR a
+example : searchDomain SAT.searchRel ∈ NP encCNF := searchDomain_mem_NP SAT.searchRel_mem_FNP
+example : SAT.searchRel ∈ FPSearch encCNF ↔ SAT ∈ P encCNF := SAT.searchRel_mem_FPSearch_iff
+example : (∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool), FNP enc ⊆ FPSearch enc) ↔ SAT ∈ P encCNF :=

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A *parameterized problem* is a problem `A : Set α` with an encoding `enc : α ↪ List Bool` of its
+parameter is any function of the instance: the number of variables of a formula, the size of a
+solution sought, a width. Running times are measured in the parameter `k = κ a` and in the length
+`L` of the encoded instance, on the multi-tape machines of `Cslib.Complexity.DecidableInTimeO`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.FPT enc κ`, **fixed-parameter tractability**: decidability within time
+  `f k * (L + 1) ^ c` up to a constant factor, for some function `f : ℕ → ℕ` and constant `c`.
+  The exponent of `L` does not depend on `k`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.XP enc κ`, **slicewise polynomial time**: decidability within time
+  `f k * (L + 1) ^ g k`, for functions `f` and `g`.
+The function `f` is arbitrary, as in the *uniform* fixed-parameter tractability of Downey and
+Fellows [DowneyFellows1999, Chapter 2]. Flum and Grohe [FlumGrohe2006, Chapter 1] and Cygan et
+al. [CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 1] require `f` to be computable (Downey and Fellows' *strongly
+uniform* tractability); that variant is not formalized here. The function `f` may be taken
+`Cslib.Complexity.FPTReducible encA encB κA κB A B`: `A` reduces to `B` by an *fpt-reduction*
+[FlumGrohe2006, Definition 2.1] [CyganEtAl2015, Definition 13.1]: a map `f` computable within
+`a ∈ A ↔ f a ∈ B` and `κB (f a) ≤ h (κA a)` for a function `h`. Polynomial-time reductions
+fpt-reductions. As for `FPT`, the functions `F` and `h` are arbitrary, where the cited
+  `κ a ≤ h (κ' a)` then tractability in `κ` gives tractability in `κ'`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.mem_FPT_iff_exists_monotone`: the function `f` may be taken monotone.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.DecidableInExpTime.mem_FPT`: time `2 ^ (δ κ a)` times a polynomial is fpt
+  time; so `SAT` and `k`-SAT are fixed-parameter tractable in the number of variables
+  is a preorder; `Cslib.Complexity.FPTReducible.compl` passes to complements.
+* [R. G. Downey, M. R. Fellows, *Parameterized Complexity*][DowneyFellows1999]
+* [M. Cygan, F. V. Fomin, Ł. Kowalik, D. Lokshtanov, D. Marx, M. Pilipczuk, M. Pilipczuk,
+/-- The partial sums of `f` bound `f` from above. -/
+private theorem le_sum_range_succ {f : ℕ → ℕ} {i k : ℕ} (h : i ≤ k) :
+    f i ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), f j :=
+/-- The partial sums of `f` are monotone. -/

+/-- **Fixed-parameter tractability.** `A ∈ FPT enc κ` when `A` is decidable within time
+`f (κ a) * (|enc a| + 1) ^ c` up to a constant factor, for some function `f : ℕ → ℕ` and some

+(`Cslib.Complexity.DecidableInTimeO`). The function `f` is arbitrary, as in the uniform
+fixed-parameter tractability of [DowneyFellows1999]; [FlumGrohe2006] also requires it to be
+def FPT (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (κ : α → ℕ) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (c : ℕ), DecidableInTimeO A enc fun a => f (κ a) * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ c}
+/-- **Slicewise polynomial time.** `A ∈ XP enc κ` when a single machine decides `A` within time
+`f (κ a) * (|enc a| + 1) ^ g (κ a)` up to a constant factor, for some functions `f` and `g`
+[DowneyFellows1999] [FlumGrohe2006]: in particular each slice `{a | κ a = k}` is decidable in
+polynomial time, with a degree depending on `k`. The functions `f` and `g` are arbitrary, where
+[FlumGrohe2006] and [CyganEtAl2015] require them to be computable. -/
+def XP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (κ : α → ℕ) : Set (Set α) :=
+    DecidableInTimeO A enc fun a => f (κ a) * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ g (κ a)}
+variable {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {κ κ' : α → ℕ} {A : Set α}
+    ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (c : ℕ), DecidableInTimeO A enc fun a => f (κ a) * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ c :=
+theorem mem_XP : A ∈ XP enc κ ↔ ∃ f g : ℕ → ℕ,
+    DecidableInTimeO A enc fun a => f (κ a) * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ g (κ a) :=
+/-- Changing the parameter and the functions of a bound of the shape of `XP`. -/

+    (hf : ∀ a, f (κ a) ≤ f' (κ' a)) (hg : ∀ a, g (κ a) ≤ g' (κ' a))
+    (h : DecidableInTimeO A enc fun a => f (κ a) * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ g (κ a)) :
+    DecidableInTimeO A enc fun a => f' (κ' a) * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ g' (κ' a) := by
+  refine h.mono 1 (fun a => ?_) fun a => by positivity
+  have h₁ : (f (κ a) : ℝ) ≤ f' (κ' a) := by exact_mod_cast hf a
+  have h₂ : (((enc a).length : ℝ) + 1) ^ g (κ a) ≤ ((enc a).length + 1) ^ g' (κ' a) :=
+  have := mul_le_mul h₁ h₂ (by positivity) (by positivity)
+theorem FPT_subset_XP : FPT enc κ ⊆ XP enc κ :=
+  fun _ ⟨f, c, h⟩ => ⟨f, fun _ => c, h⟩
+/-- **`P ⊆ FPT`**, for every parameter: a polynomial-time decider is an fpt-time decider with
+theorem P_subset_FPT : P enc ⊆ FPT enc κ := by
+    (mem_DTIME_iff_decidableInTimeO.mp hk).mono 1 (fun a => ?_) fun a => by positivity⟩
+  have : ((enc a).length : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ((enc a).length + 1) ^ k :=
+theorem P_subset_XP : P enc ⊆ XP enc κ :=
+/-- **Changing the parameter.** If `κ a ≤ h (κ' a)` for a function `h`, then a problem that is

+theorem FPT_subset_FPT_of_le_comp {h : ℕ → ℕ} (hκ : ∀ a, κ a ≤ h (κ' a)) :

+      (g := fun _ => c) (g' := fun _ => c) (fun a => le_sum_range_succ (hκ a)) (fun _ => le_rfl)
+/-- **Changing the parameter.** If `κ a ≤ h (κ' a)` for a function `h`, then a problem that is

+theorem XP_subset_XP_of_le_comp {h : ℕ → ℕ} (hκ : ∀ a, κ a ≤ h (κ' a)) :

+  ⟨fun k => ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (h k + 1), f j, fun k => ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (h k + 1), g j,

+/-- **The function of an fpt bound may be taken monotone**: replace `f` by its partial sums. -/

+/-- **Exponential time in the parameter is fpt time.** A decider within time `2 ^ (δ κ a)` times

+theorem DecidableInExpTime.mem_FPT {δ : ℝ} (h : DecidableInExpTime A enc κ δ) :

+/-- `f` is tidily computable in fpt time with respect to the parameter `κ`: within time and space

+def ComputableTidilyInFPTTime {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (encA : α ↪ List Bool)

+/-- The arithmetic of composition: a bound `F₂ (n + 1) ^ e` on an output of length `n` within

+/-- **Composition in fpt time**, along a function that bounds the parameter. -/

+/-- Bounds of the shape `T a`, cast to the reals, are tidy bounds. -/

+/-- **`FPT` in terms of fpt-time computability**: a problem is fixed-parameter tractable exactly

+/-- **Bounded parameters.** For a parameter bounded by a constant, `FPT` is `P`. -/

+  obtain ⟨g, f, e, hg, hA⟩ := mem_XP_iff_exists_computableTidilyInO.mp hA

+def FPTReducible {α β : Type*} (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (κA : α → ℕ)
+    (κB : β → ℕ) (A : Set α) (B : Set β) : Prop :=

+# Scalar query-activity run capacity and Cover enumerative coding
+When every gate of a weighted threshold program `p` reads the original inputs along a single
+direction `w : Fin n → ℝ` (`∀ j, ∃ c : ℝ, inputWeight p j = c • w`), fixing the restricted
+input-reading transcript `transcript p x` turns every gate condition into a half-line condition on
+the scalar score `scalarScore w x = ∑ i, w i * (x i).toNat`. Consequently, the fibers of
+`transcript p` (and of the full gate evaluation `p.eval interpretation`) are order-convex along
+Extending the evaluation from the finite set of realized scalar scores to all of `ℝ` produces a
+one-dimensional step function `scalarEval p w : ℝ → (Fin g → Bool)` whose level sets are indexed
+by the monotone count of transcripts realized up to `t`. This yields at most
+(`changesAtMost_scalarReadout`), bounding the length of any score-ordered alternating run of
+outputs by `(attainableTranscripts p).card` and hence by the Hamming-ball sums at `inputActivity p`
+one-dimensional representation with the multilevel rectangle-free capacity bound gives the scalar
+Finally, we formalize Cover's lexicographic rank (`coverRank`) and greedy threshold decoder
+(`coverDecode`) establishing an explicit bijection between `{z : Fin q → Bool | weight z ≤ e}` and
+`Fin (ballSize q e)` (the combinatorial core of Theorem 4.3).
+  input-reading transcripts, and readouts to `ℝ` along `scalarScore w`.
+  enumerative encoding and decoding of weight-bounded Boolean words.
+  of gate evaluations and transcripts along `scalarScore w`.
+* [*Threshold Circuits as Decision Trees and Finite-State Programs*, Section 4]
+/-! ### Section 4.1: Order-convexity of scalar-direction transcripts and run capacity -/
+/-- The scalar score `∑ i, w i * (x i).toNat` of a Boolean input `x` along direction `w`. -/
+def scalarScore (w : Fin n → ℝ) (x : Fin n → Bool) : ℝ :=
+  ∑ i : Fin n, w i * (x i).toNat
+private theorem sum_inputWeight_eq_mul_scalarScore {p : Program signature n g} {w : Fin n → ℝ}
+    {j : Fin g} {c : ℝ} (hc : inputWeight p j = c • w) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
+    (∑ i : Fin n, inputWeight p j i * (x i).toNat) = c * scalarScore w x := by
+  have hfun := fun i => congrFun hc i
+/-- **Order-convexity of gate evaluations along a scalar direction**: if every gate's input weight
+vector is a multiple of `w`, `scalarScore w x₁ ≤ scalarScore w x₂ ≤ scalarScore w x₃`, and
+`transcript p x₁ = transcript p x₃`, then `p.eval interpretation x₂ = p.eval interpretation x₁`. -/
+theorem eval_eq_of_scalarScore_between (p : Program signature n g) (w : Fin n → ℝ)
+    (hw : ∀ j : Fin g, ∃ c : ℝ, inputWeight p j = c • w)
+    (h₁₂ : scalarScore w x₁ ≤ scalarScore w x₂)
+    (h₂₃ : scalarScore w x₂ ≤ scalarScore w x₃)
+    (htr : transcript p x₁ = transcript p x₃) :
+    p.eval interpretation x₂ = p.eval interpretation x₁ := by
+  have heval₁₃ : p.eval interpretation x₁ = p.eval interpretation x₃ :=
+    have hgate₁ := eval_gate_eq p x₁ j
+    have hgate₂ := eval_gate_eq p x₂ j
+    have hgate₃ := eval_gate_eq p x₃ j
+    rw [sum_inputWeight_eq_mul_scalarScore hc] at hgate₁ hgate₂ hgate₃
+    have hsum₂₁ : (∑ k : Fin g, gateWeight p j k * (p.eval interpretation x₂ k).toNat) =
+        ∑ k : Fin g, gateWeight p j k * (p.eval interpretation x₁ k).toNat := by
+    have hsum₃₁ : (∑ k : Fin g, gateWeight p j k * (p.eval interpretation x₃ k).toNat) =
+        ∑ k : Fin g, gateWeight p j k * (p.eval interpretation x₁ k).toNat := by
+    have hj₁₃ : p.eval interpretation x₁ j = p.eval interpretation x₃ j :=
+    rcases le_total 0 c with hc0 | hc0
+    · have hle₁₂ : c * scalarScore w x₁ ≤ c * scalarScore w x₂ :=
+      have hle₂₃ : c * scalarScore w x₂ ≤ c * scalarScore w x₃ :=
+      exact ⟨fun h₂ => hj₁₃.mpr (by linarith), fun h₁ => by linarith⟩
+    · have hle₂₁ : c * scalarScore w x₂ ≤ c * scalarScore w x₁ :=
+      have hle₃₂ : c * scalarScore w x₃ ≤ c * scalarScore w x₂ :=
+      exact ⟨fun h₂ => by linarith, fun h₁ => by linarith [hj₁₃.mp h₁]⟩
+/-- **Order-convexity of input-reading transcripts along a scalar direction**. -/
+theorem transcript_eq_of_scalarScore_between (p : Program signature n g) (w : Fin n → ℝ)
+    (hw : ∀ j : Fin g, ∃ c : ℝ, inputWeight p j = c • w)
+    (h₁₂ : scalarScore w x₁ ≤ scalarScore w x₂)
+    (h₂₃ : scalarScore w x₂ ≤ scalarScore w x₃)

+/-! ### Internal gate support and syntactic bias menus -/
+/-- Earlier gates with a nonzero aggregated internal weight into `gate`. -/

+/-- The syntactic menu of all possible internal gate biases at `gate` over Boolean valuations of
+noncomputable def biasMenu (p : Program signature n g) (gate : Fin g) : Finset ℝ :=

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+An in-place machine has one writable tape whose cells are exactly the `n` input cells, a finite
+tape alphabet `Γ`, `h` heads sharing those `n` cells, and a finite control `Q`. Moves past `0` or
+`n - 1` clamp at the boundary (`Move.apply`), and when multiple heads write to the same cell in one
+step, the highest head index wins (`writeHeads`). Because native `Turing.Cfg` has a read-only
+input, separate unbounded work tapes, and a write-only output, this fixed-length shared-tape
+configuration map is formalized as a standalone finite dynamical system rather than an instance of
+This module defines configurations `(w, p, q)` with `w : Fin n → Γ`, `p : Fin h → Fin n`, and
+`q : Q`, the one-step map `Machine.step`, and the finite set `reach M n` of configurations

+the conditional halting characterization after `|Γ|^n * n^h * |Q|` steps under absorbing halting

+`fixed_power_encoded` to the forward-invariant reachable set `reach M n`, assuming an encoding
+`e : Config Q Γ n h → BitString w` injective on `reach M n`, a circuit `c` computing `M.step` on

+rather than compiling `M.δ` into gates). In `inplace_halting`, the circuit outputs the encoded

+projection `tape : Fin m → Fin w` satisfying `∀ x, e (M.init x) ∘ tape = x`.

+  halting iff the run ever halts, and equals the halting configuration when it does.
+/-- A head move. Moves past either end of the tape leave the head in place. -/
+/-- Apply a clamped move to a head position. -/
+def Move.apply {n : ℕ} : Move → Fin n → Fin n
+  | .left, p => if hp : 0 < p.val then ⟨p.val - 1, by omega⟩ else p
+  | .right, p => if hp : p.val + 1 < n then ⟨p.val + 1, hp⟩ else p
+/-- An in-place machine with `h` heads. The transition reads the state, the symbols under the
+heads, and for each head whether it is on the first and on the last cell. It returns the new
+state, a symbol to write under each head, and a move for each head. -/
+structure Machine (Q : Type u) (Γ : Type v) (h : ℕ) where
+  /-- The transition function returning the next state, written symbols, and head moves. -/
+  δ : Q → (Fin h → Γ) → (Fin h → Bool) → (Fin h → Bool) → Q × (Fin h → Γ) × (Fin h → Move)
+  /-- The halting predicate on control states. -/
+/-- Configurations: tape contents, head positions, and control state. -/
+abbrev Config (Q : Type u) (Γ : Type v) (n h : ℕ) := (Fin n → Γ) × (Fin h → Fin n) × Q
+variable {Q : Type u} {Γ : Type v} {n h : ℕ}
+/-- Write under the heads in order of increasing index, so the largest index wins. -/
+def writeHeads (w : Fin n → Γ) (p : Fin h → Fin n) (σ : Fin h → Γ) : Fin n → Γ :=
+  Fin.foldl h (fun w j => Function.update w (p j) (σ j)) w
+/-- A cell under no head is unchanged. -/
+theorem writeHeads_of_forall_ne (w : Fin n → Γ) (p : Fin h → Fin n) (σ : Fin h → Γ) (i : Fin n)
+    (hi : ∀ j, p j ≠ i) : writeHeads w p σ i = w i := by
+    exact ih (fun j => p j.castSucc) (fun j => σ j.castSucc) (fun j => hi _)
+/-- Rewriting the symbols read leaves the tape unchanged. -/
+theorem writeHeads_read (w : Fin n → Γ) (p : Fin h → Fin n) :
+    writeHeads w p (fun j => w (p j)) = w := by
+/-- The one-step map of an in-place machine. -/
+def Machine.step (M : Machine Q Γ h) (z : Config Q Γ n h) : Config Q Γ n h :=
+  let out := M.δ z.2.2 (fun j => z.1 (z.2.1 j)) (fun j => decide ((z.2.1 j).val = 0))
+  (writeHeads z.1 z.2.1 out.2.1, fun j => (out.2.2 j).apply (z.2.1 j), out.1)
+/-- The initial configuration: the input on the tape, every head on the first cell. -/
+def Machine.init [NeZero n] (M : Machine Q Γ h) (x : BitString n) : Config Q Γ n h :=
+/-- Halting states are absorbing: they write the symbols read, do not move, and keep the state. -/
+def Machine.HaltingAbsorbing (M : Machine Q Γ h) : Prop :=
+  ∀ q, M.halting q → ∀ r a b, M.δ q r a b = (q, r, fun _ => Move.stay)
+theorem Machine.step_of_halting {M : Machine Q Γ h} (hM : M.HaltingAbsorbing)
+    (z : Config Q Γ n h) (hz : M.halting z.2.2) : M.step z = z := by
+  simp only [Machine.step, hM q hz, writeHeads_read, Move.apply]
+    Fintype.card (Config Q Γ n h) = Fintype.card Γ ^ n * n ^ h * Fintype.card Q := by
+  simp only [Config, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin, Nat.mul_assoc]
+/-- The configurations reachable from some initial configuration. -/
+noncomputable def reach (M : Machine Q Γ h) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : Finset (Config Q Γ n h) :=
+  Finset.univ.filter fun z => ∃ x t, M.step^[t] (M.init x) = z
+theorem mem_reach {z : Config Q Γ n h} :
+    z ∈ reach M n ↔ ∃ x t, M.step^[t] (M.init x) = z := by
+theorem init_mem_reach (x : BitString n) : M.init x ∈ reach M n :=
+theorem iterate_mem_reach (x : BitString n) (t : ℕ) : M.step^[t] (M.init x) ∈ reach M n :=
+/-- The reachable set is forward invariant. -/
+theorem step_mem_reach {z : Config Q Γ n h} (hz : z ∈ reach M n) : M.step z ∈ reach M n := by
+/-- Every configuration is counted in the configuration bound. -/
+    (reach M n).card ≤ Fintype.card Γ ^ n * n ^ h * Fintype.card Q :=
+  card_config (Q := Q) (Γ := Γ) (n := n) (h := h) ▸ Finset.card_le_univ _
+/-- Reachable configurations are covered by the first `B` steps from every input. -/
+      ∃ y, ∃ j < B, M.step^[t] (M.init x) = M.step^[j] (M.init y)) :
+  have hsub : reach M n ⊆ (Finset.univ ×ˢ Finset.range B).image
+      (fun xj : BitString n × ℕ => M.step^[xj.2] (M.init xj.1)) := by
+    obtain ⟨y, j, hj, he⟩ := hcover x t
+    exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(y, j), by simp [hj], he.symm⟩
+/-- Under a halting-time bound `t`, at most `2 ^ n * (t + 1)` configurations are reachable. -/
+    (ht : ∀ x : BitString n, ∃ s ≤ t, M.halting (M.step^[s] (M.init x)).2.2) :
+  refine reach_card_le_of_cover M (t + 1) fun x r => ?_
+    have hfix := Function.iterate_fixed (M.step_of_halting hM _ hh) (r - s)
+    rw [← Function.iterate_add_apply, Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega)] at hfix
+/-- Running `τ * m` steps of a machine with rounds of length `τ` runs `m` rounds. -/
+theorem iterate_rounds (τ : ℕ) (P : BitString n → BitString n)
+    (hround : ∀ x, M.step^[τ] (M.init x) = M.init (P x)) (x : BitString n) (m : ℕ) :
+    M.step^[τ * m] (M.init x) = M.init (P^[m] x) := by
+/-- A machine that returns to an initial configuration every `τ` steps reaches at most
+theorem reach_card_le_round (τ : ℕ) (hτ : 0 < τ) (P : BitString n → BitString n)
+  refine reach_card_le_of_cover M τ fun x t => ⟨P^[t / τ] x, t % τ, Nat.mod_lt _ hτ, ?_⟩
+  conv_lhs => rw [← Nat.div_add_mod t τ, Nat.add_comm, Function.iterate_add_apply,
+/-- Under absorbing halting states, the configuration after `|Γ|^n * n^h * |Q|` steps is halting
+if and only if the run ever halts, and equals any halting configuration reached along the run. -/
+theorem iterate_card_halting [Fintype Q] [Fintype Γ] (M : Machine Q Γ h)
+    (hM : M.HaltingAbsorbing) (z : Config Q Γ n h) :
+        M.step^[Fintype.card (Config Q Γ n h)] z = M.step^[t] z := by
+  let H : Config Q Γ n h → Prop := fun z => M.halting z.2.2
+  have ha : absorb M.step H = M.step := by
+  · obtain ⟨t₀, _, hp, hfirst, he⟩ := absorb_iterate_card M.step H z ⟨t, ht⟩
+    have hfix := Function.iterate_fixed (M.step_of_halting hM _ hp) (t - t₀)
+    rw [← Function.iterate_add_apply, Nat.sub_add_cancel ht₀] at hfix
+/-- The integer budget is monotone in the storage count. -/
+theorem powerBudget_mono {w s M M' L : ℕ} (hM : M ≤ M') :
+    powerBudget w s M L ≤ powerBudget w s M' L := by
+  have : M / L ≤ M' / L := Nat.div_le_div_right hM
+/-- The real budget is monotone in the storage count. -/
+theorem optimizedBudget_mono {w s M M' : ℕ} (hM : M ≤ M') :
+    optimizedBudget w s M ≤ optimizedBudget w s M' := by
+variable [Fintype Q] [Fintype Γ] [NeZero n] {w : ℕ} (M : Machine Q Γ h)
+/-- The reachable set fits in the encoding width. -/
+theorem reach_card_le_two_pow (e : Config Q Γ n h → BitString w) (he : Set.InjOn e (reach M n)) :
+  simpa using Finset.card_le_univ ((reach M n).image e)
+/-- Every fixed power on the initial configurations, with any upper bound `R` on the number of
+reachable configurations in the storage term. The initial-encoding circuit `ι` is charged. -/
+theorem inplace_fixed_power (e : Config Q Γ n h → BitString w) (he : Set.InjOn e (reach M n))
+    (hstep : ∀ z ∈ reach M n, c.eval interpretation (e z) = e (M.step z))
+    (hι : ∀ x, ι.eval interpretation x = e (M.init x))
+    (R : ℕ) (hR : (reach M n).card ≤ R) (T L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) (hLw : L ≤ 2 ^ w) :
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (M.step^[T] (M.init x))) ∧
+      out.size ≤ ι.size + 40000 * powerBudget w c.size R L := by
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := fixed_power_encoded M.step (reach M n) e he c
+    (fun z hz => step_mem_reach M hz) hstep T L hL hLw
+    have := powerBudget_mono (w := w) (s := c.size) (L := L) hR
+/-- The square-root form, with any upper bound `R` on the number of reachable configurations. -/
+theorem inplace_fixed_power_optimized (e : Config Q Γ n h → BitString w)
+    (he : Set.InjOn e (reach M n)) (c : Circuit signature w w)
+    (hstep : ∀ z ∈ reach M n, c.eval interpretation (e z) = e (M.step z))
+    (hι : ∀ x, ι.eval interpretation x = e (M.init x))
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (M.step^[T] (M.init x))) ∧
+      (out.size : ℝ) ≤ ι.size + 120000 * optimizedBudget w c.size R := by
+  obtain ⟨L, hL, hLw, hopt⟩ := exists_powerBudget_le_optimizedBudget w c.size (reach M n).card
+  obtain ⟨out, hout, hs⟩ := inplace_fixed_power M e he c hstep ι hι _ le_rfl T L hL hLw
+  have hs' : (out.size : ℝ) ≤ ι.size + 40000 * (powerBudget w c.size (reach M n).card L : ℝ) := by
+  have hm := optimizedBudget_mono (w := w) (s := c.size) hR
+/-- The alphabet bound: the storage term is the number of configurations. -/
+theorem inplace_configs_optimized (e : Config Q Γ n h → BitString w)
+    (he : Set.InjOn e (reach M n)) (c : Circuit signature w w)
+    (hstep : ∀ z ∈ reach M n, c.eval interpretation (e z) = e (M.step z))
+    (hι : ∀ x, ι.eval interpretation x = e (M.init x)) (T : ℕ) :
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (M.step^[T] (M.init x))) ∧
+        optimizedBudget w c.size (Fintype.card Γ ^ n * n ^ h * Fintype.card Q) :=
+  inplace_fixed_power_optimized M e he c hstep ι hι _ (reach_card_le_configs M) T
+/-- The time bound: under absorbing halting states and a halting time `t`, the storage term is
+    (ht : ∀ x : BitString n, ∃ s ≤ t, M.halting (M.step^[s] (M.init x)).2.2)
+    (e : Config Q Γ n h → BitString w)
+    (he : Set.InjOn e (reach M n)) (c : Circuit signature w w)
+    (hstep : ∀ z ∈ reach M n, c.eval interpretation (e z) = e (M.step z))
+    (hι : ∀ x, ι.eval interpretation x = e (M.init x)) (T : ℕ) :
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (M.step^[T] (M.init x))) ∧
+      (out.size : ℝ) ≤ ι.size + 120000 * optimizedBudget w c.size (2 ^ n * (t + 1)) :=
+  inplace_fixed_power_optimized M e he c hstep ι hι _ (reach_card_le_time M hM t ht) T
+/-- Halting, the halting state, and the final configuration of a machine that need not halt:
+one circuit returns the encoding of the configuration after `|Γ|^n * n^h * |Q|` steps. It is a
+halting configuration exactly when the run halts, and it is then the final configuration. -/
+theorem inplace_halting (hM : M.HaltingAbsorbing) (e : Config Q Γ n h → BitString w)
+    (he : Set.InjOn e (reach M n)) (c : Circuit signature w w)
+    (hstep : ∀ z ∈ reach M n, c.eval interpretation (e z) = e (M.step z))
+    (hι : ∀ x, ι.eval interpretation x = e (M.init x)) :
+    ∃ (out : Circuit signature n w) (final : BitString n → Config Q Γ n h),
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (final x) ∧
+        ∀ t, M.halting (M.step^[t] (M.init x)).2.2 → final x = M.step^[t] (M.init x)) ∧
+        optimizedBudget w c.size (Fintype.card Γ ^ n * n ^ h * Fintype.card Q) := by
+  obtain ⟨out, hout, hs⟩ := inplace_configs_optimized M e he c hstep ι hι
+  exact ⟨out, fun x => M.step^[Fintype.card (Config Q Γ n h)] (M.init x),
+    fun x => ⟨hout x, iterate_card_halting M hM (M.init x)⟩, hs⟩
+variable {m w : ℕ} [NeZero m] (M : Machine Q Γ h)
+/-- A machine whose rounds of `τ` steps apply a map `P : BitString m → BitString m`, and whose
+encoding exposes the input word of an initial configuration as a projection, inherits any circuit
+lower bound for `P^[T]`: if every circuit computing `P^[T]` has size strictly greater than `q`,
+then every circuit computing the `(τ * T)`-th step from `M.init` has size strictly greater than
+theorem round_lower_bound_of_hard (τ T q : ℕ) (P : BitString m → BitString m)
+    (e : Config Q Γ m h → BitString w) (tape : Fin m → Fin w)
+    (hhard : ∀ d : Circuit signature m m, d.Computes interpretation P^[T] → q < d.size)
+    (hout : ∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (M.step^[τ * T] (M.init x))) :
+  have hc : ((Circuit.wiring signature tape).comp out).Computes interpretation P^[T] := by
+    rw [Circuit.eval_comp, hout, iterate_rounds M τ P hround, Circuit.eval_wiring, htape]
+/-- Both sides for a round machine: any circuit lower bound `q` for `P^[T]` transfers to the
+`(τ * T)`-th step of `M`, while every step `T'` has a circuit within the reachable-set upper bound
+`2 ^ m * τ`, given an encoded step circuit. -/
+theorem round_bounds_of_hard [Fintype Q] [Fintype Γ] (τ T q : ℕ) (hτ : 0 < τ)
+    (e : Config Q Γ m h → BitString w) (he : Set.InjOn e (reach M m))
+    (tape : Fin m → Fin w) (htape : ∀ x, e (M.init x) ∘ tape = x)
+    (hhard : ∀ d : Circuit signature m m, d.Computes interpretation P^[T] → q < d.size)
+    (hstep : ∀ z ∈ reach M m, c.eval interpretation (e z) = e (M.step z))
+    (hι : ∀ x, ι.eval interpretation x = e (M.init x)) :
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (M.step^[τ * T] (M.init x))) → q < out.size) ∧
+    ∀ T', ∃ out : Circuit signature m w,
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x = e (M.step^[T'] (M.init x))) ∧
+      (out.size : ℝ) ≤ ι.size + 120000 * optimizedBudget w c.size (2 ^ m * τ) :=
+  ⟨round_lower_bound_of_hard M τ T q P hround e tape htape hhard, fun T' =>
+    inplace_fixed_power_optimized M e he c hstep ι hι _
+      (reach_card_le_round M τ hτ P hround) T'⟩

+# Simulation, hardwiring, and a universal step map
+If `τ` steps of `U` simulate one step of `F` on encoded states, then `τ * T` steps of `U` simulate
+`T` steps of `F` (`iterate_simulation`). When the encoding places the input bits among constant
+bits, a circuit for the power of `U` yields one for the power of `F` with at most two more gates,
+the two constants of the De Morgan basis (`simulation_circuit`).
+The universal step map executes a straight-line program, held in its state, one gate per step, and
+after the last gate copies the output wires back into the input registers (`Universal.step`). One
+round of `G + 1` steps runs any circuit with at most `G` gates (`Universal.step_round`): each gate
+evaluation and the simultaneous output copy/reset each count as one semantic step. Because
+`Universal.Description` and `Universal.Config` carry natural-number wire indices and a
+natural-number program counter (`pc : ℕ`), `Universal.Config` is an unbounded mathematical
+configuration space rather than a finite Boolean state space or the native certified universal
+Turing machine; the generic value carrier `V` uses `[Inhabited V]` as the default for out-of-range
+wire reads and cleared work registers. The circuit reduction `Universal.universal_power_circuit`
+is conditional: it assumes a finite bit encoding `e`, the start-state hardwiring equation `he`, and
+a circuit `u` computing `(Universal.step interpretation)^[(G + 1) * T]` on start states, without
+constructing a global finite state encoding or a circuit for one universal step. A group
+and either factor of a product map (`prodMap_power_circuit`, `prodMap_power_circuit_left`), are
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.hardwired`: place input bits and constants on `m` wires.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.prodMap`: product of two maps on concatenated bit strings.
+  in the state of the universal step map.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.Universal.Config`: configuration of the universal step map.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.Universal.step`: one step of the universal step map.
+  `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.smul_inverse_circuit`: integer powers, iterates, and inverses of
+  a group action by a fixed element.
+  at most `G` gates by `G + 1` steps of the universal map.
+/-- One step of `F` is `τ` steps of `U` on encoded states, hence `T` steps are `τ * T`. -/
+theorem iterate_simulation {α β : Type*} (enc : α → β) (F : α → α) (U : β → β) (τ : ℕ)
+    (h : ∀ x, U^[τ] (enc x) = enc (F x)) (T : ℕ) (x : α) :
+    U^[τ * T] (enc x) = enc (F^[T] x) := by
+  have hs : Function.Semiconj enc F (U^[τ]) := fun x => (h x).symm
+/-- Place input bits and constants on `m` wires. -/
+def hardwired {n m : ℕ} (place : Fin m → Fin n ⊕ Bool) (x : BitString n) : BitString m :=
+  fun j => Sum.elim x id (place j)
+/-- Hardwiring constants and duplicating or permuting inputs costs the two constants. -/
+theorem exists_hardwired_comp {n m p : ℕ} (u : Circuit signature m p)
+      (∀ x, d.eval interpretation x = u.eval interpretation (hardwired place x)) ∧
+  let constants : Set (BooleanFunction n) := {fun _ => false, fun _ => true}
+  have hconst : Synthesis interpretation (inputs n) constants 2 :=
+  have hrange : Set.range (fun j (x : BitString n) => hardwired place x j) ⊆
+    rcases hp : place j with i | b
+    · exact Or.inl ⟨i, funext fun x => by simp [hardwired, hp]⟩
+      · exact Or.inl (funext fun x => by simp [hardwired, hp])
+      · exact Or.inr (funext fun x => by simp [hardwired, hp])
+/-- Hardwire constants, run `u`, and read selected output wires. -/
+theorem exists_hardwired_projection {n m p k : ℕ} (u : Circuit signature m p)
+    (place : Fin m → Fin n ⊕ Bool) (select : Fin k → Fin p) :
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := exists_hardwired_comp u place
+  refine ⟨(Circuit.wiring signature select).comp d, fun x => ?_, ?_⟩
+/-- The circuit consequence of a simulation: `C(F^[T]) ≤ C(U^[τ * T]) + 2` when the encoding
+places the input bits among constants. The circuit for the power of `U` need only be correct on
+theorem simulation_circuit {n m : ℕ} (F : BitString n → BitString n)
+    (place : Fin m → Fin n ⊕ Bool) (select : Fin n → Fin m)
+    (hsel : ∀ i, place (select i) = Sum.inl i) (τ : ℕ)
+    (hsim : ∀ x, U^[τ] (hardwired place x) = hardwired place (F x)) (T : ℕ)
+      d.Computes interpretation F^[T] ∧ d.size ≤ u.size + 2 := by
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := exists_hardwired_projection u place select
+  rw [hd x, hu x, iterate_simulation (hardwired place) F U τ hsim T x]
+/-- The product of two maps on concatenated bit strings. -/
+def prodMap {m k : ℕ} (U : BitString m → BitString m) (P : BitString k → BitString k)
+  Fin.append (U (fun i => z (Fin.castAdd k i))) (P (fun i => z (Fin.natAdd m i)))
+/-- Each power of a product map is at least as hard as the same power of its second factor: fix the
+first factor's input and read the second factor's outputs. -/
+theorem prodMap_power_circuit {m k : ℕ} (U : BitString m → BitString m)
+    (P : BitString k → BitString k) (T : ℕ) (u : Circuit signature (m + k) (m + k))
+      d.Computes interpretation P^[T] ∧ d.size ≤ u.size + 2 := by
+  let a : BitString m := fun _ => false
+  let place : Fin (m + k) → Fin k ⊕ Bool :=
+    Fin.append (fun _ : Fin m => Sum.inr false) Sum.inl
+  have hpl (y : BitString k) : ∀ b : BitString m, (∀ i, b i = false) →
+      hardwired place y = Fin.append b y := by
+      (prodMap U P)^[T] (Fin.append a y) = Fin.append (U^[T] a) (P^[T] y) := by
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := exists_hardwired_projection u place (Fin.natAdd m)
+  rw [hd y, hu, hpl y a (fun _ => rfl), hsim T y]
+/-- Each power of a product map is at least as hard as the same power of its first factor. -/
+theorem prodMap_power_circuit_left {m k : ℕ} (U : BitString m → BitString m)
+    (P : BitString k → BitString k) (T : ℕ) (u : Circuit signature (m + k) (m + k))
+      d.Computes interpretation U^[T] ∧ d.size ≤ u.size + 2 := by
+  let a : BitString k := fun _ => false
+  let place : Fin (m + k) → Fin m ⊕ Bool :=
+    Fin.append Sum.inl (fun _ : Fin k => Sum.inr false)
+  have hpl (y : BitString m) : hardwired place y = Fin.append y a := by
+      (prodMap U P)^[T] (Fin.append y a) = Fin.append (U^[T] y) (P^[T] a) := by
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := exists_hardwired_projection u place (Fin.castAdd k)
+  rw [hd y, hu, hpl y, hsim T y]
+/-! ### Group actions by a hardwired element -/
+/-- The permutation `x ↦ g • x` of a group action has inverse `x ↦ g⁻¹ • x`. -/
+theorem smul_perm_symm {G α : Type*} [Group G] [MulAction G α] (g : G) :
+    ⇑(MulAction.toPerm g : Equiv.Perm α).symm = fun x => g⁻¹ • x := by
+/-- If a circuit evaluates a group action on encodings of elements and points, every integer power
+of the action of a fixed element, including the inverse permutation, has a circuit with at most two
+theorem smul_zpow_circuit {G α : Type*} [Group G] [MulAction G α] {k n : ℕ}
+    (encG : G → BitString k) (enc : α → BitString n)
+    (hact : ∀ (g : G) (x : α), act.eval interpretation (Fin.append (encG g) (enc x)) =
+      (∀ x, d.eval interpretation (enc x) = enc (g ^ T • x)) ∧
+  let place : Fin (k + n) → Fin n ⊕ Bool :=
+    Fin.append (fun i => Sum.inr (encG (g ^ T) i)) Sum.inl
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := exists_hardwired_comp act place
+/-- Every power of the action of a fixed element, as an iterate. -/
+theorem smul_iterate_circuit {G α : Type*} [Group G] [MulAction G α] {k n : ℕ}
+    (encG : G → BitString k) (enc : α → BitString n)
+    (hact : ∀ (g : G) (x : α), act.eval interpretation (Fin.append (encG g) (enc x)) =
+      (∀ x, d.eval interpretation (enc x) = enc ((fun y : α => g • y)^[T] x)) ∧
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := smul_zpow_circuit encG enc act hact g T
+  exact ⟨d, fun x => by rw [hd, smul_iterate, zpow_natCast], hs⟩
+/-- The inverse of the action of a fixed element. -/
+theorem smul_inverse_circuit {G α : Type*} [Group G] [MulAction G α] {k n : ℕ}
+    (encG : G → BitString k) (enc : α → BitString n)
+    (hact : ∀ (g : G) (x : α), act.eval interpretation (Fin.append (encG g) (enc x)) =
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := smul_zpow_circuit encG enc act hact g (-1)
+  exact ⟨d, fun x => by rw [hd, smul_perm_symm, zpow_neg_one], hs⟩
+/-- The iterator of `(g, x) ↦ (g, g • x)` raises the carried element to the `t`th power. -/
+theorem pairAction_iterate {G α : Type*} [Monoid G] [MulAction G α] (t : ℕ) (g : G) (x : α) :
+  | succ t ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, pow_succ', mul_smul]
+variable {σ : Signature.{v}} {V : Type w} [Inhabited V] {n G : ℕ}
+/-- A straight-line program held in the state: each of `G` entries is an operation with operand
+indices, and `outputs` lists the wires copied back to the input registers. Index `i < n` names
+input `i`, and index `n + j` names work register `j`. -/
+  /-- The `G` gate entries, each pairing an operation with its operand wire indices. -/
+  entries : Fin G → Σ op : σ.Op, Fin (σ.Arity op) → ℕ
+  /-- The indices of the wires copied back into the `n` input registers after a round. -/
+/-- A state of the universal map: the program, the input registers, the work registers, and an
+unbounded natural-number program counter. Because `desc` carries natural-number wire indices and
+`pc : ℕ`, this is an infinite mathematical configuration space rather than a finite Boolean state
+structure Config (σ : Signature.{v}) (V : Type w) (n G : ℕ) where
+  /-- The straight-line program description held in the state. -/
+/-- Read the register with a given index. Indices out of range read the default value of `V`. -/
+def read (x : Fin n → V) (w : Fin G → V) (i : ℕ) : V :=
+  if h : i < n then x ⟨i, h⟩ else if h' : i - n < G then w ⟨i - n, h'⟩ else default
+/-- One semantic step: evaluate entry `pc` into work register `pc`, or, when `pc ≥ G`,
+simultaneously copy the outputs into the input registers, clear the work registers to `default`,
+def step (I : Interpretation σ V) (s : Config σ V n G) : Config σ V n G :=
+        (I (s.desc.entries ⟨s.pc, h⟩).1 fun k => read s.x s.w ((s.desc.entries ⟨s.pc, h⟩).2 k))
+      x := fun i => read s.x s.w (s.desc.outputs i)
+/-- The index of a CSLib wire. -/
+def wireIndex {g : ℕ} : Wire n g → ℕ
+/-- The description of a circuit with at most `G` gates, padded by copies of `pad`. -/
+def describe (G : ℕ) (c : Circuit σ n n) (pad : σ.Op) : Description σ n G where
+      ⟨(c.program.lines ⟨k, h⟩).op, fun a => wireIndex ((c.program.lines ⟨k, h⟩).wires a)⟩
+def start (D : Description σ n G) (x : Fin n → V) : Config σ V n G :=
+/-- The widened lines of a program read only earlier gates. -/
+theorem lines_wire_lt {g : ℕ} (p : Program σ n g) (j : Fin g) :
+      (p.lines j).wires a = Wire.gate b → b.val < j.val := by
+      have h' : (Wire.Renaming.castSucc : Wire.Renaming n g (g + 1)) (line.wires a) =
+      | input i => rw [hw] at h'; cases h'
+      have h' : (Wire.Renaming.castSucc : Wire.Renaming n g (g + 1)) ((p.lines j).wires a) =
+      | input i => rw [hw] at h'; cases h'
+        simpa using ih j a b' hw
+/-- Reading a wire by its index, from work registers that hold the gate values. -/
+theorem read_wireIndex {g : ℕ} (x : Fin n → V) (w : Fin G → V) (e : Fin g → V)
+    (wire : Wire n g) (hlt : ∀ b : Fin g, wire = Wire.gate b → b.val < G)
+    (hw : ∀ (b : Fin g) (h : b.val < G), wire = Wire.gate b → w ⟨b, h⟩ = e b) :
+    read x w (wireIndex wire) = Wire.elim x e wire := by
+    have hr : read x w (n + b.val) = w ⟨b, hb⟩ := by
+    simpa [wireIndex, Wire.elim] using hr.trans (hw b hb rfl)
+/-- After `k ≤ G` steps from the start state, the first `k` work registers hold the values of the
+theorem run (I : Interpretation σ V) (c : Circuit σ n n) (pad : σ.Op) (hG : c.size ≤ G)
+    ∀ k ≤ G, ∃ w : Fin G → V,
+      (step I)^[k] (start (describe G c pad) x) = ⟨describe G c pad, x, w, k⟩ ∧
+      ∀ (j : Fin G), j.val < k → ∀ (hs : j.val < c.size),
+        w j = c.program.eval I x ⟨j, hs⟩ := by
+  | zero => intro _; exact ⟨fun _ => default, rfl, fun _ hj => by omega⟩
+    have hkG : k < G := by omega
+    let v : V := I ((describe G c pad).entries ⟨k, hkG⟩).1 fun a =>
+      read x w (((describe G c pad).entries ⟨k, hkG⟩).2 a)
+        have hent : (describe G c pad).entries ⟨k, hkG⟩ =
+              fun a => wireIndex ((c.program.lines ⟨k, hks⟩).wires a)⟩ := by simp [describe, hks]
+        rw [hent, ← Program.lines_eval c.program I x ⟨k, hks⟩]
+          have hbk : b.val < k := lines_wire_lt c.program ⟨k, hks⟩ a b hb
+          have hbk : b.val < k := lines_wire_lt c.program ⟨k, hks⟩ a b hb
+        have hjk' : j.val ≠ k := fun h => hjk (Fin.ext h)
+/-- One round of `G + 1` steps of the universal map runs a circuit with at most `G` gates and
+theorem step_round (I : Interpretation σ V) (c : Circuit σ n n) (pad : σ.Op)
+    (step I)^[G + 1] (start (describe G c pad) x) = start (describe G c pad) (c.eval I x) := by
+  obtain ⟨w, hrun, hw⟩ := run I c pad hG x G le_rfl
+/-- `(G + 1) * T` steps of the universal map run `T` rounds of the circuit. -/
+theorem step_iterate (I : Interpretation σ V) (c : Circuit σ n n) (pad : σ.Op)
+    (hG : c.size ≤ G) (T : ℕ) (x : Fin n → V) :
+    (step I)^[(G + 1) * T] (start (describe G c pad) x) =
+      start (describe G c pad) ((c.eval I)^[T] x) :=
+  iterate_simulation (start (describe G c pad)) (c.eval I) (step I) (G + 1)
+    (step_round I c pad hG) T x
+/-- The conditional circuit consequence: assuming a bit encoding `e` of universal-map states that
+writes the input registers of a start state directly and fixes its other bits to constants
+determined by the description (`he`), together with a circuit `u` for the `(G + 1) * T`-th power of
+`Universal.step` on those start states (`hu`), one obtains a circuit for the `T`th power of `c`
+with at most two more gates. Neither `e` nor a circuit for one universal step is constructed
+theorem universal_power_circuit {m : ℕ} (c : Circuit signature n n)
+    (e : Config signature Bool n G → BitString m) (place : Fin m → Fin n ⊕ Bool)
+    (select : Fin n → Fin m) (hsel : ∀ i, place (select i) = Sum.inl i)
+    (he : ∀ x, e (start (describe G c pad) x) = hardwired place x)
+    (hu : ∀ x, u.eval interpretation (e (start (describe G c pad) x)) =
+      e ((step interpretation)^[(G + 1) * T] (start (describe G c pad) x))) :
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hs⟩ := exists_hardwired_projection u place select
+  rw [hd x, ← he, hu, step_iterate _ c pad hG, he]

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# The modular-counter permutation: exponential lower bounds, typical powers, and remainders
+On `2 k` bits split into a `k`-bit modulus `a` and a `k`-bit state `b`, `ModulusCounter.power T`
+advances `b` to `(b + T) % a` whenever `0 < a` and `b < a`, and fixes all other states (`advance`).
+For `T = 1`, this defines a permutation `counterStep k = ModulusCounter.power 1` computed by a
+native De Morgan circuit of linear size at most `50 * k + 20 ≤ 50 * (k + 1)`
+Every active modulus `1 ≤ a ≤ 2 ^ k - 1` divides `ModulusCounter.period k = lcm(1, …, 2 ^ k - 1)`,
+and distinct exponents below `ModulusCounter.period k` give distinct Boolean functions
+(`ModulusCounter.powers_injective`). By Chebyshev's lower bound on `lcmUpto (2 ^ k - 1)` and the
+* some exponent `T < ModulusCounter.period k` requires more than `lowerBudget k =
+  matching the `2 ^ Θ(n)` fixed-power upper bound up to the constant factor in the exponent;
+* at most a `2 ^ (-2 ^ (k - 1))` fraction of exponents below `ModulusCounter.period k` have
+  circuits of size at most `lowerBudget k` (`almost_all_counter_powers_hard`);
+* computing `ModulusCounter.power T` is equivalent up to `O(k)` gates to computing the fixed-integer
+  iteration of `counterStep k` is equivalent up to `O(k)` gates to `m`-bit division remainder
+* any exponent `T < 2 ^ m` has a power circuit of size at most `110 * (m + 1) * (k + 1)` via
+  streaming remainders (`ModulusCounter.short_power_circuit`), so every hard power requires an
+  exponent of binary length `m = Ω(2 ^ k / k ^ 2)`
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.counterStep_circuit`: `counterStep k` has a circuit of size at
+  power requiring more than `2 ^ k / (1024 * (k + 1))` gates.
+  `2 ^ (-2 ^ (k - 1))` fraction of powers below `period k` require more than `lowerBudget k` gates.
+/-- Advance `b` by `T` modulo `a` when `0 < a` and `b < a`; inactive pairs are fixed. -/
+def advance (a b T : ℕ) : ℕ := if 0 < a ∧ b < a then (b + T) % a else b
+@[simp] theorem advance_zero (a b : ℕ) : advance a b 0 = b := by
+theorem advance_lt {a b U T : ℕ} (ha : a < U) (hb : b < U) : advance a b T < U := by
+    advance a (advance a b S) T = advance a b (S + T) := by
+  · simp only [advance, h, and_self, ite_true, Nat.mod_lt _ h.1]
+/-- The `k`-bit modulus word in the first `k` coordinates. -/
+def leftWord (x : BitString (k + k)) : BitVec k := word fun i => x (Fin.castAdd k i)
+/-- The `k`-bit counter state word in the last `k` coordinates. -/
+def rightWord (x : BitString (k + k)) : BitVec k := word fun i => x (Fin.natAdd k i)
+/-- Pack a `k`-bit modulus word and a `k`-bit counter state word into `BitString (k + k)`. -/
+def pack (a b : BitVec k) : BitString (k + k) :=
+  Fin.append (fun i : Fin k => a.getLsbD i.val) (fun i : Fin k => b.getLsbD i.val)
+@[simp] theorem leftWord_pack (a b : BitVec k) : leftWord (pack a b) = a := by
+@[simp] theorem rightWord_pack (a b : BitVec k) : rightWord (pack a b) = b := by
+@[simp] theorem pack_words (x : BitString (k + k)) : pack (leftWord x) (rightWord x) = x := by
+  | left i => simp only [pack, leftWord, Fin.append_left, getLsbD_word]
+  | right i => simp only [pack, rightWord, Fin.append_right, getLsbD_word]
+/-- The `T`-step modular counter map on `BitString (k + k)`. -/
+def power (T : ℕ) (x : BitString (k + k)) : BitString (k + k) :=
+  pack (leftWord x) (BitVec.ofNat k (advance (leftWord x).toNat (rightWord x).toNat T))
+@[simp] theorem power_zero (x : BitString (k + k)) : power 0 x = x := by
+    power T (power S x) = power (S + T) x := by
+theorem iterate_power (T : ℕ) : (power (k := k) 1)^[T] = power T := by
+/-- The order `lcm(1, …, 2 ^ k - 1)` common to every active `k`-bit modular counter. -/
+theorem modulus_dvd_period {a : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (haU : a < 2 ^ k) : a ∣ period k := by
+  simpa only [Finset.mem_Icc] using (show 1 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 2 ^ k - 1 by omega)
+theorem power_period (x : BitString (k + k)) : power (period k) x = x := by
+    simpa only [power_add, show 1 + (period k - 1) = period k by omega, power_period] using h
+/-- Different residues modulo `period k` give different Boolean functions. -/
+    Function.Injective (fun T : Fin (period k) => power (k := k) T.val) := by
+  have hmod (a : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (haU : a < 2 ^ k) : S.val % a = T.val % a := by
+    simpa [power, advance, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt haU, ha, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hslt,
+  have helper (S T : ℕ) (hST : S ≤ T)
+      (hmod : ∀ a, 0 < a → a < 2 ^ k → S % a = T % a) : period k ∣ T - S := by
+    have ha' : 1 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 2 ^ k - 1 := Finset.mem_Icc.mp ha
+    have hm : Nat.ModEq a S T := hmod a (by omega) (by have := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := k); omega)
+  rcases le_total S.val T.val with h | h
+  · have hd := helper S.val T.val h hmod
+    have hz := Nat.eq_zero_of_dvd_of_lt hd (by have := T.isLt; omega)
+  · have hd := helper T.val S.val h (fun a ha hU => (hmod a ha hU).symm)
+    have hz := Nat.eq_zero_of_dvd_of_lt hd (by have := S.isLt; omega)
+/-- Next counter word after one step: increment `b` modulo `a` when `b < a`. -/
+def stepValue (a b : BitVec k) : BitVec k :=
+  if b.ult a then if b + 1 = a then 0 else b + 1 else b
+    stepValue a b = BitVec.ofNat k (advance a.toNat b.toNat 1) := by
+    have hs : b.toNat + 1 < 2 ^ k := by have := a.isLt; omega
+    have hn : 1 < 2 ^ k := by have := a.isLt; omega
+      simp [BitVec.toNat_add, BitVec.toNat_ofNat, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hn, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hs]
+    have he : b + 1 = a ↔ b.toNat + 1 = a.toNat := by
+    simp only [stepValue, BitVec.ult, decide_eq_true_eq, h, ite_true, he, advance,
+    · have hlt : b.toNat + 1 < a.toNat := by omega
+      simp only [hsum, BitVec.toNat_ofNat, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hs]
+  · simp only [stepValue, BitVec.ult, decide_eq_true_eq, h, ite_false, advance,
+/-- Equality of two available `k`-bit words costs at most `6 * k + 1` gates. -/
+theorem synthesis_word_eq {n : ℕ} (s : Set (BooleanFunction n)) (a b : BitString n → BitVec k)
+    (ha : ∀ i : Fin k, (fun x => (a x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ s)
+    (hb : ∀ i : Fin k, (fun x => (b x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis interpretation s {fun x => decide (a x = b x)} (6 * k + 1) := by
+  have h := synthesis_bits_eq s (fun x i => (a x).getLsbD i.val)
+    (by rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩; exact ha i) (by rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩; exact hb i)
+      ((fun i : Fin k => (a x).getLsbD i.val) = fun i : Fin k => (b x).getLsbD i.val) ↔
+    ⟨fun h => BitVec.eq_of_getLsbD_eq fun i hi => congrFun h ⟨i, hi⟩,
+      fun h => funext fun i => congrArg (fun v => v.getLsbD i.val) h⟩
+/-- Synthesizing `stepValue (a x) (b x)` from available words and constants costs at most
+    (ha : ∀ i : Fin k, (fun x => (a x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ src)
+    (hb : ∀ i : Fin k, (fun x => (b x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ src)
+    (hc : ∀ v : Bool, (fun _ : BitString n => v) ∈ src) :
+    Synthesis interpretation src (wordWires fun x => stepValue (a x) (b x))
+  let inc := fun x => b x + 1
+  have hadd := Synthesis.word_add (s := src) b (fun _ => (1 : BitVec k)) hb (fun _ => hc _)
+  have hi (i : Fin k) : (fun x => (inc x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ src1 := Or.inr ⟨i, rfl⟩
+  let equal := fun x => decide (inc x = a x)
+  let active := fun x => (b x).ult (a x)
+  have heq := synthesis_word_eq src1 inc a hi (fun i => Or.inl (ha i))
+  have hlt := Synthesis.word_ult (s := src1) b a (fun i => Or.inl (hb i)) (fun i => Or.inl (ha i))
+  let next := fun x => if equal x then (0 : BitVec k) else inc x
+  have hm := Synthesis.word_mux (s := src2) (fun _ => (0 : BitVec k)) inc equal
+  have hm' := Synthesis.word_mux (s := src3) next b active
+  simp only [stepValue, active, next, equal, inc, decide_eq_true_eq]
+/-- The single-step modular counter `power 1` has a De Morgan circuit of size at most
+      c.Computes interpretation (power (k := k) 1) ∧ c.size ≤ 50 * k + 20 := by
+  let a := fun x : BitString (k + k) => leftWord x
+  let b := fun x : BitString (k + k) => rightWord x
+  let constants : Set (BooleanFunction (k + k)) := {fun _ => false, fun _ => true}
+  have hc (v : Bool) : (fun _ : BitString (k + k) => v) ∈ src := by
+  have ha (i : Fin k) : (fun x => (a x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ src := by
+      (show (fun x : BitString (k + k) => x (Fin.castAdd k i)) ∈ src from Or.inl ⟨_, rfl⟩)
+  have hb (i : Fin k) : (fun x => (b x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ src := by
+      (show (fun x : BitString (k + k) => x (Fin.natAdd k i)) ∈ src from Or.inl ⟨_, rfl⟩)
+  have hconst : Synthesis interpretation (inputs (k + k)) constants 2 :=
+  have hstep := synthesis_stepValue src a b ha hb hc
+    (s := inputs (k + k)) (t := inputs (k + k)) Set.Subset.rfl).union hout
+        simp only [power, pack, Fin.append_left, leftWord, getLsbD_word]⟩
+/-! ### Fixed-integer remainders and equivalence with counter powers -/
+/-- Fixed-integer remainder `x ↦ T % x` on `k`-bit words, with `0` on modulus `0`. -/
+def remainder (T : ℕ) (x : BitString k) : BitString k :=
+  fun i => (BitVec.ofNat k (if (word x).toNat = 0 then 0 else T % (word x).toNat)).getLsbD i.val
+      BitVec.ofNat k (if (word x).toNat = 0 then 0 else T % (word x).toNat) := word_getLsbD _
+theorem addResidue_spec (a b r : BitVec k) (T : ℕ)
+    addResidue a b r = BitVec.ofNat k (advance a.toNat b.toNat T) := by
+    have hrlt : r.toNat < a.toNat := by rw [hr ha]; exact Nat.mod_lt _ ha
+    rw [toNat_addResidue a b r h hrlt, hr ha]
+    simp only [advance, ha, h, and_self, ↓reduceIte, BitVec.toNat_ofNat, Nat.add_mod_mod,
+/-- A circuit for `power T` yields a circuit for `remainder T` with at most one extra gate. -/
+theorem remainder_of_power (T : ℕ) (c : Circuit signature (k + k) (k + k))
+      out.Computes interpretation (remainder T) ∧ out.size ≤ c.size + 1 := by
+  let s := inputs k ∪ {fun _ : BitString k => false}
+  let init := fun x : BitString k => pack (word x) (0 : BitVec k)
+  have hi (i : Fin (k + k)) : (fun x => init x i) ∈ s := by
+    | left i => simpa only [init, pack, Fin.append_left, getLsbD_word] using
+        (show (fun x : BitString k => x i) ∈ s from Or.inl ⟨i, rfl⟩)
+    (Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := s) c (fun i x => init x i) hi)
+      wires (fun x => c.eval interpretation (init x)) := by
+    change c.eval interpretation (init x) (Fin.natAdd k i) = remainder T x i
+    · simp only [advance, remainder, hz, lt_self_iff_false, and_self, ite_false, ite_true]
+    · simp only [advance, remainder, hz, Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hz, and_self, ite_true, ite_false,
+  obtain ⟨out, ho, hs⟩ := (h.mono Set.Subset.rfl hout le_rfl).exists_circuit_outputs
+/-- A circuit for `remainder T` yields a circuit for `power T` with at most `100 * (k + 1)` extra
+theorem power_of_remainder (T : ℕ) (c : Circuit signature k k)
+      out.Computes interpretation (power T) ∧ out.size ≤ c.size + 100 * (k + 1) := by
+  let a := fun x : BitString (k + k) => leftWord x
+  let b := fun x : BitString (k + k) => rightWord x
+  let init := fun x : BitString (k + k) => fun i : Fin k => x (Fin.castAdd k i)
+  let r := fun x => word (c.eval interpretation (init x))
+  let s := inputs (k + k) ∪ wires (fun x => c.eval interpretation (init x))
+  have ha : wordWires a ⊆ s := by
+      (show (fun x : BitString (k + k) => x (Fin.castAdd k i)) ∈ s from Or.inl ⟨_, rfl⟩)
+  have hb : wordWires b ⊆ s := by
+      (show (fun x : BitString (k + k) => x (Fin.natAdd k i)) ∈ s from Or.inl ⟨_, rfl⟩)
+  have hr : wordWires r ⊆ s := by
+      (show (fun x => c.eval interpretation (init x) i) ∈ s from Or.inr ⟨i, rfl⟩)
+  have hs := synthesis_addResidue s a b r ha hb hr
+    (s := inputs (k + k)) c (fun i x => init x i) (fun i => ⟨Fin.castAdd k i, rfl⟩)
+      (s ∪ wordWires (fun x => addResidue (a x) (b x) (r x))) (c.size + 100 * (k + 1)) := by

+`BitString (m + K)` that act as a disjoint union of prime-length cycles indexed by `m`-bit hash

+/-- The `m`-bit class word in the first `m` coordinates. -/
+def classWord (x : BitString (m + K)) : BitVec m := word fun i => x (Fin.castAdd K i)
+/-- The `K`-bit position word in the last `K` coordinates. -/
