+  | left i => simp only [pack, classWord, Fin.append_left, getLsbD_word]

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# The native counting-machine characterization of GapP
+Successful witnesses contribute one chosen-sign leaf, and unsuccessful witnesses contribute
+a balanced accepting/rejecting pair. An actual two-occurrence selector combines independently
+sized witness families. No extra coin pads a halted computation. The resulting native gap is
+the difference of the two verifier counts, including odd, negative and zero values.
+All machine parameters and the polynomial clock are fixed before the encoded input. Preparation,
+framing, buffering, verification and routing are actual native machine work. Halting is asserted
+on the encoding's image, and `encBits` specializes this to all binary inputs.
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+The concrete verifier construction and native calculus credits are preserved in
+`MultiTape.Counting.Verifier`; the certified forward checker is in `Classes.SharpP.Machine`.
+/-- A verifier with `N = 2 ^ p(n)` witnesses and `f` successes has routed counts `(N, N-f)`
+for the positive sign and `(N-f, N)` for the negative sign. Routing and buffering are charged. -/
+theorem exists_signed_verifier_machine (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (hverify : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime verifier (encPair enc encBits) encBool) (sign : Bool) :
+    ∃ (k : ℕ) (State : Type) (_ : Finite State) (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State)
+            2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length - Complexity.acceptCount verifier a (p.eval (enc a).length)) ∧
+            2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length - Complexity.acceptCount verifier a (p.eval (enc a).length)
+  obtain ⟨k, State, hfinite, source, sourceClock, hnon, hm⟩ :=
+  refine ⟨_, _, inferInstance, machine, clock, hnon.comp (VerdictMachine.nonblocking sign) true,
+      (Cfg.init source.initial (enc a)), ∃ bit, result.output = encBool bit := by
+      2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length - Complexity.acceptCount verifier a (p.eval (enc a).length) := by
+      2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length - Complexity.acceptCount verifier a (p.eval (enc a).length) by lia)
+    exact HaltsWithin.comp source (verdictMachine sign) hnon (VerdictMachine.nonblocking sign)
+      true (enc a) _ 1 hhalt (fun result _ => VerdictMachine.haltsWithin sign result.output)
+  · have hc := VerdictMachine.branchCount_comp source hnon (enc a) _ hhalt hbool sign true
+    simpa [machine, hclock, acceptCount, initialConfig] using hc
+  · have hc := VerdictMachine.branchCount_comp source hnon (enc a) _ hhalt hbool sign false
+    cases sign <;> simpa [machine, hclock, rejectCount, initialConfig] using hc
+/-- One native selector combines separately prepared verifier families with their original
+witness lengths. Its signed difference is exact; halted branches acquire no padding choices. -/
+theorem exists_verifier_difference_machine (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p q : Polynomial ℕ)
+    ∃ (k : ℕ) (State : Type) (_ : Finite State) (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State)
+  obtain ⟨kp, Sp, hfinitep, mp, tp, hnonp, hp⟩ :=
+    exists_signed_verifier_machine enc p positive hpositive true
+  obtain ⟨kn, Sn, hfiniten, mn, tn, hnonn, hn⟩ :=
+    exists_signed_verifier_machine enc q negative hnegative false
+  let left : MultiTapeCTM (kp + kn) Bool Sp := mp.extendTapes (Fin.castAddEmb kn)
+  let right : MultiTapeCTM (kp + kn) Bool Sn := mn.extendTapes (Fin.natAddEmb kp)
+  refine ⟨kp + kn, _, inferInstance, machine, clock, hleft.alternative hright, fun a => ?_⟩
+  have hclock : clock.eval (enc a).length = tp.eval (enc a).length + tn.eval (enc a).length + 1 :=
+  have hpl : left.HaltsWithin (tp.eval (enc a).length) (Cfg.init left.initial (enc a)) :=
+  have hnl : right.HaltsWithin (tn.eval (enc a).length) (Cfg.init right.initial (enc a)) :=
+          mn.branchCount verdict (tn.eval (enc a).length) (Cfg.init mn.initial (enc a)) := by
+    have hpe : left.branchCount verdict (tp.eval (enc a).length + tn.eval (enc a).length)
+          (Cfg.init mp.initial (enc a)) := branchCount_extendTapes mp _ (enc a) _ verdict
+    have hne : right.branchCount verdict (tp.eval (enc a).length + tn.eval (enc a).length)
+          (Cfg.init mn.initial (enc a)) := branchCount_extendTapes mn _ (enc a) _ verdict
+    change machine.acceptCount _ _ = mp.acceptCount _ _ + mn.acceptCount _ _ at ha
+    change machine.rejectCount _ _ = mp.rejectCount _ _ + mn.rejectCount _ _ at hr
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {g : α → ℤ}
+/-- The verifier definition of GapP equals the accepting-minus-rejecting count of one fixed
+finite native machine with a polynomial all-branches clock in encoded input length. The
+construction has a globally nonblocking table and requires no input-dependent machine advice. -/
+      ∃ (k : ℕ) (State : Type) (_ : Finite State) (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State)
+  · rintro ⟨f₁, ⟨p, positive, hpositive, hf₁⟩, f₂, ⟨q, negative, hnegative, hf₂⟩, hg⟩
+    obtain ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, clock, hnon, hm⟩ :=
+      MultiTapeCTM.exists_verifier_difference_machine enc p q positive negative hpositive hnegative
+    refine ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, clock, hnon, fun a => ⟨(hm a).1, ?_⟩⟩
+    rw [(hm a).2, hg a, hf₁ a, hf₂ a]
+  · rintro ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, clock, _, hm⟩
+    have heq : g = fun a => (machine.acceptCount (clock.eval (enc a).length)
+          (Cfg.init machine.initial (enc a)) := funext fun a => (hm a).2.symm

+On an encoded Boolean verifier result, this fixed one-step machine emits the chosen sign once
+when the result is true. A false result instead produces one accepting and one rejecting branch.
+Thus unsuccessful witnesses cancel in the integer gap, including when the witness length is zero.
+Every local view has a nonempty choice list and all branches halt in one instruction.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.verdictMachine`: the actual one-versus-two native routing machine.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.VerdictMachine.haltsWithin`: one native instruction on any input.
+Balanced accepting/rejecting cancellation is the standard GapP mechanism
+[FennerFortnowKurtz1994]. Native occurrence semantics are credited in `MultiTape.Counting`.
+/-- Emit one Boolean verdict and halt without moving a head. -/

+  tr _ symbol _ _ := (if symbol = some true then [VerdictMachine.halt sign]
+/-- Both the singleton and balanced local choice lists are nonempty. -/
+/-- Every branch halts in one native instruction, even on inputs outside the Boolean encoding. -/
+  have hsame : final = action.apply (Cfg.init () input) := by simpa using hfinal
+  split at haction <;> simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil,
+  · rcases haction with rfl | rfl <;> rfl
+/-- The exact one-step verdict count: unsuccessful witnesses contribute one of each sign. -/
+theorem branchCount_eq (sign bit : Bool) (verdict : List Bool → Bool) :
+  have hsymbol : (Cfg.init () (encBool bit) : Cfg 0 Bool Unit _).inputSymbol = some bit := by
+      if bit then [halt sign] else [halt true, halt false] := by
+    simp only [actions, show (Cfg.init () (encBool bit) : Cfg 0 Bool Unit _).state = some ()

+/-- Buffered routing preserves the chosen-sign branch for every witness and cancels false ones.
+The source must really output encoded Booleans; arbitrary words beginning in `true` are not
+accepted as a substitute. The buffer and its preparation are included in the displayed clock. -/
+theorem branchCount_comp {k : ℕ} {State : Type} (source : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State)
+      ∃ bit, result.output = encBool bit) (sign verdict : Bool) :
+      if sign = verdict then (source.runList fuel (Cfg.init source.initial input)).length
+      else source.rejectCount fuel (Cfg.init source.initial input) := by
+    true input fuel 1 hhalt (fun result _ => haltsWithin sign result.output)]
+  have hsum (items : List (Cfg k Bool State input))
+      (hb : ∀ result ∈ items, ∃ bit, result.output = encBool bit) :
+        if sign = verdict then items.length else items.countP (fun result =>
+      have hrest := ih (fun final hf => hb final (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hf))
+      simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, hrest, List.length_cons, List.countP_cons]

+Adversarial clients for signed native counting: the actual one-step source, buffered router and
+selector have counts `2/1` and `1/2`, not an even multiple of those gaps. Further clients cover
+zero cancellation, different witness lengths, dirty selector tapes and first-halt clock padding.

+The witness-length routine, binary scanner, framed input writer and deterministic verifier
+are actual finite native machines. Singleton lifting and the shared compilers retain every
+occurrence. Polynomial clocks include the unary length computation, framing, buffer preparation
+and tidy workspace restoration. The contracts concern encoded instances; no behavior on
+words outside the instance encoding is asserted.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.exists_framedGuess_machine`: retain the instance in the verifier encoding.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.exists_verifier_machine`: one Boolean result occurrence per witness.
+The guess-and-verify construction is standard in counting complexity [Valiant1979]. Native
+tidy machines and their calculus are by Christian Reitwiessner and Samuel Schlesinger. The
+credit recorded there; the present singleton lift retains exact occurrence multiplicity.

+is fixed before the instance is supplied, and emits each witness once, including the empty word. -/

+  · simpa only [clock, eval_add, eval_ofNat, eval_one] using hhalt

+    simpa [runList, GuessMachine.config, Function.comp_def, encUnary_apply, initialConfig] using
+/-- A tidy frame writer surrounds the complete guessing computation, so the scanner still reads
+only the unary witness length. Every output is exactly the verifier's framed pair encoding. -/
+theorem exists_framedGuess_machine (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ) :

+  obtain ⟨t, s, ht, _, ki, InitState, hfinite', initializer, hi⟩ := hframe

+/-- Run the native verifier once for each witness. Equal Boolean outcomes retain separate List

+theorem exists_verifier_machine (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)

+# Autonomous controllers and affine-payload iteration bounds

+payload map `controlledPayload g a T u` to the payload (`controlledMap_iterate`,
+`controlledBits_iterate`). Whenever the payload maps belong to a composition-closed family

+In particular, affine maps `BitString p →ᵃ[Bool] BitString p` over `Bool` are closed under

+/-! Buffered counting clients with unequal stopping times, duplicate branches, dirty source
+scratch, a moved real input head, blank consumer scratch and ordered nonempty/empty words. -/
+private def write (bit : Option Bool) (next : Option Bool) :
+-- One occurrence emits nothing and halts early. Two identical occurrences write [true, false].
+-- Every actual instruction dirties source scratch and moves the real input head.
+private def chooseWord : MultiTapeCTM 1 Bool Bool where
+  tr state _ _ _ := if state then [write (some false) none]
+    else [write none none, write (some true) (some true), write (some true) (some true)]
+-- Read two symbols in order, checking that the consumer's own scratch is blank.
+-- The final instruction occurs twice, so each source branch has two terminal continuations.
+private def readWord : MultiTapeCTM 1 Bool Bool where
+  tr state symbol work _ := List.replicate (if state then 2 else 1)
+        output := if work 0 = none then symbol else some false
+        state := if state then none else some true }
+private noncomputable def compiled := readWord.comp chooseWord true
+-- Both table contracts are realized, including on all views that are unreachable from init.
+-- Source 2 + buffer preparation (2 + 4) + consumer 2 = 10, with no additional handoff step.
+    true input 2 2 (chooseWord_halts input) (fun result _ => readWord_halts result.output)

+-- The native counts are 4 for the two-symbol word and 2 for the empty word.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Native machine terminal counts belong to #P
+For each fixed finite-control list-choice machine and polynomial clock, both accepting and
+rejecting terminal-branch counts belong to the verifier-defined `#P`. The binary verifiers are
+the actual certified replay programs from `MultiTape.Counting.Checker`, with one fixed-width
+code per occurrence index and uniquely forced terminal padding. Invalid codes count on neither
+side. The result does not identify choices with equal actions or equal successor configurations.
+The clock counts native transitions. Only branches halted by that clock are counted; the existing
+`HaltsWithin` hypothesis additionally guarantees that every branch halts without getting stuck,
+and makes both counts stable at larger clocks. No all-branch halting assumption is needed merely
+to count bounded terminal branches. The machine, finite control, number of tapes and block width
+are fixed before the input is supplied. The reverse verifier-to-machine construction and the full
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.Checker.acceptCount_checkBinary`: exact transfer of either terminal count
+  to the corresponding fixed-length binary verifier count.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.gapCount_mem_GapP`: their integer difference belongs to GapP.
+* [L. Valiant, *The complexity of computing the permanent*][Valiant1979]
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]
+This is the forward counting-machine construction. The shared native machine, binary encoding,
+finite-storage simulation and certified calculus retain their source credits in their modules.
+/-- Every accepting binary word corresponds to exactly one canonical occurrence certificate,
+for either requested terminal verdict. Invalid words contribute to neither count. -/
+    (hbound : ∀ cfg : Cfg k Bool State input, (machine.actions cfg).length ≤ 2 ^ width)
+    Complexity.acceptCount (Checker.checkBinary machine width verdict) input (count * width) =
+  refine Finset.card_bij (fun word _ => binaryIndices count width (List.ofFn word)) ?_ ?_ ?_
+      List.ofFn left = binaryCertificate width (binaryIndices count width (List.ofFn left)) :=
+    have hsmall := machine.decodeCertificate_indices_lt (by positivity) hbound hdecode
+    have hlength : (binaryCertificate width indices).length = count * width := by
+    let word := BitString.ofList (count * width) (binaryCertificate width indices)
+    have hword : List.ofFn word = binaryCertificate width indices :=
+    have hround : binaryIndices count width (List.ofFn word) = indices := by
+    (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State) (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (clock : Polynomial ℕ)
+      (clock.eval (enc a).length) (Cfg.init machine.initial (enc a))) ∈ Complexity.SharpP enc := by
+  have hcodes (input : List Bool) (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input) :
+    fun p => Checker.checkBinary machine width verdict (enc p.1, p.2), ?_, ?_⟩
+/-- For a fixed finite-control native list-choice machine, the number of accepting branches
+halted by a polynomial clock is in #P. A complete all-branch computation additionally uses
+`HaltsWithin`; neither stuck nor unfinished branches are counted. -/
+theorem acceptCount_mem_SharpP [Finite State] (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State)
+  simpa [acceptCount] using verdictCount_mem_SharpP machine enc clock true
+/-- Rejecting terminal branches have their own valid-certificate #P verifier. It complements
+the output verdict while retaining validity, so invalid binary words are never counted. -/
+theorem rejectCount_mem_SharpP [Finite State] (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State)
+  simpa [rejectCount] using verdictCount_mem_SharpP machine enc clock false
+/-- The difference of accepting and rejecting polynomial-clock terminal counts is in GapP.
+This is the forward implication, without a reverse machine construction. -/
+theorem gapCount_mem_GapP [Finite State] (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State)

+# Finite replay of binary counting certificates
+The checker uses the existing finite configuration representation and ordinary native actions.
+Its validity flag is an option: invalid indices and nonzero terminal padding fail, including
+for the rejecting classifier. The empty communication interface introduces no oracle resource.
+The machine, its finite control, number of tapes and block width are fixed; polynomial time is
+in the encoded input/certificate pair, not uniformly in a supplied machine description.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.Checker.indexStep`: a finite-storage occurrence or canonical padding step.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.Checker.output`: finite replay followed by a genuine halting check.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.Checker.checkBinary`: the binary verifier for either terminal verdict.
+  polynomial-time, using finite dispatch and a linear encoded-storage loop invariant.
+The finite configuration, encoding and tidy calculus retain the source credits in their modules.
+Counting semantics and canonical padding are developed in `MultiTape.Counting.Certificate`.
+/-- Existing finite native storage with no communication channels. -/

+/-- Finite-storage replay computes exactly the previously proved certificate decoder's output. -/

+    have hactions : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : Storage k State × ℕ =>

+/-- A replay step retains the existing linear storage bound, including forced terminal padding. -/
+    {finite next : Storage k State} {inputSize steps index : ℕ}
+    (hnext : indexStep machine finite index = some next) :
+/-- The checker stores unconsumed bits and either a live finite replay or a permanent failure. -/

+/-- The compiled loop returns exactly the output of the canonical native decoder. The positive

+        (binaryIndices count width word)).map (fun r => r.2.output) := by
+  have hclock : word.length / width = count := by
+  rw [runBinary, hclock, initial, finishRuntime_iterate_binaryStep machine hlen,
+      (fun p : Runtime k State × Storage k State => finish p.2)
+    (body := fun _ finite => finish finite) (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.const none) hfinish
+  have hempty : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun r : Runtime k State => decide (r.1 = []))
+/-- The actual binary checker retains validity independently of its requested terminal verdict. -/
+def checkBinary (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State) (width : ℕ) (verdict : Bool)
+/-- Each terminal verdict uses the same exact validity condition as the canonical decoder. -/
+    {width count : ℕ} (hwidth : 0 < width) (verdict : Bool) (input : List Bool)
+        (Cfg.init machine.initial input) (binaryIndices count width word) := by
+  rw [checkBinary, finishRuntime_runBinary machine hwidth input hlen]
+/-- Both the accepting and rejecting binary verifiers are polynomial-time on every input pair. -/
+    (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Bool State) (width : ℕ) (verdict : Bool) :
+      (fun p : (List Bool × List Bool) × List Bool => (p.2 == [true]) == verdict)
+      (encPair (encPair encBits encBits) encBits) encBool := by fun_prop
+  have h := hout.optionElimWithInput (body := fun _ out => (out == [true]) == verdict)
+  cases finishRuntime (runBinary machine width p) <;> rfl

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+One fixed machine scans its input, choosing and emitting one bit per symbol, then takes a
+singleton halting instruction. Its occurrence-labelled terminal traces are in bijection with
+Boolean words of the input length. The final instruction makes no discarded binary choice.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.GuessMachine.trace`: the unique occurrence trace for a witness.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.GuessMachine.trace_bijOn`: one terminal branch per length-`n` word.
+The scanner is a prerequisite for a parsimonious guess/verify construction. Deterministic
+verifier composition and the reverse #P/GapP characterizations are not established here.
+The witness-guessing construction is standard in counting complexity [Valiant1979]. The scanner
+and its configuration invariant adapt `MultiTape.Probabilistic.Sampling`, credited there to the
+cslib `crypto` branch at `5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`. Here the List choice interface
+and the singleton halt preserve exact branch multiplicity, rather than only the output law.
+/-- The ordinary instruction for one guessed bit. -/
+  { inputTape := 1, workTapes := Fin.elim0, output := some bit, state := some () }
+/-- The final instruction emits nothing and halts without moving the input head. -/
+  { inputTape := 0, workTapes := Fin.elim0, output := none, state := none }
+/-- Emit one independently chosen bit per input symbol, then take a single halting occurrence. -/
+/-- The scanner at a position in the input, with its current output prefix. -/
+def config (input : List Bool) (state : Option Unit) (index : ℕ) (output : List Bool)
+    (h : index ≤ input.length) : Cfg 0 Bool Unit input where
+/-- Each bit selects its occurrence index; the last zero selects the singleton halt. -/
+def trace (word : List Bool) : List ℕ := word.map Bool.toNat ++ [0]
+    trace (bit :: word) = bit.toNat :: trace word := rfl
+@[simp] theorem length_trace (word : List Bool) : (trace word).length = word.length + 1 := by
+  have hm : first.map Bool.toNat = second.map Bool.toNat := List.append_cancel_right h
+  exact List.map_injective_iff.mpr (fun a b hab => by cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all) hm
+private theorem actions_inner {input output : List Bool} {index : ℕ}
+  have hsym := inputSymbolInner (cfg := config input (some ()) index output (by lia))
+  simp only [actions, show (config input (some ()) index output (by lia)).state = some ()
+    from rfl, guessMachine, hsym, Option.isSome_some, ↓reduceIte, List.map_map]
+    guessMachine.actions (config input (some ()) input.length output le_rfl) = [halt] := by
+    (cfg := config input (some ()) input.length output le_rfl) (Or.inr rfl)
+  simp only [actions, show (config input (some ()) input.length output le_rfl).state = some ()
+    from rfl, guessMachine, hsym, Option.isSome_none, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, List.map_map]
+private theorem apply_emit {input output : List Bool} {index : ℕ}
+      config input none input.length output le_rfl := by
+    guessMachine.step? (config input (some ()) index output (by lia)) choice =
+    guessMachine.step? (config input (some ()) input.length output le_rfl) choice =
+      if choice = 0 then some (config input none input.length output le_rfl) else none := by
+/-- Replaying the bit choices writes that word, without taking the final halting instruction. -/
+theorem runBranch_bits (input output word : List Bool) (index : ℕ)
+      some (config input (some ()) (index + word.length) (output ++ word) h) := by
+  induction word generalizing index output with
+    have hi : index < input.length := by simp only [List.length_cons] at h; lia
+    have hindex : index + 1 + word.length = index + (word.length + 1) := by lia
+      simp only [List.length_cons] at h; lia), List.append_assoc, hindex]
+/-- A word of the remaining length ends at its output and the right boundary. -/
+theorem runBranch_trace (input output word : List Bool) (index : ℕ)
+    guessMachine.runBranch (config input (some ()) index output (by lia)) (trace word) =
+      some (config input none input.length (output ++ word) le_rfl) := by
+  rw [trace, runBranch_append, runBranch_bits input output word index (by lia)]
+    ∀ (index : ℕ) (output : List Bool) (h : index + remaining = input.length),
+    have hi : index = input.length := by lia
+    simp only [actions_boundary, List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hchoice
+    have hi : index < input.length := by lia
+    simp only [actions_inner hi, List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hchoice
+    have hc : choice = 0 ∨ choice = 1 := by lia
+      simpa [actions_inner hi, hc, apply_emit hi] using
+/-- Starting from blank tapes is the zero-position scanner invariant. -/
+    Cfg.init guessMachine.initial input = config input (some ()) 0 [] (Nat.zero_le _) := by
+/-- Every branch halts in `n + 1` transitions, with a nonempty choice list at every live node. -/
+private theorem word_of_runBranch (input : List Bool) (choices : List ℕ) :
+      guessMachine.runBranch (config input (some ()) index output h) choices = some final →
+      final.Halted → ∃ word : List Bool, index + word.length = input.length ∧
+        choices = trace word ∧ final = config input none input.length (output ++ word) le_rfl := by
+    intro index output h final hrun hhalt
+    intro index output h final hrun hhalt
+            rcases this with rfl | rfl <;> rfl
+    · have hi : index = input.length := by lia
+          have heq : config input none input.length output le_rfl = final :=
+          exact ⟨[], by simp, rfl, by simpa using heq.symm⟩
+            (show (config input none input.length output le_rfl).Halted from rfl)] at hrun
+/-- Soundness and completeness of terminal replay, including its exact output. -/
+    guessMachine.runBranch (Cfg.init guessMachine.initial input) choices = some final ∧
+      ∃ word : List Bool, word.length = input.length ∧ choices = trace word ∧
+        final = config input none input.length word le_rfl := by
+      word_of_runBranch input choices 0 [] (Nat.zero_le _) final hrun hhalt
+/-- Every terminal branch has exactly one instruction per input symbol and one final halt. -/
+    (hrun : guessMachine.runBranch (Cfg.init guessMachine.initial input) choices = some final)
+  obtain ⟨word, hlen, rfl, _⟩ := (runBranch_halted_iff input choices final).mp ⟨hrun, hhalt⟩
+/-- The bounded terminal traces are exactly the encoded witnesses, with the exact clock exposed. -/
+theorem mem_branches_iff (input : List Bool) (fuel : ℕ) (choices : List ℕ) :
+        ∃ word : List Bool, word.length = input.length ∧ choices = trace word := by
+    exact ⟨by simpa [hword] using hlen, word, hword, rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨by simpa [hword] using hlen, _, word, hword, rfl, rfl⟩
+/-- Witness words and first-halting occurrence traces are in bijection. -/
+    obtain ⟨_, word, hword, heq⟩ := (mem_branches_iff input _ _).mp hchoices
+/-- The same bijection, enumerated by the existing fixed-width bit-string type. -/
+      Finset.univ.image (fun word : Cslib.BitString input.length => trace (List.ofFn word)) := by
+  simp only [mem_branches_iff, le_refl, true_and, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ]
+/-- There are exactly `2 ^ n` terminal branches, including one when the input is empty. -/
+/-- Counting any output predicate is exactly counting witnesses satisfying that predicate. -/
+theorem branchCount_eq (input : List Bool) (verdict : List Bool → Bool) :
+        some (config input none input.length (List.ofFn word) le_rfl) := by
+    simpa only [List.nil_append] using runBranch_trace input [] (List.ofFn word) 0 (by simp)
+  simp only [branchCount, branches_eq_image, Finset.filter_image, hrun, Option.any_some]
+    ∀ (index : ℕ) (output : List Bool) (h : index + remaining = input.length),
+      (OracleComp.interpret (fun n => List.ofFn (id : Fin n → Fin n))
+          (fun word => config input none input.length (output ++ word) le_rfl)) := by
+    have hi : index = input.length := by lia
+    have hi : index < input.length := by lia
+    simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil, apply_emit hi]
+        (fun word => [config input none input.length (output ++ false :: word) le_rfl])
+        (fun word => [config input none input.length (output ++ true :: word) le_rfl]))
+/-- List interpretation of the shared program returns each word once, in scanner enumeration order.
+The existing bit-string enumeration can use a different order, so the result is a permutation. -/
+    (OracleComp.interpret (fun n => List.ofFn (id : Fin n → Fin n))
+        (fun word => config input none input.length word le_rfl)) := by
+/-- The shared FreeM program generates each word of the input length with multiplicity one. -/
+    (OracleComp.interpret (fun n => List.ofFn (id : Fin n → Fin n))
+      if word.length = input.length then 1 else 0 := by
+      (fun n => List.ofFn (id : Fin n → Fin n))
+    (fun n => List.ofFn (id : Fin n → Fin n))

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+`MultiTapeCTM` specializes the shared multi-tape machine to lists of transition occurrences.
+An occurrence is identified by its list index: two equal actions in the list remain two choices.
+Deterministic instructions have singleton lists. Configurations, actions and tape operations are
+the existing `Turing` ones; no new machine storage or instruction model is introduced.
+A branch records occurrence indices and stops at its first halted configuration. In contrast to
+the upstream unlabelled step relation, halted configurations have no further labelled steps.
+An empty list at a running configuration is stuck, not a rejecting halt.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM`: the list-choice specialization of the common machine.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.lts`: labelled transitions, using the existing `Cslib.LTS` interface.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.runBranch`: replay a list of occurrence indices.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.HaltsWithin`: an all-branches time bound excluding stuck states.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.mem_branches_iff`: the enumeration is exactly the bounded terminal traces.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.HaltsWithin.branches_eq`: larger sufficient clocks preserve every branch.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.exists_branchBound`: finite control and alphabet bound occurrence counts.
+This is operational counting semantics, without a claimed polynomial-time verifier or a new
+storage/instruction model. Canonical certificates are developed in `MultiTape.Counting.Certificate`.
+* [L. Valiant, *The complexity of computing the permanent*][Valiant1979]
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]
+The shared machine calculus is adapted from the cslib `crypto` branch; its source and authors are
+credited in `MultiTape.Machine` and `MultiTape.Machine.Equivalence`. The counting layer retains
+the transition identities forgotten by the relation-based nondeterministic interface.
+/-- A shared-core machine with a finite list of transition occurrences at each local view. -/
+  MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Empty List
+/-- The live transition occurrences, in their specified order. A halted state has no choices. -/
+def actions (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
+/-- Execute one occurrence. Invalid indices and attempts to step a halted configuration fail. -/
+def step? (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (index : ℕ) :
+/-- The native labelled transition system; labels identify occurrences, not their effects. -/
+def lts (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) :
+    Cslib.LTS (Cfg k Symbol State input) ℕ where
+  Tr cfg index next := machine.step? cfg index = some next
+/-- Replay actual transitions, with no implicit padding after halting. -/
+    Cfg k Symbol State input → List ℕ → Option (Cfg k Symbol State input)
+  | cfg, index :: rest => (machine.step? cfg index).bind (fun next => machine.runBranch next rest)
+theorem runBranch_nil (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
+theorem runBranch_cons (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
+      (machine.step? cfg index).bind (fun next => machine.runBranch next rest) := rfl
+/-- Replay is exactly the existing LTS multistep relation, with the occurrence labels retained. -/
+    (cfg final : Cfg k Symbol State input) (choices : List ℕ) :
+    machine.runBranch cfg choices = some final ↔ (machine.lts input).MTr cfg choices final := by
+    exact exists_congr fun next => and_congr_right fun _ => ih next
+    {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.Halted) : machine.actions cfg = [] := by
+    {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.Halted) (index : ℕ) :
+/-- From a halted configuration, only the empty trace can be replayed. -/
+    {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.Halted) (choices : List ℕ) :
+    machine.runBranch cfg choices = if choices = [] then some cfg else none := by
+  | cons index rest => simp [runBranch_cons, machine.step?_of_halted h]
+/-- Replaying concatenated traces is sequential replay; a premature halt cannot be crossed. -/
+    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (first second : List ℕ) :
+      (machine.runBranch cfg first).bind (fun next => machine.runBranch next second) := by
+/-- Enumerate first-halting traces of at most the supplied number of actual transitions. -/
+    ℕ → Cfg k Symbol State input → Finset (List ℕ)
+    {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.Halted) (fuel : ℕ) :
+/-- A labelled step is exactly an in-range list occurrence, even if other occurrences agree. -/
+    (cfg final : Cfg k Symbol State input) (index : ℕ) :
+    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (fuel : ℕ) :
+  cases fuel <;> cases hs : cfg.state <;> simp [branches, hs, Cfg.Halted]
+    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (fuel index : ℕ) (rest : List ℕ) :
+      ∃ next, machine.step? cfg index = some next ∧ rest ∈ machine.branches fuel next := by
+/-- The finite enumeration is exactly the first-halting LTS traces within the given clock. -/
+    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (fuel : ℕ) (choices : List ℕ) :
+    choices ∈ machine.branches fuel cfg ↔ choices.length ≤ fuel ∧
+      ∃ final, machine.runBranch cfg choices = some final ∧ final.Halted := by
+  induction fuel generalizing cfg choices with
+    | cons index rest => cases hs : cfg.state <;> simp [branches, hs]
+/-- Every branch halts within this many actual transitions. Running configurations must have
+at least one occurrence, so a stuck branch cannot make a time bound hold vacuously. -/
+    ℕ → Cfg k Symbol State input → Prop
+  | halt {fuel cfg} (halted : cfg.Halted) : HaltsWithin machine fuel cfg
+/-- A successful replay cannot pass the all-branches halting bound. -/
+    {cfg final : Cfg k Symbol State input} {fuel : ℕ} (h : machine.HaltsWithin fuel cfg)
+    {choices : List ℕ} (hrun : machine.runBranch cfg choices = some final) :
+  induction h generalizing choices final with
+    | cons index rest => simp [runBranch_cons, machine.step?_of_halted halted] at hrun
+      obtain ⟨hi, rfl⟩ := (machine.step?_eq_some_iff cfg nextCfg index).mp hstep
+      simpa only [List.length_cons, Nat.add_le_add_iff_right] using ih ⟨index, hi⟩ hrest
+/-- A sufficient clock can be increased without changing any terminal branch multiplicity. -/
+    {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {fuel larger : ℕ}
+    machine.branches larger cfg = machine.branches fuel cfg := by
+/-- The no-stuck condition guarantees at least one terminal branch. -/
+    {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {fuel : ℕ} (h : machine.HaltsWithin fuel cfg) :
+    refine ⟨0 :: rest, (machine.cons_mem_branches cfg fuel 0 rest).mpr ⟨_, ?_, hrest⟩⟩
+/-- Count terminal branches whose output satisfies a Boolean verdict. A failed replay is never
+def branchCount (machine : MultiTapeCTM k Symbol State) (verdict : List Symbol → Bool)
+    (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : ℕ :=
+/-- Acceptance and rejection partition the terminal branches, without counting stuck states. -/
+    (verdict : List Symbol → Bool) (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
+    machine.branchCount verdict fuel cfg + machine.branchCount (fun out => !verdict out) fuel cfg =
+        ¬(machine.runBranch cfg choices).any (fun final => verdict final.output)) := by
+    obtain ⟨_, final, hrun, _⟩ := (machine.mem_branches_iff cfg fuel choices).mp hchoices
+/-- The accepting terminal count uses the standard one-bit `true` output convention. -/
+    {input : List Bool} (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input) : ℕ :=
+/-- Every terminal output other than the one-bit `true` word rejects. Invalid or stuck traces
+    {input : List Bool} (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input) : ℕ :=
+    {input : List Bool} (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input) :
+    machine.acceptCount fuel cfg + machine.rejectCount fuel cfg =
+    {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {fuel larger : ℕ}
+    (h : machine.HaltsWithin fuel cfg) (hle : fuel ≤ larger) (verdict : List Symbol → Bool) :
+    machine.branchCount verdict larger cfg = machine.branchCount verdict fuel cfg := by
+/-- Finite control and a fixed finite alphabet give one fixed bound on transition occurrences.
+Repeated actions are counted separately; their multiplicity is not bounded by `Nat.card Action`.
+    ∃ bound : ℕ, ∀ (input : List Symbol) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input),
+  let size (view : State × Option Symbol × (Fin k → Option Symbol)) :=

+private theorem bool_eq_of_toNat_eq : ∀ a b : Bool, a.toNat = b.toNat → a = b := by decide

+For each guessed answer word, multiply the accepting gap on true answers and target minus gap
+on false answers. Every incorrect word contributes zero. The correct word contributes the same
+nonzero product target, independent of the guessed word. Summing those products selected by an
+arbitrary polynomial-time Boolean combiner proves nonadaptive closure.
+LWPP first normalizes query lengths by many-one closure. Polynomial-family robustness then
+normalizes the possible prefix targets for an input-dependent query count.

+The WPP argument is [Spakowski, Thakur and Tripathi, Theorem 5.6(a)][SpakowskiThakurTripathi2005].
+The LWPP result is a deduction using the counting algebra of
+[Fenner, Fortnow and Kurtz][FennerFortnowKurtz1994] and polynomial-family robustness of
+These are results for the encoded verifier model. They do not prove adaptive WPP closure:
+[Spakowski, Thakur and Tripathi, Theorem 5.9][SpakowskiThakurTripathi2005] give a relativized
+obstruction to that stronger statement. Their separate UP-oracle containment is not formalized.
+private def answerGap {α : Type} (g f : α × ℕ → ℤ) (r : α → ℕ)
+    (d : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) : ℤ :=

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Two-sided polynomial-target robustness of WPP and LWPP
+Uniform polynomial-time accepting and rejecting target lists preserve WPP and LWPP when
+these lists are disjoint at each input, or each natural length for LWPP. Original targets
+may be zero, negative or repeated; only cross-family disjointness is required. The target
+indices need not be computable. Binary list output charges both counts and bit lengths.
+The proof follows [Hemaspaandra et al., Appendix A][HemaspaandraEtAl2018]: take the product
+of the differences between rejection targets and the original gap. This vanishes on rejection,
+and on acceptance takes one of a uniformly computed family of nonzero products. The uniform
+product theorem and one-sided robustness then finish the construction.
+* [E. Hemaspaandra, L. A. Hemaspaandra, H. Spakowski, O. Watanabe,
+  *The Robustness of LWPP and WPP, with an Application to Graph Reconstruction*]
+  [HemaspaandraEtAl2018], Definition 3.8, Corollary 3.11, Theorem 3.12 and Appendix A
+private def transformedTargets (yes no : List ℤ) : List ℤ :=
+  yes.map fun z => (no.map fun r => r - z).prod
+private theorem polyTime_transformedTargets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool}
+private theorem transformedTargets_nonzero {yes no : List ℤ} (hd : yes.Disjoint no) :
+  exact List.disjoint_left.mp hd hz (sub_eq_zero.mp heq ▸ hr)
+/-- Two-sided WPP robustness for disjoint uniformly computed binary integer target lists.
+Neither original list is required to avoid zero; no accepting or rejecting index is computed. -/
+theorem mem_WPP_of_disjoint_targets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+    {g : α → ℤ} {yes no : α → List ℤ} (hg : g ∈ GapP enc)
+    (hyes : ∀ a, a ∈ A → g a ∈ yes a) (hno : ∀ a, a ∉ A → g a ∈ no a) :
+    exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨g a, hyes a ha, rfl⟩
+    exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨g a, hno a ha, sub_self _⟩
+/-- Two-sided LWPP robustness with both target lists computed from unary input length.
+Disjointness is required at every natural length, including zero. Original zero targets are
+allowed on either side, provided the two lists remain disjoint. -/
+theorem mem_LWPP_of_disjoint_targets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+    {g : α → ℤ} {yes no : ℕ → List ℤ} (hg : g ∈ GapP enc)
+    (hyes : ∀ a, a ∈ A → g a ∈ yes (enc a).length)
+    (hno : ∀ a, a ∉ A → g a ∈ no (enc a).length) : A ∈ LWPP enc := by
+    exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨g a, hyes a ha, rfl⟩
+    exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨g a, hno a ha, sub_self _⟩
+private def indexedTargets {α : Type} (f : α × ℕ → ℤ) (r : α → ℕ) (a : α) : List ℤ :=
+private theorem polyTime_indexedTargets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool}
+private theorem indexedTargets_disjoint {α : Type} {yes no : α × ℕ → ℤ}
+    (hd : ∀ i < ry a, ∀ j < rn a, yes (a, i) ≠ no (a, j)) :
+    (indexedTargets yes ry a).Disjoint (indexedTargets no rn a) := by
+  exact hd i (List.mem_range.mp hi) j (List.mem_range.mp hj) he.symm
+private theorem mem_indexedTargets {α : Type} {f : α × ℕ → ℤ} {r : α → ℕ}
+    {a : α} {z : ℤ} (h : ∃ i < r a, z = f (a, i)) : z ∈ indexedTargets f r a := by
+/-- Two-sided WPP robustness for uniform indexed families, with each count computed in polynomial
+ time with unary output. Disjointness concerns used indices; zero targets are allowed. -/
+theorem mem_WPP_of_disjoint_indexed_targets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+    {g : α → ℤ} {yes no : α × ℕ → ℤ} {ry rn : α → ℕ} (hg : g ∈ GapP enc)
+    (hd : ∀ a i, i < ry a → ∀ j, j < rn a → yes (a, i) ≠ no (a, j))
+    (hyes : ∀ a, a ∈ A → ∃ i < ry a, g a = yes (a, i))
+    (hno : ∀ a, a ∉ A → ∃ j < rn a, g a = no (a, j)) : A ∈ WPP enc :=
+    (polyTime_indexedTargets hn hrn) (fun a => indexedTargets_disjoint a (hd a))
+    (fun a ha => mem_indexedTargets (hyes a ha)) (fun a ha => mem_indexedTargets (hno a ha))
+/-- Two-sided LWPP robustness for uniform indexed target families depending only on unary length.
+Cross-family disjointness holds at all natural lengths and both counts have unary polynomial-time
+certificates. The standard positive polynomial-size families are instances. -/
+theorem mem_LWPP_of_disjoint_indexed_targets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+    {g : α → ℤ} {yes no : ℕ × ℕ → ℤ} {ry rn : ℕ → ℕ} (hg : g ∈ GapP enc)
+    (hd : ∀ n i, i < ry n → ∀ j, j < rn n → yes (n, i) ≠ no (n, j))
+    (hyes : ∀ a, a ∈ A → ∃ i < ry (enc a).length, g a = yes ((enc a).length, i))
+    (hno : ∀ a, a ∉ A → ∃ j < rn (enc a).length, g a = no ((enc a).length, j)) :
+    (polyTime_indexedTargets hn hrn) (fun n => indexedTargets_disjoint n (hd n))
+    (fun a ha => mem_indexedTargets (hyes a ha)) (fun a ha => mem_indexedTargets (hno a ha))
+/-- **(Poly,Poly)-WPP = WPP**, with disjoint uniformly computed binary integer target lists.
+The converse uses singleton acceptance and zero-rejection lists. -/
+theorem mem_WPP_iff_exists_disjoint_targets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α} :
+    A ∈ WPP enc ↔ ∃ g ∈ GapP enc, ∃ yes no : α → List ℤ,
+      (∀ a, a ∈ A → g a ∈ yes a) ∧ ∀ a, a ∉ A → g a ∈ no a := by
+  · rintro ⟨g, hg, f, hf, hn, hr, hA⟩
+    refine ⟨g, hg, fun a => [f a], fun _ => [0], by fun_prop, .const _, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · rintro ⟨g, hg, yes, no, hy, hn, hd, hyes, hno⟩
+    exact mem_WPP_of_disjoint_targets hg hy hn hd hyes hno
+/-- **(Poly,Poly)-LWPP = LWPP**, with disjoint target lists uniformly computed from unary
+theorem mem_LWPP_iff_exists_disjoint_targets {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α} :
+    A ∈ LWPP enc ↔ ∃ g ∈ GapP enc, ∃ yes no : ℕ → List ℤ,
+      (∀ a, a ∈ A → g a ∈ yes (enc a).length) ∧
+      ∀ a, a ∉ A → g a ∈ no (enc a).length := by
+  · rintro ⟨g, hg, f, hf, hn, hr, hA⟩
+    refine ⟨g, hg, fun n => [f n], fun _ => [0], by fun_prop, .const _, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · rintro ⟨g, hg, yes, no, hy, hn, hd, hyes, hno⟩
+    exact mem_LWPP_of_disjoint_targets hg hy hn hd hyes hno

+The powering argument for multiplicative gap amplification in [Watson2012], Sections 1.1
+and 3, works uniformly for polynomial-time unary repetition counts. A fixed dominating
+length polynomial also handles any polynomially bounded requested exponent, even when
+that request is not itself computable. The witness remains #P, and the positive threshold
+remains polynomial-time with binary output. This is gap amplification, not an additive
+error bound on a normalized acceptance probability.
+* `exists_SBP_gap_pow_polyTime`: a positive unary polynomial-time exponent gives a uniform gap.
+* `exists_SBP_gap_pow_polyBounded`: a polynomially bounded requested exponent gives a uniform gap.
+* [T. Watson, *The Complexity of Estimating Min-Entropy*][Watson2012], Sections 1.1 and 3.
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- Uniform SBP gap strengthening by positive, polynomial-time unary powers. Both the #P
+numerator and the positive binary-output threshold are raised to the same input-dependent power. -/
+theorem exists_SBP_gap_pow_polyTime (hA : A ∈ SBP enc) {r : α → ℕ}
+    (hr : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime r enc encUnary) (hpos : ∀ a, 0 < r a) :
+    ∃ f ∈ SharpP enc, ∃ k : α → ℕ, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encNat ∧
+        (a ∉ A → 2 ^ r a * f a < k a) := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, k, hk, hkpos, h⟩ := mem_SBP_iff_exists_pos_threshold.mp hA
+  refine ⟨_, SharpP.pow_mem_polyTime hf hr, fun a => k a ^ r a,
+    hk.binary_pow' hr, fun a => pow_pos (hkpos a) _, fun a => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
+/-- **Uniform SBP amplification.** One #P witness and one positive polynomial-time binary
+threshold achieve gap `2 ^ r(a)` for every polynomially bounded requested exponent. The request
+need not be computable: the proof uses a fixed length polynomial dominating it, plus one to
+ensure positive repetition even when the request is zero. -/
+theorem exists_SBP_gap_pow_polyBounded (hA : A ∈ SBP enc) (r : α → ℕ)
+    ∃ f ∈ SharpP enc, ∃ k : α → ℕ, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encNat ∧
+        (a ∉ A → 2 ^ r a * f a < k a) := by

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A polynomial-time unary repetition count permits a verifier to check an input-dependent
+number of certificate rows. The number of accepted tuples is the corresponding power,
+including exponent zero. Exact false-bit padding supplies a length-polynomial certificate.
+* `SharpP.powerVerifier`: accept precisely when every certificate row is accepted.
+* `SharpP.acceptCount_powerVerifier`: exact counting identity, including zero rows and width.
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994].
+/-- Check every row of the repeated certificate, accepting the empty tuple. -/
+def powerVerifier (r k : α → ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (x : α × List Bool) : Bool :=
+  (BitString.listRows (r x.1) (k x.1) x.2).all fun row => V (x.1, row)
+/-- A row count and width computed in unary give a polynomial-time repeated verifier. -/
+theorem polyTime_powerVerifier {r k : α → ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (powerVerifier r k V) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+/-- The number of accepted row tuples is the power of the number of accepted rows. -/
+theorem acceptCount_powerVerifier (r k : α → ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) :
+    acceptCount (powerVerifier r k V) a (r a * k a) = acceptCount V a (k a) ^ r a := by
+  rw [show acceptCount V a (k a) ^ r a =
+    ∏ _ : Fin (r a), acceptCount V a (k a) by simp]
+  exact card_equiv BitString.blocksEquiv fun x => by
+/-- A #P function raised to an input-dependent polynomial-time unary exponent remains in #P. -/
+theorem pow_mem_polyTime {f : α → ℕ} {r : α → ℕ} (hf : f ∈ SharpP enc)
+    (fun a => f a ^ r a) ∈ SharpP enc := by
+  let k : α → ℕ := fun a => p.eval (enc a).length
+  have hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encUnary := by dsimp [k]; fun_prop
+  change f a ^ r a = acceptCount (powerVerifier r k V) a (r a * k a)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Polynomial-family robustness of WPP and LWPP
+Uniform polynomial-time lists of nonzero binary integers may replace the single accepting
+target in WPP and LWPP. The accepting index is existential, with no computability assumption.
+For LWPP the list depends only on unary input length. List output size charges both the number
+of targets and their bit lengths; fixed finite lists are only a special case.
+The interpolation product follows [Hemaspaandra et al., Theorems 3.1 and 3.7]
+[HemaspaandraEtAl2018]. We prove its uniform GapP membership by expanding over Boolean subsets:
+each term is a polynomial-time product of selected targets times a unary power of the gap.
+Thus the proof uses certified word sums and powers, without assuming indexed-product closure.
+The two-sided acceptance/rejection-target generalization and oracle lowness are separate results.
+  full one-sided polynomial-family robustness, stated with target lists.
+* [E. Hemaspaandra, L. A. Hemaspaandra, H. Spakowski, O. Watanabe,
+  *The Robustness of LWPP and WPP, with an Application to Graph Reconstruction*]
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994].
+private def selectedProduct (xs : List ℤ) (w : List Bool) : ℤ :=
+  (xs.zipIdx.map fun zi => if w.getD zi.2 false then 1 else zi.1).prod
+private theorem expansion_fin {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℤ) (g : ℤ) :
+    (∏ i, (f i - g)) = ∑ w : Fin n → Bool,
+      (∏ i, if w i then 1 else f i) * (-g) ^ #{i | w i = true} := by
+      (∏ i, if w i then -g else f i) =
+        (∏ i, if w i then 1 else f i) * (-g) ^ #{i | w i = true} := by
+      _ = ∏ i, (if w i then 1 else f i) * (if w i then -g else 1) := by
+  rw [← Fintype.prod_sum (fun (i : Fin n) (b : Bool) => if b then -g else f i)]
+  simp only [Fintype.sum_bool, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false, ite_true, sub_eq_add_neg]
+private theorem selectedProduct_ofFn (xs : List ℤ) (w : Fin xs.length → Bool) :
+    selectedProduct xs (List.ofFn w) = ∏ i, if w i then 1 else xs.get i := by
+  have he : (xs.zipIdx.map fun zi => if (List.ofFn w).getD zi.2 false then 1 else zi.1) =
+      List.ofFn (fun i => if w i then 1 else xs.get i) := by
+      have hi : i < xs.length := by simpa only [List.length_ofFn] using h₂
+    (xs.map (fun z => z - g)).prod = ∑ w : Fin xs.length → Bool,
+      selectedProduct xs (List.ofFn w) * (-g) ^ (List.ofFn w).countP id := by
+  have he : (xs.map (fun z => z - g)).prod = ∏ i, (xs.get i - g) := by
+    rw [← List.ofFn_getElem_eq_map xs (fun z => z - g), List.prod_ofFn]
+private theorem polyTime_selectedProduct {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {f : α → List ℤ}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => selectedProduct (f x.1) x.2)
+/-- A product of differences between a uniformly computed list of binary FP targets and one GapP
+value is GapP. The list length and its total encoded size may depend polynomially on the input. -/
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc (encList encIntBin)) (hg : g ∈ GapP enc) :
+    (fun a => ((f a).map (fun z => z - g a)).prod) ∈ GapP enc := by
+    (show ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => x.2.countP id)
+    (show ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (f a).length) enc encUnary by fun_prop)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Unary polynomial-time bounds permit a single verifier to aggregate an input-dependent number
+of factors or summands. Padding certificates with false bits preserves counts exactly. Signed
+products maintain two Boolean states, whose difference multiplies the signed contribution of
+each block. This gives variable powers of GapP functions, not just fixed subring powers.
+* `SharpP.sum_bits_mem`, `GapP.sum_bits_mem`: sum over all words of a computed unary length.
+* `GapP.pow_mem_polyTime`: an input-dependent unary exponent preserves GapP.
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994].
+/-- A polynomial-time unary certificate length can be padded without changing the count. -/
+theorem SharpP.of_polyTime_length {V : α × List Bool → Bool} {r : α → ℕ}
+    (fun a => acceptCount V a (r a)) ∈ SharpP enc := by
+  let p : Polynomial ℕ := Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d
+  refine ⟨p, andVerifier r V allFalseVerifier, by fun_prop, fun a => ?_⟩
+  have hle : r a ≤ p.eval (enc a).length := by simpa [p] using hb a
+/-- Summing a uniform #P family over all words of a polynomial-time unary length preserves #P. -/
+theorem SharpP.sum_bits_mem {f : α × List Bool → ℕ} {r : α → ℕ}
+    (fun a => ∑ w : Fin (r a) → Bool, f (a, List.ofFn w)) ∈ SharpP enc := by
+  let q : α → ℕ := fun a => p.eval (2 * (enc a).length + 1 + r a)
+  let W : α × List Bool → Bool := fun x => V ((x.1, x.2.take (r x.1)), x.2.drop (r x.1))
+  have hq : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime q enc encUnary := by dsimp [q]; fun_prop
+  have hW : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by dsimp [W]; fun_prop
+  change _ = acceptCount W a (r a + q a)
+/-- GapP is closed under summing over all words of a polynomial-time unary length. -/
+theorem GapP.sum_bits_mem {g : α × List Bool → ℤ} {r : α → ℕ}
+    (fun a => ∑ w : Fin (r a) → Bool, g (a, List.ofFn w)) ∈ GapP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f₁, h₁, f₂, h₂, hg⟩ := hg
+  refine ⟨_, SharpP.sum_bits_mem h₁ hr, _, SharpP.sum_bits_mem h₂ hr, fun a => ?_⟩
+/-- Positive and negative acceptance flags for a partial product. -/
+/-- Difference of the two acceptance flags. -/
+def sign (s : State) : ℤ := (if s.1 then 1 else 0) - (if s.2 then 1 else 0)
+/-- Multiplication of signed Boolean flags; overlap cancels in their difference. -/
+private theorem sign_mul (s t : State) : sign (mul s t) = sign s * sign t := by
+  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> cases d <;> decide
+private theorem sign_fold {β : Type} (v : β → State) (xs : List β) (s : State) :
+    sign (xs.foldl (fun s x => mul s (v x)) s) = sign s * (xs.map (sign ∘ v)).prod := by
+  | cons x xs ih => simp only [List.foldl_cons, ih, sign_mul, List.map_cons, List.prod_cons,
+/-- Count products of signed row contributions by two ordinary verifiers. -/
+def verifier (r k : α → ℕ) (V W : α × List Bool → Bool) (b : Bool)
+    (fun s row => mul s (V (x.1, row), W (x.1, row))) (true, false)
+  if b then s.2 else s.1
+/-- The two product verifiers run in polynomial time for unary row count and width. -/
+theorem polyTime_verifier {r k : α → ℕ} {V W : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hW : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool) (b : Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (verifier r k V W b) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+      (fun x : (α × State) × List Bool => mul x.1.2 (V (x.1.1, x.2), W (x.1.1, x.2)))
+      (encPair (encPair enc encS) encBits) encS := by dsimp [mul, encS]; fun_prop
+    (encA := encBits) (encB := encS) (par := fun x : α × List Bool => x.1)
+    (list := fun x => BitString.listRows (r x.1) (k x.1) x.2)
+    (step := fun a s row => mul s (V (a, row), W (a, row)))
+/-- The difference of the row-product counts is the power of the original difference. -/
+theorem count_sub (r k : α → ℕ) (V W : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) :
+    (acceptCount (verifier r k V W false) a (r a * k a) : ℤ) -
+      acceptCount (verifier r k V W true) a (r a * k a) =
+        ((acceptCount V a (k a) : ℤ) - acceptCount W a (k a)) ^ r a := by
+  have hs (x : Fin (r a * k a) → Bool) :
+        (fun s row => mul s (V (a, row), W (a, row))) (true, false)) =
+      ∏ i : Fin (r a), sign (V (a, List.ofFn (BitString.blocksEquiv x i)),
+    simp only [sign, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_true, ite_false, sub_zero, one_mul,
+  simp only [acceptCount, Finset.card_filter, Nat.cast_sum, Nat.cast_ite, Nat.cast_one,
+  change (∑ x, sign ((BitString.listRows (r a) (k a) (List.ofFn x)).foldl
+    (fun s row => mul s (V (a, row), W (a, row))) (true, false))) = _
+    (fun x => ∏ i : Fin (r a), sign (V (a, List.ofFn (x i)), W (a, List.ofFn (x i))))]
+  rw [← Fintype.prod_sum (fun (_ : Fin (r a)) (x : Fin (k a) → Bool) =>
+    sign (V (a, List.ofFn x), W (a, List.ofFn x)))]
+/-- A GapP function raised to an input-dependent polynomial-time unary exponent is in GapP. -/
+theorem GapP.pow_mem_polyTime {g : α → ℤ} {r : α → ℕ} (hg : g ∈ GapP enc)
+    (fun a => g a ^ r a) ∈ GapP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f₁, ⟨p₁, V₁, hV₁, hf₁⟩, f₂, ⟨p₂, V₂, hV₂, hf₂⟩, hg⟩ := hg
+  let k : α → ℕ := fun a => (p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length
+  let V := andVerifier (fun a => p₁.eval (enc a).length) V₁ allFalseVerifier
+  let W := andVerifier (fun a => p₂.eval (enc a).length) V₂ allFalseVerifier
+  have hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encUnary := by dsimp [k]; fun_prop
+  have hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by dsimp [V]; fun_prop
+  have hW : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by dsimp [W]; fun_prop
+  refine ⟨_, SharpP.of_polyTime_length (SignedProduct.polyTime_verifier hr hk hV hW false) hlength,
+    _, SharpP.of_polyTime_length (SignedProduct.polyTime_verifier hr hk hV hW true) hlength,
+    (acceptCount (SignedProduct.verifier r k V W false) a (r a * k a) : ℤ) -
+      acceptCount (SignedProduct.verifier r k V W true) a (r a * k a)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# PP and counting oracles have the same polynomial-time power
+Every PP oracle query is replaced by one bit query to a shifted `#P` count. For a query word `w`,
+the new request is the code of `(w, q(|w|))`, where `q` is fixed by the PP verifier. This only
+reads the word and its length; it does not decode an instance or recognize valid codes.
+The transformed program is fixed before the counting oracle is chosen. Its polynomial-time
+certificate follows from open oracle substitution and holds for every external oracle, even one
+returning arbitrarily long words: only the first reply bit is read. Against an oracle answering
+the specified counting function's bits, the transformed replies induce a language agreeing
+with the PP problem on its codes. Arbitrary answers elsewhere are allowed by the original
+Together with binary search in the reverse direction, this proves `P^PP = P^#P` for the existing
+encoded classes. The result is a uniform polynomial-time simulation, not merely a query bound.

+# A PP decision as one bit of a counting function
+If a verifier accepts `c` of its `2 ^ p(n)` random strings, strict majority is the bit at
+position `p(n) + 1` of `2 * c + (2 ^ p(n) - 1)`. The shift is nonnegative and computable in
+polynomial time with binary output, so the shifted count remains in `#P`.
+This includes zero random bits and a tie is rejected.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.exists_SharpP_testBit_of_mem_PP`: a PP problem is decided by one bit of
+  a counting function at a polynomially determined position.

+  PP decisions and counting-function bits. The explicit shifted count is the construction here.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A cover of length `t` yields an acyclic set circuit with exactly `t²` charged AND gates.
+Unions and constants are free. The construction works on arbitrary carriers: at each point,
+only the `t` pair coordinates can become true, so `t` synchronous rounds suffice.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Fusion.PairCover.toCircuit`: an acyclic circuit realizing an unrestricted cover.

+# Writing circuits chunk by chunk in logarithmic space
+A *writer* (`Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.WriterSpec`) is a read machine on a framed input `frame
+w` that counts the length `n` of `w`, emitting a fixed word for each bit and another at the end,
+then emits the chunks `chunk n 0, …, chunk n (N n - 1)` and a trailer, keeping only the number of
+the current chunk, and finally emits a word for each bit of `w`
+(`Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.WriterSpec.run_machine`). When the number of chunks is
+polynomially bounded and the chunks and the trailer are computed within work space linear in the
+binary lengths of `n` and of the number of the chunk, the writer runs in logarithmic space
+(`Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.WriterSpec.computableInLogSpace`). This is how encoded instances of
+circuit value problems built from uniform circuits, such as the tableau of a machine, are written
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.WriterSpec.machine`: the writer, as a read machine.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.WriterSpec.run_machine`: the writer halts with its output.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.WriterSpec.computableInLogSpace`: a writer with chunks computed in
+  linear space runs in logarithmic space.
+/-- The read address of the writer: the markers `true` of the framed input while counting, the
+def writerAddr (s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) : Option ℕ :=
+  if s.1 = 0 then some (2 * s.2.2) else if s.1 = 2 then some (2 * s.2.2 + 1) else none
+/-- The encoding of the states of the writer. -/
+abbrev encWState : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ ↪ List Bool := encPair encNat (encPair encNat encNat)
+/-- The space budget of a state of the writer: the length of its encoding. -/
+def wBudget (s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ := (encWState s).length + 1
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace writerAddr encWState (encOption encNat) wBudget := by
+  have hin : (fun s => (encWState s).length) ≼ wBudget := .of_le fun _ => by

+      ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun s => some (a s)) encWState (encOption encNat) wBudget :=

+reduces to the monotone circuit value problem in logarithmic space

+Ladner proved [Ladner1975] that the circuit value problem is `P`-complete under
+A problem `A ∈ P enc` is decided by a machine `tm` within `C (n + 1) ^ d` steps on encoded
+instances of length `n`. The reduction maps an instance `a` to the tableau circuit of `tm` for
+`C (n + 1) ^ d + n + 1` steps on inputs of length `n = |enc a|`
+(`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Tableau.circuit`), together with the input `enc a`. The circuit outputs
+whether `tm`, started on `enc a`, has written exactly `[true]` after that many steps
+(`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Tableau.eval_circuit`); since `tm` has halted by then with the answer on
+its output, this is whether `a ∈ A`. The circuit reads the bits of `enc a` as its inputs; it does
+not hardwire them as constants. The reduction is
+computable in logarithmic space: a read machine (`Turing.ReadMachine`) on the framed input counts
+its length `n`, then writes the gates one by one, keeping only the number of the current gate,
+since each gate is computed from its number within work space linear in the binary lengths of `n`,
+the time bound and the number (`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Tableau.gateCode_inSpace`), and finally
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.tableauInstance`: the instance of the circuit value problem for
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.writer`: the read machine writing the instance.

+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.logSpaceHard`: the circuit value problem is `P`-hard under
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitValue.mem_L_iff_forall_P_eq_L`: the circuit value problem is in `L`

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Order-free interpretations on structures with at least two elements
+The reductions in this module use order-free first-order interpretations. Input structures have
+no built-in order or numeric predicates; these are variants of the standard ordered setting.
+Order-free reductions (`Cslib.Logic.FO.Reduces`) are asked to be correct on every finite
+structure, including the empty one and those with one element. On these, an interpretation of the
+unordered structures of this library has little room: an interpretation of positive dimension
+maps the empty structure to the empty structure, and a structure with one element to a structure
+with at most one element. Whether a reduction to a class exists then depends on how the class
+treats its smallest members. Every structure with at most one element is an independent set
+instance with a solution, for example, while the empty clause on one element is an unsatisfiable
+CNF structure, so SAT is not order-free reducible to independent set in this sense.
+Immerman's Boolean-constant convention requires at least two elements, with distinct `0` and `1`
+[Immerman, Proviso 1.15][Immerman1999]. Here the same size restriction is used without built-in
+order: `ReducesNontrivial K K'` requires an order-free interpretation to be correct on each finite
+structure with at least two elements. It is distinct from the unrestricted `Reduces`, which also
+handles empty and singleton structures. Such reductions compose when the first interpretation
+preserves nontriviality, or when the second reduction is unrestricted. A compiled tagged
+interpretation preserves nontriviality when its tagged output is nonempty.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.ReducesNontrivial`: order-free reducibility on structures with two distinct
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Reduces.reducesNontrivial`: order-free reductions are reductions on nontrivial
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.ReducesNontrivial.of_tagged`: reductions on nontrivial structures by tagged
+  interpretations; no nonemptiness assumption is needed for correctness.
+  together with nontriviality preservation when the tagged outputs are nonempty.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Reduces.of_reducesNontrivial`: between classes containing every structure with
+  at most one element, reductions on nontrivial structures are order-free reductions.
+universe u v u' v' u'' v'' w
+variable {L : Language.{u, v}} {L' : Language.{u', v'}} {L'' : Language.{u'', v''}}
+/-- A class `K` of `L`-structures is **reducible by an order-free interpretation on nontrivial
+structures** to a class `K'` of `L'`-structures when some first-order interpretation of `L'` in
+`L` maps every finite `L`-structure with two distinct elements inside `K'` exactly when it is in
+  ∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Finite ι) (I : Interpretation L L' ι),
+/-- An order-free reduction is a reduction on nontrivial structures. -/
+theorem Reduces.reducesNontrivial (h : Reduces K K') : ReducesNontrivial K K' :=
+  ⟨ι, hι, I, fun M _ _ => hI M⟩
+/-- Reducibility on nontrivial structures is reflexive on classes closed under isomorphism. -/
+theorem refl [L.IsRelational] (hK : IsoClosed K) : ReducesNontrivial K K :=
+/-- A reduction on nontrivial structures followed by an order-free reduction. -/
+theorem trans_reduces (h : ReducesNontrivial K K') (h' : Reduces K' K'') (hK'' : IsoClosed K'') :
+  refine ⟨κ × ι, inferInstance, J.comp I, fun M _ hM => ?_⟩
+/-- A reduction on nontrivial structures through an interpretation that keeps them nontrivial,
+followed by a reduction on nontrivial structures. -/
+theorem trans_of_nontrivial {ι : Type} [Finite ι] (I : Interpretation L L' ι)
+      Nontrivial (I.Model M) ∧ (M ∈ K ↔ Bundled.of (c := L'.Structure) (I.Model M) ∈ K'))
+    (h' : ReducesNontrivial K' K'') (hK'' : IsoClosed K'') : ReducesNontrivial K K'' := by
+  refine ⟨κ × ι, inferInstance, J.comp I, fun M _ hM => ?_⟩
+/-- A reduction on nontrivial structures between classes containing every finite structure with
+at most one element is an order-free reduction: an interpretation maps a structure with at most one
+element to a structure with at most one element. -/
+    (hK : ∀ (M : Bundled.{w} L.Structure) [Finite M], Subsingleton M → M ∈ K)
+    (hK' : ∀ (N : Bundled.{w} L'.Structure) [Finite N], Subsingleton N → N ∈ K') :
+  rcases subsingleton_or_nontrivial M with hM | hM
+/-- A compiled tagged interpretation preserves class membership and nontriviality when its
+tagged outputs are nonempty and the target class is closed under isomorphism and copies. -/
+    {K' : Set (Bundled.{w} L'.Structure)} (hK' : IsoClosed K') (hcopy : CopyInvariant K')
+    {T : Type} [Finite T] {ι : T → Type} [∀ t, Finite (ι t)]
+    (hne : ∀ (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] [Finite M], Nontrivial M → Nonempty (I.Model M))
+/-- **Tagged interpretations give reductions on nontrivial structures** to classes closed under
+    {K' : Set (Bundled.{w} L'.Structure)} (hK' : IsoClosed K') (hcopy : CopyInvariant K')
+    {T : Type} [Finite T] {ι : T → Type} [∀ t, Finite (ι t)]
+  ⟨_, inferInstance, I.toInterpretation (Interpretation.empty L L'), fun M _ hM => by

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Machines with random access to their input, in logarithmic space
+A **query machine** (`Turing.QueryMachine`) reads its input by position: from a state `s` it asks
+for the input bit at position `query s`, receives it (`none` past the end of the input), moves to
+`next (s, b)` and emits `emit (s, b)`, until `halted s`; it then emits `finish s`. The state is
+abstract, so query machines are a convenient way to describe logarithmic-space algorithms that
+jump around in their input: counters, tuples of elements, indices into tables.
+Such a machine runs within logarithmic space when its states have logarithmic encodings and its
+parts are tidily computable within space linear in the encoded state
+(`Turing.QueryMachine.computableInLogSpace`). The proof is a multi-pass fold over the input
+scanning the whole input with a binary position counter to fetch the queried bit, so that only
+the state, the counter and the fetched bit are ever stored [Sipser, Section 8.4][Sipser2013].

+by step machines that move a head one cell at a time. A query machine differs in two ways that
+the algorithms built on it need: a read past the end of the input returns `none` rather than

+* `Turing.QueryMachine`: a machine with random access to its input.

+/-- A **query machine**: from the state `s` it reads the input bit at position `query s` (`none`
+past the end of the input), moves to `next (s, b)` and emits `emit (s, b)`, until `halted s`; at

+  emit : σ × Option Bool → List Bool

+/-- The state after `t` steps on the input `w`. -/

+theorem run_add_of_halted {t : ℕ} (h : M.halted (M.run w t) = true) (k : ℕ) :

+    M.halted (M.run w t) = true ↔ T ≤ t := by
+    rw [show t = T + (t - T) by omega, M.run_add_of_halted w hT]

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Bit-blasting circuits over a finite carrier
+Let `enc : F ≃ BitString w` encode the elements of a carrier `F` by `w` bits. A circuit over the
+full binary basis of `F` (`fullInterpretation (k := 2)`, where every constant and every operation
+with at most two arguments is a gate) is simulated by a De Morgan circuit on the encodings: each
+gate is replaced by `w` circuits, one for each bit of its value, each a function of the `2 * w`
+bits of the gate's arguments and so computable with `2 ^ (2 * w) * (4 * w + 2) + 1` gates by its
+disjunctive normal form (`Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.selected`). A gate of the full basis therefore
+costs at most `bitBlastCost w = w * (2 ^ (2 * w) * (4 * w + 2) + 1)` De Morgan gates. For a field
+`F` with `q = 2 ^ w` elements this is `O(w ^ 2 * q ^ 2)` gates per field operation, a polynomial
+in `q`, which suffices for reconstruction arguments whose circuits are polynomial in `q` anyway.
+The simulation is stated as a synthesis bound (`Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.bitBlast`): if the bits
+of the `F`-valued functions feeding the circuit's inputs are available, then the bits of all its
+outputs can be made available with `size * bitBlastCost w` further gates.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.bitsOf`: the bits of an `F`-valued function under an encoding.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.bitBlastCost`: the De Morgan cost of one gate of the full binary basis.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.bitBlast_program`: the bits of every wire of a program over the full
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.bitBlast`: the bits of every output of a circuit over the full binary
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.bitBlast_synthesis`: the same for a synthesis bound over the full
+* [S. Jukna, *Boolean Function Complexity: Advances and Frontiers*][Jukna2012]
+* [M. Sudan, L. Trevisan, S. Vadhan, *Pseudorandom generators without the XOR lemma*]
+/-- The `j`-th bit, under the encoding `enc`, of an `F`-valued function `φ` of the inputs. -/
+def bitsOf (enc : F ≃ BitString w) (φ : (Fin n → Bool) → F) (j : Fin w) : BooleanFunction n :=
+/-- The number of De Morgan gates that simulate one gate of the full binary basis on `w`-bit
+symbols: each of the `w` bits of the value is a function of the `2 * w` bits of the arguments. -/
+def bitBlastCost (w : ℕ) : ℕ := w * (2 ^ (2 * w) * (4 * w + 2) + 1)
+/-- One bit of a gate of the full binary basis, as a Boolean function of the bits of the gate's
+arguments, costs at most `2 ^ (2 * w) * (4 * w + 2) + 1` gates on top of these bits. -/
+private theorem bitBlast_gateBit (enc : F ≃ BitString w) {s : Set (BooleanFunction n)}
+    (op : FullOp 2 F) (args : Fin ((fullSignature 2 F).Arity op) → (Fin n → Bool) → F)
+    (hargs : ∀ a j, bitsOf enc (args a) j ∈ s) (j : Fin w) :
+      {bitsOf enc (fun x => fullInterpretation op fun a => args a x) j}
+  let ψ : BooleanFunction ((fullSignature 2 F).Arity op * w) := fun y =>
+    enc (fullInterpretation op fun a => enc.symm fun j' => y (finProdFinEquiv (a, j'))) j
+  obtain ⟨c, hc, hsize⟩ := (selected (n := (fullSignature 2 F).Arity op * w) id ψ).exists_circuit
+    simp only [single_apply, Function.comp_id, ψ, bitsOf, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
+  · have hkw : (fullSignature 2 F).Arity op * w ≤ 2 * w := Nat.mul_le_mul_right w hk
+    have hpow : 2 ^ ((fullSignature 2 F).Arity op * w) ≤ 2 ^ (2 * w) :=
+    have : 2 * ((fullSignature 2 F).Arity op * w) + 2 ≤ 4 * w + 2 := by omega
+/-- **Bit-blasting a program.** If the bits of the functions `φ i` feeding the inputs of a
+program over the full binary basis of `F` are available, then the bits of the values of all its
+wires can be made available with `bitBlastCost w` De Morgan gates for each of its gates. -/
+theorem bitBlast_program (enc : F ≃ BitString w) {s : Set (BooleanFunction n)} {N g : ℕ}
+    (p : Program (fullSignature 2 F) N g) (φ : Fin N → (Fin n → Bool) → F)
+    (hφ : ∀ i j, bitsOf enc (φ i) j ∈ s) :
+      (Set.range fun wj : Wire N g × Fin w =>
+        bitsOf enc (fun x => p.trace fullInterpretation (fun i => φ i x) wj.1) wj.2)
+    | input i => exact hφ i j
+    let T : Set (BooleanFunction n) := Set.range fun wj : Wire N g × Fin w =>
+      bitsOf enc (fun x => p.trace fullInterpretation (fun i => φ i x) wj.1) wj.2
+        (Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => line.eval fullInterpretation (fun i => φ i x)
+          (p.eval fullInterpretation fun i => φ i x)) j) (bitBlastCost w) := by
+        (fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => line.eval fullInterpretation (fun i => φ i x)
+          (p.eval fullInterpretation fun i => φ i x)) j)
+          (fun a x => p.trace fullInterpretation (fun i => φ i x) (line.wires a))
+          (fun a j' => Set.mem_union_right s (⟨(line.wires a, j'), rfl⟩ : _ ∈ T)) j)
+      simpa [bitBlastCost, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] using this
+/-- **Bit-blasting a circuit.** If the bits of the functions `φ i` feeding the inputs of a circuit
+over the full binary basis of `F` are available, then the bits of all its outputs can be made
+available with `c.size * bitBlastCost w` De Morgan gates. -/
+theorem bitBlast (enc : F ≃ BitString w) {s : Set (BooleanFunction n)} {N M : ℕ}
+    (c : Circuit (fullSignature 2 F) N M) (φ : Fin N → (Fin n → Bool) → F)
+    (hφ : ∀ i j, bitsOf enc (φ i) j ∈ s) :
+      (Set.range fun oj : Fin M × Fin w =>
+        bitsOf enc (fun x => c.eval fullInterpretation (fun i => φ i x) oj.1) oj.2)
+  refine (bitBlast_program enc c.program φ hφ).mono Set.Subset.rfl ?_ le_rfl
+/-- **Bit-blasting a synthesis bound.** If a family `Ψ` of functions of `N` field inputs is
+synthesized over the full binary basis from the input projections with `cost` gates, and the bits
+of the functions `φ i` feeding the inputs are available, then the bits of all `Ψ o (φ ·)` can be
+made available with `cost * bitBlastCost w` De Morgan gates. -/
+theorem bitBlast_synthesis (enc : F ≃ BitString w) {N : ℕ} {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
+    {s : Set (BooleanFunction n)} (φ : Fin N → (Fin n → Bool) → F)
+    (hφ : ∀ i j, bitsOf enc (φ i) j ∈ s) :
+      (Set.range fun oj : ι × Fin w => bitsOf enc (fun x => Ψ oj.1 (fun i => φ i x)) oj.2)
+    h.mono Set.Subset.rfl (by rintro _ ⟨j, rfl⟩; exact ⟨_, rfl⟩) le_rfl
+  refine (bitBlast enc c φ hφ).mono Set.Subset.rfl ?_ (Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hsize)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Exponential worst-case hardness gives exponential average-case hardness
+Let `L` be a language whose slices need De Morgan circuits of size `2 ^ (γ n)` for all large `n`.
+This module encodes the slices of `L` with the reconstruction theorem of Sudan, Trevisan and
+schedule of parameters, and proves that the encoded language is average-case hard for circuits
+of size `2 ^ ⌊N / c⌋` at all large lengths `N`
+the block length is `b = ⌊N / (4 (M + 1))⌋` (`Cslib.HardnessEncoding.blockLength`); the slice of
+`L` at length `n = M b` is encoded over the explicit binary field of degree `w = 4 b`
