+# The stages of local list decoding as De Morgan circuits
+Reconstructing a worst-case hard function from a predictor for its encoding
+[SudanTrevisanVadhan2001] runs three decoders in sequence, each of which queries the previous one
+at computed points: Goldreich–Levin decoding of the inner Hadamard code
+(`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.glPredictor`), local list decoding of the outer Reed–Muller code along
+lines with advice (`Cslib.Code.lineListDecode`), and self-correction by interpolation and majority
+trees (`Cslib.Code.lagrangeDecode`, `Cslib.Code.majTree`). This module bounds the De Morgan circuit
+size of each stage given the circuit size of the previous one.
+A field element is represented by `w` bits through an encoding `enc : F ≃ BitString w`, and a
+function `G : (Fin m → F) → F` is *bit-synthesizable with `cost` gates*
+(`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.BitSynthesis`) if, whenever the bits of the coordinates of a point are
+available, the bits of the value of `G` at that point can be made available with `cost` further
+gates. The arithmetic between queries runs over the full binary basis of the field and is
+* The Goldreich–Levin stage costs `glCost w K s` for a predictor of size `s` and `K` masks
+* The line stage costs `lineCost` for a field of size `q`, in terms of the cost of its oracle
+* The self-correction stage costs `selfCorrectCost` in terms of the cost of its oracle
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.glPredictor`: the Goldreich–Levin decoder of the inner code.
+  `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.BitSynthesis.selfCorrect`: the costs of the three stages.
+* [M. Sudan, L. Trevisan, S. Vadhan, *Pseudorandom generators without the XOR lemma*]
+* [O. Goldreich, L. Levin, *A Hard-Core Predicate for All One-Way Functions*][GoldreichLevin1989]
+/-- The point of `F ^ m` whose coordinates have the given bits: coordinate `i` decodes block `i`
+def pointOfBits (enc : F ≃ BitString w) (y : BitString (m * w)) : Fin m → F :=
+/-- The bits of the coordinates of a point of `F ^ m`, block after block
+def bitsOfPoint (enc : F ≃ BitString w) (x : Fin m → F) : BitString (m * w) :=
+/-- Decoding the bits of a point gives the point back. -/
+theorem pointOfBits_bitsOfPoint (enc : F ≃ BitString w) (x : Fin m → F) :
+    pointOfBits enc (bitsOfPoint enc x) = x := by
+/-- Encoding the point with given bits gives the bits back. -/
+theorem bitsOfPoint_pointOfBits (enc : F ≃ BitString w) (y : BitString (m * w)) :
+    bitsOfPoint enc (pointOfBits enc y) = y := by
+/-- `G` is *bit-synthesizable with `cost` gates*: whenever the bits of the coordinates of a point
+are available, the bits of the value of `G` at the point can be made available with `cost` further
+def BitSynthesis (enc : F ≃ BitString w) (G : (Fin m → F) → F) (cost : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Set (BooleanFunction n)) (φ : Fin m → (Fin n → Bool) → F),
+    (∀ i j, bitsOf enc (φ i) j ∈ S) →
+      Synthesis interpretation S (Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun v => G fun i => φ i v) j)
+/-- A bit synthesis with `a` gates is one with any larger budget. -/
+theorem BitSynthesis.mono {enc : F ≃ BitString w} {G : (Fin m → F) → F} {a b : ℕ}
+    (h : BitSynthesis enc G a) (hab : a ≤ b) : BitSynthesis enc G b :=
+  fun n S φ hφ => (h n S φ hφ).mono Set.Subset.rfl Set.Subset.rfl hab
+/-- **The Goldreich–Levin decoder of the inner code.** At a point `x`, the corrected-majority
+candidate of the predictor `r ↦ C (bits of x, r)` with fixed masks and guess, read as a field
+noncomputable def glPredictor (enc : F ≃ BitString w) (C : BooleanFunction (m * w + w)) {K : ℕ}
+    (masks : Fin K → BitString w) (guess : BitString K) : (Fin m → F) → F :=
+    (Crypto.GoldreichLevin.candidate (fun r => C (Fin.append (bitsOfPoint enc x) r)) masks guess)
+/-- The gate budget of the Goldreich–Levin stage: two constants, and for each output bit,
+`2 ^ K - 1` copies of the predictor, each with at most one negation, and a strict majority. -/
+private theorem append_apply {n p q : ℕ} (A : Fin p → BooleanFunction n)
+    (B : Fin q → BooleanFunction n) (k : Fin (p + q)) (v : Fin n → Bool) :
+    Fin.append A B k v = Fin.append (fun i => A i v) (fun i => B i v) k := by
+/-- A strict majority of the `N` votes of a finset, enumerated, is a threshold of `N` functions. -/
+private theorem strictMajorityOn_eq_atLeast {n : ℕ} {ι : Type*} (T : Finset ι)
+    (vote : ι → BooleanFunction n) (v : Fin n → Bool) :
+    BitString.strictMajorityOn T (fun i => vote i v) =
+      atLeast (fun l => if h : l < #T then vote (T.equivFin.symm ⟨l, h⟩) else fun _ => false)
+  refine card_bij (fun i hi => (T.equivFin ⟨i, (mem_filter.1 hi).1⟩ : ℕ)) (fun i hi => ?_)
+    (fun i hi i' hi' h => ?_) (fun l hl => ?_)
+/-- **The Goldreich–Levin stage.** If the predictor `C` has a De Morgan circuit with at most `s`
+gates, the Goldreich–Levin decoder with masks `masks` and guess `guess` is bit-synthesizable with
+theorem bitSynthesis_glPredictor (enc : F ≃ BitString w) {C : BooleanFunction (m * w + w)}
+    {sC : ℕ} (hC : complexity interpretation (single C) ≤ sC) {K : ℕ}
+    (masks : Fin K → BitString w) (guess : BitString K) :
+    BitSynthesis enc (glPredictor enc C masks guess) (glCost w K sC) := by

+  let xb : Fin (m * w) → BooleanFunction n := fun k v => bitsOfPoint enc (fun i => φ i v) k
+  have hxb : ∀ k, xb k ∈ S₁ := fun k =>

+  have hvote : ∀ (r : BitString w) (bit : Bool), Synthesis interpretation S₁

+    let g : Fin (m * w + w) → BooleanFunction n := Fin.append xb fun k _ => r k

+  -- the strict majority for each output bit

+    C (Fin.append (bitsOfPoint enc fun i => φ i v) (Pi.single j 1 + ∑ l ∈ t, masks l)) ^^

+      {bitsOf enc (fun v => glPredictor enc C masks guess fun i => φ i v) j}
+    have hvotes := Synthesis.biUnion (I := interpretation) (s := S₁) T (fun t => {V j t})
+    set S₂ := S₁ ∪ ⋃ t ∈ T, {V j t}
+      (fun l => if h : l < #T then V j (T.equivFin.symm ⟨l, h⟩) else fun _ => false)
+    (fun j => {bitsOf enc (fun v => glPredictor enc C masks guess fun i => φ i v) j})
+  · simp only [sum_const, card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul, glCost, T,
+/-- The gate budget of the line stage over a field with `q` elements, for points in `m`
+variables, `M` monomials, `Y`-degrees up to `ℓ`, degree `d` and an oracle of cost `SG`: the points
+of the line and the decoding with a hint are bit-blasted, and the oracle is queried at the `q`
+def lineCost (w q m M ℓ d SG : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  ((q + 5) * m + 2 + (1 + hintDecodeCost q q M ℓ d)) * bitBlastCost w + q * SG
+/-- **The line stage.** If `G` is bit-synthesizable with `SG` gates, then the local list decoder
+`lineListDecode G d D z a` is bit-synthesizable with `lineCost` gates. -/
+theorem BitSynthesis.lineListDecode {enc : F ≃ BitString w} {G : (Fin m → F) → F} {SG : ℕ}
+    (hG : BitSynthesis enc G SG) (d D : ℕ) (z : Fin m → F) (a : F) :
+    BitSynthesis enc (Code.lineListDecode G d D z a)
+      (lineCost w (Fintype.card F) m #(Sudan.monomials d D) (D / d) d SG) := by
+  -- the points of the line and the hint position
+  let ΨA : Option (F × Fin m) → (Fin m → F) → F := fun o v => match o with
+    | none => firstNonzero (z - fun i => v i)
+      ((fun i => v i) + t • (firstNonzero (z - fun i => v i))⁻¹ • (z - fun i => v i)) i
+    Synthesis.full_linePoints (s := inputs m) (fun i v => v i) (fun i => ⟨i, rfl⟩) z
+  have hA' := Synthesis.bitBlast_synthesis enc ΨA hA φ hφ
+  set TA := Set.range fun oj : Option (F × Fin m) × Fin w =>
+    bitsOf enc (fun x => ΨA oj.1 fun i => φ i x) oj.2
+  -- the oracle at the points of the line
+  let pt : F → Fin m → (Fin n → Bool) → F := fun t i x => ΨA (some (t, i)) fun k => φ k x
+      (⋃ t : F, Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => G fun i => pt t i x) j) (q * SG) := by
+      (fun t : F => Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => G fun i => pt t i x) j)
+      (fun _ => SG) (fun t => hG n (S ∪ TA) (pt t) fun i j =>
+  set TB := ⋃ t : F, Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => G fun i => pt t i x) j
+  let ΨC : Unit → (Fin (q + 1) → F) → F := fun _ v =>
+    hintDecode id (fun t => v (Fin.castSucc (e t))) d D (v (Fin.last q)) a
+      (1 + hintDecodeCost q q #(Sudan.monomials d D) (D / d) d) := by
+    have hdec := Synthesis.full_hintDecode (s := inputs (q + 1) ∪ {fun _ => a}) (ι := F) id
+        (fun v : Fin (q + 1) → F => v (Fin.castSucc (e t))) ∈ inputs (q + 1)))
+      (τ := fun v => v (Fin.last q)) (Set.mem_union_left _ (⟨Fin.last q, rfl⟩ :
+        (fun v : Fin (q + 1) → F => v (Fin.last q)) ∈ inputs (q + 1)))
+  let φC : Fin (q + 1) → (Fin n → Bool) → F :=
+    Fin.lastCases (fun x => ΨA none fun i => φ i x) fun k x => G fun i => pt (e.symm k) i x
+  have hφC : ∀ k j, bitsOf enc (φC k) j ∈ (S ∪ TA) ∪ TB := by
+  have hC' := Synthesis.bitBlast_synthesis enc ΨC hC φC hφC
+    refine Or.inr ⟨((), j), funext fun x => ?_⟩
+    simp only [bitsOf, ΨC, φC, Fin.lastCases_last, Fin.lastCases_castSucc, Equiv.symm_apply_apply,
+/-- The gate budget of the self-correction stage, for points in `m` variables, `d + 1` nodes, a
+majority tree of depth `L` and an oracle of cost `S1`: the points of the lines and the
+interpolation and majorities are bit-blasted, and the oracle is queried at `3 ^ L * (d + 1)`
+def selfCorrectCost (w m d L S1 : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+/-- **The self-correction stage.** If `C1` is bit-synthesizable with `S1` gates, then the majority
+tree of depth `L` of the interpolations of `C1` along the lines through `x` in the directions
+theorem BitSynthesis.selfCorrect {enc : F ≃ BitString w} {C1 : (Fin m → F) → F} {S1 : ℕ}
+    (hC1 : BitSynthesis enc C1 S1) {d : ℕ} (ν : Fin (d + 1) ↪ F) {L : ℕ}
+    BitSynthesis enc (fun x => majTree L fun τ => lagrangeDecode ν C1 x (V τ))
+      (selfCorrectCost w m d L S1) := by
+  let ΨA : (Fin (3 ^ L) × Fin (d + 1)) × Fin m → (Fin m → F) → F := fun o v =>
+    have := Synthesis.family (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := inputs m) ΨA (fun _ => 1)
+      (fun o => Synthesis.full_unary (fun a => a + ν o.1.2 * V o.1.1 o.2)
+        (⟨o.2, rfl⟩ : (fun v : Fin m → F => v o.2) ∈ inputs m))
+    simpa [Fintype.card_prod, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc] using this
+  have hA' := Synthesis.bitBlast_synthesis enc ΨA hA φ hφ
+  set TA := Set.range fun oj : ((Fin (3 ^ L) × Fin (d + 1)) × Fin m) × Fin w =>
+    bitsOf enc (fun x => ΨA oj.1 fun i => φ i x) oj.2
+  let pt : Fin (3 ^ L) × Fin (d + 1) → Fin m → (Fin n → Bool) → F := fun τi k x =>
+    ΨA (τi, k) fun i => φ i x
+        Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => C1 fun k => pt τi k x) j)
+        Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => C1 fun k => pt τi k x) j)
+      (fun _ => S1) (fun τi => hC1 n (S ∪ TA) (pt τi) fun k j =>
+    simpa [Fintype.card_prod, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc] using this
+  set TB := ⋃ τi : Fin (3 ^ L) × Fin (d + 1),
+    Set.range fun j => bitsOf enc (fun x => C1 fun k => pt τi k x) j
+  let ΨC : Unit → (Fin (3 ^ L * (d + 1)) → F) → F := fun _ v =>
+    majTree L fun τ => ∑ i, lagrangeWeight ν i * v (finProdFinEquiv (τ, i))
+      (fun τ v => ∑ i, lagrangeWeight ν i * v (finProdFinEquiv (τ, i)))
+        simpa using Synthesis.full_weightedSum (s := inputs (3 ^ L * (d + 1))) (lagrangeWeight ν)
+          (fun i v => v (finProdFinEquiv (τ, i))) (fun i => ⟨_, rfl⟩))
+        Set.range fun τ (v : Fin (3 ^ L * (d + 1)) → F) =>
+          ∑ i, lagrangeWeight ν i * v (finProdFinEquiv (τ, i))) L
+      (fun τ v => ∑ i, lagrangeWeight ν i * v (finProdFinEquiv (τ, i)))
+  let φC : Fin (3 ^ L * (d + 1)) → (Fin n → Bool) → F := fun k x =>
+    C1 fun i => pt (finProdFinEquiv.symm k) i x
+  have hφC : ∀ k j, bitsOf enc (φC k) j ∈ (S ∪ TA) ∪ TB := fun k j =>
+  have hC' := Synthesis.bitBlast_synthesis enc ΨC hC φC hφC
+    refine Or.inr ⟨((), j), funext fun x => ?_⟩
+    simp only [bitsOf, ΨC, φC, Equiv.symm_apply_apply, lagrangeDecode, pt, ΨA]

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Synthesis over the full binary basis
+Over the full binary basis `fullInterpretation (k := 2)` every constant and every operation with
+at most two arguments is one gate. This module records the synthesis rules used to count gates of
+algebraic computations over a carrier `U`: an operation with one or two available arguments costs
+functions over an additive commutative monoid costs `N + 1` gates, one of them for the constant
+zero (`Synthesis.full_sum`), and a sum of `N` products of available functions over a semiring costs
+`2 * N + 1` gates (`Synthesis.full_dot`). A *chain* `v 0 = c`, `v (i + 1) = op i (v i) (g i x)`
+of length `len`, fed by available functions `g i`, costs `len + 1` gates for all of its values
+(`Synthesis.full_chain`); chains compute prefix tests such as the first nonzero entry of a vector.
+Applied to a field, this counts field operations, with every operation that depends on at most two
+field elements, including tests and selections, charged one gate.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_unary`: one gate for an operation on one available function.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_binary_mem`: one gate for an operation on two available functions.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_sum`: `N + 1` gates for a sum of `N` available functions.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_dot`: `2 * N + 1` gates for a sum of `N` products.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_chain`: `len + 1` gates for all values of a chain.
+* [P. Bürgisser, M. Clausen, M. A. Shokrollahi, *Algebraic Complexity Theory*]
+variable {U : Type*} {n : ℕ} {s : Set ((Fin n → U) → U)} {f g : (Fin n → U) → U}
+/-- An operation applied to one available function costs one gate of the full binary basis. -/
+  full_gate (k := 2) (r := 1) (by decide) (fun v => op (v 0)) (fun _ => f) fun _ => hf
+/-- An operation applied to two available functions costs one gate of the full binary basis. -/
+theorem full_binary_mem (op : U → U → U) (hf : f ∈ s) (hg : g ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s {fun x => op (f x) (g x)} 1 := by
+  simpa using full_binary (of_mem hf) (of_mem hg) op
+/-- A sum of available functions, indexed by a finset `S`, costs `#S + 1` gates of the full
+binary basis: one addition for each summand and a constant zero to start from. -/
+theorem full_sum [AddCommMonoid U] {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι) (f : ι → (Fin n → U) → U)
+    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s {fun x => ∑ i ∈ S, f i x} (#S + 1) := by
+    (fun f g => full_binary_mem (s := {f, g}) (· + ·) (by simp) (by simp)) S
+    (full_const (k := 2) (s := s) (0 : U)) (cost := fun _ => 0) (fun i hi => of_mem (hf i hi))
+  simp only [zero_add, sum_const, smul_eq_mul, mul_one] at h
+/-- A sum of products of available functions, indexed by a finset `S`, costs `2 * #S + 1` gates
+    (f g : ι → (Fin n → U) → U) (hf : ∀ i ∈ S, f i ∈ s) (hg : ∀ i ∈ S, g i ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s {fun x => ∑ i ∈ S, f i x * g i x}
+  have hprod := biUnion (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := s) S
+    (fun i => {fun x => f i x * g i x}) (fun _ => 1)
+    (fun i hi => full_binary_mem (· * ·) (hf i hi) (hg i hi))
+  have hsum := full_sum (s := s ∪ ⋃ i ∈ S, {fun x => f i x * g i x}) S
+    (fun i x => f i x * g i x) (fun i hi => Set.mem_union_right _ (Set.mem_biUnion hi rfl))
+/-- The values of a *chain*: `v 0 = c` and `v (i + 1) = op i (v i) (g i x)`. -/
+def chainValue (c : U) (op : ℕ → U → U → U) (g : ℕ → (Fin n → U) → U) :
+  | i + 1 => fun x => op i (chainValue c op g i x) (g i x)
+/-- All values `v 0, …, v len` of a chain of length `len` fed by available functions cost
+`len + 1` gates of the full binary basis: a constant and one binary gate per link. -/
+theorem full_chain (c : U) (op : ℕ → U → U → U) (g : ℕ → (Fin n → U) → U) (len : ℕ)
+      (Set.range fun i : Fin (len + 1) => chainValue c op g i) (len + 1) := by
+    have hstep := full_binary_mem (s := s ∪ Set.range fun i : Fin (len + 1) =>
+      chainValue c op g i) (op len) (Set.mem_union_right _ ⟨Fin.last len, rfl⟩)
+    refine ((ih fun i hi => hg i (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hi)).comp hstep).mono Set.Subset.rfl ?_
+    rcases Fin.eq_castSucc_or_eq_last i with ⟨i, rfl⟩ | rfl

+# Circuits for Reed–Solomon decoding with a hint
+Sudan decoding with a hint (`Cslib.Code.hintDecode`) is an arithmetic computation on the received
+word, the hint and fixed constants: elimination for the interpolant of least `Y`-degree, then
+Newton iteration evaluated on all of `F`. Over the full binary basis of the field, where every
+operation on at most two field elements is one gate, it therefore has circuits of size polynomial
+in `|F|`, the number of points and the number of monomials. For `n` points, `M` monomials of
+`(1, d)`-weighted degree at most `D`, `ℓ = D / d` and `q = |F|`:
+* the interpolant costs at most `interpolantCost n M ℓ` gates
+* Newton iteration to degree `d` costs at most `henselCost q M d` gates
+* the whole decoder costs at most `hintDecodeCost n q M ℓ d`, their sum
+The word, the hint position and the hint value may be arbitrary available functions of the
+* [M. Sudan, L. Trevisan, S. Vadhan, *Pseudorandom generators without the XOR lemma*]
+* [M. Sudan, *Decoding of Reed Solomon codes beyond the error-correction bound*][Sudan1997]
+/-- The gate budget of the least-`Y`-degree interpolant for `n` points, `M` monomials and
+/-- The gate budget of one Newton step over a field with `q` elements, for `M` monomials and
+def henselStepCost (q M d : ℕ) : ℕ := q * (2 * d + 3 * M + 6) + 2
+/-- The gate budget of Newton iteration to degree `d`. -/
+def henselCost (q M d : ℕ) : ℕ := 3 * M + 1 + d * henselStepCost q M d + (2 * d + 3)
+/-- The gate budget of decoding with a hint. -/
+def hintDecodeCost (n q M ℓ d : ℕ) : ℕ := interpolantCost n M ℓ + henselCost q M d
+variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] {N : ℕ} {s : Set ((Fin N → F) → F)}
+/-- The coefficients chosen by Newton iteration up to `k` cost `k * henselStepCost q M d` gates,
+for `k ≤ d`, given the coefficients of `Q`, the hint position and value and `λ`. -/
+private theorem full_henselSeq (M : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (c : ℕ × ℕ → (Fin N → F) → F)
+    (hc : ∀ m ∈ M, c m ∈ s) {τ a lam : (Fin N → F) → F} (hτ : τ ∈ s) (ha : a ∈ s)
+        henselSeq (Sudan.bivariateOf M fun m => c m x) (τ x) (a x) (lam x) i)
+    set T := Set.range fun i : Fin (k + 1) => fun x =>
+      henselSeq (Sudan.bivariateOf M fun m => c m x) (τ x) (a x) (lam x) i
+    let h : ℕ → (Fin N → F) → F := fun i x =>
+      henselSeq (Sudan.bivariateOf M fun m => c m x) (τ x) (a x) (lam x) i
+    have hh : ∀ i ≤ k, h i ∈ s ∪ T := fun i hi =>
+    -- the values of the current iterate at all points
+    let A : F → (Fin N → F) → F := fun t x => ∑ i ∈ range (k + 1), h i x * t ^ i
+      have := family (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := s ∪ T) A (fun _ => 2 * k + 3)
+          have hmul := biUnion (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := s ∪ T) (range (k + 1))
+            (fun i => {fun x => h i x * t ^ i}) (fun _ => 1)
+            (fun i hi => full_unary (fun v => v * t ^ i) (hh i (Nat.lt_succ_iff.1
+          have hsum := full_sum (s := (s ∪ T) ∪ ⋃ i ∈ range (k + 1), {fun x => h i x * t ^ i})
+            (range (k + 1)) (fun i x => h i x * t ^ i)
+    let V : F → (Fin N → F) → F := fun t x =>
+      ∑ m ∈ M, c m x * ((t + τ x) ^ m.1 * A t x ^ m.2)
+          have hg := biUnion (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := s₁) M
+            (fun m => {fun x => (t + τ x) ^ m.1 * A t x ^ m.2}) (fun _ => 1)
+            (fun m _ => full_binary_mem (fun u v => (t + u) ^ m.1 * v ^ m.2)
+          have hdot := full_dot (s := s₁ ∪ ⋃ m ∈ M, {fun x => (t + τ x) ^ m.1 * A t x ^ m.2}) M
+            c (fun m x => (t + τ x) ^ m.1 * A t x ^ m.2)
+    let W : (Fin N → F) → F := fun x => ∑ t, coeffWeight (k + 1) t * V t x
+      have hmul := biUnion (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := s₂) univ
+        (fun t => {fun x => coeffWeight (k + 1) t * V t x}) (fun _ => 1)
+        (fun t _ => full_unary (fun v => coeffWeight (k + 1) t * v)
+      have hsum := full_sum (s := s₂ ∪ ⋃ t ∈ (univ : Finset F),
+          {fun x => coeffWeight (k + 1) t * V t x}) univ
+        (fun t x => coeffWeight (k + 1) t * V t x)
+    have h₄ : Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s₂ ∪ {W}) {fun x => -W x / lam x} 1 :=
+      rcases Fin.eq_castSucc_or_eq_last i with ⟨i, rfl⟩ | rfl
+        change henselSeq (Sudan.bivariateOf M fun m => c m x) (τ x) (a x) (lam x) (k + 1) =
+        simp only [W, V, A, h, eval_henselTrunc, Sudan.evalEval_bivariateOf, mul_assoc]
+      have hstep : Fintype.card F * (2 * k + 3) + (Fintype.card F * (3 * #M + 1) +
+          (2 * Fintype.card F + 1 + 1)) ≤ henselStepCost (Fintype.card F) #M d := by
+/-- **Newton iteration by a circuit.** Given the coefficients on `M` of `Q`, the hint position and
+the hint value as available functions, `henselValue Q τ a d` costs at most `henselCost q M d`
+theorem full_henselValue (M : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (c : ℕ × ℕ → (Fin N → F) → F)
+    (hc : ∀ m ∈ M, c m ∈ s) {τ a : (Fin N → F) → F} (hτ : τ ∈ s) (ha : a ∈ s) (d : ℕ) :
+      {fun x => henselValue (Sudan.bivariateOf M fun m => c m x) (τ x) (a x) d}
+  let lam : (Fin N → F) → F := fun x => ∑ m ∈ M, c m x * (m.2 * τ x ^ m.1 * a x ^ (m.2 - 1))
+    have hg := biUnion (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := s) M
+      (fun m _ => full_binary_mem (fun u v => (m.2 : F) * u ^ m.1 * v ^ (m.2 - 1)) hτ ha)
+    have hdot := full_dot (s := s ∪ ⋃ m ∈ M, {fun x => (m.2 : F) * τ x ^ m.1 * a x ^ (m.2 - 1)})
+      M c (fun m x => (m.2 : F) * τ x ^ m.1 * a x ^ (m.2 - 1))
+  have h₂ := full_henselSeq (s := s₁) M c (fun m hm => Set.mem_union_left _ (hc m hm))
+    (Set.mem_union_left _ hτ) (Set.mem_union_left _ ha) (Set.mem_union_right _ rfl) d d le_rfl
+  set T := Set.range fun i : Fin (d + 1) => fun x =>
+    henselSeq (Sudan.bivariateOf M fun m => c m x) (τ x) (a x) (lam x) i
+  let h : ℕ → (Fin N → F) → F := fun i x =>
+    henselSeq (Sudan.bivariateOf M fun m => c m x) (τ x) (a x) (lam x) i
+      {fun x => ∑ i ∈ range (d + 1), h i x * (-τ x) ^ i} (2 * d + 3) := by
+    have hmul := biUnion (I := fullInterpretation (k := 2)) (s := s₁ ∪ T) (range (d + 1))
+      (fun i => {fun x => h i x * (-τ x) ^ i}) (fun _ => 1)
+      (fun i hi => full_binary_mem (fun u v => u * (-v) ^ i)
+    have hsum := full_sum (s := (s₁ ∪ T) ∪ ⋃ i ∈ range (d + 1), {fun x => h i x * (-τ x) ^ i})
+      (range (d + 1)) (fun i x => h i x * (-τ x) ^ i)
+    simp only [henselValue, eval_henselTrunc, evalEval_derivative_bivariateOf, h, lam]
+/-- **The least-`Y`-degree interpolant by a circuit.** Given the received word as available
+functions, its interpolant coefficients on `monomials d D` cost at most
+`interpolantCost n M (D / d)` gates of the full binary basis, for `n` points and `M` monomials. -/
+theorem full_interpolantCoeffs (α : ι → F) (w : ι → (Fin N → F) → F) (hw : ∀ i, w i ∈ s)
+      (Set.range fun m : Sudan.monomials d D => fun x =>
+        Sudan.interpolantCoeffs α (fun i => w i x) d D m)
+  -- the entries of the interpolation matrix
+  let E : ι × M → (Fin N → F) → F := fun tm x =>
+      (fun tm => full_unary (fun v => α tm.1 ^ (tm.2 : ℕ × ℕ).1 * v ^ (tm.2 : ℕ × ℕ).2)
+  let u : (j : Fin (ℓ + 1)) → Fin #(Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j) → (Fin N → F) → F :=
+    fun j m x => Sudan.kernelVecUpTo α (fun i => w i x) d D j m
+  have hsubM : ∀ j : ℕ, Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j ⊆ M := fun _ => filter_subset _ _
+      (⋃ j : Fin (ℓ + 1), Set.range (u j)) ((ℓ + 1) * kernelVecCost (Fintype.card ι) #M) := by
+      (fun j : Fin (ℓ + 1) => Set.range (u j)) (fun _ => kernelVecCost (Fintype.card ι) #M)
+          (fun t m x => Sudan.interpMatrix α (fun i => w i x) (Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j) t m)
+            ⟨_, hsubM j ((Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j).equivFin.symm m).2⟩), rfl⟩)).mono
+          have : #(Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j) ≤ #M := card_le_card (hsubM j)
+  set s₂ := s₁ ∪ ⋃ j : Fin (ℓ + 1), Set.range (u j)
+  have hu : ∀ j m, u j m ∈ s₂ := fun j m =>
+  let z : Fin (ℓ + 1) → (Fin N → F) → F := fun j x =>
+    if (fun m => u j m x) = 0 then 0 else 1
+  have h₃ : Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s₂ (Set.range z) ((ℓ + 1) * (#M + 1)) := by
+  let f : Fin (ℓ + 1) → (Fin N → F) → F := fun j x => firstFlags (fun j => z j x) j
+  have h₄ := full_firstFlags (s := s₃) z fun j => Set.mem_union_right _ ⟨j, rfl⟩
+  let J : ℕ × ℕ → Finset (Fin (ℓ + 1)) := fun m => univ.filter fun j : Fin (ℓ + 1) =>
+  let coef : M → (Fin N → F) → F := fun m x =>
+    ∑ j ∈ J m, f j x * Sudan.coeffsOf (Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j) (fun m' => u j m' x) m
+        refine (full_dot (s := s₄) (J m) f (fun j x => Sudan.coeffsOf
+          (Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j) (fun m' => u j m' x) m)
+        · have hm : (m : ℕ × ℕ) ∈ Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j := (mem_filter.1 hj).2
+          have : (fun x => Sudan.coeffsOf (Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j) (fun m' => u j m' x) m) =
+              u j ((Sudan.monomialsUpTo d D j).equivFin ⟨m, hm⟩) := by
+    simp only [coef, J, f, z, u, Sudan.interpolantCoeffs, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply,
+/-- **Decoding with a hint by a circuit.** Given the received word, the hint position and the
+hint value as available functions, `hintDecode α w d D τ a` costs at most
+`hintDecodeCost n q M (D / d) d` gates of the full binary basis, for `n` points, `q = |F|` and
+`M` monomials of `(1, d)`-weighted degree at most `D`. -/
+theorem full_hintDecode (α : ι → F) (w : ι → (Fin N → F) → F) (hw : ∀ i, w i ∈ s)
+    {τ a : (Fin N → F) → F} (hτ : τ ∈ s) (ha : a ∈ s) (d D : ℕ) :
+      {fun x => hintDecode α (fun i => w i x) d D (τ x) (a x)}
+      (hintDecodeCost (Fintype.card ι) (Fintype.card F) #(Sudan.monomials d D) (D / d) d) := by
+  have h₁ := full_interpolantCoeffs α w hw d D
+  set T := Set.range fun m : Sudan.monomials d D => fun x =>
+    Sudan.interpolantCoeffs α (fun i => w i x) d D m
+  have h₂ := full_henselValue (s := s ∪ T) (Sudan.monomials d D)
+    (fun m x => Sudan.interpolantCoeffs α (fun i => w i x) d D m)
+    (fun m hm => Set.mem_union_right _ ⟨⟨m, hm⟩, rfl⟩) (Set.mem_union_left _ hτ)

+# Circuits for the arithmetic of Reed–Muller decoding
+The decoders `Cslib.Code.lineListDecode` and the self-correction by interpolation and majority
+trees query an oracle at computed points and combine the answers arithmetically. This module
+counts the arithmetic over the full binary basis of the field, where every operation on at most
+two field elements is one gate; the oracle queries are accounted for separately.
+* The first nonzero entry of a vector of `m` available entries costs `4 * m + 2` gates
+* The points `x + t • v`, for all `t ∈ F`, of the line through `x` and a fixed point `z`
+  parametrized as in `Cslib.Code.lineListDecode`, together with the hint position, cost
+* A combination with fixed weights of `N` available values costs `2 * N + 1` gates
+* A majority tree over `3 ^ L` available values costs at most `2 * 3 ^ L - 2` gates
+  (`Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_majTree`): four gates for each majority of three, computed as
+* [M. Sudan, L. Trevisan, S. Vadhan, *Pseudorandom generators without the XOR lemma*]
+variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [DecidableEq F] {N : ℕ} {s : Set ((Fin N → F) → F)}
+/-- **The first nonzero entry** of a vector of `m` available functions costs `4 * m + 2` gates. -/
+theorem full_firstNonzero {m : ℕ} (u : Fin m → (Fin N → F) → F) (hu : ∀ i, u i ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s {fun x => firstNonzero fun i => u i x}
+  have h₁ := full_firstFlags (s := s) u hu
+  have h₂ := full_dot (s := s ∪ Set.range fun i x => firstFlags (fun j => u j x) i) univ
+    (fun i x => firstFlags (fun j => u j x) i) u
+    (fun i _ => Set.mem_union_right _ ⟨i, rfl⟩) (fun i _ => Set.mem_union_left _ (hu i))
+/-- **The points of a line by a circuit.** Given the coordinates of `x` as available functions
+and a fixed point `z`, the hint position `firstNonzero (z - x)` and the coordinates of all points
+`x + t • (firstNonzero (z - x))⁻¹ • (z - x)`, `t ∈ F`, of the line through `x` and `z` cost
+`(q + 5) * m + 2` gates of the full binary basis. -/
+theorem full_linePoints [Fintype F] {m : ℕ} (x : Fin m → (Fin N → F) → F) (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ s)
+      (Set.range fun o : Option (F × Fin m) => fun v => match o with
+        | none => firstNonzero (z - fun i => x i v)
+        | some (t, i) => ((fun i => x i v) + t • (firstNonzero (z - fun i => x i v))⁻¹ •

+# Reed–Solomon list decoding with a hint
+List decoding a Reed–Solomon codeword from a small fraction of agreements returns several
+candidate polynomials. In local list decoding of Reed–Muller codes [SudanTrevisanVadhan2001] the
+right candidate is singled out by its value `a = P(τ)` at one further point, supplied as advice.
+This module computes the value `P(0)` of that candidate from the received word, `τ` and `a`
+alone, with linear algebra and Newton iteration, and no root finding or factoring.
+Let `Q` be the Sudan interpolant of least `Y`-degree of the received word
+(`Cslib.Code.Sudan.interpolant`). If `P` has degree at most `d` and more than `D` agreements, then
+`Q = (Y - P) * S` with `S(X, P(X)) ≠ 0` of degree at most `D - d`
+(`Cslib.Code.Sudan.exists_eq_mul_eval_ne_zero`), so for all but `D - d` points `τ` the root `P` is
+simple at `(τ, P(τ))`: `∂Q/∂Y (τ, P(τ)) = S(τ, P(τ)) ≠ 0`. Then the Taylor coefficients of `P` at
+`τ` are determined one at a time by Newton's (Hensel's) rule: if `A` has degree less than
+`k ≤ d` and agrees with `P(X + τ)` below degree `k`, then the coefficient of `X ^ k` in
+`P(X + τ)` is `-[X ^ k] Q(X + τ, A(X)) / ∂Q/∂Y (τ, a)` (`Cslib.Code.henselCoeff_eq`). The
+coefficient `[X ^ k] Q(X + τ, A(X))` is a fixed linear combination of the values

+degree at most `D < |F|`. So the whole computation `Cslib.Code.hintDecode` is an arithmetic
+computation on the received word, the hint and fixed constants, with no other branching than the
+tests for zero in the elimination; the decoded value is correct for all but `D - d` of the hint

+# Independent set, clique and vertex cover as classes of finite structures
+An instance of independent set, clique or vertex cover is a graph together with a target size.
+Here it is a finite structure of the vocabulary `sizedGraph`: a binary relation `adj`, the edges,
+and a unary relation `size`, whose number of elements is the target size. Giving the size as a set
+of elements rather than as a number keeps the vocabulary free of numeric predicates, and makes
+The edge relation need not be symmetric, and loops are ignored: an independent set has no edge
+between two distinct vertices in either direction, a clique has edges between any two distinct
+vertices in both directions, and a vertex cover contains an endpoint of every edge between
+distinct vertices. On simple graphs these are the usual problems: clique and node cover
+asked for have exactly `|size|` vertices; since subsets of independent sets and of cliques, and
+supersets of vertex covers, are again such sets, this is equivalent to the usual thresholds "at
+least `|size|`" for independent sets and cliques and "at most `|size|`" for vertex covers, as
+`|size|` never exceeds the number of vertices.
+The machine-level versions of these problems, on graphs encoded as lists of vertices and edges
+with a binary target size, are `Cslib.Complexity.IndependentSet`, `Cslib.Complexity.Clique` and
+`Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover`, which are proved `NP`-complete. Those read graphs as simple graphs
+on their declared vertices; the classes here are classes of finite structures, closed under
+isomorphism, without an encoding, and their reductions are first-order interpretations rather than
+* `sizedGraph.IndependentSet`: the graph has an independent set of `|size|` vertices.
+* `sizedGraph.Clique`: the graph has a clique of `|size|` vertices.
+* `sizedGraph.VertexCover`: the graph has a vertex cover of `|size|` vertices.
+The three classes are closed under isomorphism, and quantifier-free reducible to each other.
+Complementing the edge relation off the diagonal (`sizedGraph.complementEdges`) turns independent
+sets into cliques and back, and complementing the size relation (`sizedGraph.complementSize`)
+turns an instance asking for an independent set of size `k` into one asking for a vertex cover of
+size `n - k`: a set is independent exactly when its complement is a vertex cover. Both are
+one-dimensional quantifier-free interpretations, and their composite is Karp's reduction from
+clique to node cover [Karp1972]. The reductions are proved with `fo_reduction`, which leaves only
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.sizedGraph`: the vocabulary of graphs with a size relation.
+  the interpretations complementing the edge relation and the size relation.
+* [M. R. Garey and D. S. Johnson, *Computers and Intractability*][GareyJohnson1979]

+/-- **Vertex cover**: the structures whose graph has a vertex cover, a set of vertices containing
+an endpoint of every edge between distinct vertices, with as many vertices as the size relation

+    RelMap sizedGraph.adj ![e x, e y] ↔ RelMap sizedGraph.adj ![x, y] := by

+  exact iff_of_eq (congrArg _ (funext fun i => by fin_cases i; rfl))
+private theorem ncard_image (e : M ≃[sizedGraph] N) (s : Set M) : (e '' s).ncard = s.ncard :=
+/-- Independent set is closed under isomorphism. -/
+    ⟨e '' s, by rw [ncard_image, hs, ncard_size_eq e],

+/-- A set of vertices is independent exactly when its complement is a vertex cover. -/

+/-- **Independent set reduces to clique** by complementing the edge relation: an independent
+set of `G` is a clique of its complement. -/
+  exact fun _ _ => exists_congr fun _ => and_congr_right fun _ =>
+    ⟨fun h _ hx _ hy hxy => ⟨h hx hy hxy, hxy⟩, fun h _ hx _ hy hxy => (h hx hy hxy).1⟩
+/-- **Clique reduces to independent set** by complementing the edge relation: a clique of `G` is
+  exact fun _ _ => exists_congr fun _ => and_congr_right fun _ =>
+    ⟨fun h _ hx _ hy hxy hn => hn.1 (h hx hy hxy),
+      fun h _ hx _ hy hxy => by_contra fun hn => h hx hy hxy ⟨hn, hxy⟩⟩
+/-- **Independent set reduces to vertex cover** by complementing the size relation: a set of `k`
+vertices is independent exactly when its complement, of `n - k` vertices, is a vertex cover. -/
+    ⟨fun ⟨s, hs, hind⟩ => ⟨sᶜ, ncard_compl_eq_iff.2 hs, (pairwise_not_adj_iff_compl s).1 hind⟩,
+/-- **Vertex cover reduces to independent set** by complementing the size relation: a set of `k`
+vertices is a vertex cover exactly when its complement, of `n - k` vertices, is independent. -/
+      fun ⟨s, hs, hind⟩ => ⟨sᶜ, ncard_compl_eq_iff.1 ?_, (pairwise_not_adj_iff_compl s).1 hind⟩⟩
+/-- Clique reduces to vertex cover, through independent set. -/
+/-- Vertex cover reduces to clique, through independent set. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A class `K` of `L`-structures is **quantifier-free reducible** to a class `K'` of `L'`-structures
+(`FO.QFReduces K K'`) when it is first-order reducible to it (`FO.Reduces`) through a
+quantifier-free interpretation (`Interpretation.IsQF`): the domain and the relations of the
+interpreted structure are Boolean combinations of atomic formulas of `L`. Like first-order
+reducibility, quantifier-free reducibility is reflexive on classes closed under isomorphism of a
+relational language, because the identity interpretation is quantifier-free, and transitive when
+the last class is closed under isomorphism, because quantifier-free interpretations compose.
+The vocabularies are parameters: no order or BIT predicate is assumed, and the dimension is any
+finite type. Quantifier-free reductions are therefore not quantifier-free projections, which
+moreover allow only a single input literal for each output bit and fix the numeric vocabulary
+A reduction through a given interpretation is proved by two kinds of arguments: syntactic side
+conditions, such as quantifier-freeness, and the semantic statement that `M ∈ K` exactly when the
+interpreted structure belongs to `K'`. For a one-dimensional interpretation whose domain formula
+always holds, `QFReduces.of_unitStructure` states the semantic part on the input universe itself,
+as `Reduces.of_unitStructure` does for first-order reductions. The tactic `fo_reduction` applies
+these lemmas and proves the side conditions.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.QFReduces`: quantifier-free reducibility between classes of finite structures.
+  reducibility is a preorder on classes closed under isomorphism.
+  one-dimensional interpretations, stated on the input universe.
+* [N. Immerman and S. Landau, *The Complexity of Iterated Multiplication*][ImmermanLandau1995]
+universe u v u' v' u'' v'' w
+variable {L : Language.{u, v}} {L' : Language.{u', v'}} {L'' : Language.{u'', v''}}
+/-- A class `K` of `L`-structures is **quantifier-free reducible** to a class `K'` of

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+If `A` reduces to `B` in polynomial time and `B` has an interactive proof, so has `A`: the verifier
+for `A` computes the reduction and runs the verifier for `B` on its result, which is still strict
+oracle PPT (`Cslib.Probability.IsOraclePPTOn.preprocess`), with the same provers, completeness and
+* `Cslib.Complexity.IsInteractiveProof.comp`: an interactive proof along a reduction.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- An interactive proof for `B` gives one for every `A` that `f` maps into `B` exactly. -/
+theorem IsInteractiveProof.comp {verifier : β → WordOracleComp Operation Bool} {A : Set α}
+    {B : Set β} {c s : ENNReal} (h : IsInteractiveProof verifier B c s) {f : α → β}
+    (hf : ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a ∈ B) : IsInteractiveProof (fun a => verifier (f a)) A c s where
+  complete a ha := h.complete (f a) ((hf a).1 ha)
+  sound a ha := h.sound (f a) fun hb => ha ((hf a).2 hb)
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_IP {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+    {B : Set β} (hAB : PolyTimeReducible encA encB A B) (hB : B ∈ IP encB) : A ∈ IP encA := by
+  exact ⟨fun a => verifier (f a), hV.preprocess hf, hproof.comp hfA⟩

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# The machine verifier for quantified Boolean formulas
+The verifier of the interactive proof for `TQBF` as a program with fair coins and word messages,
+realized by a strict oracle PPT machine (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.isOraclePPTOn_verifier`).
+On a formula `ψ` it rejects when `ψ` has a free variable. Otherwise it computes the list `xs` of
+the variable components of all the tokens of `ψ`, with multiplicity and with `0` for the tokens
+without a variable (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.linVars`), which contains every variable of
+`ψ`; the degree bound `D = 2 * size ψ`; and the greatest prime `p` at most `2 * B` for
+`B = 12 * size ψ ^ 2 * (size ψ + 1)`, found by trial division
+(`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.modulus`); by Bertrand's postulate `B < p`. It then runs a stack
+machine over the tokens of the arithmetization of `ψ` that linearizes the variables of `xs` after
+(`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.Machine.step`), checking the claim that the arithmetization has
+* a state holds the remaining tokens, the stack of pending claims, each a point and a value, and
+  whether every check so far passed;
+* a variable or a constant checks the claim on top of the stack, and a negation replaces its value
+* a binary connective or an operator sends the remaining tokens and the point of the top claim,
+  reads `D + 1` rows of `width p` bits of the reply, and proceeds as
+  `Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.verifyAt`; an operator draws its random point by
+Points and values are rebuilt modulo `p` on the variables of `xs` whenever they are pushed, so that
+every step adds at most a polynomial amount of storage
+* `Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.loopInput`: the parameters and tokens computed from a formula.
+  modulus is a prime above the bound.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.isOraclePPTOn_verifier`: the verifier is strict oracle PPT.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Section 8.3][AroraBarak09]
+/-- Tokens of arithmetic formulas, the kind framed before the variable in binary. -/
+noncomputable abbrev encArithToken : ArithQBF.Kind × ℕ ↪ List Bool :=
+/-- Points as lists of pairs of a variable, in binary, and a value, in unary. -/
+noncomputable abbrev encPt : List (ℕ × ℕ) ↪ List Bool := encList (encPair encNat encUnary)
+/-- The parameters of the machine: the variables `xs` linearized after every quantifier, the
+modulus less one, so that the modulus is positive, and the degree bound `D` of every round. -/
+/-- The encoding of the parameters, the numbers in unary. -/
+/-- The input of the loop: the parameters and the tokens of the arithmetic formula. -/
+/-- The encoding of the input of the loop. -/
+/-- A pending claim: a point and a value. -/
+/-- The encoding of a claim, its value in unary. -/
+noncomputable abbrev encClaim : Claim ↪ List Bool := encPair encPt encUnary
+/-- A state of the machine: the remaining tokens, the stack of pending claims, and whether every
+abbrev VState := List (ArithQBF.Kind × ℕ) × List Claim × Bool
+/-- The data of a step: the input of the loop and the current state. -/
+/-- The encoding of the data of a step. -/
+noncomputable abbrev encStepData : StepData ↪ List Bool := encPair encLoopInput encVState
+/-- The variables linearized after every quantifier. -/
+/-- The degree bound of every round. -/
+/-- The claim on top of the stack. -/
+/-- The claims below the top of the stack. -/
+/-- The message of a step: the remaining tokens and the point of the claim on top of the stack. -/
+/-- The state after a failed check: the token and the claim are dropped. -/
+/-- The reply of a step, read as `D + 1` residues. -/
+def replyOf (a : StepData) (word : List Bool) : List ℕ := decodeReply a.modulus a.degree word
+/-- The state after the reply `word` to a binary connective `o`: the claimed values of the two
+arguments are checked against the top claim, then pushed in its place. -/
+def binNext (o : ArithQBF.Connective) (a : StepData) (word : List Bool) : VState :=
+  if connectiveMod a.modulus o ((replyOf a word).getD 0 0) ((replyOf a word).getD 1 0) %
+      (normPt a.modulus a.xs a.top.1, (replyOf a word).getD 1 0) :: a.below, true)
+/-- Whether the reply `word` to an operator `o` passes the check against the top claim. -/
+def opCheck (o : ArithQBF.Operator) (a : StepData) (word : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  decide (operatorMod a.modulus o (lookupPt a.top.1 a.head.2 % a.modulus)
+    (hornerMod a.modulus 0 (replyOf a word)) (hornerMod a.modulus 1 (replyOf a word)) %
+/-- The state after the reply `word` to an operator and the random point `z`: the claim that the
+body has the value of the reply at `z`, with the variable set to `z`. -/
+def opNext (a : StepData) (word : List Bool) (z : ℕ) : VState :=
+    hornerMod a.modulus z (replyOf a word)) :: a.below, true)
+/-- The reply to the message of a step, of which `D + 1` rows are read. -/
+noncomputable def ask (a : StepData) : WordOracleComp Unit (List Bool) :=
+    ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Unit × List Bool => List Bool) ((), message a)
+/-- The continuation of a step on an operator after the reply `word`. -/
+noncomputable def opCont (o : ArithQBF.Operator) (a : StepData) (word : List Bool) :
+  if opCheck o a word then
+    (fun z => opNext a word z) <$> ProbOracleComp.sample (sampleMod a.modulus)
+/-- A step on a token of kind `k`. -/
+noncomputable def stepAt : ArithQBF.Kind → StepData → WordOracleComp Unit VState
+      decide (lookupPt a.top.1 a.head.2 % a.modulus = a.top.2 % a.modulus))
+  | .top, a => pure (a.2.1.tail, a.below, decide (1 % a.modulus = a.top.2 % a.modulus))
+  | .bot, a => pure (a.2.1.tail, a.below, decide (0 % a.modulus = a.top.2 % a.modulus))
+      (normPt a.modulus a.xs a.top.1, subMod a.modulus 1 a.top.2) :: a.below, true)
+  | .and, a => ask a >>= fun word => pure (binNext .and a word)
+  | .or, a => ask a >>= fun word => pure (binNext .or a word)
+/-- **One step of the machine**: while every check passed and tokens remain, process the next
+noncomputable def step (I : LoopInput) (st : VState) : WordOracleComp Unit VState :=
+  if st.2.2 && !st.1.isEmpty then stepAt (st.1.headD (.top, 0)).1 (I, st) else pure st
+/-- The initial state: all the tokens, and the claim that the formula has value `1` at the
+def init (I : LoopInput) : VState := (I.2, [(I.1.1.map fun x => (x, 0), 1)], true)
+/-- The machine runs one step per token. -/
+noncomputable def loop (I : LoopInput) : WordOracleComp Unit VState :=
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a : StepData => a.2.1) encStepData (encList encArithToken) := by
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : StepData × List Bool => replyOf pair.1 pair.2)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : StepData × List Bool => binNext o pair.1 pair.2)
+  cases o <;> unfold binNext <;> simp only [connectiveMod] <;> fun_prop
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : StepData × List Bool => opCheck o pair.1 pair.2)
+  cases o <;> unfold opCheck <;> simp only [operatorMod] <;> fun_prop
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun q : (StepData × List Bool) × ℕ => opNext q.1.1 q.1.2 q.2)
+private lemma ask_pt : IsOraclePPTOn encStepData encBits ask :=
+    IsOraclePPTOn (encPair encStepData encBits) encVState (fun pair => opCont o pair.1 pair.2) := by
+  have hsample : IsOraclePPTOn (Operation := Unit) (encPair encStepData encBits) encUnary
+      (fun pair : StepData × List Bool => ProbOracleComp.sample (sampleMod pair.1.modulus)) :=
+  · exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.isOraclePPTOn (f := fun a : StepData => (a.2.1.tail, a.below,
+      decide (lookupPt a.top.1 a.head.2 % a.modulus = a.top.2 % a.modulus))) (by fun_prop)
+  · exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.isOraclePPTOn (f := fun a : StepData => (a.2.1.tail, a.below,
+  · exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.isOraclePPTOn (f := fun a : StepData => (a.2.1.tail, a.below,

+# Words of the machine verifier for quantified Boolean formulas
+The machine realizing the verifier of `Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.verifyAt` over `ZMod p`
+represents ring elements by natural numbers below `p`, in unary, which is polynomial since `p` is
+chosen of polynomial size. This file gives the arithmetic it performs and its words:
+* the operations of the arithmetization modulo `p` (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.subMod`,
+  Horner's rule modulo `p` (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.hornerMod`), which compute in `ZMod p`;
+* points as lists of pairs of a variable and its value (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.lookupPt`,
+  with the point of the protocol on the variables of a list `xs`
+* the decoding of a reply word as `D + 1` rows of `width p` bits, each read in binary modulo `p`
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.decodeReply`), and the encoding of a reply by the honest prover
+* the samples, a uniform index in the dyadic range above `p` reduced modulo `p`
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.sampleMod`), which give every residue probability at most `2 / p`
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.QBFProtocol.eval_sampleMod_le`) with a fixed number of fair coins.
+All are polynomial-time in their unary or binary inputs.
+def subMod (p a b : ℕ) : ℕ := (a % p + (p - b % p)) % p
+/-- The value of a connective on residues modulo `p`. -/
+def connectiveMod (p : ℕ) : ArithQBF.Connective → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
+  | .or, a, b => subMod p 1 (subMod p 1 a * subMod p 1 b)
+/-- The value of an operator on residues modulo `p`. -/
+def operatorMod (p : ℕ) : ArithQBF.Operator → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
+  | .ex, _, a, b => subMod p 1 (subMod p 1 a * subMod p 1 b)
+  | .lin, t, a, b => (subMod p 1 t * a + t * b) % p
+/-- The value at `z` of a coefficient list modulo `p`, by Horner's rule from the last
+coefficient. The modulus `0` is read as `1`, so that the intermediate values stay small. -/
+def hornerMod (p z : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : ℕ :=
+theorem natCast_subMod [NeZero p] (a b : ℕ) : ((subMod p a b : ℕ) : ZMod p) = a - b := by
+    ((connectiveMod p o a b : ℕ) : ZMod p) = o.apply (a : ZMod p) b := by
+theorem natCast_operatorMod [NeZero p] (o : ArithQBF.Operator) (t a b : ℕ) :
+    ((operatorMod p o t a b : ℕ) : ZMod p) = o.apply (t : ZMod p) a b := by
+  · rw [operatorMod, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_mul, natCast_subMod,
+    ((hornerMod p z l : ℕ) : ZMod p) = evalCoeffList (z : ZMod p) (l.map Nat.cast) := by
+    rw [List.foldr_cons, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_mul, ih, List.map_cons,
+theorem subMod_lt [NeZero p] (a b : ℕ) : subMod p a b < p := Nat.mod_lt _ (NeZero.pos p)
+    connectiveMod p o a b < p := by
+theorem operatorMod_lt [NeZero p] (o : ArithQBF.Operator) (t a b : ℕ) :
+    operatorMod p o t a b < p := by
+theorem hornerMod_lt [NeZero p] (z : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : hornerMod p z l < p := by
+  | cons a l => exact Nat.mod_lt _ (NeZero.pos p)

+    a % p = c.val % p ↔ (a : ZMod p) = c := by
+/-- The value of the variable `w` at a point given as a list of pairs of a variable and its value:
+the value of the first pair for `w`, or `0`. -/

+/-- The point `r` on the variables of `xs`, as a list of pairs of a variable and its value. -/

+  xs.map fun x => (x, if x = v then z % p else lookupPt pt x % p)

+/-- The rows of the honest encoding of `l` are the bits of its elements. -/

+      if h : i < l.length then BitString.binaryWord (width p) l[i]
+    have ih := ih (fun b hb => hl b (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hb))
+/-- **Decoding inverts the honest encoding** of at most `D + 1` residues, padded with zeros. -/
+theorem decodeReply_encodeReply {D : ℕ} {l : List ℕ} (hl : ∀ a ∈ l, a < p)

+  have hlength : (encodeReply p l).length ≤ replyLimit p D := by
+    have : (encodeReply p l).length = l.length * width p := by
+      rw [List.map_congr_left fun a ha => BitString.length_binaryWord (lt_two_pow_width (hl a ha)),

+/-- At most `N / p + 1` numbers below `N` have a given residue modulo `p`. -/
+    (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin N => n = i.val % p).card ≤ N / p + 1 := by
+  calc (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin N => n = i.val % p).card
+        refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun i => i.val / p) (fun i _ => ?_)
+        · simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hi hj
+          have hij : i.val / p = j.val / p := hij

+  calc ((Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin (dyadicSize p) => n = i.val % p).card : ℝ≥0∞) * p

+# Closedness of a quantified Boolean formula in polynomial time
+The free variables of a formula are computed by one scan of its tokens from right to left, with a
+stack holding the free variables of the subformulas read so far

+connective joins the two lists on top of the stack, and a quantifier removes its variable from the

+empty (`Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.isClosed_tokens`), and closedness is decided in polynomial time
+* `Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.freeVarList`: the free variables of a formula, with multiplicity.
+* `Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.mem_freeVarList`: the list has the free variables as elements.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Primality of unary naturals by trial division
+A natural `p` is prime exactly when `2 ≤ p` and no `m` with `2 ≤ m < p` divides it
+`p` takes time polynomial in `p`, hence in the length of its unary encoding
+    (decide (2 ≤ p) && (List.range p).all fun m => decide (m < 2) || decide (p % m ≠ 0)) := by
+  refine and_congr_right fun _ => ⟨fun h m hm => ?_, fun h m h2 hm => ?_⟩
+/-- Primality of a unary natural, by trial division. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ => decide p.Prime) encUnary encBool := by

+# `TQBF` in alternating prenex conjunctive normal form
+A quantified Boolean formula is in **alternating prenex conjunctive normal form** when it is
+`∃ x₁, ∀ y₁, ⋯, ∃ xₙ, ∀ yₙ, ψ` for a formula `ψ` in conjunctive normal form
+(`Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.rounds`, `Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.ofCNF`). `TQBFCNF` is the set of pairs of a list
+of rounds `(xᵢ, yᵢ)` and a formula `ψ` whose formula is a true closed formula
+The game played on such a formula is Sipser's FORMULA-GAME [Sipser, Theorem 8.11][Sipser2013],
+the starting point of the textbook `PSPACE`-hardness proofs of games such as Generalized Geography
+because writing the formula is polynomial-time, and it is `PSPACE`-hard because the formulas of
+games (`Cslib.Complexity.TQBF.gameFormula`), which every problem in `PSPACE` reduces to
+(`Cslib.Complexity.exists_isGameVerifier_of_mem_PSPACE`), are already almost in this form: rounds
+over the moves, then existential quantifiers over the variables of a Cook–Levin tableau and the
+conjunction of the tableau with equivalences linking its certificate variables to the moves. Each
+equivalence `a ↔ b` is written as the two clauses `¬a ∨ b` and `a ∨ ¬b`
+(`Cslib.Complexity.TQBF.certLinkCNF`), and each existential quantifier `∃ v` becomes the round
+`∃ v, ∀ d` over a fixed variable `d` that occurs nowhere else (`Cslib.Complexity.TQBF.dummyVar`),

+# Independent Set, Clique and Vertex Cover are NP-hard to approximate
+The values of a graph (`Cslib.Complexity.Graph`, read on its declared vertices) are its

+* `GapIndependentSet s`: is `indepNum G ≥ k`, or `indepNum G ≤ s * k`?

+oracle and the answers on words that are not codes are arbitrary.

+problem `{(b, k) | k ≤ f b}` is in `PP`, by the characterisation through `GapP`
+for bit `i` of `f b`, sent as the code `(b, i)`, is answered by a binary search

+the code of `b` and the position `i` from the request without decoding `b`, and runs for
+`r (n) + 1` rounds, for the length `n` of the request and `f b ≤ 2 ^ r (|b|)`.

+# Polynomial time relative to an oracle in polynomial time
+An oracle language decided in polynomial time adds nothing to polynomial time: `P^A = P` and
+`NP^A = NP` for `A ∈ P` [Arora and Barak, Section 3.4][AroraBarak09].
+A computation in polynomial time relative to `A` is the clocked run, with every coin fixed to
+That run iterates one instruction on finite storage (`Turing.MultiTapePTM.answerStep`), which
+answers a query with the decider of `A` on the pending request. Against an oracle computed in
+(`Turing.MultiTapePTM.computableTidilyInPolyTime_answerStep`), the storage grows by a bounded amount
+per instruction, and the clock is polynomial, so the run is polynomial-time
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.computableTidilyInPolyTime_run`: a clocked run against a polynomial-time
+  relative to an oracle in `P` is polynomial time.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+  [Fintype Operation] (machine : MultiTapePTM k Bool Control Operation)
+/-- **An instruction against a polynomial-time oracle is polynomial-time.** Against an oracle
+answering `[g w]` to a request `w`, with `g` polynomial-time, an instruction is polynomial-time in
+the encoded configuration: it either installs `g` of the pending request or is local. -/
+  have h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun cfg => if (machine.pendingQuery cfg).isSome then
+      machine.receiveBit (cfg, g (machine.pendingRequest cfg)) else machine.localStep cfg)
+  exact h.of_enc_eq fun cfg => by rw [answerStep_bit]
+/-- **A clocked run against a polynomial-time oracle is polynomial-time.** Against the oracle
+answering `[g w]` to a request `w`, where `g` is polynomial-time, the run with every coin fixed to
+`false` under the clock `c * (n + 1) ^ d` is polynomial-time in the encoded input. -/
+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_run [Finite Operation] {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {g : List Bool → Bool} (hg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime g encBits encBool) (c d : ℕ) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => OracleComp.interpret (m := Id) (fun q => [g q.2])
+        (c * ((input a).length + 1) ^ d) (input a))) input encBits := by
+  obtain ⟨cf, hcf⟩ := length_encFiniteConfig_le (k := k) (State := Control) (Oracle := Operation)
+  have hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => c * ((input a).length + 1) ^ d) input
+      (fun a => FiniteConfig.init (k := k) (Oracle := Operation) machine.initial (input a))
+  have hspace (a : α) (i : ℕ) : FiniteConfig.SpaceBound (input a).length i 1
+      (fun a => cf * ((input a).length + c * ((input a).length + 1) ^ d + 1 + 1)) :=
+      (bound := fun L => cf * (L + c * (L + 1) ^ d + 1 + 1)) (by fun_prop)) fun _ => le_rfl
+    (machine.computableTidilyInPolyTime_answerStep hg) hbound fun a i hi =>
+      (fun cfg : FiniteConfig k Bool Control Operation => cfg.tapes.output) encFiniteConfig
+  exact (hout.comp hit).of_enc_eq fun a => by rw [interpret_run_pure_false]; rfl
+variable {α β : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set (List Bool)}
+/-- **Polynomial time relative to an oracle in `P` is polynomial time.** Relative to an oracle
+language decided in polynomial time, a function computable in polynomial time relative to it is
+computable in polynomial time: every query is answered by running the decider. -/
+    {output : β ↪ List Bool} (hA : A ∈ P encBits)
+  have hg' : g = fun w => decide (w ∈ A) := funext fun w =>
+  obtain ⟨k, m, machine, c, d, hrun⟩ := hcert.exists_fin_run_pure_false
+  refine (machine.computableTidilyInPolyTime_run (input := enc) hg c d).of_enc_eq fun a => ?_
+  rw [← hprogram a, ← hrun a (languageOracle A)]
+/-- **`P` relative to an oracle in `P` is `P`.** -/
+theorem PWithOracle_eq_P (hA : A ∈ P encBits) (enc : α ↪ List Bool) :
+  Set.Subset.antisymm (fun _ ⟨f, hf, hL⟩ => ⟨f, hf.computableTidilyInPolyTime hA, hL⟩)
+/-- **`NP` relative to an oracle in `P` is `NP`.** -/
+theorem NPWithOracle_eq_NP (hA : A ∈ P encBits) (enc : α ↪ List Bool) :
+  Set.Subset.antisymm (fun _ ⟨p, V, hV, hL⟩ => ⟨p, V, hV.computableTidilyInPolyTime hA, hL⟩)

+`FewP ⊆ SPP` [Köbler, Schöning, Toda and Torán][KoeblerSchoeningTodaToran1992], in the gap
+formulation of [Fenner, Fortnow and Kurtz][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]. For a problem in `FewP`, let
+`T` be the set of certificates of length `len` accepted on an instance, of size `m ≤ q`. The subsets
+`U ⊆ T` cancel in pairs by parity: `∑ U ⊆ T, (-1) ^ |U| = (1 - 1) ^ m` is `1` when `m = 0` and `0`
+otherwise. Every subset has at most `q` elements, so it is listed, in increasing order, in `q`
+slots of `len + 1` bits, each a flag followed by a certificate. The numbers `E` and `O` of such
+listings of the subsets of even and of odd size are counted by polynomial-time verifiers, so they
+are in `#P`, and `1 + O - E` is a `GapP` function equal to `1` on members and `0` on the other
+A word of `q` slots is read from the left (`Cslib.Complexity.SortedSubsets.step`). A flagged slot
+lists its certificate, which must be accepted, come before every empty slot and exceed the last
+certificate listed in binary value; an empty slot must hold only bits `false`. The well-formed
+words are exactly the increasing listings of the subsets of `T` with at most `q` elements. The
+proof does not construct this bijection; it shows by induction on the number of slots that the
+well-formed words, counted with the sign of the parity of their number of certificates, sum to
+the sign of the starting state when no accepted certificate is above the last one listed, and to
+`0` otherwise (`Cslib.Complexity.SortedSubsets.signedSum_eq`): a first empty slot leaves one
+well-formed completion, and a first certificate `c` contributes, by induction, the opposite sign
+exactly when `c` is the largest certificate above the last one listed.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SortedSubsets.step`: read one slot of a listing.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SortedSubsets.verifier`: the verifier counting the listings of a given parity.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SortedSubsets.signedSum_eq`: the signed count of the listings.
+* [J. Köbler, U. Schöning, S. Toda, J. Torán, *Turing machines with few accepting computations
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]
+/-- The state of a scan of slots: whether the slots read so far are well formed, the parity of the
+number of certificates listed, whether an empty slot has been read, whether a certificate has been
+abbrev State := Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool × List Bool
+/-- The state before any slot is read. -/
+/-- Read one slot, a flag bit followed by a certificate. A flagged slot lists its certificate, which
+must be accepted by `acc`, come before every empty slot, and exceed the last certificate listed in
+binary value; an empty slot must hold only bits `false`. -/
+def step (acc : List Bool → Bool) (s : State) (slot : List Bool) : State :=
+  else (s.1 && !slot.tail.any (fun b => b), s.2.1, true, s.2.2.2.1, s.2.2.2.2)
+/-- A final state is accepted for the parity `b` when it is well formed and lists a number of
+def accepts (b : Bool) (s : State) : Bool := s.1 && s.2.1 == b
+/-- The sign of a final state: `0` if malformed, otherwise `1` or `-1` by the parity of the number
+def sign (s : State) : ℤ := if s.1 then (if s.2.1 then -1 else 1) else 0
+/-- The sign of a state is its acceptance for the even parity minus its acceptance for the odd
+    (if accepts false s = true then 1 else 0) - (if accepts true s = true then 1 else 0) := by
+  cases ok <;> cases par <;> simp [accepts, sign]
+/-- The certificates of length `len` accepted by `acc` that may be listed after the state `s`: above
+def above (acc : List Bool → Bool) (len : ℕ) (s : State) : Finset (Fin len → Bool) :=
+  univ.filter fun x => acc (List.ofFn x) = true ∧
+/-- The words of `k` slots of `len + 1` bits read from the state `s`, counted with the sign of the
+def signedSum (acc : List Bool → Bool) (len k : ℕ) (s : State) : ℤ :=
+  ∑ w : Fin (k * (len + 1)) → Bool, sign ((listRows k (len + 1) (List.ofFn w)).foldl (step acc) s)
+/-- Sums over the words of equal lengths agree. -/
+private theorem sum_ofFn_congr {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (F : List Bool → M) {n n' : ℕ}
+    (h : n = n') : ∑ w : Fin n → Bool, F (List.ofFn w) = ∑ w : Fin n' → Bool, F (List.ofFn w) := by
+/-- The signed count of `k + 1` slots, by the first slot. -/
+    signedSum acc len (k + 1) s = ∑ c : Fin len → Bool,
+      (signedSum acc len k (step acc s (false :: List.ofFn c)) +
+        signedSum acc len k (step acc s (true :: List.ofFn c))) := by
+  rw [sum_ofFn_congr (fun l => sign ((listRows (k + 1) (len + 1) l).foldl (step acc) s))
+  simp only [show ∀ (u : Fin (len + 1) → Bool) (v : Fin (k * (len + 1)) → Bool),
+    List.ofFn (Fin.appendEquiv (len + 1) (k * (len + 1)) (u, v)) = List.ofFn u ++ List.ofFn v from
+      fun u v => List.ofFn_fin_append u v]
+  congr 1 <;> refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ => ?_ <;>
+/-- In a nonempty finite set of words of length `len`, exactly one has the largest binary value. -/
+private theorem card_filter_isGreatest {A : Finset (Fin len → Bool)} (hA : A.Nonempty) :
+    (A.filter fun c => ∀ x ∈ A, binaryValue (List.ofFn x) ≤ binaryValue (List.ofFn c)).card =
+  obtain ⟨c, hc, hmax⟩ := A.exists_max_image (fun x => binaryValue (List.ofFn x)) hA
+    (le_antisymm (hmax d hd) (hdmax c hc))), fun h => h ▸ ⟨hc, hmax⟩⟩
+/-- Listing `c` leaves no accepted certificate above it exactly when `c` is the largest accepted
+private theorem above_eq_empty_iff {s : State} {c : Fin len → Bool} (hc : c ∈ above acc len s)
+    (o p e : Bool) : above acc len (o, p, e, true, List.ofFn c) = ∅ ↔
+      ∀ x ∈ above acc len s, binaryValue (List.ofFn x) ≤ binaryValue (List.ofFn c) := by
+  simp only [above, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, Bool.true_eq_false, false_or] at hc ⊢
+  simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, not_and, not_lt]
+  refine ⟨fun h x hx => h x hx.1, fun h x hx => ?_⟩
+  exact absurd (h x ⟨hx, hc.2.imp_right fun hp => hp.trans hlt⟩) (not_le.2 hlt)
+/-- A flagged slot read from a well-formed state before any empty slot. -/
+private theorem step_true_cons (par started : Bool) (prev : List Bool) (c : Fin len → Bool) :
+    step acc (true, par, false, started, prev) (true :: List.ofFn c) =
+/-- A flagged slot holding `c` keeps the state `(true, par, false, started, prev)` well formed
+exactly when `c` may be listed after it. -/
+private theorem cond_eq_true_iff {par started : Bool} {prev : List Bool} {c : Fin len → Bool} :
+      true ↔ c ∈ above acc len (true, par, false, started, prev) := by
+/-- **The signed count of the listings.** From a well-formed state, the words of `k` slots,
+counted with the sign of the parity of the certificates listed, sum to the sign of the state
+when an empty slot has been read or no accepted certificate is above the last one listed, and to
+`0` otherwise, provided at most `k` accepted certificates are above it. -/
+    (hk : s.1 = true → s.2.2.1 = false → (above acc len s).card ≤ k) :
+    signedSum acc len k s = if s.2.2.1 = false ∧ (above acc len s).Nonempty then 0 else sign s := by
+    rw [sum_ofFn_congr (fun l => sign ((listRows 0 (len + 1) l).foldl (step acc) s))
+    simp only [listRows, List.range_zero, List.map_nil, List.foldl_nil, Finset.univ_unique,
+    obtain ⟨ok, par, ended, started, prev⟩ := s
+      have hfail (slot : List Bool) : (step acc (false, par, ended, started, prev) slot).1 =
+      rw [ih _ (fun h => absurd h (by rw [hfail]; decide)),
+        ih _ (fun h => absurd h (by rw [hfail]; decide))]
+    have hsum₀ : ∑ c : Fin len → Bool, signedSum acc len k
+        (step acc (true, par, ended, started, prev) (false :: List.ofFn c)) =
+      have hc (c : Fin len → Bool) : signedSum acc len k
+          (step acc (true, par, ended, started, prev) (false :: List.ofFn c)) =
+            if (!(List.ofFn c).any (fun b => b)) = true then (if par then -1 else 1) else 0 := by
+        have hstep : step acc (true, par, ended, started, prev) (false :: List.ofFn c) =
+            (!(List.ofFn c).any (fun b => b), par, true, started, prev) := by
+        rw [hstep, ih _ (fun _ h => by simp at h)]
+      set A := above acc len (true, par, false, started, prev) with hA
+      have hc (c : Fin len → Bool) : signedSum acc len k
+          (step acc (true, par, false, started, prev) (true :: List.ofFn c)) =
+            if c ∈ A ∧ ∀ x ∈ A, binaryValue (List.ofFn x) ≤ binaryValue (List.ofFn c) then
+        · have hsub : above acc len (true, !par, false, true, List.ofFn c) ⊆ A.erase c := by
+            simp only [hA, above, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, Bool.true_eq_false,
+            simp only [hA, above, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and]
+          have hle : (above acc len (true, !par, false, true, List.ofFn c)).card ≤ k := by
+          rw [(cond_eq_true_iff (par := par)).2 hmem, ih (true, !par, false, true, List.ofFn c)
+          have hiff := above_eq_empty_iff hmem true (!par) false
+          by_cases hmax : ∀ x ∈ A, binaryValue (List.ofFn x) ≤ binaryValue (List.ofFn c)
+          · have hempty : ¬ (above acc len (true, !par, false, true, List.ofFn c)).Nonempty :=
+          · have hne : (above acc len (true, !par, false, true, List.ofFn c)).Nonempty :=
+            Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun h => hmem ((cond_eq_true_iff (par := par)).1 h)
+          rw [hcond, ih _ (fun h => by simp at h)]
+        show (univ.filter fun c => c ∈ A ∧ ∀ x ∈ A,
+            A.filter fun c => ∀ x ∈ A, binaryValue (List.ofFn x) ≤ binaryValue (List.ofFn c) by
+    · -- after an empty slot only the words of `false`s are well formed
+      have hfail (c : Fin len → Bool) : signedSum acc len k
+          (step acc (true, par, true, started, prev) (true :: List.ofFn c)) = 0 := by
+        have hstep : (step acc (true, par, true, started, prev) (true :: List.ofFn c)).1 =
+        rw [ih _ (fun h => by rw [hstep] at h; exact absurd h (by simp))]
+/-- The verifier counting the listings of parity `b`: on an instance `a`, the certificate, read as
+`q` slots of `len + 1` bits, where `len = p (enc a).length`, is a well-formed increasing listing of
+certificates of length `len` accepted by `V` with a number of certificates of parity `b`. -/
+def verifier (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p q : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (b : Bool)
+/-- The encoding of the states of a scan. -/
+  encPair encBool (encPair encBool (encPair encBool (encPair encBool encBits)))

+private theorem length_encState_step (acc : List Bool → Bool) (s : State) (slot : List Bool) :
+    (encState (step acc s slot)).length ≤ (encState s).length + slot.length := by
+  split <;> simp only [length_encPair, encBool_apply, List.length_singleton, encBits_apply,
+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_verifier {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool) (p q : Polynomial ℕ)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (verifier enc p q V b) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+  have hP : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => p.eval (enc x.1).length + 1)
+  have hQ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => q.eval (enc x.1).length)
+      (fun x : (α × State) × List Bool => decide (binaryValue x.1.2.2.2.2.2 < binaryValue x.2.tail))
+      (fun x : (α × State) × List Bool => step (fun c => V (x.1.1, c)) x.1.2 x.2)
+    (par := fun x : α × List Bool => x.1) (encP := enc)
+    (list := fun x => listRows (q.eval (enc x.1).length) (p.eval (enc x.1).length + 1) x.2)
+    (init := fun _ => init) (step := fun a s slot => step (fun c => V (a, c)) s slot)
+      have := length_encState_step (fun c => V (x.1, c)) s slot
+  have hacc : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (accepts b) encState encBool := by
+[Fenner, Fortnow and Kurtz][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]. For a problem in `FewP` whose instances have
+at most `q` accepted certificates, the numbers `E` and `O` of increasing listings, in `q` slots, of
+sets of accepted certificates of even and of odd size are in `#P`, and `1 + O - E`, in `GapP`, is
+`1` on members and `0` on the other instances. -/
+theorem FewP_subset_SPP : FewP enc ⊆ SPP enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨f, ⟨p, V, hV, hf⟩, q, hq, hA⟩
+  set E : α → ℕ := fun a =>
+    acceptCount (verifier enc p q V false) a ((q * (p + 1)).eval (enc a).length) with hE_def

+    acceptCount (verifier enc p q V true) a ((q * (p + 1)).eval (enc a).length) with hO_def

+    ⟨q * (p + 1), _, computableTidilyInPolyTime_verifier hV p q true, fun _ => rfl⟩
+  have hdiff (a : α) : (E a : ℤ) - O a = if 0 < f a then 0 else 1 := by
+    have hsum : (E a : ℤ) - O a =
+        signedSum (fun c => V (a, c)) (p.eval (enc a).length) (q.eval (enc a).length) init := by

+# coNP ⊆ AM collapses the polynomial hierarchy
+The theorem of Boppana, Håstad and Zachos [BoppanaHastadZachos1987],
+[Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09]: if `coNP ⊆ AM`, for problems with any encoding of
+their instances, then `Σ₂ = Π₂ = AM` and the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level,
+`PH = Σ₂`. Consequently, if graph isomorphism is `NP`-complete then `PH = Σ₂`, since graph
+* **`AM` is closed under existential quantification** over polynomially long words
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.mem_AM_of_exists`, the collapse `MAM = AM` of [Babai][Babai1985]): reduce the
+  error of the Arthur–Merlin verifier for the pairs `(a, w)` below `2 ^ (-|w| - 2)` and let Merlin
+  send `w` with his reply; by the union bound over the words `w`, Arthur's coins rarely admit an
+  accepted answer for any `w` when no `w` works.
+* A problem in `Σ₂` is the projection of a problem in `Π₁ = coNP` on pairs `(a, w₁)`, so
+  `AM ⊆ Π₂` (`Cslib.Complexity.AM_subset_PiP_two`), `Σ₂ ⊆ Π₂`, hence `Π₂ ⊆ Σ₂` by complements and
+* `Cslib.Complexity.mem_AM_of_exists`: `AM` is closed under polynomially bounded existential
+* [R. B. Boppana, J. Håstad, S. Zachos, *Does co-NP have short interactive

+which some word `w` of length `p(n)`, `n` the length of the encoded instance, makes `(a, w)` a

+    {a | ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ (a, w) ∈ B} ∈ AM enc := by
+  obtain ⟨pB, qB, VB, hVB, hB'⟩ := mem_AM_iff_forall_errorExponent.mp hB (Polynomial.X + 2)
+  -- the length of the encoded pair of an instance and a word of length `p(n)`
+  set L : Polynomial ℕ := 2 * Polynomial.X + 1 + p with hLdef
+  have hL (a : α) (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval (enc a).length) :
+      (encPair enc encBits (a, w)).length = L.eval (enc a).length := by
+    simp only [length_encPair, encBits_apply, hw, hLdef, Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_mul,
+  have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (encPair enc encBits a).length)

+  have hp : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => p.eval (enc x.1).length)
+  refine ⟨pB.comp L, p + qB.comp L, fun x => VB ((x.1,
+  -- the verifier reads the word and runs the verifier of the pairs
+      VB ((a, ((List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y).drop ((pB.comp L).eval (enc a).length)).take
+    rw [List.drop_left' List.length_ofFn, List.take_left' List.length_ofFn, ofFn_eq_append y,
+  -- the error bounds of the pairs, at the length of the encoded instance
+            VB ((a, List.ofFn w), List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y) = false} ≤
+            VB ((a, List.ofFn w), List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y) = true} ≤
+        L.eval (enc a).length + 2 by simp] at h

+              VB ((a, List.ofFn w), List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y) = true} := by
+      exact mem_biUnion.2 ⟨_, mem_univ _, mem_filter.2 ⟨mem_univ _, _, by simpa using hy⟩⟩
+    have hpos : 0 < 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length := by positivity

+          have h4 : 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length * 4 ≤ 2 ^ (L.eval (enc a).length + 2) := by
+              VB ((a, List.ofFn w), List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y) = true} := mul_sum _ _ _
+          sum_le_sum fun w _ => (herr w).2 fun hw => ha ⟨_, List.length_ofFn, hw⟩
+/-- **`coNP ⊆ AM` gives `Σ₂ ⊆ AM`**: a problem in `Σ₂` is the projection of the `Π₁` problem of
+pairs `(a, w₁)` that the universal quantifier accepts, which is in `coNP`, hence in `AM`. -/

+  rintro A ⟨ps, V, hlen, hV, hA⟩

+  have hle (y : α × List Bool) : (enc y.1).length ≤ (encPair enc encBits y).length := by
+  have hB : B ∈ PiP 1 (encPair enc encBits) := by
+    refine ⟨ps, fun z => V (z.1.1, z.1.2 ++ truncateBlocks ps (enc z.1.1).length
+      (encPair enc encBits z.1).length z.2), hlen', ?_, fun y => ?_⟩
+        (P := fun w => V (y.1, y.2 ++ w) = true)).symm
+  have hA' : A = {a | ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = p₁.eval (enc a).length ∧ (a, w) ∈ B} := by
+/-- If `coNP ⊆ AM` for every encoding, then `Π₂ ⊆ Σ₂`: the complement of a `Π₂` problem is in
+    (h : ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), coNP encB ⊆ AM encB) {β : Type}
+    (encB : β ↪ List Bool) : PiP 2 encB ⊆ SigmaP 2 encB := fun A hA => by
+[Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09]: if `coNP ⊆ AM` for problems with any encoding of
+their instances, then the polynomial hierarchy collapses to `Σ₂`. -/

+/-- If `coNP ⊆ AM` for every encoding, then `Σ₂ = AM`. -/
+    (h : ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), coNP encB ⊆ AM encB) : SigmaP 2 enc = AM enc :=
