lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The public-coin protocol of Goldwasser and Sipser for graph non-isomorphism
+[GoldwasserSipser1986], [Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09]. Let the two graphs have
+`n` distinct vertices each, with adjacency matrices `A₀` and `A₁` on positions. Permutations `τ`
+`(M, σ)` of a relabelling `M` of `A₀` or `A₁` and an automorphism `σ` of `M` form a set of
+`2 n!` elements when the graphs are not isomorphic and `n!` when they are
+(`Cslib.Complexity.GraphNonIsomorphism.PublicCoin.card_pairs`), and the two orbits coincide or are
+Merlin can certify membership of a pair, by naming the graph and a relabelling of it. Pairs are
+written as strings of `2 L² + 1` bits, `L` the length of the encoded instance
+(`Cslib.Complexity.GraphNonIsomorphism.PublicCoin.code`): the matrix `M`, the matrix of `σ`, and
+`false` bits. When the graphs have different numbers of vertices, every string is accepted. The
+set lower bound protocol with threshold `2 n!` (`Cslib.Complexity.mem_AM_of_card_certifiedSet`)
+  `Cslib.Complexity.GraphNonIsomorphism.PublicCoin.test`: strings of pairs and their certificates.
+* [S. Goldwasser, M. Sipser, *Private coins versus public coins in interactive proof
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- Relabel the rows and columns of a matrix by a permutation `τ`: entry `(τ i, τ j)` of the
+def relabelMatrix (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) : Fin n → Fin n → Bool :=
+  fun i j => M (τ.symm i) (τ.symm j)
+theorem relabelMatrix_mul (σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
+    relabelMatrix (σ * τ) M = relabelMatrix σ (relabelMatrix τ M) := by
+theorem relabelMatrix_one (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) : relabelMatrix 1 M = M := rfl
+/-- `relabelMatrix τ A = M` says that `τ` carries `A` to `M`. -/
+theorem relabelMatrix_eq_iff {τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)} {A M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool} :
+    relabelMatrix τ A = M ↔ ∀ i j, M (τ i) (τ j) = A i j := by
+def orbit (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) : Finset (Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :=
+  univ.image fun τ => relabelMatrix τ A
+theorem mem_orbit {A M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool} : M ∈ orbit A ↔ ∃ τ, relabelMatrix τ A = M := by
+theorem mem_orbit_self (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) : A ∈ orbit A :=
+theorem mem_orbit_trans {A B M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool} (hB : B ∈ orbit A) (hM : M ∈ orbit B) :
+  exact mem_orbit.2 ⟨σ * τ, relabelMatrix_mul σ τ A⟩
+theorem mem_orbit_symm {A B : Fin n → Fin n → Bool} (hB : B ∈ orbit A) : A ∈ orbit B := by
+/-- The pairs of a relabelling of `A` and an automorphism of it. -/
+def pairs (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
+    Finset ((Fin n → Fin n → Bool) × Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :=
+  univ.filter fun p => p.1 ∈ orbit A ∧ relabelMatrix p.2 p.1 = p.1
+/-- A relabelling `M` of `A` has as many automorphisms as there are permutations carrying `A` to
+theorem card_filter_relabelMatrix_eq {A M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool} (hM : M ∈ orbit A) :
+    #{σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | relabelMatrix σ M = M} =
+      #{τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | relabelMatrix τ A = M} := by
+  simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, Equiv.coe_mulRight, relabelMatrix_mul]
+/-- **Orbit–stabilizer count**: the pairs of a relabelling of `A` and an automorphism of it are
+theorem card_pairs (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) : #(pairs A) = n.factorial := by
+  have hsum : #(pairs A) = ∑ M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool,
+      #{τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | relabelMatrix τ A = M} := by
+    · simp only [hM, true_and, ← card_filter_relabelMatrix_eq hM, card_filter]
+      exact fun τ _ h => hM (mem_orbit.2 ⟨τ, h⟩)
+/-- The pairs of the two matrices are `n!` many if one is a relabelling of the other, and `2 n!`
+theorem card_pairs_union (A₀ A₁ : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
+    #(pairs A₀ ∪ pairs A₁) = if A₁ ∈ orbit A₀ then n.factorial else 2 * n.factorial := by
+  · have heq : pairs A₁ = pairs A₀ := by
+        ⟨fun hp => mem_orbit_trans h hp, fun hp => mem_orbit_trans (mem_orbit_symm h) hp⟩
+    refine disjoint_left.2 fun p hp₀ hp₁ => h ?_
+    simp only [pairs, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at hp₀ hp₁
+private theorem pos_of_fin (i : Fin n) : 0 < n := Nat.zero_lt_of_lt i.2
+private theorem index_lt (i j : Fin n) : (i : ℕ) * n + j < n * n := by
+private theorem index_div (i j : Fin n) : ((i : ℕ) * n + j) / n = i := by
+  rw [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_mul_div_right _ _ (pos_of_fin i), Nat.div_eq_of_lt j.2, zero_add]
+private theorem index_mod (i j : Fin n) : ((i : ℕ) * n + j) % n = j := by
+/-- The entry of a matrix at natural positions, `false` outside. -/
+def entry (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (i j : ℕ) : Bool :=
+  if h : i < n ∧ j < n then M ⟨i, h.1⟩ ⟨j, h.2⟩ else false
+/-- The value of a permutation at a natural position, `0` outside. -/
+  if h : i < n then σ ⟨i, h⟩ else 0
+@[simp] theorem entry_fin (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (i j : Fin n) :
+    entry M i j = M i j := by
+@[simp] theorem value_fin (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : value σ i = σ i := by
+/-- Bit `p` of the code of a pair `(M, σ)`: the entries of `M`, then the entries of the matrix of
+def codeBit (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (p : ℕ) : Bool :=
+  if p < n * n then entry M (p / n) (p % n)
+  else if p < 2 * (n * n) then decide (value σ ((p - n * n) / n) = (p - n * n) % n)
+/-- The code of a pair `(M, σ)` of a matrix and a permutation, in `E` bits. -/
+def code (E : ℕ) (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : BitString E :=
+  fun p => codeBit M σ p
+/-- Bit `q` of a certificate naming the graph `b` and a permutation `τ`. -/
+def certBit (b : Bool) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (q : ℕ) : Bool :=
+  else if q - 1 < n * n then decide (value τ ((q - 1) / n) = (q - 1) % n)
+/-- A certificate naming the graph `b` and a permutation `τ`, in `C` bits. -/
+def cert (C : ℕ) (b : Bool) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : BitString C :=
+  fun q => certBit b τ q
+private theorem getD_ofFn {E : ℕ} (x : BitString E) {p : ℕ} (hp : p < E) :
+    (List.ofFn x).getD p false = x ⟨p, hp⟩ := by
+/-- The matrix read from the first `n * n` bits of a word. -/
+def decodeMatrix (n : ℕ) (u : List Bool) : Fin n → Fin n → Bool :=
+  fun i j => u.getD (i * n + j) false
+/-- The map read from the matrix starting after `k` bits of a word: row `i` selects its first set
+def decodeMap (n k : ℕ) (u : List Bool) (i : Fin n) : Fin n :=
+theorem decodeMatrix_code {E : ℕ} (hE : n * n ≤ E) (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
+    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : decodeMatrix n (List.ofFn (code E M σ)) = M := by
+  simp only [code, codeBit, index_lt i j, ↓reduceIte, index_div, index_mod, entry_fin]
+theorem decodeMap_code {E : ℕ} (hE : 2 * (n * n) ≤ E) (M : Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
+    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : decodeMap n (n * n) (List.ofFn (code E M σ)) = σ := by
+  refine Fin.ext (GraphIsomorphism.image_eq (σ i).2 fun j hj => ?_)
+  have hlt : (i : ℕ) * n + j < n * n := index_lt i ⟨j, hj⟩

+/-- **The certified pairs**: the elements of `E` bits with a certificate of `C` bits that passes

+theorem card_filter_check {E C : ℕ} (hE : 2 * (n * n) + 1 ≤ E) (hC : n * n + 1 ≤ C)

+  · -- coding a pair and decoding it gives it back
+/-- Isomorphic graphs have equally many distinct vertices. -/
+/-- Graphs with equally many distinct vertices are isomorphic exactly when the adjacency matrix of
+the second, on positions, is a relabelling of that of the first. -/
+      (fun i j : Fin G₀.distinctVertices.length => G₁.adjIndex i j) ∈
+        orbit fun i j : Fin G₀.distinctVertices.length => G₀.adjIndex i j := by
+    exact ⟨σ.trans (finCongr h), relabelMatrix_eq_iff.2 fun i j => hσ i j⟩
+    exact ⟨τ.trans (finCongr h.symm), fun i j => relabelMatrix_eq_iff.1 hτ i j⟩
+[Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09]: the set lower bound protocol applied to the pairs

+non-isomorphic graphs with `n` distinct vertices each and `n!` many for isomorphic graphs. -/
+theorem mem_AM : GraphNonIsomorphism ∈ AM (encPair encGraph encGraph) := by
+  set N : Polynomial ℕ := 2 * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1 with hN

+  have hE (L : ℕ) : N.eval L = 2 * L ^ 2 + 1 := by simp [hN]
+  have hC (L : ℕ) : c.eval L = L ^ 2 + 1 := by simp [hc]

+  have hpairs (G₀ G₁ : Graph) (h : G₁.distinctVertices.length = G₀.distinctVertices.length) :
+      #(certifiedSet (encPair encGraph encGraph) N c (test N) (G₀, G₁)) =
+        #((pairs fun i j : Fin G₀.distinctVertices.length => G₀.adjIndex i j) ∪
+          pairs fun i j : Fin G₀.distinctVertices.length => G₁.adjIndex i j) := by
+    have hset : certifiedSet (encPair encGraph encGraph) N c (test N) (G₀, G₁) =
+        univ.filter fun x : BitString (N.eval (encPair encGraph encGraph (G₀, G₁)).length) =>
+              (fun b i j => if b then G₁.adjIndex i j else G₀.adjIndex i j)
+      refine filter_congr fun x _ => exists_congr fun z => ?_
+      simp only [test, h, ne_eq, not_true_eq_false, decide_false, Bool.false_or,
+    rw [hset, card_filter_check (by rw [hE]; omega) (by rw [hC]; omega)]
+  refine mem_AM_of_card_certifiedSet (N := N) (c := c) (R := test N)
+    (computableTidilyInPolyTime_test N) hK (fun a => by positivity) (fun a ha => ?_)

+    · -- with different numbers of vertices, every string is certified
+      have hset : certifiedSet (encPair encGraph encGraph) N c (test N) (G₀, G₁) = univ := by
+        simp only [test, h, ne_eq, not_false_eq_true, decide_true, Bool.true_or]
+    have hiso : (G₀, G₁) ∈ GraphIsomorphism := not_not.1 ha

+# The set lower bound protocol and `SBP ⊆ AM`
+The set lower bound protocol of Goldwasser and Sipser [GoldwasserSipser1986]
+[Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09] lets Merlin convince Arthur that a set `S` with
+membership certificates is large. Write `n` for the length of the encoded instance `a`, and let
+`S a` be the strings `x` of `N(n)` bits with a certificate `z` of `c(n)` bits accepted by a
+polynomial-time test, `R (a, x ++ z) = true` (`Cslib.Complexity.certifiedSet`). If a
+polynomial-time threshold `K a > 0`, computed in binary, satisfies `K a ≤ #(S a)` on members and
+`2 #(S a) ≤ K a` on non-members, then the problem is in `AM`
+* **Gap amplification.** Five copies of `S a` have at least `K a ^ 5` elements on members and at
+* **Normalisation.** With `ℓ = ⌊log₂ (K a ^ 5)⌋` and a polynomial `T(n) ≥ ℓ + 4`, appending
+  `T(n)` bits whose first `ℓ` are `false` multiplies the size by `2 ^ (T(n) - ℓ)`
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.SetLowerBound.card_amplifiedSet`): at least `2 ^ T(n)` elements on members
+  and fewer than `2 ^ T(n) / 16` on non-members.
+* **Hashing.** Arthur sends a random affine hash `h` to `m(n) = T(n) - 2` bits
+  (`Cslib.BitString.LinearHash.affineHash`), and Merlin answers with an element `e` of the
+  amplified set, the five certificates, and `h e = 0`. By pairwise independence, `0` is hit for at
+  least three quarters of the hashes on members and for at most a quarter on non-members
+With no certificates, `S a` is the set counted by a `#P` function, so `SBP ⊆ AM`
+* `Cslib.Complexity.certifiedSet`: the strings with an accepted certificate.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SetLowerBound.amplifiedSet`: five copies followed by normalising padding.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SetLowerBound.verifier`: the Arthur–Merlin verifier of the protocol.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SetLowerBound.card_amplifiedSet`: the size of the amplified set.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SetLowerBound.exists_verifier_iff`: Merlin has an accepted answer exactly when
+  the amplified set meets the kernel of Arthur's hash.
+* [S. Goldwasser, M. Sipser, *Private coins versus public coins in interactive proof
+* [E. Böhler, C. Glaßer, D. Meister, *Error-bounded probabilistic computations between
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- The strings of `N(n)` bits that have a certificate of `c(n)` bits accepted by `R`, where `n`
+is the length of the encoded instance. -/

+  univ.filter fun x => ∃ z : BitString (c.eval (enc a).length),
+    R (a, List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn z) = true
+/-- A bit string of `k + j` bits is its first `k` bits followed by its last `j` bits. -/

+    List.ofFn y = List.ofFn ((Fin.appendEquiv k j).symm y).1 ++
+/-- A string has no bit `true` exactly when it is zero. -/
+    (!(List.ofFn v).any fun b => b) = true ↔ v = 0 := by
+  exact ⟨fun h => funext h, fun h i => by rw [h]; rfl⟩
+/-- Five elements of `S`, followed by `T` bits whose first `ℓ` bits are `false`. -/

+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_verifier {N c m T : Polynomial ℕ} {ℓ : α → ℕ}

+/-- On a seed, an element and five certificates, the verifier accepts exactly when the blocks of

+theorem verifier_ofFn_append {N c m T : Polynomial ℕ} {ℓ : α → ℕ} {R : α × List Bool → Bool}

+      (∀ i : Fin 5, R (a, List.ofFn (BitString.block (BitString.ofList (5 * N.eval (enc a).length)
+      (!(((List.ofFn e).drop (5 * N.eval (enc a).length)).take (ℓ a)).any fun b => b) = true ∧
+  generalize (enc a).length = n at r e z ⊢
+  have hdrop : (List.ofFn r ++ (List.ofFn e ++ List.ofFn z)).drop

+  have hdrop' : (List.ofFn r ++ (List.ofFn e ++ List.ofFn z)).drop
+      (m.eval n * (5 * N.eval n + T.eval n) + m.eval n + (5 * N.eval n + T.eval n)) =
+  have htake : (List.ofFn r ++ (List.ofFn e ++ List.ofFn z)).take
+      (m.eval n * (5 * N.eval n + T.eval n) + m.eval n) = List.ofFn r :=
+  have hoffset : BitString.listRow (m.eval n) (5 * N.eval n + T.eval n) (List.ofFn r) =
+    rw [hr, BitString.listRow, Nat.mul_comm (5 * N.eval n + T.eval n),

+      verifier enc N c m T ℓ R (a, List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y) = true) ↔

+    refine ⟨_, mem_filter.2 ⟨mem_univ _, fun i => mem_filter.2 ⟨mem_univ _, _, hrows i⟩, hpad⟩,
+/-- **The set lower bound protocol** of Goldwasser and Sipser [GoldwasserSipser1986]
+[Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09]. Let `R` be a polynomial-time test, `N` and `c`
+polynomials, and `K` a polynomial-time threshold in binary with `K a > 0`. If the set of strings
+of `N(n)` bits with a certificate of `c(n)` bits accepted by `R` has at least `K a` elements for

+theorem mem_AM_of_card_certifiedSet {N c : Polynomial ℕ} {R : α × List Bool → Bool} {K : α → ℕ}

+    (hmem : ∀ a ∈ A, K a ≤ #(certifiedSet enc N c R a))

+      (5 * N.eval (enc a).length + T.eval (enc a).length) + m.eval (enc a).length := by simp

+  have hall (r : BitString (m.eval (enc a).length * (5 * N.eval (enc a).length +
+      (∀ y : BitString (5 * N.eval (enc a).length + T.eval (enc a).length +

+prefix it expects. Every prefix is extended by the same number of strings, so the fractions of

+# One-way functions separate P from NP
+If one-way functions exist then `P ≠ NP` [Goldreich, Chapter 2][Goldreich2001],
+[Katz and Lindell, Section 8.1][KatzLindell2020]. For a function `f` computable in polynomial
+time, the *preimage-prefix problem* (`Cslib.Crypto.preimagePrefix`) asks, given `n` in unary, an
+image `y` and a word `u`, whether some input `x` of length `n` that starts with `u` satisfies
+`f x = y`. It is in `NP`, with the missing bits of `x` as certificate
+A decision procedure for it finds preimages bit by bit (`Cslib.Crypto.preimageSearch`): starting
+from the empty prefix, extend the prefix by `false` if a preimage of length `n` still starts with
+the extension, and by `true` otherwise. After `n` steps the prefix is itself a preimage of `y`
+whenever `y` has a preimage of length `n` (`Cslib.Crypto.apply_preimageSearch`), and the search
+runs in polynomial time when the decision procedure does. So if the problem is in `P`, a
+deterministic polynomial-time algorithm inverts `f` on every image
+(`Cslib.Crypto.OneWay.preimagePrefix_notMem_P`). By the Cook–Levin theorem, `SAT` is then not in
+One-wayness is the uniform notion of `Cslib.Crypto.OneWay`: the inverter is uniform strict PPT
+and receives the unary length of the sampled input. The inverter built here is deterministic; the

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A *parsimonious* reduction from a counting function `f : α → ℕ` to `g : β → ℕ` is a function
+`r : α → β`, computable in polynomial time, that preserves counts exactly: `f a = g (r a)` for
+counting function is `#P`-hard when every function in `#P`, with any encoding of its instances,
+reduces to it parsimoniously, and `#P`-complete when it also belongs to `#P`.
+Parsimonious reductions compose (`ParsimoniousReducible.trans`) and `#P` is closed under them
+* [L. Valiant, *The complexity of computing the permanent*][Valiant1979]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- `f` reduces parsimoniously to `g`: some `r`, computable in polynomial time with respect to
+`encA` and `encB`, satisfies `f a = g (r a)` for every `a`. -/
+def ParsimoniousReducible (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (f : α → ℕ)
+  ∃ r : α → β, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime r encA encB ∧ ∀ a, f a = g (r a)
+/-- Every function in `#P`, with any encoding of its instances, reduces parsimoniously to `g`. -/
+def SharpPHard (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (g : β → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (f : α → ℕ), f ∈ SharpP enc →
+/-- `g` is in `#P` and every function in `#P` reduces parsimoniously to it. -/
+def SharpPComplete (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (g : β → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  g ∈ SharpP encB ∧ SharpPHard encB g
+variable {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encC : γ ↪ List Bool}
+  {f : α → ℕ} {g : β → ℕ} {h : γ → ℕ}
+/-- Every counting function reduces parsimoniously to itself by the identity function. -/
+theorem ParsimoniousReducible.refl (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (f : α → ℕ) :
+theorem ParsimoniousReducible.trans (hfg : ParsimoniousReducible encA encB f g)
+    (hgh : ParsimoniousReducible encB encC g h) : ParsimoniousReducible encA encC f h :=
+  ⟨s ∘ r, hs.comp hr, fun a => (hfg a).trans (hgh (r a))⟩
+theorem ParsimoniousReducible.mem_SharpP (hfg : ParsimoniousReducible encA encB f g)
+    (hg : g ∈ SharpP encB) : f ∈ SharpP encA := by
+  rwa [show g ∘ r = f from funext fun a => (hfg a).symm] at h
+theorem SharpPHard.trans (hg : SharpPHard encB g) (hgh : ParsimoniousReducible encB encC g h) :
+  fun enc f hf => (hg enc f hf).trans hgh

+# Complete problems for the counting classes
+Since the Cook–Levin reduction is parsimonious (`CookLevin.SharpSAT_sharpPHard`), each counting
+class defined by a condition on a function in `#P` has a complete problem defined by the same
+condition on the number of satisfying assignments of a formula (`SharpSAT`), under
+polynomial-time many-one reductions [Valiant][Valiant1979]. The classes are the verifier-based
+* `ParitySAT`, an odd number of satisfying assignments, is `⊕P`-complete
+* `ModSAT k`, a number of satisfying assignments not divisible by `k`, is `ModP k`-complete, and
+  its complement is `coModP k`-complete, for every modulus `k`;
+* `SharpSATAtLeast`, the pairs `(φ, m)` of a formula and a number in binary such that `φ` has at
+  least `m` satisfying assignments, is `PP`-complete; it is a threshold variant of the majority
+* `SharpSATExact`, the pairs `(φ, m)` such that `φ` has exactly `m` satisfying assignments, is

+`{a | Q (f a)}` for some `f ∈ #P`, and the parsimonious reduction `r` for `f` reduces it to
+`{φ | Q (SharpSAT φ)}`. For `PP`, the characterization of `PP` through `#P`

+formula for `2 f` with the threshold `2 ^ q(n) + 1`. For `C=P`, a problem in the class is
+`{a | f₁ a = f₂ a}` for `f₁, f₂ ∈ #P`, with `f₂ ≤ 2 ^ p(n)` and `2 ^ p(n) - f₂ ∈ #P`

+with the count `2 ^ p(n)`. In both cases the number `m` is computed in polynomial time in binary.

+/-- The pairs `(φ, m)` such that `φ` has at least `m` satisfying assignments. Instances are
+def SharpSATAtLeast : Set (CNF ℕ × ℕ) := {x | x.2 ≤ SharpSAT x.1}
+/-- The pairs `(φ, m)` such that `φ` has exactly `m` satisfying assignments. Instances are
+def SharpSATExact : Set (CNF ℕ × ℕ) := {x | SharpSAT x.1 = x.2}
+/-- A formula is uniquely satisfiable exactly when it has one satisfying assignment. -/

+/-- **Complete problems from conditions on counts.** If the problems of a class `C` are, for
+every encoding, the sets `{a | Q (f a)}` for functions `f` in `#P`, then
+theorem polyTimeComplete_sharpSAT {C : ∀ {α : Type}, (α ↪ List Bool) → Set (Set α)}
+    (Q : ℕ → Prop) (hC : ∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (A : Set α),
+      A ∈ C enc ↔ ∃ f ∈ SharpP enc, ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ Q (f a)) :
+    PolyTimeComplete C encCNF {φ | Q (SharpSAT φ)} := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, hA⟩ := (hC enc A).1 hA

+/-- **`USAT` is `US`-complete**: unique satisfiability is complete for the class of problems

+/-- **`Mod_k SAT` is `ModP k`-complete**, for every modulus `k`. -/

+/-- **The complement of `Mod_k SAT` is `coModP k`-complete**, for every modulus `k`. -/

+theorem eval_toUnbounded_atomsOf (e : Atom L n ≃ Fin N) {M : Type*} [L.Structure M]
+    (toUnbounded e φ Fin.elim0).eval Unbounded.interpretation (atomsOf (L := L) eM ∘ e.symm) =
+        Subsingleton.elim (Empty.elim : Empty → Model (atomsOf (L := L) eM)) default,
+        Subsingleton.elim (Fin.elim0 : Fin 0 → Model (atomsOf (L := L) eM)) default])).trans
+/-- The universe `Fin n` with the structure interpreting the unary relation symbol `P` as the set
+`S` and every other relation symbol as the structure `N` does: the expansion of the numerical
+def Expansion (_P : L.Relations 1) (_N : L.Structure (Fin n)) (_S : Finset (Fin n)) : Type :=
+    if (⟨l, R⟩ : Σ l, L.Relations l) = ⟨1, P⟩ then ∀ i, (t i : Fin n) ∈ S else N.RelMap R t
+@[simp] theorem relMap_self (t : Fin 1 → Expansion P N S) :
+    Structure.RelMap P t ↔ (t 0 : Fin n) ∈ S := by
+/-- The other relation symbols are interpreted as in `N`. -/
+theorem relMap_of_ne {l : ℕ} {R : L.Relations l} (h : (⟨l, R⟩ : Σ l, L.Relations l) ≠ ⟨1, P⟩)
+    (t : Fin l → Expansion P N S) : Structure.RelMap R t ↔ N.RelMap R t := by
+/-- A sentence defining even cardinality of `P` over the numerical relations `N` on `Fin n` gives a
+formula on `n` inputs computing parity, of depth at most `foDepth φ + 2` and polynomial size: the
+translation of the sentence, reading the facts `P(a)` from the input bits and the other facts from
+private theorem exists_formula_computes_parity [Finite (Σ l, L.Relations l)] (P : L.Relations 1)
+    (h : ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), Expansion P N S ⊨ φ ↔ Even #S) :
+      F.Computes Unbounded.interpretation (parity n) ∧ F.depth ≤ foDepth φ + 2 ∧
+  let e : Atom L n ≃ Fin (Fintype.card (Atom L n)) := Fintype.equivFin _
+  let G := toUnbounded e φ Fin.elim0
+  -- the facts `P(a)` are read from the input bits, the other facts from `N`
+  let sub : Fin (Fintype.card (Atom L n)) → Circuits.Formula Unbounded.signature n := fun j =>
+    if (e.symm j).1 = ⟨1, P⟩ then .gate (.and _) fun i => .input ((e.symm j).2 i)
+  have hsubd : ∀ j, (sub j).depth ≤ 1 := fun j => by
+  have hsubs : ∀ j, (sub j).size ≤ 1 := fun j => by
+    set S : Finset (Fin n) := {i | y i = true}
+    have hatoms : (fun j => (sub j).eval Unbounded.interpretation y) =
+        atomsOf (L := L) (M := Expansion P N S) (Equiv.refl _) ∘ e.symm := by
+      by_cases hR : (⟨l, R⟩ : Σ l, L.Relations l) = ⟨1, P⟩
+    have hreal : (G.bind sub).eval Unbounded.interpretation y = true ↔ Even #S := by
+      exact (eval_toUnbounded_atomsOf e (M := Expansion P N S) (Equiv.refl _) φ).trans (h S)
+    have hG : G.depth ≤ foDepth φ := depth_toUnbounded_le e φ Fin.elim0
+    have hs : G.size ≤ foSize φ * (n + 2) ^ foSize φ := size_toUnbounded_le e φ Fin.elim0
+    have hl : G.leafSize ≤ (n + 2) ^ foSize φ := leafSize_toUnbounded_le e φ Fin.elim0
+    have hpos : 1 ≤ (n + 2) ^ foSize φ := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
+/-- **Parity is not first-order definable, with arbitrary numerical relations**
+language with finitely many relation symbols, `P` a unary relation symbol of `L`, and `N n` any
+interpretation of the symbols of `L` on `Fin n`, for each `n`. No first-order sentence `φ` of `L`
+satisfies, for all large `n` and all sets `S` of elements of `Fin n`, that the structure
+interpreting `P` as `S` and the other symbols as `N n` satisfies `φ` exactly when `S` has an even
+    ¬ ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), Expansion P (N n) S ⊨ φ ↔ Even #S := by
+  -- the lengths `s (16 s + 1) ^ (foDepth φ + 2)` grow without bound
+  have htend : Filter.Tendsto (fun s => s * (16 * s + 1) ^ (foDepth φ + 2)) Filter.atTop
+  -- the size bound at those lengths is a polynomial in `s`
+      (foSize φ + 2) * (s * (16 * s + 1) ^ (foDepth φ + 2) + 2) ^ foSize φ := by
+    exists_formula_computes_parity P (N (s * (16 * s + 1) ^ (foDepth φ + 2))) φ hS
+For a relational language `L` with finitely many relation symbols and a unary relation symbol
+`P`, no first-order sentence of `L` holds, among the finite structures with at least `n₀`
+elements, in exactly those in which `P` holds of an even number of elements. -/
+    ¬ ∀ (M : Type) [L.Structure M] [Finite M], n₀ ≤ Nat.card M →
+      (M ⊨ φ ↔ Even (Nat.card {m : M // Structure.RelMap P ![m]})) := by
+  -- the numerical relations are all empty
+  let N : ∀ n, L.Structure (Fin n) := fun _ => ⟨fun f => isEmptyElim f, fun _ _ => False⟩
+  have : Finite (Expansion P (N n) S) := inferInstanceAs (Finite (Fin n))
+  have hcard : Nat.card {m : Expansion P (N n) S // Structure.RelMap P ![m]} = #S := by
+  have hn' : Nat.card (Expansion P (N n) S) = n :=

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Exponential lower bounds for graph problems under the exponential time hypothesis
+Under the exponential time hypothesis, 3-coloring, independent set and vertex cover are not
+decidable in time `2 ^ o(|V| + |E|)`, and independent set and clique are not decidable in time
+[LokshtanovMarxSaurabh2011]. Each follows from a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT whose graph
+has `O(m)` vertices and edges on formulas with `m` clauses
+lemma, which rules out subexponential time in `m` under the exponential time hypothesis:
+* for 3-coloring, the gadget reduction `Cslib.Complexity.SAT.toThreeColoring`, whose graph has at
+  most `(24 k + 12) m + 9` vertices and edges on clauses of at most `k` literals
+* for independent set, the reduction with variable edges
+  `Cslib.Complexity.SAT.toIndependentSet` has at most `3 m` vertices on formulas with clauses of
+  at most three literals, but can have quadratically many edges;
+* for vertex cover, the same graph with the complementary target
+* for clique, the complement of the same graph on its vertices (`Cslib.Complexity.Graph.compl`),
+  which has as many vertices but can have quadratically many edges.
+A graph (`Cslib.Complexity.Graph`) is a list of declared vertices and a list of edges, and the
+measures `|V|` and `|E|` are the lengths of these lists. They are at least the numbers of distinct
+vertices and edges, so the lower bounds for them imply the lower bounds for the distinct counts
+(`Cslib.Complexity.DecidableInSubexpTime.mono_measure`). As for `ETH` itself, time is measured up
+to a polynomial in the length of the encoded instance, and a lower bound says: for some `δ > 0`, no
+decider runs within time `2 ^ (δ μ)` times a polynomial.
+The diamond reduction to Hamiltonian paths and cycles (`Cslib.Complexity.SAT.toDirHamPath`) has a
+row of `3 m + 3` vertices for each variable occurrence, so up to `Θ(m ^ 2)` vertices and edges on
+formulas with `m` clauses of three literals. Through it the exponential time hypothesis rules out
+only time `2 ^ o(√(|V| + |E|))`; this is not stated here.
+  and no `2 ^ o(|V|)` algorithm for independent set.
+* [R. Impagliazzo, R. Paturi, F. Zane, *Which problems have strongly exponential
+* [M. Cygan, F. V. Fomin, Ł. Kowalik, D. Lokshtanov, D. Marx, M. Pilipczuk, M. Pilipczuk,
+* [D. Lokshtanov, D. Marx, S. Saurabh, *Lower bounds based on the Exponential Time
+private theorem length_flatMap_le {α β : Type*} {l : List α} {f : α → List β} {k : ℕ}
+    (h : ∀ a ∈ l, (f a).length ≤ k) : (l.flatMap f).length ≤ k * l.length := by
+  simpa using List.sum_le_length_nsmul (l.map fun a => (f a).length) k (by simpa using h)
+/-- **The 3-coloring reduction has linear size.** On formulas with `m` clauses of at most `k`
+literals, the graph of `SAT.toThreeColoring` has at most `(24 k + 12) m + 9` vertices and edges in
+theorem SAT.length_toThreeColoring_le {k : ℕ} {φ : CNF ℕ} (hφ : ∀ c ∈ φ, c.length ≤ k) :
+  have hzip : ∀ c ∈ φ.zipIdx, c.1.length ≤ k := fun c hc => by
+  have hvars : φ.vars.length ≤ k * φ.length := by
+    simpa using List.sum_le_length_nsmul (φ.map List.length) k (by simpa using hφ)
+  have h₂ : (φ.zipIdx.flatMap fun c => clauseEdges φ c.2 c.1).length ≤
+    simpa using length_flatMap_le (l := φ.zipIdx) fun c hc => by
+        (f := fun l => stageEdges φ c.2 l.2 l.1) fun _ _ => by simp [stageEdges]
+  have hE : (coloringEdges φ).length ≤ (8 * k + 4) * φ.length + 3 := by
+/-- **No `2 ^ o(|V| + |E|)` algorithm for 3-coloring under ETH** [CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 14]:
+for some `δ > 0`, `ThreeColoring` is not decidable within time `2 ^ (δ (|V| + |E|))` times any
+polynomial in the length of the encoded graph, for graphs with `|V|` declared vertices and `|E|`
+    ¬DecidableInSubexpTime ThreeColoring encGraph fun G => G.1.length + G.2.length :=
+    (fun φ _ => SAT.toThreeColoring_mem_iff φ) (k := 84 + 9) fun φ hφ => by
+/-- **No `2 ^ o(|V| + |E|)` algorithm for independent set under ETH** [CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 14]:
+for some `δ > 0`, `IndependentSet` is not decidable within time `2 ^ (δ (|V| + |E|))` times any
+polynomial in the length of the encoded instance, for graphs with `|V|` declared vertices and `|E|`
+    (fun φ _ => SAT.toSparseIndependentSet_mem_iff φ) (k := 24) fun φ hφ => by
+/-- **No `2 ^ o(|V|)` algorithm for independent set under ETH** [CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 14]: for
+some `δ > 0`, `IndependentSet` is not decidable within time `2 ^ (δ |V|)` times any polynomial in
+the length of the encoded instance, for graphs with `|V|` declared vertices. -/
+    ¬DecidableInSubexpTime IndependentSet (encPair encGraph encNat) fun x => x.1.1.length :=
+    (fun φ _ => SAT.toSparseIndependentSet_mem_iff φ) (k := 24) fun φ hφ => by
+/-- **No `2 ^ o(|V| + |E|)` algorithm for vertex cover under ETH** [CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 14]:
+for some `δ > 0`, `VertexCover` is not decidable within time `2 ^ (δ (|V| + |E|))` times any
+polynomial in the length of the encoded instance, for graphs with `|V|` declared vertices and `|E|`
+/-- **No `2 ^ o(|V|)` algorithm for clique under ETH** [CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 14]: for some
+`δ > 0`, `Clique` is not decidable within time `2 ^ (δ |V|)` times any polynomial in the length of
+the encoded instance, for graphs with `|V|` declared vertices. -/
+    ¬DecidableInSubexpTime Clique (encPair encGraph encNat) fun x => x.1.1.length :=
+      (encPair encGraph encNat) (encPair encGraph encNat) by fun_prop).comp

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Exponential time bounds in a parameter of the instance transfer along polynomial-time reductions
+that increase the parameter at most linearly. If `f` reduces `A` to `B` in polynomial time and
+`μB (f a) ≤ c μA a + c`, then a decider for `B` within time `2 ^ (δ μB b)` times a polynomial in
+the length of the encoded instance gives a decider for `A` within time `2 ^ (c δ μA a)` times a
+decider. The polynomial absorbs the running time of the reduction and the length of its output.
+Hence subexponential time in `μB` gives subexponential time in `μA`
+Under the exponential time hypothesis, 3SAT is not decidable in subexponential time in the number
+lemma). So a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT whose output measure is linear in the number of
+clauses shows that the target problem is not decidable in subexponential time in that measure
+[ImpagliazzoPaturiZane2001] [CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 14]. Lower bounds for larger measures are
+stronger: a measure that is at most linear in another one gives the weaker lower bound for free
+  time hypothesis through reductions of linear size from 3SAT.
+* [R. Impagliazzo, R. Paturi, F. Zane, *Which problems have strongly exponential
+* [M. Cygan, F. V. Fomin, Ł. Kowalik, D. Lokshtanov, D. Marx, M. Pilipczuk, M. Pilipczuk,
+variable {α : Type*} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α} {μ μ' : α → ℕ}
+/-- A decider within time `2 ^ (δ μ a)` times a polynomial, for a measure `μ ≤ c μ' + c`, decides
+within time `2 ^ (c δ μ' a)` times a polynomial. -/
+theorem DecidableInExpTime.mono_measure {c : ℕ} (hμ : ∀ a, μ a ≤ c * μ' a + c) {δ : ℝ}
+    (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (h : DecidableInExpTime A enc μ δ) : DecidableInExpTime A enc μ' (c * δ) := by
+  refine ⟨e, h.mono ⌈(2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * c)⌉₊ (fun a => ?_) fun a => by positivity⟩
+  have hK : (2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * c) ≤ ⌈(2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * c)⌉₊ := Nat.le_ceil _
+  have h₁ : (2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * μ a) ≤ 2 ^ (δ * c) * 2 ^ (c * δ * μ' a) := by
+    have : (μ a : ℝ) ≤ c * μ' a + c := by exact_mod_cast hμ a
+  have h₄ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ⌈(2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * c)⌉₊ := Nat.cast_nonneg _
+/-- Subexponential time in a measure `μ ≤ c μ' + c` gives subexponential time in `μ'`. So a lower
+bound for `μ'` gives the lower bound for `μ`. -/
+theorem DecidableInSubexpTime.mono_measure {c : ℕ} (hμ : ∀ a, μ a ≤ c * μ' a + c)
+    (h : DecidableInSubexpTime A enc μ) : DecidableInSubexpTime A enc μ' := by
+variable {α β : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α} {B : Set β}
+/-- **Transfer along reductions of linear size.** If `f` reduces `A` to `B` in polynomial time
+with `μB (f a) ≤ c μA a + c`, then a decider for `B` within time `2 ^ (δ μB b)` times a polynomial
+in the length of the encoded instance gives a decider for `A` within time `2 ^ (c δ μA a)` times a
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encA encB) (hfA : ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a ∈ B) {c : ℕ}
+    (hμ : ∀ a, μB (f a) ≤ c * μA a + c) {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
+    (h : DecidableInExpTime B encB μB δ) : DecidableInExpTime A encA μA (c * δ) := by
+  obtain ⟨g, t, k, hg, hgB, ht⟩ := h.exists_computableTidilyInO
+  set X : ℝ := 2 ^ (c * δ * μA a)
+  have hP : 1 ≤ P := one_le_pow₀ (by linarith [(Nat.cast_nonneg (encA a).length : (0 : ℝ) ≤ _)])
+  have hX : 1 ≤ X := Real.one_le_rpow (by norm_num) (by positivity)
+  have hk : (0 : ℝ) ≤ k := Nat.cast_nonneg k
+  have hl0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ l := Nat.cast_nonneg l
+  -- the output of the reduction has length at most `2 l P`
+  have hlen : ((encB (f a)).length : ℝ) + 1 ≤ (2 * l + 1) * P := by
+  have hexp : (2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * μB (f a)) ≤ 2 ^ (δ * c) * X := by
+    have : (μB (f a) : ℝ) ≤ c * μA a + c := by exact_mod_cast hμ a
+  -- the decider on the reduced instance
+  have hpow : (((encB (f a)).length : ℝ) + 1) ^ e ≤ (2 * l + 1) ^ e * P ^ e := by
+    have := mul_le_mul hexp hpow (by positivity) (by positivity)
+  have hPe : P ^ e ≤ P ^ (e + 1) := pow_le_pow_right₀ hP (Nat.le_succ e)
+  have hP1 : P ≤ P ^ (e + 1) := le_self_pow₀ hP (Nat.succ_ne_zero e)
+  have hXP : 1 ≤ X * P ^ (e + 1) := one_le_mul_of_one_le_of_one_le hX (one_le_pow₀ hP)
+  have hgoal : P + (t (f a) : ℝ) ≤ K * (X * P ^ (e + 1)) := by
+    have h₁ : P ≤ X * P ^ (e + 1) := hP1.trans (le_mul_of_one_le_left (by positivity) hX)
+    have h₂ : X * P ^ e ≤ X * P ^ (e + 1) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hPe (by positivity)
+      (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ k * (2 ^ (δ * c) * (2 * l + 1) ^ e))
+  have hPow : X * P ^ (e + 1) = X * (((encA a).length : ℝ) + 1) ^ (d * e + d) := by
+  calc P + (t (f a) : ℝ) ≤ K * (X * P ^ (e + 1)) := hgoal
+    _ = ⌈K⌉₊ * (X * (((encA a).length : ℝ) + 1) ^ (d * e + d)) := by rw [hPow]
+/-- **Transfer along reductions of linear size.** If `f` reduces `A` to `B` in polynomial time
+with `μB (f a) ≤ c μA a + c`, and `B` is decidable in subexponential time in `μB`, then `A` is
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encA encB) (hfA : ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a ∈ B) {c : ℕ}
+    (hμ : ∀ a, μB (f a) ≤ c * μA a + c) (h : DecidableInSubexpTime B encB μB) :
+  refine ((h (δ / (c + 1)) (by positivity)).of_reduction hf hfA hμ (by positivity)).mono ?_
+/-- **Lower bounds from the exponential time hypothesis** [ImpagliazzoPaturiZane2001]
+[CyganEtAl2015, Chapter 14]. Under `ETH`, if `f` is computable in polynomial time and, on formulas
+`φ` in conjunctive normal form with `m` clauses of at most three literals, maps `φ` to an instance
+of `B` exactly when `φ` is satisfiable, with `μB (f φ) ≤ k m + k`, then `B` is not decidable in
+subexponential time in `μB`: for some `δ > 0`, no decider runs within time `2 ^ (δ μB b)` times a
+polynomial in the length of the encoded instance. -/
+    (hfB : ∀ φ : CNF ℕ, (∀ c ∈ φ, c.length ≤ 3) → (f φ ∈ B ↔ φ ∈ SAT)) {k : ℕ}
+    (hμ : ∀ φ : CNF ℕ, (∀ c ∈ φ, c.length ≤ 3) → μB (f φ) ≤ k * φ.length + k) :
+  -- formulas with a clause of more than three literals go to the image of the empty clause
+    (h.of_reduction (f := fun φ => if φ.all (fun c => decide (c.length ≤ 3)) then f φ
+    · have hw : (φ.all fun c => decide (c.length ≤ 3)) = true := by simpa using hφ
+      simp only [hw, ite_true, hfB φ hφ]
+      exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hφ, h⟩⟩
+    · have hw : (φ.all fun c => decide (c.length ≤ 3)) = false := by simpa using hφ
+      simp only [hw, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false, hfB [[]] (by simp)]
+      exact ⟨fun h => (hφ h.1).elim, fun ⟨σ, hσ⟩ => by simp at hσ⟩
+    · have := hμ φ (by simpa using hw)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# A reduction of linear size to independent sets
+Karp's reduction `Cslib.Complexity.SAT.toIndependentSet` joins all complementary occurrences of a
+variable, so its graph can have quadratically many edges in the number of clauses even for formulas
+with three literals per clause. `SAT.toSparseIndependentSet` is the reduction with variable edges
+[Garey and Johnson, Theorem 3.3][GareyJohnson1979], stated for independent sets. It has
+* two literal vertices for each of the `n` distinct variables of the formula, joined by an edge;
+* a vertex for each position of each clause, the positions of a clause forming a clique;
+* an edge from each position to the literal vertex of the complement of its literal,
+and asks for an independent set of `n + m` vertices, for `m` clauses. An independent set has at
+most one vertex in each variable edge and in each clause clique, so one of `n + m` vertices has
+exactly one in each: the literal vertices chosen give an assignment, and the position chosen in a
+clause is not joined to its literal, which therefore holds. Conversely, a satisfying assignment
+chooses the true literal of each variable and a true position of each clause.
+On formulas whose clauses have at most `k` literals the graph has at most `(k ^ 2 + 5 k) m`
+vertices and edges in total (`Cslib.Complexity.SAT.length_toSparseIndependentSet_le`), which is
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SAT.length_toSparseIndependentSet_le`: the graph has linearly many vertices
+  and edges for clauses of bounded width.
+* [M. R. Garey and D. S. Johnson, *Computers and Intractability*][GareyJohnson1979]
+/-- The vertex of the literal `l` of `φ`, its variable numbered by its position in
+def literalVertex (φ : CNF ℕ) (l : Literal ℕ) : ℕ :=
+/-- The vertex of position `j` of clause `i`. -/
+def occurrenceVertex (i j : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.pair 1 (Nat.pair i j)
+/-- The vertices: the two literals of every variable of `φ`, and every position of every clause. -/
+      (fun x => [literalVertex φ (x, true), literalVertex φ (x, false)]) ++
+/-- The edges between the two literals of each variable. -/
+  (ThreeSAT.distinctVars φ).map fun x => (literalVertex φ (x, true), literalVertex φ (x, false))
+/-- The edges between any two positions of a clause. -/
+  φ.zipIdx.flatMap fun c => (List.range c.1.length).flatMap fun j =>
+    (List.range c.1.length).map fun j' => (occurrenceVertex c.2 j, occurrenceVertex c.2 j')
+/-- The edges from each position of a clause to the complement of its literal. -/
+    c.1.zipIdx.map fun l => (occurrenceVertex c.2 l.2, literalVertex φ (l.1.1, !l.1.2))
+def edges (φ : CNF ℕ) : List (ℕ × ℕ) := variableEdges φ ++ clauseEdges φ ++ conflictEdges φ
+/-- The reduction from `SAT` to `IndependentSet` with variable edges [Garey and Johnson,
+Theorem 3.3][GareyJohnson1979]: the graph of `φ` with the target `n + m`, for `n` distinct
+private theorem mem_zipIdx_iff {α : Type*} {l : List α} {a : α} {i : ℕ} :
+    (a, i) ∈ l.zipIdx ↔ ∃ h : i < l.length, l[i] = a := by
+private theorem mem_vars {i j : ℕ} (hi : i < φ.length) (hj : j < φ[i].length) :
+  List.mem_map.2 ⟨φ[i][j], List.mem_flatten.2 ⟨φ[i], List.getElem_mem hi, List.getElem_mem hj⟩,
+theorem literalVertex_inj {x x' : ℕ} (hx : x ∈ φ.vars) {b b' : Bool} :
+    literalVertex φ (x, b) = literalVertex φ (x', b') ↔ x = x' ∧ b = b' := by
+    literalVertex φ l ≠ occurrenceVertex i j := by
+    occurrenceVertex i j = occurrenceVertex i' j' ↔ i = i' ∧ j = j' := by
+theorem mem_vertices {v : ℕ} : v ∈ vertices φ ↔ (∃ x ∈ φ.vars, ∃ b, v = literalVertex φ (x, b)) ∨
+    ∃ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < φ.length), ∃ j < φ[i].length, v = occurrenceVertex i j := by
+  simp only [vertices, List.mem_append, List.mem_flatMap, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil,
+  · rintro ⟨c, i, hc, j, hj, rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨φ[i], i, mem_zipIdx_iff.2 ⟨hi, rfl⟩, j, hj, rfl⟩
+theorem mem_variableEdges {e : ℕ × ℕ} : e ∈ variableEdges φ ↔

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# The Arthur–Merlin classes MA and AM
+The two-message public-coin proof systems of [Babai][Babai1985] and
+[Babai and Moran][BabaiMoran1988] are defined, like `BPP` (`Cslib.Complexity.BPP`), through
+deterministic polynomial-time verifiers that read their messages as one string
+[Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09]. Write `n` for the length of the encoded
+* In `MA` (`Cslib.Complexity.MA`) Merlin speaks first: a proof `y` of `q(n)` bits, then Arthur
+  flips `p(n)` coins `r` and accepts when `V (a, y ++ r) = true`. On a member some proof is
+  accepted on at least two thirds of the random strings; on a non-member every proof is rejected
+  on at least two thirds of them.
+* In `AM` (`Cslib.Complexity.AM`) Arthur speaks first: he sends his `p(n)` random bits `r`,
+  Merlin replies with `y` of `q(n)` bits and the verifier accepts when `V (a, r ++ y) = true`. On
+  a member, at least two thirds of the random strings admit an accepted reply; on a non-member at
+  least two thirds of them admit none.
+As in `NP`, the lengths are polynomials of `n`, the messages have exactly these lengths, and the
+probabilities are counts of random strings, which are functions `Fin (p n) → Bool`. Merlin's
+messages also range over functions `Fin (q n) → Bool`, so that the counted condition of `AM` is
+decidable. The characterisations by interactive machines and the round-collapse theorem
+Both classes contain `NP` (no coins) and `BPP` (no proof), and are closed under polynomial-time
+many-one reductions. A reduction changes the lengths the verifier expects, so the new verifier
+reads only prefixes of the proof and of the random string of the lengths it needs; the ignored
+random bits multiply every count by the same power of two (`Cslib.BitString.card_filter_take`).
+Error reduction, `MA ⊆ AM` and `MA ⊆ SBP` are in
+the second level of the polynomial hierarchy in
+  scale counts and do not matter to existential quantifiers.
+* [L. Babai, S. Moran, *Arthur–Merlin games: a randomized proof system, and a hierarchy of
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- Cutting the concatenation of blocks into its blocks recovers them. -/
+@[simp] theorem block_blocksEquiv_symm {m k : ℕ} (z : Fin m → BitString k) :
+/-- A string of `k ≤ K` bits padded with `false` to `K` bits has the original string as its
+theorem take_ofFn_ofList {k K : ℕ} (h : k ≤ K) (y : BitString k) :
+    (List.ofFn (ofList K (List.ofFn y))).take k = List.ofFn y := by
+  simp [ofList, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, show i < k by omega]
+/-- **Prefixes and existential quantifiers.** For `k ≤ K`, some string of `K` bits has a prefix of
+length `k` satisfying `g` iff some string of `k` bits does. -/
+theorem exists_take_iff {k K : ℕ} (h : k ≤ K) {g : List Bool → Prop} :
+    (∃ y : BitString K, g ((List.ofFn y).take k)) ↔ ∃ y : BitString k, g (List.ofFn y) :=
+    fun ⟨y, hy⟩ => ⟨ofList K (List.ofFn y), by rwa [take_ofFn_ofList h]⟩⟩
+/-- **Prefixes and universal quantifiers.** For `k ≤ K`, every string of `K` bits has a prefix of
+length `k` satisfying `g` iff every string of `k` bits does. -/
+theorem forall_take_iff {k K : ℕ} (h : k ≤ K) {g : List Bool → Prop} :
+    (∀ y : BitString K, g ((List.ofFn y).take k)) ↔ ∀ y : BitString k, g (List.ofFn y) := by
+  simpa only [not_exists, not_not] using (exists_take_iff h (g := fun w => ¬g w)).not
+/-- **Counting by prefixes.** For `k ≤ K`, the strings of `K` bits whose prefix of length `k`
+satisfies `g` are `2 ^ (K - k)` times as many as the strings of `k` bits satisfying `g`. -/
+theorem card_filter_take {k K : ℕ} (h : k ≤ K) (g : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred g] :
+      2 ^ (K - k) * #{r : BitString k | g (List.ofFn r)} := by
+  rw [card_filter_ofFn_add k j fun u _ => g u, Nat.add_sub_cancel_left, card_filter, mul_sum]
+variable {α β : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- `V` is a Merlin–Arthur verifier for `A`, with proofs of length `q` and random strings of
+length `p`, both evaluated at the length of the encoded instance: on a member `a` some proof `y`
+makes at least two thirds of the random strings `r` accepted, `V (a, y ++ r) = true`; on a
+non-member every proof leaves at least two thirds of the random strings rejected. -/
+def IsMerlinArthurVerifier (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (q p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool)
+  ∀ a, (a ∈ A → ∃ y : Fin (q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+        V (a, List.ofFn y ++ List.ofFn r) = true).card) ∧
+    (a ∉ A → ∀ y : Fin (q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+        V (a, List.ofFn y ++ List.ofFn r) = false).card)
+/-- The problems with polynomial-time Merlin–Arthur verifiers, with polynomially long proofs and
+random strings, with respect to the encoding `enc` of instances [Babai][Babai1985]. -/
+def MA (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ (q p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧ IsMerlinArthurVerifier enc q p V A}
+theorem mem_MA : A ∈ MA enc ↔ ∃ (q p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      IsMerlinArthurVerifier enc q p V A :=
+/-- `V` is an Arthur–Merlin verifier for `A`, with random strings of length `p` and replies of
+length `q`, both evaluated at the length of the encoded instance: on a member `a` at least two
+thirds of the random strings `r` have a reply `y` with `V (a, r ++ y) = true`; on a non-member at
+least two thirds of them have none. -/
+def IsArthurMerlinVerifier (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p q : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool)
+        ∃ y : Fin (q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (a, List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y) = true).card) ∧
+        ∀ y : Fin (q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (a, List.ofFn r ++ List.ofFn y) = false).card)
+/-- The problems with polynomial-time Arthur–Merlin verifiers, with polynomially long random
+strings and replies, with respect to the encoding `enc` of instances
+def AM (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ (p q : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧ IsArthurMerlinVerifier enc p q V A}
+theorem mem_AM : A ∈ AM enc ↔ ∃ (p q : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      IsArthurMerlinVerifier enc p q V A :=
+/-- With no random bits, the single random string is accepted or rejected. -/
+    (g : (Fin m → Bool) → Prop) [DecidablePred g] (h : ∀ r, g r) :
+/-- **`NP ⊆ MA`**: an `NP` verifier is a Merlin–Arthur verifier that flips no coins. -/
+theorem NP_subset_MA : NP enc ⊆ MA enc := by
+  refine ⟨p, 0, V, hV, fun a => ⟨fun ha => ?_, fun ha y => ?_⟩⟩
+    exact ha ((hA a).2 ⟨_, List.length_ofFn, by simpa using hVy⟩)
+/-- **`BPP ⊆ MA`**: a bounded-error verifier is a Merlin–Arthur verifier that reads no proof. -/
+theorem BPP_subset_MA : BPP enc ⊆ MA enc := by
+  have hnil (a : α) (y : Fin ((0 : Polynomial ℕ).eval (enc a).length) → Bool) :
+  refine ⟨0, p, V, hV, fun a => ⟨fun ha => ⟨fun _ => false, ?_⟩, fun ha y => ?_⟩⟩
+  · simpa only [hnil, List.nil_append] using (hA a).1 ha
+  · simpa only [hnil, List.nil_append] using (hA a).2 ha
+/-- **`MA` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** The verifier runs the verifier of the
+target problem on the reduced instance, on the prefix of the proof and the prefix of the random
+string of the lengths that it expects. -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_MA {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {B : Set β}
+    (h : PolyTimeReducible enc encB A B) (hB : B ∈ MA encB) : A ∈ MA enc := by
+  obtain ⟨q, p, V, hV, hVB⟩ := hB
+  have hq : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => q.eval (encB (f a)).length) enc encUnary :=
+  have hp : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (encB (f a)).length) enc encUnary :=
+  set Q : Polynomial ℕ := Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d with hQ
+  set P : Polynomial ℕ := Polynomial.C c' * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d' with hP
+  have hQe (a : α) : q.eval (encB (f a)).length ≤ Q.eval (enc a).length := by
+  have hPe (a : α) : p.eval (encB (f a)).length ≤ P.eval (enc a).length := by
+  have hQu : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Q.eval (enc a).length) enc encUnary :=
+  refine ⟨Q, P, fun x => V (f x.1, x.2.take (q.eval (encB (f x.1)).length) ++
+  -- the verifier reads the prefixes of the proof and of the random string
+  have hsplit (y : Fin (Q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) (r : Fin (P.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) :
+  -- counts over the long random strings scale those over the short ones
+        V (f a, y ++ (List.ofFn r).take (p.eval (encB (f a)).length)) = b).card =
+          V (f a, y ++ List.ofFn r) = b).card :=
+    BitString.card_filter_take (hPe a) fun w => V (f a, y ++ w) = b
+  have hscale {y : ℕ} (hxy : 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (encB (f a)).length ≤ 3 * y) :
+    have hy := (hVB (f a)).2 (fun hb => ha ((hAB a).2 hb))
+/-- **`AM` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** The verifier runs the verifier of the
+target problem on the reduced instance, on the prefix of the random string and the prefix of the
+reply of the lengths that it expects. -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_AM {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {B : Set β}
+    (h : PolyTimeReducible enc encB A B) (hB : B ∈ AM encB) : A ∈ AM enc := by
+  obtain ⟨p, q, V, hV, hVB⟩ := hB

+  have hp : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (encB (f a)).length) enc encUnary :=
+  set Q : Polynomial ℕ := Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d with hQ

+  have hQe (a : α) : q.eval (encB (f a)).length ≤ Q.eval (enc a).length := by
+  have hPe (a : α) : p.eval (encB (f a)).length ≤ P.eval (enc a).length := by
+  have hPu : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => P.eval (enc a).length) enc encUnary :=
+  refine ⟨P, Q, fun x => V (f x.1, x.2.take (p.eval (encB (f x.1)).length) ++
+  -- the verifier reads the prefixes of the random string and of the reply
+  have hsplit (r : Fin (P.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) (y : Fin (Q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) :
+  -- a reply matters only through its prefix, and the random string only through its prefix
+      (∃ y : Fin (Q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (f a, (List.ofFn r).take
+          V (f a, (List.ofFn r).take (p.eval (encB (f a)).length) ++ List.ofFn y) = true :=
+      (g := fun w => V (f a, (List.ofFn r).take (p.eval (encB (f a)).length) ++ w) = true)
+      (∀ y : Fin (Q.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (f a, (List.ofFn r).take
+          V (f a, (List.ofFn r).take (p.eval (encB (f a)).length) ++ List.ofFn y) = false :=
+      (g := fun w => V (f a, (List.ofFn r).take (p.eval (encB (f a)).length) ++ w) = false)
+  have hscale {y : ℕ} (hxy : 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (encB (f a)).length ≤ 3 * y) :
+      ∃ y : Fin (q.eval (encB (f a)).length) → Bool, V (f a, w ++ List.ofFn y) = true]

+# MA and AM in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy
+`MA ⊆ Σ₂ ∩ Π₂` and `AM ⊆ Π₂` [Babai][Babai1985], [Babai and Moran][BabaiMoran1988],
+[Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09], by Lautemann's covering argument
+Write `n` for the length of the encoded instance.
+First reduce the error to `2 ^ (-e(n))`, with random strings of `m(n) = 12 e(n) p(n)` bits, where
+`p(n)` is the original random-string length; then `k(n) = e(n) = 12 p(n) + 1` shifts satisfy
+`m(n) < e(n) k(n)` and `k(n) < 2 ^ e(n)`. For a set `S` of random strings, with xor as addition:
+* if `S` misses at most a `2 ^ (-e(n))` fraction of the strings, some `k(n)` shifts `u i` carry
+* if `S` is at most such a fraction, for all `k(n)` shifts some `r` has every `r + u i` outside `S`
+For `MA ⊆ Σ₂`, `S` is the set of random strings accepted with a proof `y`, and
+`a ∈ A ↔ ∃ y u, ∀ r, ∃ i, V (a, y ++ (r + u i))`; Merlin's proof and the shifts form one existential
+block (`Cslib.Complexity.ArthurMerlin.sigmaTwoVerifier`). For `AM ⊆ Π₂`, `S` is the set of random
+strings with an accepted reply, and `a ∈ A ↔ ∀ u, ∃ r Y, ∀ i, V (a, (r + u i) ++ Y i)`; the
+random string and the `k(n)` replies form one existential block

+/-- **Merlin–Arthur verifiers in `Σ₂`.** If `W` is a Merlin–Arthur verifier for `A` with error at

+/-- On the shifts followed by any word `v`, the `Π₂` verifier accepts iff `W` accepts, for each

+/-- **`MA ⊆ Σ₂`** [Babai][Babai1985], [Arora and Barak, Section 8.2][AroraBarak09]: Merlin sends his

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Tidy step machines from read machines
+If the halting test, the address and the step of a read machine are tidily computable within
+bounds on its states, then so is the step of `Turing.ReadMachine.toStepMachine`, within bounds on
+its states, which add the position of the head: the work space grows by the length of the position
+in binary, and the time by a factor of the position, to compare it with the address.
+* `Turing.ReadMachine.tidy_toStepMachine`: the simulating step machine is tidy.
+variable {γ β δ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encD : δ ↪ List Bool}
+theorem budget_comp {f : γ → β} {g : β → δ} {Tg Sg : β → ℕ}
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInO g encB encD Tg Sg) (hf : ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encB Bt Bs)
+    (hT : (fun x => Tg (f x)) ≼ Bt) (hS : (fun x => Sg (f x)) ≼ Bs) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encD Bt Bs :=
+/-- Composition with a map computed in linear time and space, within the budgets. -/
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInO g encB encD (fun b => (encB b).length) fun b => (encB b).length)
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encB Bt Bs) (hst : Bs ≼ Bt) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encD Bt Bs :=
+  budget_comp hg hf (BigOLe.trans hf.length_le hst) hf.length_le
+theorem budget_prod {f : γ → β} {g : γ → δ} (hf : ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encB Bt Bs)
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInO g encIn encD Bt Bs) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun x => (f x, g x)) encIn (encPair encB encD) Bt Bs :=
+theorem budget_ite {c : γ → Bool} {f g : γ → β}
+    (hc : ComputableTidilyInO c encIn encBool Bt Bs) (hf : ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encB Bt Bs)
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInO g encIn encB Bt Bs) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun x => if c x then f x else g x) encIn encB Bt Bs :=
+theorem budget_const (b : β) (hl : (fun x => (encIn x).length) ≼ Bs) (hst : Bs ≼ Bt) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun _ : γ => b) encIn encB Bt Bs :=
+/-- A function of finitely many values, within the budgets. -/
+theorem budget_finite {f : γ → β} [Finite β] (g : β → δ)
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encB Bt Bs) (hst : Bs ≼ Bt) :
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encD Bt Bs :=
+variable {σ : Type} {m : ReadMachine σ} {encS : σ ↪ List Bool} {T S : σ → ℕ}
+/-- The input of a step of the simulating machine. -/
+abbrev encStepIn (encS : σ ↪ List Bool) : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool ↪ List Bool :=
+/-- The length of the input of a step. -/
+abbrev inLen (encS : σ ↪ List Bool) (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : ℕ := (encStepIn encS p).length
+/-- The space budget of a step. -/
+abbrev spaceB (encS : σ ↪ List Bool) (S : σ → ℕ) (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : ℕ :=
+/-- The time budget of a step. -/
+abbrev timeB (encS : σ ↪ List Bool) (T S : σ → ℕ) (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : ℕ :=
+theorem spaceB_le_timeB (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : spaceB encS S p ≤ timeB encS T S p := by
+  have h₁ : S p.1.1 + inLen encS p ≤ (T p.1.1 + S p.1.1 + inLen encS p + 1) ^ 2 :=
+    (by omega : _ ≤ T p.1.1 + S p.1.1 + inLen encS p + 1).trans (Nat.le_self_pow (by norm_num) _)
+theorem inLen_le_spaceB (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : inLen encS p ≤ spaceB encS S p := by
+theorem inLen_le_timeB (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : inLen encS p ≤ timeB encS T S p :=
+/-- The projections of the input are within the budgets. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool => p.1.1) (encStepIn encS) encS
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool => p.1.2) (encStepIn encS) encNat
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool => p.2) (encStepIn encS)
+      (encOption encBool) (timeB encS T S) (spaceB encS S) := by
+  have h₁ := fst (encPair encS encNat) (encOption encBool)
+/-- The time of a comparison with the head position is within the time budget. -/
+theorem lt_bigOLe {u : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool → ℕ} (h : u ≼ spaceB encS S) :
+    (fun p => (p.1.2 + 1) * (u p + 1) ^ 2) ≼ timeB encS T S := by
+  have h₁ : u p + 1 ≤ (c + 1) * (T p.1.1 + S p.1.1 + inLen encS p + 1) := by
+    have := hc p; simp only [spaceB] at this; nlinarith
+/-- A square of something within the space budget is within the time budget. -/
+theorem sq_bigOLe {u : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool → ℕ} (h : u ≼ spaceB encS S) :
+    (fun p => (u p + 1) ^ 2) ≼ timeB encS T S :=
+/-- The step of the simulating machine, written with its components. -/
+def stepBy (m : ReadMachine σ) (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : (σ × ℕ) × SignType × List Bool :=
+  let b := (fun q : Bool × Bool × Option Bool => if q.1 then false else if q.2.1 then
+    q.2.2.getD false else false) (isN, e, p.2)
+  let cond := (fun q : Bool × Bool × Bool × Option Bool × Bool =>
+theorem stepBy_eq (p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool) : stepBy m p = (m.toStepMachine).step p.1 p.2 := by
+  rcases hA : m.addr q with _ | A
+          · have h₄ : pos = 0 := by simpa using h₃
+/-- The time bound of a state of the simulating machine. -/
+abbrev stateT (encS : σ ↪ List Bool) (T S : σ → ℕ) (q : σ × ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  (q.2 + 1) * (T q.1 + S q.1 + 2 * (encPair encS encNat q).length + 4) ^ 2
+/-- The space bound of a state of the simulating machine. -/
+abbrev stateS (encS : σ ↪ List Bool) (S : σ → ℕ) (q : σ × ℕ) : ℕ :=
+    inLen encS p ≤ 2 * (encPair encS encNat p.1).length + 3 := by
+  rcases a with _ | b <;> simp [inLen, encStepIn]
+/-- **The simulating step machine is tidy**, if the halting test, the address and the step of the
+read machine are tidily computable within bounds on its states. -/
+theorem tidy_toStepMachine (hhalt : ComputableTidilyInO m.halt encS encBool T S)
+    (haddr : ComputableTidilyInO m.addr encS (encOption encNat) T S)
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInO (fun p : σ × Bool => m.step p.1 p.2) (encPair encS encBool)
+      (encPair encS encBits) (fun p => T p.1) fun p => S p.1) :
+    (m.toStepMachine).Tidy (encPair encS encNat) (stateT encS T S) (stateS encS S) where
+    refine ((hhalt.comp (fst encS encNat)).mono_le (fun q => ?_) fun q => ?_)
+      have : (encPair encS encNat q).length + T q.1 ≤
+          (T q.1 + S q.1 + 2 * (encPair encS encNat q).length + 4) ^ 2 :=
+        (by omega : _ ≤ T q.1 + S q.1 + 2 * (encPair encS encNat q).length + 4).trans
+    have hst : spaceB encS S ≼ timeB encS T S := .of_le spaceB_le_timeB
+    have hin : (fun p => (encStepIn encS p).length) ≼ spaceB encS S := .of_le inLen_le_spaceB
+    obtain ⟨hq, hpos, ha⟩ := budget_proj (encS := encS) (T := T) (S := S)
+    have hT : (fun p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool => T p.1.1) ≼ timeB encS T S := .of_le fun p => by
+      have : T p.1.1 ≤ (T p.1.1 + S p.1.1 + inLen encS p + 1) ^ 2 :=
+        (by omega : _ ≤ T p.1.1 + S p.1.1 + inLen encS p + 1).trans
+    have hS : (fun p : (σ × ℕ) × Option Bool => S p.1.1) ≼ spaceB encS S := .of_le fun p => by
+    have hA := budget_comp haddr hq hT hS
+      (.of_isEmpty (encIn := encOption encNat) (f := fun o : Option ℕ => o.isNone)
+        fun o => by cases o <;> simp)) hA hst
+    have hA₁ := budget_comp natSucc hgetD (sq_bigOLe hgetD.length_le)
+      ((BigOLe.of_le fun p => by simp only [length_encPair]; nlinarith).trans
+    have hl := budget_comp natLt hpair (lt_bigOLe hpair.length_le)
+    -- the bit read and the step of the read machine
+      (fun q : Bool × Bool × Option Bool => if q.1 then false else if q.2.1
+        then q.2.2.getD false else false) (budget_prod hisN (budget_prod he ha)) hst
+    have hr := budget_comp hstep (budget_prod hq hb) hT hS
+    have hz := budget_comp_linear natIsZero hpos hst
+    have hc := budget_finite (encD := encBool) (fun q : Bool × Bool × Bool × Option Bool × Bool =>
+      (budget_prod hisN (budget_prod he (budget_prod hl (budget_prod ha hz)))) hst
+    have hres₁ := budget_prod (encB := encPair encS encNat) (budget_prod (fst' hr) hpos)
+    have hres₂ := budget_prod (encB := encPair encS encNat) (budget_prod hq
+    have hres₃ := budget_prod (encB := encPair encS encNat) (budget_prod hq
+    have hall := budget_ite hc hres₁ (budget_ite hl hres₂ hres₃)
+    refine ((hall.of_enc_eq fun p => by rw [← stepBy_eq]; rfl).mono 4 (fun p => ?_)
+      have h : T p.1.1 + S p.1.1 + inLen encS p + 1 ≤
+          T p.1.1 + S p.1.1 + 2 * (encPair encS encNat p.1).length + 4 := by omega

+Truncated subtraction `b - a` iterates the predecessor `a` times, counting in binary. It takes time
+linear in the value `a` and work space linear in the lengths of the binary encodings. The order
+`a < b` tests whether `b - a` is zero.
+theorem iterate_sub_one (k n : ℕ) : (· - 1)^[k] n = n - k := Nat.pred_iterate n k
+/-- **Truncated subtraction in binary**, `b - a` from `(a, b)`. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.2 - p.1) (encPair encNat encNat) encNat
+      fun p => (encPair encNat encNat p).length + 1 := by

+      (fun p => (encPair encNat encNat p).length) fun p => (encPair encNat encNat p).length :=

+      (fun p => (encPair encNat encNat p).length) fun p => (encPair encNat encNat p).length :=
+  have hle (p : ℕ × ℕ) (k : ℕ) : (encNat ((· - 1)^[k] p.2)).length ≤ (encNat p.2).length := by
+  have h := iterate (n := fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1) (init := fun p => p.2) (step := (· - 1))
+    hfst hsnd natPred (R := fun p => ((encNat p.2).length + 1) ^ 2)
+    (Q := fun p => (encNat p.2).length + 1) (B := fun p => (encNat p.2).length)
+    (fun p k _ => Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by have := hle p k; omega) 2)
+    (fun p k _ => by have := hle p k; omega) (fun p k _ => hle p k)
+  refine (h.mono 8 (fun p => ?_) fun p => ?_).of_enc_eq fun p => by rw [iterate_sub_one]
+    ComputableTidilyInO (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => decide (p.1 < p.2)) (encPair encNat encNat) encBool

+# Tidy computability within a space bound
+`ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encOut S` says that `f` is tidily computable within space `O(S)`,
+with values of length `O(S)`, in some time. For space-bounded algorithms only the work space
+matters, and this calculus tracks it alone: composition, pairs, conditionals and loops keep the
+work space explicit and leave the time to be whatever it is. In loops, the time of a round is the
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInSpace`: tidy computability within a space bound.
+/-- `f` is tidily computable within space `O(S a)` on the input `a`, and its encoded value has
+def ComputableTidilyInSpace {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (encIn : α ↪ List Bool)
+    (encOut : β ↪ List Bool) (S : α → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ T, ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encOut T S
+variable {α β γ δ : Type} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+  {encC : γ ↪ List Bool} {encD : δ ↪ List Bool} {S S₁ S₂ : α → ℕ}
+theorem of_inO {f : α → β} {T : α → ℕ} (h : ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encB T S) :
+theorem weaken {f : α → β} (h : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S) (hS : S ≼ S₁) :
+theorem mono_le {f : α → β} (h : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S)
+    (hS : ∀ a, S a ≤ S₁ a) : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S₁ :=
+theorem length_le {f : α → β} (h : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S) :
+theorem of_enc_eq {f : α → β} {g : α → γ} (h : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S)
+    (he : ∀ a, encC (g a) = encB (f a)) : ComputableTidilyInSpace g encIn encC S :=
+theorem of_encIn_eq {α' : Type} {encIn' : α' ↪ List Bool} {f : α → β} (e : α' → α)
+    (h : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S) (he : ∀ a, encIn' a = encIn (e a)) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun a => f (e a)) encIn' encB fun a => S (e a) :=
+theorem comp {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} {S₂ : β → ℕ} (hg : ComputableTidilyInSpace g encB encC S₂)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun a => g (f a)) encIn encC fun a => S₁ a + S₂ (f a) :=
+theorem prod {f : α → β} {g : α → γ} (hf : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S₁)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun a => (f a, g a)) encIn (encPair encB encC)
+      fun a => S₁ a + S₂ a :=
+theorem append {f₁ : α → β} {f₂ : α → γ} {g : α → δ} {encD : δ ↪ List Bool}
+    (h₁ : ComputableTidilyInSpace f₁ encIn encB S₁) (h₂ : ComputableTidilyInSpace f₂ encIn encC S₂)
+    (hg : ∀ x, encD (g x) = encB (f₁ x) ++ encC (f₂ x)) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace g encIn encD fun x => S₁ x + S₂ x :=
+theorem ite {c : α → Bool} {f g : α → β} {Sc : α → ℕ}
+    (hc : ComputableTidilyInSpace c encIn encBool Sc) (hf : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB S₁)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun a => if c a then f a else g a) encIn encB
+      fun a => Sc a + if c a then S₁ a else S₂ a :=
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun _ : α => b) encIn encB fun a => (encIn a).length :=
+theorem fst (enc₁ : β ↪ List Bool) (enc₂ : γ ↪ List Bool) :
+theorem snd (enc₁ : β ↪ List Bool) (enc₂ : γ ↪ List Bool) :
+theorem fst' {f : α → β × γ} (h : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn (encPair encB encC) S) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun a => (f a).1) encIn encB S :=
+theorem snd' {f : α → β × γ} (h : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn (encPair encB encC) S) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun a => (f a).2) encIn encC S :=
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB fun a => (encIn a).length :=
+/-- **Iterating a step a computed number of times**, within the space of the counter, of the
+initial state, of a round and of the states. -/
+theorem iterate [Inhabited β] {n : α → ℕ} {init : α → β} {step : β → β} {Sn Si Q B : α → ℕ}
+    {Ss : β → ℕ} (hn : ComputableTidilyInSpace n encIn encNat Sn)
+    (hspace : ∀ x, ∀ k ≤ n x, Ss (step^[k] (init x)) ≤ Q x)
+    (hstate : ∀ x, ∀ k ≤ n x, (encB (step^[k] (init x))).length ≤ B x) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => step^[n x] (init x)) encIn encB
+      fun x => Sn x + Si x + Q x + B x + (encNat (n x)).length := by
+    (R := fun x => listMax (fun k => Ts (step^[k] (init x))) (List.range (n x + 1)))
+    (fun x k hk => le_listMax (f := fun k => Ts (step^[k] (init x)))
+/-- **Left folds**, within the space of the list, of the initial state, of a round and of the
+theorem foldl {encA : δ ↪ List Bool} {encL : List δ ↪ List Bool} [ListEncoding encA encL]
+    [SizedListEncoding encA encL] {list : α → List δ} {init : α → β} {step : β → δ → β}
+    {Sl Si Q B : α → ℕ} {Ss : β × δ → ℕ}
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : β × δ => step p.1 p.2) (encPair encB encA) encB Ss)
+      Ss (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x), (list x)[i]) ≤ Q x)
+      (encB (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x))).length ≤ B x) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => (list x).foldl step (init x)) encIn encB
+      fun x => Sl x + Si x + Q x + B x + (encL (list x)).length := by
+    (R := fun x => listMax (fun i => ((list x)[i]?).elim 0 fun a =>
+      Ts (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x), a)) (List.range (list x).length))
+      have := le_listMax (f := fun i => ((list x)[i]?).elim 0 fun a =>
+        Ts (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x), a)) (List.mem_range.mpr hi)
+      simpa [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi] using this) hspace hstate⟩
