+# Basic functions within linear work space
+Arithmetic on binary naturals and operations on lists, tidily computable within work space linear
+in the lengths of their encoded arguments, for `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInSpace`.
+Combinators keep a computation within a fixed space budget.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInSpace.getD`: the element of a list at an index.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInSpace.set`: replacing the element at an index.
+variable {α β γ δ : Type} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+theorem budget_comp {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} {Sg : β → ℕ}
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInSpace g encB encC Sg) (hf : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB Bs)
+    (hS : (fun x => Sg (f x)) ≼ Bs) : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encC Bs :=
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInSpace g encB encC fun b => (encB b).length)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encC Bs :=
+/-- A multiple of the length of the argument, plus a constant, is linear in it. -/
+theorem linear_mul (k : ℕ) : (fun b => k * ((encB b).length + 1)) ≼ fun b => (encB b).length :=
+theorem linear_succ : (fun b => (encB b).length + 1) ≼ fun b => (encB b).length :=
+/-- **Composition with a function computed in space linear in its argument**: no side condition,
+as the argument is computed within the budget. -/
+theorem budget_comp_lin {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} {Sg : β → ℕ}
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInSpace g encB encC Sg) (hSg : Sg ≼ fun b => (encB b).length)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encC Bs :=
+theorem budget_prod {f : α → β} {g : α → γ} (hf : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB Bs)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => (f x, g x)) encIn (encPair encB encC) Bs :=
+theorem budget_ite {c : α → Bool} {f g : α → β} (hc : ComputableTidilyInSpace c encIn encBool Bs)
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encB Bs) (hg : ComputableTidilyInSpace g encIn encB Bs) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => if c x then f x else g x) encIn encB Bs :=
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun _ : α => b) encIn encB Bs :=
+theorem budget_finite {f : α → β} [Finite β] (g : β → γ)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encC Bs :=
+/-- **Iterating a step computed in linear space**, a computed number of times, within a budget
+theorem budget_iterate [Inhabited β] {n : α → ℕ} {init : α → β} {step : β → β} {B : α → ℕ}
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInSpace step encB encB fun b => (encB b).length)
+    (hstate : ∀ x, ∀ k ≤ n x, (encB (step^[k] (init x))).length ≤ B x) (hB : B ≼ Bs) :
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun x => step^[n x] (init x)) encIn encB Bs :=
+theorem natSucc : ComputableTidilyInSpace (· + 1) encNat encNat fun n => (encNat n).length + 1 :=
+theorem natPred : ComputableTidilyInSpace (· - 1) encNat encNat fun n => (encNat n).length + 1 :=
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun n => decide (n = 0)) encNat encBool fun n => (encNat n).length :=
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => decide (p.1 = p.2)) (encPair encNat encNat) encBool
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => decide (p.1 < p.2)) (encPair encNat encNat) encBool
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.2 - p.1) (encPair encNat encNat) encNat
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 + p.2) (encPair encNat encNat) encNat
+/-- A step of division: subtract the divisor from the remainder and count, while it fits. -/
+def divStep (s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
+    ∀ k, divStep^[k] (d, 0, r) = (d, min k (r / d), r - d * min k (r / d)) := by
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos d with rfl | hd
+    | succ k ih => simp [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, divStep]
+      · have h₁ : (k + 1) * d ≤ r := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hd).mp hk
+        have h₂ : d ≤ r - d * k := by rw [Nat.add_mul, one_mul] at h₁; rw [Nat.mul_comm]; omega
+        rw [Nat.min_eq_left hk.le, Nat.min_eq_left (show k + 1 ≤ r / d by omega)]
+        simp only [hd, h₂, and_self, ↓reduceIte, Prod.mk.injEq, true_and]
+      · have h₁ : r - d * (r / d) < d := by
+        rw [Nat.min_eq_right (show r / d ≤ k by omega),
+          Nat.min_eq_right (show r / d ≤ k + 1 by omega)]
+        simp only [hd, true_and, show ¬d ≤ r - d * (r / d) by omega, ↓reduceIte]
+theorem iterate_divStep_self (d r : ℕ) : divStep^[r] (d, 0, r) = (d, r / d, r % d) := by
+  have : r / d ≤ r := Nat.div_le_self r d
+/-- The encoding of triples of naturals. -/
+abbrev encNat3 : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ ↪ List Bool := encPair encNat (encPair encNat encNat)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace divStep encNat3 encNat3 fun s => (encNat3 s).length + 1 := by
+  have hl : (fun s => (encNat3 s).length) ≼ fun s => (encNat3 s).length + 1 := .of_le fun _ => by
+  have h₁ : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => s.1) encNat3 encNat
+  have h₂₂ : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => s.2) encNat3 (encPair encNat encNat)
+  have hlt := budget_comp natLt (budget_prod h₃ h₁) (.of_le_linear 2 2 fun s => by
+  have hc := budget_finite (encC := encBool) (fun q : Bool × Bool => !q.1 && !q.2)
+  have hsucc := budget_comp natSucc h₂ (.of_le_linear 2 2 fun s => by
+  have hsub := budget_comp natSub (budget_prod h₁ h₃) (.of_le_linear 2 2 fun s => by
+  have hnew := budget_prod h₁ (budget_prod hsucc hsub)
+  · simp [h, h.1.ne', show ¬s.2.2 < s.1 by omega]
+  · rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos s.1 with h0 | h0
+    · simp [h, h0.ne', show s.2.2 < s.1 by omega]
+/-- **The quotient and the remainder**, `(r / d, r % d)` from `(r, d)`. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (p.1 / p.2, p.1 % p.2)) (encPair encNat encNat)
+      (encPair encNat encNat) fun p => 16 * ((encPair encNat encNat p).length + 1) := by
+  have hinit : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (p.2, 0, p.1)) (encPair encNat encNat)
+      encNat3 fun p => 2 * ((encPair encNat encNat p).length + 1) :=
+  have hlen (p : ℕ × ℕ) (k : ℕ) : (encNat3 (divStep^[k] (p.2, 0, p.1))).length ≤
+    have h₁ := ComputableTidilyInO.length_encNat_mono (show min k (p.1 / p.2) ≤ p.1 from
+      (show p.1 - p.2 * min k (p.1 / p.2) ≤ p.1 from Nat.sub_le _ _)
+  have h := iterate (n := fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1) (fst _ _) hinit divStep_inSpace
+    (fun p k _ => by have := hlen p k; omega) (fun p k _ => hlen p k)
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 / p.2) (encPair encNat encNat) encNat
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 % p.2) (encPair encNat encNat) encNat
+/-- Adding the first component to the second. -/
+def addStep (q : ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ := (q.1, q.2 + q.1)
+theorem iterate_addStep (k x a : ℕ) : addStep^[k] (x, a) = (x, a + k * x) := by
+  | succ k ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, addStep, ih]; congr 1; ring
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 * p.2) (encPair encNat encNat) encNat
+      fun p => 32 * ((encPair encNat encNat p).length + 1) := by
+  have hstep : ComputableTidilyInSpace addStep (encPair encNat encNat) (encPair encNat encNat)
+      fun q => 4 * ((encPair encNat encNat q).length + 1) := by
+    have hl : (fun q => (encPair encNat encNat q).length) ≼
+        fun q => 4 * ((encPair encNat encNat q).length + 1) := .of_le fun _ => by omega
+    have h := budget_prod ((fst encNat encNat).weaken hl)
+        ((fst encNat encNat).weaken hl)) (.of_le_linear 2 2 fun q => by
+  have hinit : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (p.1, 0)) (encPair encNat encNat)
+      (encPair encNat encNat) fun p => 2 * ((encPair encNat encNat p).length + 1) :=
+  have hlen (p : ℕ × ℕ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ p.2) :
+  have h := iterate (n := fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.2) (snd _ _) hinit hstep
+    (fun p k hk => by have := hlen p k hk; omega) hlen
+/-- **The element at an index**, `l.getD i 0` from `(l, i)`. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1.getD p.2 0)
+      fun p => 8 * ((encPair (encList encNat) encNat p).length + 1) := by
+  have htail : ComputableTidilyInSpace List.tail (encList encNat) (encList encNat)
+      fun l => (encList encNat l).length := of_inO (.of_linear (ListEncoding.tail encNat))
+  have hlen (p : List ℕ × ℕ) (k : ℕ) :
+    rw [List.tail_iterate, ← p.1.take_append_drop k, encList_append, List.length_append]; simp
+  have h := iterate (n := fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.2) (snd _ _) (fst _ _) htail
+    (Q := fun p => (encList encNat p.1).length) (B := fun p => (encList encNat p.1).length)
+    (fun p k _ => hlen p k) (fun p k _ => hlen p k)
+  have hhead : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun l : List ℕ => l.headD 0) (encList encNat) encNat
+  refine (budget_comp_linear hhead h).mono_le (fun p => ?_) |>.of_enc_eq fun p => ?_
+/-- A step of rebuilding a list with the element at `i` replaced by `v`. -/
+def setStep (s : (ℕ × ℕ) × ℕ × List ℕ) (a : ℕ) : (ℕ × ℕ) × ℕ × List ℕ :=
+theorem foldl_setStep (i v : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) (j : ℕ) (acc : List ℕ) :
+      ((i, v), j + l.length, acc ++ l.mapIdx fun k a => if j + k = i then v else a) := by
+  induction l generalizing j acc with
+    have hf : (fun k b => if j + 1 + k = i then v else b) =
+        (fun k b => if j + (k + 1) = i then v else b) := by
+      funext k b; rw [show j + 1 + k = j + (k + 1) by omega]
+    l.set i v = l.mapIdx fun k a => if k = i then v else a := by
+  refine List.ext_getElem (by simp) fun k h₁ h₂ => ?_
+  split_ifs with h₃ h₄ h₄ <;> first | rfl | omega
+    · simp only [List.set_cons_succ, length_encList, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons] at ih ⊢
+/-- The encoding of the states of `setStep`. -/
+abbrev encSetState : (ℕ × ℕ) × ℕ × List ℕ ↪ List Bool :=
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun q : ((ℕ × ℕ) × ℕ × List ℕ) × ℕ => setStep q.1 q.2)
+      fun q => 4 * ((encPair encSetState encNat q).length + 1) := by
+  have hl : (fun q => (encPair encSetState encNat q).length) ≼
+      fun q => 4 * ((encPair encSetState encNat q).length + 1) := .of_le fun _ => by omega
+  have he := budget_comp natEq (budget_prod hj hi) (.of_le_linear 2 2 fun q => by
+  have hel := budget_ite he hv ha
+  have hsnoc : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1 ++ [p.2])
+  have happ := budget_comp_linear hsnoc (budget_prod hacc hel)
+  have hsucc := budget_comp natSucc hj (.of_le_linear 2 2 fun q => by
+  refine (budget_prod hiv (budget_prod hsucc happ)).of_enc_eq fun q => ?_
+/-- **Replacing the element at an index**, `l.set i v` from `(l, i, v)`. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => p.1.set p.2.1 p.2.2)
+      fun p => 128 * ((encPair (encList encNat) (encPair encNat encNat) p).length + 1) := by
+  have hinit : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => ((p.2.1, p.2.2), 0, []))
+      fun p => 4 * ((encPair (encList encNat) (encPair encNat encNat) p).length + 1) := by
+    have hl : (fun p => (encPair (encList encNat) (encPair encNat encNat) p).length) ≼
+        fun p => 4 * ((encPair (encList encNat) (encPair encNat encNat) p).length + 1) :=
+    have h₂ := (snd (encList encNat) (encPair encNat encNat)).weaken hl
+  have hstate (p : List ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ p.1.length) :
+    simp only [zero_add, List.nil_append, List.length_take, Nat.min_eq_left hk]
+    have hset : (p.1.take k).mapIdx (fun k a => if k = p.2.1 then p.2.2 else a) =
+    have h₁ := length_encList_set_le (p.1.take k) p.2.1 p.2.2
+    have h₂ := length_encList_take_le encNat p.1 k
+  have hmem (p : List ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < p.1.length) :
+  have h := foldl (list := fun p : List ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => p.1) (step := setStep)
+    (Q := fun p => 4 * (12 * ((encPair (encList encNat) (encPair encNat encNat) p).length + 1) +
+    (B := fun p => 6 * ((encPair (encList encNat) (encPair encNat encNat) p).length + 1))
+      have h₁ := hstate p i hi.le
+      have h₂ := hmem p i hi
+    (fun p i hi => hstate p i hi)
+    (fun q : ε × List ε => (q.1, q.1 :: q.2))^[k] (a, l) = (a, List.replicate k a ++ l) := by
+  | succ k ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, List.replicate_succ]; rfl
+/-- **A list of copies**, `List.replicate n a` from `(n, a)`; its work space is that of the list. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ε => List.replicate p.1 p.2) (encPair encNat enc)
+      (encList enc) fun p => 64 * ((p.1 + 1) * ((encPair encNat enc p).length + 1)) := by
+  have hcons : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun q : ε × List ε => (q.1, q.1 :: q.2))
+      fun q => 2 * ((encPair enc (encList enc) q).length + 1) := by
+    have hl : (fun q => (encPair enc (encList enc) q).length) ≼
+        fun q => 2 * ((encPair enc (encList enc) q).length + 1) := .of_le fun _ => by omega
+    have hc : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun q : ε × List ε => q.1 :: q.2)
+        (encPair enc (encList enc)) (encList enc) fun q => (encPair enc (encList enc) q).length :=
+  have hinit : ComputableTidilyInSpace (fun p : ℕ × ε => (p.2, ([] : List ε)))
+  have hlen (p : ℕ × ε) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ p.1) :
+      (encPair enc (encList enc) ((fun q : ε × List ε => (q.1, q.1 :: q.2))^[k] (p.2, []))).length
+  have h := iterate (n := fun p : ℕ × ε => p.1) (fst _ _) hinit hcons
+    (fun p k hk => by have := hlen p k hk; omega) hlen
+  refine (snd' h).mono_le (fun p => ?_) |>.of_enc_eq fun p => by
+  have h₁ : (encPair encNat enc p).length ≤ (p.1 + 1) * ((encPair encNat enc p).length + 1) := by
+  have h₂ : (encNat p.1).length ≤ (encPair encNat enc p).length := by
+  have h₃ : 1 ≤ (p.1 + 1) * ((encPair encNat enc p).length + 1) := Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr

+# Encodings of the states of the Tree Evaluation read machine
+The states of `Cslib.TreeEval.Reader.machine` are encoded as tuples: the value length, the height
+and the prime in binary, the registers as lists of binary naturals, the stack as a list of frames,
+each a binary round with finitely many other fields, the mode as a finite tag, and the control state
+as a tag with two binary naturals and a list of them.
+def Frame.equiv : Frame ≃ ℕ × Fin 4 × Bool × Fin 3 where
+  left_inv m := by cases m <;> rfl
+  right_inv o := by rcases o with _ | ⟨_, _⟩ <;> rfl
+noncomputable def encMode : Mode ↪ List Bool := encFinite Mode
+/-- The control state as a tuple: a tag, two naturals and a list. -/
+def Ctl.toTuple : Ctl → Fin 7 × ℕ × ℕ × List ℕ
+/-- The encoding of tuples of control states. -/
+noncomputable abbrev encCtlTuple : Fin 7 × ℕ × ℕ × List ℕ ↪ List Bool :=
+abbrev Tuple := ((ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) × Regs) × (List Frame × Mode) × (Fin 7 × ℕ × ℕ × List ℕ)
+  rintro ⟨e, h, p, R, st, m, c⟩ ⟨e', h', p', R', st', m', c'⟩ hs
+  obtain ⟨⟨⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, rfl⟩, ⟨rfl, rfl⟩, hc⟩ := hs
+/-- The encoding of tuples of states. -/
+@[simp] theorem encState_apply (s : State) : encState s = encTuple s.toTuple := rfl
+@[simp] theorem encCtl_apply (c : Ctl) : encCtl c = encCtlTuple c.toTuple := rfl

+# Sums of low-degree polynomials over the units of a finite field
+Let `K` be a finite field with `q` elements. A polynomial of degree less than `q - 1` sums to zero
+over `K`, so its sum over the units `Kˣ` is minus its value at `0`. Restricting a multivariate
+polynomial to the line `u ↦ u • τ + x` turns this into the identity that removes the masks `τ`
+from masked evaluations of a low-degree polynomial: the sum over all units `u` of
+This is the algebraic core of the Cook–Mertz Tree Evaluation algorithm, there phrased with powers
+of a primitive root of unity of order `q - 1`, which run through the units.

+* [O. Goldreich, *On the Cook–Mertz Tree Evaluation procedure*][Goldreich2024TreeEval],
+/-- A polynomial of degree less than `q - 1` sums to zero over the field. -/

+polynomial of degree at most the total degree. -/
+theorem natDegree_eval₂_line_le {ι : Type*} (p : MvPolynomial ι K) (τ x : ι → K) :
+    (p.eval₂ C fun i => C (τ i) * X + C (x i)).natDegree ≤ p.totalDegree := by

+/-- **Unmasking low-degree polynomials.** If `p` has total degree less than `q - 1`, then summing

+theorem sum_units_eval_mul_add [DecidableEq K] {ι : Type*} {p : MvPolynomial ι K}

+and does not claim a nondeterministic counting-machine characterization.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+We use the constant-error, power-of-two characterization of AWPP from
+[Fenner][Fenner2003]: a GapP function divided by `2 ^ p(n)` lies in `[2/3, 1]` on
+members and `[0, 1/3]` on nonmembers. Integer inequalities avoid division and rounding.
+The counting functions are verifier-based; a nondeterministic counting-machine
+characterization, arbitrary error reduction and PP-lowness are not proved here.
+* `AWPP`: bounded-error GapP ratios with a length-dependent dyadic denominator.
+* [S. Fenner, *PP-Lowness and a Simple Definition of AWPP*][Fenner2003]
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- A GapP ratio in `[0, 1]`, at least `2/3` on members and at most `1/3` otherwise. -/
+def AWPP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ g ∈ GapP enc, ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ a,
+    (0 ≤ g a ∧ g a ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length) ∧
+    (a ∈ A → 2 * (2 : ℤ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤ 3 * g a) ∧
+    (a ∉ A → 3 * g a ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length)}
+/-- Acceptance counts are GapP functions, so bounded-error computation gives an AWPP ratio. -/

+  have hf : (fun a => acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length)) ∈ SharpP enc :=
+  refine ⟨_, SharpP.natCast_mem_GapP hf, p, fun a => ⟨⟨by positivity, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
+    have : 3 * acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) ≤ 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length := by
+/-- The characteristic GapP function has denominator one. -/

+  rcases hr a with h | h <;> simp [hA a, h]
+/-- Subtracting the gap from its dyadic denominator exchanges yes and no instances. -/

+  refine ⟨_, GapP.sub_mem' hd hg, p, fun a => ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨⟨h0, h1⟩, hy, hn⟩ := hA a
+  change (0 ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length - g a ∧ _) ∧ _
+/-- The sign of twice the gap minus the denominator recognizes the language in PP. -/
+theorem AWPP_subset_PP : AWPP enc ⊆ PP enc := by
+  have hd : (fun a => (2 : ℤ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length) ∈ GapP enc := by
+    ⟨_, GapP.sub_mem' (GapP.add_mem hg hg) hd, fun a => ?_⟩
+  have hp : 0 < (2 : ℤ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length := by positivity

+/-- An efficiently computed unary exponent can be padded to a polynomial in input length.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+SBP was introduced by [Böhler, Glaßer and Meister][BoehlerGlasserMeister2006]. We use
+[Watson, Definition 2][Watson2012]: a #P count is at least a binary FP threshold on
+members and strictly less than half the threshold on nonmembers. The threshold may
+be zero; `mem_SBP_iff_exists_pos_threshold` shows that requiring positivity is equivalent.
+These are verifier counts, without a proved nondeterministic counting-machine equivalence.
+The containments and union closure below are elementary counting-algebra consequences;
+the stronger MA and AM containments are not proved here.
+* `SBP`: small bounded-error polynomial time with an input-dependent FP threshold.
+* [E. Böhler, C. Glaßer, D. Meister, *Error-bounded probabilistic computations between
+variable {α β : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A B : Set α}
+/-- A #P count at least an FP threshold on members and strictly below half on nonmembers.
+The threshold is encoded in binary and may be exponentially large. -/
+def SBP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ f ∈ SharpP enc, ∃ k : α → ℕ, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encNat ∧
+    ∀ a, (a ∈ A → k a ≤ f a) ∧ (a ∉ A → 2 * f a < k a)}
+/-- Replacing `(f, k)` by `(2f + 1, 2k + 1)` makes the threshold positive. -/
+    ∃ f ∈ SharpP enc, ∃ k : α → ℕ, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encNat ∧
+      (∀ a, 0 < k a) ∧ ∀ a, (a ∈ A → k a ≤ f a) ∧ (a ∉ A → 2 * f a < k a) := by
+    refine ⟨f + f + 1, SharpP.add_mem (SharpP.add_mem hf hf) SharpP.one_mem,
+      fun a => k a + k a + 1, (hk.binary_add' hk).binary_add' (.const 1),
+      fun a => by positivity, fun a => ?_⟩
+/-- Threshold one recognizes precisely the positive #P counts. -/
+theorem NP_subset_SBP : NP enc ⊆ SBP enc := by
+/-- Amplifying BPP to error at most one quarter leaves a strict factor-two count gap. -/
+theorem BPP_subset_SBP : BPP enc ⊆ SBP enc := by
+  have hf : (fun a => acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length)) ∈ SharpP enc :=
+  have hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length) enc encNat :=
+  have hp : 0 < 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length := by positivity
+  change (a ∈ A → _ ≤ 3 * acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length)) ∧ _
+/-- The integer gap `2f - k + 1` is positive exactly on members, including zero thresholds. -/
+theorem SBP_subset_PP : SBP enc ⊆ PP enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨f, hf, k, hk, hA⟩
+  refine mem_PP_iff_exists_GapP.mpr ⟨_, GapP.add_mem hg GapP.one_mem, fun a => ?_⟩
+  change a ∈ A ↔ 0 < ((f a + f a : ℕ) : ℤ) - (k a : ℤ) + 1
+/-- Precomposition preserves both the count and the binary FP threshold. -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_SBP {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {B : Set β}
+    (h : PolyTimeReducible enc encB A B) (hB : B ∈ SBP encB) : A ∈ SBP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, k, hk, hB⟩ := hB
+  exact ⟨f ∘ r, SharpP.comp_mem hf hr, k ∘ r, hk.comp hr, fun a => by
+    simpa only [Function.comp_apply, ← hAB a] using hB (r a)⟩
+/-- Normalize two positive thresholds by cross multiplication, then square and add the counts. -/
+theorem union_mem_SBP (hA : A ∈ SBP enc) (hB : B ∈ SBP enc) : A ∪ B ∈ SBP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, k, hk, hkpos, hA⟩ := mem_SBP_iff_exists_pos_threshold.mp hA
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, l, hl, hlpos, hB⟩ := mem_SBP_iff_exists_pos_threshold.mp hB
+    fun a => (k a * l a) ^ 2, (hk.binary_mul' hl).binary_pow' (.const 2), fun a => ?_⟩
+  change (a ∈ A ∪ B → (k a * l a) ^ 2 ≤ (f a * l a) ^ 2 + (g a * k a) ^ 2) ∧
+    have haA : a ∉ A := fun h => ha (Or.inl h)
+    have haB : a ∉ B := fun h => ha (Or.inr h)
+    have h1 := Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right ((hA a).2 haA) (hlpos a)
+    have h2 := Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right ((hB a).2 haB) (hkpos a)
+    have h1' : 2 * (f a * l a) < k a * l a := by nlinarith
+    have h2' : 2 * (g a * k a) < k a * l a := by nlinarith

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Binary-encoded natural outputs of polynomial-time functions are in #P; binary-encoded integer
+outputs are in GapP [Fortnow, Theorem 3.5][Fortnow1997]. The verifier guesses a fixed-width
+binary word and accepts just those representing values below the computed output. The witness
+width bounds the binary output length, not its potentially exponential numeric value.
+* `SharpP.of_polyTime`: polynomial-time binary natural functions are in #P.
+* `GapP.of_polyTime`: polynomial-time binary integer functions are in GapP.
+/-- A polynomial-time function with binary natural output is a #P function. -/
+theorem SharpP.of_polyTime {f : α → ℕ} (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc encNat) :
+  let p : Polynomial ℕ := Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d
+  refine ⟨p, fun x => decide (BitString.binaryValue x.2 < f x.1), ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+    have hsize : (f a).size ≤ p.eval (enc a).length := by
+      simpa [p, encNat_apply, Nat.size_eq_bits_len] using hb a
+/-- A polynomial-time function with binary integer output is a GapP function. -/
+theorem GapP.of_polyTime {f : α → ℤ} (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc encIntBin) :
+  exact ⟨_, hp, _, hn, fun a => by simp only [Function.comp_apply]; lia⟩

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+WPP allows a GapP function to take either zero or a nonzero polynomial-time computable integer
+target; LWPP restricts that target to depend on input length. We follow
+[Hemaspaandra et al., Definitions 2.4–2.5][HemaspaandraEtAl2018], crediting the original
+`encIntBin`; the length argument of LWPP uses unary `encUnary`, so an exponentially large
+numeric target is permitted. These are verifier-based counting classes, without a proved
+nondeterministic-machine characterization. The basic containments and Boolean closures below
+are algebraic consequences; oracle lowness and robustness are not claimed.
+* `LWPP`: a nonzero FP target depending only on encoded input length.
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]
+* [E. Hemaspaandra et al., *The Robustness of LWPP and WPP, with an Application to Graph
+variable {α β : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A B : Set α}
+/-- Wide gaps: zero on nonmembers and a nonzero binary FP target on members. -/
+def WPP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ g ∈ GapP enc, ∃ f : α → ℤ, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc encIntBin ∧
+    (∀ a, f a ≠ 0) ∧ (∀ a, g a = 0 ∨ g a = f a) ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ g a = f a}
+/-- Wide gaps with a target computed in polynomial time from unary input length. -/
+def LWPP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ g ∈ GapP enc, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encUnary encIntBin ∧
+    (∀ n, f n ≠ 0) ∧ (∀ a, g a = 0 ∨ g a = f (enc a).length) ∧
+    ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ g a = f (enc a).length}
+/-- The constant target one witnesses the SPP containment. -/
+theorem SPP_subset_LWPP : SPP enc ⊆ LWPP enc := by
+  exact ⟨g, hg, fun _ => 1, .const _, fun _ => one_ne_zero, hr, hA⟩
+/-- Computing the encoded input length turns an LWPP target into a WPP target. -/
+theorem LWPP_subset_WPP : LWPP enc ⊆ WPP enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨g, hg, f, hf, hn, hr, hA⟩
+  exact ⟨g, hg, fun a => f (enc a).length,
+    hf.comp (.encoding_length enc), fun a => hn _, hr, hA⟩
+/-- Subtraction of the target gives a zero test for WPP membership. -/
+theorem WPP_subset_CeqP : WPP enc ⊆ CeqP enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨g, hg, f, hf, -, -, hA⟩
+  exact ⟨g - f, GapP.sub_mem' hg (GapP.of_polyTime hf), fun a => by
+/-- A WPP gap is nonzero exactly on members. -/
+theorem WPP_subset_coCeqP : WPP enc ⊆ coCeqP enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨g, hg, f, -, hn, hr, hA⟩
+  rcases hr a with h | h <;> simp [h, hn a, (hn a).symm]
+/-- Complement exchanges the zero and target values. -/
+theorem compl_mem_WPP (hA : A ∈ WPP enc) : Aᶜ ∈ WPP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, f, hf, hn, hr, hA⟩ := hA
+  refine ⟨f - g, GapP.sub_mem' (GapP.of_polyTime hf) hg, f, hf, hn,
+  · rcases hr a with h | h <;> simp [h]
+  · rcases hr a with h | h <;> simp [hA a, h, (hn a).symm]
+/-- Products preserve the zero-or-target condition and the target is still nonzero. -/
+theorem inter_mem_WPP (hA : A ∈ WPP enc) (hB : B ∈ WPP enc) : A ∩ B ∈ WPP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, f, hf, hn, hr, hA⟩ := hA
+  obtain ⟨g', hg', f', hf', hn', hr', hB⟩ := hB
+  refine ⟨g * g', GapP.mul_mem hg hg', f * f', hf.intBin_mul' hf',
+    fun a => mul_ne_zero (hn a) (hn' a), fun a => ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+  · rcases hr a with h | h <;> rcases hr' a with h' | h' <;> simp [h, h']
+  · rcases hr a with h | h <;> rcases hr' a with h' | h' <;>
+      simp [hA a, hB a, h, h', hn a, hn' a, (hn a).symm, (hn' a).symm]
+/-- Union follows by De Morgan's law. -/

+`FewP` allows a polynomial number of accepting certificates on each input, extending the one-witness
+condition of `UP`; see [Allender and Rubinstein][AllenderRubinstein1988] and the explicit
+This file uses exact-length verifier counts. It does not prove equivalence with a nondeterministic
+machine whose number of accepting paths is polynomially bounded.
+The containments and closures below are elementary consequences of the definition and the
+existing `SharpP` algebra: addition adds the ambiguity bounds, multiplication multiplies them,
+and polynomial-time precomposition composes a bound with a polynomially bounded output length.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.FewP`: NP with polynomially bounded accepting counts.
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A B : Set α}
+/-- A language in NP with a polynomial bound on the number of accepting certificates on every
+input. The bound is in the encoded input length, not in the certificate length. -/
+def FewP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ f ∈ SharpP enc, ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ,
+    (∀ a, f a ≤ p.eval (enc a).length) ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ 0 < f a}
+/-- A verifier characterization with a separate polynomial bound on its accepting count. -/
+theorem mem_FewP : A ∈ FewP enc ↔ ∃ (p q : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+    (∀ a, acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) ≤ q.eval (enc a).length) ∧
+    ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ 0 < acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) := by
+  · rintro ⟨f, ⟨p, V, hV, hf⟩, q, hle, hA⟩
+    exact ⟨p, q, V, hV, fun a => hf a ▸ hle a, fun a => by rw [hA a, hf a]⟩
+  · rintro ⟨p, q, V, hV, hle, hA⟩
+    exact ⟨_, ⟨p, V, hV, fun _ => rfl⟩, q, hle, hA⟩
+/-- A bound of one is a polynomial ambiguity bound. -/
+theorem UP_subset_FewP : UP enc ⊆ FewP enc := by
+  refine ⟨f, hf, 1, by simpa using hle, fun a => ?_⟩
+/-- Forgetting the ambiguity bound gives NP membership. -/
+theorem FewP_subset_NP : FewP enc ⊆ NP enc := by
+/-- Union adds the two polynomial ambiguity bounds. -/
+theorem union_mem_FewP (hA : A ∈ FewP enc) (hB : B ∈ FewP enc) : A ∪ B ∈ FewP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, p, hp, hA⟩ := hA
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, q, hq, hB⟩ := hB
+  exact ⟨f + g, SharpP.add_mem hf hg, p + q,
+    fun a => by simpa using Nat.add_le_add (hp a) (hq a), fun a => by simp [hA a, hB a]⟩
+/-- Intersection multiplies the two polynomial ambiguity bounds. -/
+theorem inter_mem_FewP (hA : A ∈ FewP enc) (hB : B ∈ FewP enc) : A ∩ B ∈ FewP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, p, hp, hA⟩ := hA
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, q, hq, hB⟩ := hB
+  exact ⟨f * g, SharpP.mul_mem hf hg, p * q,
+    fun a => by simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul (hp a) (hq a), fun a => by simp [hA a, hB a]⟩
+/-- Polynomial-time reductions preserve a polynomial ambiguity bound. -/

+    (h : PolyTimeReducible enc encB A B) (hB : B ∈ FewP encB) : A ∈ FewP enc := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, p, hp, hB⟩ := hB
+  have hlen : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (encB (g a)).length) enc encUnary :=
+  exact ⟨f ∘ g, SharpP.comp_mem hf hg, Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d,
+    fun a => (hp (g a)).trans (by simpa using hle a), fun a => (hAB a).trans (hB (g a))⟩

+variable {α β γ : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A B : Set α}
+/-- The class of languages expressible as the intersection of an NP and a coNP language. -/

+/-- DP membership and hardness under polynomial-time many-one reductions. -/

+/-- DP is exactly the differences of two NP languages. -/

+    exact ⟨B, hB, Cᶜ, hC, by simp⟩
+    exact ⟨B, hB, Cᶜ, by simpa [mem_coNP] using hC, rfl⟩

+A PCP verifier (`Cslib.Complexity.PCPVerifier`) that uses no random bits reads the same positions
+of the proof on every run, and soundness forces it to reject every proof of a non-member. The
+classes with zero randomness are therefore classes of deterministic verification
+* With no queries either, the verdict depends on the instance alone, so `PCP(0, 0) = P`
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.PCP_zero_zero`). Since more randomness and more queries give larger classes,
+* With polynomially many queries, the verifier can read a whole `NP` certificate, so
+  verifier using no random bits uses at most logarithmically many, so `PCP(0, q) ⊆ NP` for every
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- **`PCP(0, 0) = P`**: a verifier with no random bits and no queries decides by its verdict on
+theorem PCP_zero_zero : PCP (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) enc = P enc := by
+  · rintro ⟨V, c, d, ⟨-, -, hv⟩, hcoins, hqs, hcomp, hsound⟩
+    simp only [mul_zero, nonpos_iff_eq_zero] at hcoins hqs
+    · exact hv.comp (g := fun a : α => ((a, ([] : List Bool)), ([] : List Bool))) (by fun_prop)
+    · -- with no random bits there are no queries, so the verdict ignores the proof
+      have key (π : List Bool) : V.Accepts a π [] = V.verdict ((a, []), []) := by
+      have hfa : f a = false := by simpa [hA a] using ha
+theorem P_subset_PCP (r q : ℕ → ℕ) : P enc ⊆ PCP r q enc :=
+/-- **`NP ⊆ PCP(0, poly)`**: with no random bits, the verifier queries the first `p(n)` positions
+of the proof, where `n` is the length of the encoded instance and `p(n)` the length of the
+certificates, and runs the `NP` verifier on the bits read. -/
+theorem exists_mem_PCP_zero_of_mem_NP {A : Set α} (hA : A ∈ NP enc) :
+    ∃ k : ℕ, A ∈ PCP (fun _ => 0) (fun n => (n + 1) ^ k) enc := by

+    have hrej : V (a, PCPVerifier.answers π (List.range (p.eval (enc a).length))) = false := by
+/-- **`NP = PCP(0, poly)`**: a problem is in `NP` exactly when it has a polynomial-time PCP

+# Characterisations and closure properties of PP
+`PP` (`Cslib.Complexity.PP`) is defined by a strict majority of accepted random strings
+[Gill][Gill1977]. This file proves that a non-strict majority defines the same class, that `PP`
+is closed under polynomial-time reductions, and the characterisations of `PP` through `#P` and
+* **Non-strict majority.** A verifier decides `A` by strict majority exactly when its negation
+  decides the complement `Aᶜ` by non-strict majority
+  under complement (`Cslib.Complexity.compl_mem_PP`), the two majority conditions give the same
+* **Reductions.** For a reduction `f` from `A` to `B` and a verifier `W` for `B` reading `q(m)`
+  random bits on an instance of length `m`, the verifier for `A` runs `W` on `f a` and the first
+  `q (|f a|)` random bits. Since `|f a|` is polynomial in `|a|`, the random string is padded to a
+  polynomial `r(|a|)`; the ignored bits multiply the counts on both sides of the majority
+  condition by the same power of two.
+* **`#P`.** `A ∈ PP` exactly when `a ∈ A ↔ 2 ^ q(n) < 2 f(a)` for some `f ∈ #P` and some
+  polynomial `q`, not necessarily the length of the certificates counted by `f`, where `n` is the
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.mem_PP_iff_exists_SharpP`). For `f` counting the certificates of length
+  `k = p(n)` that `V` accepts and `j = q(n)`, the verifier on random strings of length
+  `k + j + 2` lets the first bit choose: on `true` it accepts the `2 f(a)` strings formed by a
+  certificate accepted by `V`, a free bit, and `j` bits `false`; on `false` it accepts the
+  `2 ^ (k + j + 1) - 2 ^ j` strings whose first `k + 1` bits are not all `false`. More than half
+  of the strings are accepted exactly when `2 ^ j < 2 f(a)`.
+* **`GapP`.** `A ∈ PP` exactly when `A = {a | 0 < g a}` for some `g ∈ GapP`
+* [J. Gill, *Computational complexity of probabilistic Turing machines*][Gill1977]
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- `V` decides `A` by non-strict majority, using random strings whose length is `p` evaluated at
+the length of the encoded instance: `a ∈ A` exactly when at least half of the random strings `r`
+def DecidesByNonstrictMajority (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (A : Set α) : Prop :=
+  ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤ 2 * acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length)
+/-- A verifier decides `A` by strict majority exactly when its negation decides `Aᶜ` by
+    {V : α × List Bool → Bool} {A : Set α} :
+    DecidesByMajority enc p V A ↔ DecidesByNonstrictMajority enc p (fun x => !V x) Aᶜ := by
+  have h := acceptCount_add_acceptCount_not V a (p.eval (enc a).length)
+      ¬2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length < 2 * acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) := by
+/-- **Non-strict majority defines `PP`**: a problem is in `PP` exactly when a polynomial-time
+verifier accepts the members of the problem, and only them, on at least half of the random
+    A ∈ PP enc ↔ ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+        DecidesByNonstrictMajority enc p V A := by
+    obtain ⟨p, V, hV, h⟩ := compl_mem_PP hA
+    refine ⟨p, fun x => !V x, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bool_not.comp hV, ?_⟩
+    have h' : DecidesByMajority enc p (fun x => !V x) Aᶜ := by
+    simpa using compl_mem_PP ⟨p, _, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bool_not.comp hV, h'⟩
+/-- **`PP` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** The verifier runs the verifier for the
+target problem on the reduced instance; the random string is padded to a polynomial in the length
+of the encoded instance, and the ignored bits multiply both sides of the majority condition by
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PP {β : Type} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α} {B : Set β}
+    (h : PolyTimeReducible enc encB A B) (hB : B ∈ PP encB) : A ∈ PP enc := by
+  have hlen : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => q.eval (encB (f a)).length) enc encUnary :=
+    andVerifier (fun a => q.eval (encB (f a)).length) (fun x => W (f x.1, x.2)) fun _ => true,
+  rw [hAB a, hWB (f a), hj, acceptCount_andVerifier_true, pow_add, ← mul_assoc]
+/-- **`PP` through `#P`**: a problem is in `PP` exactly when, for a function `f` in `#P` and a
+polynomial `q`, its members are the instances `a` with `2 ^ q(n) < 2 f(a)`, where `n` is the
+length of the encoded instance. The polynomial `q` need not be the length of the certificates
+    A ∈ PP enc ↔ ∃ f ∈ SharpP enc, ∃ q : Polynomial ℕ,
+      ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ 2 ^ q.eval (enc a).length < 2 * f a := by
+    exact ⟨_, ⟨p, V, hV, fun _ => rfl⟩, p, h⟩
+  · rintro ⟨f, ⟨p, V, hV, hf⟩, q, h⟩
+    -- on `false`, accept unless the first `k + 1` bits are `false`; on `true`, accept a
+    -- certificate of `V` followed by a free bit and bits `false`
+          (selectVerifier allFalseVerifier allFalseVerifier)), by fun_prop, fun a => ?_⟩
+        p.eval (enc a).length + q.eval (enc a).length + 1 + 1 := by simp
+    have e₀ := acceptCount_andVerifier_true (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length + 1) allFalseVerifier
+    have e₁ := acceptCount_andVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V
+    rw [acceptCount_selectVerifier, acceptCount_allFalseVerifier, ← hf a] at e₁
+        p.eval (enc a).length + 1 + q.eval (enc a).length by omega, e₀,
+        p.eval (enc a).length + (q.eval (enc a).length + 1) by omega, e₁]
+/-- **`PP` through `GapP`** [Fenner, Fortnow and Kurtz][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]: a problem is in
+`PP` exactly when its members are the instances where some function in `GapP` is positive. -/
+    A ∈ PP enc ↔ ∃ g ∈ GapP enc, ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ 0 < g a := by
+    have hf : (fun a => acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length)) ∈ SharpP enc :=
+        acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length : ℕ) : ℤ),
+      ⟨_, SharpP.add_mem hf hf, _, SharpP.two_pow_mem p, fun a => rfl⟩, fun a => ?_⟩
+  · rintro ⟨g, ⟨f₁, hf₁, f₂, hf₂, hg⟩, h⟩
+    refine mem_PP_iff_exists_SharpP.2 ⟨_, SharpP.add_mem hf₁ hsub, p + 1, fun a => ?_⟩
+    rw [h a, hg a, Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_one, pow_succ, Pi.add_apply]

+# Closure properties of RP, coRP and ZPP
+`RP` (`Cslib.Complexity.RP`) is closed under union and intersection, and so are `coRP` and
+`ZPP = RP ∩ coRP` [Arora and Barak, Section 7.3][AroraBarak09]. Both constructions run one-sided
+error deciders for the two problems on disjoint parts of the random string.
+* **Union.** Accept when either decider accepts (`Cslib.Complexity.orVerifier`). On a member of
+  one of the problems, its decider rejects at most half of its random strings, so the combined
+  decider rejects at most half of all random strings
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.acceptCount_orVerifier`); on a non-member of both, neither decider accepts.
+* **Intersection.** Accept when both deciders accept (`Cslib.Complexity.andVerifier`). Error
+  reduction makes each decider reject at most a quarter of the random strings on a member, so
+  the combined decider accepts at least `(3 / 4) ^ 2 ≥ 1 / 2` of them on a common member
+  (`Cslib.Complexity.acceptCount_andVerifier`); on a non-member of either, one of them rejects.
+A decider ignoring an empty random string shows `P ⊆ RP`; with closure of `P` under complement
+(`Cslib.Complexity.compl_mem_P`), `P ⊆ coRP` and `P ⊆ ZPP`. Since `RP ⊆ NP`, `ZPP ⊆ NP ∩ coNP`.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- **`P ⊆ RP`**: a decider is a one-sided-error decider ignoring its random string, of
+theorem P_subset_RP : P enc ⊆ RP enc := by
+  refine ⟨0, fun x => f x.1, hf.comp (.fst enc encBits), fun a => ⟨fun ha => ?_, fun ha r => ?_⟩⟩
+theorem P_subset_coRP : P enc ⊆ coRP enc := fun _ hA => P_subset_RP (compl_mem_P hA)
+theorem P_subset_ZPP : P enc ⊆ ZPP enc := fun _ hA => by
+theorem ZPP_subset_NP_inter_coNP : ZPP enc ⊆ NP enc ∩ coNP enc := fun _ hA =>
+/-- **`RP` is closed under union**: accept when the decider for either problem accepts, on
+theorem union_mem_RP {A B : Set α} (hA : A ∈ RP enc) (hB : B ∈ RP enc) : A ∪ B ∈ RP enc := by
+  refine ⟨p₁ + p₂, orVerifier (fun a => p₁.eval (enc a).length) V₁ V₂, by fun_prop,
+    fun a => ⟨fun ha => ?_, fun ha r => ?_⟩⟩
+    have hc := acceptCount_orVerifier (fun a => p₁.eval (enc a).length) V₁ V₂ a k₂
+    have n₁ := acceptCount_add_acceptCount_not V₁ a k₁
+    have n₂ := acceptCount_add_acceptCount_not V₂ a k₂
+    -- the rejected strings make up at most half of all strings
+    have hprod : 2 * (acceptCount (fun x => !V₁ x) a k₁ * acceptCount (fun x => !V₂ x) a k₂) ≤
+      · have h : 2 ^ k₁ ≤ 2 * acceptCount V₁ a k₁ := hk₁ ▸ (h₁ a).1 ha
+      · have h : 2 ^ k₂ ≤ 2 * acceptCount V₂ a k₂ := hk₂ ▸ (h₂ a).1 ha
+    refine ⟨Bool.not_eq_true _ ▸ fun hc => ha.1 ((h₁.isVerifier a).2 ⟨_, ?_, hc⟩),
+      Bool.not_eq_true _ ▸ fun hc => ha.2 ((h₂.isVerifier a).2 ⟨_, ?_, hc⟩)⟩ <;>
+/-- **`RP` is closed under intersection**: reduce the error of both deciders to `1 / 4`, and
+accept when both accept, on disjoint parts of the random string. -/
+theorem inter_mem_RP {A B : Set α} (hA : A ∈ RP enc) (hB : B ∈ RP enc) : A ∩ B ∈ RP enc := by
+  refine ⟨p₁ + p₂, andVerifier (fun a => p₁.eval (enc a).length) V₁ V₂, by fun_prop,
+    fun a => ⟨fun ha => ?_, fun ha r => ?_⟩⟩
+    -- each decider accepts at least three quarters of its random strings
+    have f₁ : 3 * 2 ^ p₁.eval (enc a).length ≤ 4 * acceptCount V₁ a (p₁.eval (enc a).length) := by
+    have f₂ : 3 * 2 ^ p₂.eval (enc a).length ≤ 4 * acceptCount V₂ a (p₂.eval (enc a).length) := by
+  · have hA' := (h₁.decidesWithOneSidedError fun _ => by simp).isVerifier a
+    have hB' := (h₂.decidesWithOneSidedError fun _ => by simp).isVerifier a
+theorem union_mem_coRP {A B : Set α} (hA : A ∈ coRP enc) (hB : B ∈ coRP enc) :
+theorem inter_mem_coRP {A B : Set α} (hA : A ∈ coRP enc) (hB : B ∈ coRP enc) :
+theorem union_mem_ZPP {A B : Set α} (hA : A ∈ ZPP enc) (hB : B ∈ ZPP enc) : A ∪ B ∈ ZPP enc := by
+  exact ⟨union_mem_RP hA.1 hB.1, union_mem_coRP hA.2 hB.2⟩
+theorem inter_mem_ZPP {A B : Set α} (hA : A ∈ ZPP enc) (hB : B ∈ ZPP enc) : A ∩ B ∈ ZPP enc := by
+  exact ⟨inter_mem_RP hA.1 hB.1, inter_mem_coRP hA.2 hB.2⟩

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The counting classes `#P`, `PP`, `RP` and `BPP` are all defined through polynomial-time functions
+`V : α × List Bool → Bool` that read an instance and a string of bits, and through the number
+`Cslib.Complexity.acceptCount V a n` of strings of length `n` that `V` accepts together with `a`.
+This file provides verifiers built from other verifiers, each with its polynomial-time rule
+(registered with `fun_prop`) and the number of strings it accepts.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.andVerifier k V₁ V₂` runs `V₁` on the first `k a` bits and `V₂` on the rest,
+  and accepts when both accept. The number of strings it accepts is the product of the numbers
+  that `V₁` and `V₂` accept (`Cslib.Complexity.acceptCount_andVerifier`). With `V₂` the verifier
+  accepting only the string of `false`s (`Cslib.Complexity.allFalseVerifier`), it pads the strings
+  of `V₁` without changing their number; with `V₂` accepting everything, it multiplies the count by
+* `Cslib.Complexity.orVerifier k V₁ V₂` accepts when either accepts; the rejected strings multiply
+* `Cslib.Complexity.selectVerifier V₀ V₁` lets the first bit choose between `V₀` and `V₁` on the
+Running two verifiers on disjoint parts of the random string is the usual way to combine
+independent random choices [Arora and Barak, Chapters 7 and 17][AroraBarak09].
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The verifier accepting, with every instance, exactly the strings of `false`s. -/
+def allFalseVerifier (x : α × List Bool) : Bool := !x.2.any fun b => b
+/-- `allFalseVerifier` accepts one string of each length. -/
+theorem acceptCount_allFalseVerifier (a : α) (n : ℕ) : acceptCount allFalseVerifier a n = 1 :=
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime allFalseVerifier (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+/-! ### Conjunction on disjoint parts of the string -/
+/-- Run `V₁` on the first `k a` bits and `V₂` on the remaining bits, and accept when both
+def andVerifier (k : α → ℕ) (V₁ V₂ : α × List Bool → Bool) (x : α × List Bool) : Bool :=
+  V₁ (x.1, x.2.take (k x.1)) && V₂ (x.1, x.2.drop (k x.1))
+/-- **Independent runs multiply**: on strings of length `k a + n`, `andVerifier k V₁ V₂` accepts
+the product of the numbers of strings that `V₁` and `V₂` accept. -/
+theorem acceptCount_andVerifier (k : α → ℕ) (V₁ V₂ : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    acceptCount (andVerifier k V₁ V₂) a (k a + n) =
+      acceptCount V₁ a (k a) * acceptCount V₂ a n := by
+    fun u w => V₁ (a, u) = true ∧ V₂ (a, w) = true
+  by_cases hu : V₁ (a, List.ofFn u) = true <;> simp [hu]
+/-- **Padding**: forcing the bits after the first `k a` to be `false` does not change the number
+theorem acceptCount_andVerifier_allFalseVerifier (k : α → ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α)
+    acceptCount (andVerifier k V allFalseVerifier) a (k a + n) = acceptCount V a (k a) := by
+/-- Ignoring the bits after the first `k a` multiplies the number of accepted strings by a power
+theorem acceptCount_andVerifier_true (k : α → ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    acceptCount (andVerifier k V fun _ => true) a (k a + n) = acceptCount V a (k a) * 2 ^ n := by
+/-- `andVerifier k V₁ V₂` is polynomial-time when `k` (in unary), `V₁` and `V₂` are. -/
+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_andVerifier {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {k : α → ℕ}
+    {V₁ V₂ : α × List Bool → Bool} (hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encUnary)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (andVerifier k V₁ V₂) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+/-! ### Disjunction on disjoint parts of the string -/
+/-- Run `V₁` on the first `k a` bits and `V₂` on the remaining bits, and accept when either
+def orVerifier (k : α → ℕ) (V₁ V₂ : α × List Bool → Bool) (x : α × List Bool) : Bool :=
+  V₁ (x.1, x.2.take (k x.1)) || V₂ (x.1, x.2.drop (k x.1))
+/-- **Independent rejections multiply**: on strings of length `k a + n`, `orVerifier k V₁ V₂`
+rejects the product of the numbers of strings that `V₁` and `V₂` reject. -/
+theorem acceptCount_orVerifier (k : α → ℕ) (V₁ V₂ : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    acceptCount (orVerifier k V₁ V₂) a (k a + n) +
+        acceptCount (fun x => !V₁ x) a (k a) * acceptCount (fun x => !V₂ x) a n =
+  have h : acceptCount (andVerifier k (fun x => !V₁ x) fun x => !V₂ x) a (k a + n) =
+      acceptCount (fun x => !orVerifier k V₁ V₂ x) a (k a + n) :=
+    acceptCount_congr (fun _ => by simp only [andVerifier, orVerifier, Bool.not_or]) _
+/-- `orVerifier k V₁ V₂` is polynomial-time when `k` (in unary), `V₁` and `V₂` are. -/
+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_orVerifier {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {k : α → ℕ}
+    {V₁ V₂ : α × List Bool → Bool} (hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k enc encUnary)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (orVerifier k V₁ V₂) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+/-- Run `V₀` on the remaining bits when the first bit is `false`, and `V₁` when it is `true`. -/
+def selectVerifier (V₀ V₁ : α × List Bool → Bool) (x : α × List Bool) : Bool :=
+  if x.2.headD false then V₁ (x.1, x.2.tail) else V₀ (x.1, x.2.tail)
+/-- **Choices add**: on strings of length `n + 1`, `selectVerifier V₀ V₁` accepts the sum of the
+numbers of strings of length `n` that `V₀` and `V₁` accept. -/
+theorem acceptCount_selectVerifier (V₀ V₁ : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    acceptCount (selectVerifier V₀ V₁) a (n + 1) = acceptCount V₀ a n + acceptCount V₁ a n := by
+  rw [acceptCount, BitString.card_filter_ofFn_succ _ fun l => selectVerifier V₀ V₁ (a, l) = true,
+  simp only [selectVerifier, List.headD_cons, List.tail_cons, ite_true, Bool.false_eq_true,
+/-- `selectVerifier V₀ V₁` is polynomial-time when `V₀` and `V₁` are. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (selectVerifier V₀ V₁) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by

+# 3SAT with clauses of exactly three literals
+`ExactThreeSAT` is the set of satisfiable formulas in conjunctive normal form all of whose clauses
+are lists of exactly three literals. The literals of a clause need not be distinct, so a clause
+`x ∨ x ∨ y` is allowed. This is weaker than 3-satisfiability as defined by Garey and Johnson
+[Garey and Johnson, Problem LO2][GareyJohnson1979], whose clauses are sets of three distinct
+literals; `NP`-completeness of that version, where short clauses are padded with fresh variables,
+`ExactThreeSAT` is `NP`-complete: `ThreeSAT` (clauses of at most three literals) reduces to it by
+repeating a literal of every clause with one or two literals
+not change the value of a clause, and the empty clause stays empty, so a formula with an empty
+* `Cslib.Complexity.toExactThreeSAT`: the reduction from `ThreeSAT`, padding every clause.
+* [M. R. Garey, D. S. Johnson, *Computers and Intractability*][GareyJohnson1979]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The satisfiable formulas all of whose clauses have exactly three literals, not necessarily
+def ExactThreeSAT : Set (CNF ℕ) := {φ | (∀ c ∈ φ, c.length = 3) ∧ φ.Satisfiable}
+/-- Pad a clause of one or two literals to three literals by repeating literals; other clauses are
+  if c.length = 1 then c ++ c ++ c
+  else if c.length = 2 then c ++ [c.headD (0, true)] else c
+/-- Padding a clause neither adds nor removes literals. -/
+theorem mem_padClause (c : Clause ℕ) (l : Literal ℕ) : l ∈ padClause c ↔ l ∈ c := by
+/-- Padding a clause does not shorten it. -/
+theorem length_le_length_padClause (c : Clause ℕ) : c.length ≤ (padClause c).length := by
+/-- Padding a nonempty clause of at most three literals gives exactly three. -/
+/-- Repeating literals does not change the value of a clause. -/
+    Clause.eval σ (padClause c) = Clause.eval σ c := by
+/-- The verifier for `ExactThreeSAT`: check that every clause has exactly three literals and
+evaluate the formula under the certificate assignment. -/
+def verifier (x : CNF ℕ × List Bool) : Bool :=
+/-- `ExactThreeSAT.verifier` verifies `ExactThreeSAT` with certificates as long as the encoded
+formula: it is `SAT.verifier` guarded by the clause-width test. -/
+theorem isVerifier : IsVerifier encCNF Polynomial.X verifier ExactThreeSAT := by
+  have h : ExactThreeSAT = {φ | (φ.all fun c => c.length == 3) = true ∧ φ ∈ SAT} := by
+    simp only [ExactThreeSAT, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, List.all_eq_true, beq_iff_eq, mem_SAT]
+/-- Checking the clause widths and evaluating the formula is polynomial-time. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime verifier (encPair encCNF encBits) encBool := by
+/-- The reduction from `ThreeSAT` to `ExactThreeSAT`: pad every clause. -/
+def toExactThreeSAT (φ : CNF ℕ) : CNF ℕ := φ.map padClause
+/-- A formula is in `ThreeSAT` exactly when padding its clauses puts it in `ExactThreeSAT`. -/
+    toExactThreeSAT φ ∈ ExactThreeSAT ↔ φ ∈ ThreeSAT := by
+  have heval (σ : ℕ → Bool) : CNF.eval σ (toExactThreeSAT φ) = CNF.eval σ φ := by
+    simp only [toExactThreeSAT, CNF.eval, List.all_map, Function.comp_def, eval_padClause]
+    refine ⟨fun c hc => ?_, σ, by rw [← heval]; exact hσ⟩
+    refine ⟨fun c' hc' => ?_, σ, by rw [heval]; exact hσ⟩
+/-- `ThreeSAT` reduces to `ExactThreeSAT` in polynomial time via `toExactThreeSAT`. -/
+/-- **3SAT with clauses of exactly three, not necessarily distinct, literals is NP-complete.** -/

+universal method is at most a constant worse than it. -/
+theorem exists_complexity_universal_le_length_add {g : List Bool → ℕ} (hg : Computable g) :

+A counting argument proves that good edge labelings exist. If `0 < r`, `120 ≤ k * k` and
+`k ^ 16 < r ^ 104`, the bad labelings for sixteen vertices are fewer than all `r ^ (k * k)`
+labelings, and any labeling avoiding them is good. Specializing to `k = 2 * M ^ 2 + 1` gives a good
+labeling of the regular cyclic tournament with `Nat.ceil (Real.sqrt M)` labels for every `M ≥ 3`.

+* `goodLabeling_exists`: every tournament on `2 * M ^ 2 + 1` vertices has a good labeling with `r`

+* `GoodLabeling.good_on_subset`: the goodness property for target maps defined only on the

+`m : Fin k → Fin r` there is an edge `v i → v j` of `T` with `A (v i, v j) ≠ m (v j)`. -/
+private theorem labeled_edge_of_not_bad {n : ℕ} (A : (Fin k × Fin k) → Fin r)
+    (hA : A ∉ T.badLabelings n r) (v : Fin n → Fin k)
+    (hv : Function.Injective v) (m : Fin k → Fin r) :
+    ∃ i j : Fin n, T.Adj (v i) (v j) ∧ A (v i, v j) ≠ m (v j) := by
+  have hc : ∀ i j, T.Adj (v i) (v j) → A (v i, v j) = m (v j) := fun i j ha =>
+    not_not.mp fun h => hn ⟨i, j, ha, h⟩
+/-- If `0 < r`, `120 ≤ k * k` and `k ^ 16 < r ^ 104`, then `T` admits a good labeling with `r`
+    (hkr : k ^ 16 < r ^ 104) : Nonempty (GoodLabeling T r) := by
+  have htotal : k ^ 16 * r ^ 16 * r ^ (k * k-120) < r ^ (k * k) := by
+      _ = r ^ (k * k) := congrArg (fun e : ℕ => r ^ e) (by omega)
+      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin k × Fin k) → Fin r)).card := by
+  let v : Fin 16 → Fin k := fun i => (e i).val
+  have hv : Function.Injective v := Subtype.val_injective.comp e.injective
+  obtain ⟨i, j, ha, hne⟩ := T.labeled_edge_of_not_bad A hA v hv m
+  exact ⟨v i, (e i).property, v j, (e j).property, ha, hne⟩
+/-- If `3 ≤ M` and `M ≤ r ^ 2`, then every tournament on `2 * M ^ 2 + 1` vertices admits a good

+/-- Goodness for targets defined on the subset: for every `I` with `I.card = 16` and every

+Real arithmetic turning the seed bounds into ratio bounds. A nonconstant function with sensitivity
+at most `2 * (d + 2) * M ^ (d + 1)` and block sensitivity at least `M ^ 2 * (2 * M ^ 2 + 1) ^ d` at
+the all-false input has `bs / s ^ 2` at least `2 ^ d / (4 * (d + 2) ^ 2)`, a quantity tending to
+infinity with `d`. At depth nine this bound equals `128 / 121 > 1`, giving the strict quadratic gap
+`(22 * M ^ 10) ^ 2 < M ^ 2 * (2 * M ^ 2 + 1) ^ 9` used for amplification.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A `Projection N N' L L' ι` interprets numeric vocabulary `N'` using only numeric vocabulary `N`,
+and each output relation of `L'` by a projection formula over `N` and the input vocabulary `L`.
+The domain is numeric as well: input bits affect neither the output universe nor numeric tests.
+This is a relativized, vocabulary-parametric extension of first-order projections
+[Immerman and Landau, Definitions 3.3--3.6][ImmermanLandau1995]. Classical projections additionally
+universe and preserve the canonical numeric predicates. Neither those restrictions nor a
+logarithmic-space encoding theorem are implicit here. The target vocabularies are relational,
+as required by `Interpretation`; numeric constants can instead be represented by unary predicates.
+* `Projection`: a numeric interpretation and a projection formula for each output relation.
+* `Projection.toInterpretation`: the ordinary interpretation on the sum vocabularies.
+* `Projection.inputStructure`: the output input-relation structure on the numeric model.
+* `Projection.onFormula`: pull back a projection formula to a projection formula.
+* `Projection.modelEquiv`: agreement with the ordinary interpretation of sum vocabularies.
+* `Projection.compEquiv`: composition agrees with successive interpretations of both vocabularies.
+* [N. Immerman and S. Landau, *The Complexity of Iterated Multiplication*][ImmermanLandau1995]
+universe u v u' v' u'' v'' w
+/-- A relativized projection between two numeric/input vocabulary pairs. Numeric predicates and
+the output domain are interpreted without access to the input relations. -/
+structure Projection (N N' L L' : Language) (ι : Type*) where
+  /-- Interpret the output numeric structure and domain using numeric formulas alone. -/
+  /-- Each output input-relation bit is a numeric choice of a constant or input literal. -/
+  rel : ∀ {n : ℕ}, L'.Relations n → ProjectionFormula N L (Fin n × ι)
+variable {N N' N'' L L' L'' : Language} {ι κ α : Type*}
+/-- Forget the projection restriction, retaining an ordinary interpretation. -/
+def toInterpretation (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) :
+/-- The output input-relation structure. It is supplied explicitly so that it does not compete
+with the numeric structure instance on the same universe. -/
+def inputStructure (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) (M : Type*)
+  RelMap R x := (I.rel R).toFormula.Realize fun p => (x p.1).1 p.2
+/-- The numeric model with projected input relations agrees with the ordinary interpretation
+of the sum vocabularies. This connects projection semantics to the existing interpretation API. -/
+    (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) (M : Type*) [N.Structure M] [L.Structure M] :
+    I.numeric.Model M ≃[N'.sum L'] I.toInterpretation.Model M := by
+        | inl R => exact LHom.realize_onFormula LHom.sumInl (I.numeric.rel R)
+/-- Pull back one literal, substituting a projection for its relation and preserving polarity. -/
+def onLiteral (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) :
+    InputLiteral L' α → ProjectionFormula N L (α × ι)
+    let p := (I.rel R).relabel fun q => (args q.1, q.2)
+    if neg then p.not else p
+/-- Pull back a projection formula. Numeric tests use the ordinary numeric interpretation;
+    (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) (p : ProjectionFormula N' L' α) :
+/-- Projection pullback is truth preserving on the interpreted numeric universe, equipped with
+the input relations specified by the projection. -/
+    (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) {M : Type*} [N.Structure M] [L.Structure M]
+    (p : ProjectionFormula N' L' α) (x : α → I.numeric.Model M) :
+    (I.onFormula p).toFormula.Realize (fun q => (x q.1).1 q.2) ↔ p.toFormula.Realize x := by
+  · exact fun g => I.numeric.realize_onFormula g x
+/-- The identity projection, with one coordinate and unchanged numeric and input relations. -/
+protected def id (N L : Language) : Projection N N L L Unit where
+/-- The identity projection preserves both numeric and input relations. -/
+    (Projection.id N L).numeric.Model M ≃[N.sum L] M := by
+      map_rel' R x := by cases R <;> rfl }
+/-- Compose projections, including their numeric interpretations. The output coordinate type is
+the product of the two coordinate types. -/
+    (J : Projection N' N'' L' L'' κ) (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) :
+    Projection N N'' L L'' (κ × ι) where
+/-- A composite projection is isomorphic to successive interpretation, preserving both numeric
+and input relations. The underlying equivalence is the existing numeric composition map. -/
+    (J : Projection N' N'' L' L'' κ) (I : Projection N N' L L' ι)
+    J.numeric.Model (I.numeric.Model M) ≃[N''.sum L''] (J.comp I).numeric.Model M := by
+        | inl R => exact (Interpretation.compEquiv J.numeric I.numeric).map_rel' R x
+          exact I.realize_onFormula (J.rel R) (fun p => (x p.1).1 p.2) }
+/-- A quantifier-free relativized projection has a quantifier-free numeric interpretation and
+quantifier-free numeric guards in every input-relation definition. A classical qfp further
+restricts the numeric vocabulary and its interpretation; in particular the convention of
+structure IsQF (I : Projection N N' L L' ι) : Prop where
+  /-- The numeric domain and relation definitions are quantifier-free. -/
+  /-- The numeric guards in each output input-relation definition are quantifier-free. -/
+theorem IsQF.toInterpretation {I : Projection N N' L L' ι} (hI : I.IsQF) :
+theorem IsQF.onLiteral {I : Projection N N' L L' ι} (hI : I.IsQF)
+theorem IsQF.onFormula [Finite ι] [N'.IsRelational] {I : Projection N N' L L' ι}
+    (hI : I.IsQF) {p : ProjectionFormula N' L' α} (hp : p.IsQF) : (I.onFormula p).IsQF :=
+/-- Quantifier-free relativized projections compose. Requiring both numeric interpretations to
+be quantifier-free prevents the substitution from introducing quantified numeric tests. -/
+    {J : Projection N' N'' L' L'' κ} {I : Projection N N' L L' ι}

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A projection chooses a constant or one signed input-relation bit using only numeric information.
+`ProjectionFormula N L α` separates the numeric language `N` from the input language `L`.
+Its internal nodes test formulas of `N`; its leaves are constants or input literals. Consequently
+neither the choice of input bit nor its polarity can depend on input-relation values.
+The syntax is a decision-tree presentation of the mutually exclusive numeric cases in the
+definition of first-order projections [Immerman and Landau, Definition 3.6][ImmermanLandau1995].
+quantifier-free interpretations with arbitrary Boolean combinations of input relations are not
+projections. The numeric vocabulary is a parameter: no interpretation of order or BIT, or
+machine resource bound, is implicit in this definition.

+* `ProjectionFormula`: numeric tests with input literals at the leaves.
+* `ProjectionFormula.toFormula`: the ordinary formula over the sum of the two languages.
+* `ProjectionFormula.select`: the literal selected by the numeric structure alone.
+* `ProjectionFormula.realize_toFormula`: realization is that of the selected literal.
+* `ProjectionFormula.exists_literal`: one selected literal works for all input structures.

+  /-- A constant or a single signed input bit. -/

+  | branch (guard : N.Formula α) (yes no : ProjectionFormula N L α)
+variable {N : Language.{u, v}} {L : Language.{u', v'}} {α β M : Type*}

+    ProjectionFormula N L α → InputLiteral L α

+/-- The output of a projection is exactly one literal selected without inspecting the input

+choice precedes the input structure: the selected literal cannot depend on input bits. -/
+theorem exists_literal [N.Structure M] (p : ProjectionFormula N L α) (x : α → M) :
+    ∃ l : InputLiteral L α, ∀ (_ : L.Structure M),

+/-- Rename every free variable in numeric tests and input literals. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Circuits for maps commuting with sparse counter modifications
+If an injective word map `h` commutes with a map `f` differing from the binary counter at `r`
+inputs, then `h` has a native De Morgan circuit of at most `100 * (n + 1) * (r + 1)` gates.
+The displacement `h x - x` changes at at most `2 * r` counter edges. A telescoping sum of
+threshold corrections reconstructs it; comparisons, selectors, additions and constants are
+all charged. In particular the bound holds for every signed fixed power of a permutation.
+These are nonuniform existence results. The correction table is chosen from the whole map;
+no efficient table-construction algorithm is asserted. A change of coordinates additionally
+requires circuits for both directions, whose sizes are charged explicitly.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.thresholdSum`: a sum of corrections at passed thresholds.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.sparse_counter_power`: the bound for every integer power.
+  [S. Schlesinger, *Square-root circuit bounds for iterated functions*]
+/-- Add the corrections whose thresholds precede the input word. -/
+def thresholdSum (S : Finset ℕ) (coeff : ℕ → BitVec w) (base x : BitVec w) : BitVec w :=
+  base + ∑ i ∈ S, if (BitVec.ofNat w i).ult x then coeff i else 0
+/-- Each threshold uses one comparison, one word selector, and one shared-carry addition. -/
+theorem synthesis_thresholdSum (S : Finset ℕ) (coeff : ℕ → BitVec w) (base : BitVec w)
+    (s : Set (BitString n → Bool)) (a : BitString n → BitVec w)
+    (ha : ∀ i : Fin w, (fun x => (a x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ s)
+    (hc : ∀ b : Bool, (fun _ : BitString n => b) ∈ s) :
+      (wordWires fun x => thresholdSum S coeff base (a x)) (S.card * (21 * w + 3)) := by
+    let previous := fun x => thresholdSum S coeff base (a x)
+    let flag := fun x => (BitVec.ofNat w j).ult (a x)
+    have ht := Synthesis.word_ult (s := src) (fun _ => BitVec.ofNat w j) a
+    let term := fun x => if flag x then coeff j else 0
+    have hm := Synthesis.word_mux (s := src1) (fun _ => coeff j) (fun _ => (0 : BitVec w)) flag
+    have hadd := Synthesis.word_add (s := src2) previous term
+      (fun i => Or.inl (Or.inl (Or.inr ⟨i, rfl⟩))) (fun i => Or.inr ⟨i, rfl⟩)
+        previous x + term x = thresholdSum (insert j S) coeff base (a x) := by
+      simp only [previous, term, flag, thresholdSum, Finset.sum_insert hj]
+/-- Word displacement relative to the counter coordinates. -/
+def displacement (h : BitVec n → BitVec n) (x : BitVec n) : BitVec n := h x - x
+/-- Changes of displacement, including the wraparound edge. -/
+def displacementCuts (h : BitVec n → BitVec n) : Finset ℕ :=
+    displacement h (BitVec.ofNat n (i + 1)) ≠ displacement h (BitVec.ofNat n i)
+theorem displacement_change_iff (h : BitVec n → BitVec n) (x : BitVec n) :
+    displacement h (x + 1) ≠ displacement h x ↔ h (x + 1) ≠ h x + 1 := by
+/-- The sparse derivative reconstructs the entire word function by telescoping. -/
+theorem thresholdSum_displacement (h : BitVec n → BitVec n) (x : BitVec n) :
+        displacement h (BitVec.ofNat n i)) (displacement h 0) x = displacement h x := by
+  let d := fun i => displacement h (BitVec.ofNat n i)
+      if (BitVec.ofNat n i).ult x then d (i + 1) - d i else 0) =
+      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range x.toNat, (d (i + 1) - d i) := by
+          if (BitVec.ofNat n i).ult x then d (i + 1) - d i else 0 := by
+        have he : d (i + 1) = d i := by
+          simpa only [displacementCuts, Finset.mem_filter, hi, true_and, not_not, d] using hn
+      _ = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range x.toNat, (d (i + 1) - d i) := by
+              if (BitVec.ofNat n i).ult x then d (i + 1) - d i else 0 := by
+            have hn' : ¬ i < x.toNat := by simpa using hn
+/-- Counter-coordinate changes inject into the commutation-defect set. -/
+theorem displacementCuts_card (f h : BitVec n → BitVec n)
+    disagreement (h ∘ (fun x => x + 1)) ((fun x => x + 1) ∘ h)) ?_ ?_).trans
+      (commutation_defect_card f (fun x => x + 1) h hc hi)
+  · intro i hi j hj he
+    simpa only [BitVec.toNat_ofNat, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hi', Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hj'] using he'
+/-- A sparse derivative gives an actual native Boolean circuit, including all selection gates. -/
+      out.Computes Boolean.interpretation (fun x i => (h (word x)).getLsbD i.val) ∧
+  let constants : Set (BitString n → Bool) := {fun _ => false, fun _ => true}
+  have hc (v : Bool) : (fun _ : BitString n => v) ∈ src := by
+  have hw (i : Fin n) : (fun x : BitString n => (word x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ src := by
+    simpa only [getLsbD_word] using (show (fun x : BitString n => x i) ∈ src from Or.inl ⟨i, rfl⟩)
+      displacement h (BitVec.ofNat n i)) (displacement h 0) src word hw hc
+  have hadd := Synthesis.word_add (s := src ∪ wordWires (fun x => displacement h (word x)))
+    word (fun x => displacement h (word x)) (fun i => Or.inl (hw i))
+  have he (x : BitString n) : word x + displacement h (word x) = h (word x) := by
+  have hconst : Synthesis Boolean.interpretation (inputs n) constants 2 :=
+  exact ⟨out, hout, by simpa only [Nat.add_assoc] using ho⟩
+/-- Every injective map commuting with an `r`-edited counter has size `O(n(r+1))`.
+No transition circuit or state-space enumeration is a hypothesis. -/
+theorem sparse_counter_centralizer (f h : BitVec n → BitVec n)
+      out.Computes Boolean.interpretation (fun x i => (h (word x)).getLsbD i.val) ∧
+  have hb := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (21 * n + 3) (displacementCuts_card f h hc hi)
+/-- The bound applies uniformly to all signed fixed powers of a permutation. -/
+      out.Computes Boolean.interpretation (fun x i => ((f ^ T) (word x)).getLsbD i.val) ∧
+  exact congrArg (fun p : Equiv.Perm (BitVec n) => p x) (Commute.zpow_self f T).eq
+/-- Cheap orbit coordinates transfer the sparse bound, charging both conversion circuits. -/
+    (he : encode.Computes Boolean.interpretation (fun x i => (e (word x)).getLsbD i.val))
+    (hd : decode.Computes Boolean.interpretation (fun x i => (e.symm (word x)).getLsbD i.val))
+      out.Computes Boolean.interpretation (fun x i => ((f ^ T) (word x)).getLsbD i.val) ∧
+      out.size ≤ encode.size + decode.size + 100 * (n + 1) * ((disagreement f g).card + 1) := by
+  have hcounter : e ∘ g ∘ e.symm = fun x => x + 1 := by
+  have hr := disagreement_conjugate_card (f : BitVec n → BitVec n)
+  obtain ⟨middle, hm, hs⟩ := sparse_counter_power (e.permCongrHom f) T
+  have hp : (e.permCongrHom f) ^ T = e.permCongrHom (f ^ T) := (map_zpow _ _ _).symm
+    rw [Circuit.eval_comp, Circuit.eval_comp, he x, hm, hd]
+      ((disagreement (e ∘ f ∘ e.symm) (fun x => x + 1)).card + 1) at hs

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The oracle classes of `Cslib.Complexity.PWithOracle` query languages. The values of a function
+`f : β → ℕ` are queried bit by bit: the *code* `encPair encβ encNat (b, i)` asks for bit `i` of
+`f b`, under an encoding `encβ` of the arguments of `f`. An oracle language *answers the bits*
+of `f` (`Cslib.Complexity.AnswersBits`) when it contains every code exactly when the requested
+bit is `1`; it may answer other words arbitrarily. The bit graph of `f`
+(`Cslib.Complexity.bitGraph`), which contains the codes of the bits `1` and nothing else,
+`P^#P` relative to the encoding `enc` of instances (`Cslib.Complexity.PWithSharpPOracle`)
+consists of the problems `L` decided by one deterministic oracle program, strict oracle PPT as
+in `Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle`, that is correct against every oracle
+language answering the bits of some function `f ∈ #P`, for some encoded type of arguments of
+`f`. As for `Cslib.Complexity.RPWithPromiseOracle`, the program is fixed before the oracle, and
+the answers on words that are not codes are arbitrary, so the program only learns bits of `f`;
+in particular the oracle does not reveal which words are codes, however hard that is to decide.
+Taking the bit graph as the oracle language, such a problem is in polynomial time relative to
+the bit graph of a function in `#P` (`Cslib.Complexity.mem_PWithOracle_bitGraph`). The class
+does not count queries; it contains `P` (`Cslib.Complexity.P_subset_PWithSharpPOracle`), and a
+problem decided by one bit, at a polynomial position, of a function in `#P` on its own instances
+is in it, by a program making one query
+* `Cslib.Complexity.AnswersBits`: an oracle language answering the bits of a function.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.bitGraph`: the bits of a function, as an oracle language.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.answersBits_bitGraph`: the bit graph answers the bits.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.mem_PWithOracle_bitGraph`: `P^#P` lies in polynomial time relative to the
+  bit graph of a function in `#P`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.mem_PWithSharpPOracle_of_testBit`: one bit of a `#P` value is in `P^#P`.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The oracle language `A` **answers the bits** of `f : β → ℕ` under the encoding `encβ`: the
+code `encPair encβ encNat (b, i)` is in `A` exactly when bit `i` of `f b` is `1`. Words that are
+not codes may be in `A` or not. -/
+def AnswersBits (encβ : β ↪ List Bool) (f : β → ℕ) (A : Set (List Bool)) : Prop :=
+  ∀ b i, encPair encβ encNat (b, i) ∈ A ↔ (f b).testBit i
+/-- The bit graph of `f : β → ℕ`: the codes `encPair encβ encNat (b, i)` such that bit `i` of
+`f b` is `1`, and no other word. -/
+def bitGraph (encβ : β ↪ List Bool) (f : β → ℕ) : Set (List Bool) :=
+/-- The bit graph answers the bits. -/
+theorem answersBits_bitGraph (encβ : β ↪ List Bool) (f : β → ℕ) :
+    AnswersBits encβ f (bitGraph encβ f) := fun _ _ =>
+/-- **`P^#P`**: the problems `L` such that, for some type `β` with encoding `encβ` and some
+`f ∈ SharpP encβ`, one deterministic oracle program, strict oracle PPT on the encoding `enc` of
+instances, decides `L` against every oracle language answering the bits of `f`. Answers on
+words that are not codes are arbitrary. -/
+def PWithSharpPOracle (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {L | ∃ (β : Type) (encβ : β ↪ List Bool) (f : β → ℕ), f ∈ SharpP encβ ∧
+      IsOraclePPTOn enc encBool (fun a => OracleComp.interpret ProbOracleComp.query (program a)) ∧
+        ∀ A : Set (List Bool), AnswersBits encβ f A →
+          ∀ a, a ∈ L ↔ OracleComp.interpret (m := Id) (languageOracle A) (program a) = true}
+/-- **`P^#P` lies in polynomial time relative to a `#P` bit graph**: against the bit graph of its
+function, the program of a problem in `P^#P` decides it. -/

+      L ∈ PWithOracle (bitGraph encβ f) enc := by

+  exact ⟨β, encβ, f, hf, _, ⟨program, hprogram, fun _ => rfl⟩,
+/-- **`P ⊆ P^#P`**: a polynomial-time decider makes no query. -/
+theorem P_subset_PWithSharpPOracle : P enc ⊆ PWithSharpPOracle enc := by
+  exact ⟨α, enc, 0, SharpP.zero_mem, fun a => pure (g a), hg.isOraclePPTOn,
+/-- **One bit of a `#P` value is in `P^#P`**: a problem decided by the bit at a polynomial
+position of a function in `#P` on its own instances is in `P^#P`. The program asks for that bit,
+theorem mem_PWithSharpPOracle_of_testBit {f : α → ℕ} (hf : f ∈ SharpP enc)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+`⊕P` is the parity operator applied to `P` (`Cslib.Complexity.ParityP`)
+`L ∈ ⊕P` when, for a polynomial `p` and a function `V : α × List Bool → Bool` computable in
+polynomial time on inputs `encPair enc encBits (a, w) = frame (enc a) ++ w`, `a ∈ L` exactly when
+an odd number of the strings `w` of length `p (enc a).length` have `V (a, w) = true`
+(`Cslib.Complexity.mem_ParityP`). Equivalently, `L` consists of the instances where some function
+`⊕P` is closed under complement (`Cslib.Complexity.compl_mem_ParityP`): the verifier
+`Cslib.Complexity.succVerifier V` accepts the string of `false`s and the strings `true :: w` with
+`V (a, w) = true`, so it accepts exactly one string more than `V`, one bit longer
+(`Cslib.Complexity.acceptCount_succVerifier`), by counting words by their first bit
+* `Cslib.Complexity.succTest`, `Cslib.Complexity.succVerifier`: a word test and a verifier
+* [C. H. Papadimitriou, S. Zachos, *Two remarks on the power of counting*][PapadimitriouZachos1983]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The word test accepting one word more than `g`, one bit longer: the word of `false`s, and
+`true :: w` for every word `w` accepted by `g`. -/
+def succTest (g : List Bool → Bool) (w : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  !(w.any fun b => b) || (w.headD false && g w.tail)
+/-- The verifier accepting one string more than `V`, one bit longer: the string of `false`s, and
+`true :: w` for every `w` with `V (a, w) = true`. -/
+def succVerifier (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (x : α × List Bool) : Bool :=
+/-- **One more accepted string**: `succVerifier V` accepts exactly one string of length `n + 1`
+theorem acceptCount_succVerifier (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    acceptCount (succVerifier V) a (n + 1) = acceptCount V a n + 1 := by
+  have h₁ : (Finset.univ.filter fun w : Fin n → Bool =>
+      succVerifier V (a, true :: List.ofFn w) = true) =
+      Finset.univ.filter fun w => V (a, List.ofFn w) = true := by
+  have h₂ : (Finset.univ.filter fun w : Fin n → Bool =>
+      succVerifier V (a, false :: List.ofFn w) = true).card = 1 := by
+    BitString.card_filter_ofFn_succ n fun w => succVerifier V (a, w) = true, h₁, h₂]
+/-- **One more accepted word**: `succTest g` accepts exactly one word of length `n + 1` more than
+theorem acceptCount_succTest (g : List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    acceptCount (fun x => succTest g x.2) a (n + 1) = acceptCount (fun x => g x.2) a n + 1 :=
+  acceptCount_succVerifier (fun y => g y.2) a n
+/-- The parity of one more accepted string is the opposite parity. -/
+theorem odd_acceptCount_succVerifier_iff (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    Odd (acceptCount (succVerifier V) a (n + 1)) ↔ ¬Odd (acceptCount V a n) := by
+/-- `succTest` is polynomial-time, with a test that may use the input. -/
+    {g : γ → List Bool → Bool} {w : γ → List Bool}

+# Counting the parities of a random string with one bit of a `#P` value
+The second half of Toda's theorem [Toda][Toda1991], [Arora and Barak, Section 17.4][AroraBarak09]:
+for numbers `f r` of accepted witnesses, given for the random strings `r` of length `R`, the
+number `G` of random strings with `f r` odd is read off one bit of a single counting function.
+Toda amplifies the modulus of a parity with a polynomial `T` such that `T (c)` is `0` modulo
+`2 ^ K` for even `c` and `-1` for odd `c`. Here the amplification comes from the binomial
+`[c odd] = ∑ i < c, (-2) ^ i * choose c (i + 1)`,
+whose terms with `i ≥ K` vanish modulo `2 ^ K`
+replaced by naturals equal to them modulo `2 ^ K` (`Cslib.Complexity.Toda.parityCoeff`), and
+`choose (f r) k` counts the `k`-element sets of accepted witnesses, written as strictly
+increasing lists of `k` words for the lexicographic order
+the words accepted by `Cslib.Complexity.Toda.countingTest` — a size `k ≤ K` in unary, one of
+`parityCoeff K (k - 1)` coefficient words, a random string `r` and a strictly increasing list of
+`k` accepted witnesses, padded with zero words — number
+`H = ∑ i < K, parityCoeff K i * ∑ r, choose (f r) (i + 1)`
+(`Cslib.Complexity.Toda.card_filter_sharpTest`). Since `G ≤ 2 ^ R`, the bit `R + 1` of this
+number says whether `2 G > 2 ^ R`, that is whether more than half of the random strings have an
+* `Cslib.BitString.wordLt`: the lexicographic order on words of equal length.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.Toda.testBit_card_filter_sharpTest`: one bit says whether `2 G > 2 ^ R`.
+* [S. Toda, *PP is as hard as the polynomial-time hierarchy*][Toda1991]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- **The parity of `c` from the binomial expansion of `(1 - 2) ^ c`**:
+`∑ i < c, (-2) ^ i * choose c (i + 1)` is `1` for odd `c` and `0` for even `c`. -/
+    ∑ i ∈ range c, (-2 : ℤ) ^ i * (c.choose (i + 1) : ℤ) = if Odd c then 1 else 0 := by
+  have hbin : ∑ i ∈ range (c + 1), (-2 : ℤ) ^ i * (c.choose i : ℤ) = (-1) ^ c := by
+    rw [show (-2 : ℤ) + 1 = -1 by norm_num] at this
+  simp only [pow_zero, Nat.choose_zero_right, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at hbin
+  have h : -2 * ∑ i ∈ range c, (-2 : ℤ) ^ i * (c.choose (i + 1) : ℤ) = (-1) ^ c - 1 := by
+/-- **The parity of `c` modulo `2 ^ K`**: only the first `K` binomial terms matter. -/
+    ∑ i ∈ range K, (-2 : ZMod (2 ^ K)) ^ i * (c.choose (i + 1) : ZMod (2 ^ K)) =
+      if Odd c then 1 else 0 := by
+  have hexact := congrArg (Int.cast : ℤ → ZMod (2 ^ K)) (sum_range_neg_two_pow_mul_choose c)
+  have hK : (-2 : ZMod (2 ^ K)) ^ K = 0 := by
+    have h2 : (2 : ZMod (2 ^ K)) ^ K = 0 := by
+  have h₁ : ∑ i ∈ range (K + c), (-2 : ZMod (2 ^ K)) ^ i * (c.choose (i + 1) : ZMod (2 ^ K)) =
+      ∑ i ∈ range K, (-2 : ZMod (2 ^ K)) ^ i * (c.choose (i + 1) : ZMod (2 ^ K)) := by
+  have h₂ : ∑ i ∈ range (c + K), (-2 : ZMod (2 ^ K)) ^ i * (c.choose (i + 1) : ZMod (2 ^ K)) =
+      ∑ i ∈ range c, (-2 : ZMod (2 ^ K)) ^ i * (c.choose (i + 1) : ZMod (2 ^ K)) := by
+/-- Natural coefficients equal to `(-2) ^ i` modulo `2 ^ K`, for `i ≤ K`: `2 ^ i` for even `i`
+def parityCoeff (K i : ℕ) : ℕ := if Even i then 2 ^ i else 2 ^ K - 2 ^ i

+/-- **One bit decides the majority.** If `H` is `G` modulo `2 ^ (R + 1)` and `G ≤ 2 ^ R`, then the
+bit `R + 1` of `2 H + (2 ^ R - 1)` says whether `2 G > 2 ^ R`. -/
+theorem testBit_two_mul_add_two_pow_sub_one {R G H : ℕ} (hG : G ≤ 2 ^ R)

+    (univ.filter fun g : Fin k → β => StrictMono g ∧ ∀ i, g i ∈ A).card = (#A).choose k := by

+      BitString.wordLt (BitString.listRow Z i zs) (BitString.listRow Z (i + 1) zs)
+    (hacc : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : γ × List Bool => acc p.1 p.2)
+    {K Z k : γ → ℕ} {zs : γ → List Bool}

+/-- **The `k`-subset test counts `k`-element sets of accepted words**, for `k ≤ K`. -/
+theorem card_filter_subsetTest (acc : List Bool → Bool) {K k : ℕ} (Z : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ K) :
