+  refine ⟨fun h _ encC => (h encC).ge, fun h _ encC => ?_⟩
+/-- A **proof system** for `L` [CookReckhow1979]: a function, computable in polynomial time, from
+words onto `L`. A word `π` is a proof of `P π`; every word proves a member of `L`, and every member
+structure ProofSystem (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (L : Set α) where
+  /-- The member of `L` that a word proves. -/
+  /-- The member a proof proves is computed in polynomial time. -/
+  /-- The proved members are exactly the members of `L`. -/
+instance : CoeFun (ProofSystem enc L) fun _ => List Bool → α := ⟨toFun⟩
+/-- **Soundness**: every word proves a member of `L`. -/
+theorem mem (P : ProofSystem enc L) (π : List Bool) : P π ∈ L :=
+/-- **Completeness**: every member of `L` has a proof. -/
+theorem exists_eq (P : ProofSystem enc L) {a : α} (ha : a ∈ L) : ∃ π, P π = a :=
+/-- A set with a proof system is nonempty. -/
+theorem nonempty (P : ProofSystem enc L) : L.Nonempty := ⟨P [], P.mem []⟩
+/-- `P` is **polynomially bounded** [CookReckhow1979]: for a polynomial `p`, every member `a` of
+`L` has a proof of length at most `p (enc a).length`. -/
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ a ∈ L, ∃ π, P π = a ∧ π.length ≤ p.eval (enc a).length
+/-- `Q` **simulates** `P`: for a polynomial `p`, every proof `π` for `P` can be replaced by a proof
+for `Q` of the same member, of length at most `p π.length`. -/
+def Simulates (Q P : ProofSystem enc L) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ π, ∃ π', Q π' = P π ∧ π'.length ≤ p.eval π.length
+/-- `Q` **p-simulates** `P` [CookReckhow1979]: a function computable in polynomial time translates
+every proof for `P` into a proof for `Q` of the same member. -/
+def PSimulates (Q P : ProofSystem enc L) : Prop :=
+  ∃ t : List Bool → List Bool, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime t encBits encBits ∧ ∀ π, Q (t π) = P π
+theorem refl : P.Simulates P := ⟨.X, fun π => ⟨π, rfl, by simp⟩⟩
+theorem trans (hRQ : R.Simulates Q) (hQP : Q.Simulates P) : R.Simulates P := by
+theorem trans (hRQ : R.PSimulates Q) (hQP : Q.PSimulates P) : R.PSimulates P := by
+  exact ⟨t ∘ u, ht.comp hu, fun π => (hRQ (u π)).trans (hQP π)⟩
+/-- **p-simulation implies simulation**: a translation computed in polynomial time produces proofs
+theorem simulates (h : Q.PSimulates P) : Q.Simulates P := by
+  exact ⟨.C c * (.X + 1) ^ d, fun π => ⟨t π, htQP π, by simpa using hle π⟩⟩
+/-- **Simulation transfers polynomial bounds**: a proof system simulating a polynomially bounded
+theorem PolynomiallyBounded.of_simulates {P Q : ProofSystem enc L} (hP : P.PolynomiallyBounded)
+  obtain ⟨π, rfl, hlen⟩ := hp a ha
+/-- Words are their own encoding, decoded by the identity. -/

+variable {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}

+def verifierInstance (D : Decoder enc) (π : List Bool) : α := D.decode (unframe π)
+/-- Whether the verifier `V` accepts a word as an instance followed by a certificate of the
+def verifierAccepts (D : Decoder enc) (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool)
+/-- The **proof system of a verifier** `V` for `L`, with a default member `a₀`. Each word is
+decoded into an instance and a certificate using the total decoder `D`, `unframe` and `dropFrame`.
+It proves the decoded instance if `V` accepts and the certificate has the prescribed length;
+otherwise it proves `a₀`. A malformed frame can pass these checks. -/
+def ofVerifier (D : Decoder enc) (hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool)
+    (hVL : IsVerifier enc p V L) {a₀ : α} (ha₀ : a₀ ∈ L) : ProofSystem enc L where
+  toFun π := if verifierAccepts D p V π then verifierInstance D π else a₀
+    have hi : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (verifierInstance D) encBits enc :=
+        (fun π => p.eval (enc (verifierInstance D π)).length) encBits encUnary :=
+    have hacc : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (verifierAccepts D p V) encBits encBool :=
+      · simp only [verifierAccepts, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
+      have hi : verifierInstance D (frame (enc a) ++ w) = a := by
+      have hacc : verifierAccepts D p V (frame (enc a) ++ w) = true := by
+        simp only [verifierAccepts, hi, dropFrame_frame_append, hVw, hw, decide_true,
+/-- A framed encoded instance followed by an accepted certificate of the prescribed length proves
+    (hVL : IsVerifier enc p V L) {a₀ : α} (ha₀ : a₀ ∈ L) {a : α} {w : List Bool}
+    (hw : w.length = p.eval (enc a).length) (hVw : V (a, w) = true) :
+    ofVerifier D hV hVL ha₀ (frame (enc a) ++ w) = a := by
+  have hi : verifierInstance D (frame (enc a) ++ w) = a := by
+  have hacc : verifierAccepts D p V (frame (enc a) ++ w) = true := by
+    simp only [verifierAccepts, hi, dropFrame_frame_append, hVw, hw, decide_true, Bool.and_self]
+  change (if verifierAccepts D p V _ then _ else _) = a
+/-- The proof system of a verifier is polynomially bounded: an instance `a` has a proof of length
+    (hVL : IsVerifier enc p V L) {a₀ : α} (ha₀ : a₀ ∈ L) :
+  exact ⟨_, ofVerifier_frame_append D hV hVL ha₀ hw hVw, by simp [length_frame, hw]⟩
+/-- **A set is in `NP` exactly when it has a polynomially bounded proof system**
+[CookReckhow1979], for nonempty sets whose encoding has a decoder. -/
+    (∃ P : ProofSystem enc L, P.PolynomiallyBounded) ↔ L ∈ NP enc := by
+  refine ⟨fun ⟨_, hP⟩ => hP.mem_NP, fun ⟨p, V, hV, hVL⟩ => ?_⟩
+  exact ⟨_, polynomiallyBounded_ofVerifier D hV hVL ha₀⟩
+/-! ### The theorem of Cook and Reckhow -/
+/-- **Cook and Reckhow, for `coNP`-complete sets** [CookReckhow1979]: `coNP ⊆ NP`, for problems
+with every encoding of their instances, exactly when a nonempty `coNP`-complete set with a
+decodable encoding has a polynomially bounded proof system. -/
+    {B : Set β} (hB : coNPComplete encB B) (D : Decoder encB) (hne : B.Nonempty) :

+The sparsification lemma of Impagliazzo, Paturi and Zane [ImpagliazzoPaturiZane2001] on the native
+machines: a depth-first search of the sparsification tree, with a decider applied at its leaves,
+runs within time `2 ^ (ε n)` times the sum of a polynomial and the time of the decider on formulas
+with at most `c n + 1` clauses, on formulas with `n` variables. Hence a decider for `k`-SAT within
+time `2 ^ (δ m)` times a polynomial, on formulas with `m` clauses, gives one within time
+`2 ^ ((ε + c δ) n)` times a polynomial, on formulas with `n` variables
+hypothesis says that 3SAT is not decidable in subexponential time in the number of clauses
+The search (`Cslib.Complexity.Sparsify.search`) keeps a stack of formulas and an accumulator
+(`Cslib.Complexity.Sparsify.step`). It starts from the normal form of the formula
+(`Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF.Sparsification.normalize`); at a sparse formula on top of the stack it runs
+the decider, and at any other formula it pushes the two children of the list-level step
+(`Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF.Sparsification.next`), which is polynomial-time. This is the depth-first
+search of the branching tree of the list-level rule
+every leaf within twice the number of leaves of steps, which is at most `2 ^ (ε n)` up to a
+`Cslib.Logic.PL.ClauseSet.Sparsification.exists_sum_choose_le`. Meanwhile the stack holds at most
+`O(n)` formulas of the tree, each with `O(n + m)` clauses, and the leaves, being sparse, have at
+runs a fixed number `2 ^ (n / M + 2)` of rounds, the last ones on the empty stack, for `ε = 1 / M`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.DecidableInSubexpTime.numVars_of_length`: subexponential time in the number of
+  clauses gives subexponential time in the number of variables.
+* [R. Impagliazzo, R. Paturi, F. Zane, *Which problems have strongly exponential
+* [C. Calabro, R. Impagliazzo, R. Paturi, *A duality between clause width and clause density for
+/-- The states of the search: a stack of formulas and an accumulator. -/
+abbrev encState : State ↪ List Bool := encPair (encList encCNF) encBool
+/-- One step of the depth-first search of the sparsification tree, for width `K` and the
+thresholds `threshold K α`: a sparse formula on top of the stack is popped and the decider `g` is
+run on it; any other formula on top is replaced by its two children. -/
+def step (K α : ℕ) (g : CNF ℕ → Bool) (s : State) : State :=
+  else if isSparse (threshold K α) K (s.1.headD []) then (s.1.tail, s.2 || g (s.1.headD []))
+    next (threshold K α) K (s.1.headD []) true :: s.1.tail, s.2)
+/-- The root of the search: the normal form of a formula of width `k`, and the formula without
+def root (k : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) : CNF ℕ :=
+  if φ.all fun c => decide (c.length ≤ k) then normalize φ else []
+/-- The number of rounds of the search, `2 ^ (n / M + 2)` on formulas with `n` variables. -/
+def rounds (M : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ ((ThreeSAT.distinctVars φ).length / M + 2)
+/-- **The sparsification search**: run the search for the given number of rounds from the root,
+def search (K α k M : ℕ) (g : CNF ℕ → Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ) : Bool :=
+  ((step K α g)^[rounds M φ] ([root k φ], false)).2
+/-! ### The search is the depth-first search of the tree -/
+/-- The list-level branching rule for width `K` and the thresholds `threshold K α`. -/
+abbrev rule : BranchingRule (threshold K α) ℕ {ψ : CNF ℕ // Normalized K ψ} :=
+theorem step_map (g : CNF ℕ → Bool) (stk : List {ψ : CNF ℕ // Normalized K ψ}) (acc : Bool) :
+    step K α g (stk.map Subtype.val, acc) =
+    have hiff := isSparse_eq_true_iff (one_le_threshold hK hα) s.2
+    by_cases hs : ClauseSet.Sparsification.Sparse (threshold K α) s.1.toClauseSet
+    · have hs' : isSparse (threshold K α) K s.1 = true := hiff.mpr hs
+    · have hs' : isSparse (threshold K α) K s.1 = false := by
+        simpa using fun h => hs (hiff.mp h)
+      simp [step, BranchingRule.searchStep, hs, hs', rule, CNF.Sparsification.rule]
+theorem iterate_step_map (g : CNF ℕ → Bool) (n : ℕ) (stk : List {ψ : CNF ℕ // Normalized K ψ})
+  induction n generalizing stk acc with
+    obtain ⟨stk', acc'⟩ := (rule hK hα).searchStep (g ∘ Subtype.val) (stk, acc)
+theorem step_nil (g : CNF ℕ → Bool) (acc : Bool) : step K α g ([], acc) = ([], acc) := rfl
+theorem iterate_step_nil (g : CNF ℕ → Bool) (n : ℕ) (acc : Bool) :
+theorem normalized_root {k : ℕ} (hkK : k ≤ K) (φ : CNF ℕ) : Normalized K (root k φ) := by

+  · exact ⟨by simp, by simp, by simp, by simp [CNF.toClauseSet, ClauseSet.Sparsification.Reduced]⟩
+/-- Every clause of the root has the literals of a clause of the formula. -/
+theorem exists_of_mem_root {k : ℕ} {φ : CNF ℕ} {C : Clause ℕ} (hC : C ∈ root k φ) :
+  · have hsub : normalize φ <+ φ.map dedup :=
+theorem length_root_le (k : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) : (root k φ).length ≤ φ.length := by
+/-- The root as a state of the list-level rule. -/
+def rootState {k : ℕ} (hkK : k ≤ K) (φ : CNF ℕ) : {ψ : CNF ℕ // Normalized K ψ} :=
+    ∀ C ∈ (root k φ).toClauseSet, ∀ l ∈ C, l.1 ∈ φ.vars.toFinset := by
+  exact List.mem_toFinset.mpr (List.mem_map.mpr ⟨l, List.mem_flatten.mpr ⟨D, hD, hl⟩, rfl⟩)
+/-- The bound `2 ∑_{j < K} θ j` on the occurrences of a variable in a sparse formula. -/

+# Gap problems and hardness of approximation
+Hardness of approximation is stated through **gap problems** [Arora and Barak, Chapter
+11][AroraBarak09]. For a maximization objective `val`, the gap problem `gapMax val c s` is the
+promise problem whose yes-instances have value at least `c` and whose no-instances have value at
+most `s`, below `c`. When this gap problem is NP-hard, the maximization problem is **NP-hard to
+approximate** within every ratio better than `s / c`: an algorithm estimating `val` from below
+within such a ratio would tell the two kinds of instances apart.
+Reductions between promise problems are the polynomial-time many-one reductions of
+`Cslib.Complexity.PolyTimeReducible`, required to map yes-instances to yes-instances and
+no-instances to no-instances; on decision problems they are exactly those reductions
+(`PromiseProblem.polyTimeReducible_ofSet_iff`). Between gap problems they are the
+**gap-preserving reductions** used to transfer inapproximability from one problem to another.
+A promise problem is NP-hard when every problem in `NP` reduces to it; for decision problems this
+Reductions of promise problems are Karp reductions in the sense of Goldreich's survey
+[Goldreich2006]: one function serves for every instance in the promise. This is stronger than
+asking every problem separating the yes-instances from the no-instances to be NP-hard, which
+  problems, which between gap problems are the gap-preserving reductions.

+theorem NPHard.NP_subset_P_of_mem_PromiseP (hY : NPHard encB Y) (h : Y ∈ PromiseP encB)

+/-- The **gap problem** of a maximization objective `val`, with completeness threshold `c` and
+soundness threshold `s`: the yes-instances have value at least `c`, the no-instances value at most

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Local decoding of Reed–Muller codes along lines
+Let `F` be a finite field with `q` elements and let `f` be a codeword of the Reed–Muller code of
+degree `d` in `m` variables over `F`, the evaluation table of a polynomial of total degree at most
+`d`. Along every affine line `c ↦ x + c • v` the codeword is a polynomial in `c` of degree at most
+`d`, and the values of a polynomial of degree below `q - 1` sum to zero over `F`. So for
+`d + 1 < q` the sum of `f` over every line vanishes
+(`Cslib.Code.sum_add_smul_eq_zero_of_mem_reedMuller`), and the value of `f` at `x` is minus the
+sum of its values on the punctured line `Cslib.LineCode.puncturedLine x v` of the `q - 1` points
+The *line decoder* `Cslib.Code.lineDecode w x v` reads a received word `w` at the `q - 1` points of
+that punctured line only (`Cslib.Code.lineDecode_congr`) and returns minus their sum. This is the
+basic local decoder of Reed–Muller codes, which interpolates the restriction of the received word to
+a random line through `x` [Arora and Barak, Chapter 19][AroraBarak09], [GuruswamiRudraSudan2019];
+interpolating a polynomial of degree below `q - 1` from all `q - 1` points other than `x` gives
+minus their sum at `x`. On a codeword it returns the value at `x` for every direction
+(`Cslib.Code.lineDecode_eq_of_mem_reedMuller`), and on a corrupted codeword it still does whenever
+the punctured line avoids the corrupted points (`Cslib.Code.lineDecode_eq_of_disjoint`). By the
+other than `x` lies on the punctured lines of only `q - 1` of the `q ^ m - 1` nonzero directions, so
+at most `(q - 1) * Δ(w, f)` nonzero directions make the decoder err
+(`Cslib.Code.card_filter_lineDecode_ne_le`): for a uniformly random nonzero direction the decoder
+reads `f x` from `w` with `q - 1` queries except with probability at most
+`(q - 1) * Δ(w, f) / (q ^ m - 1)`. In particular, if `2 * (q - 1) * Δ(w, f) < q ^ m - 1`, more than
+half of the nonzero directions recover `f x` at every point `x`
+  `q - 1` sum to zero on every line.
+* `Cslib.Code.lineDecode_congr`: the decoder queries only the punctured line.
+* `Cslib.Code.lineDecode_eq_of_mem_reedMuller`: the decoder is exact on codewords.
+* `Cslib.Code.lineDecode_eq_of_disjoint`: the decoder is exact on lines avoiding the errors.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09], Chapter 19
+* [V. Guruswami, A. Rudra, M. Sudan, *Essential Coding Theory*]
+/-- The restriction of a polynomial `P` in `m` variables to the line `c ↦ x + c • v`: a polynomial
+in `c` of degree at most the total degree of `P`. -/
+private theorem exists_natDegree_le_and_eval_eq (P : MvPolynomial (Fin m) F) (x v : Fin m → F) :
+      ∀ c : F, g.eval c = MvPolynomial.eval (x + c • v) P := by
+  let line : Fin m → Polynomial F := fun i => Polynomial.C (x i) + Polynomial.C (v i) * Polynomial.X
+  refine ⟨MvPolynomial.eval₂ Polynomial.C line P, ?_, fun c => ?_⟩
+    calc ∑ i, (line i ^ s i).natDegree ≤ ∑ i, s i := by
+      _ = s.sum fun _ e => e := (Finsupp.sum_fintype s (fun _ e => e) fun _ => rfl).symm
+  · have hC : (Polynomial.evalRingHom c).comp Polynomial.C = RingHom.id F :=
+    change MvPolynomial.eval₂ _ _ P = MvPolynomial.eval₂ (RingHom.id F) _ P
+/-- **Line sums of Reed–Muller codewords.** For `d + 1 < q`, the values of a codeword of the
+Reed–Muller code of degree `d` over a field with `q` elements sum to zero on every affine line
+`c ↦ x + c • v`, including the degenerate line `v = 0`. -/
+    {f : (Fin m → F) → F} (hf : f ∈ reedMuller F m d) (x v : Fin m → F) :
+    ∑ c : F, f (x + c • v) = 0 := by
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgeval⟩ := exists_natDegree_le_and_eval_eq P x v
+/-- The *line decoder*: the value at `x` read off a received word `w` along the direction `v`,
+minus the sum of the values of `w` at the `q - 1` points `x + c • v` with `c ≠ 0`. -/
+def lineDecode (w : (Fin m → F) → F) (x v : Fin m → F) : F :=
+  -∑ c ∈ (univ : Finset F).erase 0, w (x + c • v)
+/-- **Locality.** The line decoder queries the received word only at the points of the punctured
+line `puncturedLine x v`, of which there are at most `q - 1`. -/
+theorem lineDecode_congr {w w' : (Fin m → F) → F} {x v : Fin m → F}
+    (h : ∀ y ∈ puncturedLine x v, w y = w' y) : lineDecode w x v = lineDecode w' x v := by
+  rw [lineDecode, lineDecode, sum_congr rfl fun c hc =>
+/-- **The line decoder is exact on codewords.** For `d + 1 < q`, on a codeword `f` of the
+Reed–Muller code of degree `d` the line decoder returns `f x` for every direction `v`. -/
+theorem lineDecode_eq_of_mem_reedMuller (hd : d + 1 < Fintype.card F) {f : (Fin m → F) → F}
+    (hf : f ∈ reedMuller F m d) (x v : Fin m → F) : lineDecode f x v = f x := by
+  have h := sum_add_smul_eq_zero_of_mem_reedMuller hd hf x v
+  rw [← add_sum_erase _ _ (mem_univ 0), zero_smul, add_zero] at h
+/-- For `d + 1 < q`, if the punctured line through `x` in the direction `v` avoids the points where
+the received word `w` differs from a codeword `f` of the Reed–Muller code of degree `d`, the line
+decoder reads `f x` from `w`. An error at `x` itself is corrected. -/
+theorem lineDecode_eq_of_disjoint (hd : d + 1 < Fintype.card F) {f w : (Fin m → F) → F}
+    (hf : f ∈ reedMuller F m d) {x v : Fin m → F}
+    (h : Disjoint (puncturedLine x v) ({y | w y ≠ f y} : Finset (Fin m → F))) :
+    lineDecode w x v = f x := by
+  rw [← lineDecode_eq_of_mem_reedMuller hd hf x v]
+  exact disjoint_left.1 h hy (mem_filter.2 ⟨mem_univ y, hne⟩)
+/-- **Local decoding of Reed–Muller codes.** For `d + 1 < q`, let `w` be a received word and `f` a
+codeword of the Reed–Muller code of degree `d` over a field with `q` elements. At every point `x`,
+at most `(q - 1) * Δ(w, f)` of the `q ^ m - 1` nonzero directions `v` make the line decoder err. -/
+theorem card_filter_lineDecode_ne_le (hd : d + 1 < Fintype.card F) {f : (Fin m → F) → F}
+    (hf : f ∈ reedMuller F m d) (w : (Fin m → F) → F) (x : Fin m → F) :
+    #{v ∈ univ.erase 0 | lineDecode w x v ≠ f x} ≤ hammingDist w f * (Fintype.card F - 1) := by
+  let B : Finset (Fin m → F) := {y | w y ≠ f y}
+  calc #{v ∈ univ.erase 0 | lineDecode w x v ≠ f x}
+          exact ⟨hv.1, fun hdisj => hv.2 (lineDecode_eq_of_disjoint hd hf hdisj)⟩
+/-- **Self-correction of Reed–Muller codes.** For `d + 1 < q`, if a received word `w` and a
+codeword `f` of the Reed–Muller code of degree `d` over a field with `q` elements satisfy
+`2 * (q - 1) * Δ(w, f) < q ^ m - 1`, then at every point `x` more than half of the `q ^ m - 1`
+nonzero directions make the line decoder return `f x`. -/
+    {f w : (Fin m → F) → F} (hf : f ∈ reedMuller F m d)
+    (h : 2 * (hammingDist w f * (Fintype.card F - 1)) < Fintype.card F ^ m - 1) (x : Fin m → F) :
+    Fintype.card F ^ m - 1 < 2 * #{v ∈ univ.erase 0 | lineDecode w x v = f x} := by
+  have hsplit := card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := (univ : Finset (Fin m → F)).erase 0)
+    (fun v => lineDecode w x v = f x)
+  rw [card_erase_of_mem (mem_univ 0), card_univ, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin] at hsplit
+  have hne := card_filter_lineDecode_ne_le hd hf w x

+# Averaging and the minimax principle for finite distributions
+Think of a two-player game in which one player picks a strategy `a` and the other an input `b`,
+with loss `loss a b`; for an algorithm, `loss a b` may be whether `a` errs on `b`. Drawing the
+strategy from a distribution `μ` and the input from a distribution `ν` relates the two classical
+guarantees of randomized algorithms [Yao1977]. Distributions appear in two forms: finitely
+supported ones as points of the standard simplex (`Convexity.StdSimplex`), and probability mass
+functions (`PMF`), whose supports may be infinite. On a finite type the two correspond
+* *The averaging argument*: some outcome of a distribution is at most the mean
+  `Probability.PMF.exists_mem_support_le_tsum_mul`). So if a strategy drawn from `μ` has expected
+  loss at most `ε` on every input, then for every `ν` some single strategy has expected loss at
+  most `ε` on inputs drawn from `ν` (`Probability.PMF.exists_mem_support_tsum_mul_le`; for the
+  probability of failing, `Probability.PMF.exists_mem_support_toOuterMeasure_le`). This is the easy
+* *The minimax theorem* [vonNeumann1928]: for finitely many strategies and inputs, the converse
+  holds. If against every distribution `ν` on the inputs some strategy has expected loss at most
+  `ε`, then some distribution `μ` on the strategies has expected loss at most `ε` on every input
+  distributions as probability mass functions). For the probability of failing, only the inputs
+  need to be finite: strategies failing on the same inputs are interchangeable, so `μ` can be taken
+  with finite support (`Probability.PMF.exists_forall_toOuterMeasure_le`). This is the hard
+  finite type as points of the standard simplex.
+  `Cslib.Probability.PMF.exists_mem_support_le_tsum_mul`: some outcome is at most the mean.
+  `Cslib.Probability.PMF.exists_forall_sum_mul_le`: the minimax theorem for finite games.
+* [A. C.-C. Yao, *Probabilistic computations: toward a unified measure of complexity*][Yao1977]
+variable {α : Type*} {μ : StdSimplex ℝ α} {g : α → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
+/-- An average under a finitely supported distribution is at most any bound on the support. -/
+theorem sum_mul_le_of_forall_le (h : ∀ a ∈ μ.weights.support, g a ≤ c) :
+    (μ.weights.sum fun a w => w * g a) ≤ c :=
+  calc (μ.weights.sum fun a w => w * g a) ≤ μ.weights.sum fun _ w => w * c :=
+        Finset.sum_le_sum fun a ha => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h a ha) (μ.weights_nonneg a)
+    _ = c := by rw [← Finsupp.sum_mul, μ.total, one_mul]
+/-- **The averaging argument**: some point of the support of a finitely supported distribution is
+theorem exists_mem_support_le_sum_mul (μ : StdSimplex ℝ α) (g : α → ℝ) :
+    ∃ a ∈ μ.weights.support, g a ≤ μ.weights.sum fun a w => w * g a := by
+  have hlt : (μ.weights.sum fun a w => w * (μ.weights.sum fun a w => w * g a)) <
+      μ.weights.sum fun a w => w * g a :=
+  rw [← Finsupp.sum_mul, μ.total, one_mul] at hlt
+/-! ### The minimax theorem for finite games -/

+    IsLinearMap ℝ fun x : I → ℝ => ∑ i, x i * a i :=
+    fun c x => by simp [Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]⟩
+/-- The weight vectors of the distributions on a finite type form a convex set. -/

+  · exact convex_halfSpace_ge ⟨fun x y => rfl, fun c x => rfl⟩ 0
+/-- The weight vectors of the distributions on a finite type form a compact set. -/
+    IsCompact (Set.range fun p : StdSimplex ℝ I => (p.weights : I → ℝ)) :=
+/-- **The minimax theorem for finite two-player zero-sum games** [Sion1958], in the form used by
+Yao's principle. A row player picks `i : I`, a column player picks `j : J`, and the row player pays
+`M i j`. If against every mixed strategy `q` of the column player some row `i` has expected payment
+at most `c`, then some mixed strategy `p` of the row player has expected payment at most `c` against

+/-- The distribution on a finite type whose probabilities are the weights of a point of the
+noncomputable def ofStdSimplex (p : StdSimplex ℝ I) : PMF I :=
+    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg fun i _ => p.weights_nonneg i, p.total_of_fintype,

+@[simp] theorem ofStdSimplex_toStdSimplex (μ : PMF I) : ofStdSimplex (toStdSimplex μ) = μ :=
+/-- **The minimax theorem for finite games** [vonNeumann1928], for distributions. Let `M i j` be
+the loss of a strategy `i` on an input `j`. If against every distribution `ν` on the inputs some
+strategy has expected loss at most `ε`, then some distribution `μ` on the strategies has expected
+loss at most `ε` on every input. This is the hard direction of Yao's principle; it is
+theorem exists_forall_sum_mul_le [Nonempty I] (M : I → J → ℝ) {ε : ℝ}
+    (h : ∀ ν : PMF J, ∃ i, ∑ j, (ν j).toReal * M i j ≤ ε) :
+    ∃ μ : PMF I, ∀ j, ∑ i, (μ i).toReal * M i j ≤ ε := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := StdSimplex.exists_forall_sum_le_of_forall_exists_sum_le M fun q => by
+  exact ⟨ofStdSimplex p, by simpa using hp⟩
+/-- The probability of an event in a finite space as a sum. -/
+private theorem toReal_toOuterMeasure_eq_sum {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ] (π : PMF γ) (s : Set γ)
+    (π.toOuterMeasure s).toReal = ∑ c, (π c).toReal * if c ∈ s then 1 else 0 := by
+  exact sum_congr rfl fun c _ => by by_cases hc : c ∈ s <;> simp [hc]
+/-- **Yao's minimax principle** for finite sets of inputs. Let `E i j` say that a strategy `i`
+fails on an input `j`, where there may be infinitely many strategies but only finitely many inputs.
+If against every distribution `ν` on the inputs some strategy fails with probability at most `ε`,
+then some distribution `μ` on finitely many strategies fails with probability at most `ε` on every
+theorem exists_forall_toOuterMeasure_le {I J : Type*} [Finite J] [Nonempty I] (E : I → J → Prop)
+    {ε : ℝ} (h : ∀ ν : PMF J, ∃ i, (ν.toOuterMeasure {j | E i j}).toReal ≤ ε) :
+    ∃ μ : PMF I, μ.support.Finite ∧ ∀ j, (μ.toOuterMeasure {i | E i j}).toReal ≤ ε := by
+  -- Strategies with the same failures are interchangeable: play on the finitely many sets of
+  -- failures, each represented by one strategy.
+  let r : I → Set J := fun i => {j | E i j}
+  let rep : Set.range r → I := fun s => s.2.choose
+  have hrep (s : Set.range r) (j : J) : E (rep s) j ↔ j ∈ s.1 := by
+  obtain ⟨μ, hμ⟩ := exists_forall_sum_mul_le (fun (s : Set.range r) j => if j ∈ s.1 then 1 else 0)
+  refine ⟨μ.map rep, by rw [PMF.support_map]; exact (Set.toFinite _).image _, fun j => ?_⟩
+  refine le_of_eq_of_le (sum_congr rfl fun s _ => ?_) (hμ j)

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Questions about arbitrarily late times reduce to one fixed power. Two orbits are ever in the
+same state at the same time exactly when they are at time `2 ^ n`
+(`FunctionalGraph.exists_iterate_eq_iterate_iff`), so synchronous coalescence costs two fixed
+powers and an equality test (`synchronous_coalescence`). A recognized target recurs arbitrarily
+late exactly when it is reachable from the cycle projection `f^[(2 ^ n)!] x`
+(`recurring_target_circuit`), and it holds from some time on exactly when its complement does not
+recur (`eventually_always_target_circuit`). Balancing the parameter gives the square-root bounds
+The circuits are native De Morgan circuits: every NOT, AND and OR gate and every constant is
+charged, while wiring and fanout are free. They exist for each parameter choice; nothing here
+/-- **Synchronous coalescence.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`80000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L + 6 * n + 1` decides, for two states given as the two
+halves of its input, whether their orbits are ever in the same state at the same time. -/
+theorem synchronous_coalescence (c : Circuit signature n n) (L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L)
+        ∃ t, (c.eval interpretation)^[t] (fun i => z (Fin.castAdd n i)) =
+      out.size ≤ 80000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L + 6 * n + 1 := by
+  obtain ⟨power, hp, hs⟩ := fixed_power n c (Fintype.card (BitString n)) L hL hLN
+  let left := fun z : BitString (n + n) => fun i : Fin n => z (Fin.castAdd n i)
+  let right := fun z : BitString (n + n) => fun i : Fin n => z (Fin.natAdd n i)
+  have ha := Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs (n + n)) power
+    (fun i z => left z i) fun i => ⟨_, rfl⟩
+  have hb := Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs (n + n)) power
+    (fun i z => right z i) fun i => ⟨_, rfl⟩
+  have heq := synthesis_bits_eq (inputs (n + n) ∪ (wires (fun z => power.eval interpretation
+      (left z)) ∪ wires fun z => power.eval interpretation (right z)))
+    (fun z => power.eval interpretation (left z)) (fun z => power.eval interpretation (right z))
+    (fun _ h => Or.inr (Or.inl h)) fun _ h => Or.inr (Or.inr h)
+  change decide (power.eval interpretation (left z) = power.eval interpretation (right z)) = true ↔
+        ∃ t, (c.eval interpretation)^[t] (fun i => z (Fin.castAdd n i)) =
+      (out.size : ℝ) ≤ 240000 * optimizedBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) + 6 * n + 1 := by
+  obtain ⟨L, hL, hLN, hopt⟩ := exists_powerBudget_le_optimizedBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) le_rfl
+  obtain ⟨out, ho, hs⟩ := synchronous_coalescence c L hL hLN
+  have hs' : (out.size : ℝ) ≤ 80000 * (powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L : ℝ) + 6 * n + 1 := by
+/-- **Recurring targets.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`80000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L + p.size` decides whether the orbit of
+its input visits a state accepted by `p` at arbitrarily late times. -/
+theorem recurring_target_circuit (c : Circuit signature n n) (p : Circuit signature n 1)
+        ∀ a, ∃ t, a ≤ t ∧ p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x) 0 = true) ∧
+      out.size ≤ 80000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L + p.size := by

+  · have hb : powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L ≤
+        powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L := by
+/-- Negating a one-bit circuit costs one gate. -/
+      (∀ x, out.eval interpretation x 0 = !p.eval interpretation x 0) ∧ out.size ≤ p.size + 1 := by
+  have hp : Synthesis interpretation (inputs n) {fun x => p.eval interpretation x 0} p.size :=
+    (Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs n) p (fun i x => x i)
+      fun i => ⟨i, rfl⟩).mono Set.Subset.rfl (by rintro _ rfl; exact ⟨0, rfl⟩) le_rfl
+  exact ⟨out, fun x => congrFun (ho x) 0, hs⟩
+/-- **Eventually permanent targets.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`80000 * powerBudget n (c.size + (p.size + 1) + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L + p.size + 2` decides whether
+the orbit of its input is accepted by `p` from some time on. -/
+    (p : Circuit signature n 1) (L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) (hLN : L ≤ 2 ^ n) :
+        ∃ a, ∀ t, a ≤ t → p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x) 0 = true) ∧
+      out.size ≤ 80000 * powerBudget n (c.size + (p.size + 1) + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L +
+  obtain ⟨recurs, hc, hcs⟩ := recurring_target_circuit c reject L hL hLN

+        powerBudget n (c.size + (p.size + 1) + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L := by

+        240000 * optimizedBudget n (c.size + (p.size + 1) + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) + p.size + 2 := by
+  obtain ⟨out, ho, hs⟩ := eventually_always_target_circuit c p L hL hLN

+# Canonical cycle labels as bit strings
+Order `n`-bit states lexicographically, coordinate zero first (`lexOrder`). The canonical label
+of a state `x` under `f` lists the least state of its eventual cycle, the cycle length and the
+phase of `x` on the cycle, the last two in `n + 3` bits (`canonicalLabel`). Labels along an
+orbit differ only in the phase, so the label of `x` is recovered from the label of `f^[j] x` by

+contain the whole cycle. A scan for the least of them, the first return to `x` and the first
+visit to the least state give its label directly (`shortLabel_eq_canonicalLabel`), in
+`O(K * n + n ^ 2)` gates once the orbit prefix is available (`synthesis_shortLabel`).
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.correctLabel`: shift a label back along the orbit.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.shortLabel`: the label read from one traversal of a short
+/-- A state followed by two words. -/

+  Fin.append c (Fin.append (fun i => ell.getLsbD i.val) fun i => phi.getLsbD i.val)
+/-- The first word of a label: the cycle length. -/
+  word fun i => r (Fin.natAdd n (Fin.castAdd w i))
+/-- The second word of a label: the phase. -/
+  word fun i => r (Fin.natAdd n (Fin.natAdd w i))

+    labelRepresentative (labelBits c ell phi) = c := by

+    labelLength (labelBits c ell phi) = ell := by

+@[simp] theorem labelPhase_labelBits (c : BitString n) (ell phi : BitVec w) :
+    labelPhase (labelBits c ell phi) = phi := by
+/-- The width of a canonical label: a state, then two words of `n + 3` bits. -/
+/-- **Canonical labels.** The lexicographically least state of the eventual cycle of `x`, the
+cycle length, and the phase of `x` on the cycle, the last two in `n + 3` bits. -/

+theorem cycleLength_le_two_pow (f : BitString n → BitString n) (x : BitString n) :

+/-- Shift a label back by `j` steps: subtract `j` from its phase modulo its cycle length. -/

+/-- The bits of a label of available parts are available. -/

+    | right bit => simpa only [labelBits, Fin.append_right] using hp ⟨bit, rfl⟩
+/-- Correcting an available label costs one modular difference. -/

+/-- The least of the first `K + 1` states of the orbit of `x`. -/

+/-- The first positive time up to `K` at which the orbit of `x` returns to `x`. -/

+  firstIndex fun j : Fin (K + 1) => decide (f^[j.val] x = shortRepresentative f K x)
+/-- The label read from the first `K + 1` states of the orbit of `x`. -/
+noncomputable def shortLabel (f : BitString n → BitString n) (K : ℕ) (x : BitString n) :
+  labelBits (shortRepresentative f K x) (shortLength f K x)
+    (subMod 0 (shortTime f K x) (shortLength f K x))
+variable (f : BitString n → BitString n) (K : ℕ) {x : BitString n}
+  (hx : x ∈ Function.periodicPts f) (hK : cycleLength f x ≤ K)
+theorem shortRepresentative_eq : shortRepresentative f K x = canonicalCycle f x := by
+  have hs := scanMin_spec (fun j : Fin (K + 1) => f^[j.val] x) x (K + 1)
+  · have ht := canonicalTime_lt_cycleLength f x hx
+    have h := hs.2.2 ⟨canonicalTime f x, by omega⟩ (by simp only; omega)
+theorem shortLength_eq : shortLength (w := w) f K x = BitVec.ofNat w (cycleLength f x) := by
+  have hmin : Function.minimalPeriod f x = cycleLength f x := by
+    simp only [cycleLength, (transientDepth_eq_zero_iff f x).mpr hx, Function.iterate_zero_apply]
+  apply firstIndex_spec _ ⟨cycleLength f x, by omega⟩
+    change f^[cycleLength f x] x = x
+theorem shortTime_eq : shortTime (w := w) f K x = BitVec.ofNat w (canonicalTime f x) := by
+  exact firstIndex_spec _ ⟨canonicalTime f x, (canonicalTime_lt_cycleLength f x hx).trans_le
+    fun i hi => decide_eq_false (canonicalTime_min f x hi)
+/-- **Short cycles.** On a periodic state whose cycle has length at most `K`, the label read
+from the first `K + 1` states of its orbit is its canonical label. -/
+theorem shortLabel_eq_canonicalLabel : shortLabel f K x = canonicalLabel f x := by
+  simp only [shortLabel, canonicalLabel, shortRepresentative_eq f K hx hK, shortLength_eq f K hx hK,
+/-- **Short-cycle labels.** Once the first `K + 1` states of an orbit are available, its short
+label costs one minimum scan, two first-position scans, their equality tests and one modular
+theorem synthesis_shortLabel (s : Set (BooleanFunction a)) (f : BitString n → BitString n)
+    (hp : ∀ j : Fin (K + 1), ∀ bit, (fun x => f^[j.val] (init x) bit) ∈ s)
+    (hc : ∀ b : Bool, (fun _ : BitString a => b) ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis interpretation s (wires fun x => shortLabel f K (init x))
+  let rep := fun x => shortRepresentative f K (init x)
+  have hm : Synthesis interpretation s (wires rep) ((K + 1) * (10 * n + 1)) :=
+    synthesis_scanMin s (fun x j => f^[j.val] (init x)) init (fun j bit => hp j bit) (hp 0)
+  have hprefix (j : Fin (K + 1)) : wires (fun x => f^[j.val] (init x)) ⊆ src := by
+  let back := fun x (j : Fin (K + 1)) => decide (0 < j.val ∧ f^[j.val] (init x) = init x)
+  have hback := Synthesis.family (I := interpretation) (s := src) (fun j x => back x j)
+      · simpa only [back, hj, true_and] using synthesis_bits_eq src (fun x => f^[j.val] (init x))
+      · simpa only [back, hj, false_and, decide_false] using
+  have hl := synthesis_firstIndex (w := n + 3) (src ∪ Set.range fun j x => back x j) back
+    (fun j => Or.inr ⟨j, rfl⟩) fun b => Or.inl (Or.inl (hc b))
+  let hit := fun x (j : Fin (K + 1)) => decide (f^[j.val] (init x) = rep x)
+  have hhit := Synthesis.family (I := interpretation) (s := src) (fun j x => hit x j)
+      synthesis_bits_eq src (fun x => f^[j.val] (init x)) rep (hprefix j) fun _ h => Or.inr h
+  have ht := synthesis_firstIndex (w := n + 3) (src ∪ Set.range fun j x => hit x j) hit
+    (fun j => Or.inr ⟨j, rfl⟩) fun b => Or.inl (Or.inl (hc b))
+  let ell := fun x => shortLength (w := n + 3) f K (init x)
+  let time := fun x => shortTime (w := n + 3) f K (init x)
+  let src2 := s ∪ (wires rep ∪ (wordWires ell ∪ wordWires time))
+  have hphase := synthesis_subMod src2 (fun _ => (0 : BitVec (n + 3))) time ell
+      rw [show (fun _ : BitString a => (0 : BitVec (n + 3)).getLsbD i.val) = fun _ => false from
+    (labelBits_wires_subset (src2 ∪ wordWires fun x => subMod 0 (time x) (ell x)) rep ell
+      (fun x => subMod 0 (time x) (ell x)) (fun _ h => Or.inl (Or.inr (Or.inl h)))
+      (fun _ h => Or.inl (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl h)))) fun _ h => Or.inr h)

+Let `c` be a circuit of size `s` computing `f` on `n`-bit states. Some circuit of size at most
+`60000 * powerBudget n s (2 ^ n) L` computes the canonical label of every state: the
+lexicographically least state of its eventual cycle, the cycle length and its phase
+(`cycle_label_circuit`), for every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`; with the balanced parameter the size is at
+The construction first applies `f^[(2 ^ n)!]` with a fixed-power circuit. This moves every state
+onto its cycle without changing its label. On a periodic state, choose checkpoints as for fixed
+powers and hardwire the label of each. The first `2 L + 1` states of the orbit are looked up in
+one shared dictionary (`lookupOr`); a checkpoint hit at time `j` gives the label after shifting
+its phase back by `j` (`correctLabel_canonicalLabel`). Without a hit the orbit repeats within `L`
+steps, so its cycle is short and is read off the orbit prefix (`shortLabel_eq_canonicalLabel`).
+The circuits are native De Morgan circuits: every NOT, AND and OR gate and every constant is
+charged, while wiring and fanout are free. The checkpoints and their labels are chosen
+nonconstructively, so the circuits exist for each `L`; nothing here bounds the time to construct
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.labelCost`: the gate count of the checkpoint construction.
+  bounds have the constants `10040000` and `30120000`. The dictionary here is the library's
+/-- The gate count of the label construction from `M` checkpoints with parameter `L`: constants,
+the orbit prefix, the shared dictionary, one label correction per prefix state, the short-cycle
+def labelCost (n s M L : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+/-- **Labels from checkpoints.** Let `cp` be injective checkpoints such that every orbit repeats
+among its first `L` states or reaches a checkpoint in fewer than `2 L` steps. Then some circuit of
+size at most `labelCost n c.size M L` computes the canonical label of every periodic state. -/
+theorem cyclic_labels_from_checkpoints (c : Circuit signature n n) (L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L)
+    (hLN : L ≤ 2 ^ n) (cp : Fin M → BitString n) (hcp : Function.Injective cp)
+      ∃ t < 2 * L, ∃ j, (c.eval interpretation)^[t] x = cp j) :
+        out.eval interpretation x = canonicalLabel (c.eval interpretation) x) ∧
+      out.size ≤ labelCost n c.size M L := by
+  let constants : Set (BooleanFunction n) := {fun _ => false, fun _ => true}
+  have hconst : Synthesis interpretation (inputs n) constants 2 :=
+  have hc (b : Bool) : (fun _ : BitString n => b) ∈ s0 := by cases b <;> simp [s0, constants]
+  have horbit : Synthesis interpretation s0 (prefixWires f K) (K * c.size) :=
+    Synthesis.orbit c id (fun bit => Or.inl ⟨bit, rfl⟩) K
+  let s1 := s0 ∪ prefixWires f K
+  have hp (j : Fin (K + 1)) (bit : Fin n) : (fun x => f^[j.val] x bit) ∈ s1 :=
+  let stored : Fin M → BitString (W + 1) := fun i => Fin.cons true (canonicalLabel f (cp i))
+  let queries : BitString n → Fin (K + 1) → BitString n := fun x j => f^[j.val] x
+  have hdict := synthesis_lookupOr s1 cp stored queries fun j bit => hp j bit
+  let result := fun x (j : Fin (K + 1)) => lookupOr cp stored (queries x j)
+  let s2 := s1 ∪ ⋃ j, wires fun x => result x j
+  have hresult (j : Fin (K + 1)) (bit : Fin (W + 1)) : (fun x => result x j bit) ∈ s2 :=
+  let flags := fun x (j : Fin (K + 1)) => result x j 0
+  let records := fun x (j : Fin (K + 1)) (bit : Fin W) => result x j bit.succ
+  let corrected := fun (j : Fin (K + 1)) x => correctLabel (records x j) j.val
+  have hcorrect := Synthesis.iUnion (fun j => wires (corrected j)) (fun _ => 50 * (n + 4) ^ 2)
+    fun j => synthesis_correctLabel s2 (fun x => records x j)
+      (by rintro _ ⟨bit, rfl⟩; exact hresult j bit.succ) (fun b => Or.inl (Or.inl (hc b))) j.val
+  have hshort := synthesis_shortLabel s2 f id K (fun j bit => Or.inl (hp j bit))
+  let s3 := s2 ∪ ((⋃ j, wires (corrected j)) ∪ wires fun x => shortLabel f K x)
+  have hselect := synthesis_chooseRecord s3 flags (fun x j => corrected j x)
+    (fun x => shortLabel f K x) (fun j => Or.inl (hresult j 0))
+    change chooseRecord (flags x) (fun j => corrected j x) (shortLabel f K x) (K + 1) =
+    by_cases hh : ∃ j, flags x j = true
+    · obtain ⟨j, -, hj, he⟩ := chooseRecord_spec (flags x) (fun j => corrected j x)
+        (shortLabel f K x) (K + 1) (by obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hh; exact ⟨j, j.isLt, hj⟩)
+      obtain ⟨i, hi, -⟩ := (decide_eq_true_iff.mp hj : ∃ i, cp i = _ ∧ stored i 0 = true)
+      have hrecord : records x j = canonicalLabel f (f^[j.val] x) := by
+    · have hnone : ∀ j, flags x j = false := fun j => Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr fun hj => hh ⟨j, hj⟩
+      rcases hcover x with ⟨i, j, hij, hj, he⟩ | ⟨t, ht, i, hi⟩
+        simp only [flags, result, queries, lookupOr, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at hj
+    simp only [K, W, labelWidth] at hs ⊢
+/-- The label construction is within `20000` times the fixed-power tradeoff. -/
+theorem labelCost_le (n s M L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) (hLN : L ≤ 2 ^ n) (hM : M ≤ 2 ^ n / L) :
+    labelCost n s M L ≤ 20000 * powerBudget n s (2 ^ n) L := by
+    have h4 : 2 ^ (n + 2) = 4 * N := by rw [hNdef, pow_add]; ring
+    simpa only [pow_one] using Nat.pow_le_pow_right (show 0 < n + 1 by omega) (by decide : 1 ≤ 3)
+  have hn2 : (n + 1) ^ 2 ≤ P := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by decide)
+    have h2 : n + (labelWidth n + 1) + 1 ≤ 8 * (n + 1) := by unfold labelWidth; omega
+    have h3 : (2 * L + 1) + M + 1 ≤ 4 * (L + N / L + 1) := by omega
+      _ = 13824 * P * (L + N / L + 1) := by simp only [P]; ring
+    have h3L : 2 * L + 1 ≤ 3 * L := by omega
+    have hw : 4 * labelWidth n ≤ 24 * (n + 1) := by unfold labelWidth; omega
+    have e2 : (2 * L + 1) * (30 * n + 27) ≤ 3 * L * (57 * P) := Nat.mul_le_mul h3L (by omega)
+    have e3 : (2 * L + 1) * (4 * labelWidth n) ≤ 3 * L * (24 * P) :=
+    have hLP : L * P ≤ P * (L + N / L + 1) := by nlinarith
+/-- **Labels of periodic states.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`20000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L` computes the canonical label of every periodic state. -/
+theorem cyclic_label_circuit (c : Circuit signature n n) (L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) (hLN : L ≤ 2 ^ n) :
+        out.eval interpretation x = canonicalLabel (c.eval interpretation) x) ∧
+      out.size ≤ 20000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L := by
+  obtain ⟨H, hcard, hcover⟩ := exists_checkpoints_finite (c.eval interpretation) hL
+  let cp : Fin H.card → BitString n := fun j => (H.equivFin.symm j).val
+  have hcp : Function.Injective cp := fun _ _ h => H.equivFin.symm.injective (Subtype.ext h)
+  have hcov (x : BitString n) : Repeats (c.eval interpretation) x L ∨
+      ∃ t < 2 * L, ∃ j, (c.eval interpretation)^[t] x = cp j := by
+    rcases hcover x with hr | ⟨t, ht, hm⟩
+    · exact Or.inr ⟨t, ht, H.equivFin ⟨_, hm⟩, by simp [cp]⟩
+  obtain ⟨out, hout, hs⟩ := cyclic_labels_from_checkpoints c L hL hLN cp hcp hcov
+  exact ⟨out, hout, hs.trans (labelCost_le _ _ _ _ hL hLN (by simpa using hcard))⟩
+/-- Moving a state onto its cycle with `f^[(2 ^ n)!]` does not change its label. -/
+theorem canonicalLabel_iterate_factorial (f : BitString n → BitString n) (x : BitString n) :
+    canonicalLabel f (f^[(2 ^ n).factorial] x) = canonicalLabel f x := by
+  have hd := Nat.dvd_factorial (cycleLength_pos f x) (cycleLength_le_two_pow f x)
+    Nat.add_mod, Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd hd, Nat.add_zero, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (phase_lt f x)]
+theorem iterate_factorial_mem_periodicPts (f : BitString n → BitString n) (x : BitString n) :
+    f^[(2 ^ n).factorial] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f := by
+  have hd : transientDepth f x < 2 ^ n := by simpa using transientDepth_lt_card f x
+/-- **Cycle labels.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`60000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L` computes the canonical label of every state: the
+lexicographically least state of its eventual cycle, the cycle length and its phase. -/
+theorem cycle_label_circuit (c : Circuit signature n n) (L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) (hLN : L ≤ 2 ^ n) :
+      out.size ≤ 60000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L := by
+  obtain ⟨project, hp, hps⟩ := fixed_power n c (2 ^ n).factorial L hL hLN
+  obtain ⟨labels, hl, hls⟩ := cyclic_label_circuit c L hL hLN
+/-- **Square-root cycle labels.** Some circuit of size at most
+`180000 * optimizedBudget n c.size (2 ^ n)` computes the canonical label of every state. -/
+      (out.size : ℝ) ≤ 180000 * optimizedBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) := by
+  obtain ⟨L, hL, hLN, hopt⟩ := exists_powerBudget_le_optimizedBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) le_rfl
+  obtain ⟨out, hout, hs⟩ := cycle_label_circuit c L hL hLN
+  have hs' : (out.size : ℝ) ≤ 60000 * (powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L : ℝ) := by

+# Circuits for first targets and halting
+Let `c` compute `f` on `n`-bit states and let a circuit `p` recognize a target set. Stopping at
+targets is computed by a circuit of size `c.size + p.size + 4 * n` (`absorbing_circuit`), and
+`2 ^ n` steps of it reach the first target of every orbit that has one
+(`FunctionalGraph.absorb_iterate_card`). With the fixed-power bound this gives the first target
+state (`first_target_state`) and whether a target is ever reached (`target_reachability`). When
+the halting states are fixed by `f` itself, `2 ^ n` steps of `f` reach the halting configuration
+of every halting computation, and no recognizer is charged (`halting_computation`).
+The first visit to a target is the transient depth of the map that stops at targets
+(`FunctionalGraph.first_target_depth`), so the depth circuits give a reachability flag and the
+exact first target time (`first_target_time`, `first_target_time_optimized`), and the first
+The circuits are native De Morgan circuits: every NOT, AND and OR gate and every constant is
+charged, while wiring and fanout are free. They exist for each parameter choice; nothing here
+bounds the time to construct them. For halting computations the state holds every persistent
+bit of the computation, including its input and workspace.
+  first-time and halting-time bounds have the constants `3120000` and `3000000`.
+/-- **Absorbing targets.** The map that stops at states accepted by `p` and otherwise applies
+`c` has a circuit of size at most `c.size + p.size + 4 * n`. -/
+theorem absorbing_circuit (c : Circuit signature n n) (p : Circuit signature n 1) :
+        (absorb (c.eval interpretation) fun x => p.eval interpretation x 0 = true) ∧
+  have hc := Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs n) c (fun i x => x i)
+  have hp : Synthesis interpretation (inputs n) {fun x => p.eval interpretation x 0} p.size :=
+    (Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs n) p (fun i x => x i)
+      fun i => ⟨i, rfl⟩).mono Set.Subset.rfl (by rintro _ rfl; exact ⟨0, rfl⟩) le_rfl
+  have hi : Synthesis interpretation (inputs n) (wires fun x : BitString n => x) 0 :=
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, hs⟩ := (synthesis_ite hi hc hp).exists_circuit_outputs
+  refine ⟨g, fun x => ?_, by simpa using hs⟩
+  by_cases hx : p.eval interpretation x 0 = true <;> simp [absorb, hx]
+/-- **First target states.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`40000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L` returns a state accepted by `p`
+exactly when the orbit of its input ever reaches one, and then returns the first such state,
+theorem first_target_state (c : Circuit signature n n) (p : Circuit signature n 1) (L : ℕ)
+      (∀ x, p.eval interpretation (out.eval interpretation x) 0 = true ↔
+        ∃ t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x) 0 = true) ∧
+      (∀ x, (∃ t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x) 0 = true) →
+        ∃ t < 2 ^ n, out.eval interpretation x = (c.eval interpretation)^[t] x ∧
+          ∀ j < t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[j] x) 0 ≠ true) ∧
+      out.size ≤ 40000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L := by
+  let P := fun x => p.eval interpretation x 0 = true
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgs⟩ := absorbing_circuit c p
+  obtain ⟨out, hout, hs⟩ := fixed_power n g (2 ^ n) L hL hLN
+  have hcard : Fintype.card (BitString n) = 2 ^ n := by simp
+  have ho (x) : out.eval interpretation x = (absorb f P)^[Fintype.card (BitString n)] x := by
+  refine ⟨out, fun x => ?_, fun x hx => ?_, hs.trans ?_⟩
+  · obtain ⟨t, ht, hp, hfirst, heq⟩ := absorb_iterate_card f P x hx
+    exact ⟨t, hcard ▸ ht, (ho x).trans heq, hp, hfirst⟩
+/-- **Target reachability.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`40000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L + p.size` decides whether the orbit
+of its input ever reaches a state accepted by `p`. -/
+theorem target_reachability (c : Circuit signature n n) (p : Circuit signature n 1) (L : ℕ)
+        ∃ t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x) 0 = true) ∧
+      out.size ≤ 40000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L + p.size := by
+  obtain ⟨state, hp, -, hs⟩ := first_target_state c p L hL hLN
+/-- **Halting computations.** If `c` fixes every halting state and the orbit of every initial
+state halts, then for every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n` some circuit of size at most
+`40000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L` returns the halting state of every initial state, first
+reached before time `2 ^ n`. No circuit recognizing halting states is needed. -/
+theorem halting_computation (c : Circuit signature n n) (H : BitString n → Prop)
+    (initial : Set (BitString n)) (hstop : ∀ x, H x → c.eval interpretation x = x)
+    (hhalt : ∀ x ∈ initial, ∃ t, H ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x)) (L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L)
+        ∃ t < 2 ^ n, out.eval interpretation x = (c.eval interpretation)^[t] x ∧
+      out.size ≤ 40000 * powerBudget n c.size (2 ^ n) L := by
+  have ha : absorb f H = f := by
+  obtain ⟨out, hout, hs⟩ := fixed_power n c (2 ^ n) L hL hLN
+  obtain ⟨t, ht, hp, hfirst, he⟩ := absorb_iterate_card f H x (hhalt x hx)
+  have hcard : Fintype.card (BitString n) = 2 ^ n := by simp
+  have ho : out.eval interpretation x = f^[t] x := (hout x).trans he
+  exact ⟨ho ▸ hp, t, hcard ▸ ht, ho, hfirst⟩
+/-- **First target times.** For every `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n`, some circuit of size at most
+`90000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L + p.size` returns a flag, set exactly
+when the orbit of its input reaches a state accepted by `p`, followed by `n + 2` bits. When the
+flag is set they are the first time a target is visited, which is below `2 ^ n`; otherwise
+theorem first_target_time (c : Circuit signature n n) (p : Circuit signature n 1) (L : ℕ)
+        ∃ t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x) 0 = true) ∧
+        let t := (word fun i : Fin (n + 2) => out.eval interpretation x (Fin.natAdd 1 i)).toNat
+          (∀ j < t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[j] x) 0 ≠ true) ∧ t < 2 ^ n) ∧
+      out.size ≤ 90000 * powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L + p.size := by
+  let P := fun x => p.eval interpretation x 0 = true
+  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgs⟩ := absorbing_circuit c p
+  have he : g.eval interpretation = absorb f P := funext hg
+  obtain ⟨depth, hd, hds⟩ := checkpoint_depth_circuit g L hL hLN
+  obtain ⟨flag, hf, hfs⟩ := target_reachability c p L hL hLN
+  have hdepth := Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs n) depth (fun i x => x i)
+  have hflag := Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs n) flag (fun i x => x i)
+  let output := fun x => Fin.append (flag.eval interpretation x) (depth.eval interpretation x)
+    (show wires output ⊆ wires (fun x => flag.eval interpretation x) ∪
+      wires (fun x => depth.eval interpretation x) by
+      | left i => exact Or.inl ⟨i, by simp only [output, Fin.append_left]⟩
+      | right i => exact Or.inr ⟨i, by simp only [output, Fin.append_right]⟩) le_rfl
+  have hflagout (x) : out.eval interpretation x 0 = flag.eval interpretation x 0 := by
+  refine ⟨out, fun x => by rw [hflagout, hf], fun x hx => ?_, hsize.trans ?_⟩
+  · have hex := (hf x).mp (by rwa [hflagout] at hx)
+    have hb : transientDepth (absorb f P) x < 2 ^ n := by
+      simpa using transientDepth_lt_card (absorb f P) x
+    have ht : (word fun i : Fin (n + 2) => out.eval interpretation x (Fin.natAdd 1 i)).toNat =
+    exact ⟨(first_target_depth f P x hex).1, (first_target_depth f P x hex).2, hb⟩
+  · have hb : powerBudget n g.size (2 ^ n) L ≤
+        powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L := by
+/-- **Square-root first target times.** Some circuit of size at most
+`270000 * optimizedBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) + p.size` returns the
+reachability flag and, when it is set, the first target time, as in `first_target_time`. -/
+theorem first_target_time_optimized (c : Circuit signature n n) (p : Circuit signature n 1) :
+        ∃ t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[t] x) 0 = true) ∧
+        let t := (word fun i : Fin (n + 2) => out.eval interpretation x (Fin.natAdd 1 i)).toNat
+          (∀ j < t, p.eval interpretation ((c.eval interpretation)^[j] x) 0 ≠ true) ∧ t < 2 ^ n) ∧
+        270000 * optimizedBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) + p.size := by
+    exists_powerBudget_le_optimizedBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) le_rfl
+  obtain ⟨out, hf, ht, hs⟩ := first_target_time c p L hL hLN
+      90000 * (powerBudget n (c.size + p.size + 4 * n) (2 ^ n) L : ℝ) + p.size := by
+/-- **Halting times.** If `c` fixes every halting state and the orbit of every initial state

+For every `k`, some language in `Σ₂` has no circuits of size `O(n ^ k)`: it lies in no class
+[Kannan][Kannan1982], [Arora and Barak, Chapter 6][AroraBarak09]. Size counts gates, as in
+Kannan's language (`Cslib.Complexity.Kannan.language`) is first built in `Σ₃`. At input length
+`n`, let `m = (k + 3) (⌊log₂ (n + 1)⌋ + 1)`; the language evaluates, on the first `m` bits of the
+input, the function of the first truth table on `m` inputs, in lexicographic order, that needs
+more than `(n + 1) ^ (k + 1)` gates. Shannon's counting argument provides such tables at all
+large lengths. Fixing the inputs after the first `m` to `false` turns the slice of the language
+at length `n` into the hard function and adds at most two gates, so the language is in no
+`SIZE (c (n + 1) ^ k)` (`Cslib.Complexity.Kannan.language_notMem_SIZE`). A truth table has at
+most `2 ^ (k + 3) (n + 1) ^ (k + 3)` bits and the MCSP verifier checks circuits for it in
+polynomial time, so a `Σ₃` verifier guesses the table `T`, then for every table `T'` and every
+circuit `c` of at most `(n + 1) ^ (k + 1)` gates guesses such a circuit `c'`, and checks that `c`
+does not compute `T`, that `c'` computes `T'` if `T'` comes before `T`, and that `T` gives `true`

+The error `1 / 3` in the definition of `BPP` (`Cslib.Complexity.BPP`) can be made exponentially
+small [Arora and Barak, Section 7.4.1][AroraBarak09]. Cut the random string into `2 r(n)` blocks of

+If `SAT` has circuits of polynomial size, the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level
+[Karp and Lipton][KarpLipton1980], [Arora and Barak, Theorem 6.19][AroraBarak09]. The hypothesis is
+that some language `L ∈ P/poly` contains exactly the encodings `encCNF φ` of the satisfiable
+formulas; it follows from `NP ⊆ P/poly`, for problems with any encoding of their instances.
+`a ∈ A ↔ ∀ u, ∃ v, V (a, u ++ v)`. The pairs `(a, u)` for which some `v` is accepted form a
+`f` maps to `SAT`. A `Σ₂` verifier guesses circuits for `SAT` on all the lengths the
+self-reduction (`Cslib.Complexity.SAT.search`) of a formula `f (a, u)` asks about, and then checks,
+for every `u`, that the self-reduction answered by the guessed circuits finds a satisfying
+assignment of `f (a, u)`. A satisfying assignment proves `(a, u)` in the problem whatever circuits
+were guessed, and correct circuits always find one when there is one. Since `Π₂ ⊆ Σ₂` holds for
+every encoding of instances, the hierarchy collapses to `Σ₂`
+The guessed circuits are listed in an advice string (`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.familyAdvice`): the
+circuits `C 0, …, C N`, each in the certificate format of
+`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.readCertificate`, padded to a common length. The circuit for an input `x`
+is read from the block at position `x.length` and evaluated on `x`
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.familyAdvice`: the advice string listing a family of circuits.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.evalAdvice`: evaluation of the circuit for the length of the input read
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.evalAdvice_familyAdvice`: evaluation from the advice string of a family
+* `Cslib.Complexity.mem_NP_setOf_exists_append`: the inner existential quantifier of a `Π₂`
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PiP_two_subset_SigmaP_two_of_SAT`: if `SAT` has circuits of polynomial size,
+* [R. M. Karp, R. J. Lipton, *Some connections between nonuniform and uniform complexity
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Section 6.4][AroraBarak09]

+# Alternating polynomial time as a game of moves
+An alternating machine running within `t` steps plays a game of `t` moves, each chosen by the
+player that the state labels. This file makes the order of the players fixed: an existential and
+a universal move per step. The strict table of a machine (`Turing.MultiTapeATM.strict`) spends two
+coins on each step of the machine: it stores the first coin, and on the second takes the step of
+the machine with the second coin in a universal state and with the first in an existential state.
+The coin that is not used is a vacuous move. Hence, if every branch halts within `t` steps, the
+machine accepts within `t` moves exactly when the existential player wins the game of `2 * t`
+single-bit moves, alternately chosen by an existential and a universal player, in which the
+existential player wins when the strict table, replayed from the moves, emits `[true]`

+# Deterministic space classes and the space hierarchy theorem
+`Cslib.Complexity.DSPACE enc s` consists of the problems that some machine with a binary alphabet
+and finitely many states decides within space `c₁ * s n + c₂`, for constants `c₁` and `c₂`, on
+instances whose encoding under `enc` has length `n`, within some time bound of `n` (upstream
+definition of the classes proposed upstream in cslib pull request #767, stated for encoded
+instances, beside `Cslib.Complexity.DTIME`. Space counts the visited work-tape cells: the input
+tape is read-only and the output tape write-only. The time bound is no restriction
+(`Cslib.Complexity.mem_DSPACE_iff`): a machine that halts within space `s n` halts within the
+number of its configurations, `(n + 2) * 2 ^ O(s n)`, a function of `n`
+`DSPACE s ⊆ DTIME ((n + 2) * 2 ^ (c * s n))` for a constant `c` of the decider
+(`Cslib.Complexity.exists_mem_DTIME_of_mem_DSPACE`), and `DTIME t ⊆ DSPACE t`. As in #767, `L` is
+`DSPACE (log₂)` and `PSPACE` the union of the classes `DSPACE (n ^ k)`.
+A bound `s` is *space-constructible* (`Cslib.Complexity.SpaceConstructible`) when such a machine
+computes `s n` in binary from any word of length `n` within space `O(s n)`; time-constructible
+bounds are, and so are the constants, `n`, `(n + 1) ^ k` and `2 ^ n`.
+`Cslib.Complexity.spaceDiagonal G` runs the machine described at the start of its input `x`, when
+the description is short (`Cslib.Complexity.Diagonal.shortDesc`), on `x` with the universal machine
+within a space budget (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetedUniversal`): for `2 ^ G n` steps, with
+the configurations of the simulation encoded within `G n` bits. It negates the verdict, and answers
+`false` on other inputs. The budgeted universal machine is the in-place universal run with a budget
+test at the end of each pass, within space linear in the description, the budget and the lengths
+of the clock and of `n` in binary (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetSpace_le`). The diagonal
+also holds its input, to test shortness and to convert it to symbols, so it takes space
+`O(n + G n)` (`Cslib.Complexity.computableTidilyInO_spaceDiagonal`) and decides a problem in
+Let a machine decide the same problem within space `c₁ * f n + c₂`, where every `c * f n + c` is
+eventually below `G n`. It halts within its number of configurations, `(n + 2) * 2 ^ O(f n)`, which
+is eventually below the clock. The configurations of its simulation take `O(f n + log n)` bits,
+with a factor linear in its description: the overhead of the universal machine is a constant factor
+for each simulated machine, eventually within the budget. So on its own description, padded, the
+diagonal answers the negation of its answer (`Cslib.Complexity.setOf_spaceDiagonal_notMem_DSPACE`).

+The gap `f = o(g)` is the textbook one. The lower bound `n ≤ g n`, where the textbook asks
+`log n ≤ g n`, is the space the diagonal takes to hold its input; hierarchies below linear space

+  bound on the time of a space-bounded computation.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.spaceDiagonal_desc`: the diagonal negates the answer of a machine on its padded
+  description, within the clock and the budget.

+/-- **The diagonal within space `G` decides a problem in `DSPACE G`**, for a space-constructible
+    (hn : ∀ n, n ≤ G n) : {x | spaceDiagonal G x = true} ∈ DSPACE encBits G := by
+/-- On a short padded description, the diagonal within space `G` negates the answer of a machine
+that halts within the clock `2 ^ G n` and whose simulated configurations fit within the budget
+theorem spaceDiagonal_desc {k : ℕ} {State : Type} [Fintype State] (eS : State ↪ ℕ)
+    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool State) (pad : List Bool) (G : ℕ → ℕ) {b : Bool}
+    (hshort : shortDesc (frame (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)) ++ pad) = true)
+    (hbudget : cfgSpace (desc eS eBit tm) ((frame (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)) ++ pad).map eBit)
+    spaceDiagonal G (frame (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)) ++ pad) = !b := by
+  rw [decodeDesc_unframe_frame_append, budgetedUniversal_desc eS eBit tm _ _ _ hbudget]
+/-- Eventually, `n + 1` has at most `n / 4` binary digits. -/
+/-- **The diagonal argument for space.** If every `c * f n + c` is eventually below `G n` and
+`n ≤ G n`, the problem of the diagonal within space `G` is not in `DSPACE f`. A decider within
+space `O(f)` halts within its number of configurations, `2 ^ O(f n)` times a polynomial, which is
+eventually below the clock `2 ^ G n`, and the configurations of its simulation take
+`O(f n + log n)` bits, eventually within the budget `G n`; so on its own description, padded to a
+short one beyond these points, the diagonal answers the negation of its answer. -/
+theorem setOf_spaceDiagonal_notMem_DSPACE {f G : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : ∀ n, n ≤ G n)
+    (hfG : ∀ c, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c * f n + c ≤ G n) :
+    {x | spaceDiagonal G x = true} ∉ DSPACE encBits f := by
+  obtain ⟨g, ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, htm⟩, hg⟩ := decidableInTimeAndSpace_iff.mp hA
+  let eS : State ↪ ℕ := (Fintype.equivFin State).toEmbedding.trans Fin.valEmbedding
+  set D := descLen (desc eS eBit tm) with hD
+  set P := 6 * (2 * D + 5) * (c₁ + c₂) + 3 * D + 4 with hP
+  set base := storageBoundBase Bool State k
+  have hpoly : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ((n + 2) * base) ^ 2 < 2 ^ n :=
+  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp ((((hfG (2 * e * (c₁ + c₂))).and (hfG (2 * P))).and
+  -- the description, padded beyond `N` and to a length where it is short
+  suffices ∀ pad : List Bool, N + 2 ^ (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)).length ≤ pad.length → False from
+  have hpow := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)).length)
+  have hlen : (frame (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)) ++ pad).length =
+  have hshort : shortDesc (frame (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)) ++ pad) = true := by
+  generalize hx : frame (eDesc (desc eS eBit tm)) ++ pad = x at hlen hshort
+  obtain ⟨⟨⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h₃⟩, h₄⟩ := hN x.length (by omega)
+  set s := c₁ * f x.length + c₂ with hs
+  have hsf : s ≤ (c₁ + c₂) * (f x.length + 1) := by rw [hs]; nlinarith
+  -- the decider halts within the clock
+  have hclock : (x.length + 2) * storageBound Bool State k s ≤ 2 ^ G x.length := by
+    have he : 2 * (e * s) ≤ G x.length := by
+          2 * e * (c₁ + c₂) * f x.length + 2 * e * (c₁ + c₂) := by ring
+      have e₂ : 2 * (e * s) = 2 * e * s := by ring
+    have hsq : ((x.length + 2) * base * 2 ^ (e * s)) ^ 2 ≤ (2 ^ G x.length) ^ 2 := by
+  -- the configurations of the simulation fit within the budget
+  have hbudget : cfgSpace (desc eS eBit tm) (x.map eBit) (2 ^ G x.length) ≤ G x.length := by
+    have hsp : simSpace (desc eS eBit tm) (x.map eBit) (2 ^ G x.length) ≤ s := by
+    have hk : (desc eS eBit tm).tapes ≤ D := by
+      simp only [hD, descLen, eDesc_apply, length_encPair, encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate]
+    have hP' : 6 * (2 * D + 5) * s + 3 * D + 4 ≤ P * (f x.length + 1) := by
+      have e₁ : P * (f x.length + 1) = 6 * (2 * D + 5) * ((c₁ + c₂) * (f x.length + 1)) +
+      have : 3 * D + 4 ≤ (3 * D + 4) * (f x.length + 1) := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
+    have e₂ : 2 * P * f x.length + 2 * P = 2 * (P * (f x.length + 1)) := by ring
+    have e₃ : 3 * (2 * D + 5) * 2 * simSpace (desc eS eBit tm) (x.map eBit) (2 ^ G x.length) ≤
+  -- so the diagonal negates the answer of the decider
+  have hd : spaceDiagonal G x = !g x := by
+    exact spaceDiagonal_desc eS tm pad G hshort hbudget hhalt hout
+/-- **The space hierarchy theorem.** If `g` is space-constructible, `n ≤ g n`, and every
+`c * f n + c` is eventually below `g n`, then `DSPACE f` is strictly contained in `DSPACE g`
+[Sipser, Theorem 9.3 and Corollary 9.4][Sipser2013], [Arora and Barak, Theorem 4.8][AroraBarak09].
+The universal machine simulates within a budget with a constant overhead for each simulated
+machine, so the gap is the textbook `f = o(g)`; the condition `n ≤ g n`, where the textbook asks
+`log n ≤ g n`, is the space the diagonal takes to hold its input and decode its description. -/
+theorem DSPACE_ssubset_DSPACE {f g : ℕ → ℕ} (hg : SpaceConstructible g) (hn : ∀ n, n ≤ g n)
+    (hfg : ∀ c, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c * f n + c ≤ g n) : DSPACE encBits f ⊂ DSPACE encBits g := by
+  have hsub : DSPACE encBits f ⊆ DSPACE encBits g := DSPACE_mono_of_eventually_le <| by
+/-- **Logarithmic space is strictly within polynomial space**: `L ⊆ DSPACE n`, and the diagonal
+within space `(n + 1) ^ 2` is in `PSPACE` but not in `DSPACE n`. This is the deterministic part of
+theorem L_ssubset_PSPACE : L encBits ⊂ PSPACE encBits := by
+  have hL : L encBits ⊆ DSPACE encBits fun n => n := fun A hA =>
+      fun n => (Nat.le_succ n).trans (Nat.le_self_pow two_ne_zero _)), fun h =>
+/-- **Polynomial space has a strict hierarchy**: `DSPACE (n ^ k) ⊂ DSPACE (n ^ (k + 1))`
+[Sipser, Corollary 9.5][Sipser2013]. The diagonal within space `(n + 1) ^ (k + 1)` separates
+    DSPACE encBits (· ^ k) ⊂ DSPACE encBits (· ^ (k + 1)) := by
+  have hsub : DSPACE encBits (· ^ k) ⊆ DSPACE encBits (· ^ (k + 1)) :=
+      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hpos
+      · rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with rfl | hk <;> simp_all
+      · have : n ^ k ≤ n ^ (k + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hpos (Nat.le_succ k)
+  have h₁ : n ^ k ≤ (n + 1) ^ k := Nat.pow_le_pow_left (Nat.le_succ n) k

+# The universal machine within a space budget
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetedUniversal (d, x, t, b)` runs the machine described by `d` on
+`x` for `t` steps, as the universal function does, but within the *budget* `b`: a step whose
+configuration of the simulation is encoded by more than `b` bits is not taken, and the simulation
+stays at the last configuration within the budget (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetStep`). It
+returns the first two symbols of the output and whether the machine has halted: enough to tell
+whether the output is a single given symbol, without storing an output that may be as long as the
+It is computed by the in-place run of the universal machine
+multi-pass fold over the input, one pass per step, reading the symbol under the simulated input
+head by counting down the symbols of `x`, with the budget and the first two symbols of the output
+added to its state, and a budget test at the end of each pass. So it is tidily computable within
+space linear in `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetSpace`: the description, the budget, the
+number of steps and the length of `x` in binary, and the largest symbol of `x`
+itself or the space the described machine would use beyond the budget.
+Within the budget it agrees with the universal function
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetedUniversal_eq_of_le`), and on the description of a machine
+it returns the first two symbols of the output of the machine whenever the bound
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.cfgSpace` on the configurations of the simulation, linear in the
+cells the machine visits, is within the budget
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetStep`: a step of the simulation within a budget.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetedUniversal`: the universal function within a space budget.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetSpace`: the bound on the states of its fold.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetStep_iterate`: the run within the budget is the run of the
+  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetedUniversal_desc`: within the budget, the universal function.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.budgetSpace_le`: `budgetSpace` is linear in the description, the
+  budget and the lengths of the number of steps and of the length of the input in binary, plus
+  the largest symbol of the input.
+The fold reuses the parts of the in-place fold (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.foldNext`,
+in-place fold, and its proof of computability adapts that of
+Reitwiessner. The events of the input, the extraction of the parts the initial state reads, the
+bounds on the countdown and the simplified time bound restate private lemmas and the extracting
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.eInS`, whose input ends in a budget.
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, Theorem 9.3][Sipser2013]: the
+  simulation within a space budget in the proof of the space hierarchy theorem.
+/-- A step of the simulation within the budget `b`, keeping the first two symbols of the output:

+/-- **The universal function within a space budget.** The machine described by `i.1` runs on the

+first two symbols of its output and whether it has halted. -/

+The construction of Goldreich, Goldwasser and Micali [GGM1986] turns a length-doubling generator
+`G` with seeds of `k` bits into a keyed family of functions: the key labels the root of a binary
+tree of depth `n`, the two children of a node labelled `s` are labelled by the two blocks of `k`
+bits of `G s` (`Cslib.BitString.block`), and the value at an input `x` of `n` bits is the label
+of the leaf reached by following `x` (`evalBits`). This is the list-based `Cslib.Crypto.GGM.eval`
+for words of fixed width (`ofFn_evalBits`). Keeping the first bit of the label gives a keyed
+family of Boolean functions (`booleanFamily`), the family used by Razborov and Rudich
+This module proves the nonuniform security of that family with concrete losses. Circuit sizes
+count every AND, OR, NOT and constant gate of the De Morgan basis, and the tests are deterministic
+circuits on the whole truth table (`Cslib.Crypto.PRG.IsCircuitTest`), which query the
+function at every input. Write `C` for the circuit complexity of `G` as a function with `2 k`
+* **Size of the members.** Every function of the family is computed with `n (C + 4 k) + 2`
+* **Security.** If no test with `t + 2 ^ n (n C + 1)` gates distinguishes `G` from uniform with
+  advantage more than `ε`, then no test with `t` gates distinguishes the truth table of a random
+  member of the family from a uniformly random truth table with advantage more than
+  `(2 ^ n - 1) ε` (`secure_truthTableGenerator_booleanFamily`). The proof is the hybrid argument
+  over the levels of the tree. The hybrid at depth `j` labels the `2 ^ j` nodes at depth `j`
+  uniformly at random; between depths `j` and `j + 1`, the `2 ^ j` expansions are replaced by
+  uniform strings one at a time (`Cslib.Crypto.PRG.abs_expect_comp_sub_expect_le`). Fixing all
+  of them but one turns a test of truth tables into a test of that expansion, which computes the
+  subtree below it; every bit of the truth table is then a constant or a bit of an evaluation
