+/-- A generator of fixed-width strings as a generator of lists: it reads the first `k` bits of its
+  fun seed => List.ofFn (G fun i => seed.getD i false)
+/-- The block selected by a bit is the child selected by `Cslib.Crypto.GGM.selectChild`. -/
+    List.ofFn (BitString.block y (finTwoEquiv.symm bit)) = selectChild k (List.ofFn y) bit := by
+    cases bit <;> simp [selectChild, finProdFinEquiv, finTwoEquiv, Nat.add_comm]
+/-- **Agreement with the list construction.** Evaluation with labels of fixed width is
+`Cslib.Crypto.GGM.eval` for the generator read as a generator of lists. -/
+    List.ofFn (evalBits G seed x) = eval (listGenerator G) (List.ofFn seed) (List.ofFn x) := by
+/-- **The GGM family of Boolean functions** [RazborovRudich1997]: the function with key `seed`
+maps an input of `n` bits to the first bit of the label it reaches in the GGM tree. -/
+def booleanFamily [NeZero k] (G : PRG.Generator (BitString k) (BitString (2 * k))) (n : ℕ)
+  fun x => evalBits G seed x 0
+/-- Evaluation along a fixed query of length `n` costs at most `n` copies of a circuit for the
+generator: as a function of the seed, each step is the generator followed by a wiring. -/
+    complexity interpretation (fun seed => evalBits G seed x) ≤
+    have h : (fun seed : BitString k => evalBits G seed x) = fun seed => seed ∘ id := rfl
+    have h : (fun seed : BitString k => evalBits G seed x) =
+          (fun y => y ∘ fun i : Fin k => finProdFinEquiv (finTwoEquiv.symm (x 0), i)) ∘ ⇑G := rfl
+      (fun y => y ∘ fun i : Fin k => finProdFinEquiv (finTwoEquiv.symm (x 0), i))
+/-- One bit of the evaluation along a fixed query of length `n`, as a function of a string of
+length `2 k` whose selected block is the seed, costs at most `n` copies of a circuit for the
+    complexity interpretation (single fun y => evalBits G (BitString.block y b) x i) ≤
+  have h : (single fun y => evalBits G (BitString.block y b) x i) =
+      (fun z => z ∘ fun _ : Fin 1 => i) ∘ (fun seed => evalBits G seed x) ∘
+        (fun y => y ∘ fun i : Fin k => finProdFinEquiv (b, i)) := rfl
+/-- **Circuits for tree evaluation.** If the bits of a seed and of a query of length `n` are
+available, the bits of the label reached are synthesized with, per query bit, a smallest circuit
+for the generator and `k` multiplexers of four gates. -/
+    {s : Set (BooleanFunction N)} (seed : BitString N → BitString k)
+    (query : BitString N → BitString n) (hseed : ∀ i, (fun z => seed z i) ∈ s)
+    (hquery : ∀ i, (fun z => query z i) ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis interpretation s (Set.range fun i z => evalBits G (seed z) (query z) i)
+  induction n generalizing s seed with
+    -- the expansion of the current label, by a smallest circuit for the generator
+    have h1 : Synthesis interpretation s (Set.range fun j z => G (seed z) j)
+      have h := Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) c (fun i z => seed z i) hseed
+    -- the block selected by the first query bit, by one multiplexer per bit
+    have h2 : Synthesis interpretation (s ∪ Set.range fun j z => G (seed z) j)
+        (Set.range fun i z => BitString.block (G (seed z)) (finTwoEquiv.symm (query z 0)) i)
+        (s := s ∪ Set.range fun j z => G (seed z) j)
+        (fun i : Fin k => fun z => BitString.block (G (seed z)) (finTwoEquiv.symm (query z 0)) i)
+          have hmux := Synthesis.mux (s := s ∪ Set.range fun j z => G (seed z) j)
+      (s := s ∪ Set.range fun i z => BitString.block (G (seed z)) (finTwoEquiv.symm (query z 0)) i)
+      (fun i => Or.inr ⟨i, rfl⟩) (fun i => Or.inl (hquery i.succ))
+    exact ((h1.trans h2).trans h3).mono Set.Subset.rfl Set.Subset.rfl (le_of_eq (by ring))
+/-- **The members of the GGM family have small circuits**: two constants for the key, then per
+input bit a smallest circuit for the generator and `k` multiplexers of four gates. -/
+    (G : PRG.Generator (BitString k) (BitString (2 * k))) (n : ℕ) (seed : BitString k) :
+  have hconst := (Synthesis.const (s := inputs n) false).union (Synthesis.const true)
+  have h := synthesis_evalBits G (s := inputs n ∪ ({fun _ => false} ∪ {fun _ => true}))
+    (fun _ => seed) id (fun i => by cases seed i <;> simp) (fun i => Or.inl ⟨i, rfl⟩)
+/-- The first bits of uniformly random labels are uniformly random. -/
+    𝔼 L : ι → BitString k, F (fun x => L x 0) = 𝔼 f, F f := by
+  let e : (ι → Fin (k + 1) → Bool) ≃ (ι → Bool) × (ι → Fin k → Bool) :=
+  rw [← Fintype.expect_comp_fst (β := ι → Fin k → Bool) F]
+/-- The leaves of a hybrid tree of depth `n = j + m`: the labels at depth `j` are given, and the
+remaining `m` levels are expanded by the generator. -/
+private def leaves (G : PRG.Generator (BitString k) (BitString (2 * k))) (j m : ℕ)
+    (h : j + m = n) (labels : BitString j → BitString k) (x : BitString n) : BitString k :=
+  evalBits G (labels fun i : Fin j => x ⟨i, by omega⟩) fun i : Fin m => x ⟨j + i, by omega⟩
+/-- The labels at depth `j + 1` given by the expansions of the labels at depth `j`: the label of
+`p` is the block of the expansion at `Fin.init p` selected by its last bit. Expansions and labels
+private def reshape : (BitString j → BitString (2 * k)) ≃ (BitString (j + 1) → BitString k) :=
+private theorem reshape_apply (Y : BitString j → BitString (2 * k)) (p : BitString (j + 1)) :
+    reshape Y p = BitString.block (Y (Fin.init p)) (finTwoEquiv.symm (p (Fin.last j))) :=
+/-- Expanding one level of a hybrid tree. -/
+    (h : j + (m + 1) = n) (labels : BitString j → BitString k) :
+      leaves G (j + 1) m (by omega) (reshape fun q => G (labels q)) := by
+/-- The probability that a test of truth tables accepts the hybrid with uniformly random labels at
+private noncomputable def hybridProb (G : PRG.Generator (BitString k) (BitString (2 * k)))
+    (D : BitString (2 ^ n) → Bool) (j m : ℕ) (h : j + m = n) : ℝ :=
+  𝔼 labels : BitString j → BitString k,
+    if D (truthTable n fun x => leaves G j m h labels x 0) then 1 else 0
+/-- **One hybrid step.** If no test obtained from `D` by fixing all expansions at depth `j` but
+one distinguishes the generator with advantage more than `ε`, the hybrids at depths `j` and
+`j + 1` differ by at most `2 ^ j ε`. -/
+    (D : BitString (2 ^ n) → Bool) (h : j + (m + 1) = n) {ε : ℝ}
+    (hε : ∀ (c : BitString j → BitString (2 * k)) (q : BitString j),
+          leaves G (j + 1) m (by omega) (reshape (update c q (G a))) x 0) then 1 else 0 : ℝ) -
+        𝔼 b, (if D (truthTable n fun x =>
+          leaves G (j + 1) m (by omega) (reshape (update c q b)) x 0) then 1 else 0 : ℝ)| ≤ ε) :
+    |hybridProb G D j (m + 1) h - hybridProb G D (j + 1) m (by omega)| ≤ 2 ^ j * ε := by
+  have h0 : hybridProb G D j (m + 1) h = 𝔼 labels : BitString j → BitString k,
+      (if D (truthTable n fun x => leaves G (j + 1) m (by omega)
+        (reshape fun q => G (labels q)) x 0) then 1 else 0 : ℝ) := by
+  have h1 : hybridProb G D (j + 1) m (by omega) = 𝔼 Y : BitString j → BitString (2 * k),
+      (if D (truthTable n fun x => leaves G (j + 1) m (by omega) (reshape Y) x 0)
+    (fun Y => (if D (truthTable n fun x => leaves G (j + 1) m (by omega) (reshape Y) x 0)
+/-- **The size of the reduction.** Fixing all expansions at depth `j` but the one at `q`, a test
+of truth tables becomes a test of that expansion. Each bit of the truth table is then a constant or
+a bit of the evaluation along the remaining `m` levels, so the test costs at most `2 ^ n (m C + 1)`
+gates more than the test of truth tables, where `C` is the circuit complexity of the
+    (D : BitString (2 ^ n) → Bool) (h : j + 1 + m = n)
+    (c : BitString j → BitString (2 * k)) (q : BitString j) :
+    complexity interpretation (single fun y => D (truthTable n fun x =>
+        leaves G (j + 1) m h (reshape (update c q y)) x 0)) ≤
+      2 ^ n * (m * complexity interpretation ⇑G + 1) + complexity interpretation (single D) := by
+  refine (complexity_comp_le (fun y => truthTable n fun x =>
+    leaves G (j + 1) m h (reshape (update c q y)) x 0) (single D)).trans
+  refine (complexity_pi_le (I := interpretation) fun i y => truthTable n (fun x =>
+    leaves G (j + 1) m h (reshape (update c q y)) x 0) i).trans ?_
+  refine (sum_le_sum (g := fun _ => m * complexity interpretation ⇑G + 1) fun i _ => ?_).trans_eq
+  -- the bit of the truth table at the input `x`
+  set p : BitString (j + 1) := fun l => x ⟨l, by omega⟩
+  · have he : (fun y => truthTable n (fun x =>
+        leaves G (j + 1) m h (reshape (update c q y)) x 0) i) =
+        fun y => evalBits G (BitString.block y (finTwoEquiv.symm (p (Fin.last j))))
+          (fun l : Fin m => x ⟨j + 1 + l, by omega⟩) 0 := by
+  · have he : (fun y => truthTable n (fun x =>
+        leaves G (j + 1) m h (reshape (update c q y)) x 0) i) =
+          (fun l : Fin m => x ⟨j + 1 + l, by omega⟩) 0 := by
+/-- The first hybrid is the GGM family with a uniformly random key. -/
+  have hx (x : BitString n) : (fun i : Fin n => x ⟨0 + i, by omega⟩) = x :=
+  have hL (x : BitString n) : L (fun i : Fin 0 => x ⟨i, by omega⟩) =
+/-- The last hybrid is a uniformly random function. -/
+    ← Fintype.expect_equiv (truthTable n) (fun f => if D (truthTable n f) then (1 : ℝ) else 0) _
+/-! ### Security of the GGM family against circuits -/
+/-- **The GGM family is pseudorandom against circuits** [GGM1986], [RazborovRudich1997]. Let `G`
+be a length-doubling generator with labels of width `k ≥ 1` whose circuit complexity is `C`. If no
+test computed with `t + 2 ^ n (n C + 1)` gates distinguishes the output of `G` from uniform with
+advantage more than `ε`, then no test computed with `t` gates distinguishes the truth table of the
+GGM function on `n` inputs with a uniformly random key from a uniformly random truth table with
+The proof is the hybrid argument over the levels of the tree, where the hybrid at depth `j`
+labels the nodes at depth `j` uniformly at random. Between depths `j` and `j + 1` the `2 ^ j`
+expansions are replaced by uniform strings one at a time; fixing the others, a test of truth
+tables computes the subtree below the remaining one with at most `2 ^ n (n C + 1)` more
+    (truthTableGenerator (booleanFamily G n)).Secure (IsCircuitTest t) ((2 ^ n - 1) * ε) := by
+  -- the hybrids at depths `j` and `n` differ by at most `(2 ^ n - 2 ^ j) ε`
+  have htel (m : ℕ) : ∀ j (h : j + m = n),
+      |hybridProb G D j m h - hybridProb G D n 0 (add_zero n)| ≤ (2 ^ n - 2 ^ j) * ε := by
+      have hstep := abs_hybridProb_sub_le G D h (ε := ε) fun c q => by
+        have hslice := complexity_slice_le G D (j := j) (m := m) (by omega) c q
+        have hadv := hG (fun y => PMF.pure (D (truthTable n fun x =>
+          leaves G (j + 1) m (by omega) (reshape (update c q y)) x 0)))
+      calc _ ≤ |hybridProb G D j (m + 1) h - hybridProb G D (j + 1) m (by omega)| +
+            |hybridProb G D (j + 1) m (by omega) - hybridProb G D n 0 (add_zero n)| :=
+        _ ≤ 2 ^ j * ε + (2 ^ n - 2 ^ (j + 1)) * ε := add_le_add hstep (ih (j + 1) (by omega))
+/-- **The GGM family from a subexponentially secure generator is exponentially secure**
+[GGM1986], [RazborovRudich1997, Section 4]. Let `G` be a family of length-doubling generators of
+polynomial circuit complexity, subexponentially secure with exponent `1 / d`. With keys of length
+`(n + 1) ^ (2 d + 1)`, the GGM functions on `n` inputs are pseudorandom against circuits of size
+`2 ^ (c n)` with error `2 ^ (-c n)` for every `c` and all large `n`: the generator on these keys
+    (hsize : PolynomiallyBounded fun k => complexity interpretation ⇑(G k))
+    IsExponentiallySecure fun n => booleanFamily (G ((n + 1) ^ (2 * d + 1))) n := by
+  -- the keys are eventually long enough for the security of the generator
+  have hkey : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ m, m ^ d ≤ (n + 1) ^ (2 * d + 1) →
+    have := hsize.comp (g := fun n => (n + 1) ^ (2 * d + 1)) (by fun_prop)
+  filter_upwards [hkey, hpoly.eventually_lt_two_pow, eventually_ge_atTop (c + 3)] with n hG hn hc
+  -- the generator resists circuits with `2 ^ (n ^ 2)` gates
+  -- which exceeds the size of the reduction
+    have h1 : 2 ^ (c * n) ≤ 2 ^ ((c + 3) * n - 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right two_pos (by
+    have h2 : 2 ^ n * (n * complexity interpretation ⇑(G ((n + 1) ^ (2 * d + 1))) + 1) ≤
+      _ ≤ 2 ^ (n ^ 2) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right two_pos (by rw [sq]; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hc)
+  -- and the loss `2 ^ n` in the advantage is absorbed

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+If `Πₖ ⊆ Σₖ` for some `k ≥ 1`, for problems with any encoding of their instances, then the
+polynomial hierarchy collapses to its level `k`: `PH = Σₖ`
+[Stockmeyer][Stockmeyer1976]. Consequently `NP = coNP` collapses the hierarchy to `NP`
+The collapse goes one level at a time (`Cslib.Complexity.SigmaP_succ_subset_SigmaP`). For a
+problem `A` in `Σₖ₊₁`, the pairs `(a, w₁)` of an instance and a first certificate from which the
+remaining `k` alternating quantifiers accept form a problem `B` in `Πₖ`, with respect to the
+encoding of pairs. Its blocks of certificates are lengths of the instance `a`, while `Πₖ` asks for
+polynomials in the length of the encoded pair; the verifier reads longer blocks and cuts each to
+its first bits (`Cslib.Complexity.truncateBlocks`), which does not change the quantifiers
+(`Cslib.Complexity.alternation_truncateBlocks`). Then `B` is in `Σₖ`, and the existential
+quantifier over `w₁` merges with the first quantifier of `B`, whose block lengths are polynomials
+in the length of the encoded pair `(a, w₁)`, hence in the length of `enc a`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.truncateBlocks`: cut blocks of certificates to shorter blocks.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The blocks of `w` of lengths `p.eval m`, for the polynomials `p` of `ps` in order, each cut to
+def truncateBlocks : List (Polynomial ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ → List Bool → List Bool
+  | p :: ps, n, m, w => w.take (p.eval n) ++ truncateBlocks ps n m (w.drop (p.eval m))
+/-- **Cutting longer blocks does not change alternating quantifiers**: quantifying over blocks of
+lengths `p.eval m` and cutting each to `p.eval n ≤ p.eval m` bits quantifies over all blocks of
+theorem alternation_truncateBlocks {ps : List (Polynomial ℕ)} {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) {q : Bool}
+    Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval m) (fun w => P (truncateBlocks ps n m w)) ↔
+      Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval n) P := by
+  induction ps generalizing q P with
+    -- a long block, appended to anything, cuts to its first `p.eval n` bits
+    have hcut (w v : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval m) :
+        truncateBlocks (p :: ps) n m (w ++ v) = w.take (p.eval n) ++ truncateBlocks ps n m v := by
+    have key (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval m) {q : Bool} :
+        Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval m)
+          (fun v => P (truncateBlocks (p :: ps) n m (w ++ v))) ↔
+        Alternation q (ps.map fun p => p.eval n) fun v => P (w.take (p.eval n) ++ v) :=
+      (alternation_congr fun v => by rw [hcut w v hw]).trans
+    -- a short block is the cut of its padding
+    have hpad (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval n) :
+        (w ++ List.replicate (p.eval m - p.eval n) false).length = p.eval m := by
+    have htake (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval n) :
+        (w ++ List.replicate (p.eval m - p.eval n) false).take (p.eval n) = w := by
+    have hlen (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval m) : (w.take (p.eval n)).length = p.eval n :=
+        exact ⟨_, hlen w hw, (key w hw).mp hP⟩
+        refine ⟨_, hpad w hw, (key _ (hpad w hw)).mpr ?_⟩
+/-- Cutting blocks is polynomial-time, for a fixed list of polynomials and lengths `n`, `m` computed
+    (hM : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime M encIn encUnary) {W : γ → List Bool}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => truncateBlocks ps (N x) (M x) (W x)) encIn encBits := by
+/-- A word of length `a + b` is a word of length `a` followed by one of length `b`. -/
+private theorem exists_length_add_iff {a b : ℕ} {P : List Bool → Prop} :
+    (∃ w : List Bool, w.length = a + b ∧ P w) ↔
+      ∃ u : List Bool, u.length = a ∧ ∃ v : List Bool, v.length = b ∧ P (u ++ v) := by
+    refine ⟨w.take a, by simp [hw], w.drop a, by simp [hw], by rwa [List.take_append_drop]⟩
+    exact ⟨u ++ v, by simp [hu, hv], hP⟩
+/-- **One level of the collapse.** If `Πₖ ⊆ Σₖ` for problems on pairs of an instance and a word,
+for some `k ≥ 1`, then `Σₖ₊₁ ⊆ Σₖ`: the pairs `(a, w₁)` from which the last `k` quantifiers
+accept form a problem in `Πₖ`, hence in `Σₖ`, and the quantifier over `w₁` merges with its first
+    (h : PiP k (encPair enc encBits) ⊆ SigmaP k (encPair enc encBits)) :
+    SigmaP (k + 1) enc ⊆ SigmaP k enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨ps, V, hlen, hV, hA⟩
+  have hlen' : ps.length = k := by simpa using hlen
+  -- the last `k` quantifiers, on pairs of an instance and a first certificate
+  let B : Set (α × List Bool) := {y | Alternation false
+    (ps.map fun r => r.eval (enc y.1).length) fun w => V (y.1, y.2 ++ w) = true}
+  have hle (y : α × List Bool) : (enc y.1).length ≤ (encPair enc encBits y).length := by
+  have hB : B ∈ PiP k (encPair enc encBits) := by
+    refine ⟨ps, fun z => V (z.1.1, z.1.2 ++ truncateBlocks ps (enc z.1.1).length
+      (encPair enc encBits z.1).length z.2), hlen', ?_, fun y => ?_⟩
+        (P := fun w => V (y.1, y.2 ++ w) = true)).symm
+  obtain ⟨rs, V', hrs, hV', hB'⟩ := h hB
+  -- the length of the encoded pair of an instance and a first certificate
+  let L : Polynomial ℕ := 2 * Polynomial.X + 1 + p
+  have hL (a : α) (w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = p.eval (enc a).length) :
+      (encPair enc encBits (a, w)).length = L.eval (enc a).length := by
+    simp only [length_encPair, encBits_apply, hw, L, Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_mul,
+    fun x => V' ((x.1, x.2.take (p.eval (enc x.1).length)), x.2.drop (p.eval (enc x.1).length)),
+    by simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_map]; omega, ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+  · have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => p.eval (enc x.1).length)
+    refine exists_congr fun w => and_congr_right fun hw => ?_
+    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq, B, List.map_cons, alternation_true_cons, hL a w hw] at hmem
+    refine exists_congr fun v => and_congr_right fun hv => alternation_congr fun u => ?_
+/-- **`Πₖ ⊆ Σₖ` collapses the polynomial hierarchy to `Σₖ`**, for `k ≥ 1`
+[Arora and Barak, Theorem 5.4][AroraBarak09]: if `Πₖ ⊆ Σₖ` for problems with any encoding of their
+    (h : ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), PiP k encB ⊆ SigmaP k encB) :
+    PH enc = SigmaP k enc := by
+  -- every level from `k` on is within `Σₖ`, for every encoding
+      ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), SigmaP (k + j) encB ⊆ SigmaP k encB := by
+    | zero => intro β encB; exact le_rfl
+      refine (SigmaP_succ_subset_SigmaP (k := k + j) (by omega) fun A hA => ?_).trans
+      -- `Πₖ₊ⱼ` is the complement of `Σₖ₊ⱼ ⊆ Σₖ`, within `Πₖ ⊆ Σₖ ⊆ Σₖ₊ⱼ`
+      have hc : Aᶜ ∈ SigmaP k _ := ih _ (compl_mem_SigmaP_of_mem_PiP hA)
+      have := h _ (by simpa using compl_mem_PiP_of_mem_SigmaP hc)
+  rcases le_total j k with hj | hj
+/-- **`NP = coNP` collapses the polynomial hierarchy to `NP`** [Arora and Barak, Theorem 5.4]
+theorem PH_eq_NP_of_coNP_subset_NP (h : ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), coNP encB ⊆ NP encB) :
+  exact PH_eq_SigmaP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP le_rfl fun encB => by
+/-- **`P = NP` collapses the polynomial hierarchy to `P`** [Arora and Barak, Theorem 5.4]
+[AroraBarak09]: then `coNP ⊆ NP`, since `P` is closed under complement. -/
+theorem PH_eq_P_of_NP_subset_P (h : ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), NP encB ⊆ P encB) :
+  have hNP : ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), NP encB = P encB := fun encB =>
+  rw [PH_eq_NP_of_coNP_subset_NP fun encB A hA => ?_, hNP]
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfA⟩ := h encB hA
+  exact ⟨fun a => !f a, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bool_not.comp hf, fun a => by
+/-- **`Σₖ₊₁ ⊆ Σₖ` collapses the polynomial hierarchy to `Σₖ`**, for every `k`: then
+`Πₖ ⊆ Σₖ₊₁ ⊆ Σₖ`, and for `k = 0` the hypothesis is `NP ⊆ P`. -/
+    (h : ∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), SigmaP (k + 1) encB ⊆ SigmaP k encB) :
+    PH enc = SigmaP k enc := by
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with rfl | hk
+      simpa only [zero_add, SigmaP_one, SigmaP_zero] using h encB

+**Hardness versus randomness** [NisanWigderson1994]: if some problem in `E`, decidable in time
+`2 ^ O(n)`, is average-case hard for circuits of size `2 ^ (n / c)`, then `BPP = P`
+[Arora and Barak, Chapter 20][AroraBarak09]. Here the hardness is
+`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.IsAverageCaseHard` for nonuniform De Morgan circuits, with the non-strict
+bound produced by Yao's XOR lemma, and the conclusion is uniform: every problem in `BPP enc` is in
+`P enc`, for every encoding `enc` of instances (`BPP_subset_P_of_isAverageCaseHard`), so
+`P enc = BPP enc` (`P_eq_BPP_of_isAverageCaseHard`). A hardness `2 ^ (ε n)` for a real `ε > 0`

+The deterministic algorithm is `Cslib.Complexity.nwDecider`. On an instance of length `N` it sets

+The library has one divergence notion, Mathlib's `InformationTheory.klDiv`, and one entropy
+notion, `Cslib.Probability.PMF.entropy`. This file bridges them. For PMFs on a finite type with
+a discrete measurable structure, `klDiv p.toMeasure q.toMeasure` is finite exactly when the
+support of `p` is contained in that of `q`, and is then the finite sum
+`∑ a, p a * log (p a / q a)` in nats. Consequences:
+* Gibbs' inequality: the sum is nonnegative and vanishes only at `p = q`. Equivalently, the
+  entropy of `p` is at most its cross-entropy `∑ a, p a * surprisal q a`.
+* Entropy is the logarithm of the alphabet size minus the divergence from uniform.
+* Mutual information, `H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)`, is the divergence of the joint law from the
+  product of its marginals. Entropy is subadditive and conditioning cannot increase it; by the
+  equality case of Gibbs' inequality, subadditivity is an equality exactly for independent
+* Pinsker's inequality `2 δ(p, q)² ≤ D(p ‖ q)` for the statistical distance `δ`. It is proved
+  for arbitrary probability measures and events, following the variational proof: Gibbs'
+  inequality for an exponentially tilted measure (Mathlib's `integral_llr_tilted_right`) and
+  Hoeffding's lemma for the indicator of the event. A Hahn decomposition gives the form with
+  Mathlib's total variation distance `tvDist`, which is twice the statistical distance.
+Divergences are in nats and entropies in bits, so the bridges divide by `log 2`.

+A verifier that guesses a circuit reads it from a certificate of a fixed length. This file fixes
+such a format for De Morgan circuits with `n` inputs, one output and at most `s` gates, of length
+`certLength n s`. Wire numbers are below `w = n + s` and are written in unary in fields of `w`
+bits (`unaryField`); an operation takes three bits (`Op.bits`). A certificate lists the number of
+gates in a field of `s` bits, the output wire, and then `s` rows of `3 + 2 w` bits, the first of
+Every bit string reads as a list of gates and an output wire (`readCertificate`): a field is read
+as its number of ones, any three bits as an operation, and the arguments of a gate are cut to the
+arity of its operation. Reading is polynomial-time
+circuit, followed by any bits, reads as its code (`readCertificate_certificate_append`). A string
+that is not the certificate of a circuit may read as gates that read wires not yet computed; the
+polynomial-time test `codeCheck` tells the codes of circuits apart (`codeCheck_eq_true_iff`).

+def evalCode (I : Interpretation σ U) (d : U) (x : List U) (gates : List (σ.Op × List ℕ)) :
+  gates.foldl (fun values g => values ++ [I g.1 fun a => g.2[a.val]?.elim d (values.getD · d)]) x

+    evalCode I d x [] = x := rfl
+theorem evalCode_append_singleton (I : Interpretation σ U) (d : U) (x : List U)
+    (gates : List (σ.Op × List ℕ)) (g : σ.Op × List ℕ) :
+        [I g.1 fun a => g.2[a.val]?.elim d ((evalCode I d x gates).getD · d)] := by
+theorem evalCode_append (I : Interpretation σ U) (d : U) (x : List U)
+    evalCode I d x (gates ++ gates') = evalCode I d (evalCode I d x gates) gates' := by

+    (gates : List (σ.Op × List ℕ)) : (evalCode I d x gates).length = x.length + gates.length := by

+verifier evaluates the circuit on the first `n` bits of the certificate. It is `NP`-hard because
+`NP`-complete by the Cook–Levin theorem. The circuit of a formula (`Cslib.Complexity.SAT.toCircuit`)
+has one input for each literal occurrence; a variable is read at the input of its first
+occurrence, as for the certificates of `SAT.verifier`. Its gates come in blocks of three, one block
+for each literal and one for the end of each clause, which keep the disjunction of the current
+clause and the conjunction of the finished clauses at fixed offsets from the end.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitSAT`: the satisfiable De Morgan circuits with one output.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CircuitSAT.verifier`: evaluation on the first bits of a certificate.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SAT.toCircuit`: the circuit of a formula in conjunctive normal form.

+its truth table followed by the threshold in binary (`Cslib.MCSP.encInstance`); the length of

+it is a circuit and evaluates it on all `2 ^ n` inputs. The threshold may be exponentially larger
+than the table; certificates are capped at the truth-table bound `2 ^ n (2 n + 3) + 1`, which
+so they stay polynomially long in the length of the table.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Two distinct codewords of a code of minimum distance at least `d` differ on at least `d`
+coordinates, so they already differ on any set `S` of coordinates that leaves out fewer than `d`
+of them: the codewords are determined by their letters on `S`
+(`Cslib.Code.injOn_restrict_of_card_lt_add`). Taking `n - d + 1` coordinates, a code of length `n`
+and minimum distance at least `d` over an alphabet of `q` letters has at most `q ^ (n - d + 1)`
+[GuruswamiRudraSudan2019]. For a nonzero linear code over a field the same restriction is an
+injective linear map, so the dimension `k` satisfies `k + d ≤ n + 1`
+(`Cslib.Code.finrank_add_le_card_add_one`). Codes meeting this bound, such as Reed–Solomon codes,
+* `Cslib.Code.injOn_restrict_of_card_lt_add`: codewords are determined by any `n - d + 1`
+* `Cslib.Code.finrank_add_le_card_add_one`: the Singleton bound for linear codes.
+* [V. Guruswami, A. Rudra, M. Sudan, *Essential Coding Theory*][GuruswamiRudraSudan2019]
+variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {β : ι → Type*} [∀ i, DecidableEq (β i)]
+/-- The codewords of a code of minimum distance at least `d` are determined by their letters on any
+set `S` of coordinates that leaves out fewer than `d` coordinates. -/
+theorem injOn_restrict_of_card_lt_add {C : Set (∀ i, β i)} {d : ℕ} (hd : (d : ℕ∞) ≤ minDist C)
+    {S : Finset ι} (hS : Fintype.card ι < #S + d) : C.InjOn S.restrict := by
+  intro x hx y hy hxy
+  have hsub : ({i | x i ≠ y i} : Finset ι) ⊆ univ \ S := fun i hi =>
+    mem_sdiff.2 ⟨mem_univ i, fun hiS => (mem_filter.1 hi).2 (congrFun hxy ⟨i, hiS⟩)⟩
+  have hdist : hammingDist x y ≤ Fintype.card ι - #S :=
+  have := Nat.cast_le.1 (le_minDist.1 hd x hx y hy hne)
+/-- **The Singleton bound** [Singleton1964]: a code of length `n` and minimum distance at least `d`
+over an alphabet of `q` letters has at most `q ^ (n - d + 1)` codewords. -/
+    {C : Finset (ι → α)} {d : ℕ} (hd : (d : ℕ∞) ≤ minDist (C : Set (ι → α))) :
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos d with rfl | hd0
+    (n := min (Fintype.card ι) (Fintype.card ι - d + 1)) (by rw [card_univ]; exact min_le_left _ _)
+  have hinj := injOn_restrict_of_card_lt_add hd (S := S) (by omega)
+/-- **The Singleton bound for linear codes**: a nonzero linear code of length `n` over a field,
+with dimension `k` and minimum distance at least `d`, satisfies `k + d ≤ n + 1`. -/
+    {C : Submodule F (ι → F)} (hC : C ≠ ⊥) {d : ℕ} (hd : (d : ℕ∞) ≤ minDist (C : Set (ι → F))) :
+    Module.finrank F C + d ≤ Fintype.card ι + 1 := by
+  -- a nonzero codeword has weight at most `n`, so `d ≤ n`
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos d with rfl | hd0
+  have hinj := injOn_restrict_of_card_lt_add hd (S := S) (by omega)
+  let f : C →ₗ[F] S → F := (LinearMap.funLeft F F ((↑) : S → ι)).comp C.subtype
+  have hf : Function.Injective f := fun x y h => Subtype.ext (hinj x.2 y.2 h)

+  evaluated at the weight it has degree at most `d` on the cube

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A real polynomial `p` of degree at most `n` with `|p| ≤ M` on `[-1, 1]` has `|p'| ≤ n² M` on
+`[-1, 1]` (`Polynomial.abs_eval_derivative_le`), the inequality of A. A. Markov
+([BorweinErdelyi1995], [Rivlin1990]). The proof combines two classical inequalities.
+* **Schur's inequality**: a polynomial `q` of degree less than `n ≥ 1` with
+  `√(1 - x²) |q(x)| ≤ M` on `[-1, 1]` has `|q| ≤ n M` there
+  this is immediate. Beyond the largest zero `cos (π / 2n)` of the Chebyshev polynomial `T n`,
+  interpolate `q` at the `n` zeros `ηₖ` of `T n`. There every Lagrange basis polynomial is
+  `T n(x) / ((x - ηₖ) T n'(ηₖ))` with `T n(x) / (x - ηₖ) ≥ 0`, the identity
+  `|T n'(ηₖ)| √(1 - ηₖ²) = n` turns the bound on `√(1 - ηₖ²) |q(ηₖ)|` into a bound on each term,
+  and the terms add up to `M T n'(x) / n ≤ M T n'(1) / n = n M`.
+  odd part `(p(ac + bs) - p(ac - bs)) / 2` of `p` along the circle `c² + s² = 1` is `s r(c)` for a
+  polynomial `r` of degree less than `n` with `r(1) = b p'(a)`, read off the Taylor expansion of
+  `p` at `ac`. Since `|ac ± bs| ≤ 1`, Schur's inequality at `1` bounds `r(1)`.
+Schur's inequality applied to `p'` with Bernstein's bound gives Markov's.
+Rescaled to an interval `[a, b]`, Markov's inequality reads `(b - a) |p'| ≤ 2 n² M`
+(`Polynomial.sub_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le`). A polynomial of degree at most `d` whose values at
+the integers `0, …, N` lie in `[b₁, b₂]` therefore has `(N - d²) |q'| ≤ d² (b₂ - b₁)` on `[0, N]`
+(`Polynomial.sub_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le_of_forall_nat`): every point of `[0, N]` is within
+`1/2` of an integer, so the largest value `c` of `|q'|` on `[0, N]` keeps `q` within `c / 2` of
+`[b₁, b₂]`, and Markov's inequality gives `N c ≤ d² (b₂ - b₁ + c)`. The same argument bounds `q`
+bound of Ehlich and Zeller [EhlichZeller1964] (see also [CoppersmithRivlin1992]), and gives the
+lemma behind the degree bounds of Nisan and Szegedy [NisanSzegedy1994]
+* `Polynomial.sub_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le`: Markov's inequality on an interval `[a, b]`.
+  `Polynomial.sub_mul_abs_eval_le_of_forall_nat`: polynomials bounded at the integers of `[0, N]`.
+  `|q'(ξ)| ≥ c ≥ 0` at some `ξ ∈ [0, N]`, then `c N ≤ d² (c + b₂ - b₁)`.
+* [P. Borwein, T. Erdélyi, *Polynomials and Polynomial Inequalities*][BorweinErdelyi1995]
+* [H. Ehlich, K. Zeller, *Schwankung von Polynomen zwischen Gitterpunkten*][EhlichZeller1964]
+* [D. Coppersmith, T. J. Rivlin, *The growth of polynomials bounded at equally spaced
+* [N. Nisan, M. Szegedy, *On the degree of Boolean functions as real polynomials*][NisanSzegedy1994]
+/-- The zeros `cos ((2k + 1) π / 2n)`, `k < n`, of the Chebyshev polynomial `T n`. -/
+private noncomputable def chebyshevZero (n k : ℕ) : ℝ := cos ((2 * k + 1) * π / (2 * n))
+private theorem injOn_chebyshevZero (n : ℕ) : Set.InjOn (chebyshevZero n) (range n) :=
+/-- The angle of a zero of `T n` lies in `[π / 2n, π]`. -/
+private theorem angle_mem {n k : ℕ} (hk : k < n) :
+  have hk' : (2 * k + 1 : ℝ) ≤ 2 * n := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 2 * k + 1 ≤ 2 * n)
+/-- `T n = 2ⁿ⁻¹ ∏ₖ (X - ηₖ)` over the zeros `ηₖ` of `T n`. -/
+    Chebyshev.T ℝ n = C (2 ^ (n - 1)) * Lagrange.nodal (range n) (chebyshevZero n) := by
+  have hroots : (Chebyshev.T ℝ n).roots = ((range n).image (chebyshevZero n)).val :=
+  have hcard : Multiset.card (Chebyshev.T ℝ n).roots = (Chebyshev.T ℝ n).natDegree := by
+/-- At a zero `η` of `T n`, `|T n'(η)| √(1 - η²) = n`. -/
+private theorem abs_eval_derivative_T_mul_sqrt {n k : ℕ} (hk : k < n) :
+  have hn : (n : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : n ≠ 0)
+  set θ := (2 * k + 1) * π / (2 * n) with hθ
+  have hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ := (by positivity : 0 ≤ π / (2 * n)).trans h₁
+  rw [chebyshevZero, ← hθ, ← sin_eq_sqrt_one_sub_cos_sq hθ0 h₂, ← abs_of_nonneg
+  have hnθ : ((((n : ℤ) - 1 : ℤ) : ℝ) + 1) * θ = k * π + π / 2 := by
+  rw [hnθ, sin_add_pi_div_two, cos_nat_mul_pi, eval_intCast, Int.cast_natCast, abs_mul, abs_pow,
+/-- Schur's inequality beyond the largest zero `cos (π / 2n)` of `T n`, by Lagrange interpolation at
+private theorem abs_eval_le_mul_of_cos_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {q : ℝ[X]} (hq : q.natDegree < n)
+    (hx₁ : cos (π / (2 * n)) ≤ x) (hx₂ : x ≤ 1) : |q.eval x| ≤ n * M := by
+  have hnR : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
+  -- every node lies at or below `x`
+  have hvx (j : ℕ) (hj : j ∈ s) : v j ≤ x := by
+  have hv (j : ℕ) (hj : j ∈ s) : v j ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 := ⟨neg_one_le_cos _, cos_le_one _⟩
+  -- the derivative of `T n` is `c` times that of the node polynomial
+  have hT' (y : ℝ) : (derivative (Chebyshev.T ℝ n)).eval y =
+  -- interpolation at the zeros of `T n`
+  have heval : q.eval x = ∑ k ∈ s, q.eval (v k) *
+      ((∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (x - v j)) / ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j)) := by
+    rw [Lagrange.basisDivisor, eval_mul, eval_C, eval_sub, eval_X, eval_C, div_eq_inv_mul]
+      n * |q.eval (v k)| ≤ c * M * |∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j)| := by
+    have hd : (derivative (Lagrange.nodal s v)).eval (v k) = ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j) := by
+        = |c * ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j)| * (√(1 - v k ^ 2) * |q.eval (v k)|) := by
+      _ ≤ |c * ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j)| * M := by gcongr; exact hM _ (hv k hk)
+      _ = c * M * |∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j)| := by rw [abs_mul, abs_of_pos hc]; ring
+  have hsum : ∑ k ∈ s, ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (x - v j) = (derivative (Lagrange.nodal s v)).eval x := by
+    exact sum_congr rfl fun k _ => Lagrange.eval_nodal.symm
+  have hn1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
+    cos_nonneg_of_mem_Icc ⟨by linarith [(by positivity : 0 ≤ π / (2 * n)), pi_pos],
+  have hTx : (derivative (Chebyshev.T ℝ n)).eval x ≤ n ^ 2 := by
+          ((∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (x - v j)) / ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j))| := by
+    _ ≤ ∑ k ∈ s, c * M / n * ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (x - v j) := by
+        have hw : 0 ≤ ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (x - v j) :=
+          prod_nonneg fun j hj => sub_nonneg.2 (hvx j (mem_of_mem_erase hj))
+        have hd : ∏ j ∈ s.erase k, (v k - v j) ≠ 0 := prod_ne_zero_iff.2 fun j hj =>
+          sub_ne_zero.2 fun h => (mem_erase.1 hj).1 (hinj (mem_of_mem_erase hj) hk h.symm)
+        have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hweight k hk) hw
+        rw [abs_mul, abs_div, abs_of_nonneg hw, mul_div_assoc', div_le_iff₀ (abs_pos.2 hd),
+    _ = M / n * (derivative (Chebyshev.T ℝ n)).eval x := by
+/-- **Schur's inequality**: a real polynomial `q` of degree less than `n ≥ 1` with
+    (hq : q.natDegree < n) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ y ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, √(1 - y ^ 2) * |q.eval y| ≤ M)
+    {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) : |q.eval x| ≤ n * M := by
+  rcases le_or_gt (cos (π / (2 * n))) x with h | h
+  · exact abs_eval_le_mul_of_cos_le hn hq hM h hx.2
+  rcases le_or_gt x (-cos (π / (2 * n))) with h' | h'
+    have := abs_eval_le_mul_of_cos_le hn hq' (M := M) (fun y hy => by
+      simpa [eval_comp] using hM (-y) ⟨by linarith [hy.2], by linarith [hy.1]⟩)
+    have hnR : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
+    have hsin : 1 / n ≤ sin (π / (2 * n)) := by
+      have h := mul_le_sin (x := π / (2 * n)) (by positivity)
+      calc 1 / (n : ℝ) = 2 / π * (π / (2 * n)) := by field_simp
+    have hsq : x ^ 2 < cos (π / (2 * n)) ^ 2 := sq_lt_sq' (by linarith) h
+      rw [show (1 : ℝ) / n = √((1 / n) ^ 2) from (sqrt_sq (by positivity)).symm]
+    calc |q.eval x| = n * (1 / n * |q.eval x|) := by field_simp
+      _ ≤ n * M := by gcongr; exact hM x hx
+/-- `∑_{j < 2n} g j` groups into the pairs `g (2m) + g (2m + 1)`. -/
+private theorem sum_range_two_mul {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (g : ℕ → M) (n : ℕ) :
+    ∑ j ∈ range (2 * n), g j = ∑ m ∈ range n, (g (2 * m) + g (2 * m + 1)) := by
+    rw [show 2 * (n + 1) = 2 * n + 1 + 1 by ring, sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ, ih,
+/-- The odd part of `p` along the circle through `a + b i`: the polynomial `r` with
+`s r(c) = (p(ac + bs) - p(ac - bs)) / 2` whenever `c² + s² = 1`. -/
+private noncomputable def oddPart (p : ℝ[X]) (n : ℕ) (a b : ℝ) : ℝ[X] :=
+  ∑ m ∈ range n, (hasseDeriv (2 * m + 1) p).comp (C a * X) * C (b ^ (2 * m + 1)) *
+private theorem natDegree_oddPart_lt {p : ℝ[X]} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n)
+    (a b : ℝ) : (oddPart p n a b).natDegree < n := by
+  have hX : (C a * X).natDegree ≤ 1 := (natDegree_C_mul_le a X).trans natDegree_X_le
+private theorem eval_oddPart_one {p : ℝ[X]} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (a b : ℝ) :
+    (oddPart p n a b).eval 1 = (derivative p).eval a * b := by
+  rw [oddPart, eval_finsetSum, sum_eq_single_of_mem 0 (mem_range.2 hn) fun m _ hm => by
+/-- The defining identity of the odd part. -/
+private theorem two_mul_mul_eval_oddPart {p : ℝ[X]} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n)
+    2 * (s * (oddPart p n a b).eval c) = p.eval (a * c + b * s) - p.eval (a * c - b * s) := by
+  have htaylor (y : ℝ) : p.eval (a * c + y) =
+      ∑ j ∈ range (2 * n), (hasseDeriv j p).eval (a * c) * y ^ j := by
+    rw [add_comm, ← taylor_eval, eval_eq_sum_range' (n := 2 * n) (by rw [natDegree_taylor]; omega)]
+  rw [sub_eq_add_neg _ (b * s), htaylor, htaylor, ← sum_sub_distrib, sum_range_two_mul, oddPart,
+  have hodd : (-(b * s)) ^ (2 * m + 1) = -(b * s) ^ (2 * m + 1) := Odd.neg_pow ⟨m, rfl⟩ _
+  have heven : (-(b * s)) ^ (2 * m) = (b * s) ^ (2 * m) := Even.neg_pow ⟨m, two_mul m⟩ _
+  simp only [eval_mul, eval_comp, eval_C, eval_X, eval_pow, eval_sub, eval_one, hodd, heven]
+/-- **Bernstein's inequality**: a real polynomial `p` of degree at most `n` with `|p| ≤ M` on
+theorem sqrt_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le {n : ℕ} {p : ℝ[X]} (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n) {M : ℝ}
+    (hM : ∀ y ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, |p.eval y| ≤ M) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) :
+    √(1 - x ^ 2) * |(derivative p).eval x| ≤ n * M := by
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
+  have hb : b ^ 2 = 1 - x ^ 2 := sq_sqrt (by nlinarith [hx.1, hx.2])
+  -- the odd part of `p` along the circle is bounded by `M`
+  have hr : ∀ c ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, √(1 - c ^ 2) * |(oddPart p n x b).eval c| ≤ M := by
+    have hs : s ^ 2 = 1 - c ^ 2 := sq_sqrt (by nlinarith [hc.1, hc.2])
+    have hcirc (σ : ℝ) (hσ : σ ^ 2 = 1) : x * c + σ * b * s ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 := by
+      have key : (x * c + σ * b * s) ^ 2 + (x * s - σ * b * c) ^ 2 = 1 := by
+        have : (x * c + σ * b * s) ^ 2 + (x * s - σ * b * c) ^ 2 =
+    have h := two_mul_mul_eval_oddPart hn hp x b c s hs
+    have h₁ := hM _ (by simpa only [one_mul] using hcirc 1 (one_pow 2))
+    have h₂ := hM (x * c - b * s) (by
+      rwa [show x * c + -1 * b * s = x * c - b * s by ring] at hm)
+    have : |2 * (s * (oddPart p n x b).eval c)| ≤ 2 * M :=
+    rw [abs_mul, abs_two, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg hs0] at this
+  have h := abs_eval_le_mul_of_sqrt_mul_abs_eval_le hn (natDegree_oddPart_lt hn hp x b) hr
+  rwa [eval_oddPart_one hn, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (sqrt_nonneg _), mul_comm] at h
+/-- **The Markov brothers' inequality**: a real polynomial `p` of degree at most `n` with `|p| ≤ M`
+theorem abs_eval_derivative_le {n : ℕ} {p : ℝ[X]} (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n) {M : ℝ}
+    (hM : ∀ y ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, |p.eval y| ≤ M) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) :
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
+  have hq : (derivative p).natDegree < n := (natDegree_derivative_le p).trans_lt (by omega)
+    (fun y hy => sqrt_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le hp hM hy) hx
+/-- **Markov's inequality on an interval**: a real polynomial `p` of degree at most `n` with
+`|p| ≤ M` on `[a, b]` satisfies `(b - a) |p'| ≤ 2 n² M` on `[a, b]`. -/
+theorem sub_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le {n : ℕ} {p : ℝ[X]} (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n) {a b M : ℝ}
+    (hab : a < b) (hM : ∀ y ∈ Icc a b, |p.eval y| ≤ M) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc a b) :
+    (b - a) * |(derivative p).eval x| ≤ 2 * n ^ 2 * M := by
+  have hL (t : ℝ) : L.eval t = (b - a) / 2 * t + (a + b) / 2 := by simp [L]
+  have hbound : ∀ t ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, |(p.comp L).eval t| ≤ M := fun t ht => by
+  have hba : 0 < b - a := sub_pos.2 hab
+  set t := (2 * x - a - b) / (b - a)
+  have ht : t ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 := by
+  have hLt : L.eval t = x := by
+    rw [hL, show t = (2 * x - a - b) / (b - a) from rfl]
+  have h := abs_eval_derivative_le hdeg hbound ht
+  rw [derivative_comp, eval_mul, eval_comp, hLt, abs_mul] at h
+  have hL' : (derivative L).eval t = (b - a) / 2 := by simp [L]
+/-- The largest value `c` of `|q'|` on `[0, N]` satisfies `N c ≤ d² (b₂ - b₁ + c)` when the
+values of `q` at the integers of `[0, N]` lie in `[b₁, b₂]`, and `q` stays within `c / 2` of
+private theorem exists_max_abs_eval_derivative {d N : ℕ} {q : ℝ[X]} (hq : q.natDegree ≤ d)
+    (hN : 0 < N) {b₁ b₂ : ℝ} (hb : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → q.eval (k : ℝ) ∈ Icc b₁ b₂) :
+    ∃ c, (∀ y ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N, |(derivative q).eval y| ≤ c) ∧
+      ∀ y ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N, |q.eval y - (b₁ + b₂) / 2| ≤ (b₂ - b₁ + c) / 2 := by
+  have hNR : (0 : ℝ) < N := by exact_mod_cast hN
+  have hc (y : ℝ) (hy : y ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N) : |(derivative q).eval y| ≤ c := hmax hy
+  -- `q` is within `c / 2` of its value at the nearest integer
+  have hval : ∀ y ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N, |q.eval y - (b₁ + b₂) / 2| ≤ (b₂ - b₁ + c) / 2 := by
+    have hk₁ : (k : ℝ) ≤ y + 1 / 2 := Nat.floor_le (by linarith [hy.1])
+    have hkI : (k : ℝ) ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N := ⟨k.cast_nonneg, by exact_mod_cast hkN⟩
+      (f := fun z => q.eval z) (fun z _ => (q.hasDerivAt z).hasDerivWithinAt) hc hkI hy
+    have hyk : |y - k| ≤ 1 / 2 := abs_le.2 ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩
+  -- Markov's inequality on `[0, N]` at the maximum
+  have h := sub_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le (p := q - C ((b₁ + b₂) / 2))
+    ((natDegree_sub_C).le.trans hq) hNR (fun y hy => by simpa using hval y hy) hy₀
+  rw [derivative_sub, derivative_C, sub_zero, sub_zero] at h
+/-- **Polynomials bounded at the integers, derivative form**: a real polynomial `q` of degree at
+most `d` whose values at the integers `0, …, N` lie in `[b₁, b₂]` satisfies
+    (hN : 0 < N) {b₁ b₂ : ℝ} (hb : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → q.eval (k : ℝ) ∈ Icc b₁ b₂) {x : ℝ}
+    (hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N) : (N - d ^ 2) * |(derivative q).eval x| ≤ d ^ 2 * (b₂ - b₁) := by
+  obtain ⟨c, hc, hNc, -⟩ := exists_max_abs_eval_derivative hq hN hb
+  have hB : 0 ≤ b₂ - b₁ := by linarith [(hb 0 (Nat.zero_le _)).1, (hb 0 (Nat.zero_le _)).2]
+  rcases le_or_gt ((N : ℝ) - d ^ 2) 0 with h | h
+/-- **The Ehlich–Zeller bound**: a real polynomial `q` of degree at most `d` with `|q| ≤ B` at the
+integers `0, …, N` satisfies `(N - d²) |q| ≤ N B` on `[0, N]`; for `d² < N` this bounds `q` on the
+theorem sub_mul_abs_eval_le_of_forall_nat {d N : ℕ} {q : ℝ[X]} (hq : q.natDegree ≤ d) (hN : 0 < N)
+    {B : ℝ} (hb : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → |q.eval (k : ℝ)| ≤ B) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N) :
+  obtain ⟨c, hc, hNc, hval⟩ := exists_max_abs_eval_derivative hq hN (b₁ := -B) (b₂ := B)
+    fun k hk => abs_le.1 (hb k hk)
+  have hq' : |q.eval x| ≤ B + c / 2 := by
+  rcases le_or_gt ((N : ℝ) - d ^ 2) 0 with h | h
+/-- **The Nisan–Szegedy lemma**: a real polynomial `q` of degree at most `d` whose values at the
+integers `0, …, N` lie in `[b₁, b₂]`, and with `|q'(ξ)| ≥ c ≥ 0` at some `ξ ∈ [0, N]`, satisfies
+theorem mul_le_sq_mul_of_le_abs_eval_derivative {d N : ℕ} {q : ℝ[X]} (hq : q.natDegree ≤ d)
+    (hN : 0 < N) {b₁ b₂ : ℝ} (hb : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → q.eval (k : ℝ) ∈ Icc b₁ b₂) {ξ c : ℝ}
+    (hξ : ξ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) N) (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hcξ : c ≤ |(derivative q).eval ξ|) :
+  have h := sub_mul_abs_eval_derivative_le_of_forall_nat hq hN hb hξ
+  have hB : 0 ≤ b₂ - b₁ := by linarith [(hb 0 (Nat.zero_le _)).1, (hb 0 (Nat.zero_le _)).2]
+  rcases le_or_gt ((N : ℝ) - d ^ 2) 0 with h' | h'

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The parameters of the hitting-list generator are computed in polynomial time from the number of
+variables `n` and the node-count bound `s`, both in unary. Every parameter is polynomial in
+`Cslib.Circuits.Rational.Parameters.polynomial_H`), so its unary encoding has polynomial length;
+the later stages use these parameters as loop counts, dimensions and moduli. The rank bound, the
+dimension allowance and the threshold `rankBound s * delta n s` are fixed polynomials. The
+exponent is a binary logarithm of the threshold. The ambient dimension `2 ^ (exponent + 1)` is the
+power of two at the ceiling logarithm of the threshold plus one
+(`Parameters.ambientDimension_eq`), and the cyclotomic degree is half of it. The truncation, the
+grid size and the matrix dimension follow by unary arithmetic.
+Each certificate is stated compositionally, for parameters computed in unary from an arbitrary
+  `(truncation, exponent, ambientDimension, degree, gridSize, matrixDimension)` of the generator.
+  `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.degree_eq`: the ambient dimension and the cyclotomic degree in
+  dimension of the hitting list, in unary and in binary.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The rank expansion threshold: the ambient dimension is the least power of two above it. -/
+def threshold (n s : ℕ) : ℕ := Parameters.rankBound s * Parameters.delta n s
+private theorem clog_two_succ {t : ℕ} (ht : 0 < t) : Nat.clog 2 (t + 1) = Nat.log 2 t + 1 := by
+/-- The ambient dimension is two to the ceiling logarithm of the threshold plus one. -/
+    Parameters.ambientDimension n s = 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 (threshold n s + 1) := by
+/-- The cyclotomic degree is half of the ambient dimension. -/
+    CyclotomicRing.degree (Parameters.exponent n s) = Parameters.ambientDimension n s / 2 := by
+/-- The common dimension of the hitting list is the generator's matrix dimension. -/
+    (hittingList n s).dimension = Generator.matrixDimension (Parameters.exponent n s) := rfl
+/-- The parameters `(N, e, M, Dg, H, d)` of the hitting-list generator: the truncation, the
+exponent, the ambient dimension, the cyclotomic degree, the grid size and the matrix dimension. -/
+def generatorParameters (n s : ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
+  (Parameters.truncation n s, Parameters.exponent n s, Parameters.ambientDimension n s,
+    CyclotomicRing.degree (Parameters.exponent n s), Parameters.gridSize n s,
+variable {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {n s : α → ℕ}
+/-- The number of matrices in a lifted tuple, in unary. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Parameters.w (n a)) input encUnary := by
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Parameters.rankBound (s a)) input encUnary := by
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Parameters.delta (n a) (s a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The rank expansion threshold, in unary. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => threshold (n a) (s a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The exponent, the binary logarithm of the threshold, in unary. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Parameters.exponent (n a) (s a)) input encUnary := by
+  change ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Nat.log 2 (threshold (n a) (s a))) input encUnary
+/-- The ambient dimension, in unary, by repeated doubling up to the ceiling logarithm. -/

+Over `𝔽₂`, a map between additive groups is *affine* when it preserves sums of three points:
+`g (x + y + z) = g x + g y + g z` (`Cslib.BitString.IsAffine`). For maps between `𝔽₂`-vector
+spaces this is meant to be the usual notion, a translate of a linear map, and the images of the
+injective affine maps from `BitString d` are meant to be the affine subspaces of dimension `d` of
+the cube `BitString n`; neither correspondence is formalized here, and everything below is stated
+A Boolean function `f` on `n` bits is an *affine disperser for dimension `d`* when it is
+nonconstant on the image of every injective affine map from `BitString d`
+(`Cslib.BitString.IsAffineDisperser`), informally on every affine subspace of dimension `d`.
+Dispersers for dimension `d` are dispersers for every larger dimension
+(`IsAffineDisperser.mono`), and no function is a disperser for dimension `0`
+Affine dispersers exist for every dimension `d` with `n (d + 1) + 1 < 2 ^ d`
+(`exists_isAffineDisperser`), for instance for `n = 100` and `d = 11`. The proof counts: an affine
+map from `BitString d` is determined by its values at `0` and at the unit vectors

+theorem isAffine_const {α β : Type*} [Add α] [AddGroup β] (h : ∀ b : β, b + b = 0) (c : β) :

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The inclusions between the standard classes that papers cite in their preliminaries
+[Arora and Barak, Chapters 2, 4, 5 and 7][AroraBarak09], [Sipser, Chapters 8 and 10][Sipser2013]:
+* `P ⊆ BPP` (`Cslib.Complexity.P_subset_BPP`): a decider ignores its random string.
+* `NP ⊆ PP` (`Cslib.Complexity.NP_subset_PP`): accept on half of the random strings outright, and
+  on the other half run the verifier, so the majority accepts exactly when some certificate does.
+* `PP` is closed under complement (`Cslib.Complexity.compl_mem_PP`): with two more random bits,
+  accept on a quarter of the random strings and one more, and on half of them reject what the
+  verifier accepts; the majority accepts exactly when the verifier accepts at most half of its
+* `NP ⊆ PSPACE` (`Cslib.Complexity.NP_subset_PSPACE`): a nondeterministic machine visits at most
+  one new cell per step on each work tape (`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunsInTime.runsInSpace`), so `NP`
+  is within `NPSPACE`, which is `PSPACE` by Savitch's theorem
+* `PSPACE ⊆ EXP` (`Cslib.Complexity.PSPACE_subset_EXP`): Savitch's decider runs within time
+  quantification (`Cslib.Complexity.setOf_exists_mem_PSPACE`), so it evaluates the alternating
+  quantifiers of every level of the hierarchy one at a time. The existential quantifier over the
+  words `w` of length `ℓ` is reachability within two steps from the all-zero word to the all-one
+  word of width `ℓ + 1`, along edges to `true :: w` for the accepted `w` and from every word
+  starting with `true` to the all-one word; Savitch's algorithm decides it at depth `1`,
+  enumerating the candidates in place and reusing the space of the decider for each.
+With `Cslib.Complexity.P_subset_NP`, these give the chain `P ⊆ NP ⊆ PSPACE ⊆ EXP`. The other
+inclusions of the chains are elsewhere: `P ⊆ PSPACE` (`Cslib.Complexity.P_subset_PSPACE`),
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*][Sipser2013]
+* [J. Gill, *Computational complexity of probabilistic Turing machines*][Gill1977]
+variable {k : ℕ} {State Symbol : Type*} {input : List Symbol} {ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State}
+/-- **Space is at most time.** Under a time bound `t`, every computation path visits at most
+`k * (t + 1)` work-tape cells: within `t` steps each head visits at most `t + 1` cells, and from
+step `t` on the path stays at a halted configuration. -/
+  rcases le_or_gt p.time t with hle | hlt
+  -- the first `t` steps have halted, and the path stays there
+  have ht : t < p.length + 1 := by unfold ComputationPath.time RunPath.time at hlt; omega
+    have hlast : q.last = p.toRunPath ⟨t, ht⟩ := RelSeries.last_take _ _
+  have hsub : ∀ c ∈ p.toRunPath, c ∈ q.toRunPath := by
+    rcases le_or_gt j.val t with hj | hj

+/-- **`P ⊆ BPP`**: a decider is a bounded-error verifier ignoring its random string, of length

+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PSPACE {β : Type} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {B : Set β}

+The three parametric time classes, each relative to an encoding `enc : α ↪ List Bool` of
+instances, with a bound `t : ℕ → ℕ` of the length `n` of the encoded instance, up to constants
+* `Cslib.Complexity.DTIME enc t`: decided by a deterministic machine with a binary alphabet and
+  finitely many states within time `O(t n)`, with any space bound (upstream
+  This is the definition of the classes proposed upstream in cslib pull request #767, stated for
+* `Cslib.Complexity.NTIME enc t`: decided by a nondeterministic machine within time `O(t n)`
+  (`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.DecidesInTime`): every computation path of that length has halted, and the
+  instance is a member exactly when some computation path halts with output `[true]`
+* `Cslib.Complexity.BPTIME enc t`: decided with bounded error by a fair-coin machine within time
+  `O(t n)` (`Turing.MultiTapePTM.DecidesWithBoundedErrorInTime`): every run on `T` coins has
+  halted, for the clock `T = c₁ * t n + c₂`, and the run outputs the right answer, `[true]` for
+  members and `[false]` for the others, with probability at least `2 / 3`
+Each polynomial class of the library is the union of the corresponding classes of time
+`O(n ^ k)`, as in the textbook [Arora and Barak, Definition 1.13, Theorem 2.6,
+verifiers reading random strings, this is the characterisation by probabilistic machines: a
+verifier is run on sampled coins by a fair-coin machine compiled with a halting polynomial clock
+(`Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.exists_halting_machine`), and a fair-coin machine halting within `T`
+  `Cslib.Complexity.BPTIME_mono_of_eventually_le`: the classes only depend on the bound eventually.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.DTIME_subset_NTIME`: a deterministic machine is a nondeterministic machine.
+  `Cslib.Complexity.mem_BPP_iff_exists_mem_BPTIME`: the polynomial classes are unions of time
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- `machine` decides `A` with bounded error within `t`, relative to the encoding `enc`: on every
+encoded instance `enc a`, every run of `t a` steps with fair coins has halted, and the run outputs
+`[true]` if `a ∈ A`, and `[false]` otherwise, with probability at least `2 / 3`. -/
+def DecidesWithBoundedErrorInTime (machine : MultiTapePTM k Bool State) (enc : α ↪ List Bool)
+/-- Time bounds can be increased: a halted run ignores further coins. -/
+    {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α} {t t' : α → ℕ}
+    (h : machine.DecidesWithBoundedErrorInTime enc A t) (ht : ∀ a, t a ≤ t' a) :
+    machine.DecidesWithBoundedErrorInTime enc A t' := fun a => by
+/-- A bound on all but finitely many arguments is a bound up to an additive constant. -/
+private theorem exists_add_of_eventually_le {t₁ t₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, t₁ n ≤ t₂ n) :
+    ∃ C, ∀ n, t₁ n ≤ t₂ n + C := by
+  refine ⟨∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, t₁ n, fun n => ?_⟩
+  rcases le_or_gt N n with h | h
+/-- Linear bounds `c₁ * t n + c₂` absorb a bound that holds eventually. -/
+private theorem exists_linear_of_eventually_le {t₁ t₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, t₁ n ≤ t₂ n)
+    (c₁ c₂ : ℕ) : ∃ c₂', ∀ n, c₁ * t₁ n + c₂ ≤ c₁ * t₂ n + c₂' := by
+/-- The problems decidable within time `O(t n)`, that is `c₁ * t n + c₂` for constants `c₁` and
+`c₂`, on instances whose encoding under `enc` has length `n`, by a machine with a binary alphabet
+and finitely many states, with any space bound. -/
+def DTIME (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (t : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℕ, ∃ s : ℕ → ℕ,
+    DecidableInTimeAndSpace A enc (fun a => c₁ * t (enc a).length + c₂) fun a => s (enc a).length}
+/-- `DTIME` is monotone in the time bound. -/
+theorem DTIME_mono {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {t₁ t₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ n, t₁ n ≤ t₂ n) :
+    DTIME enc t₁ ⊆ DTIME enc t₂ := by
+/-- `DTIME` only depends on the time bound eventually: the finitely many other values are absorbed
+theorem DTIME_mono_of_eventually_le {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {t₁ t₂ : ℕ → ℕ}
+    (h : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, t₁ n ≤ t₂ n) : DTIME enc t₁ ⊆ DTIME enc t₂ := by
+  obtain ⟨c₂', hc⟩ := exists_linear_of_eventually_le h c₁ c₂
+  exact ⟨c₁, c₂', s, ComputableInTimeAndSpace.mono hA (fun a => hc _) fun _ => le_rfl⟩
+/-- Every function of the instances is bounded by a function of the length of the encoded
+instance: there are finitely many instances of each length. -/

+    ∃ s : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ a, S a ≤ s (enc a).length := by
+  exact ⟨fun n => (hfin n).toFinset.sup S, fun a =>
+/-- A Boolean function, tidily computable within a time bound of the length of the encoded

+theorem setOf_mem_DTIME_of_computableTidilyInO {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {f : α → Bool}

+  refine ⟨c, c, fun n => c * (s n + 1), decidableInTimeAndSpace_iff.mpr ⟨f, ?_, fun a => Iff.rfl⟩⟩
+/-- The problems decidable within time `O(t n)`, that is `c₁ * t n + c₂` for constants `c₁` and
+`c₂`, on instances whose encoding under `enc` has length `n`, by a nondeterministic machine with a

+  rintro A ⟨c₁, c₂, k, State, hfinite, ntm, hA⟩

+/-- `NTIME` only depends on the time bound eventually. -/
+theorem NTIME_mono_of_eventually_le {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {t₁ t₂ : ℕ → ℕ}

+  obtain ⟨f, ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, htm⟩, hf⟩ := decidableInTimeAndSpace_iff.mp hA

+  obtain ⟨⟨u, hhalt, hout⟩, htime, -⟩ := htm a
+/-- The problems decidable with bounded error within time `O(t n)`, that is `c₁ * t n + c₂` for

+    BPTIME enc t₁ ⊆ BPTIME enc t₂ := by
+  rintro A ⟨c₁, c₂, k, State, hfinite, machine, hA⟩
+  exact ⟨c₁, c₂, k, State, hfinite, machine,
+/-- `BPTIME` only depends on the time bound eventually. -/
+theorem BPTIME_mono_of_eventually_le {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {t₁ t₂ : ℕ → ℕ}
+    (h : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, t₁ n ≤ t₂ n) : BPTIME enc t₁ ⊆ BPTIME enc t₂ := by
+  rintro A ⟨c₁, c₂, k, State, hfinite, machine, hA⟩
+  obtain ⟨c₂', hc⟩ := exists_linear_of_eventually_le h c₁ c₂
+  exact ⟨c₁, c₂', k, State, hfinite, machine, hA.mono fun a => hc _⟩
+/-- An explicit polynomial bound `c * (n + 1) ^ d` is a bound `O(n ^ d)`. -/

+a function `V : α × List Bool → Option Bool`, computable in polynomial time on inputs
+`frame (enc a) ++ r`, such that for every instance `a` an answer `V (a, r) = some b` is always
+right, `b = true` exactly when `a ∈ A`, and at least half of the random strings `r` of length
+`p (enc a).length` give an answer (`Cslib.Complexity.DecidesWithZeroError`). These are the
+algorithms that never err and say "don't know" with probability at most `1 / 2`
+[Arora and Barak, Section 7.3][AroraBarak09]; the definition through expected polynomial running
+time defines the same class, but expected running time is not modelled here.
+(`Cslib.Complexity.ZPP_eq_RP_inter_coRP`). Answering `true` only on the answer `some true` decides
+a problem in `ZPP` with one-sided error, and so does answering `false` only on `some false` for its
+complement. Conversely, for one-sided-error deciders of a problem and of its complement, which
+read disjoint parts of the random string, the first accepting gives the answer `some true`, the
+second the answer `some false`, and neither errs; on a member the first accepts on at least half of
+the random strings, and on a non-member the second does.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- `V` decides `A` with zero error, using random strings whose length is `p` evaluated at the
+length of the encoded instance: for every instance `a`, an answer `V (a, r) = some b` is right,
+`b = true` exactly when `a ∈ A`, and at least half of the random strings give an answer. -/
+def DecidesWithZeroError (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : α × List Bool → Option Bool) (A : Set α) : Prop :=
+  ∀ a, (∀ r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, ∀ b, V (a, List.ofFn r) = some b →
+/-- The problems decided with zero error by polynomial-time machines reading polynomially long
+random strings, with respect to the encoding `enc` of instances. -/
+def ZPP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α) :=
+  {A | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Option Bool),
+theorem mem_ZPP {A : Set α} : A ∈ ZPP enc ↔ ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+variable {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Option Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- Accepting exactly on the answer `some true` decides the problem with one-sided error. -/
+theorem decidesWithOneSidedError (h : DecidesWithZeroError enc p V A) :
+    DecidesWithOneSidedError enc p (fun x => (V x).getD false) A := fun a => by
+    rw [hb, Option.getD_some, (hright r b hb).mpr ha]
+    cases hV : V (a, List.ofFn r) with
+/-- Negating the answers decides the complement with zero error. -/
+theorem compl (h : DecidesWithZeroError enc p V A) :
+    DecidesWithZeroError enc p (fun x => (V x).map Bool.not) Aᶜ := fun a => by
+  refine ⟨fun r b hb => ?_, by simpa only [Option.isSome_map] using hhalf⟩
+theorem compl_mem_ZPP {A : Set α} (hA : A ∈ ZPP enc) : Aᶜ ∈ ZPP enc := by
+  refine ⟨p, fun x => (V x).map Bool.not, ?_, h.compl⟩
+  have : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => (V x).elim none fun b => some !b)
+/-- **`ZPP ⊆ RP`**: accept exactly on the answer `some true`. -/
+theorem ZPP_subset_RP : ZPP enc ⊆ RP enc := fun _ ⟨p, V, hV, h⟩ =>
+/-- **`ZPP ⊆ coRP`**: the complement is in `ZPP`, hence in `RP`. -/
+theorem ZPP_subset_coRP : ZPP enc ⊆ coRP enc := fun _ hA => ZPP_subset_RP (compl_mem_ZPP hA)
+/-- A random string of length `m + k` is a random string of length `m` followed by one of
+private def splitEquiv (m k : ℕ) : (Fin (m + k) → Bool) ≃ (Fin m → Bool) × (Fin k → Bool) :=
+private theorem ofFn_eq_append (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin (m + k) → Bool) :
+    List.ofFn r = List.ofFn (splitEquiv m k r).1 ++ List.ofFn (splitEquiv m k r).2 := by
+/-- Counting the random strings of length `m + k` by their first `m` and last `k` bits. -/
+private theorem card_filter_take_drop (m k : ℕ) (P : List Bool → List Bool → Prop)
+      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : (Fin m → Bool) × (Fin k → Bool) =>
+  refine Finset.card_equiv (splitEquiv m k) fun r => ?_
+  rw [ofFn_eq_append m k r, List.take_left' (List.length_ofFn), List.drop_left' List.length_ofFn]
+/-- The random strings of length `m + k` whose first `m` bits satisfy `P`. -/
+private theorem card_filter_take (m k : ℕ) (P : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
+    (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (m + k) → Bool => P ((List.ofFn r).take m)).card =
+      (Finset.univ.filter fun u : Fin m → Bool => P (List.ofFn u)).card * 2 ^ k := by
+  rw [card_filter_take_drop m k fun u _ => P u, ← Finset.univ_product_univ,
+    Finset.filter_product_left (fun u : Fin m → Bool => P (List.ofFn u)), Finset.card_product]
+/-- The random strings of length `m + k` whose last `k` bits satisfy `P`. -/
+private theorem card_filter_drop (m k : ℕ) (P : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
+    (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (m + k) → Bool => P ((List.ofFn r).drop m)).card =
+      2 ^ m * (Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin k → Bool => P (List.ofFn v)).card := by
+  rw [card_filter_take_drop m k fun _ v => P v, ← Finset.univ_product_univ,
+    Finset.filter_product_right (fun v : Fin k → Bool => P (List.ofFn v)), Finset.card_product]
+/-- A prefix of the right length is a random string of that length. -/
+private theorem exists_ofFn_eq_take {m k : ℕ} (r : Fin (m + k) → Bool) :
+    ∃ u : Fin m → Bool, List.ofFn u = (List.ofFn r).take m :=
+  ⟨(splitEquiv m k r).1, by rw [ofFn_eq_append m k r, List.take_left' List.length_ofFn]⟩
+/-- A suffix of the right length is a random string of that length. -/
+private theorem exists_ofFn_eq_drop {m k : ℕ} (r : Fin (m + k) → Bool) :
+    ∃ v : Fin k → Bool, List.ofFn v = (List.ofFn r).drop m :=
+  ⟨(splitEquiv m k r).2, by rw [ofFn_eq_append m k r, List.drop_left' List.length_ofFn]⟩
+/-- **`RP ∩ coRP ⊆ ZPP`**: with one-sided-error deciders `V₁` of `A` and `V₂` of its complement,
+reading the first and the last part of the random string, answer `some true` when `V₁` accepts,
+theorem RP_inter_coRP_subset_ZPP : RP enc ∩ coRP enc ⊆ ZPP enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨⟨p₁, V₁, hV₁, h₁⟩, ⟨p₂, V₂, hV₂, h₂⟩⟩
+  let len (a : α) : ℕ := p₁.eval (enc a).length
+  let V (x : α × List Bool) : Option Bool :=
+    if V₁ (x.1, x.2.take (len x.1)) then some true
+    else if V₂ (x.1, x.2.drop (len x.1)) then some false else none
+  have hlen : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => len x.1) (encPair enc encBits)
+  have hpoly : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) (encOption encBool) :=
+  refine ⟨p₁ + p₂, V, hpoly, fun a => ?_⟩
+  have heval : (p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length = len a + p₂.eval (enc a).length :=
+  -- `V₁` never accepts a non-member, and `V₂` never accepts a member
+  have hV₁ (ha : a ∉ A) (r : Fin (len a + p₂.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) :
+  have hV₂ (ha : a ∈ A) (r : Fin (len a + p₂.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) :
+    split_ifs at hb with hacc hrej <;> cases hb
+    · -- on a member, `V₁` accepts on at least half of its random strings
+              V₁ (a, List.ofFn u) = true).card * 2 ^ p₂.eval (enc a).length :=
+        _ = 2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (len a + p₂.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+    · -- on a non-member, `V₂` accepts on at least half of its random strings
+        _ ≤ 2 ^ len a * (2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin (p₂.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+        _ = 2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (len a + p₂.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+theorem ZPP_eq_RP_inter_coRP : ZPP enc = RP enc ∩ coRP enc :=

+For every input length `N` we fix the parameters of Ben-Sasson and Kopparty's construction
+* the field degree `n` is the product of the primes chosen greedily, in increasing order, from
+  the primes in `(L, 4 L]` with product at most `N / (ℓ + 1) ^ 2`
+* `F = 𝔽_{2 ^ n}` with the monomial basis in roots of the irreducible polynomials of least code of
+  the prime degrees (`Cslib.AffineDisperser.compositeBasis`); each of these polynomials is found
+  by an exhaustive search over fewer than `2 ^ (4 L + 1) ≤ 2 N ^ (4 / 3)` codes;
+* `r = ⌊N / n⌋` blocks of `n` bits, read from the first `r n` input bits, block after block, each
+  block in the mixed-radix order of the monomials (`Cslib.AffineDisperser.explicitPos`);
+The function `Cslib.AffineDisperser.explicitDisperser N : BitString N → Bool` is
+`traceSym 1 r t` on these blocks. Every prime factor of `n` exceeds `L`, so proper subfields of
+`F` have at most `2 ^ s` elements, `s = ⌊n / (L + 1)⌋`, and the function is nonconstant on every
+affine subspace of `BitString N` of dimension greater than
+`d(N) = N - r n + r * max (r + 1) s + r * (r + 1) + n t + ⌊n r / t⌋`
+Ben-Sasson and Kopparty take `n` prime and reach dimension `6 N ^ (4 / 5)`
+[BenSassonKopparty2012]; the field then needs an irreducible polynomial of large prime degree,
+which exhaustive search cannot find in polynomial time. The composite degree keeps every search
+small at the price of the subfield term `r s ≤ N / (L + 1)`, so our threshold is `O(N / log N)`
+  every affine subspace of `BitString N` of dimension greater than `explicitThreshold N`.
+* [E. Ben-Sasson, S. Kopparty, *Affine dispersers from subspace polynomials*][BenSassonKopparty2012]
+/-- The prime bound `L = ⌊⌊log₂ N⌋ / 3⌋`: the field degree is a product of primes in
+/-- The primes whose product is the field degree on `N` bits: chosen greedily, in increasing order,

+/-- The subfield exponent `s = ⌊n / (L + 1)⌋`: proper subfields of `𝔽_{2 ^ n}` have at most
+/-- **The dimension threshold** `d(N) = N - r n + r * max (r + 1) s + r * (r + 1) + n t + ⌊n r / t⌋`
+    (numBlocks N * max (numBlocks N + 1) (subfieldExp N) + numBlocks N * (numBlocks N + 1) +
+      fieldDegree N * symDegree N + fieldDegree N * numBlocks N / symDegree N)

+theorem fieldDegree_eq_prod (N : ℕ) : fieldDegree N = (degreePrimes N).prod := by

+/-- The monomials indexing the basis of `ExplicitField N`. -/
+/-- The monomial basis of `ExplicitField N` in roots of the irreducible polynomials of least code of
+noncomputable def explicitBasis (N : ℕ) : Basis (ExplicitMonomial N) (ZMod 2) (ExplicitField N) :=
+theorem numBlocks_mul_le (N : ℕ) : numBlocks N * fieldDegree N ≤ N :=
+/-- The input position of coordinate `J` of block `i`: blocks follow each other, and coordinates
+within a block are numbered in the mixed-radix order of `finPiFinEquiv`. -/
+def explicitPos (N : ℕ) (q : Fin (numBlocks N) × ExplicitMonomial N) : Fin N :=
+/-- **The explicit affine disperser** on `N` bits: Ben-Sasson and Kopparty's function

+# Products of primes in an interval
+The explicit affine disperser works over `𝔽_{2 ^ n}` for `n` a product of distinct primes from an
+interval `(L, 4 L]`, kept below a target `T` by a greedy walk through the primes in increasing
+order (`Cslib.AffineDisperser.selectBelow`). The walk either takes every prime or ends within a
+bounds show that the product of all primes in `(L, 4 L]` is at least `4 ^ L` up to a factor
+`θ (4 L) ≥ 4 L log 2 - O(√L log L)` beats the upper bound `θ L ≤ 2 L log 2` by `2 L log 2`.
+* `Cslib.AffineDisperser.primesIoc`: the primes in `(a, b]`, in increasing order.
+* `Cslib.AffineDisperser.selectBelow`: the greedy choice of primes with product at most `T`.
+* `Cslib.AffineDisperser.prod_selectBelow_le`: the chosen product is at most `T`.
+* `Cslib.AffineDisperser.prod_le_or_lt_mul_prod_selectBelow`: either every prime is chosen or the
+  product exceeds `T / B`, for `B` a bound on the primes.
+  `(4 L + 1) ^ (4 ⌊√L⌋ + 5)` times the product of the primes in `(L, 4 L]`.
+* [P. L. Chebyshev, *Mémoire sur les nombres premiers*][Chebyshev1852]
+/-- The primes `p` with `a < p ≤ b`, in increasing order. -/
+theorem mem_primesIoc {a b p : ℕ} : p ∈ primesIoc a b ↔ a < p ∧ p ≤ b ∧ p.Prime := by
+/-- The greedy choice from a list `ps` of primes with product at most `T`: walk through `ps`,
+keeping each prime that fits into the remaining budget. -/
+def selectBelow : ℕ → List ℕ → List ℕ
+  | T, p :: ps => if p ≤ T then p :: selectBelow (T / p) ps else selectBelow T ps
+theorem selectBelow_sublist (T : ℕ) (ps : List ℕ) : (selectBelow T ps).Sublist ps := by
+/-- The greedy choice has product at most the budget `T ≥ 1`. -/
+theorem prod_selectBelow_le {T : ℕ} (hT : 1 ≤ T) (ps : List ℕ) : (selectBelow T ps).prod ≤ T := by
+      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos p with rfl | hp0
+      · calc p * (selectBelow (T / p) ps).prod ≤ p * (T / p) :=
+/-- **The greedy choice is large**: if every element of `ps` is positive and at most `B`, either
+every element is chosen (the product of `ps` is at most the chosen product) or the chosen product
+    ps.prod ≤ (selectBelow T ps).prod ∨ T < B * (selectBelow T ps).prod := by
+    have hps' : ∀ q ∈ ps, 0 < q ∧ q ≤ B := fun q hq => hps q (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hq)
+      rcases ih (T / p) hps' with h | h
+        calc T < B * (selectBelow (T / p) ps).prod * p := h
+        List.prod_pos fun q hq => (hps' q ((selectBelow_sublist T ps).subset hq)).1
+    (primesIoc a b).prod = ∏ p ∈ Finset.Ico (a + 1) (b + 1) with p.Prime, p := by
+    show b + 1 - (a + 1) = b - a by omega]
+/-- **Chebyshev's bounds on primes in `(L, 4 L]`**: `4 ^ L ≤ (4 L + 1) ^ (4 ⌊√L⌋ + 5)` times
+    4 ^ L ≤ (4 * L + 1) ^ (4 * Nat.sqrt L + 5) * (primesIoc L (4 * L)).prod := by
+  have hP : primorial (4 * L) = primorial L * P := by
+    rw [show P = _ from prod_primesIoc L (4 * L), show 4 * L = L + 3 * L by ring, primorial_add]
+  have hPpos : 0 < P := List.prod_pos fun p hp => (mem_primesIoc.1 hp).2.2.pos
+  have hPr : 0 < (P : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hPpos
+  have hprim : 0 < (primorial L : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast primorial_pos L
+  -- Chebyshev's bounds `θ (4 L) ≥ 4 L log 2 - log (4 L + 1) - 2 √(4 L) log (4 L)`, `θ L ≤ L log 4`
+  rw [hP, Nat.cast_mul (primorial L) P, Real.log_mul hprim.ne' hPr.ne'] at h1
+    rw [Real.sqrt_mul (by norm_num), show (4 : ℝ) = 2 ^ 2 by norm_num, Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)]
+  have hs : √(L : ℝ) ≤ Nat.sqrt L + 1 := by
+    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos L with rfl | hL
+    · have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ L := by exact_mod_cast hL
+  have hlog : Real.log (4 * L) ≤ Real.log (4 * L + 1) := by
+    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos L with rfl | hL
+  have hmul : √(L : ℝ) * Real.log (4 * L) ≤ (Nat.sqrt L + 1) * Real.log (4 * L + 1) :=
+  have key : (L : ℝ) * Real.log 4 ≤ (4 * Nat.sqrt L + 5) * Real.log (4 * L + 1) + Real.log P := by
+  have hreal : ((4 ^ L : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (((4 * L + 1) ^ (4 * Nat.sqrt L + 5) * P : ℕ) : ℝ) := by

+# The threshold of the explicit affine disperser
+The explicit disperser on `N` bits is nonconstant on affine subspaces of dimension greater than
+`explicitThreshold N`. With `ℓ = ⌊log₂ N⌋`, `L = ⌊ℓ / 3⌋` and `n`, `r`, `s`, `t` as in
+`Cslib.AffineDisperser.explicitThreshold`, every term is at most a constant times `N / (ℓ + 1)`,
+except `2 r (r + 1)`, which is small because `n` is large:
+* the unread bits number `N - r n < n ≤ N / (ℓ + 1) ^ 2`, and `n t, ⌊n r / t⌋ ≤ N / (ℓ + 1)`;
+* the subfield term is `r s ≤ N / (L + 1) ≤ 3 N / (ℓ + 1)`;
+* either the greedy choice of primes stops within a factor `4 L` of its budget
+  `N / (ℓ + 1) ^ 2`, and then `r < 2 (ℓ + 1) ^ 3`, or it takes every prime in `(L, 4 L]`, whose
+  product is at least `4 ^ L / (4 L + 1) ^ (4 ⌊√L⌋ + 5) ≥ √(8 (ℓ + 1) N)` for large `N` by
+Hence `(ℓ + 1) * explicitThreshold N ≤ 6 N` for all large `N`
+(`Cslib.AffineDisperser.eventually_explicitThreshold_le`), and the threshold is `O(N / log N)`.
+  `(⌊log₂ N⌋ + 1) * explicitThreshold N ≤ 6 N` for all large `N`.
+  `N`, so the disperser theorem is not vacuous.
+/-- Exponentials beat polynomials: `c * (n + 1) ^ k ≤ 2 ^ n` for all large `n`. -/
+theorem eventually_mul_pow_le_two_pow (c k : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * (n + 1) ^ k ≤ 2 ^ n := by
+  filter_upwards [h.eventually (gt_mem_nhds one_pos), eventually_ge_atTop 1] with n hn hn1
+  have hn1' : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn1
+  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 2 ^ n := by positivity
+  rw [← mul_div_assoc, div_lt_one hpos] at hn
+  have h2 : ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ k ≤ 2 ^ k * (n : ℝ) ^ k := by
+      _ = c * 2 ^ k * n ^ k := by ring
+/-- The Chebyshev factor is small: `64 (3 L + 3) (4 L + 1) ^ (8 ⌊√L⌋ + 10) ≤ 2 ^ L` for all large
+    ∀ᶠ L : ℕ in atTop, 64 * (3 * L + 3) * (4 * L + 1) ^ (8 * Nat.sqrt L + 10) ≤ 2 ^ L := by
+  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop ((10 * Q + S + 10) ^ 2)] with L hL
+  have hs : 10 * Q + S + 10 ≤ s := Nat.le_sqrt'.2 hL
+  have hsL : s ^ 2 ≤ L := Nat.sqrt_le' L
+  have hq : 10 * q ≤ s := Nat.mul_div_le s 10
+  have hqQ : Q ≤ q := by omega
+  have h3 : s + q * (8 * s + 10) ≤ L := by nlinarith
+    _ = 2 ^ (s + q * (8 * s + 10)) := by rw [← pow_mul, ← pow_add]
+  tendsto_atTop_atTop.2 fun b => ⟨2 ^ b, fun _ hN => Nat.le_log_of_pow_le one_lt_two hN⟩
+/-- **The threshold is `O(N / log N)`**, with exact constants:
+`(⌊log₂ N⌋ + 1) * explicitThreshold N ≤ 6 N` for all large `N`. -/
+    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (Nat.log 2 N + 1) * explicitThreshold N ≤ 6 * N := by
+  set ℓ := Nat.log 2 N with hℓ
+  have hNℓ : 2 ^ ℓ ≤ N := Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 hN0
+  have hNlt : N < 2 ^ (ℓ + 1) := Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self one_lt_two N
+  have hr : r = N / n := rfl
+  have hn : n = (selectBelow T (primesIoc L (4 * L))).prod := fieldDegree_eq_prod N
+  have hnT : n ≤ T := hn ▸ prod_selectBelow_le hT1 _
+  have hrn : r * n ≤ N := numBlocks_mul_le N
+  have hwaste : N - r * n < n := by
+  have hmax : r * max (r + 1) (subfieldExp N) ≤ r * (r + 1) + r * subfieldExp N := by
+  have hrs : r * subfieldExp N ≤ N / (L + 1) :=
+  have hnt : n * symDegree N ≤ N / (ℓ + 1) :=
+    calc n * symDegree N ≤ T * (ℓ + 1) := Nat.mul_le_mul hnT le_rfl
+  have hnrt : n * r / symDegree N ≤ N / (ℓ + 1) :=
+  have hthr : explicitThreshold N ≤ T + 2 * (r * (r + 1)) + N / (L + 1) + 2 * (N / (ℓ + 1)) := by
+    change N - r * n + (r * max (r + 1) (subfieldExp N) + r * (r + 1) + n * symDegree N +
+  -- the number of blocks is small
+    have hps : ∀ p ∈ primesIoc L (4 * L), 0 < p ∧ p ≤ 4 * L := fun p hp => by
+    rcases prod_le_or_lt_mul_prod_selectBelow T hps with hP | hTn
+    · -- every prime in `(L, 4 L]` is chosen
+      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos r with hr0 | hr0
+      have hPpos : 0 < P := List.prod_pos fun p hp => (hps p hp).1
+        calc 16 ^ L = (4 ^ L) ^ 2 := by rw [← pow_mul, mul_comm, pow_mul]; norm_num

+# Monotonicity of the oracle classes under reductions
+If the oracle language `A` reduces to `B` by a polynomial-time map `g`, a computation relative to
+`A` becomes one relative to `B`: every request `w` is replaced by the request `g w`, of which one
+to `A` is itself an oracle program querying `B`, charged for computing `g w` and for reading one
+bit of the reply. Hence `P^A ⊆ P^B` and `NP^A ⊆ NP^B`

+relative to `A` is polynomial time relative to `B`: every request `w` is replaced by the request
+`g w`, keeping one bit of the reply. -/

+# Polynomial time relative to an oracle in polynomial space
+Relative to an oracle language decided within polynomial space, polynomial time and
+nondeterministic polynomial time are within polynomial space [Arora and Barak, Theorem
+A computation in polynomial time relative to `A` is the clocked run, with every coin fixed to
+The run is simulated instruction by instruction, answering each query with the decider of `A` on
+the request, which is no longer than the clock
+So the space is polynomial, while the time charges the decider of `A` once per instruction
+For `NP` relative to `A`, the certificates of the required length are tried one after another, in
+binary order, keeping only the current certificate and whether some certificate was accepted
+deterministic search replaces the passage through `NPSPACE` and Savitch's theorem.
+  relative to an oracle in `PSPACE` is within polynomial space.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- A problem in `PSPACE` has a tidy decider within explicit bounds, the space polynomial in the
+theorem exists_computableTidilyInO_of_mem_PSPACE {L : Set α} (hL : L ∈ PSPACE enc) :
+    ∃ T S, PolyBounded (fun a => (enc a).length) S ∧
+      ∃ f : α → Bool, ComputableTidilyInO f enc encBool T S ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ L ↔ f a = true := by
+  obtain ⟨f, ⟨t, s, hs, hf⟩, hL⟩ := hL

+    .of_bounds hc 1 (fun a => by omega) (fun a => by omega) (fun a => ?_), hL⟩
+/-- A tidy decider within polynomial space puts a problem in `PSPACE`. -/

+    (hL : ∀ a, a ∈ L ↔ f a = true) : L ∈ PSPACE enc :=
+/-- Binary increment, least significant bit first, discarding the final carry. -/
