+# From directed to undirected Hamiltonian paths and cycles
+Splitting every vertex of a directed graph into three reduces directed Hamiltonian cycles and paths
+to undirected ones: for cycles this is Karp's reduction [Karp1972], for paths a variant of
+[Sipser, Theorem 7.55][Sipser2013]. In `Graph.split G`, every declared vertex `v` of `G` becomes a
+path `in(v) - mid(v) - out(v)` (`Graph.splitVertex G v r` for `r = 0, 1, 2`), and every arc
+`(u, v)` of `G` becomes an edge `out(u) - in(v)`. A middle vertex is adjacent only to the two other
+vertices of its gadget, so an undirected Hamiltonian path from `in(s)` to `out(t)` traverses every
+gadget from its entry to its exit, and the order of the gadgets is a directed Hamiltonian path from
+`s` to `t`; an undirected Hamiltonian cycle, read in a suitable direction, likewise traverses every
+gadget from its entry to its exit. Unlike Sipser's construction, the gadgets of `s` and `t` keep
+all three vertices, which treats the endpoints uniformly and covers `s = t`.
+Vertices of the split graph are numbered by first occurrence in the vertex list, so repeated vertex
+entries share one gadget. An undeclared vertex gets labels that no declared vertex has: arcs with an
+undeclared endpoint become edges with an undeclared endpoint, which the undirected problems ignore,
+and an undeclared `s` or `t` makes both path instances negative. A self-loop `(v, v)` becomes the
+edge `out(v) - in(v)`, so a single vertex with a self-loop, which is a directed Hamiltonian cycle,
+  `(G.split, G.splitVertex s 0, G.splitVertex t 2) ∈ HamPath ↔ (G, s, t) ∈ DirHamPath`.
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*][Sipser2013]
+/-- Vertex `r` of the gadget of `v` in `Graph.split G`: `r = 0` is `in(v)`, `r = 1` is `mid(v)`
+and `r = 2` is `out(v)`. Vertices are numbered by their first occurrence in `G.1`, so an
+undeclared vertex gets the number `G.1.length`, which no declared vertex has. -/
+def splitVertex (G : Graph) (v r : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.pair (G.1.idxOf v) r
+/-- The vertex-splitting graph of a directed graph `G`: every declared vertex `v` becomes a path
+`in(v) - mid(v) - out(v)`, and every arc `(u, v)` becomes an edge `out(u) - in(v)`. -/
+  (G.1.flatMap fun v => [G.splitVertex v 0, G.splitVertex v 1, G.splitVertex v 2],
+    G.2.map fun e => (G.splitVertex e.1 2, G.splitVertex e.2 0))
+/-- Gadget vertices are equal exactly when their vertices have the same first occurrence and their
+theorem splitVertex_eq_splitVertex_iff {G : Graph} {u v r r' : ℕ} :
+    G.splitVertex u r = G.splitVertex v r' ↔ G.1.idxOf u = G.1.idxOf v ∧ r = r' :=
+private theorem eq_of_idxOf_eq {G : Graph} {u v : ℕ} (hv : v ∈ G.1)
+    (h : G.1.idxOf u = G.1.idxOf v) : u = v :=
+/-- Gadget vertices of a declared vertex determine the vertex and the position in the gadget. -/
+theorem splitVertex_eq_splitVertex_iff_of_mem {G : Graph} {u v r r' : ℕ} (hv : v ∈ G.1) :
+    G.splitVertex u r = G.splitVertex v r' ↔ u = v ∧ r = r' := by
+  exact ⟨fun h => ⟨eq_of_idxOf_eq hv h.1, h.2⟩, fun h => ⟨h.1 ▸ rfl, h.2⟩⟩
+    x ∈ [G.splitVertex v 0, G.splitVertex v 1, G.splitVertex v 2] ↔
+      ∃ r < 3, x = G.splitVertex v r := by
+    exacts [⟨0, by omega, rfl⟩, ⟨1, by omega, rfl⟩, ⟨2, by omega, rfl⟩]
+    obtain rfl | rfl | rfl : r = 0 ∨ r = 1 ∨ r = 2 := by omega
+    exacts [Or.inl rfl, Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), Or.inr (Or.inr rfl)]
+/-- The declared vertices of the split graph are the gadget vertices of declared vertices. -/
+    x ∈ G.split.1 ↔ ∃ v ∈ G.1, ∃ r < 3, x = G.splitVertex v r := by
+/-- A gadget vertex is a declared vertex of the split graph exactly when its vertex is declared
+    G.splitVertex v r ∈ G.split.1 ↔ v ∈ G.1 ∧ r < 3 := by
+    (a, b) ∈ G.split.2 ↔ (∃ v ∈ G.1, (a = G.splitVertex v 0 ∧ b = G.splitVertex v 1) ∨
+      ∃ e ∈ G.2, a = G.splitVertex e.1 2 ∧ b = G.splitVertex e.2 0 := by
+  simp only [split, List.mem_append, List.mem_flatMap, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false,
+  refine or_congr Iff.rfl (exists_congr fun e => and_congr_right fun _ => ?_)
+  exact ⟨fun ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ => ⟨h₁.symm, h₂.symm⟩, fun ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ => ⟨h₁.symm, h₂.symm⟩⟩
+    G.split.toSimpleGraph.Adj a b ↔ a ≠ b ∧ ((a, b) ∈ G.split.2 ∨ (b, a) ∈ G.split.2) :=
+private theorem adj_in_mid {G : Graph} {v : ℕ} (hv : v ∈ G.1) :
+private theorem adj_mid_out {G : Graph} {v : ℕ} (hv : v ∈ G.1) :
+/-- Between declared vertices, an exit is adjacent to an entry exactly along an arc. -/
+private theorem adj_out_in_iff {G : Graph} {u v : ℕ} (hu : u ∈ G.1) (hv : v ∈ G.1) :
+    G.split.toSimpleGraph.Adj (G.splitVertex u 2) (G.splitVertex v 0) ↔ (u, v) ∈ G.2 := by
+  · rintro ⟨-, (⟨w, -, h | h⟩ | ⟨e, he, h₁, h₂⟩) | (⟨w, -, h | h⟩ | ⟨e, -, h₁, h₂⟩)⟩
+/-- A middle vertex is adjacent only to the two other vertices of its gadget. -/
+    x = G.splitVertex v 0 ∨ x = G.splitVertex v 2 := by
+  rcases h with ⟨-, (⟨w, -, ⟨h₁, rfl⟩ | ⟨h₁, rfl⟩⟩ | ⟨e, -, h₁, rfl⟩) |
+/-- An exit vertex of a declared vertex is adjacent only to its middle vertex and to entries of
+private theorem eq_of_adj_out {G : Graph} {v x : ℕ} (hv : v ∈ G.1)
+    x = G.splitVertex v 1 ∨ ∃ w, (v, w) ∈ G.2 ∧ x = G.splitVertex w 0 := by
+  rcases h with ⟨-, (⟨w, -, ⟨h₁, rfl⟩ | ⟨h₁, rfl⟩⟩ | ⟨e, he, h₁, rfl⟩) |
+/-- The gadgets of the vertices of `p`, in order. -/
+private def gadgets (G : Graph) (p : List ℕ) : List ℕ :=
+  p.flatMap fun v => [G.splitVertex v 0, G.splitVertex v 1, G.splitVertex v 2]
+private theorem split_fst (G : Graph) : G.split.1 = gadgets G G.1 := rfl
+private theorem gadgets_nil (G : Graph) : gadgets G [] = [] := rfl
+private theorem gadgets_cons (G : Graph) (v : ℕ) (p : List ℕ) :
+      G.splitVertex v 0 :: G.splitVertex v 1 :: G.splitVertex v 2 :: gadgets G p := rfl
+private theorem gadgets_append (G : Graph) (p p' : List ℕ) :
+    gadgets G (p ++ p') = gadgets G p ++ gadgets G p' :=
+private theorem mem_gadgets {G : Graph} {p : List ℕ} {x : ℕ} :
+    x ∈ gadgets G p ↔ ∃ v ∈ p, ∃ r < 3, x = G.splitVertex v r := by
+private theorem length_gadgets (G : Graph) (p : List ℕ) : (gadgets G p).length = 3 * p.length := by
+    rw [gadgets_cons, List.length_cons, List.length_cons, List.length_cons, ih, List.length_cons]
+/-- The gadgets of distinct declared vertices are disjoint. -/
+private theorem nodup_gadgets_iff {G : Graph} {p : List ℕ} (hp : ∀ v ∈ p, v ∈ G.1) :
+    refine ⟨fun v _ => ?_, h.imp_of_mem fun {a b} _ hb hab x hxa hxb => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hxa hxb
+      rcases hxa with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hxb with h | h | h <;>
+    (hp : ∀ v, v ∈ p ↔ v ∈ G.1) (x : ℕ) : x ∈ gadgets G p ↔ x ∈ G.split.1 := by
+    (hp : ∀ v ∈ p, v ∈ G.1) (hcov : ∀ x, x ∈ gadgets G p ↔ x ∈ G.split.1) (v : ℕ) :
+/-- Along declared vertices, a chain of gadgets is a directed walk. -/
+private theorem isChain_gadgets_iff {G : Graph} {p : List ℕ} (hp : ∀ v ∈ p, v ∈ G.1) :
+    (gadgets G p).IsChain G.split.toSimpleGraph.Adj ↔ p.IsChain fun u v => (u, v) ∈ G.2 := by
+    have hp' : ∀ v ∈ p, v ∈ G.1 := fun v hv => hp v (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hv)
+    have h₃ : [G.splitVertex a 0, G.splitVertex a 1, G.splitVertex a 2].IsChain
+    have hhead : (∀ x ∈ [G.splitVertex a 0, G.splitVertex a 1, G.splitVertex a 2].getLast?,
+      | cons b p => simp [adj_out_in_iff ha (hp' b (List.mem_cons_self ..))]
+    rw [gadgets_cons, show ∀ l : List ℕ, G.splitVertex a 0 :: G.splitVertex a 1 ::
+      G.splitVertex a 2 :: l = [G.splitVertex a 0, G.splitVertex a 1, G.splitVertex a 2] ++ l
+      from fun _ => rfl, List.isChain_append, ih hp', head?_gadgets, hhead,
+    exact ⟨fun ⟨_, h₁, h₂⟩ => ⟨h₂, h₁⟩, fun ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ => ⟨h₃, h₂, h₁⟩⟩
+/-- Along declared vertices, a closed chain of gadgets is a closed directed walk. -/
+private theorem chain_gadgets_iff {G : Graph} {p : List ℕ} (hp : ∀ v ∈ p, v ∈ G.1) :
+      (p : Cycle ℕ).Chain fun u v => (u, v) ∈ G.2 := by
+    have hp' : ∀ v ∈ a :: (p ++ [a]), v ∈ G.1 := by
+      simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_append, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hv
+      rcases hv with rfl | hv | rfl
+    have e : gadgets G (a :: (p ++ [a])) = (G.splitVertex a 0 :: G.splitVertex a 1 ::
+    have hl : (G.splitVertex a 2 :: (gadgets G p ++ [G.splitVertex a 0])).getLast? =
+    rw [gadgets_cons, Cycle.chain_coe_cons, Cycle.chain_coe_cons, ← isChain_gadgets_iff hp', e,
+/-- A chain of the split graph without repetitions through declared vertices that starts at an
+entry, does not end at a middle vertex, and contains the middle vertex of each entry it contains,
+private theorem exists_eq_gadgets {G : Graph} (n : ℕ) : ∀ (l : List ℕ) (v : ℕ), l.length ≤ n →
+    l.IsChain G.split.toSimpleGraph.Adj → l.Nodup → (∀ x ∈ l, x ∈ G.split.1) →
+    l.head? = some (G.splitVertex v 0) → (∀ u, l.getLast? ≠ some (G.splitVertex u 1)) →
+    (∀ u ∈ G.1, G.splitVertex u 0 ∈ l → G.splitVertex u 1 ∈ l) →
+    ∃ p, (∀ u ∈ p, u ∈ G.1) ∧ l = gadgets G p := by
+    intro l v hlen hch hnd hdecl hhead hlast hmid
+    have hnd₀ : G.splitVertex v 0 ∉ l₁ := (List.nodup_cons.1 hnd).1

+`TSP` is the decision version of the traveling salesman problem
+[Papadimitriou, Section 9.3][Papadimitriou94]: an instance is a distance matrix `D`, given as a list
+of rows (row `i` lists the distances from city `i`), together with a budget `b`, and it belongs to
+`TSP` when some closed tour visiting every city exactly once has length at most `b`. The
+* The cities are the row indices `0, …, D.length - 1`. Rows may have any length: an entry missing
+  from a ragged or short matrix reads `0` (`TSP.dist`).
+* Distances need not be symmetric, and the diagonal entries are only used by the tour of a single
+  city, which costs `TSP.dist D 0 0`. The matrix without rows is a yes-instance, through the empty
+* A tour is a permutation `p` of the cities, and its length `TSP.tourLength D p` is the sum of the
+  distances from each city of `p` to the next one, the last city returning to the first.
+* Distances and the budget are binary (`encTSP`).
+`TSP` is in `NP`. As for the Hamiltonian problems, a certificate names an ordering of the cities,
+decoded by `Graph.decodeVertexList` from the list `0, …, D.length - 1` of cities; it has length
+`m ^ 2` for instances of encoded length `m`. The verifier checks that the ordering lists every city
+exactly once, and compares the length of its tour with the budget using the binary arithmetic of
+`PolyTime/Nat/Binary.lean`, so distances and budgets of any size are handled without unary
+The reduction `HamCycle.toTSP` from `HamCycle` takes the distinct declared vertices of a graph as
+cities, at distance `1` when they are adjacent and `2` otherwise, with the number `n` of cities as
+the budget. A closed tour has `n` steps of length at least `1`, so it has length at most `n`
+exactly when every step joins adjacent vertices, that is, when it is a Hamiltonian cycle. Graphs
+with fewer than three vertices have no Hamiltonian cycle and are mapped to a fixed no-instance.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.TSP.tourLength_eq_sum`: the tour length as a sum over the positions of the
+  reduces to `TSP` in polynomial time, so `TSP` is `NP`-hard.
+* [M. R. Garey and D. S. Johnson, *Computers and Intractability*][GareyJohnson1979]

+encoded by framed lists of binary distances and a binary budget. -/

+/-- The distance from city `i` to city `j` in the matrix `D`: entry `j` of row `i`. Entries missing
+from a ragged or short matrix read `0`. -/
+def dist (D : List (List ℕ)) (i j : ℕ) : ℕ := (D.getD i []).getD j 0
+/-- The length of the closed tour visiting the cities of `p` in order: the sum of the distances
+from each city of `p` to the next one, the last city returning to the first. A tour of one city
+`c` has length `dist D c c`, and the empty tour has length `0`. -/
+def tourLength (D : List (List ℕ)) (p : List ℕ) : ℕ :=
+/-- The traveling salesman problem: the distance matrices `D` with a budget `b` such that some
+closed tour visiting each city `0, …, D.length - 1` exactly once has length at most `b`. -/

+/-- The tour length as a sum over the positions of the tour: with `q = p ++ p.take 1`, the tour

+`VertexCover` is the set of graphs, given by a list of vertices and a list of edges, together with
+a number `k`, such that `k` of the declared vertices meet every edge between declared vertices
+[Karp1972]. Graphs are read through `Cslib.Complexity.Graph.toSimpleGraph` restricted to the
+with an undeclared endpoint and self-loops are therefore ignored, and repeated vertex entries
+The cover has exactly `k` distinct vertices, matching `IndependentSet`. Since a set of declared
+vertices containing a cover is a cover, this agrees with the textbook formulation "a cover of at
+most `k` vertices" for every `k` up to the number `n` of distinct declared vertices, and
+`VertexCover` rejects every `k > n` (`mem_VertexCover_iff_exists_card_le`). In particular a graph
+without declared vertices belongs to `VertexCover` only with `k = 0`.

+`IndependentSet.toVertexCover` maps `(G, m)` to `(G, n - m)`, where `n` is the number of distinct
+declared vertices; a target `m > n` is mapped to the unsatisfiable target `n + 1` [Karp1972].

+  have hL' : L ≤ Nat.log 2 n := Nat.le_log_of_pow_le one_lt_two hn
+  calc clock i (word j).length ≤ (2 * Nat.log 2 n + 2) ^ i :=
+    _ ≤ n := Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 (by have := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := L); omega)
+/-- **If `SATH` is in `P`, then `H` is bounded**: some index of a machine deciding `SATH` has a
+clock exceeding its polynomial time bound, and from some point on `H` is at most that index. -/
+theorem exists_H_le_of_mem_P (h : SATH ∈ P encBits) : ∃ C, ∀ n, H n ≤ C := by
+  obtain ⟨f, ⟨t, s, ht, -, k, State, hfinite, tm, htm⟩, hf⟩ := h
+  let eS : State ↪ ℕ := (Fintype.equivFin State).toEmbedding.trans Fin.valEmbedding
+  have hrun (x : List Bool) : (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg x) (t x)).Halted ∧
+  obtain ⟨i, hi, hdesc⟩ := exists_index_ge (desc eS eBit tm) (c + e)
+  -- the clock of the index exceeds the time bound
+  have hclock (x : List Bool) : t x ≤ clock i x.length := by
+    calc t x ≤ c * (x.length + 1) ^ e := hle x
+      _ = clock i x.length := by rw [clock, ← mul_pow]; ring_nf
+  rcases lt_or_ge n N with hn | hn
+  · refine (H_le_of_agrees fun j hj => ⟨f (word j), ?_, hf (word j) |>.symm⟩).trans
+    rw [runIndexed, hdesc, min_eq_left (hN n hn j hj)]
+/-! ### The first hole: padding along a bounded exponent -/
+/-- The padding of `φ` along `H`, computed with powers capped at `(m + 1) ^ C` for the length `m`
+noncomputable def padBounded (C : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) : List Bool :=
+  pad (encCNF φ) (capPow (encCNF φ).length (H (encCNF φ).length) (((encCNF φ).length + 1) ^ C))
+  have henc : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun φ => encCNF φ) encCNF encBits :=
+/-- **If `H` is bounded, padding reduces `SAT` to `SATH` in polynomial time.** -/
+theorem reducible_of_H_le {C : ℕ} (hC : ∀ n, H n ≤ C) :
+    PolyTimeReducible encCNF encBits SAT SATH := by
+  refine ⟨padBounded C, computableTidilyInPolyTime_padBounded C, fun φ => ?_⟩
+  have hpow : (encCNF φ).length ^ H (encCNF φ).length ≤ ((encCNF φ).length + 1) ^ C :=
+  rw [padBounded, capPow, min_eq_left hpow, SATH, pad_mem_padSAT_iff]
+theorem SAT_mem_P_of_SATH_mem_P (h : SATH ∈ P encBits) : SAT ∈ P encCNF :=
+/-! ### A frequent value of the exponent -/
+/-- **If `H` takes the value `i` infinitely often, the machine with index `i` agrees with `SATH`
+theorem agrees_of_frequently_H_eq {i : ℕ} (h : ∃ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, H n = i) (w : List Bool) :
+    ∃ b : Bool, runIndexed i w (clock i w.length) = ([eBit b], true) ∧
+  obtain ⟨b, hb, hiff⟩ := agrees_H (hHn ▸ hlog) (index w) (by omega)
+  rw [hHn, word_index, min_eq_left (by omega)] at hb
+/-- **If `H` takes a value infinitely often, `SATH` is in `P`**, decided by running the machine
+with that index within its polynomial clock. -/
+theorem SATH_mem_P_of_frequently_H_eq {i : ℕ} (h : ∃ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, H n = i) :
+  refine ⟨fun w => decide (runIndexed i w (clock i w.length) = ([eBit true], true)), ?_,
+  · obtain ⟨b, hb, hiff⟩ := agrees_of_frequently_H_eq h w
+/-- **If `SATH` is not in `P`, then `H` tends to infinity.** -/
+  have hne (i : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, H n ≠ i :=
+  filter_upwards [(Filter.eventually_all_finset (Finset.range C)).mpr fun i _ => hne i]
+/-! ### The second hole: an unbounded exponent -/
+/-- The unsatisfiable formula with one empty clause. -/
+/-- One round of the self-reduction of `SAT` along a map `R` into words: a formula shorter than
+`N` is kept, and otherwise replaced by the formula padded along `H` in `R φ`, or by `falseCNF` if
+`R φ` is not such a padded word. -/
+noncomputable def shrink (R : CNF ℕ → List Bool) (N : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) : CNF ℕ :=
+  if (encCNF φ).length < N then φ else (padCheck H (R φ)).getD falseCNF
+/-- Along a reduction from `SAT` to `SATH`, a round of the self-reduction preserves
+theorem shrink_mem_SAT_iff {R : CNF ℕ → List Bool} (hR : ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ R φ ∈ SATH) (N : ℕ)
+    (φ : CNF ℕ) : shrink R N φ ∈ SAT ↔ φ ∈ SAT := by
+/-- **A round of the self-reduction shortens long formulas.** Let `R` have output length at most
+`c * (n + 1) ^ d` on formulas of length `n`, and let `H` exceed `d` from `M` on. If `R φ` padded a
+formula at least as long as `φ`, with `φ` of length at least `N`, its padding would be longer than
+theorem length_shrink_lt {R : CNF ℕ → List Bool} {c d M N : ℕ}
+    (hRlen : ∀ φ, (R φ).length ≤ c * ((encCNF φ).length + 1) ^ d) (hM : ∀ m ≥ M, d + 1 ≤ H m)
+    (hN₁ : (encCNF falseCNF).length < N) (hN₂ : M ≤ N) (hN₃ : c * 2 ^ d < N) {φ : CNF ℕ}
+    (hφ : N ≤ (encCNF φ).length) : (encCNF (shrink R N φ)).length < (encCNF φ).length := by
+  cases hc : padCheck H (R φ) with
+    have hpad : n ^ (d + 1) ≤ m ^ H m :=
+    -- the output bound is less than `n ^ (d + 1)`
+      calc c * (n + 1) ^ d ≤ c * (2 ^ d * n ^ d) := by
+        _ = c * 2 ^ d * n ^ d := by ring
+        _ < N * n ^ d := Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hN₃ (Nat.pow_pos hn)
+/-- The self-reduction: as many rounds as the encoded formula is long. -/
+noncomputable def selfReduce (R : CNF ℕ → List Bool) (N : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) : CNF ℕ :=
+/-- The satisfiable formulas whose encodings are shorter than `N`, as their encodings. -/
+    (t := {w : List Bool | w.length < N ∧ ∃ φ ∈ SAT, encCNF φ = w}) fun _ hw => hw.1).toFinset
+theorem mem_smallSAT {N : ℕ} {φ : CNF ℕ} (h : (encCNF φ).length < N) :
+    encCNF φ ∈ smallSAT N ↔ φ ∈ SAT := by
+/-- **The second hole.** If `SAT` reduces to `SATH` in polynomial time and `H` tends to infinity,
+then `SAT` is in `P`: the self-reduction leaves a formula of bounded length, decided by a finite
+theorem SAT_mem_P_of_reducible_of_tendsto (hR : PolyTimeReducible encCNF encBits SAT SATH)
+    (hH : Filter.Tendsto H Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) : SAT ∈ P encCNF := by
+  set N := max ((encCNF falseCNF).length + 1) (max M (c * 2 ^ d + 1)) with hN
+  have hlt (φ : CNF ℕ) (hφ : N ≤ (encCNF φ).length) :=
+    length_shrink_lt hRlen hM (by omega) (by omega) (by omega) hφ
+  -- the polynomial-time certificate of a round
+  have hshrink : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (shrink R N) encCNF encCNF := by
+    have hH' : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : CNF ℕ × ℕ => H p.2) (encPair encCNF encUnary)
+  -- the rounds preserve satisfiability and shorten the formula to below `N`
+    (count := fun φ => (encCNF φ).length) (init := fun φ => φ) (step := shrink R N)
+    (fun φ k ψ => (ψ ∈ SAT ↔ φ ∈ SAT) ∧ (encCNF ψ).length ≤ max ((encCNF φ).length - k) (N - 1))
+    (fun φ k ψ _ ⟨_, hlen⟩ => by omega)
+  refine ⟨fun φ => (smallSAT N).any fun w => decide (encCNF (selfReduce R N φ) = w), ?_,
+        (fun φ => (smallSAT N).any fun w => decide (encCNF φ = w)) encCNF encBool :=
+    have hmem := mem_smallSAT (N := N) (φ := selfReduce R N φ) (by rw [selfReduce]; omega)
+/-- **If `SATH` is `NP`-hard, then `SAT` is in `P`**: either `SATH` is in `P`, and the first hole
+applies, or `H` tends to infinity, and the second hole applies to the reduction of `SAT`. -/
+theorem SAT_mem_P_of_NPHard_SATH (h : NPHard encBits SATH) : SAT ∈ P encCNF := by
+  · exact SAT_mem_P_of_reducible_of_tendsto (h encCNF SAT SAT.mem_NP) (tendsto_H_of_notMem_P hP)
+/-- If Ladner's language is in `P`, then `P = NP`. -/
+theorem P_eq_NP_of_SATH_mem_P (h : SATH ∈ P encBits) {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) :
+/-- If Ladner's language is `NP`-complete, then `P = NP`. -/
+    (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : P enc = NP enc :=
+/-- If `P ≠ NP`, Ladner's language is not in `P`. -/
+theorem SATH_notMem_P {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} (h : P enc ≠ NP enc) :
+/-- If `P ≠ NP`, Ladner's language is not `NP`-complete. -/
+theorem not_NPComplete_SATH {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} (h : P enc ≠ NP enc) :
+/-- **Ladner's theorem.** If `P ≠ NP` (for some encoding of instances), some problem in `NP` is
+neither in `P` nor `NP`-complete: Ladner's language `SATH` [Arora and Barak, Theorem
+theorem exists_NP_not_P_not_NPComplete {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} (h : P enc ≠ NP enc) :
+    ∃ L : Set (List Bool), L ∈ NP encBits ∧ L ∉ P encBits ∧ ¬NPComplete encBits L :=

+# Ladner's language in polynomial time and in NP
+The exponent function `Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.H` of Ladner's language is tidily computable in
+Ladner's language is in `NP` (`Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.SATH_mem_NP`), with a verifier that reads
+the padded formula and evaluates it under the assignment the certificate describes.
+The table of the values `H m`, `m < n`, is built by iterating one step `n` times. The step
+`log₂ (log₂ n)` machine indices; for each, it runs the machine on each of the `n` words with
+indices below `n` with the universal function, for at most `n` steps, and compares the answer with
+membership in the padded language along the table. A word with index below `n` has length at most
+`log₂ n`, so membership is decided by decoding the padded formula and trying the `n` words with
+value is polynomial in `n`, and the polynomial-time calculus certifies the composite.
+The certificate rests on general tools proved first: total decoders for binary numbers, Booleans
+and formulas (`Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.cnfDecoder`), capped powers on unary numbers
+number of steps in unary (`Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.computableTidilyInPolyTime_universal`), and the
+* `Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.bruteSAT`: satisfiability by trying the words with small indices.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.hstepB`: the step of the exponent function as a search.
+  number of steps in unary, is polynomial-time.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.mem_padSAT_iff`: membership in a padded language through `padCheck`.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+theorem rdropWhile_append {α : Type*} (p : α → Bool) (l₁ l₂ : List α) :
+      if l₂.rdropWhile p = [] then l₁.rdropWhile p else l₁ ++ l₂.rdropWhile p := by
+/-- Binary digits, least significant first, read as a number. -/
+def ofBits (w : List Bool) : ℕ := w.foldr Nat.bit 0
+/-- The binary digits of a word read as a number are the word up to its last `true`. -/
+theorem bits_ofBits (w : List Bool) : (ofBits w).bits = w.rdropWhile (!·) := by
+    rw [ofBits, List.foldr_cons, ← ofBits, ← List.singleton_append, rdropWhile_append, ← ih]
+    by_cases h : ofBits w = 0 ∧ b = false
+    · rw [Nat.bits_append_bit _ _ fun h₀ => by simpa [h₀] using h]
+      · obtain rfl : b = true := by simpa [h₀] using h
+/-- Drops the `false`s at the start of a word. -/
+  length_step_le q b := by cases q <;> cases b <;> simp
+theorem dropFalsesT_run_true (w : List Bool) : dropFalsesT.run true w = w := by
+  | cons b w ih => exact congrArg (b :: ·) ih
+theorem dropFalsesT_run (w : List Bool) : dropFalsesT.run false w = w.dropWhile (!·) := by
+/-- Binary numbers are decoded from their digits up to the last `true`. -/
+  -- a tactic proof keeps `Kolmogorov.SelfDelimiting` a proof-only import
+  decode_enc n := by exact Nat.foldr_bit_bits n
+    have hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun w : List Bool => w.dropWhile (!·)) encBits encBits :=
+    have h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun w : List Bool => (w.reverse.dropWhile (!·)).reverse)
+    exact (h.of_enc_eq fun w => by rw [encNat_apply, bits_ofBits]; rfl).exists_degree
+/-- Booleans are decoded from the first symbol. -/
+/-- Formulas in conjunctive normal form are decoded along their encoding. -/
+/-- The formula decoded from a word. -/
+def decodeCNF (w : List Bool) : CNF ℕ := cnfDecoder.decode w
+theorem decodeCNF_encCNF (φ : CNF ℕ) : decodeCNF (encCNF φ) = φ := cnfDecoder.decode_enc φ
+theorem min_min_mul (a b c : ℕ) : min (min a c * b) c = min (a * b) c := by
+  rcases le_total a c with h | h
+    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos b with rfl | hb
+    (fun x => min (x * b) c)^[e] (min a c) = min (a * b ^ e) c := by
+def capPow (b e c : ℕ) : ℕ := min (b ^ e) c
+/-- **Capped powers in unary.** `min (b ^ e) c` is polynomial-time on unary numbers: multiplying
+`e` times and capping at `c` never holds a number larger than the input. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => capPow p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+  have h := iterateWith (encIn := encPair encUnary (encPair encUnary encUnary))
+    (par := fun p => (p.1, p.2.2)) (count := fun p => p.2.1) (init := fun p => min 1 p.2.2)
+    (step := fun q x => min (x * q.1) q.2) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
+    (bound := fun p => (encPair encUnary (encPair encUnary encUnary) p).length) .self
+  simpa only [iterate_min_mul, one_mul, capPow] using h
+    {base exp cap : α → ℕ} (hbase : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime base input encUnary)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => capPow (base x) (exp x) (cap x)) input encUnary :=
+/-! ### The universal function with a unary clock -/
+theorem runBound_mono {D N t t' : ℕ} (h : t ≤ t') : runBound D N t ≤ runBound D N t' := by
+/-- The time and space of the universal function, polynomially in the length of its input with
+    runBound (descLen i.1) (encList encUnary i.2.1).length i.2.2 + (eIn i).length ≤
+  set n := (encPair eDesc (encPair (encList encUnary) encUnary) (d, x, t)).length with hn
+  have hlen : n = 2 * descLen d + 1 + (2 * (encList encUnary x).length + 1 + t) := by
+  have hIn : (eIn (d, x, t)).length ≤ 5 * n + 2 := by
+  have hstep := stepBound_mono (D := descLen d) (N := (encList encUnary x).length) le_rfl le_rfl
+  have hrun := runBound_mono (D := descLen d) (N := (encList encUnary x).length)
+  have ht : t + 1 ≤ n + 1 := by omega
+  simp only at h₁ h₂ hstep hrun ⊢
+  · have hA : (t + 1) * (stepBound (descLen d) (encList encUnary x).length t +
+        runBound (descLen d) (encList encUnary x).length t + ((encNat t).length + 1) ^ 2) ≤
+  · have hA : runBound (descLen d) (encList encUnary x).length t ≤ 200 * (n + 1) ^ 3 :=
+/-- **The universal function with a unary clock is polynomial-time**: written in unary, the number
+of steps counts towards the length of the input. -/
+  have hconv : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun i : Desc × List ℕ × ℕ => i)
+    have : (fun i : Desc × List ℕ × ℕ => i) = fun i => (i.1, i.2.1, i.2.2) := rfl
+/-- The word with a given index is polynomial-time in the index in unary. -/
+theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_word : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime word encUnary encBits := by
+  have h : word = fun j => (encNat (j + 1)).take ((encNat (j + 1)).length - 1) := by
+/-- The formula `φ` such that `y` is `encCNF φ` padded with `(encCNF φ).length ^ h` ones, if there
+def padCheckAt (y : List Bool) (h : ℕ) : Option (CNF ℕ) :=
+  if (unpad y).2 < y.length ∧ encCNF (decodeCNF (unpad y).1) = (unpad y).1 ∧
+      capPow (unpad y).1.length h ((unpad y).2 + 1) = (unpad y).2 then
+theorem padCheckAt_eq_some_iff {y : List Bool} {h : ℕ} {φ : CNF ℕ} :
+    padCheckAt y h = some φ ↔ y = pad (encCNF φ) ((encCNF φ).length ^ h) := by
+    have hk : (unpad y).1.length ^ h = (unpad y).2 := by
+      rcases le_total ((unpad y).1.length ^ h) ((unpad y).2 + 1) with h₁ | h₁
+/-- The formula padded in `y` along the exponent function `e`, if any. -/
+def padCheck (e : ℕ → ℕ) (y : List Bool) : Option (CNF ℕ) :=
+theorem padCheck_eq_some_iff {e : ℕ → ℕ} {y : List Bool} {φ : CNF ℕ} :
+    padCheck e y = some φ ↔ y = pad (encCNF φ) ((encCNF φ).length ^ e (encCNF φ).length) := by
+    have hu : (unpad y).1 = encCNF φ := by rw [h, unpad_pad]
+    y ∈ padSAT e ↔ ∃ φ, padCheck e y = some φ ∧ φ ∈ SAT := by
+  exact ⟨fun ⟨φ, hφ, h⟩ => ⟨φ, h, hφ⟩, fun ⟨φ, h, hφ⟩ => ⟨φ, hφ, h⟩⟩
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun y : List Bool => y.reverse.idxOf false) encBits encUnary :=
+  idxOfWithInput (encA := encBool) (list := fun y : List Bool => y.reverse)
+/-- Splitting a padded word is polynomial-time. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime unpad encBits (encPair encBits encUnary) := by
+/-- Reading the formula padded with a given exponent is polynomial-time. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × ℕ => padCheckAt p.1 p.2)
+  have henc : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun φ => encCNF φ) encCNF encBits := encode encCNF
+/-- Reading the formula padded along a computed exponent function is polynomial-time. The
+    {e : α → ℕ → ℕ} {y : α → List Bool}
+    (he : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : α × ℕ => e p.1 p.2) (encPair input encUnary)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => padCheck (e x) (y x)) input (encOption encCNF) := by
+/-- Whether one of the words with indices below `n` is a satisfying certificate for `φ`. -/
+def bruteSAT (n : ℕ) (φ : CNF ℕ) : Bool := (List.range n).any fun j => SAT.verifier (φ, word j)
+/-- **Short formulas are decided by trying the words with small indices**: every certificate of
+the length of the encoded formula has a smaller index than `n`. -/
+theorem bruteSAT_iff {n : ℕ} {φ : CNF ℕ} (h : 2 ^ ((encCNF φ).length + 1) ≤ n + 1) :
+    bruteSAT n φ = true ↔ φ ∈ SAT := by
+    exact List.any_eq_true.mpr ⟨index w, List.mem_range.mpr (by omega), by rwa [word_index]⟩
+    {n : α → ℕ} {φ : α → CNF ℕ} (hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime n input encUnary)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => bruteSAT (n x) (φ x)) input encBool := by
+/-! ### The step of the exponent function -/
+/-- Membership in the padded language along the table `T`, decided by `bruteSAT` with the
+words with indices below the length of `T`. -/
+def memB (T : List ℕ) (y : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  (padCheck (fun m => T.getD m 0) y).elim false (bruteSAT T.length)
+theorem memB_word_iff {T : List ℕ} {j : ℕ} (hj : j < T.length) :
+    memB T (word j) = true ↔ word j ∈ padSAT (fun m => T.getD m 0) := by
+  cases hc : padCheck (fun m => T.getD m 0) (word j) with
+/-- The test of `Cslib.Complexity.Ladner.Agrees` along the table `T`, as a Boolean. -/
+def agreesB (T : List ℕ) (i j : ℕ) : Bool :=
+  decide (runIndexed i (word j) (capPow (2 * (word j).length + 2) i T.length) =
+theorem agreesB_iff {T : List ℕ} {i j : ℕ} (hj : j < T.length) :
+    agreesB T i j = true ↔ Agrees (fun m => T.getD m 0) T.length i j := by
+    have : memB T (word j) = b := by
+      cases b <;> cases hm : memB T (word j) <;> simp_all
+/-- The step of the exponent function as a search over machine indices and words. -/
+    (List.range T.length).all fun j => agreesB T i j).getD (Nat.log 2 (Nat.log 2 T.length))
+/-- The least index below `m` passing a test, or `m`, as a search over `List.range m`. -/
+    ((List.range m).find? p).getD m = sInf {i | i = m ∨ p i = true} := by
+  set v := ((List.range m).find? p).getD m with hv
+  have hmem : v ∈ {i | i = m ∨ p i = true} ∧ ∀ i < v, i ∉ {i | i = m ∨ p i = true} := by
+      refine ⟨Or.inl rfl, fun i hi hmem => ?_⟩
+      obtain ⟨hp, k, hk, hki, hmin⟩ := List.find?_eq_some_iff_getElem.mp hf
+      refine ⟨Or.inr hp, fun i hi hmem => ?_⟩
+  exact le_antisymm (not_lt.mp fun h => hmem.2 _ h (Nat.sInf_mem ⟨v, hmem.1⟩)) (Nat.sInf_le hmem.1)
+theorem hstepB_eq (T : List ℕ) : hstepB T = Hstep T := by
+  exact or_congr_right (forall₂_congr fun j hj => agreesB_iff hj)
+/-- The description of the machine with a given index is polynomial-time in the index. -/
+/-- The input of a machine as symbols is linear. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun w : List Bool => w.map eBit) encBits (encList encUnary) :=
+/-- The coding of bits as symbols is a finite computation. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun b => eBit b) encBool encUnary :=
+/-- The run of an indexed machine, with the number of steps in unary, is polynomial-time. -/
+    {i : α → ℕ} {w : α → List Bool} {t : α → ℕ}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => runIndexed (i x) (w x) (t x)) input eOut := by
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List ℕ × List Bool => memB p.1 p.2)
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : (List ℕ × ℕ) × ℕ => agreesB p.1.1 p.1.2 p.2)
+/-- The step of the exponent function is polynomial-time in its table. -/
+      (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => (List.range p.1.length).all fun j => agreesB p.1 p.2 j)

+# Polynomial time relative to an oracle language
+An oracle language `A : Set (List Bool)` answers a word request `w` with the one-bit word
+`[decide (w ∈ A)]` (`Cslib.Complexity.languageOracle`). A deterministic oracle algorithm is a
+program `WordQueryComp Unit β`: a `PFunctor.FreeM` program whose calls are word requests and
+whose later requests may depend on earlier replies. Run against `A`, it returns
+`f` is computable in polynomial time relative to `A`
+against `A` and the program is strict oracle PPT (`Cslib.Probability.IsOraclePPTOn`) with one
+channel: one finite-control machine, under one polynomial clock in the encoded input length,
+reproduces the program's complete interaction with every stateful oracle. This is the oracle
+Turing machine of [Arora and Barak, Section 3.4][AroraBarak09] on the common machine
+(`Turing.MultiTapeMachine` with oracle channels): each request symbol is written onto the query
+buffer at the cost of one instruction, submitting a request costs one instruction, and the reply
+bit is the first cell of the answer tape, read by the answer head with no further instruction.
+The oracle's own computation is not charged. The certificate quantifies over every handler, not
+only language oracles, so the program, not the oracle, determines which requests are made; the
+machine's clock also bounds their number and length (`IsOraclePPTOn.query_bounds`).
+The classes relativize `P` and `NP` by this one substitution: `PWithOracle A enc` and
+uses verifiers with an oracle and certificates of exactly polynomial length.
+For a deterministic program and an answer function, `OracleComp.queriesWith` lists the requests
+made. Only their answers matter (`OracleComp.interpret_id_congr`), which is the locality on which
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.queriesWith`: the requests a deterministic program makes under given answers.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.languageOracle`: the replies of an oracle language.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle`: polynomial time relative to an oracle.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.interpret_id_congr`: answers to requests that are not made do not matter.
+  is polynomial time relative to every oracle.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The requests made by `program`, in order, when every call `q` is answered by `answer q`. -/
+def queriesWith (answer : (q : ι) → spec q) : OracleComp spec α → List ι
+  | .liftBind q next => q :: queriesWith answer (next (answer q))

+    queriesWith answer (pure a : OracleComp spec α) = [] := rfl

+@[simp] theorem queriesWith_query_bind (answer : (q : ι) → spec q) (q : ι)
+    queriesWith answer (query q >>= next) = q :: queriesWith answer (next (answer q)) := rfl
+/-- Answering the first call and continuing. -/
+@[simp] theorem interpret_id_query_bind (answer : (q : ι) → spec q) (q : ι)
+    interpret (m := Id) answer (query q >>= next) = interpret (m := Id) answer (next (answer q)) :=
+/-- A sequence makes the requests of its first part, then those of the continuation selected by
+theorem queriesWith_bind (answer : (q : ι) → spec q) (program : OracleComp spec α)
+    queriesWith answer (program >>= next) = queriesWith answer program ++
+      queriesWith answer (next (interpret (m := Id) answer program)) := by
+/-- Postprocessing the result makes no request. -/
+@[simp] theorem queriesWith_map (answer : (q : ι) → spec q) (f : α → β)
+    queriesWith answer (f <$> program) = queriesWith answer program := by
+/-- **Locality.** Answer functions that agree on the requests made under one of them give the
+theorem interpret_id_congr (answer answer' : (q : ι) → spec q) (program : OracleComp spec α)
+    (h : ∀ q ∈ queriesWith answer program, answer' q = answer q) :
+    interpret (m := Id) answer' program = interpret (m := Id) answer program ∧
+      queriesWith answer' program = queriesWith answer program := by
+    have hq : answer' q = answer q := h q (List.mem_cons_self ..)
+    have hrest := ih (answer q) fun q' hq' => h q' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hq')

+    (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f input output) (A : Set (List Bool)) :

+/-- The problems with verifiers computable in polynomial time relative to the oracle language `A`

+# An oracle relative to which `P` and `NP` differ
+For an oracle language `B`, the unary language `Cslib.Complexity.unaryLanguage B` consists of the
+words `1ⁿ` such that `B` has a word of length `n`. Baker, Gill and Solovay construct an oracle `B`
+for which this language is not in `P` relative to `B`, while it is in `NP` relative to every
+oracle (a certificate is a word of length `n` in `B`) [BakerGillSolovay1975]; we follow the proof
+The oracle diagonalizes against all candidate deciders at once
+(`Cslib.Complexity.exists_oracle_diagonal`). The candidates are the fair-coin tables with one
+oracle channel and control states `Fin m`, under the clocks `c * (n + 1) ^ d`, run on `1ⁿ` with
+every coin fixed to `false`. They are countably many, and each makes at most one request per
+instruction, hence fewer than `2 ^ n` requests for all large `n`. Every decider in `P` relative to
+`B` is one of them on the instances `1ⁿ`
+(`Cslib.Probability.IsOraclePPTOn.exists_fin_run_pure_false`), so none decides the unary language
+The verifier checks that the instance consists of `true` symbols, by a two-state transducer, and
+Relative to the diagonal oracle, `P` is therefore strictly contained in `NP`
+* `Cslib.Complexity.unaryLanguage`: the words `1ⁿ` such that the oracle has a word of length `n`.
+  language of `B` is not in `P` relative to `B`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.unaryLanguage_mem_NPWithOracle`: the unary language of every oracle is in `NP`
+* [T. Baker, J. Gill, R. Solovay, *Relativizations of the P =? NP Question*][BakerGillSolovay1975]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The words `1ⁿ` such that `B` has a word of length `n`. -/
+  {x | (∀ b ∈ x, b = true) ∧ ∃ w ∈ B, w.length = x.length}
+    List.replicate n true ∈ unaryLanguage B ↔ ∃ w ∈ B, w.length = n := by
+  exact and_iff_right fun b hb => (List.eq_of_mem_replicate hb)
+/-- A candidate decider: a fair-coin table with `k` work tapes, control `Fin m` and one oracle
+channel, together with the constants `c` and `d` of its clock `c * (n + 1) ^ d`. -/
+abbrev Candidate : Type := Σ k m : ℕ, MultiTapePTM k Bool (Fin m) Unit × ℕ × ℕ
+/-- The clock `c * (n + 1) ^ d` of a candidate on inputs of length `n`. -/
+/-- The verdict of a candidate on `1ⁿ`: its clocked run with every coin fixed to `false`, accepting
+def Candidate.verdict (candidate : Candidate) (n : ℕ) : WordQueryComp Unit Bool :=
+    (fun op word => OracleComp.query (op, word)) (candidate.clock n) (List.replicate n true)
+/-- A candidate makes at most one request per instruction. -/
+/-- Every clock is eventually below `2 ^ n`. -/
+    ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, candidate.clock n < 2 ^ n :=
+/-- **Baker–Gill–Solovay, the lower bound** [Arora and Barak, Theorem 3.7][AroraBarak09]: for some
+oracle language `B`, the unary language of `B` is not decidable in polynomial time relative to
+    ∃ B : Set (List Bool), unaryLanguage B ∉ PWithOracle B encBits := by
+  obtain ⟨k, m, machine, c, d, hrun⟩ := hcertificate.exists_fin_run_pure_false
+  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := hB ⟨k, m, machine, c, d⟩
+  have hlength : (encBits (List.replicate n true)).length = n := by
+  have hverdict := hrun (List.replicate n true) (languageOracle B)
+      (Candidate.verdict ⟨k, m, machine, c, d⟩ n) = f (List.replicate n true) := by
+/-- Tracks whether every symbol read so far is `true`, and emits the verdict at the end. -/
+theorem allTrue_run (q : Bool) (x : List Bool) : allTrue.run q x = [q && x.all id] := by
+/-- Whether the first word consists of `true` symbols only, beside a Boolean, in polynomial
+      (fun pair : (List Bool × List Bool) × Bool => pair.1.1.all id && pair.2)
+  have hall : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => x.all id) encBits encBool :=
+  have hand : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun q : Bool × Bool => q.1 && q.2)
+      fun q : Bool × Bool => q.1 && q.2).computableTidilyInPolyTime
+/-- **The unary language is in `NP` relative to its oracle**: a certificate for `1ⁿ` is a word of
+length `n` in the oracle, checked with one request. -/

+      (g := fun (xu : List Bool × List Bool) b => xu.1.all id && b)
+relative to some oracle language, `P` is strictly contained in `NP`. -/

+/-- **Baker–Gill–Solovay**: relative to some oracle language, `P ≠ NP`. -/

+# Closure properties of the oracle classes
+Polynomial time relative to an oracle composes with polynomial-time pre- and postprocessing
+`Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle.map`), through the compositional rules of strict
+oracle PPT. One request decides the oracle language itself
+(`Cslib.Complexity.computableInPolyTimeWithOracle_mem`): the request is copied onto the query
+buffer, and only the first bit of the reply is read.
+Hence `P` relative to `A` contains `A` and lies inside `NP` relative to `A`, and both classes are
+closed under polynomial-time many-one reductions of the problem
+`Cslib.Complexity.PolyTimeReducible.mem_NPWithOracle`). For `NP` the certificates are padded to a
+polynomial of the instance length, and the verifier reads only the prefix of the length the
+  one request decides the oracle language.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+variable {α β γ : Type} {A : Set (List Bool)} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {middle : β ↪ List Bool}
+theorem preprocess {f : β → γ} {g : α → β} (hf : ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle A f middle output)
+    ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle A (fun a => f (g a)) input output :=
+  ⟨fun a => program (g a), hprogram.preprocess hg, fun a => heq (g a)⟩
+/-- Polynomial-time postprocessing of the result, which may also use the argument. -/
+theorem map_with {f : α → β} {g : α → β → γ}
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair => g pair.1 pair.2) (encPair input middle) output) :
+    ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle A (fun a => g a (f a)) input output := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => g a <$> program a, ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+theorem map {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} (hf : ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle A f input middle)
+    ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle A (fun a => g (f a)) input output := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => g <$> program a, ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+/-- **One request decides the oracle language.** The word is copied onto the query buffer and
+the first bit of the reply is read. -/
+    ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle A (fun w => decide (w ∈ A)) encBits encBool := by
+  · change decide (List.take 1 (languageOracle A ((), w)) = [true]) = decide (w ∈ A)
+theorem mem_PWithOracle_self (A : Set (List Bool)) : A ∈ PWithOracle A encBits := by
+  exact ⟨_, computableInPolyTimeWithOracle_mem A, fun w => decide_eq_true_iff.symm⟩
+/-- **`P` relative to `A` lies inside `NP` relative to `A`**: a decider ignores the empty
+theorem PWithOracle_subset_NPWithOracle (A : Set (List Bool)) (enc : α ↪ List Bool) :
+    PWithOracle A enc ⊆ NPWithOracle A enc := fun _ ⟨f, hf, h⟩ =>
+  ⟨0, fun aw => f aw.1, hf.preprocess (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst enc encBits), fun a => by
+/-- **`P` relative to an oracle is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PWithOracle {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {L : Set α} {L' : Set β} (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB L L')
+    (hL' : L' ∈ PWithOracle A encB) : L ∈ PWithOracle A encA :=
+  ⟨fun a => f (g a), hf.preprocess hg, fun a => (hL a).trans (hL' (g a))⟩
+/-- Polynomials with natural coefficients are monotone on the naturals. -/
+private theorem eval_le_eval {p : Polynomial ℕ} {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : p.eval m ≤ p.eval n := by
+  | add p q hp hq => simpa only [Polynomial.eval_add] using Nat.add_le_add hp hq

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+machine for `2 ^ L` steps on a formula whose encoding has length `L`. This file bounds its time
+and space in the quantitative calculus of tidy computability
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInO`), charging every stored frame, the input, the counter of
+The states of the machine are encoded by framed tuples (`Cslib.Complexity.TQBF.encState`). A step
+it branches on whether a value is being returned, on the kind of the next token or of the top
+frame, and looks variables up in the stack. Along a run on a formula with encoding of length `L`,
+the stack holds at most `L` frames, each storing a token and a suffix of the tokens of the formula,
+so every state has an encoding of length `O((L + 1) ^ 2)`
+(`Cslib.Complexity.TQBF.length_encState_le`). The rounds are counted by a binary counter of
+`L + 1` digits, from `2 ^ L` written in linear time
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInDegree.two_pow_length`), so the evaluator runs in space
+polynomial in `L` and in time `2 ^ L` times a polynomial in `L`
+* `Cslib.Complexity.TQBF.length_encState_le`: the states of a run are of quadratic size.

+# The problem of true quantified Boolean formulas
+`TQBF` is the set of true closed quantified Boolean formulas over variables numbered by `ℕ`:
+formulas without free variables whose value is `true` [Sipser, Section 8.3][Sipser2013]
+[Arora and Barak, Section 4.2][AroraBarak09]. A closed formula has the same value under every
+assignment (`Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.eval_eq_of_closed`), so the assignment `fun _ => false` in the
+definition is immaterial. Instances are formulas, not words, and every formula is an instance:
+formulas with a free variable are simply not in `TQBF`. Formulas are not required to be in prenex
+form; the prenex formulas of the textbooks are among them.
+A formula is encoded by its tokens in prefix (Polish) order (`Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.tokens`): the
+kind of each node, with its variable for variables and quantifiers and `0` otherwise, as a framed
+list of framed pairs of the kind in unary and the variable in binary (`Cslib.Complexity.encQBF`).
+The prefix order makes the encoding injective without delimiters
+(`Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.tokens_append_inj`), and every node takes at least three bits, so a formula
+with `n` nodes has an encoding of length at least `3 * n`.
+Boundary cases: the empty list is the tokens of no formula; the formulas without variables are
+built from `top` and `bot`, and `top ∈ TQBF` while `bot ∉ TQBF`; a variable on its own is never
+closed, so `var v ∉ TQBF`, while `ex v (var v) ∈ TQBF` and `all v (var v) ∉ TQBF`.
+* `Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.tokens_append_inj`: tokens in prefix order determine the formula.
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*][Sipser2013]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The kinds of nodes of a quantified Boolean formula. -/
+  ⟨{.var, .top, .bot, .not, .and, .or, .ex, .all}, fun k => by cases k <;> simp⟩
+/-- The tokens of a formula in prefix order: the kind of each node, with its variable for
+variables and quantifiers, and `0` for the other nodes. -/
+/-- **Tokens in prefix order determine the formula**, and what follows them. -/
+theorem tokens_append_inj {φ ψ : QBF ℕ} {r r' : List (Kind × ℕ)}
+    (h : φ.tokens ++ r = ψ.tokens ++ r') : φ = ψ ∧ r = r' := by
+  induction φ generalizing ψ r r' with
+    cases ψ <;> simp only [tokens, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq,
+    cases ψ <;> simp only [tokens, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq,
+    cases ψ <;> simp only [tokens, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq,
+    cases ψ <;> simp only [tokens, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq,
+    cases ψ <;> simp only [tokens, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq,
+theorem tokens_injective : Function.Injective tokens := fun φ ψ h =>
+/-- The index of a kind, from `0` for variables to `7` for universal quantifiers. -/
+/-- Kinds encoded by their index in unary. -/
+/-- Tokens encoded as framed pairs of the kind in unary and the variable in binary. -/
+abbrev encToken : QBF.Kind × ℕ ↪ List Bool := encPair encKind encNat
+/-- Formulas encoded by their tokens in prefix order (`Cslib.Logic.PL.QBF.tokens`), as a list of
+theorem encQBF_apply (φ : QBF ℕ) : encQBF φ = encList TQBF.encToken φ.tokens := rfl
+/-- Every node takes at least three bits. -/
+theorem three_mul_length_tokens_le (φ : QBF ℕ) : 3 * φ.tokens.length ≤ (encQBF φ).length := by
+    simp only [encList_cons, List.length_append, length_frame, List.length_cons, length_encPair]
+/-- **The true closed quantified Boolean formulas** over variables numbered by natural numbers. -/
+def TQBF : Set (QBF ℕ) := {φ | φ.Closed ∧ φ.eval (fun _ => false) = true}
+theorem mem_TQBF {φ : QBF ℕ} : φ ∈ TQBF ↔ φ.Closed ∧ φ.eval (fun _ => false) = true := Iff.rfl
+/-- A closed formula is in `TQBF` exactly when it is true under some, equivalently every,
+theorem mem_TQBF_iff_of_closed {φ : QBF ℕ} (hφ : φ.Closed) (σ : ℕ → Bool) :
+    φ ∈ TQBF ↔ φ.eval σ = true := by
+/-- The constant true is a true closed formula. -/
+/-- The constant false is not true. -/
+theorem bot_notMem_TQBF : QBF.bot ∉ TQBF := fun h => absurd h.2 (by simp)
+/-- A variable on its own is not closed. -/
+theorem var_notMem_TQBF (v : ℕ) : QBF.var v ∉ TQBF := fun h =>

+The fixed-power bound applies to a map `f` on any finite invariant set `S` of a type in any
+universe, given an injective bit encoding `e` of `S` and a Boolean circuit realizing `f` on the
+encodings (`fixed_power_encoded`). All computation is charged on the encoding; no gate evaluates
+After a burn-in of `d` steps, computed by a separate circuit, every orbit lies in the image of
+`f^[d]`, so the storage term of the remaining steps counts only that image
+/-- A circuit realizing `f` on the encodings of an invariant set realizes its powers. -/
+theorem iterate_encoded (f : α → α) (S : Finset α) (e : α → BitString n)
+    (c : Circuit signature n n) (hS : ∀ x ∈ S, f x ∈ S)
+    (hstep : ∀ x ∈ S, c.eval interpretation (e x) = e (f x)) {x : α} (hx : x ∈ S) (T : ℕ) :
+    exact hstep _ (Set.MapsTo.iterate (f := f) (s := ↑S) hS T hx)
+/-- **Encoded fixed powers.** If an injective encoding `e` of a finite invariant set `S` of an
+arbitrary type is realized by a circuit `c`, then for every exponent `T` and `0 < L ≤ 2 ^ n` some
+circuit of size at most `40000 * powerBudget n c.size S.card L` realizes `f^[T]` on `S`. -/
+theorem fixed_power_encoded (f : α → α) (S : Finset α) (e : α → BitString n)
+    (he : Set.InjOn e S) (c : Circuit signature n n) (hS : ∀ x ∈ S, f x ∈ S)
+    (hstep : ∀ x ∈ S, c.eval interpretation (e x) = e (f x))
+      (∀ x ∈ S, out.eval interpretation (e x) = e (f^[T] x)) ∧
+      out.size ≤ 40000 * powerBudget n c.size S.card L := by
+  have himage : ∀ y ∈ S.image e, c.eval interpretation y ∈ S.image e := by
+    exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨f x, hS x hx, rfl⟩
+  obtain ⟨out, hout, hsize⟩ := fixed_power_on n c (S.image e) T L himage hL hLN
+  refine ⟨out, fun x hx => ?_, by simpa only [Finset.card_image_of_injOn he] using hsize⟩
+  exact iterate_encoded f S e c hS hstep hx T
+/-- **Fixed powers after a burn-in.** Given a circuit for `d ≤ T` steps, the remaining `T - d`
+steps cost the fixed-power bound with storage term the size of the image of `f^[d]`. -/
+theorem fixed_power_image (c burn : Circuit signature n n) (d T L : ℕ)
+  have hS : ∀ y ∈ S, f y ∈ S := by
+  obtain ⟨tail, htail, hsize⟩ := fixed_power_on n c S (T - d) L hS hL hLN

+# Moving a residue into a repeated interval
+If an orbit repeats with `f^[i] x = f^[j] x` for `i < j`, the state at any time `T ≥ i` is the
+state at the unique time in `[i, j)` congruent to `T` modulo `j - i`. A circuit finds that time
+without division: it looks up `T % (j - i)` in a table indexed by the period, which depends on the
+fixed exponent `T` only through its residues, and then adds the period while the value is below
+`i`. At most `K` additions suffice when `i ≤ K` (`liftResidue_reconstructs`).
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.liftResidue`: one bounded correction of a residue.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.repeatWordIndex`: the word computation of the time in the
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.Iteration.repeatWordIndex_spec`: the same for the word computation.

+/-- One bounded correction of a residue: add the period once if below the interval. -/
+def liftResidue (lower period r : ℕ) : ℕ := if r < lower then r + period else r
+/-- Repeated correction preserves the residue and never passes the interval. -/
+theorem liftResidue_invariant (lower period r t : ℕ) (hp : 0 < period) (hr : r < period) :
+    (lower ≤ v ∨ t ≤ v) ∧ v < lower + period ∧ v % period = r := by
+  | zero => exact ⟨Or.inr (Nat.zero_le _), by simp; omega, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hr⟩
+    · refine ⟨?_, by omega, by simpa using ih.2.2⟩
+/-- Enough corrections place the residue in the interval. -/
+theorem liftResidue_spec (lower period T K : ℕ) (hp : 0 < period) (hK : lower ≤ K) :
+    lower ≤ v ∧ v < lower + period ∧ v % period = T % period := by
+  have h := liftResidue_invariant lower period (T % period) K hp (Nat.mod_lt _ hp)
+/-- The corrected residue lies in the repeated interval and gives the state at time `T`. -/
+theorem liftResidue_reconstructs {α : Type*} {f : α → α} {x : α} {i j T K : ℕ}
+    (hij : i < j) (heq : f^[i] x = f^[j] x) (hK : i ≤ K) (hT : i ≤ T) :
+    i ≤ r ∧ r < j ∧ f^[r] x = f^[T] x := by
+  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi, hmod⟩ := liftResidue_spec i (j - i) T K (by omega) hK
+  exact ⟨hlo, by omega, FunctionalGraph.iterate_eq_iterate_of_mod_eq hij.le heq hlo hT hmod⟩
+def liftWord {w : ℕ} (lower period r : BitVec w) : BitVec w :=
+  if r.ult lower then r + period else r
+/-- The word correction agrees with the natural-number one when the interval fits. -/
+theorem liftWord_toNat {w : ℕ} (lower period r : BitVec w)
+    (liftWord lower period r).toNat = liftResidue lower.toNat period.toNat r.toNat := by
+theorem liftWord_iterate_toNat {w : ℕ} (lower period r : BitVec w)
+  | succ K ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', liftWord_toNat _ _ _ hfit, ih,
+/-- The residues of `T` modulo every period up to `K`, selected by the period. -/
+def residueWord {w : ℕ} (T K : ℕ) (period : BitVec w) : BitVec w :=
+    fun i : Fin w => (BitVec.ofNat w (T % j.val)).getLsbD i.val)
+theorem residueWord_toNat {w T K : ℕ} (period : BitVec w)
+    (residueWord T K period).toNat = T % period.toNat := by
+/-- The time in the repeated interval `[lo, hi)` that is congruent to `T`. -/
+def repeatWordIndex {w : ℕ} (T K : ℕ) (lo hi : BitVec w) : BitVec w :=
+/-- The word computation lies in the repeated interval and selects the state at time `T`. -/
+theorem repeatWordIndex_spec {α : Type*} {f : α → α} {x : α} {w T K : ℕ}
+    (lo hi : BitVec w) (hlt : lo.toNat < hi.toNat) (hhi : hi.toNat ≤ K)
+    (hK : K < 2 ^ w) (hT : K ≤ T) (heq : f^[lo.toNat] x = f^[hi.toNat] x) :
+    let r := (repeatWordIndex T K lo hi).toNat
+    lo.toNat ≤ r ∧ r < hi.toNat ∧ f^[r] x = f^[T] x := by
+  have hp : (hi - lo).toNat = hi.toNat - lo.toNat := BitVec.toNat_sub_of_le hlt.le
+  have hfit : lo.toNat + (hi - lo).toNat ≤ 2 ^ w := by rw [hp]; have := hi.isLt; omega
+    residueWord_toNat _ hK (by rw [hp]; omega) (by rw [hp]; omega), hp]
+  exact liftResidue_reconstructs hlt heq (by omega) (by omega)
+/-- One word correction: an addition, a comparison and a multiplexer. -/

+        (fun i => Or.inl (hl i)) (fun i => Or.inl (hp i))
+/-- A residue table costs only its word width and entry count, whatever `T` is. -/
+    (T K : ℕ) (period : BitString n → BitVec w)
+    (hp : ∀ i : Fin w, (fun x => (period x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ s)
+    (hconst : ∀ b : Bool, (fun _ : BitString n => b) ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis interpretation s (wordWires fun x => residueWord T K (period x))

+      (BitVec.ofNat w (T % j.val)).getLsbD i.val) hp fun _ _ => hconst _
+  simpa only [wordWires, residueWord, getLsbD_word] using h
+/-- The repeated-interval index circuit has no dependence on the bit length of `T`. -/
+    (T K : ℕ) (lo hi : BitString n → BitVec w)
+    (hlo : ∀ i : Fin w, (fun x => (lo x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ s)
+    (hhi : ∀ i : Fin w, (fun x => (hi x).getLsbD i.val) ∈ s)
+    (hconst : ∀ b : Bool, (fun _ : BitString n => b) ∈ s) :
+    Synthesis interpretation s (wordWires fun x => repeatWordIndex T K (lo x) (hi x))
+  let p := fun x => hi x - lo x
+  let r := fun x => residueWord T K (p x)
+  have hp := Synthesis.word_sub (s := s) hi lo hhi hlo

+  have hout := synthesis_liftWord_iterate (s ∪ (wordWires p ∪ wordWires r)) lo p r

+Every problem in `BPP` lies in the second level `Σ₂ ∩ Π₂` of the polynomial hierarchy, and hence
+in `PH`. This is the Sipser–Gács–Lautemann theorem: [Sipser][Sipser1983] placed `BPP` in `PH`,
+Gács improved the placement to `Σ₂ ∩ Π₂`, and [Lautemann][Lautemann1983] gave the proof
+formalised here; see also [Arora and Barak, Theorem 7.15][AroraBarak09].

+/-- Length of an amplified universal seed: `runs m * m` bits. -/
+def seedLen (m : ℕ) : ℕ := runs m * m
+/-- Length of the existential witness concatenating `shifts m` shift vectors:

+/-! ### Combinatorial shift-cover and soundness on amplified seeds -/
+/-- An amplified seed for single-trial seed length `m`: `runs m` blocks of `m` bits each. Seeds
+form an additive group under pointwise bit-string addition (xor). -/
+abbrev Seed (m : ℕ) : Type := Fin (runs m) → BitString m
+/-- The amplified test accepts `ω : Seed m` when a strict majority (`> halfRuns m`) of the
+`runs m = 2 * halfRuns m` blocks satisfy the single-trial predicate `P`. -/
+def majorityAccepts {m : ℕ} (P : (Fin m → Bool) → Bool) (ω : Seed m) : Prop :=
+  halfRuns m < (univ.filter fun j : Fin (runs m) => P (ω j) = true).card
+instance {m : ℕ} (P : (Fin m → Bool) → Bool) : DecidablePred (majorityAccepts P) :=
+private theorem card_seed_eq (m : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Seed m) = (2 ^ m) ^ runs m := by
+/-- If at least two thirds of the single-trial seeds lie in `G`, then at most an
+`(8 / 9) ^ halfRuns m` fraction of the amplified seeds have at most `halfRuns m` blocks in `G`:
+private theorem nine_pow_mul_card_filter_le {m : ℕ} {G : Finset (Fin m → Bool)}
+        (univ.filter fun ω : Seed m => (univ.filter fun j => ω j ∈ G).card ≤ halfRuns m).card ≤
+  have hcard : Fintype.card (Seed m) = Fintype.card (Fin m → Bool) ^ (2 * halfRuns m) := by
+/-- **Completeness on amplified seeds.** If at least two thirds of the single-trial seeds satisfy
+`P s = true`, then there exist `shifts m` shift vectors covering every amplified seed `r : Seed m`

+    ∃ tests : Fin (shifts m) → Seed m, ∀ r : Seed m, ∃ i,

+  have hN : N * 8 ^ (halfRuns m * shifts m) < 9 ^ (halfRuns m * shifts m) := by

+        calc 9 ^ (halfRuns m * shifts m) * (N * #Sᶜ ^ shifts m)

+          _ = N * 8 ^ (halfRuns m * shifts m) * N ^ shifts m := by ring

+  exact ⟨tests, fun r => (htests r).imp fun i hi => (mem_filter.1 hi).2⟩
+/-- **Soundness on amplified seeds.** If at least two thirds of the single-trial seeds satisfy

+`Cslib.exists_forall_add_notMem_of_mul_card_lt` of Lautemann's covering lemma on `Seed m`. -/

+/-! ### The functional matrix verifier and its polynomial-time certificate -/

+`w = u ++ r`, where `u` lists `shifts m` shift vectors of `seedLen m` bits and `r` is the

+def trialSeed (m : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (i j : ℕ) : List Bool :=
+  List.zipWith Bool.xor (BitString.listRow m (shifts m * runs m + j) w)
+/-- Whether the `i`-th shift vector causes a strict majority (`> halfRuns m`) of the `runs m`
+def shiftAccepts (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool)
+  decide (halfRuns m < (List.range (runs m)).countP fun j => V (a, trialSeed m w i j))
+/-- The Sipser–Lautemann `Σ₂` matrix verifier: given `(a, w)` where `w = u ++ r` consists of an
+existential shift-table certificate `u` of length `witnessLen m` and a universal seed `r` of length
+`seedLen m` (for `m = p.eval (enc a).length`), test whether some shift `i < shifts m` makes a
+strict majority of the `runs m` shifted trials accept. The verifier is total: bits missing from a
+short `w` read as `false` and extra bits of `w` are ignored (`trialSeed`). -/
+def verifier (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool)
+  (List.range (shifts m)).any fun i => shiftAccepts enc p V x.1 x.2 i
+/-- If `V` is computable tidily in polynomial time, then so is the Sipser–Lautemann matrix verifier
+theorem verifier_polyTime {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}

+    simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, List.mem_toFinset, List.mem_filter,
+/-- On a combined certificate `u ++ r` with `u.length = witnessLen (p.eval (enc a).length)`,
+`shiftAccepts` agrees with `majorityAccepts` on the `i`-th shifted seed. -/
+theorem shiftAccepts_append_iff {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {p : Polynomial ℕ}
+    {V : α × List Bool → Bool} {a : α} {u r : List Bool}

+`ZeroOneIP` is the feasibility problem of zero-one integer programming in equality form: a system
+of linear equations `∑ j, a j * x j = t` with natural coefficients and right-hand sides, encoded in

+listing the coefficients of the variables `0, 1, …`; missing coefficients are zero.

+[Karp1972]; the equality form with natural coefficients is the special case used here, and it is
+already `NP`-complete. A subset sum instance is a single equation, so `SubsetSum` reduces to

+`Partition` is the set of lists of natural numbers, possibly with repetitions, that split into two
+sub-multisets with equal sums [Karp1972]. Numbers are encoded in binary (`encNat`).
+Appending the two numbers `a.sum + 1` and `2 * t + 1` to the numbers `a` reduces `SubsetSum` to
+`Partition`: together these two exceed half of the new total, so they lie on opposite sides of any
+partition, and the side holding `a.sum + 1` holds numbers of `a` summing to exactly `t`. Neither
+number needs subtraction, so the reduction is defined for every target, including targets larger
+  is a sub-multiset, or a subsequence, with half the total sum.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- The lists of natural numbers that split into two sub-multisets with equal sums. -/
+def Partition : Set (List ℕ) := {l | ∃ s t : Multiset ℕ, s + t = l ∧ s.sum = t.sum}
+/-- A partition is a sub-multiset holding half of the total sum. -/
+    l ∈ Partition ↔ ∃ s ≤ (l : Multiset ℕ), 2 * s.sum = l.sum := by
+    rw [← Multiset.sum_coe, ← hst, Multiset.sum_add, hsum, two_mul]
+/-- A partition is a subsequence holding half of the total sum. -/
+    l ∈ Partition ↔ ∃ s, s <+ l ∧ 2 * s.sum = l.sum := by
+/-- The verifier for `Partition`: the numbers selected by the certificate mask hold half of the
+def verifier (x : List ℕ × List Bool) : Bool := decide (2 * (maskSelect x.1 x.2).sum = x.1.sum)

+theorem isVerifier : IsVerifier (encList encNat) Polynomial.X verifier Partition := by
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime verifier (encPair (encList encNat) encBits) encBool := by
+/-- The reduction from `SubsetSum` to `Partition`: append `a.sum + 1` and `2 * t + 1`. -/
+def toPartition (x : List ℕ × ℕ) : List ℕ := x.1 ++ [x.1.sum + 1, 2 * x.2 + 1]

+    simp only [toPartition, List.sum_append, List.sum_cons, List.sum_nil] at hsum hl
+    rcases hmem with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
+    · -- The numbers of `l` beside `2 * t + 1` leave numbers of `l` summing to `t`.

+    PolyTimeReducible (encPair (encList encNat) encNat) (encList encNat) SubsetSum Partition :=

+`SubsetSum` is the set of pairs `(a, t)` of a list `a` of natural numbers, possibly with
+repetitions, and a target `t` such that some sub-multiset of `a` sums to `t` [Sipser, Section
+7.4][Sipser2013]. All numbers are encoded in binary (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.encNat`, digits least
+significant first); the `NP`-hardness proved here is for this encoding and is not strong
+`NP`-hardness. A certificate is a mask selecting entries of `a` (`Cslib.Complexity.maskSelect`),
+and the verifier adds the selected numbers in binary.
+Sipser's reduction from 3SAT [Sipser, Theorem 7.56][Sipser2013] gives each of the `n` variables
+of a formula, numbered by first occurrence (`ThreeSAT.distinctVars`), and each of its `m` clauses
+a digit position. Each variable has two literal numbers, with digit one at the position of the
+variable and at the positions of the clauses containing the literal (`ThreeSAT.literalDigits`);
+each clause has two slack numbers with digit one at its position only. The target has digit one
+at every variable position and three at every clause position. At each position, all numbers
+together have at most five digits one, so no subfamily produces carries in any base above five
+(`Cslib.Complexity.sum_sum_pow_eq_iff`). We use base 8 rather than Sipser's base 10, so that
+digits are blocks of three bits; every number has at most `n + m` base-8 digits
+their order of first occurrence, so large binary labels do not enlarge the numbers. A literal
+repeated in a clause counts once, and a clause containing both literals of a variable is covered
+by both of its literal numbers. Formulas with a clause of more than three literals are not in
+`ThreeSAT` and are mapped to an instance without solutions.

+  `Cslib.Complexity.ThreeSAT.counts_iff_satisfiable`: the digit construction has a solution
+  exactly when the digit positions can be filled, exactly when the formula is satisfiable.

+# Selecting list entries by a mask
+`Cslib.Complexity.maskSelect l w` keeps the entries of `l` at the positions where the bit string
+`w` is `true`. Masks describe exactly the sublists of `l`, and therefore, up to order, exactly the
+sub-multisets of `l`; this makes them polynomially long certificates for problems that ask for a
+sub-multiset of the input numbers, such as subset sum, partition and knapsack.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.exists_le_coe_iff_exists_sublist`: sub-multisets are sublists up to order.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.exists_le_iff_exists_maskSelect`: a property of sub-multisets holds for one of
+  them exactly when it holds for the selection of some mask of any length at least the length of
+/-- The entries of `l` at the positions where `w` is `true`; positions beyond the end of `w` are
+def maskSelect (l : List α) (w : List Bool) : List α :=
+  (l.zipIdx.filter fun p => w.getD p.2 false).map Prod.fst
+theorem maskSelect_nil (w : List Bool) : maskSelect ([] : List α) w = [] := rfl
+theorem maskSelect_cons (a : α) (l : List α) (w : List Bool) :
+    maskSelect (a :: l) w = (if w.headD false then [a] else []) ++ maskSelect l w.tail := by
+  have hshift : (fun p : α × ℕ => w.getD p.2 false) ∘ Prod.map id (· + 1) =
+      fun p => w.tail.getD p.2 false := by
+  simp only [maskSelect, List.zipIdx_cons', List.filter_cons, List.filter_map, hshift]
+  | cons b w => cases b <;> simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def]
+theorem maskSelect_sublist (l : List α) (w : List Bool) : maskSelect l w <+ l := by
+    (List.filter_sublist (p := fun p : α × ℕ => w.getD p.2 false) (l := l.zipIdx)).map Prod.fst
+/-- Every sublist is selected by a mask as long as the list. -/
+theorem exists_maskSelect_eq {s l : List α} (h : s <+ l) :
+    ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = l.length ∧ maskSelect l w = s := by
+    exact ⟨false :: w, by simp [hw], by simp [maskSelect_cons, hs]⟩
+    exact ⟨true :: w, by simp [hw], by simp [maskSelect_cons, hs]⟩
+/-- Unselected positions beyond the list do not change the selection. -/
+theorem maskSelect_append_replicate_false (l : List α) (w : List Bool) (k : ℕ) :
+    maskSelect l (w ++ List.replicate k false) = maskSelect l w := by
+    by_cases h : p.2 - w.length < k <;> simp [h]
+/-- The sub-multisets of a list are the sublists, up to order. -/
+theorem exists_le_coe_iff_exists_sublist {l : List α} (P : Multiset α → Prop) :
+    (∃ s ≤ (l : Multiset α), P s) ↔ ∃ s, s <+ l ∧ P s := by
+/-- A property of sub-multisets of `l` holds for one of them exactly when it holds for the
+selection of a mask of length `n`, for any `n` at least the length of `l`. -/
+theorem exists_le_iff_exists_maskSelect {l : List α} {n : ℕ} (hn : l.length ≤ n)
+      ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = n ∧ P (maskSelect l w : Multiset α) := by
+    exact ⟨w ++ List.replicate (n - l.length) false, by simp [hw, hn],
+/-- Selecting the entries of a list by a mask is polynomial-time. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List α × List Bool => maskSelect p.1 p.2)

+Polynomial-time certificates for arithmetic on the binary encoding `Turing.MultiTapeTM.encNat`
+(digits least significant first), the binary counterparts of the unary certificates in
+`PolyTime/Nat.lean`. Addition and multiplication are Christian Reitwiessner's degree-bounded

+exactly when some position holds a one in `n` and a zero in `m` and all higher positions agree

+of the number problems (`Cslib.Complexity.SubsetSum` and its relatives) are built from these.

+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` asks for a *tidy* machine, which clears its work
+tapes and rewinds its heads before halting, within polynomially bounded time and space. Neither
+requirement changes the class. A machine that halts within `t` steps visits at most `k t + k`
+work-tape cells, where `k` is its number of work tapes
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesInTimeAndSpace.space_linear`), and the tidy normal form makes any
+machine tidy at a linear cost in time and space
+is tidily computable in polynomial time exactly when some machine computes it in the sense of
+upstream `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInTimeAndSpace`, within polynomially bounded time and space
+a polynomial time bound alone already suffices
+Passing from tidy to plain computations is lossless: a tidy machine is a machine, with the same
+bounds. Passing from plain to tidy computations changes the bounds by linear functions whose
+Upstream `Turing.MultiTapeTM.DecidableInTimeAndSpace` decides a problem through its Boolean
+indicator. `Turing.MultiTapeTM.decidableInTimeAndSpace_iff` restates it for any Boolean function
+deciding membership, the form used by the classes in `Cslib.Complexity`.
+  bound for any machine, with any space bound, gives tidy polynomial time.
+  polynomial time gives a machine within polynomially bounded time and space.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]

+/-- A computation within `t` steps needs no separate space bound: it visits at most `k t + k`

+/-- A function computable within time `t` is computable within time `t` and space `c t + c`, for

+/-- The indicator of `A` is the Boolean function that is `true` exactly on `A`. -/
+    indicator A = g ↔ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ g a = true := by

+# Tidy combinators for probabilistic oracle machines
+This module lifts the deterministic tidy-machine combinators (`extendTapes`, `outputToWord`,

+tape words, emitted output and external oracle state, and maintains clean query buffers at phase
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.outputToWord`: redirect output to a new last work tape and rewind its head.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.inputFromWord`: read input from a work tape flagged by `markFlag`.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.onWords`: run a tidy probabilistic machine between two work tapes.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.tidyComp`: sequential composition of tidy probabilistic machines.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.appendPTM`: concatenate the outputs of two tidy probabilistic machines.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.branch`: branch on whether a work tape is blank without executing the
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.itePTM`: tidy case distinction on a work tape word.

+# Bounded adaptive loops of clean oracle phases
+A loop of clean phases is a clean phase when one invariant bounds the encoded size of every
+reachable state. Unlike closed loops, an adaptive loop with an external oracle cannot presample
+its randomness: every iteration may query the shared stateful oracle, and its replies may be
+arbitrarily long. The loop therefore runs the step machine itself, once per iteration, with a
+unary counter stored beside the state; the counter stops the loop after exactly the requested
+number of steps and the final round executes no step.
+The invariant quantifies over every result possible for some stateful handler, so it holds for
+every shared oracle. Storage growth is controlled by the client's size bound, not assumed.

+# Clean realizations of arbitrary oracle PPT certificates
+A strict `IsOraclePPTOn` witness may be cut off by its clock while still live, leave partial
+requests in its query buffers, read stale answer tapes and leave arbitrary storage behind. It is
+nevertheless equivalent to a clean phase. During `fuel` instructions from blank storage, a machine
+reads at most `fuel` symbols of any reply. The native run is therefore exactly the finite
+interpreter loop in which every external call returns its `fuel`-symbol prefix. Each interpreter
+step is certified by the clean calculus: a fair bit, a fixed table lookup, and at most one
+bounded-prefix query. The loop makes the same adaptive external calls in the same order, with
+identical requests, and preserves the complete joint law of the output and external oracle state.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsTidyOraclePPTOn.finiteStep`: one truncated interpreter step is clean.

+  has a clean realization with the same joint output and external-state law.

+# Tidy realizations of oracle PPT programs
+`IsTidyOraclePPTOn` strengthens `IsOraclePPTOn` by requiring one finite machine that halts
+within a polynomial clock as a clean phase: it starts with blank work tapes and empty query
+buffers, works for arbitrary retained answer tapes, and finishes with blank work tapes, empty
+query buffers and its input head restored. Its output is appended to the output tape, and the
+complete joint law of that output and every external oracle state is exact.
+Clean phases compose. This module gives the shared core of the open calculus: deterministic
+programs, the bounded-prefix query, fair bits, captured data, monadic composition and branching.
+Only the selected branch of a conditional is executed, so unselected branches make no external
+call. An unbounded oracle reply is never copied for free: `query_take` charges its prefix length.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsTidyOraclePPTOn.query_take`: one external call returning a reply prefix.
+The clean-phase combinators adapt the tidy deterministic calculus of cslib (Christian
+Reitwiessner) to the probabilistic oracle machines of the cslib `crypto` branch at
+/-- One finite machine computes the encoded program as a clean phase within a uniform polynomial
+clock, preserving the joint law of the output and every shared stateful oracle. -/
+    (input : α ↪ List Bool) (output : β ↪ List Bool)
+  Finite Operation ∧ ∃ (k : ℕ) (Control : Type) (_ : Finite Control)
+    (machine : MultiTapePTM k Bool Control Operation) (c d : ℕ),
+    ∀ a, machine.ComputesTidily (input a) (c * ((input a).length + 1) ^ d) (output <$> program a)
+  {input : α ↪ List Bool} {middle : β ↪ List Bool} {output : γ ↪ List Bool}
+/-- A fixed finite machine with a polynomially bounded clean-phase clock is a certificate. -/
+    (machine : MultiTapePTM k Bool Control Operation) {time : α → ℕ}
+    (h : ∀ a, machine.ComputesTidily (input a) (time a) (output <$> program a)) :
+  exact ⟨inferInstance, k, Control, inferInstance, machine, c, d, fun a => (h a).mono (htime a)⟩
+/-- A clean realization is in particular a strict oracle PPT certificate. -/
+    (h : IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output program) : IsOraclePPTOn input output program := by
+  obtain ⟨hops, k, Control, hfinite, machine, c, d, h⟩ := h

+/-- Equality of the complete stateful semantics preserves a clean realization. -/

+theorem map {program : α → WordOracleComp Operation β} {f : β → γ}

+/-- A deterministic callback may capture the original argument. -/
+theorem map_with {program : α → WordOracleComp Operation β} {f : α → β → γ}
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair => f pair.1 pair.2) (encPair input middle) output) :
+    IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output (fun a => f a <$> program a) := by
+    hprogram.bind_with (second := fun a b => pure (f a b)) (of_computableTidilyInPolyTime hf)
+/-- Select a branch with an efficient Boolean condition. Only the selected branch runs, so an
+unselected branch makes no external call and cannot change any oracle state. -/
+theorem cond {condition : α → Bool} {yes no : α → WordOracleComp Operation γ}
+    (hyes : IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output yes) (hno : IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output no) :
+    IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output (fun a => if condition a then yes a else no a) := by
+  let test (a : α) : List Bool := if condition a then [true] else []
+  have htest : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime test input encBits :=
+      (fun b : Bool => if b then [true] else [])).comp hcondition
+  obtain ⟨tt, _, htt, _, kt, Test, hfiniteT, tester, htester⟩ := htest
+  obtain ⟨hops, k₁, Control₁, hfinite₁, yesMachine, c₁, d₁, hyesMachine⟩ := hyes
+  obtain ⟨_, k₂, Control₂, hfinite₂, noMachine, c₂, d₂, hnoMachine⟩ := hno
+    simp only [test, hc, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, List.length_nil] at hite ⊢
+    simp only [test, hc, ↓reduceIte, reduceCtorEq, List.length_singleton] at hite ⊢
+/-- Select a branch with an efficiently decidable condition, executing only that branch. -/
+theorem ite {condition : α → Prop} [∀ a, Decidable (condition a)]
+    (hcondition : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => decide (condition a)) input encBool)
+    (hyes : IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output yes) (hno : IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output no) :
+    IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output (fun a => if condition a then yes a else no a) := by
+  simpa only [decide_eq_true_eq] using hyes.cond hcondition hno
+/-- A computed finite tag selects one certified branch, which alone is executed. -/
+theorem finite_cases {Tag : Type} [Finite Tag] {tagEncoding : Tag ↪ List Bool} {tag : α → Tag}
+    {branch : Tag → α → WordOracleComp Operation γ} [Finite Operation]
+    IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output (fun a => branch (tag a) a) := by
+    let : IsEmpty α := ⟨fun a => isEmptyElim (tag a)⟩
+    have hselect (tags : List Tag) : IsTidyOraclePPTOn input output (fun a =>
+        tags.foldr (fun choice rest => if tag a = choice then branch choice a else rest)

+# Savitch's algorithm in the space of its stack
+Savitch's algorithm (`Cslib.Reachability.savitch`) runs the midpoint recursion on an explicit
+stack, for `Cslib.Reachability.Savitch.steps w d` steps. This file bounds its time and space in the
