+# Savitch's decider for space-bounded nondeterministic machines
+A nondeterministic machine with finitely many states, all of whose computation paths on an input
+of length `n` visit at most `c * (n + 1) ^ d` work cells, is decided by the deterministic
+`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.savitchDecide`: Savitch's midpoint recursion with an explicit stack
+(`Cslib.Reachability.savitch`) on the codes of the finite views of the machine, asking whether
+the accepting code is reachable from the code of the initial view.
+Every view reachable from the initial view has an encoding of length at most
+`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.viewLengthBound`, linear in `n` and the space bound, whatever the length of
+the path reaching it (`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.length_encFiniteCfg_le`), so the codes have a width `W`
+polynomial in `n`. Acceptance is reachability of the accepting code along the edges between codes
+`2 ^ (2 * W + 2)` such words, so it is reachability within as many steps, which the recursion
+decides at depth `2 * W + 2`. The edge test, the codes and the width are polynomial-time, so the
+decider runs in space polynomial in `n`, charging the stack of frames, the counters and the edge
+The decider retains the whole input, so this is the polynomial-space consequence of Savitch's
+theorem; the quadratic bound `NSPACE(s) ⊆ DSPACE(s ^ 2)` for sublinear `s` is not claimed.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeNTM.codeWidth`: the width of the codes of the views.
+* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, Theorem 8.5][Sipser2013]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Section 4.2][AroraBarak09]

+`c * (input.length + 1) ^ d`: the length of the encoding of the initial view plus the bound
+`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.viewLengthBound` on the encodings of all reachable views. -/

+/-- **Savitch's decider**: whether the accepting code is reachable from the code of the initial
+view, by Savitch's midpoint recursion on words of `2 * W + 2` bits at depth `2 * W + 2`, for the
+noncomputable def savitchDecide (c d : ℕ) (input : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  Cslib.Reachability.savitch ntm.codeEdge (2 * ntm.codeWidth c d input + 2)

+The binary counter, in the order of `Cslib.BitString.enumList`; the midpoint recursion and the
+stack machine on a directed path through the words of width two, on a graph whose target is
+unreachable, and on the trivial walk at depth zero; walks of the path through
+`Cslib.Reachability.savitch_iff`; instances of the quantitative certificate and of its
+polynomial-space form for a family of depths, so that their hypotheses are satisfiable; and the
+axioms of the headline theorems of both modules.
+example : BitString.enumList 2 = [[false, false], [true, false], [false, true], [true, true]] := by
+example : Savitch.next [true, false, true] = some [false, true, true] := rfl
+/-- The path `00 → 10 → 01 → 11` through the words of width two, in counter order. -/
+private def path (u v : List Bool) : Bool := decide (Savitch.next u = some v)
+-- At level `i`, the walks of at most `2 ^ i` steps.
+example : reach path 2 0 [false, false] [true, false] = true := by decide
+example : reach path 2 0 [false, false] [false, true] = false := by decide
+example : reach path 2 1 [false, false] [false, true] = true := by decide
+example : reach path 2 1 [false, false] [true, true] = false := by decide
+example : reach path 2 2 [false, false] [true, true] = true := by decide
+example : reach path 2 3 [true, true] [false, false] = false := by decide
+-- The machine itself, run for `2 ^ 8 - 1` steps by the kernel.
+example : savitch path 2 1 [false, false] [false, true] = true := by decide +kernel
+example : savitch path 2 1 [false, false] [true, true] = false := by decide +kernel
+-- At depth two the machine runs for `2 ^ 12 - 1` steps; the correctness theorem shortcuts them.
+example : savitch path 2 2 [false, false] [true, true] = true := by
+    (fun a b => a.length = 2 ∧ b.length = 2 ∧ path a b = true) [false, false] [true, true]
+    (fun a b => a.length = 2 ∧ b.length = 2 ∧ path a b = true) [false, false] [true, true]
+  rw [← savitch_iff (w := 2) (u := [false, false]) (v := [true, true]) rfl rfl]
+/-- Edges between the words with the same last bit: `{00, 10}` and `{01, 11}` are disconnected. -/
+private def halves (u v : List Bool) : Bool := decide (u.getLast? = v.getLast?)
+example : reach halves 2 1 [false, false] [true, false] = true := by decide
+example : reach halves 2 3 [false, false] [true, true] = false := by decide
+example : savitch halves 2 1 [false, false] [true, true] = false := by decide +kernel
+    (fun a b => a.length = 2 ∧ b.length = 2 ∧ halves a b = true) [false, false] [true, true]
+  rw [← reach_iff (w := 2) (u := [false, false]) (v := [true, true]) rfl rfl]
+example : savitch (fun _ _ => false) 2 0 [true, false] [true, false] = true := by decide
+example : savitch (fun _ _ => false) 2 0 [true, false] [false, true] = false := by decide
+/-! ### The certificates, for a family of depths -/
+/-- The equality of words, as an edge test with a trivial parameter, in the calculus. -/
+    (fun q : Unit × List Bool × List Bool => decide (q.2.1 = q.2.2))
+    (encPair encUnit (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool T S :=
+-- Savitch's algorithm at depth `n`, with the width, the endpoints and the edge test fixed.
+    (fun n : ℕ => savitch (fun u v => decide (u = v)) 1 n [false] [true]) encUnary encBool T S := by
+  have hin : ComputableTidilyInO (fun n : ℕ => ((), 1, n, [false], [true])) encUnary
+  exact ⟨_, _, computableTidilyInO_savitch (edge := fun _ u v => decide (u = v)) hedge hin
+-- The same family, in polynomial space.
+example : ∃ t s, PolyBounded (fun n : ℕ => (encUnary n).length) s ∧
+      (fun n : ℕ => savitch (fun u v => decide (u = v)) 1 n [false] [true]) encUnary encBool
+      (fun q : Unit × List Bool × List Bool => decide (q.2.1 = q.2.2))
+  have hin : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun n : ℕ => ((), 1, n, [false], [true])) encUnary
+  exact exists_polyBounded_space_savitch (edge := fun _ u v => decide (u = v)) hedge hin

+The diagonal function `Cslib.Complexity.diagonal` reads a description of a machine framed at the
+start of its input `x` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.decodeDesc`), runs the described machine on
+the whole of `x`, symbol by symbol under the fixed coding `false ↦ 0`, `true ↦ 1`, for
+`2 ^ x.length` steps with the universal function, and negates the verdict: it returns `false`
+exactly when the described machine has halted with output `[true]` by then.
+The diagonal is itself computed, by one fixed machine, within time `O(2 ^ (4 * n))` and space
+`O(2 ^ (2 * n))` on inputs of length `n` (`Cslib.Complexity.computableTidilyInO_diagonal`). The
+bound charges decoding, converting the input to symbols, writing the clock `2 ^ n` in binary, the
+universal run and the final test; the universal run dominates, within time polynomial in `n` times
+`2 ^ (3 * n)` and space polynomial in `n` times `2 ^ n`, and one more factor `2 ^ n` absorbs the
+No machine computing a Boolean function in polynomial time decides the diagonal problem, by the
+diagonal argument of the time hierarchy theorem [Arora and Barak, Theorem 3.1][AroraBarak09]. Its
+description, padded to a length where the machine halts within the exponential clock, is an input
+on which the diagonal returns the negation of the machine's answer
+(`Cslib.Complexity.diagonal_not_mem_P`). The argument uses only that the machine halts with its
+answer within a polynomial time bound, so it applies to plain, not necessarily tidy, machines as
+an explicit exponential-time computation is not in `P`. No time-bounded classes are defined here.

+/-- Guarding a verifier by its certificate-length check preserves `IsVerifier`. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+For `2 ^ D` requests, a fixed De Morgan circuit maps the bits of arbitrary target points of
+`K ^ ℓ`, which may repeat, to listed punctured lines through them with nonzero directions and
+pairwise disjoint lines, in the original request order (`IsScheduler`). Universal menus of
+direction tuples are a hypothesis: for every `0 < k ≤ 2 ^ D` pending requests some menu of `r`
+entries with `k * r ≤ 2 ^ D * (2 + 3 ℓ b) + 2 k` serves every state with `2 ^ D` occupied lines.
+The circuit labels every request with its position, then runs `D + 1` phases with `2 ^ D`,
+`2 ^ (D - 1)`, …, `1` pending requests. Each phase tests its menu and accepts the clean half of
+the pending requests (`Scheduler.next`), keeping the state good (`Scheduler.good_next`). Finally
+the records are sorted by label, which returns every request's line to its original position
+The size counts every gate, including constants, and is at most
+`524288 * 2 ^ D * (s + 1) * (D + ℓ * b + 2) ^ 5` (`schedulerBound`). The circuit is obtained
+existentially from synthesis bounds; its size does not certify the running time of any
+  [K. E. Batcher, *Sorting Networks and Their Applications*][Batcher1968].
+variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {ℓ b s D : ℕ}
+/-- Some circuit computes `finalOutput` exactly, by sorting the records by label and reading every
+request's line from the rank of its label, within the displayed number of gates. -/
+    ∃ c : Circuit signature (2 ^ D * width D L s) (2 ^ D * (s * L)),
+        c.size ≤ (D + 1) ^ 2 * 2 ^ D * (2 * D + 2 * width D L s + 1) := by
+  let g : Fin (arity D * width D L s) → BooleanFunction (2 ^ D * width D L s) := fun w x =>
+  have hsyn := Synthesis.circuit (I := interpretation) (s := inputs (2 ^ D * width D L s))
+    (bitonicSortCircuit labelBit D true) g fun w => ⟨_, rfl⟩
+  have hsub : (Set.range fun q x => finalOutput (D := D) (L := L) (s := s) x q) ⊆
+      Set.range fun j x => (bitonicSortCircuit labelBit D true).eval interpretation
+        (fun i => g i x) j := by
+    refine ⟨finProdFinEquiv (Fin.cast h2.symm (rank ip.1), lineBit cb.1 cb.2),
+    have h := congrFun (congrFun (eval_bitonicSortCircuit labelBit D true (fun i => g i x))
+    have hin : directProductInput (fun i => g i x) =
+        fun j f => x (finProdFinEquiv (Fin.cast h2 j, f)) := by
+  exact size_bitonicSortCircuit_le (labelBit (D := D) (L := L) (s := s)) D true
+/-- The phases with `2 ^ p, 2 ^ (p - 1), …, 1` pending requests accept every remaining request:
+some circuit maps every good state with `2 ^ D - 2 ^ p` accepted records to a good state with all
+theorem exists_phases_circuit (bits : K ≃+ BitString b) (scalar : Fin s ≃ {c : K // c ≠ 0})
+      ∃ menu : Fin r → Fin k → Fin ℓ → K, IsUniversalMenu (2 ^ D) menu)
+    ∃ c : Circuit signature (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s),
+      (∀ targets x, Good bits scalar targets (2 ^ D - arity p) x →
+        Good bits scalar targets (2 ^ D) (c.eval interpretation x)) ∧
+  have hkD (q : ℕ) (hq : q ≤ D) : arity q ≤ 2 ^ D := by
+  have hk1 (q : ℕ) : 0 < arity q := by
+  -- One phase with `2 ^ q` pending requests.
+      ∃ c : Circuit signature (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s),
+        (∀ targets x, Good bits scalar targets (2 ^ D - arity q) x →
+          Good bits scalar targets (2 ^ D - arity q + (arity q + 1) / 2)
+    obtain ⟨r, hr, menu, hU⟩ := hmenu (arity q) (hk1 q) (hkD q hq)
+    have hk : 2 ^ D - arity q + arity q = 2 ^ D := Nat.sub_add_cancel (hkD q hq)
+    obtain ⟨c, hc, hsize⟩ := exists_next_circuit hk bits scalar menu
+    refine ⟨c, fun targets x hx => ?_, hsize.trans (phaseCost_le hk hr hs)⟩
+    exact good_next bits scalar menu hU hx
+    refine ⟨c, fun targets x hx => ?_, by lia⟩
+    have h := hc targets x hx
+    have e : 2 ^ D - arity 0 + (arity 0 + 1) / 2 = 2 ^ D := by
+    refine ⟨c'.comp c, fun targets x hx => ?_, ?_⟩
+      have h := hc targets x hx
+      have e : 2 ^ D - arity (p + 1) + (arity (p + 1) + 1) / 2 = 2 ^ D - arity p := by
+        have h2 : arity (p + 1) = arity p + arity p := rfl
+/-- The gate bound of the scheduler: `524288 * 2 ^ D * (s + 1) * (D + ℓ * b + 2) ^ 5`. -/
+def schedulerBound (D ℓ b s : ℕ) : ℕ := 524288 * 2 ^ D * (s + 1) * (D + ℓ * b + 2) ^ 5
+private theorem total_le {D L b s P F : ℕ} (hb : b ≤ L)
+    (hF : F ≤ (D + 1) ^ 2 * 2 ^ D * (2 * D + 2 * Scheduler.width D L s + 1)) :
+  set V := D + L + 2 with hV
+  have hW : D + L + b + 2 ≤ 2 * V := by lia
+  have hD : D + 1 ≤ V := by lia
+  have hwidth : 2 * D + 2 * Scheduler.width D L s + 1 ≤ 6 * ((s + 1) * V) := by
+    have : s * L ≤ s * V := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by lia)
+    have : (s + 1) * V = s * V + V := by ring
+    calc F ≤ (D + 1) ^ 2 * n * (2 * D + 2 * Scheduler.width D L s + 1) := hF
+/-- **A near-linear scheduler circuit.** Given universal menus for every number `0 < k ≤ 2 ^ D`
+of pending requests, of `r` entries with `k * r ≤ 2 ^ D * (2 + 3 ℓ b) + 2 k`, some De Morgan
+circuit schedules `2 ^ D` requests: for all targets, repeated or not, it outputs in the
+original order listed punctured lines through them with nonzero directions and pairwise disjoint
+lines. Its size, counting every gate including constants, is at most `schedulerBound D ℓ b s`. -/
+theorem exists_isScheduler (bits : K ≃+ BitString b) (scalar : Fin s ≃ {c : K // c ≠ 0})
+      ∃ menu : Fin r → Fin k → Fin ℓ → K, IsUniversalMenu (2 ^ D) menu) :
+    ∃ c : Circuit signature (2 ^ D * (ℓ * b)) (2 ^ D * (s * (ℓ * b))),
+      IsScheduler bits scalar c ∧ c.size ≤ schedulerBound D ℓ b s := by
+  -- The scalars are the nonzero field elements, and the field has `2 ^ b` elements.
+    have h1 : s = Fintype.card {c : K // c ≠ 0} := by
+    have h2 : Fintype.card K = 2 ^ b := by
+  -- A universal menu has nonzero directions, so the points have a coordinate.
+    obtain ⟨r, -, menu, hU⟩ := hmenu 1 one_pos Nat.one_le_two_pow
+    exact hU.1 e 0 (funext fun i => i.elim0)
+  obtain ⟨cP, hP, hPsize⟩ := exists_phases_circuit bits scalar hmenu hs D le_rfl
+  obtain ⟨cF, hF, hFsize⟩ := exists_finalOutput_circuit D (ℓ * b) s
+  let cI := substituteCircuit (initialSubstitution D (ℓ * b) s)
+  · have h0 : Good bits scalar targets (2 ^ D - arity D)
+    obtain ⟨dirs, hne, hdisj, heq⟩ := finalOutput_eq_lineBits bits scalar (hP targets _ h0)
+    exact total_le (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left b hℓ) hPsize hFsize

+# Synthesis tools for the scheduler circuit
+The scheduler uses the shared circuit synthesis rule (`Synthesis.circuit`),
+shared prefix disjunctions (`Synthesis.prefixOr`), and two facts about
+sorted arrays: a permuted finite array is a reindexing (`List.Perm.exists_equiv_ofFn`), and in an
+array of flags sorted with true flags first, a position holds a true flag exactly when it precedes
+Gate counts are synthesis budgets: they count every gate, including constants, and do not
+certify the running time of any construction.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.prefixOr`: all prefix disjunctions of `r` available functions.
+* `List.Perm.exists_equiv_ofFn`: permuted finite arrays differ by a permutation of positions.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.sort_flag_eq_true_iff`: positions of true keys after sorting.
+/-- Permuted finite arrays differ by a permutation of their positions. -/
+theorem List.Perm.exists_equiv_ofFn {α : Type*} {n : ℕ} {f g : Fin n → α}
+    (h : (List.ofFn f).Perm (List.ofFn g)) : ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ i, f i = g (σ i) := by
+  refine ⟨⟨fun i => Fin.cast hg (h.idxBij (Fin.cast hf.symm i)),
+    fun j => Fin.cast hf (h.symm.idxBij (Fin.cast hg.symm j)), fun i => ?_, fun j => ?_⟩,
+/-- Every flag is false after a false flag; flags are sorted with true flags first. -/
+    (sorted : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → g i = false → g j = false) (j : Fin k) :
+    g j = true ↔ j.val < #{i | g i = true} := by
+    have hsub : Iic j ⊆ ({i | g i = true} : Finset (Fin k)) := by
+      exact absurd (sorted i j (mem_Iic.mp hi) (by simpa using hn)) (by simp [hj])
+    have hsub : ({i | g i = true} : Finset (Fin k)) ⊆ Iio j := by
+      simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at hi
+      exact absurd (sorted j i (not_lt.mp hle) (by simpa using hn)) (by simp [hi])
+/-- On one coordinate, lexicographic order is the order of the bit. -/
+theorem apply_zero_le_of_toLex_le {x y : Fin 1 → Bool} (h : toLex x ≤ toLex y) : x 0 ≤ y 0 :=
+  Pi.apply_le_of_toLex h fun j hj => absurd hj (Fin.not_lt_zero j)
+/-- Sorting records by a one-bit key with true keys first puts a true key at position `j` exactly
+when `j` is less than the number of true keys. -/
+theorem sort_flag_eq_true_iff {α : Type*} (φ : α → Fin 1 → Bool) (p : ℕ)
+    φ (BitonicSort.sort (fun r => toLex (φ r)) p false input j) 0 = true ↔
+  rw [← (BitonicSort.sort_perm (fun r => toLex (φ r)) p false input).card_filter_ofFn_eq
+    (fun j => φ (BitonicSort.sort (fun r => toLex (φ r)) p false input j) 0)
+    (BitonicSort.antitone_sort (fun r => toLex (φ r)) p input hjj')
+  exact Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr fun h' => by rw [h'] at h; exact absurd h (by decide)
+/-- The disjunction of the first `j + 1` of `r` functions. -/
+def prefixOr {r : ℕ} (F : Fin r → BooleanFunction n) (j : ℕ) : BooleanFunction n :=
+  fun x => decide (∃ e : Fin r, e.val ≤ j ∧ F e x = true)
+private theorem prefixOr_zero {r : ℕ} (F : Fin r → BooleanFunction n) (h : 0 < r) :
+    rwa [show e = ⟨0, h⟩ from Fin.ext (by lia)] at hx
+  · exact fun hx => ⟨⟨0, h⟩, le_rfl, hx⟩
+private theorem prefixOr_succ {r : ℕ} (F : Fin r → BooleanFunction n) (j : ℕ) (h : j + 1 < r) :
+    prefixOr F (j + 1) = fun x => prefixOr F j x || F ⟨j + 1, h⟩ x := by
+    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge e.val (j + 1) with hlt | hge
+    · exact Or.inr (by rwa [show e = ⟨j + 1, h⟩ from Fin.ext (by lia)] at hx)
+/-- All prefix disjunctions of `r` available functions, sharing each prefix with the next: one OR
+theorem Synthesis.prefixOr {r : ℕ} {s : Set (BooleanFunction n)} (F : Fin r → BooleanFunction n)
+    Synthesis interpretation s (Set.range fun e : Fin r => Boolean.prefixOr F e.val) r := by
+  suffices h : ∀ J ≤ r, Synthesis interpretation s
+      {f | ∃ e : Fin r, e.val < J ∧ f = Boolean.prefixOr F e.val} J by
+    exact (h r le_rfl).mono Set.Subset.rfl (by rintro _ ⟨e, rfl⟩; exact ⟨e, e.isLt, rfl⟩) le_rfl
+    exact Synthesis.of_subset (by rintro _ ⟨e, he, -⟩; exact absurd he (Nat.not_lt_zero _))
+    have hstep : Synthesis interpretation (s ∪ {f | ∃ e : Fin r, e.val < J ∧
+        f = Boolean.prefixOr F e.val}) {Boolean.prefixOr F J} 1 := by
+        exact (Synthesis.of_mem (Or.inr ⟨⟨J, by lia⟩, by simp, rfl⟩)).or
+    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge e.val J with hlt | hge
+    · exact Or.inr (by rw [show e.val = J by lia]; rfl)

+# A circuit for one scheduler phase
+The phase function `next` is synthesized stage by stage, each stage reading wires built by the
+1. candidate bits: the target bits plus fixed offsets, one negation per set offset bit;
+2. occupancy: one shared OR lookup of all candidates among the accepted line points
+3. duplicates: for each menu entry, duplicate flags among its candidates
+   (`duplicateFlagsCircuit`), with padding records marked by a tag bit;
+4. clean flags, a disjunction over the scalars per request;
+5. success: the clean flags of each entry, sorted, read at position `⌈2 ^ p / 2⌉ - 1`;
+6. the first successful entry, from shared prefix disjunctions;
+7. the chosen clean flags and candidate lines, disjunctions over the entries;
+8. the enriched pending records, sorted with clean records first.
+`phaseCost` is the exact sum of the stage budgets; it counts every gate, including constants. The
+construction is existential and does not certify the running time of any constructor.
+  [K. E. Batcher, *Sorting Networks and Their Applications*][Batcher1968].
+variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {ℓ b s D p a r : ℕ}
+  (hk : a + arity p = 2 ^ D) (bits : K ≃+ BitString b) (scalar : Fin s ≃ {c : K // c ≠ 0})
+  (menu : Fin r → Fin (arity p) → Fin ℓ → K)
+  {src : Set (BooleanFunction (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s))}
+private theorem add_false (x : Bool) : x + false = x := by cases x <;> rfl
+private theorem add_true (x : Bool) : x + true = !x := by cases x <;> rfl
+/-- Stage 1: each candidate bit is an input bit or its negation. -/
+      (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b) =>
+        fun x => candidate hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2.1 q.2.2.2)
+    let w := finProdFinEquiv (pending hk i, targetBit (D := D) (s := s) β)
+    have hw : (fun x : BitString (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) => x w) ∈ src := hin ⟨w, rfl⟩
+    cases hb : pointBits bits ((scalar c : K) • menu e i) β
+    · have : (fun x => candidate hk bits scalar menu x e i c β) = fun x => x w := by
+      simpa only [this] using (Synthesis.of_mem hw).mono Set.Subset.rfl Set.Subset.rfl
+    · have : (fun x => candidate hk bits scalar menu x e i c β) = fun x => !x w := by
+  · simp only [sum_const, card_univ, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul, mul_one,
+/-- Stage 2: occupancy by one shared OR lookup among the accepted line points. -/
+    (hcand : (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b) =>
+      fun x => candidate hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2.1 q.2.2.2) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s =>
+        fun x => occupied hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2)
+      (48 * (r * arity p * s + a * s + 1) * (Nat.clog 2 (r * arity p * s + a * s) + 1) ^ 2 *
+  let ι := (Fin a × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b)) ⊕ (Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b))
+  let eS := Fintype.equivFin (Fin a × Fin s)
+  let eQ := Fintype.equivFin (Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s)
+  let g : Fin (Fintype.card ι) → BooleanFunction (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) := fun w =>
+    Sum.elim (fun q x => x (finProdFinEquiv (accepted hk q.1, lineBit q.2.1 q.2.2)))
+      (fun q x => candidate hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2.1 q.2.2.2) (eι.symm w)
+  have hg : ∀ w, g w ∈ src := by
+    rcases h : eι.symm w with q | q
+  let sourceKeys : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin a × Fin s)) → Fin (ℓ * b) →
+    fun q β => .inl (eι (.inl ((eS.symm q).1, (eS.symm q).2, β)))
+  let sourceValues : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin a × Fin s)) → Fin 1 →
+  let queryKeys : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s)) → Fin (ℓ * b) →
+    fun q β => .inl (eι (.inr ((eQ.symm q).1, (eQ.symm q).2.1, (eQ.symm q).2.2, β)))
+  refine (Synthesis.circuit (batchOrCircuit sourceKeys sourceValues queryKeys) g hg).mono
+    refine ⟨finProdFinEquiv (eQ (e, i, c), 0), funext fun x => Bool.eq_iff_iff.mpr ?_⟩
+    have hsk (q : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin a × Fin s))) :
+        substitute (sourceKeys q) (fun w => g w x) =
+          line x (accepted hk (eS.symm q).1) (eS.symm q).2 := by
+      simp only [substitute, sourceKeys, g, Sum.elim_inl, Equiv.symm_apply_apply, line]
+    have hqk : substitute (queryKeys (eQ (e, i, c))) (fun w => g w x) =
+        candidate hk bits scalar menu x e i c := by
+      simp only [substitute, queryKeys, g, Sum.elim_inr, Sum.elim_inl, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
+    have hsv (q : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin a × Fin s))) :
+        substitute (sourceValues q) (fun w => g w x) 0 = true := rfl
+      exact ⟨eS (m, c'), by simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hm⟩
+/-- Stage 3: for each menu entry, duplicate flags among its candidates. Padding records carry a
+true tag bit, so they never repeat a candidate. -/
+    (hcand : (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b) =>
+      fun x => candidate hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2.1 q.2.2.2) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s =>
+        fun x => duplicate hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2)
+  let pad := arity d - arity p * s
+  have hpad : arity p * s + pad = arity d := by
+    have : arity p * s ≤ arity d := by
+  let ι := Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b)
+  let slot : Fin (arity p) × Fin s → Fin (arity d) :=
+    fun ic => Fin.cast hpad (Fin.castAdd pad (finProdFinEquiv ic))
+  let ρ : Fin (arity d * (ℓ * b + 1)) → Fin (Fintype.card ι) ⊕ Bool := fun q =>
+  let circuit := (duplicateFlagsCircuit (id : Fin (ℓ * b + 1) → Fin (ℓ * b + 1)) d).comp
+  have hentry (e : Fin r) : Synthesis interpretation src
+      (Set.range fun q : Fin (arity p) × Fin s =>
+        fun x => duplicate hk bits scalar menu x e q.1 q.2)
+      ((duplicateFlagsCircuit (id : Fin (ℓ * b + 1) → Fin (ℓ * b + 1)) d).size + 2) := by
+    let g : Fin (Fintype.card ι) → BooleanFunction (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) := fun w x =>
+      candidate hk bits scalar menu x e (eι.symm w).1 (eι.symm w).2.1 (eι.symm w).2.2
+    refine (Synthesis.circuit circuit g fun w => hcand ⟨(e, eι.symm w), rfl⟩).mono
+      Set.Subset.rfl ?_ (by simp only [circuit, Circuit.size_comp, size_substituteCircuit]; lia)
+    refine ⟨slot (i, c), funext fun x => Bool.eq_iff_iff.mpr ?_⟩
+    let y : BitString (Fintype.card ι) := fun w => g w x
+    -- The records seen by the duplicate circuit.
+    have hreal (i' : Fin (arity p)) (c' : Fin s) :
+        row (slot (i', c')) = Fin.cons false (candidate hk bits scalar menu x e i' c') := by
+      simp only [row, directProductInput, substitute, ρ, slot, Equiv.symm_apply_apply,
+      · simp only [Fin.cases_succ, Fin.cons_succ, Sum.elim_inl, y, g, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
+    have hpadRow (j : Fin pad) : row (Fin.cast hpad (Fin.natAdd _ j)) 0 = true := by
+      simp only [row, directProductInput, substitute, ρ, Equiv.symm_apply_apply,
+        Fin.cast_cast, Fin.cast_eq_self, Fin.addCases_right, Fin.cases_zero, Sum.elim_inr, id]
+    change (∃ j, j ≠ slot (i, c) ∧ row j = row (slot (i, c))) ↔ _
+        change slot (i', c') ≠ slot (i, c) at hne
+        change row (slot (i', c')) = row (slot (i, c)) at heq
+        exact ⟨i', c', fun h => hne (congrArg slot h), funext fun β => congrFun heq β.succ⟩
+        rw [show (finCongr hpad) (Fin.natAdd _ j) = Fin.cast hpad (Fin.natAdd _ j) from rfl,
+      refine ⟨slot (i', c'), fun h => hne ?_, by rw [hreal, hreal, heq]⟩
+/-- Stage 4: a request is clean when no candidate is occupied or a duplicate. -/
+    (hocc : (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s =>
+      fun x => occupied hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2) ⊆ src)
+    (hdup : (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s =>
+      fun x => duplicate hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) => fun x => clean hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2)
+      (fun c x => occupied hk bits scalar menu x e i c || duplicate hk bits scalar menu x e i c)
+    refine (Synthesis.congr_iff h fun x => ?_).mono Set.Subset.rfl Set.Subset.rfl (le_of_eq ?_)
+      simp only [mem_univ, true_and, Bool.or_eq_true, not_exists, not_or, Bool.not_eq_true]
+  · simp only [sum_const, card_univ, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul]
+/-- Stage 5: an entry succeeds when its sorted clean flags are true at position
+    (hclean : (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) =>
+      fun x => clean hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun e : Fin r => fun x => success hk bits scalar menu x e)
+  let j₀ : Fin (arity p) := ⟨(arity p + 1) / 2 - 1, by lia⟩
+  have hentry (e : Fin r) : Synthesis interpretation src
+      (Set.range fun _ : Unit => fun x => success hk bits scalar menu x e)
+    let g : Fin (arity p * 1) → BooleanFunction (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) :=
+      fun q x => clean hk bits scalar menu x e (finProdFinEquiv.symm q).1
+      fun q => hclean ⟨(e, _), rfl⟩).mono Set.Subset.rfl ?_ le_rfl
+      (eval_bitonicSortCircuit (id : Fin 1 → Fin 1) p false (fun q => g q x)) j₀) 0
+    have hin : directProductInput (fun q => g q x) =
+        fun i _ => clean hk bits scalar menu x e i := by
+    have hflag := sort_flag_eq_true_iff (fun r : BitString 1 => r ∘ id) p
+      (fun i _ => clean hk bits scalar menu x e i) j₀
+    change (bitonicSortCircuit id p false).eval interpretation (fun q => g q x)
+      (finProdFinEquiv (j₀, 0)) = success hk bits scalar menu x e
+    rw [show (bitonicSortCircuit id p false).eval interpretation (fun q => g q x)
+/-- Stage 6: the first successful entry, from shared prefix disjunctions. -/
+    (hsucc : (Set.range fun e : Fin r => fun x => success hk bits scalar menu x e) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun e : Fin r => fun x => chosen hk bits scalar menu x e) (3 * r) := by
+  let F : Fin r → BooleanFunction (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) :=
+    fun e x => success hk bits scalar menu x e
+  have hpre := Synthesis.prefixOr F fun e => hsucc ⟨e, rfl⟩
+  · have hF : F e ∈ src ∪ Set.range fun e : Fin r => Boolean.prefixOr F e.val :=
+    · have : (fun x => chosen hk bits scalar menu x e) = F e := by
+        refine ⟨And.left, fun h => ⟨h, fun e' he' => ?_⟩⟩
+    · have hj : j < r := by have := e.isLt; lia
+          src ∪ Set.range fun e : Fin r => Boolean.prefixOr F e.val :=
+      have : (fun x => chosen hk bits scalar menu x e) =
+          fun x => F e x && !Boolean.prefixOr F j x := by
+        refine and_congr Iff.rfl ⟨fun h e' he' => h e' (Fin.lt_def.mpr (by lia)),
+          fun h e' he' => h e' (by have := Fin.lt_def.mp he'; lia)⟩
+/-- Stage 7: the clean flag of each request for the chosen entry. -/
+    (hchosen : (Set.range fun e : Fin r => fun x => chosen hk bits scalar menu x e) ⊆ src)
+    (hclean : (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) =>
+      fun x => clean hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun i : Fin (arity p) => fun x => flag hk bits scalar menu x i)
+      (fun e x => chosen hk bits scalar menu x e && clean hk bits scalar menu x e i)
+    refine (Synthesis.congr_iff h fun x => ?_).mono Set.Subset.rfl Set.Subset.rfl (le_of_eq ?_)
+    · simp only [flag, decide_eq_true_iff, mem_univ, true_and, Bool.and_eq_true]
+/-- Stage 7: the candidate line of each request for the chosen entry. -/
+    (hchosen : (Set.range fun e : Fin r => fun x => chosen hk bits scalar menu x e) ⊆ src)
+    (hcand : (Set.range fun q : Fin r × Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b) =>
+      fun x => candidate hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2.1 q.2.2.2) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun q : Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b) =>
+        fun x => newLine hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2)
+      (fun e x => chosen hk bits scalar menu x e && candidate hk bits scalar menu x e i c β)
+    refine (Synthesis.congr_iff h fun x => ?_).mono Set.Subset.rfl Set.Subset.rfl (le_of_eq ?_)
+    · simp only [newLine, decide_eq_true_iff, mem_univ, true_and, Bool.and_eq_true]
+  · simp only [sum_const, card_univ, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul,
+/-- Stage 8: the enriched pending records, sorted with clean records first. -/
+    (hflag : (Set.range fun i : Fin (arity p) => fun x => flag hk bits scalar menu x i) ⊆ src)
+    (hnew : (Set.range fun q : Fin (arity p) × Fin s × Fin (ℓ * b) =>
+      fun x => newLine hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2) ⊆ src) :
+      (Set.range fun q : Fin (arity p) × Fin (1 + width D (ℓ * b) s) =>
+        fun x => sortedPending hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2)
+      (bitonicSortCircuit (flagKey (D := D) (ℓ := ℓ) (b := b) (s := s)) p false).size := by
+  let g : Fin (arity p * (1 + width D (ℓ * b) s)) →
+      BooleanFunction (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) := fun w x =>
+    enriched hk bits scalar menu x (finProdFinEquiv.symm w).1 (finProdFinEquiv.symm w).2
+  have hg (w) : g w ∈ src := by
+  refine (Synthesis.circuit (bitonicSortCircuit flagKey p false) g hg).mono Set.Subset.rfl ?_
+    (eval_bitonicSortCircuit flagKey p false (fun w => g w x)) j) f
+  have hin : directProductInput (fun w => g w x) = enriched hk bits scalar menu x := by
+/-- The phase output is available once the sorted pending records are. -/
+    (hsort : (Set.range fun q : Fin (arity p) × Fin (1 + width D (ℓ * b) s) =>
+      fun x => sortedPending hk bits scalar menu x q.1 q.2) ⊆ src)
+    (q : Fin (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s)) : (fun x => next hk bits scalar menu x q) ∈ src := by
+  rcases accepted_or_pending (hk := hk) m with ⟨m', rfl⟩ | ⟨j, rfl⟩
+/-- The gate budget of one phase with `2 ^ p` pending and `a` accepted records and a menu of `r`
+entries: the sum of the eight stage budgets. It counts every gate, including constants. -/
+def phaseCost (D L s p a r : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  48 * (r * arity p * s + a * s + 1) * (Nat.clog 2 (r * arity p * s + a * s) + 1) ^ 2 *
+  (bitonicSortCircuit (Fin.castAdd (width D L s) : Fin 1 → Fin (1 + width D L s)) p false).size
+/-- **One scheduler phase.** Some circuit computes `next` exactly, on every input, within
+`phaseCost` gates; the size counts every gate, including constants. -/
+    ∃ c : Circuit signature (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s) (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s),
+      c.Computes interpretation (next hk bits scalar menu) ∧
+        c.size ≤ phaseCost D (ℓ * b) s p a r := by
+  have h1 := synthesis_candidate hk bits scalar menu
+    (src := inputs (2 ^ D * width D (ℓ * b) s)) Set.Subset.rfl
+  have h2 := h1.comp (synthesis_occupied hk bits scalar menu Set.subset_union_left
+  have h3 := h2.comp (synthesis_duplicate hk bits scalar menu
+  have h4 := h3.comp (synthesis_clean hk bits scalar menu
+  have h5 := h4.comp (synthesis_success hk bits scalar menu
+  have h6 := h5.comp (synthesis_chosen hk bits scalar menu
+  have h7 := h6.comp (synthesis_flag hk bits scalar menu
+  have h8 := h7.comp (synthesis_newLine hk bits scalar menu
+  have h9 := h8.comp (synthesis_sortedPending hk bits scalar menu
+  have h10 := h9.trans (Synthesis.of_subset (t := Set.range fun q x =>
+    next hk bits scalar menu x q) (by
+      exact next_mem hk bits scalar menu (fun _ h => Or.inl h)
+        (by intro _ h; simp only [Set.mem_union]; tauto) q))

+A circuit `c` with as many outputs as inputs computes a map `c.eval I` on states. Composing `t`
+copies gives `c.iterate t`, which computes the `t`-th power of that map
+(`Circuit.eval_iterate`); its arbitrary weighted cost and its size are exactly `t` times those of
+When the intermediate states are needed as well, the orbit prefix can be retained within the same
+budget: `Synthesis.orbit` makes every state `(c.eval I)^[j] (init x)` with `j ≤ t` available at
+cost `t * c.size`, sharing each state with every later construction (`Synthesis.stages`,
+`Synthesis.steps`). This uses one copy of `c` per transition, applied to wires that are already
+The signature and the carrier are arbitrary. Sizes bound circuits; they do not certify the running
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.iterate`: `t` copies of a circuit composed in sequence.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.stages`: the values retained through a stage.
+  `Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.size_iterate`: exact semantics, weighted cost and size.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.steps`: a sequence of constructions adds its costs.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.orbit`: retain an orbit prefix with one circuit per transition.
+* `Circuit.iterate` and its semantics and costs follow `Algebraic/Iteration.lean` in
+  with Mathlib's `Nat.iterate` in place of its own function iteration.
+* The retained orbits are adapted from `lean/Proofs/{Iteration,Synthesis}.lean` in
+/-- `t` copies of `c` composed in sequence; zero copies are the identity wiring. -/
+def iterate (c : Circuit σ m m) : ℕ → Circuit σ m m
+/-- Iterating a circuit computes the power of its map. -/
+@[simp] theorem eval_iterate (c : Circuit σ m m) (I : Interpretation σ U) (t : ℕ) :
+/-- Iterating a circuit multiplies its arbitrary weighted cost exactly. -/
+theorem cost_program_iterate (c : Circuit σ m m) (t : ℕ) (cost : σ.Op → ℕ) :
+    (c.iterate t).program.cost cost = t * c.program.cost cost := by
+/-- Iterating a circuit multiplies its size exactly. -/
+@[simp] theorem size_iterate (c : Circuit σ m m) (t : ℕ) : (c.iterate t).size = t * c.size := by
+  simpa only [Program.cost_const, one_mul] using c.cost_program_iterate t (fun _ => 1)
+/-- A circuit computing `f` iterates to a circuit computing the powers of `f`. -/
+theorem Computes.iterate {c : Circuit σ m m} {I : Interpretation σ U}
+    {f : (Fin m → U) → Fin m → U} (hc : c.Computes I f) (t : ℕ) :
+    (c.iterate t).Computes I f^[t] := fun x => by
+  rw [eval_iterate, show c.eval I = f from funext hc]
+/-- The values retained through stage `t` of a straight-line construction. -/
+def stages (q : ℕ → Set ((Fin n → U) → U)) (t : ℕ) : Set ((Fin n → U) → U) :=
+@[simp] theorem stages_zero (q : ℕ → Set ((Fin n → U) → U)) : stages q 0 = q 0 := by
+theorem stages_succ (q : ℕ → Set ((Fin n → U) → U)) (t : ℕ) :

+Every problem in `Cslib.Complexity.NP` is decided in polynomial time by a nondeterministic
+machine with a binary alphabet and finitely many states, which guesses a certificate and runs the
+verifier on it: the inclusion of `NP` in nondeterministic polynomial time
+[Arora and Barak, Theorem 2.6][AroraBarak09]. The converse, and hence the characterization of
+The machine is built from the PPT calculus and its clock compiler rather than by hand. For a
+verifier `V` with certificates of length `p (enc a).length`, the probabilistic program that samples
+a word of this length and returns the verdict of `V` is uniformly polynomial-time. The clock
+compiler `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.exists_halting_machine` turns it into a finite fair-coin
+machine that actually halts on every branch within a polynomial clock. Its nondeterministic machine
+`Turing.MultiTapePTM.toNTM` guesses the coins: its computation paths are exactly the coin
+replays, so it accepts exactly when some certificate of the required length is accepted. It is
+never stuck, so every branch actually halts within the bound.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.IsVerifier.exists_decidesInTime`: a verifier gives a fair-coin machine whose
+  nondeterministic machine decides the problem within an explicit polynomial and is never stuck.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+/-- **Guess and verify**, the inclusion of `NP` in nondeterministic polynomial time
+[Arora and Barak, Theorem 2.6][AroraBarak09]. A polynomial-time verifier gives a finite fair-coin
+machine whose nondeterministic machine decides the problem within the explicit polynomial
+`c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d`. That machine is never stuck, so its branches
+    (hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool) (hA : IsVerifier enc p V A) :
+    ∃ (k : ℕ) (State : Type) (_ : Finite State) (machine : MultiTapePTM k Bool State) (c d : ℕ),
+      machine.toNTM.DecidesInTime enc A (fun a => c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) ∧
+      ∀ input (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input), ∃ cfg', machine.toNTM.Step cfg cfg' := by
+  -- guess a certificate of the required length, then verify it
+  have hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) enc encUnary :=
+  have hprogram : IsPPTOn enc encBool program := hcount.sampleList.map_with hV
+  obtain ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, c, d, heval, hhalt⟩ := hprogram.exists_halting_machine
+  refine ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, c, d, fun a => ?_, fun _ => machine.exists_step_toNTM⟩
+  have htime : machine.toNTM.RunsInTime (enc a) (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) :=
+  -- both sides say that `[true]` is a supported output
+  have hsupport := congrArg (fun μ => [true] ∈ μ.support) (heval a)
+/-- Problems in `NP` are decidable in polynomial time by nondeterministic machines with a binary
+  obtain ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, c, d, hdecides, -⟩ := hA.exists_decidesInTime hV
+  exact ⟨_, .of_forall_le c d fun _ => le_rfl, k, State, hfinite, machine.toNTM, hdecides⟩

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The verifier class `Cslib.Complexity.NP` consists exactly of the problems decided in polynomial
+time by nondeterministic machines with a binary alphabet and finitely many states
+[Arora and Barak, Theorem 2.6][AroraBarak09]. Guessing a certificate and verifying it gives one
+inclusion (`Cslib.Complexity.decidableInPolyTime_of_mem_NP`). This file proves the converse by
+A computation path is encoded by its choices, as coins of the fixed finite choice table
+`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.choiceTable`: a step taking the permitted action of zero-based index `j`
+costs `j + 1` coins, at most `M = Nat.card` of the action type. If every computation path on
+`enc a` with at least `c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d` steps has halted (stuck paths may be
+shorter), accepting computations are encoded within `M * c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d` coins, and
+padded to exactly this polynomial length, which a halted table ignores. The verifier
+`Turing.MultiTapeNTM.checkChoices` replays the certificate with the choice table and accepts when
+the table emits `[true]`: then the coins encode a computation path that halts with output
+`[true]`. Every coin list selects permitted actions, except at a stuck configuration, which has
+none; there the table rejects. Replaying a fixed finite fair-coin table from encoded coins and
+the verifier needs no machine built by hand.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeNTM.checkChoices`: the verifier of encoded accepting computations.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeNTM.DecidesInTime.isVerifier`: a machine deciding a problem within
+  `c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d` steps yields a verifier with certificates of length
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+variable {k : ℕ} {State : Type} [Finite State] {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool}
+/-- **The verifier of encoded accepting computations.** It accepts when the certificate, read as
+coins of the choice table, replays a computation path on the encoded instance that halts with
+noncomputable def checkChoices (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Bool State) (enc : α ↪ List Bool)
+/-- Checking an encoded computation is polynomial-time: it replays a fixed finite fair-coin
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (ntm.checkChoices enc) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+  have hswap : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool => (x.2, enc x.1))
+/-- **Accepting computations as certificates.** A machine deciding `A` within
+`c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d` steps (every computation path with at least that many steps has
+halted) yields a verifier whose certificates have length exactly
+`M * c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d`, for the number `M` of actions. -/
+theorem DecidesInTime.isVerifier {ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Bool State} {A : Set α} {c d : ℕ}
+    (h : ntm.DecidesInTime enc A fun a => c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) :
+  have heval : (Polynomial.C (Nat.card (Turing.Action k Bool State) * c) *
+      Nat.card (Turing.Action k Bool State) * (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) := by
+      exists_runClosedCoins_choiceTable p ((h a).1 p hp.ge) hout
+    exact accepts_of_runClosedCoins_choiceTable (coins := w) (by simpa [checkChoices] using hw)
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {A : Set α}
+/-- **Checking accepting computations**, the inclusion of nondeterministic polynomial time in
+  obtain ⟨t, ht, k, State, hfinite, ntm, hdecides⟩ := h
+/-- **`NP` is nondeterministic polynomial time** [Arora and Barak, Theorem 2.6][AroraBarak09]:
+a problem has a polynomial-time verifier with certificates of polynomial length exactly when a
+nondeterministic machine with a binary alphabet and finitely many states decides it in
+polynomial time, relative to the same encoding of instances. -/
+    A ∈ NP enc ↔ MultiTapeNTM.DecidableInPolyTime A enc :=

+# Existential second-order definable classes are in NP
+The easy direction of Fagin's theorem [Fagin, Theorem 6][Fagin1974],
+[Immerman, Proposition 7.6][Immerman1999]: for a fixed existential second-order sentence
+`Φ = ∃ R₁ … Rₖ, φ` over a vocabulary, the inputs encoding the finite structures satisfying `Φ`
+form a problem in `NP`. The certificate for an input of encoded length `N` is a bit string of
+length `blocks * N ^ degree`, where a layout (`Cslib.Logic.ESO.Sentence.Layout`) gives each
+relation variable its own block of `N ^ degree` bits and `degree` bounds the arities. The block
+of a relation variable is its truth table, indexed like the tables of the input by
+`Cslib.Logic.tupleIndex`; since the cardinality `n` of the structure is at most `N`, every tuple
+has a bit, and the unused bits of a block are ignored. Reading the blocks as relations
+(`Cslib.Logic.ESO.Sentence.Layout.certRel`) expands the decoded structure by the relation
+variables, and the verifier (`Cslib.Logic.ESO.Sentence.Layout.verifier`) checks that the input is
+well formed and evaluates the first-order part in the expansion. The evaluator
+(`Cslib.Logic.ESO.Sentence.Layout.eval`) recurses on the fixed formula and ranges over the `n`
+elements at each quantifier, so it is a polynomial-time program for each fixed sentence;
+`fun_prop` certifies it with the closure rules of `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`.
+The sentence and the vocabulary are fixed parameters: the degree of the polynomial time bound
+depends on the quantifier depth and the arities of the sentence, and the number of relation symbols
+enters the length of the input. Malformed inputs are rejected by the verifier and are not in the
+problem. Which certificates are accepted depends on the layout; the problem does not. The converse
+direction, that every isomorphism-closed problem in `NP` is existential second-order definable,
+* `Cslib.Logic.ESO.Sentence.Layout`: a certificate layout for a sentence, with its polynomial
+* `Cslib.Logic.ESO.Sentence.Layout.eval`: the evaluator of the first-order part on an input and a
+* `Cslib.Logic.ESO.Sentence.Layout.eval_eq_true_iff`: the evaluator decides truth in the expansion
+  of the decoded structure by the certificate relations.
+  the sentence exactly when some certificate is accepted.
+  `Cslib.Logic.ESO.Definable.queryLanguage_mem_NP`: the problem of a sentence, and the query
+  language of a definable class, are in `NP`.
+* [R. Fagin, *Generalized first-order spectra and polynomial-time recognizable sets*][Fagin1974]
+open FirstOrder Language Structure CategoryTheory Turing.MultiTapeTM Cslib.Complexity
+/-- A **certificate layout** for `Φ`: a block number for each relation variable, and a bound on
+their arities. A certificate for an input of encoded length `N` has `blocks * N ^ degree` bits,
+block `i` holding the truth table of relation variable `i`. -/
+  /-- The block of each relation variable. -/
+  /-- A bound on the arities of the relation variables. -/
+/-- Every sentence has a layout, numbering its finitely many relation variables. -/
+/-- The polynomial giving the length of certificates in the encoded length of the input. -/
+theorem eval_polynomial (N : ℕ) : ℓ.polynomial.eval N = ℓ.blocks * N ^ ℓ.degree := by
+/-- The position of the bit of relation variable `i` at the tuple of index `idx`, in a certificate
+theorem position_lt (N : ℕ) (i : Φ.Var) {idx : ℕ} (h : idx < N ^ ℓ.degree) :
+    ℓ.position N i idx < ℓ.blocks * N ^ ℓ.degree := by
+  calc ℓ.block i * N ^ ℓ.degree + idx < (ℓ.block i + 1) * N ^ ℓ.degree := by
+/-- Positions determine the relation variable and the index of the tuple. -/
+theorem position_injective (N : ℕ) {i j : Φ.Var} {idx idx' : ℕ} (h : idx < N ^ ℓ.degree)
+    (h' : idx' < N ^ ℓ.degree) (he : ℓ.position N i idx = ℓ.position N j idx') :
+  have hB : 0 < N ^ ℓ.degree := by omega
+  have hdiv : ∀ (b idx : ℕ), idx < N ^ ℓ.degree → (b * N ^ ℓ.degree + idx) / N ^ ℓ.degree = b :=
+    fun b idx h => by rw [Nat.mul_comm, Nat.mul_add_div hB, Nat.div_eq_of_lt h, Nat.add_zero]

+    fun b idx h => by rw [Nat.mul_add_mod', Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h]
+  have h₁ := congrArg (· / N ^ ℓ.degree) he
+  have h₂ := congrArg (· % N ^ ℓ.degree) he

+/-- The number of tuples of the arity of a relation variable is at most the block size, for inputs
+theorem pow_arity_le {n N : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ N) (hN : 0 < N) (i : Φ.Var) :

+its position is set; missing bits read as false. -/
+def certRel (n N : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (i : Φ.Var) : Set (Fin (Φ.arity i) → Fin n) :=
+  {x | w.getD (ℓ.position N i (tupleIndex x)) false = true}
+/-- The certificate encoding relations `R` on `Fin n`, for inputs of encoded length `N`: the bit

+noncomputable def certificate (n N : ℕ) (R : ∀ i, Set (Fin (Φ.arity i) → Fin n)) : List Bool :=
+    decide (∃ (i : Φ.Var) (x : Fin (Φ.arity i) → Fin n),

+/-- The time bound holds vacuously although no branch halts. -/

+  fun p hp => absurd (time_stuck p) (by omega)
+/-- A stuck branch does not accept. -/
+private theorem not_accepts_stuck (input : List Bool) : ¬stuck.Accepts input := by
+  fun a => ⟨runsInTime_stuck a, by simpa using not_accepts_stuck a⟩

+/-- Emit one fair bit and halt. -/

+    { inputTape := 0, workTapes := Fin.elim0, output := some bit, state := none }

+/-- One step with a given coin halts with that bit as output. -/

+/-- For each bit, a computation path of one step halts with that bit as output. -/

+  have hhalt : (p.toRunPath ⟨1, hlt⟩).Halted := by rw [hone]; rfl

+  | mul hf hg ihf ihg => cases hb with
+    | mul hf' hg' => rw [ihf hf', ihg hg']

+        _ = b := by rw [← mul_assoc, hva, one_mul]

+    exact .inv ih (by rw [← map_mul, hab, map_one]) (by rw [← map_mul, hba, map_one])

+    Submodule.coe_smul, component] using congrArg Subtype.val (b.sum_repr (component (F := F) f α))
+/-- The output map of the wk possible component images. -/
+def imageCombination {w k : ℕ} (T : Fin w → P →ₗ[F] Q) (u : Fin k → P) :
+  Fintype.linearCombination F (fun ij => T ij.1 (u ij.2))
+def concatMatrix {w q k : ℕ} (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F)
+    (P : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin k) F) : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin w × Fin k) F :=
+  fun α ij => (A ij.1 * P) α ij.2
+    (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F) (T : Fin w → P →ₗ[F] Q)
+    (f : Fin q → P) (b : Basis (Fin k) F (componentSpace (F := F) f))
+    (hker : ∀ α, ∑ i, ∑ γ, A i α γ • T i (f γ) = 0) (α : Fin q) :
+  change (∑ ij : Fin w × Fin k,
+    (∑ γ, A ij.1 α γ * coefficientMatrix f b γ ij.2) • T ij.1 (b ij.2 : P)) = 0
+    (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F) (T : Fin w → P →ₗ[F] Q)
+    (f : Fin q → P) (b : Basis (Fin k) F (componentSpace (F := F) f))
+    (hker : ∀ α, ∑ i, ∑ γ, A i α γ • T i (f γ) = 0)
+    (hex : (w-1)*k < finrank F (imageCombination T (fun j => (b j : P))).range)
+    (hw : 1 ≤ w) : (concatMatrix A (coefficientMatrix f b)).rank < k := by
+  let H := imageCombination T (fun j => (b j : P))
+  have hle : Submodule.span F (Set.range (concatMatrix A (coefficientMatrix f b)).row) ≤
+    exact concat_row_relation A T f b hker α
+  simp only [Module.finrank_pi, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fin] at hd
+  change (w-1)*k < finrank F H.range at hex
+    (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F) (P : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin k) F) (i : Fin w) :
+lemma component_image_le_range {w q k : ℕ} (T : Fin w → P →ₗ[F] Q)
+    (f : Fin q → P) (b : Basis (Fin k) F (componentSpace (F := F) f)) (i : Fin w) :
+  have he : (∑ j, (b.repr ⟨x,hx⟩) j • (b j : P)) = x := by
+/-- A kernel vector with sufficiently expansive component span contradicts
+any invertible block evaluation of the same coefficient matrices. -/
+theorem kernel_impossible {w q k e : ℕ} (hw : 1 ≤ w) (he : 0 < e)
+    (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F) (T : Fin w → P →ₗ[F] Q)
+    (X : Fin w → Matrix (Fin e) (Fin e) F)
+    (f : Fin q → P) (b : Basis (Fin k) F (componentSpace (F := F) f))
+    (hker : ∀ α, ∑ i, ∑ γ, A i α γ • T i (f γ) = 0)
+    (hex : (w-1)*k < finrank F (imageCombination T (fun j => (b j : P))).range) :
+  have hVW : ∀ i, V.map (A i).mulVecLin ≤ W :=
+    fun i => coefficient_image_le_concat A Pmat i
+  have hd := no_shrunk_subspace he A X hX V W hVW
+  have hV : finrank F V = k := by
+  have hW : finrank F W < k := by
+    exact rank_concat_lt A T f b hker hex hw
+/-- The block matrix obtained as a sum of Kronecker products. -/
+def blockMatrix {w q e : ℕ} (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F)
+    (X : Fin w → Matrix (Fin e) (Fin e) F) :
+    Matrix (Fin q × Fin e) (Fin q × Fin e) F := ∑ i, A i ⊗ₖ X i
+lemma blockMatrix_mulVec {w q e : ℕ} (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F)
+    (X : Fin w → Matrix (Fin e) (Fin e) F) (v : Fin e → Fin q → F)
+    (blockMatrix A X).mulVec (fun j => v j.2 j.1) (α,β) = blockEval A X v β α := by
+    (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) F)
+    (X : Fin w → Matrix (Fin e) (Fin e) F) (h : IsUnit (blockMatrix A X)) :
+  have hflat : (fun j : Fin q × Fin e => v j.2 j.1) = (fun j => u j.2 j.1) := by
+/-- The rectangular Taylor tests have no nonzero kernel component family when
+the same coefficients have an invertible matrix witness. -/
+theorem rectangular_kernel_zero (w B M N q e : ℕ) (hw : 1 ≤ w) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
+    (A : Fin w → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) (F K))
+    (X : Fin w → Matrix (Fin e) (Fin e) (F K))
+    (f : Fin q → Fin M → F K)
+    (hf : ∀ α j, N ≤ j.val → f α j = 0)
+    (hker : ∀ α, ∑ i, ∑ γ, A i α γ • testMap M (points i) (f γ) = 0) : f = 0 := by
+  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ : ∃ α, f α ≠ 0 := by
+  let U := componentSpace (F := F K) f
+  let T := fun i => testMap M (points i)
+  let W := (imageCombination T (fun j => (b j : Fin M → F K))).range
+    simpa using finrank_le_of_span_eq_top (span_component_top (F := F K) f)
+  have hU : ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ j : Fin M, N ≤ j.val → x j = 0 := by
+    | mem x hx => obtain ⟨α, rfl⟩ := hx; exact hf α
+    | add x y _ _ hx hy => intro j hj; simp [hx j hj, hy j hj]
+    | smul c x _ hx => intro j hj; simp [hx j hj]
+  have hW : ∀ i, U.map (T i) ≤ W := fun i => component_image_le_range T f b i
+  have hex := small_expansion w B M N hw hN hMN points hp U W hU hW hk (hkq.trans hq)
+  exact kernel_impossible hw he A T X hX f b hker hex

+for complexitylib. The source theorem statements and mathematical arguments are retained.
+/-- The coefficient realization of P_M(K), with its exact degree bound. -/
+@[simp] lemma polynomialMap_coeff (M : ℕ) (x : Fin M → K) (j : Fin M) :
+    (polynomialMap M x).coeff j = x j := by
+  exact congrFun ((Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K M).apply_symm_apply x) j
+    polynomialMap M x ∈ Polynomial.degreeLT K M :=
+lemma polynomialMap_coeff_high (M : ℕ) (x : Fin M → K) (j : ℕ) (hj : M ≤ j) :
+/-- The polynomial subspace corresponding to a subspace of coefficient vectors. -/
+def polynomialSpace {M : ℕ} (V : Submodule K (Fin M → K)) : Submodule K K[X] :=
+lemma finrank_polynomialSpace {M : ℕ} (V : Submodule K (Fin M → K)) :
+    finrank K (polynomialSpace V) = finrank K V :=
+lemma polynomialSpace_bound {M : ℕ} (V : Submodule K (Fin M → K)) :
+    ∀ f ∈ polynomialSpace V, f ≠ 0 → f.natDegree < M := by
+/-- Change coefficient vectors to Taylor coordinates at the specified point. -/
+def taylorCoordinates (M : ℕ) (a : K) : (Fin M → K) ≃ₗ[K] (Fin M → K) :=
+lemma taylorCoordinates_apply (M : ℕ) (a : K) (x : Fin M → K) (j : Fin M) :
+    taylorCoordinates M a x j = (taylor a (polynomialMap M x)).coeff j := rfl
+/-- Reverse the order of a finite coefficient vector. -/
+def reverseCoordinates (M : ℕ) : (Fin M → K) ≃ₗ[K] (Fin M → K) where
+  left_inv := by intro x; funext j; simp
+  right_inv := by intro x; funext j; simp
+/-- Take Taylor coordinates and reverse their order. -/
+def reverseTaylorCoordinates (M : ℕ) (a : K) : (Fin M → K) ≃ₗ[K] (Fin M → K) :=
+/-- The reverse-Taylor test on bounded-degree polynomials multiplies each
+Taylor coefficient by t^a and places it in output degree M-1-a. -/
+def testMap (M : ℕ) (a : K) : (Fin M → F K) →ₗ[F K] (Fin M → F K) :=
+  conjugatedWeight (taylorCoordinates M a) (reverseTaylorCoordinates M a) Fin.val
+lemma testMap_injective (M : ℕ) (a : K) : Function.Injective (testMap M a) :=
+/-- Kernel of the low Taylor projection is precisely the vanishing filtration. -/
+    · have he := congrFun hx (⟨⟨j, hjM⟩, by change j ≤ A; omega⟩ : {i : Fin M // i.val ≤ A})
+    change (lowProjection Fin.val A) (taylorCoordinates M a x) = 0
+    exact hx j.val.val (by have := j.property; omega)
+/-- The output-side low reverse coordinates mean high ordinary Taylor order. -/
+    have hjM : j < M := by omega
+    have hh := hy (Fin.rev ⟨j, hjM⟩) (by simp only [Fin.val_rev]; omega)
+    change taylorCoordinates M a x ((Fin.rev ⟨j, hjM⟩).rev) = 0 at hh
+    refine ⟨reverseTaylorCoordinates M a x, ⟨⟨x, hxV, rfl⟩, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
+      change taylorCoordinates M a x j.rev = 0
+      exact hx j.rev.val (by simp only [Fin.val_rev]; omega)
+    finrank K ((V.map (taylorCoordinates M a).toLinearMap).map (lowProjection Fin.val A)) =
+      Fintype.card {j : Fin h // (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ A} := by
+  rw [map_taylor_projection_kernel, finrank_vanishingFiltration b a hb] at hk
+  have hdim : finrank K V = h := by
+  have hc : Fintype.card {j : Fin h // (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ A} +
+      Fintype.card {j : Fin h // A+1 ≤ (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a} = h := by
+        (fun j : Fin h => (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ A)
+    finrank K ↥((V.map (reverseTaylorCoordinates M a).toLinearMap) ⊓ lowSupported Fin.val A) =
+      Fintype.card {j : Fin h // M-1-A ≤ (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a} := by
+/-- The rank form of order reversal, at every threshold. -/
+    (U W : Submodule (F K) (Fin M → F K)) (hW : U.map (testMap M a) ≤ W)
+    {k l : ℕ} (b : Basis (Fin k) K (polynomialSpace (reducedSubspace U)))
+    Fintype.card {j : Fin k // (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ A} ≤
+      Fintype.card {j : Fin l // M-1-A ≤ (c j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a} := by
+  have hh := conjugated_filtration_rank (taylorCoordinates M a) (reverseTaylorCoordinates M a)
+  rwa [finrank_lowTaylor M a A _ b hb, finrank_reverseTaylor M a A _ c hc] at hh
+/-- Counting all thresholds counts each order with its exact multiplicity. -/
+lemma sum_threshold_counts {h : ℕ} (d : Fin h → ℕ) (L : ℕ) :
+    (∑ A ∈ Finset.range L, Fintype.card {j : Fin h // d j ≤ A}) =
+  have he : (Finset.range L).filter (fun A => d j ≤ A) = Finset.Ico (d j) L := by
+lemma sum_reversed_counts {h : ℕ} (d : Fin h → ℕ) (L : ℕ) (hd : ∀ j, d j ≤ L) :
+    (∑ A ∈ Finset.range L, Fintype.card {j : Fin h // L-A ≤ d j}) = ∑ j, d j := by
+  have he : ∀ A, (fun j : Fin h => L-A ≤ d j) = (fun j : Fin h => L-d j ≤ A) := by
+/-- Summation of order reversal, without selecting incompatible auxiliary
+subspaces: all inequalities concern the fixed filtration of the same W. -/
+    (U W : Submodule (F K) (Fin M → F K)) (hW : U.map (testMap M a) ≤ W)
+    {k l : ℕ} (b : Basis (Fin k) K (polynomialSpace (reducedSubspace U)))
+  have hbd : ∀ j, (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ M-1 := by
+    have hle : (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ (b j : K[X]).natDegree := by
+  have hcd : ∀ j, (c j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ M-1 := by
+    have hle : (c j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a ≤ (c j : K[X]).natDegree := by
+    (fun A _ => order_reversal_counts M a A U W hW b c hb hc)
+  have he : (∑ j, (M-1 - (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a)) +
+      (∑ j, (b j : K[X]).rootMultiplicity a) = k * (M-1) := by
+lemma sum_fin_val_le_square (h : ℕ) : (∑ j : Fin h, j.val) ≤ h*h := by
+    _ ≤ ∑ _j : Fin h, h := Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => Nat.le_of_lt j.isLt
+lemma expansion_numeric (w B M N k l : ℕ) (hw : 1 ≤ w) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
+  have hgap : M-1 = N-1 + 2*w^3*B := by omega
+  have hw' : w-1+1 = w := by omega
+  have hsq : k*k + l*l ≤ w*w*(k*k) := by
+  have hkSq : k*k ≤ B*k := Nat.mul_le_mul_right k hkB
+  have hfinal : w*(k*k + l*l) ≤ w^3*B*k := by
+lemma reduced_degree_bound {M N : ℕ} (U : Submodule (F K) (Fin M → F K))
+    (hU : ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ j : Fin M, N ≤ j.val → x j = 0) :
+    ∀ f ∈ polynomialSpace (reducedSubspace U), f ≠ 0 → f.natDegree < N := by
+  have hr : ∀ y ∈ reducedSubspace U, ∀ j : Fin M, N ≤ j.val → y j = 0 := by
+    have hyy : y ∈ reducedSet U := by
+    simp only [reduce, hU x hx j hj, reduction_zero]
+  · exact (polynomialMap_coeff M x ⟨j, hjM⟩).trans (hr x hx ⟨j, hjM⟩ hj)
+  · exact polynomialMap_coeff_high M x j (Nat.le_of_not_gt hjM)
+/-- Small-subspace expansion in monomial coordinates in a common output space.
+The input subspace is restricted to degrees < N, not changed by padding. -/
+theorem small_expansion [CharZero K] (w B M N : ℕ) (hw : 1 ≤ w) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
+    (hMN : M = N + 2*w^3*B) (points : Fin w → K) (hp : Function.Injective points)
+    (U W : Submodule (F K) (Fin M → F K))
+    (hU : ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ j : Fin M, N ≤ j.val → x j = 0)
+    (hk : 1 ≤ finrank (F K) U) (hkB : finrank (F K) U ≤ B) :
+    (w-1) * finrank (F K) U < finrank (F K) W := by
+  have hVdim : finrank K V = k := by
+  have hZdim : finrank K Z = l := by
+  let b : Basis (Fin k) K V := (Module.finBasis K V).reindex (finCongr hVdim)
+  let c : Basis (Fin l) K Z := (Module.finBasis K Z).reindex (finCongr hZdim)
+  choose be hbe using (fun i : Fin w => exists_echelon_basis_at N V b hV (points i))
+  choose ce hce using (fun i : Fin w => exists_echelon_basis_at M Z c hZ (points i))
+    (fun i _ => order_reversal_sum M (points i) U W (hW i) (be i) (ce i) (hbe i) (hce i))
+  have hWrU := wronskian_order_bound N b points hp be hV hbe
+  have hWrW := wronskian_order_bound M c points hp ce hZ hce
+  exact expansion_numeric w B M N k l hw hN hMN hk hkB

+/-- The Wronskian with derivative orders 0, ..., h - 1. -/
+def wronskian {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {h : ℕ} (f : Fin h → K[X]) : K[X] :=
+  Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => derivative^[i.val] (f j))
+lemma coeff_prod_sum_degrees {K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (s : Finset ι)
+    (f : ι → K[X]) (d : ι → ℕ) (hd : ∀ i ∈ s, (f i).natDegree ≤ d i) :
+    (∏ i ∈ s, f i).coeff (∑ i ∈ s, d i) = ∏ i ∈ s, (f i).coeff (d i) := by
+    rw [Finset.prod_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.prod_insert ha,
+    · rw [ih (fun i hi => hd i (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi))]
+        (Finset.sum_le_sum fun i hi => hd i (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi))
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K[X]) (d : ι → ℕ)
+    (hd : ∀ i j, (A i j).natDegree ≤ d j) :
+    A.det.coeff (∑ j, d j) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => (A i j).coeff (d j)) := by
+  rw [coeff_smul, coeff_prod_sum_degrees _ _ d (fun j _ => hd (g j) j)]
+    {h : ℕ} (f : Fin h → K[X]) (hf : ∀ j, f j ≠ 0)
+  let A : Matrix (Fin h) (Fin h) K[X] :=
+    Matrix.of fun i j => X ^ i.val * derivative^[i.val] (f j)
+      Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => ((f j).natDegree.descFactorial i.val : K) *
+  have hfall : Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => ((f j).natDegree.descFactorial i.val :
+    let p : Fin h → K[X] := fun j => descPochhammer K j.val
+      (fun j : Fin h => ((f j).natDegree : K)) p
+      (fun j => by simp [p]) (fun j => monic_descPochhammer K j.val)
+    have he : (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => ((f j).natDegree.descFactorial i.val : K)) =
+        (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => (p j).eval ((f i).natDegree : K)).transpose := by
+  have htop : A.det.coeff (∑ j, (f j).natDegree) ≠ 0 := by
+    have he : (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => ((f j).natDegree.descFactorial i.val : K) *
+        Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin h => (f j).leadingCoeff *
+      (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => ((f j).natDegree.descFactorial i.val : K))
+    exact mul_ne_zero (Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr fun j _ => leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mpr (hf j)) hfall
+    change Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => (X : K[X]) ^ i.val * derivative^[i.val] (f
+    have hscale := Matrix.det_mul_column (fun i : Fin h => (X : K[X]) ^ i.val)
+      (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => derivative^[i.val] (f j))
+    change (∏ i : Fin h, (X : K[X]) ^ i.val) * wronskian f = 0
+/-- Factoring prescribed powers from the columns keeps track of the first
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K[X]) (d : ι → ℕ)
+    (hd : ∀ i j, X ^ d j ∣ A i j) :
+      A.det = X ^ (∑ j, d j) * B.det ∧
+      (∀ i j, (B i j).coeff 0 = (A i j).coeff (d j)) := by
+  · have hA : A = Matrix.of (fun i j => X ^ d j * (Matrix.of B) i j) := by
+    (f : K[X]) (r : ℕ) : X ^ f.natTrailingDegree ∣ X ^ r * derivative^[r] f := by
+/-- The local order formula at zero, before translation to an arbitrary point.
+The sum of the row numbers is C(h,2). -/
+    {h : ℕ} (f : Fin h → K[X]) (hf : ∀ j, f j ≠ 0)
+  let A : Matrix (Fin h) (Fin h) K[X] :=
+    Matrix.of fun i j => X ^ i.val * derivative^[i.val] (f j)
+    (fun j => (f j).natTrailingDegree) (fun i j => scaled_derivative_order (f j) i.val)
+  have hfall : Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h =>
+    let p : Fin h → K[X] := fun j => descPochhammer K j.val
+      (fun j : Fin h => ((f j).natTrailingDegree : K)) p
+      (fun j => by simp [p]) (fun j => monic_descPochhammer K j.val)
+    have he : (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h =>
+        (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => (p j).eval ((f i).natTrailingDegree : K)).transpose := by
+        Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin h => (f j).trailingCoeff *
+      (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => ((f j).natTrailingDegree.descFactorial i.val : K))
+  have hB0 : B.det ≠ 0 := by intro hz; simp [hz] at hBc
+  have hscale : A.det = X ^ (∑ i : Fin h, i.val) * wronskian f := by
+    have he := Matrix.det_mul_column (fun i : Fin h => (X : K[X]) ^ i.val)
+      (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => derivative^[i.val] (f j))
+    change _ = _ * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin h => derivative^[i.val] (f j))
+  have ho : A.det.natTrailingDegree = ∑ j, (f j).natTrailingDegree := by
+  rw [hscale, mul_comm, natTrailingDegree_mul_X_pow hw] at ho
+/-- Polynomial row reduction, derived rather than assumed: every bounded-degree
+subspace has a basis with distinct largest degrees. -/
+    ∃ (h : ℕ) (f : Fin h → K[X]), LinearIndependent K f ∧
+    by_cases hall : ∀ f ∈ V, f.coeff d = 0
+      have hl := hV f hf hn
+      have hf0 : f ≠ 0 := by intro hz; simp [hz] at hfc
+        have hl := hV f hfV hf0
+      let W : Submodule K K[X] := V ⊓ LinearMap.ker (lcoeff K d)
+      have hW : ∀ g ∈ W, g ≠ 0 → g.natDegree < d := by
+        have hl := hV g hg.1 hn
+      obtain ⟨h, g, hgLI, hgspan, hgdeg⟩ := ih W hW
+      have hgmem : ∀ j, g j ∈ W := by
+      have hnot : f ∉ Submodule.span K (Set.range g) := by
+      refine ⟨h + 1, Fin.cons f g, hgLI.finCons hnot, ?_, ?_⟩
+          let c : K := u.coeff d / f.coeff d
+          have hr : u - c • f ∈ W := by
+          have hsub : W ≤ Submodule.span K (Set.range (Fin.cons f g)) := by
+          have hfj : f ∈ Submodule.span K (Set.range (Fin.cons f g)) :=
+            (hsub hr) ((Submodule.span K (Set.range (Fin.cons f g))).smul_mem c hfj)
+      · have he : (fun i => ((Fin.cons f g : Fin (h + 1) → K[X]) i).natDegree) =
+        have hh := hW (g j) (hgmem j) (hgLI.ne_zero j)
+/-- Fixed-length coefficient reversal is linear, unlike degree-dependent
+def reflectLinearEquiv (K : Type*) [Field K] (N : ℕ) : K[X] ≃ₗ[K] K[X] where
+  map_add' := fun f g => reflect_add f g N
+    simpa only [smul_eq_C_mul, RingHom.id_apply] using reflect_C_mul f c N
+    ∃ (h : ℕ) (f : Fin h → K[X]), LinearIndependent K f ∧
+  have hW : ∀ g ∈ W, g ≠ 0 → g.natDegree < d := by
+    have hf : f ≠ 0 := by intro hz; simp [hz] at hfn
+    have hd := hV f hfV hf
+  obtain ⟨h, g, hgLI, hgspan, hgdeg⟩ := exists_degree_echelon_family d W hW
+  have hgW : ∀ i, g i ∈ W := by
+  refine ⟨h, fun i => e.symm (g i), hgLI.map' e.symm.toLinearMap (by simp), ?_, ?_⟩
+  · have hs : Submodule.span K (Set.range (fun i => e.symm (g i))) =
+    have hi := hW (g i) (hgW i) (hgLI.ne_zero i)

+into `t` pairs. In each pair, every resource reads the suffix of the copy that uses it

+resource yield `2 t` copies of `f`, at an overhead linear in `t`.
+The routing and decoding gates are disjunctive normal forms of the two prefixes in a pair, so
+their number is polynomial in `2 ^ p` and `w`. This is far from optimal, but it is negligible in
+the recursion of `Uhlig`, where `2 ^ p` is polynomial in the input length.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The transport supplies observations of Git and a clock. This module decides which board updates
+are permitted. Publication, pending-token persistence, checkout and validation remain IO duties.
+Agent identities describe cooperating sessions; they are not an authentication mechanism.
+/-- Exact Git observations are supplied by the IO shell, never inferred from branch names. -/
+  | plan (epic : EpicId) (goal : String) (paths : List String) (dependencies : List EpicId)
+  | submit (epic : EpicId) (snapshot : Snapshot) (changedPaths : List String) (summary : String)
+/-- A landing must publish both refs atomically and guard the exact old main OID. -/
+private def check (condition : Prop) [Decidable condition] (message : String) : Except String Unit :=
+  if condition then pure () else throw message
+  let lower (c : Char) := decide ('a' ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 'z')
+  let digit (c : Char) := decide ('0' ≤ c ∧ c ≤ '9')
+    chars.all (fun c => lower c || digit c || c == '-')
+  scopeContains left right || scopeContains right left
+private def findAgent (state : State) (id : AgentId) : Except String Agent :=
+  match state.agents.find? (fun a => a.actor.agent == id) with
+private def findEpic (state : State) (id : EpicId) : Except String Epic :=
+  match state.epics.find? (fun e => e.id == id) with
+  if state.agents.any (fun a => a.actor.agent == agent.actor.agent) then
+    { state with agents := state.agents.map fun a =>
+        if a.actor.agent == agent.actor.agent then agent else a }
+  if state.epics.any (fun e => e.id == epic.id) then
+    { state with epics := state.epics.map fun e => if e.id == epic.id then epic else e }
+private def validate (state : State) : Except String Unit := do
+  check (agents.eraseDups.length == agents.length) "Duplicate agent IDs in board"
+  check (epics.eraseDups.length == epics.length) "Duplicate epic IDs in board"
+private def actor (ctx : Context) (state : State) : Except String Agent := do
+  lease.holder == ctx.actor && ctx.heldTokens.contains lease.token && decide (ctx.now ≤ lease.expires)
+theorem holds_not_expired {ctx : Context} {lease : Lease} (h : holds ctx lease = true) :
+private def requireHeld (ctx : Context) (lease : Option Lease) : Except String Lease := do
+  let some lease := lease | throw "Claim is absent"
+  check (holds ctx lease) "Claim generation is absent, expired or replaced"
+private def coordinator (ctx : Context) (state : State) : Except String Agent := do
+private def checkToken (ctx : Context) (token : Token) : Except String Unit := do
+    "Persist the pending claim token locally before publication"
+private def makeLease (ctx : Context) (agent : Agent) (token : Token) : Lease :=
+  { holder := ctx.actor, token, expires := ctx.now + agent.leaseSeconds }
+private def replaceable (ctx : Context) (lease : Option Lease) (replace : Bool) : Bool :=
+  lease.all (fun l => replace || decide (l.expires + grace < ctx.now))
+private def acquire (ctx : Context) (lease : Option Lease) : Bool :=
+  lease.all (fun l => holds ctx l || decide (l.expires + grace < ctx.now))
+  epic.dependencies.all fun id => state.epics.any fun e =>
+    e.id == id && match e.phase with | .merged _ => true | _ => false
+private def workOf (epic : Epic) : Except String Work :=
+  | _ => throw "Epic is not assigned for implementation; reopen a submission before editing"
+private def submissionOf (epic : Epic) : Except String Submission :=
+  if state.integration.any (fun i => i.epic == epic) then { state with integration := none }
+private def renewLease (ctx : Context) (expires : Nat) (lease : Lease) : Lease :=
+  if holds ctx lease then { lease with expires } else lease
+private def renewSlot (ctx : Context) (expires : Nat) : ReviewSlot → ReviewSlot
+  | .active lease report blocked => .active (renewLease ctx expires lease) report blocked
+private def renewEpic (ctx : Context) (expires : Nat) (epic : Epic) : Epic :=
+    let work := { work with lease := work.lease.map (renewLease ctx expires) }
+    let work := { s.work with lease := s.work.lease.map (renewLease ctx expires) }
+    { epic with phase := .submitted { s with work, reviews } }
+  let .finished api := s.reviews.api | throw "Missing current API approval"
+  let .finished correctness := s.reviews.correctness | throw "Missing current correctness approval"
+    "Reviews concern a different base or head"
+    "Reviews must be independent of every author and each other"
+  check (dependenciesDone state epic) "A dependency has not landed"
+  check (ctx.main == some s.snapshot.base) "Main moved; reopen, merge main and obtain new reviews"
+private def result (state : State) (message : String) : Outcome := { state, message }
+/-- Apply one command to a freshly fetched board. IO must retry this transition on a new board
+after a rejected push, retaining its pending identity and generation tokens. -/
+def apply (ctx : Context) (state : State) (command : Command) : Except String Outcome := do
+    check (300 ≤ seconds ∧ seconds ≤ 86400) "Lease duration must be 300 to 86400 seconds"
+    if let some previous := state.agents.find? (fun a => a.actor.agent == ctx.actor.agent) then
+      if previous.actor == ctx.actor && previous.role == role && previous.leaseSeconds == seconds &&
+        "Agent name is in use; only explicit expired takeover is permitted"
+      check (previous.actor != ctx.actor) "Expired takeover requires a new session identity"
+        "A coordinator is already active; takeover must be explicit"
+      check (state.coordinator.isNone || takeover) "Coordinator takeover must be explicit"
+      check (state.coordinator.all (fun l => l.holder != ctx.actor && l.token != token))
+        "Coordinator takeover requires a new identity and generation"
+      return result { state with coordinator := some (makeLease ctx agent token) } "Coordinator joined"
+    let state := putAgent state { agent with expires }
+      integration := state.integration.map fun i => { i with lease := renewLease ctx expires i.lease }
+      epics := state.epics.map (renewEpic ctx expires) } "Heartbeat renewed held generations"
+    check (!state.epics.any (fun e => e.id == id)) "Epic already exists"
+    check (!goal.isEmpty && !paths.isEmpty && paths.all validScope) "Goal and canonical scopes required"
+    check (dependencies.all fun d => state.epics.any (fun e => e.id == d)) "Unknown dependency"
+        | _ => throw "Reopen a submission before changing its implementation assignment"
+      check (replaceable ctx (previous.bind (·.lease)) replace) "Work claim is live; explicitly replace it"
+      check (state.epics.all fun other => other.id == id || !occupiesScope other ||
+        !(epic.paths.any fun a => other.paths.any (scopesOverlap a))) "Scopes overlap an assigned epic"
+        | some work => if work.assignee == worker then work.resume else some work.branch
+      let work : Work := { assignee := worker, branch, resume }
+      return result (putEpic state { epic with phase := .working work }) "Implementation assigned"
+      check (!epic.authors.contains worker) "Contributing authors cannot review this epic"
+      check (slotAgent (s.reviews.get (otherKind rk)) != some worker) "Use two distinct reviewers"
+      check (replaceable ctx (slotLease (s.reviews.get rk)) replace) "Review claim is live; explicitly replace it"
+      let s := { s with reviews := s.reviews.set rk (.assigned worker) }
+      return result (putEpic state { epic with phase := .submitted s }) "Review assigned"
+    let lease := makeLease ctx agent token
+      check (work.assignee == ctx.actor.agent) "Implementation is assigned to another worker"
+      check (acquire ctx work.lease) "Another live generation holds the implementation"
+      check (dependenciesDone state epic) "A dependency has not landed"
+      let work := { work with lease := some lease }
+      let authors := if epic.authors.contains ctx.actor.agent then epic.authors
+        state := putEpic state { epic with authors, phase := .working work }
+      check (slotAgent (s.reviews.get rk) == some ctx.actor.agent) "Review is assigned to another worker"
+      check (!epic.authors.contains ctx.actor.agent) "Authors cannot review their work"
+      check (acquire ctx (slotLease (s.reviews.get rk))) "Another live generation holds the review"
+      let reviews := s.reviews.set rk (.active lease "" false)
+        state := putEpic state { epic with phase := .submitted { s with reviews } }
+        message := "Review started; any prior approval is revoked"
+      let work := { work with report := text, blocked }
+      return result (putEpic state { epic with phase := .working work }) "Implementation report recorded"
+      let s := { s with reviews := s.reviews.set rk (.active lease text blocked) }
+      return result (putEpic state { epic with phase := .submitted s }) "Review report recorded"
+      | _ => throw "Only assigned or submitted work can be reopened"
+    let work := { work with lease := none, report := reason, blocked := false }
+    let epic := { epic with report := reason, phase := .working work }
+    return result (clearIntegration (putEpic state epic) id) "Reopened; reviews and integration revoked"
+      | .merged _ => throw "Completed work remains in the journal"
+    let epic := { epic with resume, report := reason, phase := .unassigned }
+    return result (clearIntegration (putEpic state epic) id) "Assignment released; authors and resume ref preserved"
+    check (ctx.cleanHead == some snapshot.head && ctx.branchHead == some snapshot.head)
+      "Clean worktree and pushed assigned branch must match the submitted head"
+      ctx.ancestry.contains snapshot) "Merge the observed current main before submission"
+      epic.paths.any (fun scope => scopeContains scope path)) "Change exceeds assigned paths"
+    let s : Submission := { work, snapshot, summary }
+    return result (putEpic state { epic with phase := .submitted s }) "Immutable snapshot submitted"
+    check (ctx.cleanHead == some snapshot.head) "Review worktree does not match the snapshot"
+    check (!epic.authors.contains ctx.actor.agent) "Authors cannot review their work"
+    let review : Review := { reviewer := ctx.actor, snapshot, verdict, note, time := ctx.now }
+    let s := { s with reviews := s.reviews.set rk (.finished review) }
+    return result (putEpic state { epic with phase := .submitted s }) "Review evidence recorded"
+    if let some previous := state.integration then
+      if previous.epic == id && previous.snapshot == s.snapshot && holds ctx previous.lease then
+        return result state "Integration already reserved by this held generation"
+      check (previous.lease.expires + grace < ctx.now) "Integration is reserved; finish or cancel it"
+    return result { state with integration := some integration } "Integration reserved"
+    let some integration := state.integration | throw "Integration reservation is absent"
+    check (holds ctx integration.lease) "Integration generation was lost"
+    check (integration.epic == id && integration.snapshot == snapshot) "Integration reservation changed"
+    let (s, api, correctness) ← approved ctx state epic
+      ctx.ancestry.contains snapshot) "Validated clean head or fast-forward evidence differs"
+    let state := putEpic state { epic with phase := .merged completion }
+    if let some integration := state.integration then
+      check (holds ctx integration.lease || decide (integration.lease.expires + grace < ctx.now))
+    return result { state with integration := none } "Integration cancelled; approvals preserved"
