+/-! Worktree-local identities and the IO interpretation of the typed protocol.
+Pending claims are durable before publication; retries can recognize an accepted
+claim after a lost response. Git observations are refreshed inside each transaction. -/
+def readJson {α : Type} [FromJson α] (path : System.FilePath) : IO α := do
+  let json ← IO.ofExcept <| Json.parse (← IO.FS.readFile path)
+def writeJson {α : Type} [ToJson α] (path : System.FilePath) (value : α) : IO Unit := do
+/-- Serialize mutating CLI commands in one worktree, including local identity updates. -/
+def withLock {α : Type} (repo : Repository) (action : IO α) : IO α := do
+    throw <| IO.userError s!"Another command holds {lock}. If interrupted, check its owner PID before removing the lock."
+    throw <| IO.userError "Join from the primary checkout, then use the printed linked worktree"
+    throw <| IO.userError "Run join first, then work inside the printed worktree"
+def claim (repo : Repository) (key : String) : IO (Identity × Token) := do
+  let token ← match self.pending.find? (·.key == key) with
+      self := { self with pending := { key, token } :: self.pending }
+def finishClaim (repo : Repository) (key : String) (token : Token) : IO Unit := do
+  let some (_, json) ← repo.readBoard | throw <| IO.userError "Initialize the board first"
+  let state : State ← IO.ofExcept <| fromJson? json
+  unless state.version == 1 do throw <| IO.userError "Unsupported coordination schema"
+def getEpic (state : State) (id : EpicId) : IO Epic := do
+  let some epic := state.epics.find? (·.id == id) | throw <| IO.userError "Unknown epic"
+def submission (state : State) (id : EpicId) : IO Submission := do
+  | _ => throw <| IO.userError "Epic has no submitted snapshot"
+def requiredRef (repo : Repository) (ref : String) : IO String := do
+  let some head ← repo.fetch ref | throw <| IO.userError s!"Missing ref {ref}"
+    let .working work := task.phase | throw <| IO.userError "Epic is not being implemented"
+    ctx := { ctx with cleanHead := some snapshot.head }
+    ctx := { ctx with main := some ⟨(← requiredRef repo mainRef)⟩ }
+/-- Execute one typed command, rerunning observations and pure checks on every retry. -/
+def dispatch (repo : Repository) (self : Identity) (cmd : Command) : IO Outcome := do
+  discard <| repo.update ({} : State) (reprStr cmd) (fun state => do
+    let outcome ← IO.ofExcept <| Coordination.apply (← context repo self state cmd) state cmd
+      | .atomicLanding s => some { base := s.base.value, head := s.head.value : Landing }
+  let some outcome ← result.get | throw <| IO.userError "Transaction produced no result"
+def checkout (repo : Repository) (action : Checkout) : IO Unit := do
+      throw <| IO.userError "Submitted commit is no longer on its work branch"
+    let resumeHead ← resume.mapM fun prior => requiredRef repo ("refs/heads/" ++ prior)
+    let head ← if found.exitCode == 0 then pure ("refs/heads/" ++ branch) else do
+    if let some tip := resumeHead then
+        throw <| IO.userError s!"Existing {branch} omits its continuation branch; merge {resume.getD ""} before restarting"
+def run (repo : Repository) (cmd : Command) : IO Outcome := do
+  let outcome ← dispatch repo (← identity repo) cmd
+  if let some action := outcome.checkout then checkout repo action
+def start (repo : Repository) (epic : EpicId) (kind : AssignmentKind) : IO Outcome := do
+  let outcome ← dispatch repo self (.start epic kind token)
+  if let some action := outcome.checkout then checkout repo action
+/-- Stage the identity before joining; a rejected takeover leaves the live identity intact. -/
+def join (repo : Repository) (name : AgentId) (role : Role) (here takeover : Bool)
+    throw <| IO.userError "Lease duration must be 300 to 86400 seconds"
+  -- Reuse the protocol's identifier check before constructing paths or branch names.
+  unless !name.value.isEmpty && name.value.toList.all (fun c => c.isLower || c.isDigit || c == '-')
+    throw <| IO.userError "Names must start with a lowercase letter and contain letters, digits or hyphens"
+  let worker ← if here then pure repo else do
+    unless (← common repo) == (← common worker) do
+      throw <| IO.userError "Destination belongs to a different repository"
+    let mut candidate : Option Identity ← if ← pendingPath.pathExists then
+      some <$> readJson pendingPath else pure none
+    -- A lost response followed by a long outage must not make --takeover unrecoverable.
+    if let some self := candidate then
+          if agent.actor != self.actor || (← now) > agent.expires + 60 then candidate := none
+        if self.actor.agent == name && self.role == role && self.leaseSeconds == leaseSeconds then
+        else throw <| IO.userError "Retry the pending join with the same name, role and duration"
+          throw <| IO.userError "This worktree has an identity; use heartbeat, or takeover after expiry"
+    let some token := self.tokens.head? | throw <| IO.userError "Pending identity has no join token"
+    discard <| dispatch worker self (.join role leaseSeconds token takeover)
+def ready (repo : Repository) (epic : EpicId) (summary : String) : IO Outcome := do
+  run repo (.submit epic { base := ⟨base⟩, head := ⟨head⟩ } paths summary)
+/-- Run validation with inherited output, renewing the lease while the child runs. -/
+def validate (repo : Repository) (cmd : String) (args : Array String) : IO Unit := do
+  let child ← IO.Process.spawn { cmd, args, cwd := repo.root }
+    if let some code ← child.tryWait then
+        throw <| IO.userError s!"{cmd} failed; no code was published. Use cancel if abandoning integration."
+def land (repo : Repository) (epic : EpicId) : IO Outcome := do
+  let reserved ← dispatch repo self (.reserve epic token)
+  run repo (.land epic target.snapshot "scripts/check.sh: six gates passed; coordination tests: passed")

+Protocol tests use explicit logical time. Integration tests use disposable local bare Git
+repositories; they never invoke project validation or contact a hosting service.
+private def initializeBoard (repository : Git.Repository) : IO Unit := do
+  discard <| repository.update ({} : Journal) "initialize tests" (fun state => pure (state, none)) true
+private def journal (repository : Git.Repository) : IO Journal := do
+  let some (_, value) ← repository.readBoard | throw <| IO.userError "Missing board"
+private def testJournalAndFetch : IO Unit := withFixture fun fixture => do
+  check ((← repository.fetch Git.boardRef false).isNone) "Missing optional board must be none"
+  discard <| repository.update ({} : Journal) "unchanged" (fun state => pure (state, none))
+  check ((← fixture.ref Git.boardRef) == before) "No-op update created a journal commit"
+  check ((← repository.fetch Git.mainRef) == some fixture.base) "Fetched wrong main"
+  check ((← journal repository) == {}) "Initial journal did not round-trip"
+private def testRawPathsAndRename : IO Unit := withFixture fun fixture => do
+  for path in paths do discard <| fixture.commit path "unusual filename\n"
+    check (changed.contains path) s!"Path was lost or trimmed: {repr path}; got {repr changed}"
+private def testCallerPreservation : IO Unit := withFixture fun fixture => do
+  discard <| repository.update ({} : Journal) "dirty caller" fun state =>
+private def testCleanPreservesIndex : IO Unit := withFixture fun fixture => do
+  -- Rewriting identical bytes changes stat data, so ordinary git status refreshes the index.
+  check ((← IO.FS.readBinFile (gitdir / "index")) == before) "Cleanliness check rewrote caller index"
+  check ((← IO.FS.readBinFile (gitdir / "index")) == dirtyBefore) "Rejected dirty check rewrote caller index"
+private def testAtomicLanding : IO Unit := withFixture fun fixture => do
+  let result ← repository.update ({} : Journal) "atomic landing" fun state =>
+    pure ({state with landed := true}, some {base := fixture.base, head})
+  check result.landed "Landing did not return committed state"
+  check ((← fixture.ref Git.mainRef) == head) "Atomic landing did not publish main"
+  check (← journal repository).landed "Atomic landing did not publish board"
+    "Journal did not advance from its exact parent"
+private def testAncestorRace : IO Unit := withFixture fun fixture => do
+  let racing := {repository with execute := fun args input => do
+    if args[0]? == some "push" && args.contains "--atomic" && !(← fired.get) then
+      discard <| git fixture.origin #["update-ref", Git.mainRef, intermediate, fixture.base]
+  expectError (racing.update ({} : Journal) "racing atomic landing" fun state =>
+    pure ({state with landed := true}, some {base := fixture.base, head})) "Push rejected"
+  check (← fired.get) "Ancestor race hook did not run"
+  check (← repository.ancestor intermediate head) "Race main was not an ancestor of candidate"
+  check ((← fixture.ref Git.mainRef) == intermediate) "Race main was overwritten"
+  check ((← fixture.ref Git.boardRef) == before) "Failed atomic landing advanced board"
+  check (!(← journal repository).landed) "Failed atomic landing marked work merged"
+private def testNonFastForwardRefused : IO Unit := withFixture fun fixture => do
+    pure ({state with landed := true}, some {base := head, head := fixture.base})) "fast-forward"

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A function has at most `T` changes when every nondecreasing sequence has at most `T`
+adjacent positions with unequal outputs. Sorting a finite set by a key and splitting it into
+consecutive groups yields a large group on which most functions in a finite family are constant.
+The key may have ties, and the size bound uses natural-number division.
+* `Function.ChangesAtMost`: a uniform bound on changes along nondecreasing sequences.
+* `Function.ChangesAtMost.exists_sorted_group`: a group of at least `|P| / G` points,
+  with at most `T |Q| / G` exceptional functions.
+/-- Every nondecreasing sequence has at most `T` adjacent changes under `f`. -/
+def ChangesAtMost [Preorder α] (f : α → β) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∀ z : ℕ → α, Monotone z → ∀ S : Finset ℕ,
+    (∀ i ∈ S, f (z i) ≠ f (z (i + 1))) → S.card ≤ T
+/-- Increasing a change bound preserves it. -/
+theorem ChangesAtMost.mono [Preorder α] {f : α → β} {T T' : ℕ}
+    (h : ChangesAtMost f T) (hT : T ≤ T') : ChangesAtMost f T' :=
+  fun z hz S hS => (h z hz S hS).trans hT
+/-- Monotone precomposition preserves a change bound. -/

+/-- The nondecreasing order of a finite set along a linearly ordered key. -/
+private theorem exists_sorted_list {ι : Type*} (P : Finset ι) (key : ι → α) :
+    ∃ l : List ι, l.length = P.card ∧ l.Nodup ∧ (∀ a, a ∈ l ↔ a ∈ P) ∧

+groups of `⌊|P| / G⌋` elements. If every `Ψ q` changes at most `T` times, some group `P'` is
+such that the functions `p ↦ Ψ q (key p)` are constant on `P'` for every `q ∈ Q` outside a set
+theorem ChangesAtMost.exists_sorted_group {ι κ : Type*} (P : Finset ι) (Q : Finset κ) (key : ι → α)

+    ∃ P' ⊆ P, ∃ Qbad ⊆ Q, P.card / G ≤ P'.card ∧ G * Qbad.card ≤ T * Q.card ∧
+      ∀ q ∈ Q, q ∉ Qbad → ∀ p ∈ P', ∀ p' ∈ P', Ψ q (key p) = Ψ q (key p') := by

+  let z : ℕ → α := fun i => key (l[min i (N - 1)]'(by omega))
+  let grp : ℕ → Finset ι := fun g => ((l.drop (g * L)).take L).toFinset
+  have hgrp_mem : ∀ g < G, ∀ p ∈ grp g, ∃ j < L, key p = z (g * L + j) := by
+    have hp' : p ∈ (l.drop (g * L)).take L := List.mem_toFinset.mp hp

+      have : (g + 1) * L ≤ G * L := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
+  have hgrp_sub : ∀ g, grp g ⊆ P := by
+  have hgrp_card : ∀ g < G, (grp g).card = L := by
+    have : (g + 1) * L ≤ G * L := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
+  -- Bad groups for each function, and double counting.
+  let bad : ℕ → κ → Prop := fun g q =>

+    fun q hq => card_nonconstant_groups_le (hΨ q hq) hz L G
+  have hsum : ∑ g ∈ Finset.range G, (Q.filter fun q => bad g q).card ≤ T * Q.card := by
+    calc ∑ q ∈ Q, ((Finset.range G).filter fun g => bad g q).card
+      _ = T * Q.card := by rw [Finset.sum_const, Nat.nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm]

+    (f := fun g => G * (Q.filter fun q => bad g q).card) (g := fun _ => T * Q.card)
+  have hgG : g < G := Finset.mem_range.mp hg
+  refine ⟨grp g, hgrp_sub g, Q.filter fun q => bad g q, Finset.filter_subset _ _,

+  exact hnot ⟨j, hj, j', hj', hne⟩

+# Shared OR lookup over dynamic records
+Sources supply keys and value fields; queries supply keys. One source array serves every query,
+including repeated queries. A query receives the bitwise OR of all matching source values;
+missing keys receive zero. The circuit sorts once and reverses saved swaps on the answer fields,
+so it needs neither request identifiers nor a second sort.
+Inputs are ordinary variables or Boolean constants, using the existing `substitute` interface.
+All constants and negations are charged. Input preparation uses two shared constant gates even
+when unused. Sources, queries, keys, and values may all be empty. Padding records are destinations
+and cannot introduce a spurious source. These gate bounds do not certify constructor runtime.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.batchOrCircuit`: shared OR lookup with automatic padding.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.batchOrCircuit.withPadding`: the same construction with supplied padding.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.size_batchOrCircuit_le`: a factored bound for canonical padding.
+variable {input sources requests k v padding d : ℕ}
+variable (sourceKeys : Fin sources → Fin k → Fin input ⊕ Bool)
+  (sourceValues : Fin sources → Fin v → Fin input ⊕ Bool)
+  (queryKeys : Fin requests → Fin k → Fin input ⊕ Bool)
+/-- Symbolic request records, source records, and padding destinations. -/

+/-- Flatten symbolic records into variables and constants for the padded network. -/
+    Fin (BitonicSort.arity d * (k + 1 + v)) → Fin input ⊕ Bool :=
+  fun i => let jb := finProdFinEquiv.symm i
+    rows sourceKeys sourceValues queryKeys (Fin.cast h.symm jb.1) jb.2
+/-- Interpret the record layout on the circuit input. -/
+private def layout (h : requests + (sources + padding) = BitonicSort.arity d)
+  substitute (substitution sourceKeys sourceValues queryKeys h) x
+/-- The original position of a request in the padded layout. -/
+/-- The original position of a source in the padded layout. -/
+private def sourceIndex (h : requests + (sources + padding) = BitonicSort.arity d)
+private theorem layout_apply (h : requests + (sources + padding) = BitonicSort.arity d)
+    (x : BitString input) (i : Fin (requests + (sources + padding))) (bit : Fin (k + 1 + v)) :
+    directProductInput (layout sourceKeys sourceValues queryKeys h x) (Fin.cast h i) bit =
+      (rows sourceKeys sourceValues queryKeys i bit).elim x id := by
+private theorem request_key (h : requests + (sources + padding) = BitonicSort.arity d)
+    header (layout sourceKeys sourceValues queryKeys h x) (requestIndex h request) ∘ Fin.castSucc =

+  simp [value, Function.comp_def, sourceIndex, layout_apply, rows, substitute]

+variable (sourceKeys : Fin sources → Fin k → Fin input ⊕ Bool)
+  (sourceValues : Fin sources → Fin v → Fin input ⊕ Bool)
+  (queryKeys : Fin requests → Fin k → Fin input ⊕ Bool)
+/-- Look up bitwise ORs of dynamic source values with automatic padding.
+Source and query keys may repeat, and absent keys return false. -/

+/-- An output bit is true exactly when a matching source bit is true. -/
+theorem eval_batchOrCircuit_iff (x : BitString input) (request : Fin requests) (bit : Fin v) :
+      ∃ source, substitute (sourceKeys source) x = substitute (queryKeys request) x ∧
+  eval_withPadding_iff sourceKeys sourceValues queryKeys (add_padding_eq_arity requests sources)

+# Duplicate flags with shared comparisons and saved swaps
+A sorted array has a repeated key at a position exactly when that key equals a neighbor.
+`adjacentDuplicateCircuit` computes each adjacent equality once and shares it between the

+which is false, for its missing successor. The empty array uses no gates.
+`duplicateFlagsCircuit` accepts an arbitrary array of `2 ^ d` records. It sorts by selected key
+coordinates, computes the flags, then reverses the saved swaps on the flags alone. Outputs refer
+to the original positions, including when complete records repeat. No record identifiers or
+second sort are needed. Header and payload bits can be retained by free input wiring.
+Costs include constants and negations. Gate counts do not certify construction runtime.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.duplicateFlagsCircuit`: duplicate flags in original input order.
+[K. E. Batcher, *Sorting Networks and Their Applications*][Batcher1968].

+    ((Formula.input i).or (Formula.input (if h : i.val + 1 < count then ⟨i.val + 1, h⟩
+/-- On sorted keys, adjacent equality detects every repeated key. -/

+      ∃ j, j ≠ i ∧ x ∘ key j = x ∘ key i := by
+  rw [show (∃ j, j ≠ i ∧ x ∘ key j = x ∘ key i) ↔
+    ∃ j, j ≠ i ∧ toLex (x ∘ key j) = toLex (x ∘ key i) by simp only [toLex_inj],
+/-- Sharing the equality outputs adds exactly one OR gate per record. -/

+    exact hn ((hu j hj).trans (hu i rfl).symm)
+    exact hn ⟨i, rfl, fun j hj => by
+/-- Regard a vector of flags as an array of one-bit records. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Batched table lookup with one sort
+A fixed table is hardwired into one source record per address. Query addresses are input wires;
+queries and padding are destination records. Sort once, broadcast matching source values, and
+reverse the saved sorting decisions on the values alone. Selecting the original request positions
+then returns the answers in input order, including repeated addresses. No request identifiers or
+restoration ranks are used. Empty keys, empty values, and zero requests are allowed.
+The circuit uses CSLib's native `Circuit` representation. Input preparation shares exactly two
+constant gates, including when one or both are unused. The exact weighted cost and total gate count
+include these constants; the polynomial gate bound does not certify constructor runtime.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.batchLookupCircuit`: lookup with inferred sorting depth and padding.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.batchLookupCircuit.withPadding`: lookup with a supplied record count.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.eval_batchLookupCircuit`: arbitrary repeated queries are answered exactly.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.size_batchLookupCircuit_le`: a bound linear in table size plus request
+  count and field width, and quadratic in sorting depth.
+[K. E. Batcher, *Sorting Networks and Their Applications*][Batcher1968].

+    directProductInput (layout table h x) (Fin.cast h i) bit = (rows table i bit).elim x id := by

+# Sorting records by a computed key
+Compute each record's key once, sort the enriched records, and discard the temporary
+keys. The same record layout can therefore support successive sorts with different keys.
+Keys are ordered lexicographically, with coordinate zero most significant. Complete records,
+including duplicates and payload, are preserved; sorting need not be stable.

+      Fin.append (key.eval interpretation (directProductInput x j)) (directProductInput x j) := by

+        ((keyedSortCircuit.pack key depth).eval interpretation x)) j ∘ Fin.natAdd k := by

+Both total gate count and arbitrary weighted cost add exactly.

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The comparator reads key coordinates in selector order, with coordinate zero most
+significant. Its formula has `6 * k + 1` gates for `k` selected input bits. Compare-exchange

+three gates per output bit. Ties preserve the input order, including payload bits outside the key.
+For two nonempty records of width `r`, the circuit uses exactly `6 * k + 6 * r + 2` gates,
+including constants and negations. Empty records use no gates. Key positions may be arbitrary;

+Inputs and outputs are arranged in consecutive blocks. Replication preserves sharing between
+the outputs of each copy, and multiplies both gate count and arbitrary weighted cost exactly.

+/-- Apply a scalar function independently to each input block. -/
+def directProduct (f : (Fin n → U) → U) (k : ℕ) : (Fin (k * n) → U) → Fin k → U :=

+/-- Replication computes the blockwise application of the original circuit. -/

+/-- Replication multiplies the gate count exactly. -/

+  pi fun j => c.comp (Circuit.wiring σ fun i => finProdFinEquiv (j, i))

+large unary indices. The alphabet decoder and block width are fixed before the runtime graph.

+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.edgeVerifier_accepts`: the exact constraint checked for every proof.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.accepts_proofOfLabels`: a satisfying labelling gives a finite proof.

+# From efficient gap reductions to PCP verifiers
+An efficient reduction to well-formed constraint graphs with a fixed positive gap gives a
+polynomial-time verifier with logarithmic randomness and constantly many queries. The verifier
+constructs the graph before performing fixed many local checks. Its cost includes that complete
+construction, every sampled edge, all copied queries, and every verdict.
+The alphabet has a fixed-width binary representation with a decoding left inverse. Completeness
+packs one block per declared vertex; soundness interprets every proof, even a short one, as a
+consistent labelling. Random strings of arbitrary length remain covered by the cost certificate.

+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.mem_PCP_of_gapReduction`: a positive-gap reduction gives membership in
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09], Chapter 11.
+* [I. Dinur, *The PCP theorem by gap amplification*][Dinur2007]
+/-- Construct a constraint graph and perform a fixed number of independent local checks. -/
+def reductionVerifier (graph : Input → Graph C) (width repeats : ℕ)
+    (decode : (Fin width → Bool) → α) (eval : C → α → α → Bool) : PCPVerifier Input :=
+  let check := repeatedEdgeVerifier width repeats decode eval
+    queries := fun p => check.queries (graph p.1, p.2)
+    verdict := fun p => check.verdict ((graph p.1.1, p.1.2), p.2) }
+/-- Graph construction and each verifier component compose through their ordinary certificates. -/
+theorem polyTime_reductionVerifier {graph : Input → Graph C} (width repeats : ℕ)
+    {input : Input ↪ List Bool} {enc : C ↪ List Bool} {alphabet : α ↪ List Bool}
+    (heval : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : C × α × α => eval p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+    (reductionVerifier graph width repeats decode eval).PolyTime input := by
+  obtain ⟨hcoins, hqueries, hverdict⟩ := polyTime_repeatedEdgeVerifier width repeats decode heval

+    (encode : α → Fin width → Bool) (decode : (Fin width → Bool) → α)

+# Independent repetitions of the encoded edge verifier
+Disjoint coin blocks select independent edges. Every round reads the same number of proof bits,
+so its answer block has an explicit fixed offset. All rounds must accept. The repetition count
+and alphabet width are fixed before the runtime graph.

+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.repeatedEdgeVerifier_accepts`: each answer block preserves its check.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09], Chapter 11.
+/-- Run fixed many edge checks on disjoint coin and answer blocks, accepting their conjunction. -/

+    verdict := fun p => (List.range repeats).all fun i =>

+    (eval : C → α → α → Bool) (g : Graph C) :
+    (rows : Fin count → List Bool) (hlen : ∀ i, (rows i).length = width) (i : Fin count) :

+  let bits := fun i => BitString.ofList width (rows i)
+  have hrows : (fun i => List.ofFn (bits i)) = rows := by
+  change List.ofFn (BitString.blocksEquiv (BitString.blocksEquiv.symm bits) i) = rows i
+    (rows : ℕ → List Bool) (hlen : ∀ i < count, (rows i).length = width) (i : Fin count) :
+    BitString.listRow width i.val ((List.range count).flatMap rows) = rows i := by
+  have hmap : (List.range count).map rows = List.ofFn (fun i : Fin count => rows i.val) := by
+  have hflat : ((List.range count).map rows).flatten = (List.range count).flatMap rows := by

+/-- Repeated checks retain a fixed answer block even when a selected edge is padding. -/

lines: +Copyright (c) 2026 Bolton Bailey, Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.

+# An executable constant-gap reduction from SAT
+Split clauses to width three, compact variable names, construct the initial constraint graph,
+normalize its alphabet by composition, and apply logarithmically many arithmetic amplification
+rounds. Every stage is a functional program. The expander and all finite enumerations are fixed
+constructively; the enormous fixed parameters make this an asymptotic construction.
+The reduction accepts arbitrary CNF formulas and preserves satisfiability. Unsatisfiable inputs
+produce graphs above the fixed positive gap, with all endpoints in the declared vertex range.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.isPolyTime_gapGraph`: a uniform certificate for the complete reduction.
+* [I. Dinur, *The PCP theorem by gap amplification*][Dinur2007]
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Chapter 22][AroraBarak09]
+/-- Split, compact, normalize, and amplify a CNF formula using the concrete arithmetic family. -/
+/-- The whole reduction is polynomial-time in any efficiently computed input formula. Variable
+names retain their supplied encoding until compaction, including sparse or repeated names. -/
+    {enc : V ↪ List Bool} {input : Input ↪ List Bool} {formula : Input → CNF V}
+/-- Every output edge has endpoints in the declared finite vertex range. -/
+/-- The complete construction preserves satisfiability for arbitrary clause lengths. -/
+/-- Every unsatisfiable formula produces a graph above the fixed arithmetic gap. -/

+# Extending an expanding family to every seed length
+Choose the largest parameter whose seed fits the input, run that family member on a prefix,
+and retain the unused suffix. A finite initial range uses a trivial one-bit extension.
+The schedule need not be monotone. Bounded search is efficient, and adjacent parameters give
+the polynomial relation needed to preserve negligible decay.
+Security uses `ComputationallyIndistinguishable.uniform_bound`: the padding test receives the
+prospective input length as an ordinary index, and one negligible bound covers all relevant
+lengths. No nonuniform choice of a bad length is supplied to the reduction.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.GeneratorReindex.parameter`: bounded search for the greatest fitting parameter.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.GeneratorReindex.generate`: prefix generation with the unused suffix preserved.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.GeneratorReindex.pseudorandomGenerator`: one-bit stretch at every seed length.
+This completes the seed-length convention for the construction in
+[T. Holenstein, *Pseudorandom Generators from One-Way Functions*][Holenstein2006], Section 5.
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using typed machine certificates and the
+/-- The greatest parameter at most `size` whose prescribed seed fits, or zero when none fits. -/
+  Nat.findGreatest (fun n => length n ≤ size) size

+theorem isPolyTime_parameter {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {length : ℕ → ℕ} {size : α → ℕ}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => parameter length (size a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The bounded search never returns a parameter above its input size. -/

+/-- Once the zeroth seed fits, the selected seed fits too. -/
+theorem parameter_fits {length : ℕ → ℕ} {size : ℕ} (hsize : length 0 ≤ size) :
+  Nat.findGreatest_spec (P := fun n => length n ≤ size) (Nat.zero_le _) hsize
+/-- The next parameter's seed is too large, even when the schedule is not monotone. -/
+theorem lt_length_succ_parameter {length : ℕ → ℕ} (hge : ∀ n, n + 1 ≤ length n) (size : ℕ) :
+  by_cases hlt : parameter length size < size
+  · exact Nat.lt_of_not_ge (Nat.findGreatest_is_greatest (P := fun n => length n ≤ size)
+      (Nat.lt_succ_self (parameter length size)) (by lia : parameter length size + 1 ≤ size))
+/-- Every fixed parameter eventually fits, so the selected parameter tends to infinity. -/
+theorem parameter_tendsto (length : ℕ → ℕ) : Tendsto (parameter length) atTop atTop := by
+  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (max n (length n))] with size hsize
+  exact Nat.le_findGreatest (by lia : n ≤ size) (by lia : length n ≤ size)
+/-- Search for a family member that fits, then preserve the remaining seed bits as padding. -/

+/-- Generation composes bounded search, the supplied family, and padding. -/

+/-- Every input is expanded by exactly one bit, including the finite initial range. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# One negligible bound for a bounded family of tests
+Sample a dyadic index and calibrate its test with a fresh sample from the selected reference
+The resulting advantage is the average of the indexed squared advantages, so positive and
+negative gaps cannot cancel. This supplies one negligible bound for all indices in a
+polynomially bounded range, even if the chosen index is not computable.
+Both ensembles must have uniform efficient samplers: calibration samples a direction and runs
+the selected real-or-ideal reference experiment, followed by the challenge. The adversary is one
+uniformly efficient indexed program, not a family of separate certificates. Runtime charges
+include the unary index, reference sample and challenge.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.ComputationallyIndistinguishable.uniform_bound`: one bound for every allowed index.
+This uniform sampling argument supplies the parameter conversion used with
+[T. Holenstein, *Pseudorandom Generators from One-Way Functions*][Holenstein2006], Section 5.
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using typed machine certificates and the
+/-- Sample an index and calibrate its test using a fresh real-or-ideal reference sample. -/
+noncomputable def test (bound : ℕ) (real ideal : ProbComp (List Bool))
+    (adversary : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp Bool) (challenge : List Bool) : ProbComp Bool := do
+/-- The reduction charges sampling, reference data and both captured adversary calls. -/
+    {bound : α → ℕ} {real ideal : α → ProbComp (List Bool)}
+    {adversary : α → ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp Bool} {challenge : α → List Bool}
+      (fun a => test (bound a) (real a) (ideal a) (adversary a) (challenge a)) := by
+/-- The challenge commutes with the independent index and calibration trial. -/
+theorem eval_bind_test (bound : ℕ) (real ideal source : ProbComp (List Bool))
+    ProbComp.eval (source >>= test bound real ideal adversary) =
+/-- Averaging calibrated tests averages their squared advantages without sign cancellation. -/
+    Game.advantage (ProbComp.eval (real >>= test bound real ideal adversary))
+  have hgap := fun index : Fin (dyadicSize bound) =>
+/-- A particular index is used only in this inequality; it need not be computed by the test. -/
+    (adversary : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp Bool) {index : ℕ} (hindex : index ≤ bound) :
+      dyadicSize bound * Game.advantage (ProbComp.eval (real >>= test bound real ideal adversary))
+        (ProbComp.eval (ideal >>= test bound real ideal adversary)) := by
+  have hpos : (0 : ℝ≥0) < dyadicSize bound := by exact_mod_cast dyadicSize_pos bound
+/-- Efficient samplers allow one negligible bound for every polynomially bounded index of

+Degree reduction replaces a vertex by its incident half-edges. The executable enumeration uses
+edge indices and Boolean endpoint tags, including both ends of a loop and every parallel edge.
+`cloudEquiv` proves that this enumeration is exactly the cloud in the existing mathematical
+degree-reduction construction. Its inverse is list search, not a choice of a finite enumeration.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.halfEdges`: the ordered half-edges of an edge list.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.endpoint`: read the endpoint of a numbered half-edge.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.cloud`: enumerate the half-edges incident to a vertex.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.cloudEquiv`: identify this enumeration with the mathematical cloud.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.mem_cloud_iff`: the enumeration includes exactly incident half-edges.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.isPolyTime_cloud`: enumeration, scanning and endpoint lookup are
+  uniformly polynomial-time in the encoded graph and vertex.
+* [I. Dinur, *The PCP theorem by gap amplification*][Dinur2007]
+* [I. Dinur, *The PCP theorem by gap amplification*, ECCC TR05-046, revision 1][Dinur2005]
+variable {C α Input : Type} {input : Input ↪ List Bool} {enc : C ↪ List Bool}
+/-- The ordered half-edges: first and second endpoint of every edge, retaining multiplicities
+of the edges. The two ends of a loop remain distinct half-edges. -/
+/-- Read the first endpoint for `false` and the second endpoint for `true`.
+def endpoint (fallback : C) (g : Graph C) (p : ℕ × Bool) : ℕ :=
+  if p.2 then e.dst else e.src
+/-- Enumerate the half-edges incident to a vertex in edge-list order. -/
+def cloud (fallback : C) (g : Graph C) (vertex : ℕ) : List (ℕ × Bool) :=
+  g.halfEdges.filter fun p => g.endpoint fallback p == vertex
+/-- Enumerating both ends of every edge is polynomial-time. -/
+/-- Endpoint lookup is uniform in the graph and the half-edge. -/
+theorem isPolyTime_endpoint {graph : Input → Graph C} {halfEdge : Input → ℕ × Bool}
+/-- Cloud enumeration charges each endpoint lookup and the entire filtered output. -/
+theorem isPolyTime_cloud {graph : Input → Graph C} {vertex : Input → ℕ}
+/-- Every edge contributes exactly two half-edges. -/
+theorem length_halfEdges (g : Graph C) : g.halfEdges.length = 2 * g.edges.length := by
+/-- A numbered half-edge exists exactly when its edge index exists. -/
+  cases p with | mk i b => cases b <;> simp [halfEdges]
+/-- Both ends of every edge have distinct names, even for loops and parallel edges. -/
+/-- Cloud membership means that the edge exists and the selected endpoint is the vertex. -/
+theorem mem_cloud_iff (g : Graph C) (fallback : C) (vertex : ℕ) (p : ℕ × Bool) :
+      p.1 < g.edges.length ∧ g.endpoint fallback p = vertex := by
+/-- A cloud has no repeated half-edge. -/
+/-- Every cloud has at most two half-edges per original edge. -/
+/-- Endpoint lookup agrees with the mathematical graph on existing edges. -/
+theorem endpoint_eq (g : Graph C) (eval : C → α → α → Bool) (fallback : C)
+    g.endpoint fallback (p.1.val, p.2) = (g.toGraph eval).endpoint p := by
+  cases b <;> simp [endpoint, edgeAt, toGraph, ConstraintGraph.endpoint]
+/-- The computed cloud list is precisely the mathematical cloud, with an explicit inverse
+def cloudEquiv (g : Graph C) (eval : C → α → α → Bool) (fallback : C) (vertex : ℕ) :
+      right_inv := fun p => Subtype.ext (Prod.ext (Fin.ext rfl) rfl) }
+/-- The forward cloud identification reads the selected list entry. -/
+theorem cloudEquiv_apply (g : Graph C) (eval : C → α → α → Bool) (fallback : C)
+      (g.cloudEquiv eval fallback vertex i).val.2) = (g.cloud fallback vertex).get i :=
+/-- The inverse cloud identification is the ordinary index-of operation. -/
+theorem cloudEquiv_symm_apply (g : Graph C) (eval : C → α → α → Bool) (fallback : C)

lines: +Copyright (c) 2026 Bolton Bailey, Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Executable rotation within a vertex cloud
+Cloud rotation enumerates the incident half-edges, finds the current one, calls a uniformly
+certified numerical rotation algorithm, and reads the resulting half-edge. It retains the
+return edge label. The correctness theorem identifies it with the existing mathematical
+cloud graph whenever the supplied rotation algorithm realizes its family on `Fin n`.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.cloudFamily`: the mathematical family transported to the clouds.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.isPolyTime_cloudRotation`: a uniform certificate charging the full
+  graph, enumeration, search, rotation, and result lookup.
+* `Cslib.PCP.Encoded.Graph.cloudRotation_eq`: exact agreement with the transported rotation,
+* [I. Dinur, *The PCP theorem by gap amplification*][Dinur2007]
+* [I. Dinur, *The PCP theorem by gap amplification*, ECCC TR05-046, revision 1][Dinur2005]
+variable {C α D Input : Type} {input : Input ↪ List Bool}
+  {enc : C ↪ List Bool} {labelEncoding : D ↪ List Bool}
+/-- Rotate within the current endpoint's cloud using its ordered half-edge enumeration.
+An out-of-range answer retains the input half-edge. -/
+def cloudRotation (fallback : C) (rotate : ℕ × (ℕ × D) → ℕ × D)
+    (g : Graph C) (p : (ℕ × Bool) × D) : (ℕ × Bool) × D :=
+  let members := g.cloud fallback (g.endpoint fallback p.1)
+  let next := rotate (members.length, members.idxOf p.1, p.2)
+/-- The polynomial-time hypothesis on the numerical rotation is joint in the cloud size,
+vertex and label. A separate machine for each size is insufficient. -/
+    {halfEdge : Input → (ℕ × Bool) × D} {rotate : ℕ × (ℕ × D) → ℕ × D}
+/-- Transport a numbered graph family to the explicitly enumerated mathematical clouds. -/
+def cloudFamily (g : Graph C) (eval : C → α → α → Bool) (fallback : C)
+/-- Exact agreement of the numerical program with the transported rotation on a cloud.
+The equality includes the return edge label, not only the neighboring half-edge. -/
+theorem cloudRotation_eq (g : Graph C) (eval : C → α → α → Bool) (fallback : C)
+    (family : (n : ℕ) → RotationMap (Fin n) D) (rotate : ℕ × (ℕ × D) → ℕ × D)
+    (hrotate : ∀ n (v : Fin n) d, rotate (n, v.val, d) =
+      let next := (g.cloudFamily eval fallback family vertex).rot (p, d)
+  rw [← g.cloudEquiv_symm_apply eval fallback vertex p, hrotate]

+# An expanding grid of entropy guesses
+A dyadic grid guesses the observation entropy and the conditional label entropy. Every guess
+assigns enough total digest bits to expand, including incorrect guesses. Rounding the true
+entropies down gives a candidate satisfying all three extraction budgets whenever the prediction
+gap covers four grid steps. The entropy-dependent choice appears only in the existence proof.
+The grid and its output lengths use ordinary unary arithmetic. Their polynomial-time
+certificates apply to arbitrary captured inputs, so later reductions can enumerate the family.
+* `size`, `observationBits`, `labelBits`, `remainingBits`: the executable grid and digest lengths.
+* `Valid`: the entropy budgets required of a successful candidate.
+* `expands`: every candidate expands, including inaccurate guesses.
+* `exists_valid`: a sufficiently large prediction gap guarantees a valid grid entry.
+* Thomas Holenstein, *Pseudorandom Generators from One-Way Functions: A Simple Construction for
+  Any Hardness*, TCC 2006, Section 5, final proof of Theorem 1.
+  The constants below accommodate our repetition schedule and binary-matrix extractors.
+/-- Enumerate an observation guess up to the seed entropy and a label guess below one. -/
+/-- The grid is nonempty, including when the source has no seed bits. -/
+@[simp] theorem size_pos (sourceBits bound : ℕ) : 0 < size sourceBits bound :=
+/-- One unit is the two-slack reserve in the extraction schedule. -/
+/-- Digest length for the observation source, with a zero floor. -/
+def observationBits (n sourceBits bound index : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  scale n sourceBits bound * (2 * (index / dyadicSize bound) - 1)
+/-- Digest length for the hidden labels, using part of the pseudoentropy surplus. -/
+def labelBits (n sourceBits bound index : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  scale n sourceBits bound * (2 * (index % dyadicSize bound) + 7)
+/-- Digest length for the saved seed after revealing both components. -/
+def remainingBits (n sourceBits bound index : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+/-- The soft-mask density numerator, four grid steps above the label guess. -/
+def numerator (bound index : ℕ) : ℕ := index % dyadicSize bound + 4
+/-- The grid has polynomially many entries. -/

+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => size (sourceBits a) (bound a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The common slack unit is uniformly efficient. -/
+theorem isPolyTime_scale {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {n sourceBits bound : α → ℕ}
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => scale (n a) (sourceBits a) (bound a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The observation digest length is uniformly efficient in the candidate index. -/
+      (fun a => observationBits (n a) (sourceBits a) (bound a) (index a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The label digest length is uniformly efficient in the candidate index. -/
+      (fun a => labelBits (n a) (sourceBits a) (bound a) (index a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The retained-seed digest length is uniformly efficient in the candidate index. -/
+      (fun a => remainingBits (n a) (sourceBits a) (bound a) (index a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- The requested density is uniformly efficient in the candidate index. -/

+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => numerator (bound a) (index a)) input encUnary := by
+/-- No candidate asks for zero soft-mask mass. -/

+/-- The integer unit is positive even at security parameter zero. -/

+/-- The repetition count is exactly two units per grid step. -/

+/-- All candidates expand, whether or not their entropy guesses are accurate. -/

+        remainingBits n sourceBits bound index := by
+/-- The label budget holds exactly for every candidate, independent of entropy assumptions. -/

+        ((numerator bound index : ℝ) / dyadicSize bound) := by
+  have hD : (dyadicSize bound : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (dyadicSize_pos bound).ne'

+    (observationBits n sourceBits bound index : ℝ) + scale n sourceBits bound ≤
+  /-- The last extractor respects the entropy left in the saved sampler seed. -/

+    (remainingBits n sourceBits bound index : ℝ) + scale n sourceBits bound ≤

+  have hDr : (0 : ℝ) < D := by exact_mod_cast hD

+  have hsecond_mod : second < D := by lia

+uniform predictor then performs almost as well as every candidate in a polynomial-size family.

+inverse-polynomial slack. The bound allows the best candidate to vary arbitrarily with the

+# Saving the randomness of a coordinate predictor
+A predictor description stores the sampled surrounding examples, a trial bit, and the test's
+coins. It contains no program for generating those examples, so its size does not recursively
+include earlier predictors used during training. The evaluator accepts arbitrary word codes;
+the decoder is total even when a boosting loop truncates a description.
+Replay is pointwise in the supplied observation; reusing a description also reuses its coins.
+The saved test input is split into two encoded fragments around the missing labeled example.
+This avoids requiring an efficient inverse for an arbitrary observation or parameter encoding.

+* `save`, `splice`, `sample`: sample the context and coins before receiving an observation.

+* `eval_sample`, `exists_evaluator`: exact replay from one fixed efficient evaluator.
+* `length_sample_le`, `isPPTOn_sample`: all-execution size and strict PPT certificates.

+  Any Hardness*, TCC 2006, Section 5, Games 3--5 and the following prediction reduction.
+  We save the sampled context explicitly to bound descriptions in the constructive learner.
+/-- Finite data needed to reuse one coordinate predictor on arbitrary observations. -/

+  /-- Encoded test input before the inserted example. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# A sequence learner for the boosting loop
+Each boosting state defines a fresh soft mask. The learner samples saved coordinate predictors
+using that mask, then validates them on fresh labeled examples. Stored descriptions contain the
+sampled data and test coins; they do not recursively contain the state that generated them.
+Their uniform size bound therefore justifies the loop's truncation on every execution.
+The evaluator is obtained from the sequence test's strict PPT certificate. Its signed version
+interprets the learner's orientation bit, and is also the evaluator used by subsequent rounds.
+* `parameters`: configure the loop from the density and distinguishing gap.
+* `candidates`, `learn`, `predict`: save coordinate predictors, learn, and predict.
+* `exists_evaluator`: discharge the replay law from one sequence-test certificate.
+* `predict_extracted_error`: turn a gap against every dense masked source into prediction bias.
+* Thomas Holenstein, *Pseudorandom Generators from One-Way Functions: A Simple Construction for
+  Any Hardness*, TCC 2006, Section 5, Games 3--5 and the prediction reduction.
+* Thomas Holenstein, *Key Agreement from Weak Bit Agreement*, STOC 2005, Section 2.2.
+  We use fresh soft masks and the clocked boosting implementation.
+/-- Configure the loop at the learner's required correlation. The density denominator and
+inverse distinguishing gap determine the rate; the supplied bound covers signed descriptions. -/
+def parameters (confidence numerator densityBound inverseGap codeBound : ℕ) : Parameters :=
+  ⟨confidence, numerator, densityBound, 2 * inverseGap * dyadicSize densityBound, codeBound⟩
+/-- Polynomial-time numerical inputs construct the complete encoded loop parameters. -/
+    {confidence numerator densityBound inverseGap codeBound : α → ℕ}
+      parameters (confidence a) (numerator a) (densityBound a) (inverseGap a) (codeBound a))
+/-- A positive density numerator and the configured rate meet the learner's correlation budget. -/
+theorem parameters_gamma_le (confidence numerator densityBound inverseGap codeBound : ℕ)
+  let params := parameters confidence numerator densityBound inverseGap codeBound
+  have hden : (0 : ℝ) < params.denominator := by exact_mod_cast params.denominator_pos
+  have hrate : (0 : ℝ) < params.inverseRate := by exact_mod_cast params.inverseRate_pos
+  have hnum : (1 : ℝ) ≤ numerator := by exact_mod_cast hvalid.1
+  have hgap' : (0 : ℝ) < inverseGap := by exact_mod_cast hgap
+  have hbudget : 2 * (inverseGap : ℝ) * params.denominator ≤ params.inverseRate := by
+/-- Sample the current soft weight on a fresh labeled observation. -/
+noncomputable def mask (evaluate : List Bool → List Bool → Bool)

+/-- Draw saved coordinate descriptions before receiving any challenge observation. -/

+    (maskedSample source Prod.fst Prod.snd (mask evaluate params state)) source count c d width

+# Repeated extraction with public side information
+Sample a list of observation-label pairs, hash its labels, and retain the observations and the
+complete independent hash seed. Labels may be arbitrary finite values, including observations
+or saved sampler seeds. Boolean labels retain their ordinary word-based PPT interface.
+The exact product law and conditional-entropy extraction bound are shared by all three parts of
+the pseudoentropy construction. The ideal experiment preserves the original public marginal.
+The statistical statements quantify over every randomized finite-output test of the complete
+output, including every Boolean test, with no computational restriction. This uses the existing
+finite-PMF metric without requiring a metric on the infinite ambient type of lists.
+* `extractLabels`, `extractLabelsIdeal`: real extraction and the ideal public-marginal experiment.
+* `eval_replicate_extractLabels`: exact agreement with the finite product experiment.
+* `extractLabels_dist_bind_le`: conditional entropy bounds every randomized finite-output test.
+* `extractLabels_indistinguishable`: statistical security for the common repetition schedule.
+* `isPPTOn_extractLabels`, `isPPTOn_extractLabels_list`: strict PPT with raw or framed labels.
+* Thomas Holenstein, *Pseudorandom Generators from One-Way Functions: A Simple Construction for
+  Any Hardness*, TCC 2006, Section 3.3 and Section 5, Games 0--2.
+  The statistical bound uses the seed-information concentration variant documented in
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the shared nonnegative game API.
+/-- Hash the sampled labels, retaining every public observation and the independent hash seed. -/
+def extractLabels {Observation Label Seed Output : Type} (seed : ProbComp Seed)
+    (hash : Seed → List Label → Output) (samples : List (Observation × Label)) :
+  return (samples.map Prod.fst, key, hash key (samples.map Prod.snd))
+/-- Preserve the sampled observations and public seed, replacing the extracted labels by an
+independent uniform output. The ambient observation and seed types need not be finite. -/
+    (seed : ProbComp Seed) : PMF (List Observation × Seed × Output) :=
+/-- Re-encoding the public marginal commutes with the ideal extraction experiment. -/
+    [Fintype Output] [Nonempty Output] (observe : α → β) (source : ProbComp α)
+/-- Forgetting side information leaves an independent public seed and uniform output. -/
+  simp only [extractLabelsIdeal, PMF.map_bind, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, PMF.bind_const]
+/-- Re-encoding the public observations commutes with extraction of the hidden labels. -/
+theorem extractLabels_map_observation {α β Label Seed Output : Type} (observe : α → β)
+    (seed : ProbComp Seed) (hash : Seed → List Label → Output) (samples : List (α × Label)) :
+    extractLabels seed hash (samples.map (fun sample => (observe sample.1, sample.2))) =
+      (fun result => (result.1.map observe, result.2)) <$> extractLabels seed hash samples := by
+  simp only [extractLabels, map_bind, map_pure, List.map_map, Function.comp_def]
+/-- Re-encoding both fields changes only the hash's input representation and public output. -/
+theorem extractLabels_map_pair {α β Label Value Seed Output : Type}
+    (observe : α → β) (encode : Label → Value) (seed : ProbComp Seed)
+    (hash : Seed → List Value → Output) (samples : List (α × Label)) :
+    extractLabels seed hash (samples.map (fun sample => (observe sample.1, encode sample.2))) =
+        extractLabels seed (fun key values => hash key (values.map encode)) samples := by
+  simp only [extractLabels, map_bind, map_pure, List.map_map, Function.comp_def]
+/-- The full repeated experiment commutes with re-encoding observations and hash inputs. -/

+    (observe : α → β) (encode : Label → Value) (source : ProbComp (α × Label))
+    (count : ℕ) (seed : ProbComp Seed) (hash : Seed → List Value → Output) :
+        extractLabels seed (fun key values => hash key (values.map encode)))).map
+/-- The observation map also commutes with a complete repeated extraction experiment. -/

+/-- Label extraction composes ordinary sampling, list projections, and an efficient hash. -/

+theorem isPPTOn_extractLabels_list {Param Observation Label Seed Output : Type}

+    (hhash : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair => hash pair.1.1 pair.1.2 pair.2)

+/-- Extraction error for the supplied test is the only loss when converting its distinguishing

+    (test : List Observation × Seed × Output → ProbComp Bool)

+      fun samples => extractLabels seed hash samples >>= test))
+/-- The list-based extractor inherits the conditional Shannon-entropy bound for repeated
+samples against every randomized finite-output test. The test receives all observations and
+the independent seed. It has no efficiency restriction. -/

+    {Result : Type*} [Fintype Result] (test : List Observation × Seed × Output → PMF Result) :
+    dist ((ProbComp.eval (OracleComp.replicate count source >>= extractLabels seed hash)).bind test)

+/-- Extracting into a singleton is exactly ideal, including its public observations and seed.
+This handles a zero-bit component without requiring a positive entropy budget. -/
+    ProbComp.eval (OracleComp.replicate count source >>= extractLabels seed hash) =
+      extractLabelsIdeal (Output := Output) (Prod.fst <$> source) count seed := by
+  have huniform (value : Output) : PMF.uniformOfFintype Output = PMF.pure value := by
+    let : Unique Output := { default := value, uniq := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
+/-- A shared repetition schedule makes conditional extraction statistically uniform. A
+zero-bit output is always permitted; positive lengths reserve two slacks below conditional
+entropy. Every randomized Boolean test is admissible, with no computability assumption on
+    [∀ n, Finite (Observation n)] [∀ n, Finite (Label n)] [∀ n, Fintype (Seed n)]
+    (seed : ∀ n, ProbComp (Seed n)) (hash : ∀ n, Seed n → List (Label n) → BitString (outputBits n))
+        Label n) => hash n key (List.ofFn values)))
+      outputBits n + 2 * (ExtractionSchedule.slack n (sourceBits n) (inverseSlack n) : ℝ) ≤
+      (fun (test : ∀ n, List (Observation n) × Seed n × BitString (outputBits n) → Game) n =>
+  · have : Subsingleton (BitString (outputBits n)) := by rw [hzero]; infer_instance
+      exact neg_le_neg (by exact_mod_cast (by lia : sourceBits n ≤ sourceBits n + n + 2))
+    simpa only [BitString, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool, Fintype.card_fin, Nat.cast_pow,
+      Nat.cast_ofNat] using ExtractionSchedule.error_le n (sourceBits n) (inverseSlack n)
+/-- Unconditional extraction is the constant-observation specialization. It hashes ordinary
+lists and reveals the entire seed; zero-bit outputs need no entropy. -/
+    [∀ n, Finite (Label n)] [∀ n, Fintype (Seed n)]
+    (source : ∀ n, ProbComp (Label n)) (sourceBits inverseSlack outputBits : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (seed : ∀ n, ProbComp (Seed n)) (hash : ∀ n, Seed n → List (Label n) → BitString (outputBits n))
+        Label n) => hash n key (List.ofFn values)))
+      outputBits n + 2 * (ExtractionSchedule.slack n (sourceBits n) (inverseSlack n) : ℝ) ≤

+    (fun n => ((), ·) <$> source n) sourceBits inverseSlack outputBits
+  have htest := h (fun n result => test n result.2) trivial
+  have hideal := congrArg (fun law => law.bind (test n))

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Candidate selection composes an efficient indexed trial with polynomial candidate and repetition
+counts. The common adaptive-loop certificate charges for both indices and the running success
+count. Their bounds hold on every execution, independently of the statistical accuracy theorem.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.selectFrom`: charge the input list, lookup and validation.
+/-- Selecting among polynomially many efficient tests using polynomially many trials is strict
+PPT. The test may capture the complete original input. -/
+    {count trials : α → ℕ} {test : α → ℕ → ProbComp Bool}
+    (htest : IsPPTOn (encPair input encUnary) encBool (fun pair => test pair.1 pair.2))
+    IsPPTOn input encUnary (fun a => OracleComp.selectBest (count a) (trials a) (test a)) := by
+  let stateEncoding := encPair encUnary (encPair encUnary encUnary)
+  have htest' : IsPPTOn (encPair input stateEncoding) encBool
+    htest.preprocess (prepare := fun pair : α × (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) => (pair.1, pair.2.1))
+  have htrials' : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : α × (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) => trials pair.1)
+  have hstep : IsPPTOn (encPair input stateEncoding) stateEncoding
+      (fun pair => OracleComp.selectStep (trials pair.1) (test pair.1) pair.2) := by
+  simp only [encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate] at hc ht
+    (step := fun a => OracleComp.selectStep (trials a) (test a)) hcount (by fun_prop) hstep
+    (fun a i state => state.1 = i ∧ state.2.1 ≤ i ∧ state.2.2 ≤ trials a)
+    (by simp) (fun a i state _ hstate next hnext =>
+      ProbComp.selectStep_bounded (trials a) (test a) i state hstate next hnext)
+      intro a i state hi hstate
+/-- Selecting from an efficiently computed list charges for the whole list and each test. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.selectFrom {α β : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {values : α → List β} {trials : α → ℕ} {test : α → β → ProbComp Bool} (fallback : β)
+    (htest : IsPPTOn (encPair input output) encBool (fun pair => test pair.1 pair.2)) :
+      (fun a => OracleComp.selectFrom (values a) (trials a) (test a) fallback) := by
+/-- Sampling a polynomial candidate pool and selecting empirically is a uniform strict PPT
+program. Both the generator and the validation test may capture the original input. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.sampleBest {α β : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {source : α → ProbComp β} {test : α → β → ProbComp Bool} {count trials : α → ℕ}
+    (htest : IsPPTOn (encPair input output) encBool (fun pair => test pair.1 pair.2))
+      OracleComp.sampleBest (count a) (trials a) (source a) (test a) fallback) := by

+The predictor returns true with probability `clippedProbability slope (listVoteMargin votes true)`.
+Its implementation uses a natural numerator and an exact dyadic coin. The label is needed only
+by the correctness statement, not by the predictor.
+The lower-tail argument turns a positive margin on every dense soft set into a prediction
+advantage. Its cutoff is only an analysis witness. Approximating its reciprocal by a finite
+grid gives an efficiently representable candidate; empirical selection is a separate program.
+* `clippedProbability`, `clippedError`: the clipped affine law and its average error.
+* `clippedPredict`: exact fair-bit prediction from a public vote list.
+* `exists_dyadic_clippedError_le`: a finite slope grid contains a good dense-margin predictor.
+[Holenstein2005], Lemma 2.4 and Claim 2.15. Fractional lower tails handle arbitrary finite
+sources, and a finite slope grid permits exact fair-bit sampling.
+/-- The clipped affine probability associated with a signed margin. -/
+/-- Clipping always gives a probability, including for arbitrary parameter values. -/
+/-- A margin at the positive clipping threshold is predicted with certainty. -/
+/-- Below the positive threshold, clipping can only increase the affine probability. -/
+/-- A margin at the negative clipping threshold is predicted incorrectly with certainty. -/
+/-- Negating the signed margin complements the probability. -/
+    clippedProbability slope (-margin) = 1 - clippedProbability slope margin := by
+    · have hpos : (1 + slope * margin) / 2 ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 := by
+      have hneg : (1 + slope * -margin) / 2 ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 := by
+      simp only [clippedProbability, max_eq_right hpos.1, max_eq_right hneg.1,
+/-- Rounding the slope loses at most half the margin times the rounding error. -/
+  have hmin := abs_min_sub_min_le_max (1 : ℝ) (max 0 ((1 + slope * margin) / 2))
+  have hmax := abs_max_sub_max_le_max (0 : ℝ) ((1 + slope * margin) / 2)
+  have hmaxabs (x : ℝ) : max 0 |x| = |x| := max_eq_right (abs_nonneg x)
+  simp only [sub_self, abs_zero, hmaxabs] at hmin hmax
+    _ ≤ |(1 + slope * margin) / 2 - (1 + slope' * margin) / 2| := hmin.trans hmax
+        (slope - slope') * margin / 2 by ring, abs_div, abs_mul]
+/-- Predict from the observable vote word with slope `numerator / dyadicSize bound`.
+The larger dyadic range supplies the additional fair bit needed for the factor `1 / 2`. -/
+noncomputable def clippedPredict (bound numerator : ℕ) (votes : List Bool) : ProbComp Bool :=
+    (dyadicSize bound + numerator * (2 * votes.count true) - numerator * votes.length)
+/-- The executable predictor realizes the clipped affine probability exactly. -/

+  have hd : (0 : ℝ) < dyadicSize bound := by exact_mod_cast dyadicSize_pos bound

+    have hmargin : listVoteMargin votes false = -listVoteMargin votes true :=
+/-- The opposite label has the complementary clipped probability. -/

+/-- The average error of clipped prediction on a finite source with signed margins. -/

+/-- The abstract error is exactly the source-averaged error of the executable dyadic predictor. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Empirical selection of a clipped-vote predictor
+Fresh labeled vote samples estimate each dyadic candidate's prediction probability.
+`selectSlope` returns a natural numerator for use by `clippedPredict`; the analytic lower-tail
+cutoff is never supplied to the program. The error bound combines the lower-tail argument,
+slope discretization, and empirical selection with explicit losses.
+* `clippedTrial`, `selectSlope`: validate and select a finite dyadic candidate.
+* `isPPTOn_selectSlope`: charge the complete grid search and its fresh validation samples.
+  dense-margin guarantee to the selected predictor.
+[Holenstein2005], Lemma 2.4 and Claim 2.15. Empirical selection over a finite slope grid replaces
+/-- Test a candidate on one fresh labeled vote sample. -/
+noncomputable def clippedTrial (precision numerator : ℕ) (source : ProbComp (List Bool × Bool)) :
+  (fun answer => answer == sample.2) <$> clippedPredict precision numerator sample.1
+/-- Select a dyadic slope by comparing empirical correctness on fresh labeled samples. -/
+/-- A certified training sampler and efficient parameters give a strict PPT correctness trial. -/
+    {precision numerator : α → ℕ} {source : α → ProbComp (List Bool × Bool)}
+    IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => clippedTrial (precision a) (numerator a) (source a)) := by
+/-- Selecting a clipped predictor is uniformly strict PPT, including the complete grid search. -/
+    {confidence inverseTolerance precision : α → ℕ} {source : α → ProbComp (List Bool × Bool)}
+      selectSlope (confidence a) (inverseTolerance a) (precision a) (source a)) := by
+/-- Polynomial inverse tolerance for selecting a predictor, also bounding its final advantage. -/
+/-- A polynomial slope grid fine enough for the maximum possible vote margin. -/
+/-- The selection tolerance is computed from the encoded parameter record. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (params a).predictionInverseTolerance) input encUnary := by

+# Sampling the soft weights of hard-core boosting
+Votes are ordinary Boolean words. The number of correct votes, the threshold, and the dyadic
+rate determine a natural-number numerator. Saturating subtraction implements both clipped
+regions of the real weight curve; neither real arithmetic nor rejection sampling is needed.
+`isPPTOn_sampleWeight` certifies the whole program through the shared programming combinators.
+`sampleWeight_density_deviation` estimates the source-averaged density with a Hoeffding bound,
+using a natural success counter and independent source examples.
+Each call draws a fresh coin. An implementation of a random set must additionally cache answers
+to repeated membership queries; this program alone is not such a stateful oracle.
+[Holenstein, Section 2.2, Figure 1 and Claims 2.6–2.8][Holenstein2005]. Adapted from
+/-- The numerator of a clipped linear weight, computed entirely with natural numbers.
+The excess of correct over incorrect votes is `2 * votes.count truth - votes.length` in
+integer arithmetic; the inner natural subtraction keeps only its excess over the threshold. -/
+/-- Every generated numerator is within its denominator, including malformed parameter choices. -/
+    weightNumerator denominator rateNumerator threshold votes truth ≤ denominator :=
+/-- Saturating natural arithmetic exactly implements the clipped real-valued weight curve. -/
+    (weightNumerator denominator rateNumerator threshold votes truth : ℝ) / denominator =
+      weight (rateNumerator / denominator) (listVoteMargin votes truth - threshold) := by
+  have hd : (0 : ℝ) < denominator := by exact_mod_cast hdenominator
+  by_cases hlow : 2 * votes.count truth ≤ votes.length + threshold
+  · have hm : 2 * (votes.count truth : ℝ) - votes.length - threshold ≤ 0 := by
+      have h : 2 * (votes.count truth : ℝ) ≤ votes.length + threshold := by exact_mod_cast hlow
+    have hnonneg : 0 ≤ (rateNumerator : ℝ) / denominator * excess := by positivity
+    · have hratio : (rateNumerator : ℝ) / denominator * excess ≤ 1 := by
+    · have hratio : 1 ≤ (rateNumerator : ℝ) / denominator * excess := by
+        exact_mod_cast (show denominator ≤ rateNumerator * excess by lia)
+/-- The weight's natural numerator is polynomial time in its complete encoded input. -/
+@[fun_prop] theorem isPolyTime_weightNumerator {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {denominator rateNumerator threshold : α → ℕ} {votes : α → List Bool} {truth : α → Bool}

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Fresh masks for a pseudoentropy pair
+A mask coin chooses whether to replace a label by a fresh fair bit. Conditional on any
+deterministic observation, the resulting label has at least as much entropy as the average
+replacement probability. This remains true when the mask probability depends on the original
+Every occurrence draws a fresh mask, including repeated inputs. The executable boosting weights
+provide such coins exactly, so their density is a lower bound on the masked label's conditional
+entropy. The sampler and its strict PPT certificate use the usual programming combinators.
+The distinguishing-to-prediction reduction then samples a random coordinate and supplies a trial
+bit at that coordinate. Its weighted prediction bias is exactly the complete sequence gap divided
+by the dyadic coordinate range. The target observation is its only target-dependent input; labels
+and masks are computed only on fresh surrounding samples.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Pseudoentropy.maskBit`, `.maskedSample`: replace labels using fresh mask coins.
+* [Holenstein, Section 5, Games 3–5][Holenstein2006]. The fresh soft-mask coin replaces the set
+  indicator in that experiment; [Holenstein, Section 2.1.1][Holenstein2005] discusses measures.
+Adapted from `Crypto/Computational/Pseudoentropy/Masking.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`. These are ingredients of the subsequent extraction
+and learning arguments, not a complete pseudorandomness theorem.
+private theorem probability_bind {α : Type} [Fintype α] (source : ProbComp α)
+    Pr[source >>= test] = ∑ x, (ProbComp.eval source x).toReal * Pr[test x] := by
+/-- Replace a label by a fresh fair bit when the supplied mask accepts. -/
+noncomputable def maskBit (mask : ProbComp Bool) (truth : Bool) : ProbComp Bool := do
+  if replace then ProbComp.uniform Bool else pure truth
+/-- Sample an observation and a label with a fresh input-dependent randomization mask. -/
+noncomputable def maskedSample {α β : Type} (source : ProbComp α)
+    (observe : α → β) (truth : α → Bool) (mask : α → ProbComp Bool) : ProbComp (β × Bool) := do
+/-- The mask's law is an ordinary mixture of a fair bit and the original label. -/
+      (fun replace => if replace then PMF.uniformOfFintype Bool else PMF.pure truth) := by
+/-- The original label remains with probability `1 - maskProbability / 2`. -/
+      if bit = truth then 1 - (ProbComp.eval mask true).toReal / 2
+/-- A fresh replacement contributes one bit of conditional randomness whenever the mask accepts. -/
+    (ProbComp.eval mask true).toReal ≤ entropy (ProbComp.eval (maskBit mask truth)) := by
+    (fun replace => if replace then PMF.uniformOfFintype Bool else PMF.pure truth)
+/-- The masked pair reveals the original observation and averages the pointwise masked laws. -/
+    (observe : α → β) (truth : α → Bool) (mask : α → ProbComp Bool) :
+/-- Hiding all but a deterministic observation leaves at least the average mask probability
+in conditional label entropy. In particular, mask probabilities may depend on hidden labels. -/
+theorem maskedSample_entropy_ge {α β : Type} [Fintype α] [Finite β] (source : ProbComp α)
+    (observe : α → β) (truth : α → Bool) (mask : α → ProbComp Bool) :
+      conditionalEntropy (ProbComp.eval (maskedSample source observe truth mask)) := by
+/-- The entropy available from executable boosting masks is at least their exact soft density. -/
+    (source : ProbComp α) (observe : α → β) (truth : α → Bool) (votes : α → List Bool)
+          Boosting.sampleWeight bound numerator threshold (votes x) (truth x)))) := by
+      (fun x => Boosting.sampleWeight bound numerator threshold (votes x) (truth x))
+/-- Distinguishing a real label from its masked version gives prediction bias weighted by the
+mask probability. The predictor itself receives only the test, not the mask or hidden label. -/
+theorem maskBit_prediction_gap (test : Bool → ProbComp Bool) (mask : ProbComp Bool)
+    Pr[test truth] - Pr[maskBit mask truth >>= test] =
+        (Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth) <$> bitPredictor test] - 1 / 2) := by
+/-- The exact masked distinguishing gap is the source-averaged weighted prediction bias.
+Only the observation is passed to the predictor; the mask may depend on the entire source. -/
+theorem maskedSample_prediction_gap {α β : Type} [Fintype α] (source : ProbComp α)
+    (observe : α → β) (truth : α → Bool) (mask : α → ProbComp Bool)
+    Pr[source >>= fun x => test (observe x) (truth x)] -
+        Pr[maskedSample source observe truth mask >>= fun pair => test pair.1 pair.2] =
+        (Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth x) <$> bitPredictor (test (observe x))] -
+/-- A certified mask and an efficiently supplied label give a strict PPT randomized label. -/
+theorem isPPTOn_maskBit {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {mask : α → ProbComp Bool}
+    {truth : α → Bool} (hmask : IsPPTOn input encBool mask)
+    IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => maskBit (mask a) (truth a)) := by
+/-- Masked sampling composes a certified source, observation, label, and mask. All callbacks may
+capture the original input, and all intermediate encodings are charged. -/
+theorem isPPTOn_maskedSample {α β γ : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {sample : β ↪ List Bool} {output : γ ↪ List Bool} {source : α → ProbComp β}
+    {observe : α → β → γ} {truth : α → β → Bool} {mask : α → β → ProbComp Bool}
+    (hobserve : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : α × β => observe pair.1 pair.2)
+    (htruth : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : α × β => truth pair.1 pair.2)
+    (hmask : IsPPTOn (encPair input sample) encBool (fun pair => mask pair.1 pair.2)) :
+      (fun a => maskedSample (source a) (observe a) (truth a) (mask a)) := by
+/-- Predict from one public observation by simulating a random-coordinate masked hybrid.
+Hidden labels and masks are computed only on independently generated surrounding samples. -/
+noncomputable def maskedSequencePredictor {α β : Type} (source : ProbComp α)
+    (observe : α → β) (truth : α → Bool) (mask : α → ProbComp Bool) (count : ℕ)
+    (test : List (β × Bool) → ProbComp Bool) (observation : β) : ProbComp Bool :=
+  bitPredictor (fun trial => sequenceTest (maskedSample source observe truth mask)
+    ((fun x => (observe x, truth x)) <$> source) count test (observation, trial))
+/-- A sequence distinguisher gives one predictor whose mask-weighted bias equals the complete
+distinguishing gap divided by the dyadic coordinate range. This allows arbitrary finite sources,
+arbitrary observations, hidden-label-dependent masks, and zero repetitions. -/
+theorem maskedSequence_prediction_gap {α β : Type} [Fintype α] (source : ProbComp α)
+    (observe : α → β) (truth : α → Bool) (mask : α → ProbComp Bool) (count : ℕ)
+    Pr[OracleComp.replicate count ((fun x => (observe x, truth x)) <$> source)
+      Pr[OracleComp.replicate count (maskedSample source observe truth mask)
+            maskedSequencePredictor source observe truth mask count test (observe x)] - 1 / 2) := by
+  simpa only [bind_map_left] using maskedSample_prediction_gap source observe truth mask
+    (fun observation trial => sequenceTest (maskedSample source observe truth mask)
+      ((fun x => (observe x, truth x)) <$> source) count test (observation, trial))
+/-- The complete masked-coordinate prediction reduction is strict PPT whenever its source,
+observation, labels, masks, test, and repetition count have certificates. -/
+theorem isPPTOn_maskedSequencePredictor {Param α β : Type} {input : Param ↪ List Bool}
+    {sample : α ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool} {source : Param → ProbComp α}
+    {observe : Param → α → β} {truth : Param → α → Bool} {mask : Param → α → ProbComp Bool}
+    {count : Param → ℕ} {test : Param → List (β × Bool) → ProbComp Bool}
+    (hobserve : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : Param × α => observe pair.1 pair.2)
+    (htruth : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : Param × α => truth pair.1 pair.2)
+    (hmask : IsPPTOn (encPair input sample) encBool (fun pair => mask pair.1 pair.2))
+    IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => maskedSequencePredictor (source a) (observe a)
+      (truth a) (mask a) (count a) (test a) (observation a)) := by
+  have hmasked := isPPTOn_maskedSample hsource hobserve htruth hmask
+  have horiginal : IsPPTOn input (encPair output encBool)
+      (fun a => (fun x => (observe a x, truth a x)) <$> source a) := by ppt

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Continuing a native program concatenates its semantic atoms with those of the continuation,
+evaluated on the values supplied by the feeding wires. The identity keeps gate order and

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Compiling Waring circuits to arithmetic circuits
+Each Waring term computes its linear form once, raises the result by binary powering, and
+multiplies by its scale. Generic formulas compile the linear form and scaling; circuit
+composition preserves sharing through the power computation. Contextual simulation then makes
+the same variable block available to every term gadget and preserves every source output.
+The construction accepts arbitrary coefficient symbols, with explicit symbols for zero and
+one. Correctness requires their interpretations to be zero and one. Costs count all generated
+gates, including unused source gates, coefficient constants and the initial zero. Multiplication
+and addition counts specialize the exact arbitrary-weight formula. These are circuit costs,
+not TM-time certificates for generating or evaluating encoded circuits, and no optimality of
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Waring.Term.toCircuit`: linear form, binary power and final scaling.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Waring.compile`: compile a sum-of-terms circuit with shared variable inputs.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Waring.compilationCost`: the exact charge of each source operation.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Waring.eval_compile`: all outputs agree under a semiring interpretation.
+  `Cslib.Circuits.Waring.size_compile`: closed multiplication, addition and gate counts.
+  extension in [S. Schlesinger, *Algebraic circuit formalizations in
+  Complexitylib*][Schlesinger2026Algebraic]. The source's separate arithmetic expression and
+  contextual translation frameworks are replaced by the shared formula and circuit APIs.
+variable {C : Type v} {R : Type u} {d n m : ℕ}
+/-- Compute the linear form once, use a binary-power DAG, and apply the scale once. -/
+def Term.toCircuit (zero one : C) (t : Term C d) : Circuit (arithSignature C) d 1 :=
+/-- Term compilation preserves evaluation under any semiring interpretation of the symbols. -/
+theorem Term.eval_toCircuit [Semiring R] (zero one : C) (constant : C → R)
+    (hzero : constant zero = 0) (hone : constant one = 1) (t : Term C d) (x : Fin d → R) :
+    (t.toCircuit zero one).eval (arithInterpretationWith C constant) x 0 = t.eval constant x := by
+/-- Exact weighted term cost, including all coefficient and zero/one constants. -/
+theorem Term.cost_program_toCircuit (zero one : C) (weight : ArithOp C → ℕ) (t : Term C d) :
+        (if d = 0 then weight (.const one) else binaryMultiplicationCount d * weight .mul) +
+/-- The multiplication count of a compiled term, including coefficient and scale products. -/
+def termMultiplicationCount (d : ℕ) : ℕ := d + binaryMultiplicationCount d + 1
+/-- Exact term multiplication count, including the final scale multiplication at degree zero. -/
+theorem Term.mulCost_toCircuit (zero one : C) (t : Term C d) :
+    (t.toCircuit zero one).program.cost ArithOp.mulCost = termMultiplicationCount d := by
+  by_cases hd : d = 0 <;> simp [ArithOp.mulCost, termMultiplicationCount, hd]
+/-- There is one linear-form addition per variable, including the initial addition to zero. -/
+theorem Term.addCost_toCircuit (zero one : C) (t : Term C d) :
+/-- The total gate count includes coefficient constants, zero, scaling, and the power circuit. -/

+/-- One arithmetic gadget for a source operation, reading variables before source arguments. -/
+    (op : SumOfTerms.Op (Term C d)) → Circuit (arithSignature C) (d + op.arity) 1
+/-- Compile every source operation, sharing the first `d` inputs as the variable context.
+Any original inputs follow that context and remain available to the source program. -/

+    (c : Circuit (SumOfTerms.signature (Term C d)) n m) (weight : ArithOp C → ℕ) :

title: feat(Circuit): add contextual simulation and binary powering

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Binary powering computes each intermediate power once and shares it between the two inputs
+of a squaring gate. Every further binary digit adds one squaring and, for a one bit, a
+multiplication by the retained original input. A positive exponent `e` uses at most
+`2 * Nat.log2 e` gates, all multiplications. Exponent zero uses a single named constant gate;
+exponent one uses only the input wire.
+The constant symbol denoting one is an explicit parameter. Its interpretation is required to
+equal one only in the correctness theorem. Arbitrary weighted costs, including constant costs,
+are accounted for exactly. These are circuit-size results, not uniform TM-time certificates
+* `Cslib.Circuits.eval_binaryPowerCircuit`: correctness over a monoid with addition.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.cost_program_binaryPowerCircuit`: exact cost for any operation weights.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.size_binaryPowerCircuit_le`: logarithmic gate count for positive exponents.
+/-- Add a binary digit to a shared power: square, then multiply by the original input for
+private theorem eval_binaryPowerStep [Add R] [Mul R] (constant : C → R) (bit : Bool)
+      if bit then (c.eval (arithInterpretationWith C constant) x 0 *
+    (cost : ArithOp C → ℕ) : (Circuit.binaryPowerStep bit c).program.cost cost =
+/-- Binary powering with a specified constant symbol for one. -/
+/-- Exact multiplication count of binary powering: one squaring per nonleading bit and
+one further multiplication per nonleading one bit. -/
+  Nat.binaryRecFromOne 0 0 (fun bit _ _ count => count + 1 + bit.toNat) e
+    Circuit.oneGate (σ := arithSignature C) (.const one) Fin.elim0 := by
+private theorem binaryPowerCircuit_bit (one : C) (bit : Bool) (e : ℕ) (he : e ≠ 0) :
+    binaryMultiplicationCount (Nat.bit bit e) = binaryMultiplicationCount e + 1 + bit.toNat :=
+/-- The circuit computes the natural power, including exponents zero and one. -/
+theorem eval_binaryPowerCircuit [Add R] [Monoid R] (one : C) (constant : C → R)
+    (binaryPowerCircuit one e).eval (arithInterpretationWith C constant) x 0 = x 0 ^ e := by
+    rw [binaryPowerCircuit_bit one bit e he, eval_binaryPowerStep, ih]
+/-- Exact weighted cost, charging the constant gate for exponent zero. -/
+theorem cost_program_binaryPowerCircuit (one : C) (e : ℕ) (cost : ArithOp C → ℕ) :
+      if e = 0 then cost (.const one) else binaryMultiplicationCount e * cost .mul := by
+    rw [binaryPowerCircuit_bit one bit e he, cost_program_binaryPowerStep, ih,
+    cases bit <;> simp [Nat.bit, he, Nat.add_mul, Nat.add_assoc]
+/-- Every gate at a positive exponent is a multiplication; exponent zero has one constant. -/
+    (binaryPowerCircuit one e).size = if e = 0 then 1 else binaryMultiplicationCount e := by
+/-- The multiplication count includes multiplication by scalars. -/
+    (binaryPowerCircuit one e).program.cost ArithOp.mulCost = binaryMultiplicationCount e := by
+/-- Binary powering uses at most twice the base-two logarithm many multiplications. -/
+    rw [binaryMultiplicationCount_bit bit e he, Nat.log2_eq_log_two, Nat.log_two_bit he]
+    cases bit <;> simp only [Bool.toNat_false, Bool.toNat_true] <;> lia
+/-- A positive exponent needs at most `2 * log₂ e` gates, all multiplications. -/
