lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+An operation gadget can read a shared block of ambient inputs as well as its ordinary
+arguments. This permits a nullary dictionary term to depend on ambient variables, as in
+Waring decompositions. All gadgets read the same input block; no context gates are added.
+Compilation first adds context arguments to each line, then uses `Program.simulate` through
+`Circuit.simulate`. Thus the existing wire-renaming and gate-replacement machinery handles
+sharing and output wiring. Costs count every gadget gate, including gates unused by outputs.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Signature.withContext`: prepend ambient inputs to every operation's arguments.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.withContext`: pass the same ambient inputs to every gate.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.simulateWithContext`: replace each operation by a contextual gadget.
+  formalizations in Complexitylib*][Schlesinger2026Algebraic], using native circuit simulation.
+variable {σ : Signature.{v}} {τ : Signature.{w}} {U : Type u} {n m g : ℕ}
+/-- Add a `q`-input context before each operation's ordinary arguments. -/
+/-- Prepend references to the ambient input block to a line's arguments. -/
+def Line.withContext (q : ℕ) (line : Line σ (q + n) g) :
+/-- Every gate receives the shared context, followed by its original arguments. -/
+def Circuit.withContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ) : Circuit (σ.withContext q) (q + n) m :=
+/-- Adding context does not add gates or change their costs. -/
+theorem Circuit.cost_program_withContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ) (cost : σ.Op → ℕ) :
+/-- Adding context keeps the number of gates. -/
+@[simp] theorem Circuit.size_withContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ) :
+/-- Evaluating a context-bearing circuit fixes the same context in every operation. -/
+theorem Circuit.eval_withContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ)
+    (J : Interpretation (σ.withContext q) U) (context : Fin q → U) (x : Fin n → U) :
+      c.eval (fun op args => J op (Fin.append context args)) x := by
+    (f := Line.withContext q) (I := fun op args => J op (Fin.append context args))
+  change J line.op (Wire.elim (Fin.append context x) gates ∘
+      J line.op (Fin.append context (Wire.elim (Fin.append context x) gates ∘ line.wires))
+/-- Replace every gate by a gadget receiving shared ambient inputs and its local arguments. -/
+def Circuit.simulateWithContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ)
+    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (q + σ.Arity op) 1) : Circuit τ (q + n) m :=
+/-- Contextual simulation computes every output with the supplied gadget semantics. -/
+theorem Circuit.eval_simulateWithContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ)
+    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (q + σ.Arity op) 1)
+    (J : Interpretation τ U) (context : Fin q → U) (x : Fin n → U) :
+      c.eval (fun op args => (impl op).eval J (Fin.append context args) 0) x := by
+  let I : Interpretation (σ.withContext q) U := fun op args => (impl op).eval J args 0
+  have h : ∀ op, (impl op).Computes J (single (I op)) :=
+    fun _ _ => funext fun j => congrArg _ (Subsingleton.elim j 0)
+/-- Contextual simulation charges exactly the weighted cost of each operation gadget. -/
+theorem Circuit.cost_program_simulateWithContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ)
+    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (q + σ.Arity op) 1) (cost : τ.Op → ℕ) :
+      c.program.cost fun op => (impl op).program.cost cost := by
+/-- The compiled gate count is exactly the sum of the gadget sizes. -/
+@[simp] theorem Circuit.size_simulateWithContext (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ)
+    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (q + σ.Arity op) 1) :
+    (c.simulateWithContext q impl).size = c.program.cost fun op => (impl op).size := by
+/-- A uniform gadget-size bound gives a uniform factor on circuit size. -/
+theorem Circuit.size_simulateWithContext_le (c : Circuit σ n m) (q : ℕ)
+    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (q + σ.Arity op) 1) {b : ℕ}
+    (h : ∀ op, (impl op).size ≤ b) : (c.simulateWithContext q impl).size ≤ b * c.size := by

title: feat(Circuit): add weighted complexity from supplied sources

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Weighted circuit complexity from supplied values
+A source family `sources : X → Fin n → U` supplies exactly the inputs available to a circuit
+computing `target : X → Fin m → U`. The common domain may be arbitrary. No coordinates of `X`
+are implicitly available, and supplying the sources has no cost. The minimum of `Program.cost`
+over implementing circuits is recorded in `ℕ∞`, with `⊤` when no circuit exists.
+Operation costs may be zero. Consequently, zero weighted complexity need not mean that the
+target is obtained by wiring. Even with an empty common domain, a syntactic circuit must exist;
+vacuous correctness alone does not provide outputs from zero inputs over an empty signature.
+Unit costs recover native support complexity by taking the support subtype as the common domain.
+Supplying both raw inputs and helper values recovers native `ecomplexityGiven`. These bridges
+require no chosen extension of the target outside the range of the sources.
+The model allows arbitrary finite gate arities and natural-number weights. Every output must
+be wired; constants must be supplied or implemented by gates. In particular, the syntax does
+not use Boyack's convention assigning zero to disconnected vertices.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.ComputesFrom`: computation from exactly the supplied source family.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityFrom`: minimum weighted cost of such a computation.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityFrom_le_iff`: every finite budget has a circuit witness.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityFrom_comp_le`: composition through an intermediate supplied family.
+* [S. W. Boyack, *The Robustness of Combinatorial Measures of Boolean Matrix
+  Complexity*][Boyack1985], Definition 2.1 and Proposition 2.2, pp. 29–30, for computation
+  relative to supplied functions and its composition inequality.
+variable {σ : Signature.{v}} {U : Type u} {X : Type w} {n m p : ℕ}
+/-- Compute the target family from exactly the supplied values, without implicit raw inputs. -/
+def Circuit.ComputesFrom (c : Circuit σ n m) (I : Interpretation σ U)
+    (target : X → Fin m → U) (sources : X → Fin n → U) : Prop :=
+  ∀ x, c.eval I (sources x) = target x
+variable {I : Interpretation σ U} {cost cost' : σ.Op → ℕ}
+  {target : X → Fin m → U} {sources : X → Fin n → U}
+/-- Equal supplied values must give equal target values. -/
+    (hc : c.ComputesFrom I target sources) {x y : X} (h : sources x = sources y) :
+  rw [← hc x, ← hc y, h]
+/-- Compose computations through an intermediate supplied family. -/
+theorem Circuit.ComputesFrom.comp {c : Circuit σ n m} {d : Circuit σ m p}
+    {f : X → Fin m → U} {g : X → Fin p → U}
+    (hc : c.ComputesFrom I f sources) (hd : d.ComputesFrom I g f) :
+    (d.comp c).ComputesFrom I g sources := fun x => by
+/-- Compute two target families from the same supplied values. -/
+theorem Circuit.ComputesFrom.append {c : Circuit σ n m} {d : Circuit σ n p}
+    {f : X → Fin m → U} {g : X → Fin p → U}
+    (hc : c.ComputesFrom I f sources) (hd : d.ComputesFrom I g sources) :
+    (c.append d).ComputesFrom I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x)) sources := fun x => by
+@[simp] theorem Circuit.computesFrom_subtype_iff (c : Circuit σ n m)
+    (S : Set (Fin n → U)) (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) :
+    c.ComputesFrom I (fun x : S => f x) Subtype.val ↔ c.ComputesOn I S f := by
+/-- An explicitly supplied extension identifies source computation with computation on its range. -/
+    (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (hf : ∀ x, f (sources x) = target x) :
+    c.ComputesFrom I target sources ↔ c.ComputesOn I (Set.range sources) f := by
+  simp only [ComputesFrom, ComputesOn, Set.EqOn, Set.forall_mem_range, hf]
+/-- Minimum weighted cost of computing a target from the supplied values, or `⊤` if no circuit
+does so. Every operation has finite natural-number cost; supplying the sources is free. -/
+noncomputable def ecomplexityFrom (I : Interpretation σ U) (cost : σ.Op → ℕ)
+    (target : X → Fin m → U) (sources : X → Fin n → U) : ℕ∞ :=
+  ⨅ c : {c : Circuit σ n m // c.ComputesFrom I target sources}, (c.1.program.cost cost : ℕ∞)
+    ecomplexityFrom I cost target sources ≤ c.program.cost cost :=
+  iInf_le (fun c : {c // c.ComputesFrom I target sources} => (c.1.program.cost cost : ℕ∞)) ⟨c, hc⟩
+      ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesFrom I target sources := by
+      ¬ ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesFrom I target sources := by
+/-- A representable target has a circuit attaining its minimum weighted cost. -/
+    (h : ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesFrom I target sources) :
+    ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesFrom I target sources ∧
+      (c.program.cost cost : ℕ∞) = ecomplexityFrom I cost target sources := by
+  have : Nonempty {c : Circuit σ n m // c.ComputesFrom I target sources} := nonempty_subtype.mpr h
+    (fun c : {c : Circuit σ n m // c.ComputesFrom I target sources} =>
+/-- Every finite weighted budget is witnessed by a circuit. -/
+    ecomplexityFrom I cost target sources ≤ k ↔
+      ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesFrom I target sources ∧ c.program.cost cost ≤ k := by
+    exact ⟨c, hc, by exact_mod_cast hcost.trans_le h⟩
+/-- A lower bound holds exactly when it holds for every implementing circuit. -/
+    k ≤ ecomplexityFrom I cost target sources ↔
+      ∀ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesFrom I target sources → k ≤ c.program.cost cost := by
+theorem ecomplexityFrom_mono_cost (h : ∀ op, cost op ≤ cost' op) :
+    ecomplexityFrom I cost target sources ≤ ecomplexityFrom I cost' target sources :=
+/-- Selecting, permuting or duplicating supplied values is free. -/
+@[simp] theorem ecomplexityFrom_wiring (sources : X → Fin n → U) (select : Fin m → Fin n) :
+    ecomplexityFrom I cost (fun x => sources x ∘ select) sources = 0 := by
+@[simp] theorem ecomplexityFrom_self (sources : X → Fin n → U) :
+/-- If the sources identify two points distinguished by the target, no implementation exists. -/
+theorem ecomplexityFrom_eq_top_of_fiber_collision {x y : X} (h : sources x = sources y)
+    (hne : target x ≠ target y) : ecomplexityFrom I cost target sources = ⊤ := by
+/-- Computing through an intermediate family adds at most the two weighted complexities. -/
+theorem ecomplexityFrom_comp_le (f : X → Fin m → U) (g : X → Fin p → U)
+      ecomplexityFrom I cost f sources + ecomplexityFrom I cost g f := by
+  refine le_iInf fun d => le_iInf fun c => ?_
+/-- Computing two families from the same sources costs at most the sum of their complexities. -/
+theorem ecomplexityFrom_append_le (f : X → Fin m → U) (g : X → Fin p → U)
+    ecomplexityFrom I cost (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x)) sources ≤
+      ecomplexityFrom I cost f sources + ecomplexityFrom I cost g sources := by
+  refine le_iInf fun d => le_iInf fun c => ?_
+/-- Unit weights and the support subtype recover native support complexity. -/
+    ecomplexityFrom I (fun _ => 1) (fun x : S => f x) Subtype.val = ecomplexityOn I S f := by
+/-- Unit weights with raw inputs and helpers recover native relative complexity. -/
+theorem ecomplexityFrom_unit_append {k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
+    ecomplexityFrom I (fun _ => 1) f (fun x => Fin.append x (g x)) = ecomplexityGiven I f g := by
+  simp only [ecomplexityFrom, ecomplexityGiven, ecomplexityOn, iInf_subtype, Circuit.ComputesFrom,

title: feat(Circuit): bound Waring term counts by catalecticant rank

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Waring term counts for a squarefree monomial
+A sum of scaled `d`-th powers of linear forms representing the product of `d` variables needs
+at least `choose d k` terms, for every split `k`. At degree `2*n`, the middle split gives the
+central binomial coefficient. The field may be any characteristic-zero field.
+Restrict the normalized coefficient matrix to squarefree row exponents of degree `k` and
+complemented column exponents. Each power term gives rank at most one; the target gives a
+nonzero scalar identity. The finite-sum endpoint needs no circuit encoding. The circuit endpoint
+uses native circuits adding dictionary terms, with free additions and wiring. A reused term
+gate is charged once. These are bounds for this restricted representation model, not for
+unrestricted arithmetic circuits. All computation premises are formal polynomial equalities.
+  homogeneous linear forms, used as the dictionary of `SumOfTerms.signature`.
+  lower bounds for ordinary finite sums.
+  lower bounds for any selected output of a zero-input sum-of-terms circuit.
+  and `Applications/Waring.lean` in [S. Schlesinger, *Algebraic circuit formalizations in
+* [J. M. Landsberg and Z. Teitler, *On the ranks and border ranks of symmetric
+  tensors*][LandsbergTeitler2009], equation (1) and Remark 6.5. We use a squarefree restriction
+  of the catalecticant argument; this does not identify the exact Waring rank or formalize
+  the paper's border-rank and singularity bounds.
+/-- A scalar multiple of a `d`-th power of a homogeneous linear form in `d` variables. -/
+  /-- Coefficients of the homogeneous linear form. -/
+/-- The polynomial represented by a Waring dictionary term. -/
+    (t : Term K d) : MvPolynomial (Fin d) K :=
+  C t.scale * (∑ i, t.coefficients i • X i) ^ d
+private abbrev Layer (d k : ℕ) := ↥(Finset.powersetCard k (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin d)))
+private noncomputable def exponent {d : ℕ} (s : Finset (Fin d)) : Fin d →₀ ℕ :=
+private theorem exponent_apply {d : ℕ} (s : Finset (Fin d)) (i : Fin d) :
+    exponent s i = if i ∈ s then 1 else 0 := by
+private theorem exponent_add_compl_eq_univ_iff {d k : ℕ} (r c : Layer d k) :
+    exponent r.1 + exponent c.1ᶜ = exponent Finset.univ ↔ r = c := by
+    by_cases hr : i ∈ r.1 <;> by_cases hc : i ∈ c.1 <;>
+    by_cases hi : i ∈ r.1 <;> simp [exponent_apply, hi]
+private theorem exponent_add_compl_sum {d k : ℕ} (r c : Layer d k) :
+    (exponent r.1 + exponent c.1ᶜ).sum (fun _ e => e) = d := by
+private noncomputable def feature (K : Type*) [Field K] (d k : ℕ) :
+    MvPolynomial (Fin d) K →ₗ[K] (Layer d k → K) →ₗ[K] Layer d k → K :=
+    (catalecticant (fun r : Layer d k => exponent r.1) (fun c : Layer d k => exponent c.1ᶜ))
+private theorem rank_feature_term_le (t : Term K d) (k : ℕ) :
+    (feature K d k (∏ i : Fin d, X i)).rank = (d.choose k : Cardinal) := by
+  have htarget : (∏ i : Fin d, (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin d) K)) =
+    simpa [exponent] using prod_X_pow (R := K) (fun _ : Fin d => 1) Finset.univ
+  have hmatrix : catalecticant (fun r : Layer d k => exponent r.1)
+      (fun c : Layer d k => exponent c.1ᶜ) (∏ i : Fin d, (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin d) K)) =
+        (1 : Matrix (Layer d k) (Layer d k) K) := by
+    · have he := mt (exponent_add_compl_eq_univ_iff r c).mp h
+/-- Every split of the degree gives a term-count bound for an ordinary sum of scaled powers.
+The premise is equality of formal polynomials. -/
+    (scale : ι → K) (coefficients : ι → Fin d → K)
+    (hcompute : ∑ i ∈ indices, C (scale i) * (∑ j, C (coefficients i j) * X j) ^ d =
+      ∏ j : Fin d, X j) : d.choose k ≤ indices.card := by
+  let terms (i : ι) : Term K d := ⟨scale i, coefficients i⟩
+  have hsum : ∑ i ∈ indices, (terms i).polynomial = ∏ j : Fin d, X j := by
+    (fun i => feature K d k (terms i).polynomial)).trans
+  rw [← map_sum, hsum, rank_feature_prod_X] at h
+/-- The middle split gives a central-binomial lower bound for a sum of even-degree powers. -/
+    (scale : ι → K) (coefficients : ι → Fin (2 * n) → K)
+    (hcompute : ∑ i ∈ indices, C (scale i) * (∑ j, C (coefficients i j) * X j) ^ (2 * n) =
+      ∏ j : Fin (2 * n), X j) : Nat.centralBinom n ≤ indices.card :=
+  choose_le_card n indices scale coefficients hcompute
+/-- A sum-of-terms circuit for the squarefree monomial needs at least `choose d k` term gates.
+Additions and wiring are free, and shared gates are charged once. -/
+theorem choose_le_cost {m : ℕ} (c : Circuit (SumOfTerms.signature (Term K d)) 0 m)

+The entry indexed by exponent vectors `r` and `c` is the coefficient of `r + c`, divided by
+its multinomial coefficient. Over a characteristic-zero field, when all queried exponents have
+degree `d`, a `d`-th power of a linear form gives an outer product. Row and column families may be
+arbitrary restrictions of the homogeneous exponent layers; no enumeration of all monomials is
+* `MvPolynomial.catalecticant`: the normalized coefficient matrix, linear in the polynomial.
+* The coefficient argument is adapted from `LowerBound/Fusion/SumOfTerms/Waring.lean` in
+* [J. M. Landsberg and Z. Teitler, *On the ranks and border ranks of symmetric
+  tensors*][LandsbergTeitler2009], equation (1) and Remark 6.5, describe the catalecticant bound.
+/-- Multinomial coefficients remain nonzero in characteristic zero. -/
+/-- Coefficients indexed by sums of row and column exponents, normalized by multinomials. -/
+noncomputable def catalecticant (rows : m → σ →₀ ℕ) (columns : n → σ →₀ ℕ) :
+    MvPolynomial σ K →ₗ[K] Matrix m n K where
+  toFun p i j := p.coeff (rows i + columns j) / ((rows i + columns j).multinomial : K)
+@[simp] theorem catalecticant_apply (rows : m → σ →₀ ℕ) (columns : n → σ →₀ ℕ)

+combined degree is the power. The normalization is invertible in characteristic zero. -/

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+At level `depth`, sample an independent label for each newly queried prefix of that length.
+Remember it for later queries with the same prefix, and evaluate the remaining suffix using the

+The cache is an ordinary list. One call preserves a label-width invariant and adds at most one
+entry. The shared stateful interpreter certifies the entire adaptive game, including copying,
+sampling, replies and growing storage. This module identifies the endpoint games; adjacent-hybrid
+* `Cslib.Crypto.GGM.frontierOracle`: memoized prefix labels followed by tree evaluation.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.GGM.isPPTOn_hybridGame`: uniform strict PPT for the complete experiment.

+  Section 3.3, the algorithms `A_i` in the proof of Theorem 3.

+noncomputable def frontierOracle (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (n depth : ℕ)
+    (query : List Bool) : StateT Cache ProbComp (List Bool) := fun cache =>
+    let (seed, cache') ← memoize (fun _ : List Bool => BitString.sampleList n)
+/-- The adaptive hybrid game starts with an empty prefix cache. -/

+      (fun request => frontierOracle generator n depth request.2)) (adversary n [])).run []
+/-- At level zero, all valid queries share one root label. Sampling that label on demand agrees
+with choosing the key at the start of the real PRF game, even if there are no valid queries. -/
+theorem hybridGame_zero (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (adversary : OracleDistinguisher)
+  let root := fun cache : Cache => (cache.lookup []).elim (BitString.uniformList n) PMF.pure
+        (PMF.pure (prfOracle (eval generator) n seed query)).map (·, seed)) := by
+    by_cases hquery : query.length = n <;> cases hcache : cache.lookup [] <;>

+    (fun request seed => (PMF.pure (prfOracle (eval generator) n seed request.2)).map (·, seed))
+/-- The final level caches full query answers directly. There is no suffix left to evaluate. -/

+# An executable finite-list oracle for the PRF ideal game

+the cache. Injective key representations and the shared eager/lazy theorem identify this program
+with the ideal PRF game for every randomized adaptive adversary.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.cachedRandomFunctionOracle`: a list cache with fair-bit sampling on misses.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.prfIdealGame_eq_cached`: exact equality of the eager and cached experiments.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isPPT_prfIdealGame`: a strict PPT realization for every oracle-PPT adversary.
+* [O. Goldreich, S. Goldwasser, S. Micali, *How to Construct Random Functions*][GGM1986].
+branch at `5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8` to the shared typed interpreter.
+/-- Memoize sampled words on valid queries, rejecting malformed words without altering the cache. -/
+    StateT (List (List Bool × List Bool)) ProbComp (List Bool) := fun cache =>
+  if query.length = n then memoize (fun _ => BitString.sampleList n) query cache
+/-- Each cached call charges the parameter, query and complete input and output cache. -/
+      (fun a => cachedRandomFunctionOracle (parameter a) (query a) (cache a)) := by
+/-- An executable list cache realizes the ideal experiment, preserving repeated-query
+consistency and independent private randomness under arbitrary adaptive interaction. -/
+          (fun request => cachedRandomFunctionOracle n request.2)) (adversary n [])).run []) := by
+  let adapter := fun query : List Bool => if query.length = n then
+      ProbOracleComp (fun _ : BitString n => List Bool) (List Bool))
+    (⟨List.ofFn, List.ofFn_injective⟩ : BitString n ↪ List Bool) List.ofFn
+        (fun request : Unit × List Bool => adapter request.2)) (adversary n []))
+        fun cache => ProbComp.eval (cachedRandomFunctionOracle n query cache) := by
+  have heager (table : BitString n → BitString n) (query : List Bool) : OracleComp.interpret
+        (adapter query) = PMF.pure (randomFunctionOracle n table query) := by
+    by_cases hquery : query.length = n <;> simp [adapter, randomFunctionOracle, hquery]
+/-- The ideal experiment has a strict PPT realization through its lazy cache. This does not

+# Polynomial stretch from one-bit pseudorandom generators
+Keep a seed of the original length at the front of a word. Each iteration expands that seed
+by one bit and retains the previously emitted suffix. The security proof replaces successive

+polynomially bounded. These are explicit size bounds, not machine-runtime certificates.
+The prediction advantage is at most `1 / p + 8 * inversion_success`. Consequently, if the
+inverter at each fixed precision degree has negligible success, prediction bias is negligible.
+Each degree defines one inverter for all lengths. No length-dependent choice of adversary or
+sign of the bias is used. One-wayness can discharge these success hypotheses once the
+word-based game correspondence and uniform PPT certificates for the inverters are proved.

+  success implies negligible prediction bias, in the shared nonnegative game API.

+/-- A computable number of base masks sufficient for prediction bias at least `1 / precision`. -/

+theorem maskCount_pos (n precision : ℕ) : 0 < maskCount n precision := by
+/-- The subset masks meet the recovery theorem's required count. -/

+  change 2 * n * precision ^ 2 + 1 < 2 ^ maskCount n precision at h
+/-- Rounding the mask count up costs at most a factor of two in the number of guesses. -/
+    2 ^ maskCount n precision ≤ 4 * n * precision ^ 2 + 2 := by
+  have h := Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 (x := 2 * n * precision ^ 2 + 1) (by lia)
+/-- A simple polynomial upper bound also controls the base-mask count. -/
+theorem maskCount_le (n precision : ℕ) : maskCount n precision ≤ 2 * n * precision ^ 2 + 1 := by
+  have h := Nat.log_lt_self 2 (x := 2 * n * precision ^ 2 + 1) (by lia)
+/-- The chosen count satisfies the exact real-valued inequality used by the finite reduction. -/
+      (2 ^ maskCount n precision - 1 : ℕ) := by exact_mod_cast h
+  have hpReal : (0 : ℝ) < precision := by exact_mod_cast hp
+      (2 ^ maskCount n precision - 1 : ℕ) / (2 * (precision : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
+/-- Signed parity correlation is bounded by decoder success and its chosen accuracy.
+This pointwise form allows auxiliary input to be guessed in later reductions. -/
+    (f : BitString n → Image) (predictor : BitString n → Bool) (x : BitString n)
+        (fun z => f z == f x)) true).toReal := by
+  have hpReal : (0 : ℝ) < precision := by exact_mod_cast hp
+  by_cases h : 1 / 2 + (1 / (precision : ℝ)) / 2 ≤ agreement predictor x
+  · have hsuccess := invertFixed_success_ge_half f predictor x _
+  · have hsuccess : 0 ≤ (((invertFixed f predictor (maskCount n precision) (f x)).map
+        (fun z => f z == f x)) true).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
+/-- The same inverter bounds all prediction biases, with an additive error of `1 / precision`.
+When the actual bias exceeds that error, the recovery bound applies to the actual bias itself. -/
+    (predictor : (image : Image) → Coins image → BitString n → Bool)
+          (invertSigned f predictor coins (maskCount n precision)) true).toReal := by

+  have hbound : PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => 4 * n * precision degree n ^ 2 + 2) := by

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The decoder samples `k` uniform base masks, forms their nonempty subset sums, and enumerates
+the `2 ^ k` guesses for their inner products with the unknown string. Each guess gives one
+candidate, by correcting the predictor's answers and taking a majority for each coordinate.
+The bitstrings are CSLib's `Fin n → Bool`. Mathlib's Boolean ring uses XOR for addition
+and AND for multiplication, so its ordinary dot product `x ⬝ᵥ r` is the required parity.
+Bilinearity, pairwise independence of subset sums, and Chebyshev's inequality give an explicit
+failure bound of `n / (4 * ε ^ 2 * (2 ^ k - 1))` for a predictor of agreement at least
+`1 / 2 + ε`. Taking `2 ^ k - 1 ≥ n / (2 * ε ^ 2)` makes the failure probability at most one half.
+This direct-coordinate variant has a larger candidate list than the sharper decoder in the
+reference, but the list remains polynomial in `n` and `1 / ε` when `k` is chosen accordingly.
+These theorems concern a deterministic predictor and finite probability distributions. The
+uniform PPT implementation and the hard-core reduction are separate steps. This module is
+* `agreement`: the predictor's agreement with a parity function.
+* `decode`: the finite distribution of candidate sets.
+* `decode_failure_le_half`: sufficient mask count gives success probability at least one half.
+* `candidate_parity`: a perfect parity predictor recovers the target for every choice of masks.

title: feat(Crypto): derive one-bit PRGs from hard-core predicates

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+A hard-core predicate is efficiently computable from a seed but unpredictable from its image.
+Security quantifies over uniform PPT predictors and measures absolute bias from one half, so it
+also rules out reliable anticorrelation. This property alone does not require the image function
+The reduction appends a fixed trial bit to the image, runs a distinguisher, and predicts the trial
+on acceptance or its complement on rejection. The distinguishing gap is the average of the signed
+biases of the two fixed predictors. Both are single uniform programs, with no choice depending on
+the security parameter. `Pr[p]` abbreviates the existing game's success probability in the reals.
+Appending a hard-core predicate to an efficient length-preserving permutation gives a one-bit PRG
+in the existing finite-family security API. This is conditional on the hard-core predicate;
+the Goldreich–Levin construction is a separate step in the OWP-to-PRG reduction.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.HardCore`: efficient evaluation and uniform computational unpredictability.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.HardCore.indistinguishable`: replace a hidden predicate by an independent bit.
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09], Chapter 9.

+# Predicting a bit from a distinguishing test
+The predictor supplies a trial bit to a test and returns that bit on acceptance, or its complement
+on rejection. Averaging over an independent fair trial turns the test's signed distinguishing gap
+into prediction bias. The hidden bit is not an input to the predictor.
+`Pr[p]` below is local notation for the existing game's success probability, coerced to the reals
+to express signed differences. It introduces no additional probability or security definition.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.trialPredictor`: prediction using a fixed trial bit.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.bitPredictor`: prediction using an independent fair trial.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.trialPredictor_gap`: the gap is the average of two signed prediction biases.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.bitPredictor_bias`: a randomized trial realizes that average.
+  scribed by Siu-On Chan, the prediction reduction in Theorem 2.
+Adapted from `Crypto/Computational/Prediction.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the shared nonnegative game API.
+private theorem probability_not (p : ProbComp Bool) : Pr[Bool.not <$> p] = 1 - Pr[p] := by
+/-- Predict a trial bit on acceptance and its complement on rejection. -/
+def trialPredictor (test : Bool → ProbComp Bool) (trial : Bool) : ProbComp Bool :=
+  (fun accept => if accept then trial else !trial) <$> test trial
+/-- A fresh fair trial gives one uniform predictor from a bit test. -/
+noncomputable def bitPredictor (test : Bool → ProbComp Bool) : ProbComp Bool := do
+/-- The two fixed trials recover the test's signed distinguishing gap. -/
+      (Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth) <$> trialPredictor test false] +
+        Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth) <$> trialPredictor test true] - 1) / 2 := by
+/-- Randomizing the trial averages the two fixed predictors' correctness probabilities. -/
+    Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth) <$> bitPredictor test] =
+      (Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth) <$> trialPredictor test false] +
+        Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth) <$> trialPredictor test true]) / 2 := by
+/-- The randomized predictor's bias equals the gap between the real label and a fair label. -/
+    Pr[(fun guess => guess == truth) <$> bitPredictor test] - 1 / 2 =
+      Pr[test truth] - (Pr[test false] + Pr[test true]) / 2 := by
+/-- Trial prediction charges for both the supplied bit and the complete test. -/
+    {test : α → Bool → ProbComp Bool} {trial : α → Bool}
+    (htest : IsPPTOn (encPair input encBool) encBool (fun pair => test pair.1 pair.2))
+    IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => trialPredictor (test a) (trial a)) := by
+/-- A certified test gives a strict PPT predictor without a length-dependent choice of trial. -/
+    (htest : IsPPTOn (encPair input encBool) encBool (fun pair => test pair.1 pair.2)) :
+    IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => bitPredictor (test a)) := by

+A generator is ordinary functional code on lists of bits. Its finite family uses the existing
+`PRG.Generator` API on `BitString n` and `BitString (length n)`. The output-length condition makes
+this representation exact: no padding or truncation enters the real experiment. Admissible finite
+tests must be realized by one uniform PPT program on every parameter and valid output word.
+Security is the existing `PRG.Family.Secure`, with the seed length supplied as the parameter in
+both experiments. Its equivalence to computational indistinguishability lets reductions use
+list programs without manipulating dependent finite types. The real and ideal experiments below
+are executable fair-bit programs; their efficiency follows from the generator and length routine.

+Its behavior on other word lengths is unrestricted, but its machine clock bounds every input. -/
+    ∀ n bits, ProbComp.eval (program n (List.ofFn bits)) = test n bits
+/-- Exact output lengths identify finite generated samples with the original word distribution. -/
+theorem generatorEnsemble_eq_outputDist {generator : List Bool → List Bool} {length : ℕ → ℕ}

+/-- The finite and word experiments coincide for every uniformly realized test. -/

+/-- The ideal finite test sees exactly the uniform word of the declared output length. -/
+      (fun bits : BitString (length n) => ProbComp.eval (adversary n (List.ofFn bits))) =
+/-- Finite-family security against uniformly realizable tests is exactly computational

+/-- The real program denotes the generated-word experiment. -/

+    IsPPTOn encUnary encBool (prgIdealGame length adversary) := by
+/-- A uniform polynomial-time stretching generator, secure in the existing finite-family API. -/
+structure PseudorandomGenerator (generator : List Bool → List Bool) (length : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop where
+  /-- One deterministic polynomial-time machine evaluates the generator. -/
+  /-- The output length depends only on the seed length. -/
+  /-- Every seed length is strictly expanded. -/
+  /-- The finite family is secure against uniformly realizable PPT tests. -/
+/-- Establish a uniform PRG with an ordinary word-ensemble security argument. -/

+      (fun n => BitString.uniformList (length n))) : PseudorandomGenerator generator length :=
+/-- The generated words are computationally indistinguishable from uniform words. -/

title: feat(PPT): certify total typed saved-seed evaluation

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Efficient saved-coin evaluators for typed PPT programs
+A strict PPT witness realizes its result from a uniformly sampled polynomial-length tape. Its
+deterministic saved-coin evaluator has a genuine TM certificate, including tape preparation and
+cleanup. Normalizing arbitrary tapes to the witness budget gives a total typed evaluator whose
+every result belongs to the original program's support. No decoder on arbitrary output words is
+assumed: supported output words have unique preimages under the declared encoding.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.exists_coin_machine`: one finite machine realizes all inputs from
+  supported on every seed and exact under any sufficiently long uniform seed.
+  `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.exists_padded_bool_coin_evaluator`: one longer saved tape can be
+  reused across inputs of different lengths.
+Adapted from `Computability/Probabilistic/CoinTape.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the common machine, standard pair encoding and
+variable {α β : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool}
+/-- One finite machine and one polynomial budget realize the whole program family from saved
+fair bits. Neither witness depends on the input value. -/
+    ∃ (k : ℕ) (State : Type) (_ : Finite State) (machine : MultiTapePTM k Bool State)
+  obtain ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, c, d, hm⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨k, State, hfinite, machine, c, d, fun a =>
+/-- The encoded evaluator accepts arbitrary raw input and coin words and is uniformly
+polynomial time. Its exact realization law applies to encoded inputs at the stated budget. -/
+    ∃ (c d : ℕ) (evaluate : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool),
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => evaluate p.1 p.2)
+  obtain ⟨k, State, _, machine, c, d, hm⟩ := h.exists_coin_machine
+/-- Every typed PPT program has a total deterministic polynomial-time evaluator. Every seed
+produces a supported result. Short seeds are padded; longer seeds are truncated to the program's
+budget. Every uniform seed at least that long yields exactly the program's distribution.
+Computability is relative to the output encoding and requires no decoder for invalid words. -/
+    ∃ (c d : ℕ) (evaluate : α → List Bool → β),
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : α × List Bool => evaluate p.1 p.2)
+      (∀ a coins, evaluate a coins ∈ (ProbComp.eval (program a)).support) ∧
+      ∀ a length, c * ((input a).length + 1) ^ d ≤ length →
+  obtain ⟨c, d, raw, hraw, hlaw⟩ := h.exists_polyTime_coin_evaluator
+  let budget (a : α) := c * ((input a).length + 1) ^ d
+  let tape (a : α) (coins : List Bool) := (coins ++ List.replicate (budget a) true).take (budget a)
+  have hlength (a : α) (coins : List Bool) : (tape a coins).length = budget a := by
+  have hvalid (a : α) (coins : List Bool) : ∃ result,

+    have hs : raw (tape a coins) (input a) ∈
+        ⟨tape a coins, BitString.mem_support_uniformList_iff.mpr (hlength a coins), rfl⟩
+  let evaluate (a : α) (coins : List Bool) := (hvalid a coins).choose
+      output (evaluate a coins) = raw (tape a coins) (input a) := (hvalid a coins).choose_spec.2
+  refine ⟨c, d, evaluate, ?_, fun a coins => (hvalid a coins).choose_spec.1, ?_⟩
+  · have hinput : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime input input encBits := .of_eq fun _ => rfl
+    have hbudget : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime budget input encUnary := by
+    have hpad : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => List.replicate (budget a) true)
+        (fun p : α × List Bool => (tape p.1 p.2, input p.1))
+    exact (hraw.comp ht).of_enc_eq (fun p => hencode p.1 p.2)
+      (show budget a ≤ coins.length by simpa only [budget, hcoinsLength] using hbudget)]
+/-- The exact-budget specialization of the total seeded evaluator. -/
+    ∃ (c d : ℕ) (evaluate : α → List Bool → β),
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : α × List Bool => evaluate p.1 p.2)
+  obtain ⟨c, d, evaluate, hefficient, _, hlaw⟩ := h.exists_total_seeded_evaluator
+  exact ⟨c, d, evaluate, hefficient, fun a => hlaw a _ le_rfl⟩
+/-- A typed program can use one larger saved tape across inputs of different lengths. The
+raw word evaluator trims to each input's own budget and accepts arbitrary encoded words. -/
+    ∃ (c d : ℕ) (evaluate : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool),

+      ∀ a length, c * ((input a).length + 1) ^ d ≤ length →

+private noncomputable def markedSample (n : ℕ) : ProbComp (List Bool) := do
+-- A nontrivial support invariant survives every supplied seed, including the empty seed.
+example : ∃ evaluate : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool,
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => evaluate p.1 p.2)
+    ∀ n coins, (evaluate n coins).length = n + 1 ∧ (evaluate n coins).headD false = true := by
+  have hp : IsPPTOn encUnary encBits markedSample := by unfold markedSample; ppt
+  simp only [markedSample, ProbComp.eval_bind, BitString.eval_sampleList, ProbComp.eval_pure] at hs
+-- A unary output encoding is not a decoder for arbitrary words. The evaluator still returns
+-- a valid natural number on every seed, and preserves the entire distribution for longer seeds.
+example : ∃ (c d : ℕ) (evaluate : ℕ → List Bool → ℕ),
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => evaluate p.1 p.2)
+    (∀ n coins, evaluate n coins = n ∨ evaluate n coins = n + 1) ∧
+      return if bit then n else n + 1) =
+  let program (n : ℕ) : ProbComp ℕ := do
+    return if bit then n else n + 1
+  have hp : IsPPTOn encUnary encUnary program := by dsimp only [program]; ppt

+-- This asserts the two marginal laws; it does not assert independence when coins are reused.

+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => evaluate p.1 p.2)

+  exact ⟨c, d, evaluate, hefficient, fun a b length ha hb =>
+    ⟨(hlaw a length ha).symm, (hlaw b length hb).symm⟩⟩

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+The existing verifier is polynomial-time on the framed binary encoding of CNF formulas and raw
+certificate bits. It looks up each variable's first occurrence, so arbitrary binary variable
+labels do not inflate certificates. Repeated variables read the same certificate position.
+[Arora and Barak, Section 2.3][AroraBarak09]. NP-hardness still requires the polynomial-time bound
+* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]
+/-- Listing the variables in order of occurrence is polynomial-time. -/
+/-- Reading the certificate at the first occurrence of a variable is polynomial-time. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : (CNF ℕ × List Bool) × ℕ => assignment p.1.1 p.1.2 p.2)
+  have hx := fst (encPair encCNF encBits) encNat
+/-- Evaluating a literal with the certificate assignment is polynomial-time. -/
+      (fun p : (CNF ℕ × List Bool) × Literal ℕ => Literal.eval (assignment p.1.1 p.1.2) p.2)
+      (encPair (encPair encCNF encBits) (encPair encNat encBool)) encBool := by
+  have hx := fst (encPair encCNF encBits) (encPair encNat encBool)
+  have hl := snd (encPair encCNF encBits) (encPair encNat encBool)
+/-- Evaluating a clause with the certificate assignment is polynomial-time. -/
+      (fun p : (CNF ℕ × List Bool) × Clause ℕ => Clause.eval (assignment p.1.1 p.1.2) p.2)
+      (encPair (encPair encCNF encBits) (encList (encPair encNat encBool))) encBool := by
+/-- The SAT verifier is polynomial-time, including on certificates of arbitrary length. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime verifier (encPair encCNF encBits) encBool := by
+  exact allWith computableTidilyInPolyTime_clause id' (fst encCNF encBits)
+/-- Satisfiability is in NP, with certificates of length equal to the encoded formula length. -/
+  simpa only [mem_coNP, ← compl_SAT, compl_compl] using SAT.mem_NP

+# SAT polynomial-time and encoding regression tests
+The verifier must handle empty formulas and clauses, repeated variables, sparse binary labels
+and certificates of any length. The calculus tests check composition through `fun_prop`.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime SAT.verifier (encPair encCNF encBits) encBool := by
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1.idxOf p.2)
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × ℕ => p.1.getD p.2 false)

+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1.getD (p.1.idxOf p.2) 0)
+-- Scans, like folds, use an explicit rule for the captured parameter.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1.any fun n => decide (p.2 = n))

+example : SAT.verifier ([[(7, true)], [(7, false)]], [true, false]) = false := rfl
+-- The label is stored in binary; its value is not an index into the certificate.
+example : SAT.verifier ([[(2 ^ 100, true)]], [true, false, false]) = true := by decide
+-- A short certificate defaults missing positions to false, including on negative literals.

+# The cost of a step of the simulation
+States, symbols and moves are encoded in unary (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.encUnary`), head positions on
+the work tapes as integers (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.encInt`), the position of the input head in binary
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.encNat`), and a structure as the framed tuple of its fields.
+Reading, writing and moving on a zipper are tidily computable in linear time and space. A step of
+the simulation (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.step_inO`) takes space linear in the length `L` of
+the encoded context (the description, the input and the configuration), and time
+`(K + E + p + 1) * (L + 1) ^ 2` for `K` work tapes, `E` transitions and the input head at `p`:
+reading and changing a work tape is linear, comparing the key with a transition is quadratic, and
+finding the input symbol counts down from `p`.

+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.stepTime`: the time bound of a step.

+# The universal machine, reading its input in place

+This file also states, as classes indexed by the encodings, what is required of encodings of

+The fold is computed by `Turing.MultiTapeTM.iterateWhile` on the state `some (l, b)`, holding the
+rest `l` of the list and the accumulator `b`: one round replaces it by `some (l.tail, step b a)`,
+where `a` is the head of `l`, or by `none` once `l` is empty. The case distinction is made by
+/-! ### Bounds up to a constant factor -/
+/-- `f` is tidily computable within a constant factor of `t + 1` steps and `s + 1` cells. -/
+def BigO (f : α → β) (encIn : α ↪ List Bool) (encOut : β ↪ List Bool) (t s : α → ℕ) : Prop :=
+    (fun a => c * (t a + 1)) (fun a => c * (s a + 1))
+variable {f : β → δ} {g : α → β} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encMid : β ↪ List Bool}
+  {encOut : δ ↪ List Bool} {t s t' s' : α → ℕ}
+lemma BigO.of_computable {f : α → β} {encOut : β ↪ List Bool}
+    (h : ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t s) : BigO f encIn encOut t s :=
+  ⟨1, h.mono (fun a => by omega) (fun a => by omega)⟩
+/-- Bounds can be weakened up to a constant factor. -/
+lemma BigO.mono {f : α → β} {encOut : β ↪ List Bool} (h : BigO f encIn encOut t s) (c : ℕ)
+    BigO f encIn encOut t' s' := by

+/-- Composition, given a bound `m` on the length of the intermediate word. -/

+/-- Pairing, with space for the encoded pair. -/
+lemma BigO.pair {α α₁ α₂ : Type u} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {t s : α → ℕ}
+    {enc₁ : α₁ ↪ List Bool} {enc₂ : α₂ ↪ List Bool}
+    {enc : α₁ × α₂ ↪ List Bool} (hP : PairEncoding enc₁ enc₂ enc) {f₁ : α → α₁} {f₂ : α → α₂}

+    BigO (fun a => (f₁ a, f₂ a)) encIn enc t (fun a => s a + (enc (f₁ a, f₂ a)).length) := by
+/-- A function tidily computable in linear time and space. -/
+lemma BigO.of_linear {f : α → β} {encOut : β ↪ List Bool}
+    BigO f encIn encOut (fun a => (encIn a).length) (fun a => (encIn a).length) :=
+variable {α β : Type u} (step : β → α → β) (a₀ : α) (b₀ : β)
+/-- The argument of `step` in a round: the accumulator and the head of the rest of the list. -/
+def arg (o : Option (List α × β)) : β × α :=
+/-- The state after a round: the tail of the rest of the list, and the new accumulator. -/
+def next (o : Option (List α × β)) : List α × β :=
+  ((o.getD ([], b₀)).1.tail, step (arg a₀ b₀ o).1 (arg a₀ b₀ o).2)
+/-- One round of the fold on the state `some (l, b)`: `some (l.tail, step b a)` for the head `a` of
+`l`, or `none` if `l` is empty. Defaults `a₀` and `b₀` make it total. -/
+def foldStep (o : Option (List α × β)) : Option (List α × β) :=
+  if (o.getD ([], b₀)).1.isEmpty then none else some (next step a₀ b₀ o)
+lemma foldStep_none : foldStep step a₀ b₀ none = none := by
+    foldStep step a₀ b₀ (some (a :: l, b)) = some (l, step b a) := by
+lemma iterate_foldStep (l : List α) (b : β) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ l.length) :
+    (foldStep step a₀ b₀)^[n] (some (l, b)) = some (l.drop n, (l.take n).foldl step b) := by
+  induction n generalizing l b with
+      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, foldStep_cons, ih l (step b a) (by simpa using hn)]
+/-- The number of rounds of the fold on a state. -/

+lemma isLeast_rounds {enc₁ : List α × β ↪ List Bool} {enc : Option (List α × β) ↪ List Bool}
+    (h : OptionEncoding enc₁ enc) (o : Option (List α × β)) :
+    IsLeast {n | enc ((foldStep step a₀ b₀)^[n + 1] o) = []} (rounds o) := by
+  have hnone (x : Option (List α × β)) : enc x = [] ↔ x = none := by
+  · exact ⟨Function.iterate_fixed (foldStep_none step a₀ b₀) _, fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _⟩
+        iterate_foldStep step a₀ b₀ l b le_rfl]
+      rw [iterate_foldStep step a₀ b₀ l b (by simp only [rounds, Option.elim_some] at hlt; omega)]
+/-- The cost of a round beyond reading the state: `u` of the argument of `step` plus the length of
+the next state, unless the list is empty. -/
+def roundCost (encS : List α × β ↪ List Bool) (u : β × α → ℕ) (o : Option (List α × β)) : ℕ :=
+  if (o.getD ([], b₀)).1.isEmpty then 0 else u (arg a₀ b₀ o) + (encS (next step a₀ b₀ o)).length
+variable {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encL : List α ↪ List Bool}
+  {encBA : β × α ↪ List Bool} {encS : List α × β ↪ List Bool}
+/-- One round costs time linear in the length of the state, plus, unless the list is empty, the

+    (m := fun o => (encS (next step a₀ b₀ o)).length)
+    (t' := fun o => (encO o).length + ts (arg a₀ b₀ o) + (encS (next step a₀ b₀ o)).length)
+    (s' := fun o => (encO o).length + ss (arg a₀ b₀ o) + (encS (next step a₀ b₀ o)).length)
+    (fun o => by simp only [Function.comp_apply, next, arg]; omega)
+    (fun o => by simp only [Function.comp_apply, next, arg]; omega)
+  refine ⟨c₁ + c₂ + c₃ + k, hk.mono (fun o => ?_) (fun o => ?_)⟩ <;>
+/-- If `list` and `init` are tidily computable from a common input and `step` is tidily computable
+on pairs, then `fun x => (list x).foldl step (init x)` is tidily computable. Each of the
+`(list x).length` steps is bounded by `tMax x` steps and `sMax x` cells, and the encodings of the
+intermediate states `((list x).drop i, ((list x).take i).foldl step (init x))` by `lMax x`. -/
+public theorem ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace.foldl {γ α β : Type u} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encL : List α ↪ List Bool}
+    {encBA : β × α ↪ List Bool} {encS : List α × β ↪ List Bool}
+    [hLE : ListEncoding encA encL] [hBA : PairEncoding encB encA encBA]
+    [hSE : PairEncoding encL encB encS] [hOE : OptionEncoding encS encO]

+    {t s : γ → ℕ} {tStep sStep : β × α → ℕ} {tMax sMax lMax : γ → ℕ}
+    (hlist : ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace list encIn encL t s)
+    (hinit : ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace init encIn encB t s)
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace (fun p : β × α => step p.1 p.2) encBA encB tStep sStep)
+      tStep (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x), (list x)[i]) ≤ tMax x)
+      sStep (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x), (list x)[i]) ≤ sMax x)
+      (encS ((list x).drop i, ((list x).take i).foldl step (init x))).length ≤ lMax x) :
+    ∃ c, ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace (fun x => (list x).foldl step (init x)) encIn encB
+      (fun x => c * (t x + ((list x).length + 1) * (tMax x + lMax x + 1)))
+      (fun x => c * (s x + sMax x + lMax x + 1)) := by
+  · -- every list is empty, so the fold is `init`
+    have heq : (fun x => (list x).foldl step (init x)) = init := funext fun x => by
+    exact ⟨1, hinit.mono (fun x => by omega) (fun x => by omega)⟩
+  obtain ⟨cF, hF⟩ := bigO_foldStep step a₀ (init x₀) hLE hBA hSE hOE hstep
+  obtain ⟨ci, hiter⟩ := hF.iterateWhile (r := rounds) (isLeast_rounds step a₀ (init x₀) hOE)
+  -- the largest cost of a step and the longest state along the run from a state
+  set g := foldStep step a₀ (init x₀)
+  obtain ⟨tAlong, htAlong⟩ : ∃ tAlong : Option (List α × β) → ℕ, ∀ o,
+      fun n => roundCost step a₀ (init x₀) encS tStep (g^[n] o) :=
+  obtain ⟨sAlong, hsAlong⟩ : ∃ sAlong : Option (List α × β) → ℕ, ∀ o,
+      fun n => roundCost step a₀ (init x₀) encS sStep (g^[n] o) :=
+  obtain ⟨lAlong, hlAlong⟩ : ∃ lAlong : Option (List α × β) → ℕ, ∀ o,

+  have hloop := hiter.mono (t' := fun o => (cF + ci) * ((rounds o + 1) * (tAlong o + lAlong o + 1)))

+          (hlAlong o ▸ Finset.le_sup (f := fun n => (encO (g^[n] o)).length) hn)
+            (f := fun n => roundCost step a₀ (init x₀) encS tStep (g^[n] o)) hn)) 1))
+        (a := cF * (lAlong o + sAlong o + 1)) fun n hn =>
+          (hlAlong o ▸ Finset.le_sup (f := fun n => (encO (g^[n] o)).length) hn)
+            (f := fun n => roundCost step a₀ (init x₀) encS sStep (g^[n] o)) hn)) 1))
+  have hstart := (BigO.of_linear hOE.some).comp (hSE.pair hlist hinit) (m := lMax)
+    (fun x => by simpa using hlMax x 0 (Nat.zero_le _))
+  have hrun := (BigO.of_computable hloop).comp hstart (m := fun x => cs * (lMax x + 1))
+    (fun x => (hcs _).trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left cs (by simpa using hlMax x 0 (Nat.zero_le _))))
+  -- the final state, and its accumulator

+      (some (list x, init x)) = some ([], (list x).foldl step (init x)) := by
+    rw [rounds, Option.elim_some, iterate_foldStep step a₀ (init x₀) _ _ le_rfl]
+    (m := fun x => cs * (lMax x + 1)) (fun x => by
+      exact (hcs _).trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left cs (by simpa using hlMax x _ le_rfl)))
+  have heq : (Prod.snd ∘ fun o => o.getD ([], init x₀)) ∘
+        (some ∘ fun x => (list x, init x))) = fun x => (list x).foldl step (init x) := by
+  -- the run from the initial state

+  have hstate (x : γ) {i : ℕ} (hi : i ≤ (list x).length) : g^[i] (some (list x, init x)) =
+      some ((list x).drop i, ((list x).take i).foldl step (init x)) :=
+  have hstep_le (x : γ) {u : β × α → ℕ} {U : ℕ}
+        u (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x), (list x)[i]) ≤ U)

+        simp [List.drop_eq_nil_of_le (by omega : (list x).length ≤ i)] at h
+        simp only [next, arg, Option.getD_some, hdrop, List.tail_cons, List.headD_cons]

+    exact Finset.sup_le fun i hi => hstep_le x (htMax x) (by rwa [Finset.mem_Iic, hrounds] at hi)
+  have hsx (x : γ) : sAlong (some (list x, init x)) ≤ sMax x + lMax x := by
+    exact Finset.sup_le fun i hi => hstep_le x (hsMax x) (by rwa [Finset.mem_Iic, hrounds] at hi)

+# Addition and multiplication with bounds of given degrees
+Natural numbers are encoded in binary (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.encNat`). Addition is a left fold over
+the digits of the first summand that keeps the carry, the rest of the digits of the second summand
+and the digits of the sum so far; at the end the carry is added to the rest of the second summand.
+Multiplication is a left fold over the digits of the first factor that keeps the product so far and
+the second factor shifted by the digits read, adding the shifted factor for every digit `1`.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.computableTidilyInDegree_add`: addition in quadratic time and space.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.computableTidilyInDegree_mul`: multiplication in cubic time and space.
+/-- The binary digits of `2 * n + b`, if they do not end in a zero. -/
+lemma bits_bit (b : Bool) (n : ℕ) (h : n = 0 → b = true) :
+/-- The carry of adding three digits. -/
+def carry (a b c : Bool) : Bool := a && b || c && (a ^^ b)
+/-- Adds the digits `l` and `r` with the carry `c`, least significant first; `r` is padded with
+def addBits : Bool → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool
+  | c, a :: l, r => (a ^^ (r.headD false ^^ c)) :: addBits (carry a (r.headD false) c) l r.tail
+lemma incr_bits (c : Bool) (n : ℕ) : incr c n.bits = (n + c.toNat).bits := by
+lemma addBits_bits (c : Bool) (m n : ℕ) : addBits c m.bits n.bits = (m + n + c.toNat).bits := by
+  induction m using Nat.binaryRec' generalizing c n with
+      have h := ih (carry a false c) 0
+        show 2 * m + a.toNat + 0 + c.toNat = 2 * (m + 0 + (carry a false c).toNat) +
+          (a ^^ (false ^^ c)).toNat by cases a <;> cases c <;> simp [carry]; omega,
+      rw [Nat.bits_append_bit _ _ hn, List.headD_cons, List.tail_cons, ih, Nat.bit_val,
+        Nat.bit_val, show 2 * m + a.toNat + (2 * n + b.toNat) + c.toNat =
+          2 * (m + n + (carry a b c).toNat) + (a ^^ (b ^^ c)).toNat by
+          cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> simp [carry] <;> omega, bits_bit]
+      cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> simp_all [carry]
+/-- One round: add the digit `a`, the next digit of the rest `r` and the carry `c`. -/
+def addStep (s : Bool × List Bool × List Bool) (a : Bool) : Bool × List Bool × List Bool :=
+  (carry a (s.2.1.headD false) s.1, s.2.1.tail, s.2.2 ++ [a ^^ (s.2.1.headD false ^^ s.1)])
+lemma foldl_addStep (l : List Bool) (c : Bool) (r out : List Bool) :
+    let s := l.foldl addStep (c, r, out)

+  induction l generalizing c r out with
+  | cons a l ih => simp [addBits, ← ih, addStep]

+/-- **Addition is tidily computable in quadratic time and space**, in the binary encoding. -/

+    have habc := (snd encS encBool).prod (((headD (enc₁ := encBool) false).comp hr).prod hs.fst')
+    have hcarry := (of_finite (encIn := encPair encBool (encPair encBool encBool))

+  have hsize : DegreeBounded (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (encPair encNat encNat p).length)
+  -- the first fold, over the digits of the first summand
+    (list := fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.bits) (init := fun p => (false, p.2.bits, []))
+    simp only [encS, length_encPair, encBool_apply, List.length_singleton, encBits_apply,
+      encNat_apply, List.length_take, List.length_nil] at h₁ h₂ ⊢
+  -- the second fold adds the carry to the rest of the second summand
+  have hfin : ComputableTidilyInDegree (fun s : Bool × List Bool × List Bool =>
+      succFinish (s.2.1.foldl succStep (s.1, s.2.2))) encS encBits 2 1 := by
+    have hs := of_eq (encIn := encS) (encMid := encS) (f := id) fun _ => rfl
+    simp only [length_foldl_succStep, encS, length_encPair, encBool_apply, id_eq,
+/-- One round: add the shifted factor `s.2` to the product `s.1` if the digit `a` is `1`, and shift
+def mulStep (s : ℕ × ℕ) (a : Bool) : ℕ × ℕ := (if a then s.1 + s.2 else s.1, s.2 + s.2)
+lemma foldl_mulStep (m acc sh : ℕ) : (m.bits.foldl mulStep (acc, sh)).1 = acc + m * sh := by
+  induction m using Nat.binaryRec' generalizing acc sh with
+    rw [Nat.bits_append_bit _ _ hm, List.foldl_cons, mulStep, ih, Nat.bit_val]
+    (l.foldl mulStep (acc, sh)).1 + sh ≤ acc + 2 ^ l.length * sh ∧
+  induction l generalizing acc sh with
+    obtain ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ := ih (if a then acc + sh else acc) (sh + sh)
+    have h : (if a then acc + sh else acc) ≤ acc + sh := by split <;> omega
+    simp only [List.foldl_cons, mulStep, List.length_cons, pow_succ] at h₁ h₂ ⊢
+lemma size_le_of_le {x n : ℕ} (i : ℕ) (h : x ≤ 2 ^ i * n) : x.size ≤ i + n.size :=
+/-- **Multiplication is tidily computable in cubic time and space**, in the binary encoding. -/

+# Tidy computability within given bounds, up to constants
+`ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encOut T S`: `f` is tidily computable within time `O(T a)` and space
+`O(S a)` on the input `a`, and its encoded value has length `O(S a)`. Unlike
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInDegree`, the bounds are any functions of the input, not of the
+length of its encoding, so that they can be stated in several measures of the input, such as the
+length of a description, the length of an input and a number of steps.
+The closure properties are exact up to constants: composition adds the bounds of the outer function
+at the intermediate value, a case distinction adds the bounds of the branch taken, and a left fold
+adds, for every round, a bound on the round and on the state to the time, but only once to the
+space. The encoded value counts towards the space since a combinator keeps it on a work tape.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.listMax`: the largest value of a function on a list, to bound rounds.
+/-- `f` is tidily computable within time `O(T a)` and space `O(S a)` on the input `a`, and its
+@[expose] public def ComputableTidilyInO {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (encIn : α ↪ List Bool)
+    (encOut : β ↪ List Bool) (T S : α → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ c, ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut (fun a => c * (T a + 1))
+    (fun a => c * (S a + 1)) ∧ ∀ a, (encOut (f a)).length ≤ c * (S a + 1)
+/-- The largest value of `f` on the elements of `l`, or `0`. -/

+public lemma le_listMax {α : Type*} {f : α → ℕ} {l : List α} {a : α} (ha : a ∈ l) :
+    f a ≤ listMax f l := by

+# Tidy computability with polynomial bounds of a given degree
+`ComputableTidilyInDegree f encIn encOut d e`: `f` is tidily computable within time and space
+`O(n ^ d)`, and its encoded values have length `O(n ^ e)`, where `n` is the length of the encoded
+input. The constants are existential, the degrees are explicit. The closure properties compute the
+degrees: composition multiplies the degree of the outer function by the output degree of the inner
+one, pairing and case distinctions take maxima, and a left fold adds the output degree of the list
+Results are stated with the degrees the closure properties produce; `mono` moves to larger degrees,
+proving the inequalities by `decide` or `omega`. Left folds are in
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInDegree`: tidy computability with bounds of given degrees.
+/-- `u` is bounded by a polynomial of degree `d` in `size`. -/
+@[expose] public def DegreeBounded {α : Type*} (size u : α → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ c, ∀ a, u a ≤ c * (size a + 1) ^ d
+variable {α β : Type*} {size : α → ℕ} {u v : α → ℕ} {d d₁ d₂ : ℕ}
+public theorem mono (h : DegreeBounded size v d) (huv : ∀ a, u a ≤ v a) :
+public theorem mono_deg (h : DegreeBounded size u d₁) (hd : d₁ ≤ d₂) : DegreeBounded size u d₂ :=
+public theorem const (k : ℕ) : DegreeBounded size (fun _ => k) d :=
+public theorem add (hu : DegreeBounded size u d) (hv : DegreeBounded size v d) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => u a + v a) d :=
+public theorem smul (k : ℕ) (hu : DegreeBounded size u d) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => k * u a) d :=
+public theorem add_const (k : ℕ) (hu : DegreeBounded size u d) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => u a + k) d :=
+public theorem mul (hu : DegreeBounded size u d₁) (hv : DegreeBounded size v d₂) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => u a * v a) (d₁ + d₂) :=
+  ⟨c₁ * c₂, fun a => (Nat.mul_le_mul (h₁ a) (h₂ a)).trans_eq (by rw [Nat.pow_add]; ring)⟩
+/-- Substitution: if `v` has degree `d₂` in `size'` and `size' ∘ g` has degree `d₁` in `size`,
+public theorem comp {size' : β → ℕ} {v : β → ℕ} {g : α → β} (hv : DegreeBounded size' v d₂)
+    (hg : DegreeBounded size (fun a => size' (g a)) d₁) :
+    DegreeBounded size (fun a => v (g a)) (d₁ * d₂) :=
+    have h : size' (g a) + 1 ≤ (c₁ + 1) * (size a + 1) ^ d₁ := by
+public theorem polyBounded (h : DegreeBounded size u d) : PolyBounded size u :=
+/-! ### Tidy computability with bounds of given degrees -/
+/-- `f` is tidily computable within time and space bounded by polynomials of degree `d` in the
+length of the encoded input, and its encoded values have length bounded by a polynomial of
+@[expose] public def ComputableTidilyInDegree {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (encIn : α ↪ List Bool)
+    (encOut : β ↪ List Bool) (d e : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  (∃ t s, DegreeBounded (fun a => (encIn a).length) t d ∧
+    ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t s) ∧
+  DegreeBounded (fun a => (encIn a).length) (fun a => (encOut (f a)).length) e
+variable {α β γ δ : Type*} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encMid : β ↪ List Bool}
+  {encOut : γ ↪ List Bool} {d e d₁ e₁ d₂ e₂ : ℕ}
+public theorem mono {f : α → β} {d' e' : ℕ} (h : ComputableTidilyInDegree f encIn encMid d e)
+    (hd : d ≤ d' := by first | decide | omega) (he : e ≤ e' := by first | decide | omega) :
+    ComputableTidilyInDegree f encIn encMid d' e' :=
+  let ⟨⟨t, s, ht, hs, hf⟩, hl⟩ := h
+  ⟨⟨t, s, ht.mono_deg hd, hs.mono_deg hd, hf⟩, hl.mono_deg he⟩
+/-- Bounds of degree `d` give tidy computability of degree `d`, with output of degree `d`. -/
+public theorem of_bounds {f : α → β} {t s : α → ℕ}
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace f encIn encMid t s) :
+    ComputableTidilyInDegree f encIn encMid d d :=
+  ⟨⟨t, s, ht, hs, hf⟩, ht.mono hf.length_le⟩
+    (h : ComputableTidilyInDegree f encIn encMid d e) : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encMid :=
+public theorem of_linear {f : α → β} (h : ComputableTidilyInLinearTimeAndSpace f encIn encMid) :
+  of_bounds ⟨c, fun _ => by simp⟩ ⟨c, fun _ => by simp⟩ hc
+public theorem comp {f : β → γ} {g : α → β} (hf : ComputableTidilyInDegree f encMid encOut d₂ e₂)
+    (hg : ComputableTidilyInDegree g encIn encMid d₁ e₁) :
+    ComputableTidilyInDegree (f ∘ g) encIn encOut (max d₁ (e₁ * d₂)) (e₁ * e₂) := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨t₁, s₁, ht₁, hs₁, h₁⟩, hl₁⟩ := hg
+  obtain ⟨⟨t₂, s₂, ht₂, hs₂, h₂⟩, hl₂⟩ := hf
+  -- vendored: crei's `comp` is `comp_linear` here, as cslib #1111 restates `comp`
+  -- the length of the intermediate value is bounded by the time of `g`
+  have hd₁ : d₁ ≤ max d₁ (e₁ * d₂) := le_max_left _ _
+  have hd₂ : e₁ * d₂ ≤ max d₁ (e₁ * d₂) := le_max_right _ _
+public theorem restrict {f : α → β} (h : ComputableTidilyInDegree f encIn encMid d e)
+  let ⟨⟨_, _, ⟨ct, ht⟩, ⟨cs, hs⟩, hf⟩, ⟨cl, hl⟩⟩ := h
+  ⟨⟨_, _, ⟨ct, fun a => ht a⟩, ⟨cs, fun a => hs a⟩, hf.restrict p⟩, ⟨cl, fun a => hl a⟩⟩
+public theorem ite {encC : Bool ↪ List Bool} {c : α → Bool} {f g : α → β} {dc ec : ℕ}
+    (hc : ComputableTidilyInDegree c encIn encC dc ec)
+    ComputableTidilyInDegree (fun x => if c x then f x else g x) encIn encMid
+      (max dc (max d₁ d₂)) (max e₁ e₂) := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨tc, sc, htc, hsc, h₀⟩, -⟩ := hc
+  obtain ⟨⟨tf, sf, ⟨ctf, htf⟩, ⟨csf, hsf⟩, h₁⟩, ⟨clf, hlf⟩⟩ := hf
+  obtain ⟨⟨tg, sg, ⟨ctg, htg⟩, ⟨csg, hsg⟩, h₂⟩, ⟨clg, hlg⟩⟩ := hg
+  -- the bounds of the branches, extended to all inputs
+  let ext (u : {x // c x = true} → ℕ) (v : {x // c x = false} → ℕ) (x : α) : ℕ :=
+    if h : c x = true then u ⟨x, h⟩ else v ⟨x, by simpa using h⟩
+  obtain ⟨k, h⟩ := ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace.ite h₀ (tf := ext tf tg) (sf := ext sf sg)
+    (tg := ext tf tg) (sg := ext sf sg)
+    (h₁.mono (fun x => by simp [ext, x.2]) (fun x => by simp [ext, x.2]))
+    (h₂.mono (fun x => by simp [ext, x.2]) (fun x => by simp [ext, x.2]))
+  have hext {u v} {cu du cv dv : ℕ}
+      (hu : ∀ x : {x // c x = true}, u x ≤ cu * ((encIn x).length + 1) ^ du)
+      (hv : ∀ x : {x // c x = false}, v x ≤ cv * ((encIn x).length + 1) ^ dv) :
+      DegreeBounded (fun a => (encIn a).length) (ext u v) (max du dv) :=
+      (DegreeBounded.mono_deg ⟨cv, fun _ => le_rfl⟩ (le_max_right du dv))).mono fun x => by
+      · simpa [ext, hx] using Nat.le_add_left_of_le (hv ⟨x, by simpa using hx⟩)
+  have hd : max d₁ d₂ ≤ max dc (max d₁ d₂) := le_max_right _ _
+    h.mono (fun x => ?_) (fun x => ?_)⟩, (hext hlf hlg).mono fun x => ?_⟩ <;>
+  · by_cases hx : c x = true <;> simp [ext, hx]

+public theorem pair {α β₁ β₂ : Type u} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool}

+# Left folds with bounds of given degrees
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace.foldl` asks for bounds on the arguments of the
+step function and on the intermediate states paired with the rest of the list. For list encodings
+whose elements, suffixes and lengths are bounded by the encoded list (`SizedListEncoding`), and the
+framed encodings of pairs and options, only a bound on the intermediate states is left.
+A fold whose step also needs a fixed parameter, such as a key to look up, keeps the parameter in its
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.SizedListEncoding`: list encodings that bound their elements, suffixes and
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInDegree.foldl'`: left folds, with the degree of a round
+  plus the degree of the number of rounds.
+/-- A list encoding whose encoded lists are at least as long as their elements, their suffixes and
+public class SizedListEncoding {α : Type*} (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encL : List α ↪ List Bool) :
+  length_elem_le (l : List α) : ∀ a ∈ l, (encA a).length ≤ (encL l).length
+  length_drop_le (l : List α) (i : ℕ) : (encL (l.drop i)).length ≤ (encL l).length
+public instance {α : Type*} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : SizedListEncoding enc (encList enc) where
+  length_le l := by induction l <;> grind [encList_cons, length_frame]
+  length_elem_le l a ha := by induction l <;> grind [encList_cons, length_frame]
+    induction l generalizing i <;> cases i <;> grind [encList_cons, length_frame]
+/-- **Left folds with bounds of given degrees.** If the list has output degree `eL`, the states have
+length of degree `b`, and a round has degree `dS`, a fold takes time of degree
+`eL + max 1 dS * max b eL`: at most `O(n ^ eL)` rounds, on arguments of length `O(n ^ max b eL)`. -/
+public theorem ComputableTidilyInDegree.foldl' {γ α β : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encL : List α ↪ List Bool}
+    {list : γ → List α} {init : γ → β} {step : β → α → β} {dL eL dI eI dS eS b : ℕ}
+    (hlist : ComputableTidilyInDegree list encIn encL dL eL)
+    (hinit : ComputableTidilyInDegree init encIn encB dI eI)
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInDegree (fun p : β × α => step p.1 p.2) (encPair encB encA) encB
+    {B : γ → ℕ} (hB : DegreeBounded (fun x => (encIn x).length) B b)
+      (encB (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x))).length ≤ B x) :
+    ComputableTidilyInDegree (fun x => (list x).foldl step (init x)) encIn encB
+      (max (max dL dI) (eL + max 1 dS * max b eL)) b := by
+  obtain ⟨⟨t₁, s₁, ht₁, hs₁, h₁⟩, hl⟩ := hlist
+  obtain ⟨⟨t₂, s₂, ht₂, hs₂, h₂⟩, -⟩ := hinit
+  obtain ⟨⟨tS, sS, ⟨ct, htS⟩, ⟨cs, hsS⟩, hS'⟩, -⟩ := hstep
+  -- the arguments of a round and the states with the rest of the list
+  have hround {c : ℕ} : DegreeBounded (fun x => (encIn x).length)
+      (fun x => c * (2 * B x + 1 + (encL (list x)).length + 1) ^ dS) D :=
+    (DegreeBounded.comp (size' := id) (v := fun n => c * (n + 1) ^ dS) ⟨c, fun _ => le_rfl⟩
+  have hargs : ∀ x i (hi : i < (list x).length),
+      (encPair encB encA (((list x).take i).foldl step (init x), (list x)[i])).length ≤
+        2 * B x + 1 + (encL (list x)).length := fun x i hi => by
+    have h₁ := hstates x i hi.le
+      (encPair encL encB ((list x).drop i, ((list x).take i).foldl step (init x))).length ≤
+        2 * (encL (list x)).length + 1 + B x := fun x i hi => by
+    have h₁ := hstates x i hi
+  have haD : a ≤ D := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.one_pos (le_max_left _ _))
+    (encBA := encPair encB encA) (encS := encPair encL encB)
+    (h₁.mono (t' := fun x => t₁ x + t₂ x) (s' := fun x => s₁ x + s₂ x)
+    (tMax := fun x => ct * (2 * B x + 1 + (encL (list x)).length + 1) ^ dS)
+    (sMax := fun x => cs * (2 * B x + 1 + (encL (list x)).length + 1) ^ dS)
+  · have hd₀ : max dL dI ≤ max (max dL dI) (eL + D) := le_max_left _ _
+    have hd₁ : eL + D ≤ max (max dL dI) (eL + D) := le_max_right _ _
+    have hlen : DegreeBounded (fun x => (encIn x).length) (fun x => (list x).length + 1) eL :=
+        (hlMax.mono_deg (by omega))).add_const 1).smul c, h⟩, hB.mono fun x => ?_⟩
+/-- **Left folds with a parameter, with bounds of given degrees.** The step may depend on a
+parameter `par x`, which is kept in the state. -/
+public theorem ComputableTidilyInDegree.foldlWith {γ α β π : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encL : List α ↪ List Bool}
+    {encP : π ↪ List Bool} [ListEncoding encA encL] [SizedListEncoding encA encL]
+    {par : γ → π} {list : γ → List α} {init : γ → β} {step : π → β → α → β}
+    {dP eP dL eL dI eI dS eS b : ℕ}
+    (hpar : ComputableTidilyInDegree par encIn encP dP eP)
+    (hlist : ComputableTidilyInDegree list encIn encL dL eL)
+    (hinit : ComputableTidilyInDegree init encIn encB dI eI)
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInDegree (fun p : (π × β) × α => step p.1.1 p.1.2 p.2)
+      (encPair (encPair encP encB) encA) encB dS eS)
+    {B : γ → ℕ} (hB : DegreeBounded (fun x => (encIn x).length) B b)
+      (encB (((list x).take i).foldl (step (par x)) (init x))).length ≤ B x) :
+    ComputableTidilyInDegree (fun x => (list x).foldl (step (par x)) (init x)) encIn encB
+      (max (max dL (max dP dI)) (eL + max 1 dS * max (max eP b) eL)) b := by
+  -- fold over the state `(par x, acc)`, keeping the parameter unchanged
+  have heq (l : List α) (s : π × β) :
+      l.foldl (fun s a => (s.1, step s.1 s.2 a)) s = (s.1, l.foldl (step s.1) s.2) := by
+  have hfold := ComputableTidilyInDegree.foldl' (encB := encPair encP encB) hlist
+    (hpar.prod hinit) (step := fun s a => (s.1, step s.1 s.2 a))
+  have hf : (Prod.snd ∘ fun x => (list x).foldl (fun s a => (s.1, step s.1 s.2 a))
+      (par x, init x)) = fun x => (list x).foldl (step (par x)) (init x) := by
+  rw [hf, show max 1 (max (max 1 (1 * 1)) dS) = max 1 dS by omega, Nat.mul_one] at h
+  have hY : max eP b ≤ max (max dL (max dP dI)) (eL + max 1 dS * max (max eP b) eL) :=
+  exact ⟨(h.mono (max_le le_rfl hY) le_rfl).1, hB.mono fun x => by simpa using hstates x _ le_rfl⟩

+# List operations with bounds of given degrees
+Operations on lists encoded by `Turing.MultiTapeTM.encList`, with explicit degrees
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInDegree`): adding an element at either end and concatenation
+in linear time; finding the first element that passes a test and keeping the elements that pass a
+test, one degree above the test; and dropping a number of elements in quadratic time. The tests may
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInDegree.findWith`: the first element passing a test.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInDegree.dropUnary`: dropping a number of elements, given
+public lemma encList_append (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (l₁ l₂ : List α) :
+    encList enc (l₁ ++ l₂) = encList enc l₁ ++ encList enc l₂ := by

+/-- A list of elements of bounded size has bounded size. -/

+    have h₂ := ih fun a ha => h a (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ha)
+/-- Adding an element in front: the identity on encoded words. -/

+variable {π : Type} {encP : π ↪ List Bool} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {dt et dP eP dL : ℕ}
+/-- One step of finding the first element passing the test `t`. -/
+@[expose] public def findStep (t : π × α → Bool) (p : π) (acc : Option α) (a : α) : Option α :=
+  if acc.isSome then acc else if t (p, a) then some a else none
+public lemma foldl_findStep (t : π × α → Bool) (p : π) (l : List α) (acc : Option α) :
+    l.foldl (findStep t p) acc = acc.or (l.find? fun a => t (p, a)) := by
+  induction l generalizing acc <;> cases acc <;> grind [findStep]
+/-- The first element of `list x` passing the test `t` with the parameter `par x`, for a list of
+public theorem findWith {t : π × α → Bool} {par : γ → π} {list : γ → List α}
+    (ht : ComputableTidilyInDegree t (encPair encP enc) encBool dt et)
+    (hpar : ComputableTidilyInDegree par encIn encP dP eP)

+      (encOption enc) (max (max dL dP) (1 + max 1 dt * max 1 eP)) 1 := by
+  -- the step, as a function of `((p, acc), a)`
+  have hq := fst (encPair encP (encOption enc)) enc
+  have hel := snd (encPair encP (encOption enc)) enc
+  have hisSome := (of_finite (encIn := encBool) (encMid := encBool) (fun b : Bool => !b)).comp
+      (f := fun o : Option α => o.isNone) fun o => by cases o <;> simp)).comp hq.snd')
+  simp only [max_self, Nat.one_mul, Nat.mul_one] at h

+    (const none) hstep (B := fun x => (encList enc (list x)).length + 1) (hlist.2.add_const 1)
+  · convert hfold.mono (d' := max (max dL dP) (1 + max 1 dt * max 1 eP)) (e' := 1)
+      (max_le (by have := le_max_right (max dL dP) (1 + max 1 dt * max 1 eP); omega)

+/-- One step of keeping the elements that pass the test `t`. -/
+@[expose] public def filterStep (t : π × α → Bool) (p : π) (acc : List α) (a : α) : List α :=

+public lemma foldl_filterStep (t : π × α → Bool) (p : π) (l acc : List α) :

+public lemma length_encList_filter_le (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (f : α → Bool) (l : List α) :
+  | cons a l ih => by_cases h : f a <;> simp [h] <;> omega
+/-- The elements of `list x` passing the test `t` with the parameter `par x`, for a list of linear
+public theorem filterWith {t : π × α → Bool} {par : γ → π} {list : γ → List α}
+    (ht : ComputableTidilyInDegree t (encPair encP enc) encBool dt et)

+      (encPair (encPair encP (encList enc)) enc) (encList enc) (max 1 dt) 1 := by
+  have hfold := foldlWith (encL := encList enc) (encB := encList enc) hpar hlist
+    (const []) hstep (B := fun x => (encList enc (list x)).length) hlist.2
+  convert hfold.mono (d' := max (max dL dP) (1 + max 1 dt * max 1 eP)) (e' := 1)
+    (max_le (by have := le_max_right (max dL dP) (1 + max 1 dt * max 1 eP); omega)
+/-- Dropping the first `n` elements, with `n` in unary. -/
+    ComputableTidilyInDegree (fun p : List α × ℕ => p.1.drop p.2)
+  have hrep (l : List α) (n : ℕ) : (List.replicate n true).foldl (fun acc _ => acc.tail) l =
+  have hfold := foldl' (encA := encBool) (encL := encBits) (encB := encList enc)
+    (list := fun p : List α × ℕ => List.replicate p.2 true) (step := fun acc _ => acc.tail)
+    ((of_eq (f := fun n => List.replicate n true) (encIn := encUnary) (encMid := encBits)
+    (B := fun p => (encPair (encList enc) encUnary p).length) .self (fun p i hi => by
+      have := SizedListEncoding.length_drop_le (encA := enc) (encL := encList enc) p.1
+/-- One step of mapping with the parameter `p`. -/
+@[expose] public def mapStep {β : Type} (f : π × α → β) (p : π) (acc : List β) (a : α) :

+A translator reads bits and emits, for each bit, at most one event, with a finite state in between.
+A fold over the events of a word is a fold over its bits, whose state also holds the state of the
+translator: each bit steps the translator and, if it emits an event, steps the inner fold. This
+turns a fold over a convenient encoding into a fold over another one, at the cost of a constant
+amount of state, so it applies to streaming and multi-pass folds alike.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Translator`: finite-state translators from bits to events.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Translator.lift`: the step of a fold on bits from one on events.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.Translator.foldl_lift`: the lifted fold folds over the events.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInO.lift`: the lifted step is tidily computable.
+/-- A translator from bits to events: from each state, a bit leads to a state and at most one
+  /-- The next state and the emitted event, if any. -/
+  step : Q → Bool → Q × Option E
+variable {Q E σ : Type*} (tr : Translator Q E)
+/-- The state and the events after reading `w` from the state `q`. -/
+@[expose] public def run : Q → List Bool → Q × List E
+  | q, b :: w => ((run (tr.step q b).1 w).1, (tr.step q b).2.toList ++ (run (tr.step q b).1 w).2)
+@[expose] public def events (w : List Bool) : List E := (tr.run tr.q₀ w).2
+/-- The step of a fold on bits from the step `next` of a fold on events: step the translator and,
+if it emits an event, the fold. -/
+@[expose] public def lift (next : σ × E → σ) (p : (Q × σ) × Bool) : Q × σ :=
+  ((tr.step p.1.1 p.2).1, (tr.step p.1.1 p.2).2.elim p.1.2 fun e => next (p.1.2, e))
+/-- **The lifted fold** folds over the events, and ends in the state of the translator. -/
+public theorem foldl_lift (next : σ × E → σ) (q : Q) (s : σ) (w : List Bool) :
+    w.foldl (fun p b => tr.lift next (p, b)) (q, s) =
+      ((tr.run q w).1, (tr.run q w).2.foldl (fun s e => next (s, e)) s) := by
+  induction w generalizing q s with
+public lemma run_append (q : Q) (u v : List Bool) :
+      ((tr.run (tr.run q u).1 v).1, (tr.run q u).2 ++ (tr.run (tr.run q u).1 v).2) := by
+  | cons b u ih => simp [run, ih]
+/-- The events of a prefix are a prefix of the events. -/
+public lemma run_take (q : Q) (w : List Bool) (k : ℕ) :
+    (tr.run q w).2.take (tr.run q (w.take k)).2.length = (tr.run q (w.take k)).2 := by
+  conv_lhs => rw [← List.take_append_drop k w, run_append]
