title: feat(Circuit/Frontier): dense rectangle-free sets and sets of small bias exist

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Dense rectangle-free sets and sets of small bias exist
+The frontier lower bounds are stated for families of sets `S_n ⊆ U^n` that are rectangle-free,
+or of small bias on large rectangles, with thresholds `K_n` such that `log K_n = o(n)`. This file
+shows, by counting, that such families exist over the binary alphabet, so that the hypotheses of
+set of at least `2 ^ (n - 1)` bit strings, half of the cube, is `(n + 2)`-rectangle-free. A set
+containing a rectangle with both sides of size at least `K` contains one with sides of size
+exactly `K`, and such a rectangle is spanned by `K` inputs `z i`: its sides are the parts of the
+`z i` on the cut and off it. So there are at most `2 ^ n · (2 ^ n) ^ K` of them, each with `K ^ 2`
+points, and at most `2 ^ (n + n K - K ^ 2)` of the `2 ^ (2 ^ n)` sets of bit strings contain one.
+For `K = n + 2` this is a `2 ^ (-n - 4)` fraction, while at least half of all sets have at least
+**Sets of small bias** (`exists_rectangleBias`). If `n + 1 ≤ b ^ 2 K`, some set of bit strings
+has density within `b` of `1/2` on every rectangle with both sides of size at least `K`. A
+rectangle with sides of sizes `k₁` and `k₂` is spanned by `k₁ + k₂` inputs, and by Hoeffding's
+`2 exp (-2 b ^ 2 k₁ k₂)` fraction of all sets has bias more than `b` on it. The union bound over
+all sizes and all spanning inputs is less than one.
+For families over `Fin n`, the first gives the hypotheses of the worst-case claims with
+`K_n = n + 2` (`exists_rectangleFree_family`), and the second those of the average-case claims with
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.exists_rectangleFree_family`: a family meeting the hypotheses of the
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.exists_rectangleBias`: sets of small bias on large rectangles.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.exists_rectangleBias_family`: a family meeting the hypotheses of the
+  average-case frontier lower bounds, with bias tending to zero.
+* [N. Alon, J. H. Spencer, *The Probabilistic Method*][AlonSpencer2016]
+/-- A set with `k` elements, counted with `encard`, is the range of an injective map from
+private theorem exists_injective_range_eq {α : Type*} {s : Set α} {k : ℕ} (hs : s.encard = k) :
+    ∃ a : Fin k → α, Function.Injective a ∧ range a = s := by
+  have hcard : Nat.card (Fin k) = Nat.card s := by
+  exact ⟨fun i => (e i : α), Subtype.val_injective.comp e.injective, by
+    rw [show (fun i => (e i : α)) = Subtype.val ∘ e from rfl, e.surjective.range_comp,
+/-- An input with a given part on `X` and a given part off `X`. -/
+private theorem exists_domRestrict_eq (X : Set ι) (u : X → U) (v : ↥Xᶜ → U) :
+    ∃ x : ι → U, X.domRestrict x = u ∧ Xᶜ.domRestrict x = v := by
+  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (Equiv.piEquivPiSubtypeProd (· ∈ X) fun _ => U).surjective (u, v)
+  exact ⟨x, congrArg Prod.fst hx, congrArg Prod.snd hx⟩
+/-- A rectangle inside a set with both sides of size at least `K` gives `K` inputs `z i` spanning
+a rectangle inside it with `K ^ 2` points: the parts of the `z i` on `X` and off `X` are the
+private theorem exists_rectangle_range_subset {X : Set ι} {A : Set (X → U)} {B : Set (↥Xᶜ → U)}
+      rectangle X (range fun i => X.domRestrict (z i)) (range fun j => Xᶜ.domRestrict (z j)) ⊆
+        (range fun j => Xᶜ.domRestrict (z j))).ncard = K * K := by
+  choose z hz using fun i => exists_domRestrict_eq X (a i) (b i)
+  have hza : (fun i => X.domRestrict (z i)) = a := funext fun i => (hz i).1
+  have hzb : (fun j => Xᶜ.domRestrict (z j)) = b := funext fun j => (hz j).2
+    exact fun x hx => ⟨hA'A hx.1, hB'B hx.2⟩
+  · rw [hza, hzb, ncard_rectangle, ncard_range_of_injective ha, ncard_range_of_injective hb,
+/-- Every rectangle with finite sides is spanned by inputs, one for each element of each side:
+its sides are the parts on `X` of the inputs `x i` and the parts off `X` of the inputs `y j`. -/
+private theorem exists_eq_rectangle_range [Nonempty U] {X : Set ι} {A : Set (X → U)}
+    ∃ (x : Fin A.ncard → ι → U) (y : Fin B.ncard → ι → U),
+      rectangle X (range fun i => X.domRestrict (x i)) (range fun j => Xᶜ.domRestrict (y j)) =
+  choose x hx using fun i => exists_domRestrict_eq X (a i) fun _ => Classical.arbitrary U
+  choose y hy using fun j => exists_domRestrict_eq X (fun _ => Classical.arbitrary U) (b j)
+  rw [show (fun i => X.domRestrict (x i)) = a from funext fun i => (hx i).1,
+    show (fun j => Xᶜ.domRestrict (y j)) = b from funext fun j => (hy j).2, ha, hb]
+/-- At least half of the sets of bit strings have at least `2 ^ (n - 1)` elements: complementing
+a smaller set gives a larger one. -/
+      2 * #{f : (ι → Bool) → Bool | 2 ^ (Fintype.card ι - 1) ≤ #{x | f x = true}} := by
+  have hN : 2 * t ≤ Fintype.card (ι → Bool) + 1 := by
+  -- Complementing is an injection from the small sets into the large ones.
+  have hsmall : #{f : (ι → Bool) → Bool | ¬ t ≤ #{x | f x = true}} ≤
+      #{f : (ι → Bool) → Bool | t ≤ #{x | f x = true}} := by
+    refine card_le_card_of_injOn (fun f x => !f x) (fun f hf => ?_)
+      fun f _ g _ h => funext fun x => by simpa using congrFun h x
+    have hf : #{x | f x = true} < t := by simpa using hf
+    have hneg : #{x | (!f x) = true} = #{x | f x = false} := by
+    simp only [coe_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, hneg]
+  have hsplit := card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := (univ : Finset ((ι → Bool) → Bool)))
+    fun f => t ≤ #{x | f x = true}
+/-- **Dense rectangle-free sets exist.** For `n` coordinates, some set of at least `2 ^ (n - 1)`
+bit strings, half of the cube, is `(n + 2)`-rectangle-free.
+At most `2 ^ (n + n K)` rectangles with sides of size exactly `K` are spanned by `K` inputs, each
+with `K ^ 2` points; for `K = n + 2` at most a `2 ^ (-n - 4)` fraction of all sets of bit strings
+contains one, while at least half of them have at least `2 ^ (n - 1)` elements. -/
+    ∃ S : Set (ι → Bool), RectangleFree S (Fintype.card ι + 2) ∧
+  have hN : N = 2 ^ n := by simp [N, n]
+  -- The rectangle spanned by `K` inputs, and the sets containing it with `K ^ 2` points.
+  let R (w : Set ι × (Fin K → ι → Bool)) : Set (ι → Bool) :=
+    rectangle w.1 (range fun i => w.1.domRestrict (w.2 i))
+  let E (w : Set ι × (Fin K → ι → Bool)) : Finset ((ι → Bool) → Bool) :=
+    {f : (ι → Bool) → Bool | (R w).ncard = K * K ∧ ∀ x ∈ R w, f x = true}
+  have hE (w : Set ι × (Fin K → ι → Bool)) : #(E w) * 2 ^ (K * K) ≤ 2 ^ N := by
+    · have hEw : E w = ({f : (ι → Bool) → Bool |
+          ∀ x ∉ (R w).toFinsetᶜ, f x = (fun _ => true) x} : Finset _) := by
+      have hle : K * K ≤ N := hw ▸ (ncard_le_card _).trans_eq Nat.card_eq_fintype_card
+  -- Every set that is not `K`-rectangle-free contains a spanned rectangle with `K ^ 2` points.
+    {f : (ι → Bool) → Bool | ¬ RectangleFree {x | f x = true} K}
+  have hbad : bad ⊆ univ.biUnion E := by
+    simp only [bad, RectangleFree, mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, not_forall, not_or,
+    obtain ⟨X, A, B, hAB, hA, hB⟩ := hf
+    obtain ⟨z, hz, hcard⟩ := exists_rectangle_range_subset hA hB
+      mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hcard, fun x hx => hAB (hz hx)⟩⟩
+    have hW : Fintype.card (Set ι × (Fin K → ι → Bool)) = 2 ^ n * 2 ^ (n * K) := by
+    have hsum : #bad * 2 ^ (K * K) ≤ 2 ^ n * 2 ^ (n * K) * 2 ^ N := by
+        _ ≤ ∑ _w : Set ι × (Fin K → ι → Bool), 2 ^ N := sum_le_sum fun w _ => hE w
+        _ = 2 ^ n * 2 ^ (n * K) * 2 ^ N := by rw [sum_const, card_univ, hW, smul_eq_mul]
+    have hKK : K * K = n + n * K + (n + 4) := by simp only [K]; ring
+    have hpos : 0 < 2 ^ n * 2 ^ (n * K) := by positivity
+  have hlt : #bad < #{f : (ι → Bool) → Bool | 2 ^ (n - 1) ≤ #{x | f x = true}} := by
+    generalize 2 ^ N = P at hcount hlarge hone
+  · have : ({x | f x = true} : Set (ι → Bool)) = ↑({x | f x = true} : Finset (ι → Bool)) := by
+private theorem two_pow_le_exp (m : ℕ) : (2 : ℝ) ^ m ≤ exp m := by
+    _ = exp m := by rw [← exp_nat_mul, mul_one]
+/-- **Hoeffding's inequality for a random set of inputs.** For a fixed set `T`, the sets
+`{x | f x = true}` whose density on `T` is more than `b` away from `1/2` are at most a
+`2 exp (-2 b ^ 2 |T|)` fraction of all sets. -/
+private theorem card_filter_lt_abs_le {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (T : Set α) {b : ℝ}
+    (#{f : α → Bool | b * T.ncard < |((T ∩ {x | f x = true}).ncard : ℝ) - T.ncard / 2|} : ℝ) ≤
+      2 * 2 ^ Fintype.card α * exp (-(2 * b ^ 2 * T.ncard)) := by
+  have hTS (f : α → Bool) : (T ∩ {x | f x = true}).ncard = #{x ∈ R | f x = true} := by
+  calc (#{f : α → Bool | b * T.ncard < |((T ∩ {x | f x = true}).ncard : ℝ) - T.ncard / 2|} : ℝ)
+      ≤ #{f : α → Bool | b * #R ≤ |(#{x ∈ R | f x = true} : ℝ) - #R / 2|} := by
+        simp only [mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hf ⊢
+    _ = 2 * 2 ^ Fintype.card α * exp (-(2 * b ^ 2 * T.ncard)) := by
+        rcases eq_or_ne (#R : ℝ) 0 with h | h
+/-- **Sets of small bias exist.** If `n + 1 ≤ b ^ 2 K` for `n = |ι|` and `b > 0`, some set of bit
+strings has density within `b` of `1/2` on every rectangle with both sides of size at least `K`.
+A rectangle with sides of sizes `k₁, k₂ ≥ K` is spanned by `k₁ + k₂` inputs, so there are at
+most `2 ^ (n + n k₁ + n k₂)` of them, and by Hoeffding's inequality at most a
+`2 exp (-2 b ^ 2 k₁ k₂) ≤ 2 exp (-(n + 1) (k₁ + k₂))` fraction of all sets of bit strings has bias
+more than `b` on each. Summed over all sizes, this is less than one. -/
+    (hK : (Fintype.card ι + 1 : ℝ) ≤ b ^ 2 * K) : ∃ S : Set (ι → Bool), RectangleBias S K b := by
+  -- Every set has bias at most `1/2`.

+  have hK1 : 1 ≤ K := by exact_mod_cast hKpos

+  let R (k₁ k₂ : ℕ) (w : Set ι × (Fin k₁ → ι → Bool) × (Fin k₂ → ι → Bool)) : Set (ι → Bool) :=

+  let E (k₁ k₂ : ℕ) (w : Set ι × (Fin k₁ → ι → Bool) × (Fin k₂ → ι → Bool)) :

+    {f : (ι → Bool) → Bool | ¬ RectangleBias {x | f x = true} K b}
+  have hbad : bad ⊆ (Finset.Icc K N).biUnion fun k₁ => (Finset.Icc K N).biUnion fun k₂ =>
+    simp only [bad, RectangleBias, mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, not_forall,
+    obtain ⟨X, A, B, hA, hB, hbias⟩ := hf

+# Totally regular matrices and Cauchy matrices
+A matrix is *totally regular* when every square submatrix, on distinct rows and distinct
+columns, is nonsingular; Valiant calls such matrices *superregular* [Valiant1977]. The definition
+follows `Matrix.IsTotallyUnimodular` and `Matrix.IsTotallyNonneg`. For the linear map `x ↦ A x`
+of a totally regular matrix, no small set of outputs is blind to a large set of inputs: a vector
+supported on a set `C` of columns that `A` maps to zero on a set `R` of at least `|C|` rows is zero
+*Cauchy matrices* `A i j = 1 / (x i - y j)`, with distinct `x i`, distinct `y j` and
+`x i ≠ y j`, are totally regular: every square submatrix is again a Cauchy matrix, and a square
+Cauchy matrix is nonsingular (`Matrix.det_cauchy_ne_zero`). The proof avoids Cauchy's
+determinant formula: a vector `v` in the kernel gives a polynomial of degree less than `k`, the
+Lagrange interpolant of `v j / w j` at the nodes `y j` (where the `w j` are the nodal weights),
+The explicit family `1 / (i - (N + j))` for `0 ≤ i, j < N` is totally regular over every field
+of characteristic zero (`Matrix.isTotallyRegular_cauchyNat`) and over `ZMod q` for every prime
+* `Matrix.cauchy`: the Cauchy matrix with nodes `x` and `y`.
+* `Matrix.cauchyNat`: the Cauchy matrix with nodes `0, ..., N - 1` and `N, ..., 2 N - 1`.
+* `Matrix.isTotallyRegular_iff_fintype`: square submatrices indexed by any finite type.
+* [L. G. Valiant, *Graph-theoretic arguments in low-level complexity*][Valiant1977]
+/-- `A.IsTotallyRegular` means that every square submatrix of `A`, on distinct rows and distinct
+columns, is nonsingular. These are the *superregular* matrices of [Valiant1977]. -/
+def IsTotallyRegular (A : Matrix m n R) : Prop :=
+  ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ f : Fin k → m, ∀ g : Fin k → n, f.Injective → g.Injective →
+/-- A matrix is totally regular exactly when its square submatrices on distinct rows and distinct
+columns, indexed by any finite type, are nonsingular. -/
+theorem isTotallyRegular_iff_fintype.{w} (A : Matrix m n R) : A.IsTotallyRegular ↔
+    ∀ (ι : Type w) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (f : ι → m) (g : ι → n), f.Injective →
+  · intro hA ι _ _ f g hf hg
+  · intro hA k f g hf hg
+/-- Every entry of a totally regular matrix is nonzero: it is a `1 × 1` submatrix. -/
+theorem IsTotallyRegular.apply_ne_zero (hA : A.IsTotallyRegular) (i : m) (j : n) : A i j ≠ 0 := by
+/-- A submatrix of a totally regular matrix, on distinct rows and distinct columns, is totally
+theorem IsTotallyRegular.submatrix (hA : A.IsTotallyRegular) {f : m' → m} {g : n' → n}
+  fun k f' g' hf' hg' => by
+    simpa only [submatrix_submatrix] using hA k (f ∘ f') (g ∘ g') (hf.comp hf') (hg.comp hg')
+/-- The transpose of a totally regular matrix is totally regular. -/
+  fun k f g hf hg => by
+    exact hA k g f hg hf
+/-- Reindexing a totally regular matrix keeps it totally regular. -/
+theorem IsTotallyRegular.reindex (hA : A.IsTotallyRegular) (em : m ≃ m') (en : n ≃ n') :
+theorem reindex_isTotallyRegular (A : Matrix m n R) (em : m ≃ m') (en : n ≃ n') :
+  ⟨fun hA => by simpa using hA.reindex em.symm en.symm, fun hA => hA.reindex em en⟩
+/-- **Square submatrices act injectively.** If `A` is totally regular, `v` is supported on a set
+`cols` of columns, and `A v` vanishes on a set `rows` of rows with `|cols| ≤ |rows|`, then
+    (hA : A.IsTotallyRegular) {rows : Finset m} {cols : Finset n} (hcard : cols.card ≤ rows.card)
+    {v : n → R} (hv : ∀ j ∉ cols, v j = 0) (hAv : ∀ i ∈ rows, (A *ᵥ v) i = 0) : v = 0 := by
+  -- Pair the columns with some of the rows.
+  let f : cols → m := fun j => r j
+  -- On the rows `f`, the vector `A v` is the submatrix on `f` and `g` applied to `v ∘ g`.
+  have hzero : A.submatrix f g *ᵥ (v ∘ g) = 0 := by
+    simp only [mulVec, dotProduct, submatrix_apply, Function.comp_apply, g]
+    rw [Finset.sum_coe_sort cols fun j' => A (f j) j' * v j']
+    exact Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ cols) fun j' _ hj' => by simp [hv j' hj']
+    ((isTotallyRegular_iff_fintype A).1 hA cols f g hf Subtype.val_injective) hzero
+/-- The *Cauchy matrix* with nodes `x` and `y`: `A i j = 1 / (x i - y j)`. -/
+def cauchy (x : m → F) (y : n → F) : Matrix m n F :=
+  of fun i j => (x i - y j)⁻¹
+@[simp] theorem cauchy_apply (x : m → F) (y : n → F) (i : m) (j : n) :
+    cauchy x y i j = (x i - y j)⁻¹ :=
+/-- A submatrix of a Cauchy matrix is the Cauchy matrix of the restricted nodes. -/
+@[simp] theorem submatrix_cauchy (x : m → F) (y : n → F) (r : m' → m) (c : n' → n) :
+    (cauchy x y).submatrix r c = cauchy (x ∘ r) (y ∘ c) :=
+/-- **Square Cauchy matrices are nonsingular.** If `∑ j, v j / (x i - y j) = 0` for every `i`,
+then the polynomial interpolating `v j / w j` at the nodes `y j`, where the `w j` are the nodal
+weights, vanishes at the `k` points `x i`. Its degree is less than `k`, so it is zero, and so is
+theorem det_cauchy_ne_zero [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {x y : n → F}
+    (hx : Function.Injective x) (hy : Function.Injective y) (hxy : ∀ i j, x i ≠ y j) :
+  have hweight : ∀ j, Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ y j ≠ 0 := fun j =>
+  let w : n → F := fun j => (Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ y j)⁻¹ * v j
+  have hP : Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ y w = 0 := by
+    rw [Lagrange.eval_interpolate_not_at_node w fun j _ => hxy i j]
+    have hsum : ∑ j, Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ y j * (x i - y j)⁻¹ * w j =
+  have h := Lagrange.eval_interpolate_at_node w hy.injOn (Finset.mem_univ j)
+/-- **Cauchy matrices are totally regular**: every square submatrix is again a square Cauchy
+theorem isTotallyRegular_cauchy {x : m → F} {y : n → F} (hx : Function.Injective x)
+    (hy : Function.Injective y) (hxy : ∀ i j, x i ≠ y j) : (cauchy x y).IsTotallyRegular :=
+  fun _ r c hr hc => by
+    exact det_cauchy_ne_zero (hx.comp hr) (hy.comp hc) fun i j => hxy (r i) (c j)
+/-- The explicit `N × N` Cauchy matrix `A i j = 1 / (i - (N + j))`, with nodes `0, ..., N - 1`
+def cauchyNat (N : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) F :=
+  cauchy (fun i : Fin N => ((i : ℕ) : F)) fun j : Fin N => ((N + j : ℕ) : F)
+/-- **The explicit Cauchy matrices are totally regular** over fields of characteristic zero. -/
+  isTotallyRegular_cauchy (fun i i' h => Fin.ext (by exact_mod_cast h))
+    (fun j j' h => Fin.ext (Nat.add_left_cancel (by exact_mod_cast h)))
+      have : (i : ℕ) = N + j := by exact_mod_cast h
+/-- **The explicit Cauchy matrices are totally regular** over `ZMod q`, for every prime
+theorem isTotallyRegular_cauchyNat_zmod {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] {N : ℕ} (hq : 2 * N ≤ q) :
+  have hcast : ∀ a b : ℕ, a < q → b < q → ((a : ZMod q) = b ↔ a = b) := fun a b ha hb => by
+  refine isTotallyRegular_cauchy (fun i i' h => Fin.ext ?_) (fun j j' h => Fin.ext ?_)

+**Existence by counting** (`Matrix.exists_submatrixRobust`). A square block of an `m × m` matrix
+over `𝔽₂` with `k` rows and rank `r` has `r` columns spanning all of its columns. So the matrix is
+determined by those columns, the coefficients expressing each other column of the block in terms

+most `2 ^ (m² - (k - r)²)` matrices are deficient by `k - r` on given sets of rows and columns with
+a given spanning set. A union bound over the fewer than `2 ^ (3 m)` choices shows that some matrix
+has every square block of rank at least `k - t` once `(t + 1)² > 3 m`. The deficiency
+**Cut ranks of bilinear forms** (`Matrix.SubmatrixRobust.le_cutRank_add`). Place a robust `k × k`
+matrix `R` on a block of a square matrix `M` whose rows and columns are disjoint sets of indices,
+with zeros elsewhere, so that the quadratic form of `M` is a bilinear form `xᵀ R y`. A set `U` of

+**The random layout.** Give each vertex `v` its unit kernel row `x_v`

+direction of `x_u + x_v`. Draw a standard Gaussian vector `ω` and score each edge by `⟪y_e, ω⟫`.
+List the vertices by the median of their three edge scores

title: feat(Circuit/Frontier): layouts of disconnected graphs, ledgers for aggregate gates of unbounded fan-in, and the frontier lower bound with them

+with `log |M| ≤ β(n)`, has `s` ordinary inner gates (inner gates that are not special) with
+Constants and special gates are free; the ledger contributes only to the sublinear error. So the
+coefficient of the frontier method survives a sublinear amount of unbounded fan-in. For instance,
+`k` special gates that aggregate in a fixed finite commutative monoid `T`, such as unbounded AND,
+OR, parity, or counts modulo a fixed `m`, have a ledger with `log |M| = k log |T|`

title: feat(Circuit/Frontier): the frontier lower bound for totally regular linear maps

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# The frontier lower bound for linear maps
+The frontier method applies to circuits with many outputs. For a circuit computing a linear map,
+the demand comes from linear algebra instead of from counting rectangles.
+Let a circuit over a field `F` compute `x ↦ M x` for an `N × N` matrix `M`, and cut its graph
+(`Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.Compiler.graph`) along a set `P` of vertices: `P` reads the inputs `X`
+and holds the outputs `Y`. If the runs on two inputs agree on the cut, splicing them
+(`Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.Compiler.eval_splice`) shows that the outputs in `Y` do not see the
+inputs outside `X`, and the outputs outside `Y` do not see the inputs in `X`. When `M` is totally
+regular and `|X| + |Y| = N`, both blocks `M[Y, Xᶜ]` and `M[Yᶜ, X]` are square and nonsingular,
+so the values on the cut determine the input. Every layout passes through such a `P`, since
+`|X| + |Y|` grows by at most one per vertex, from `0` to `2 N`
+How many values can a cut of `k` edges carry? A circuit has *linear capacity*
+(`Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.LinearCapacity`) when the values of `k` wires never determine more than
+`k` coordinates of the input. This holds
+* over a finite alphabet, for every basis: `k` wires take at most `|F| ^ k` values
+* over any field, for the affine basis: the values of `k` wires are an affine function of the
+* over an infinite field, for polynomial operations, after linearizing the circuit
+It fails over infinite fields for arbitrary operations: an injection `F × F → F` lets one wire
+So every layout of the graph of the circuit has a frontier of at least `N` edges: the demand is
+exactly `N`. For `s` inner gates of fan-in at most `r` the graph has cycle rank at most
+`(r - 1) s + 1 - N`, and the comparison of demand and supply (`eventually_lt_of_demand`) gives
+the coefficient of the frontier lower bound for decision problems.

+# Totally regular matrices and Cauchy matrices
+A matrix is *totally regular* when every square submatrix, on distinct rows and distinct
+columns, is nonsingular. For the linear map `x ↦ M x` of a totally regular matrix, no small set
+of outputs is blind to a large set of inputs: a vector supported on a set `C` of columns that
+`M` maps to zero on a set `R` of at least `|C|` rows is zero
+*Cauchy matrices* `M i j = 1 / (x i - y j)`, with distinct `x i`, distinct `y j` and
+`x i ≠ y j`, are totally regular: every square submatrix is again a Cauchy matrix, and a square
+Cauchy matrix is nonsingular (`Matrix.det_cauchy_ne_zero`). The proof avoids Cauchy's
+determinant formula: a vector `v` in the kernel gives a polynomial of degree less than `k`, the
+Lagrange interpolant of `v j / w j` at the nodes `y j` (where the `w j` are the nodal weights),
+The explicit family `1 / (i - (N + j))` for `0 ≤ i, j < N` is totally regular over every field
+of characteristic zero (`Matrix.totallyRegular_cauchyNat`) and over `ZMod q` for every prime
+* `Matrix.cauchy`: the Cauchy matrix with nodes `x` and `y`.
+* `Matrix.cauchyNat`: the Cauchy matrix with nodes `0, ..., N - 1` and `N, ..., 2 N - 1`.
+/-- A matrix is *totally regular* when every square submatrix, on distinct rows and distinct
+def TotallyRegular (M : Matrix m n R) : Prop :=
+  ∀ (k : ℕ) (r : Fin k → m) (c : Fin k → n), Function.Injective r → Function.Injective c →
+/-- A submatrix of a totally regular matrix, on distinct rows and distinct columns, is totally
+theorem submatrix (hM : M.TotallyRegular) {r : m' → m} {c : n' → n}
+    (hr : Function.Injective r) (hc : Function.Injective c) : (M.submatrix r c).TotallyRegular :=
+  fun k r' c' hr' hc' => by
+    simpa only [submatrix_submatrix] using hM k (r ∘ r') (c ∘ c') (hr.comp hr') (hc.comp hc')
+/-- The transpose of a totally regular matrix is totally regular. -/
+theorem transpose (hM : M.TotallyRegular) : Mᵀ.TotallyRegular := fun k r c hr hc => by
+  exact hM k c r hc hr
+/-- Every entry of a totally regular matrix is nonzero: it is a `1 × 1` submatrix. -/
+theorem apply_ne_zero (hM : M.TotallyRegular) (i : m) (j : n) : M i j ≠ 0 := by
+/-- **Square submatrices act injectively.** If `M` is totally regular, `v` is supported on a set
+`C` of columns, and `M v` vanishes on a set `R` of rows with `|C| ≤ |R|`, then `v = 0`. -/
+    {rows : Finset m} {cols : Finset n} (hcard : cols.card ≤ rows.card) {v : n → R}
+    (hv : ∀ j ∉ cols, v j = 0) (hMv : ∀ i ∈ rows, (M *ᵥ v) i = 0) : v = 0 := by
+  let r : Fin k → m := fun i => rows'.equivFin.symm (Fin.cast hcard'.symm i)
+  let c : Fin k → n := fun j => cols.equivFin.symm j
+  have hr : Function.Injective r := fun i i' h => by
+  have hc : Function.Injective c := fun j j' h => cols.equivFin.symm.injective (Subtype.ext h)
+  -- On the rows `r`, the vector `M v` is the submatrix on `r` and `c` applied to `v ∘ c`.
+  have hsum : ∀ i : m, (M *ᵥ v) i = ∑ j : Fin k, M i (c j) * v (c j) := by
+    rw [← Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ cols) fun j _ hj => by simp [hv j hj],
+    exact (Equiv.sum_comp cols.equivFin.symm fun j : cols => M i j * v j).symm
+  have hzero : M.submatrix r c *ᵥ (v ∘ c) = 0 := by
+    simp only [mulVec, dotProduct, submatrix_apply, Function.comp_apply, Pi.zero_apply]
+  have hvc := Matrix.eq_zero_of_mulVec_eq_zero (hM k r c hr hc) hzero
+/-- The *Cauchy matrix* with nodes `x` and `y`: `M i j = 1 / (x i - y j)`. -/
+def cauchy (x : m → F) (y : n → F) : Matrix m n F :=
+  of fun i j => (x i - y j)⁻¹
+@[simp] theorem cauchy_apply (x : m → F) (y : n → F) (i : m) (j : n) :
+    cauchy x y i j = (x i - y j)⁻¹ :=
+/-- A submatrix of a Cauchy matrix is the Cauchy matrix of the restricted nodes. -/
+@[simp] theorem submatrix_cauchy (x : m → F) (y : n → F) (r : m' → m) (c : n' → n) :
+    (cauchy x y).submatrix r c = cauchy (x ∘ r) (y ∘ c) :=
+/-- **Square Cauchy matrices are nonsingular.** If `∑ j, v j / (x i - y j) = 0` for every `i`,
+then the polynomial interpolating `v j / w j` at the nodes `y j`, where the `w j` are the nodal
+weights, vanishes at the `k` points `x i`. Its degree is less than `k`, so it is zero, and so is
+theorem det_cauchy_ne_zero [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {x y : n → F}
+    (hx : Function.Injective x) (hy : Function.Injective y) (hxy : ∀ i j, x i ≠ y j) :
+  have hweight : ∀ j, Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ y j ≠ 0 := fun j =>
+  let w : n → F := fun j => (Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ y j)⁻¹ * v j
+  have hP : Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ y w = 0 := by
+    rw [Lagrange.eval_interpolate_not_at_node w fun j _ => hxy i j]
+    have hsum : ∑ j, Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ y j * (x i - y j)⁻¹ * w j =
+  have h := Lagrange.eval_interpolate_at_node w hy.injOn (Finset.mem_univ j)
+/-- **Cauchy matrices are totally regular**: every square submatrix is again a square Cauchy
+theorem totallyRegular_cauchy {x : m → F} {y : n → F} (hx : Function.Injective x)
+    (hy : Function.Injective y) (hxy : ∀ i j, x i ≠ y j) : (cauchy x y).TotallyRegular :=
+  fun _ r c hr hc => by
+    exact det_cauchy_ne_zero (hx.comp hr) (hy.comp hc) fun i j => hxy (r i) (c j)
+/-- The explicit `N × N` Cauchy matrix `M i j = 1 / (i - (N + j))`, with nodes `0, ..., N - 1`
+def cauchyNat (N : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) F :=
+  cauchy (fun i : Fin N => ((i : ℕ) : F)) fun j : Fin N => ((N + j : ℕ) : F)
+/-- **The explicit Cauchy matrices are totally regular** over fields of characteristic zero. -/
+  totallyRegular_cauchy (fun i i' h => Fin.ext (by exact_mod_cast h))
+    (fun j j' h => Fin.ext (Nat.add_left_cancel (by exact_mod_cast h)))
+      have : (i : ℕ) = N + j := by exact_mod_cast h
+/-- **The explicit Cauchy matrices are totally regular** over `ZMod q`, for every prime
+theorem totallyRegular_cauchyNat_zmod {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] {N : ℕ} (hq : 2 * N ≤ q) :
+  have hcast : ∀ a b : ℕ, a < q → b < q → ((a : ZMod q) = b ↔ a = b) := fun a b ha hb => by
+  refine totallyRegular_cauchy (fun i i' h => Fin.ext ?_) (fun j j' h => Fin.ext ?_)

+# Projections of the standard Gaussian measure
+Let `X` be a standard Gaussian vector of a finite-dimensional real inner product space `E`
+(`stdGaussian E`). Its covariance is the inner product, so:
+* the projection `⟪u, X⟫` is a centered Gaussian of variance `‖u‖ ^ 2`
+* projections onto orthogonal vectors are uncorrelated, and since they are jointly Gaussian,
+  independent (`indepFun_inner_stdGaussian`), so their joint law is the product of their laws
+Hence the projection onto a nonzero `u` lands in a set `s` with probability at most
+`volume s / (√(2π) ‖u‖)` (`stdGaussian_inner_mem_le`), and has absolute value at least `c > 0`
+The standard Gaussian vector of `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι` is a vector of independent standard Gaussian
+coordinates (`measurePreserving_toLp_pi_gaussianReal`), which transfers these facts to the
+product measure `Measure.pi fun _ : ι => gaussianReal 0 1` on `ι → ℝ`.
+* `ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian_map_inner_prod`: the joint law of projections onto orthogonal
+  window and tail bounds for a projection.
+  coordinates form a standard Gaussian vector of `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι`.

+and `⟪v, ·⟫` are jointly Gaussian with covariance `⟪u, v⟫`, so they are independent when `u` and
+    IndepFun (fun x => ⟪u, x⟫) (fun x => ⟪v, x⟫) (stdGaussian E) := by

+/-- **Window bound.** The projection of a standard Gaussian vector onto a nonzero vector `u` lands

+# Partial recursive description methods and the invariance theorem
+A code `c` of a partial recursive function (Mathlib's `Nat.Partrec.Code`) gives a description
+method `ofCode c` for natural numbers: a program `p` is the input `encode p` of `c`, and after `t`
+steps its output is `Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln t c (encode p)`, the result of evaluating `c` with
+fuel `t`. More generally, a description method is *partial recursive* (`IsPartrec`) when a partial
+recursive function of the programs has exactly its outputs, whatever its clock.
+The *universal* description method `universal` reads a program as the self-delimiting code of the
+binary representation of `encode c`, for a code `c`, followed by a program `p`, and runs `p` under
+`ofCode c`, with the same clock. The header of `c` costs a constant number of bits, so `universal`
+is at most a constant worse than `ofCode c` (`ecomplexity_universal_le`). It is itself partial
+recursive, since the decoder of the self-delimiting code is primitive recursive and evaluating
+codes is partial recursive (`Nat.Partrec.Code.eval_part`), and every partial recursive method has
+the outputs of some `ofCode c`. So `universal` is additively optimal for the class of partial
+recursive description methods: this is the invariance theorem of Kolmogorov complexity
+partial recursive methods have complexities within an additive constant of each other. Every
+natural number has a description under `universal`, so its complexity is a natural number

title: feat(Circuit/Frontier): rectangle-free sets, sweeps, layouts, networks, demand and supply

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+# Sweeps and the frontier counting lemma
+A *sweep* of a set of inputs `S ⊆ U^ι` reveals the coordinates of an input a few at a time:
+`∅ = X 0, X 1, ..., X T = ι`. At each time `t` an input has a *message* `μ t x`, which may
+depend on the whole input. The defining property is that messages permit splicing: if two inputs
+of `S` send the same message at time `t`, then the revealed part of one may be spliced onto the
+unrevealed part of the other without leaving `S`. The last message, sent once everything is
+revealed, is the same for all inputs of `S`.
+Between times `t` and `t + 1` an input `x` takes the *transition*
+`(μ t x, μ (t + 1) x, x|_{X (t + 1) \ X t})`: the message before the step, the message after it,
+**The frontier counting lemma** (`Sweep.ncard_le`). If `S` is `K`-rectangle-free and has at
+least `K` elements, then `|S| ≤ (K - 1) ^ 2 · ∑ₜ #{transitions taken at step t}`.
+The proof charges each input `x` to the first time `t + 1` at which the inputs sharing its
+message (its *peers*) have at least `K` distinct revealed parts. The rectangular hull of the
+peers lies inside `S`, so they have fewer than `K` distinct unrevealed parts. At time `t` the
+peers of `x` still had fewer than `K` distinct revealed parts. An input charged to a step is
+determined by its transition, its part revealed by time `t` and its part unrevealed at time
+`t + 1`; hence at most `(K - 1) ^ 2` inputs share a charged step and a transition.
+Nothing here mentions graphs or circuits: a sweep is an abstract family of splicing messages.
+Constraint networks swept along a layout produce sweeps whose messages are the values on the
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.Sweep S M`: a sweep of `S` with messages in `M`.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.Sweep.transition`: the transition taken by an input at a step.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Frontier.Sweep.transitionCount`: the number of transitions taken by inputs of
+  two thresholds that bound the two sides of every message class.
+/-- A *sweep* of a set of inputs `S`: coordinates revealed over time, starting from none and
+ending with all, and a message at each time such that inputs of `S` sending the same message
+  /-- Nothing is revealed at the start. -/
+  /-- Everything is revealed at the end. -/
+  /-- The message at time `t`, possibly depending on the whole input. -/
+  /-- The final message is the same for all inputs of `S`. -/

+  /-- Messages permit splicing: if two inputs of `S` send the same message at time `t`, the
+  revealed part of one and the unrevealed part of the other form an input of `S`. -/
+  splice : ∀ t, ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, message t x = message t y →
+    ∀ z, EqOn z x (revealed t) → EqOn z y (revealed t)ᶜ → z ∈ S

+A first-order interpretation `I` of a relational language `L'` in a language `L`, of dimension `ι`
+(a finite type), consists of a domain formula `δ` of `L` in variables `ι` and, for each relation
+symbol `R` of `L'` of arity `n`, a formula `I.rel R` of `L` with a block of variables `ι` for each
+of the `n` arguments. In an `L`-structure `M` it defines the `L'`-structure `I.Model M` whose
+elements are the tuples `x : ι → M` satisfying `δ`, with `R` holding of `x₁, …, xₙ` when `I.rel R`
+holds of their coordinates. Equality of the interpreted structure is equality of tuples. These are
+Immerman's first-order queries [Immerman, Section 1.4][Immerman1999], with a finite type of
+coordinates in place of the dimension `k`, so that composites need no reindexing.
+Every formula `φ` of `L'` pulls back to a formula `I.onFormula φ` of `L`, obtained by replacing each
+variable by a tuple of variables, each relation symbol by its defining formula, equality by
+equality of coordinates, and each quantifier by a quantifier over a block of variables relativized
+to `δ`. Truth is preserved: `M ⊨ I.onSentence φ ↔ I.Model M ⊨ φ`
+[Immerman, Definition 3.3 and Proposition 3.5][Immerman1999]. Interpretations act on isomorphisms
+(`Interpretation.mapEquiv`) and compose (`Interpretation.comp`), the interpreted structure of a
+composite being isomorphic to the iterated one (`Interpretation.compEquiv`).
+The arguments of `Interpretation L L' ι` are in the order of the map on structures, which turns
+`L`-structures into `L'`-structures as a reduction turns instances of one problem into instances
+of another; formulas are mapped the other way, from `L'` to `L`.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Interpretation`: a first-order interpretation of `L'` in `L` of dimension `ι`.
+  pullback of formulas and sentences of `L'` to formulas and sentences of `L`.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Interpretation.id`: the identity interpretation of a relational language.
+  `Cslib.Logic.FO.Interpretation.realize_onSentence`: the pullback of a formula holds in `M`
+  exactly when the formula holds in the interpreted structure.
+  and composite interpretations, up to isomorphism.
+The interpreted language is relational, as in finite model theory: interpreting function symbols
+would need, in every structure, a proof that their defining formulas define functions. There is no
+congruence relation, so equality is interpreted by equality of tuples, as in Immerman's
+first-order queries. The pullback uses Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language.Formula.iAlls` and
+`FirstOrder.Language.Formula.iInf`, which choose an enumeration of `ι`, so it is noncomputable.

+variable become the variables `Sum.inr`, to be quantified. -/
+def snocVar {n : ℕ} (p : (α ⊕ Fin (n + 1)) × ι) : ((α ⊕ Fin n) × ι) ⊕ ι :=
+/-- The pullback of a bounded formula of `L'` along `I`, with each free or bound variable replaced
+by a block of free variables: relation symbols are replaced by their defining formulas, equality by
+equality of all coordinates, and quantifiers by quantifiers over tuples satisfying the domain
+noncomputable def onBoundedFormula : ∀ {n : ℕ}, L'.BoundedFormula α n → L.Formula ((α ⊕ Fin n) × ι)
+    Formula.iInf fun i => Term.equal (.var (termVar t₁, i)) (.var (termVar t₂, i))
+  | _, .rel R ts => (I.rel R).relabel fun p => (termVar (ts p.1), p.2)
+/-- Under `snocVar`, the values of the coordinates of a sequence of elements extended by `y` are
+theorem sumElim_comp_snocVar {n : ℕ} (v : α → I.Model M) (xs : Fin n → I.Model M)
+    Sum.elim (fun p : (α ⊕ Fin n) × ι => (Sum.elim v xs p.1).1 p.2) y.1 ∘ snocVar =
+      fun p => (Sum.elim v (Fin.snoc xs y) p.1).1 p.2 := by
+/-- **The pullback of a bounded formula** holds of the coordinates of some elements of the
+interpreted structure exactly when the formula holds of these elements. -/
+theorem realize_onBoundedFormula {n : ℕ} (φ : L'.BoundedFormula α n) (v : α → I.Model M)
+    (I.onBoundedFormula φ).Realize (fun p => (Sum.elim v xs p.1).1 p.2) ↔ φ.Realize v xs := by
+    exact ⟨fun h => Model.ext (funext h), fun h _ => by rw [h]⟩
+    change _ ↔ (I.rel R).Realize fun p => ((ts p.1).realize (Sum.elim v xs)).1 p.2
+    refine ⟨fun h y => ?_, fun h y hy => ?_⟩
+/-- The pullback of a formula of `L'` along `I`: a formula of `L` with a block of variables `ι`
+noncomputable def onFormula (φ : L'.Formula α) : L.Formula (α × ι) :=
+  (I.onBoundedFormula φ).relabel fun p => (p.1.elim id finZeroElim, p.2)
+/-- **The pullback of a formula** holds of the coordinates of some elements of the interpreted
+structure exactly when the formula holds of these elements
+theorem realize_onFormula (φ : L'.Formula α) (v : α → I.Model M) :
+    (I.onFormula φ).Realize (fun p => (v p.1).1 p.2) ↔ φ.Realize v := by
+/-- The pullback of a sentence of `L'` along `I`, a sentence of `L`
+/-- **The pullback of a sentence** holds in `M` exactly when the sentence holds in the structure
+theorem realize_onSentence (φ : L'.Sentence) : M ⊨ I.onSentence φ ↔ I.Model M ⊨ φ := by
+variable {L : Language.{u, v}} {L' : Language.{u', v'}} {L'' : Language.{u'', v''}}
+/-- The identity interpretation of a relational language, of dimension one: every element is in
+the domain and every relation symbol defines itself. -/
+protected def id : Interpretation L L Unit where
+/-- The structure interpreted by the identity interpretation is the structure itself. -/
+/-- The composite of an interpretation `I` of `L'` in `L` and an interpretation `J` of `L''` in
+`L'`, an interpretation of `L''` in `L` whose tuples are indexed by pairs: the domain formula says
+that each block is in the domain of `I` and that the blocks satisfy the pullback of the domain
+formula of `J`, and the relation symbols are defined by the pullbacks of their definitions in `J`.
+noncomputable def comp [Finite κ] (J : Interpretation L' L'' κ) (I : Interpretation L L' ι) :
+  domain := Formula.iInf (fun j : κ => I.domain.relabel (j, ·)) ⊓ I.onFormula J.domain
+/-- **The composite of interpretations** interprets, up to isomorphism, the structure interpreted
+noncomputable def compEquiv [Finite κ] (J : Interpretation L' L'' κ)
+    (I : Interpretation L L' ι) : J.Model (I.Model M) ≃[L''] (J.comp I).Model M where
+  toFun x := ⟨fun p => (x.1 p.1).1 p.2, by
+    exact ⟨fun j => (x.1 j).2, (realize_onFormula J.domain x.1).2 x.2⟩⟩
+  invFun z := ⟨fun j => ⟨fun i => z.1 (j, i), by
+    simp only [comp, Formula.realize_inf, Formula.realize_iInf, Formula.realize_relabel] at h

title: feat(Probability): relative-error approximate counting by Cartesian powers

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Stockmeyer's estimate of the size of a set `S` from hashing (`hashEstimate`) is only accurate
+within a constant factor: with high probability it lies between `#S / 16` and `8 #S`. Applied to
+the Cartesian power `S ^ k`, whose size is `#S ^ k`, the same constant factor becomes the factor
+`128 ^ (1 / k)` after taking a `k`-th root, so a large enough number `k` of copies gives an
+estimate of `#S` with any prescribed relative error [Stockmeyer1983]. In integers: if
+`s ^ k ≤ e ≤ c s ^ k` and `c p ^ k ≤ (p + 1) ^ k`, then the integer `k`-th root `⌊e ^ (1 / k)⌋` of
+`e` lies between `s` and `(1 + 1 / p) s`, and `k = 7 p` copies suffice for the factor
+The failure probability of the estimate is amplified by the majority votes inside it: answering
+each of the `n + 1` questions by the majority of `12 (n + 1 + t)` trials makes the estimate fail
+  `k`-th root of Stockmeyer's estimate of the size of `S ^ k`.
+  within a factor `c ≤ (1 + 1 / p) ^ k` gives an estimate of `s` within relative error `1 / p`.
+  the factor `2 ^ m` at most `(1 + 1 / p) ^ k`.
+  fails to lie between `#S / 16` and `8 #S` with probability at most `(n + 1) (8 / 9) ^ r`.
+  the relative estimate lies between `#S` and `(1 + 1 / p) #S` except with probability at most
+  `(n + 1) (8 / 9) ^ r`, and so with probability at least `1 - 2 ^ (-t)` for `r = 6 (n + 1 + t)`.
+  the same for a set of vectors in `(ZMod 2) ^ m`, with `7 p` copies and affine hash families.
+/-- **Relative error from an estimate of a power.** If `e` over-estimates `s ^ k` by at most a
+factor `c`, that is `s ^ k ≤ e ≤ c s ^ k` with `k ≠ 0`, and `c ≤ (1 + 1 / p) ^ k`, then the
+integer `k`-th root of `e` estimates `s` from above within the relative error `1 / p`:
+theorem le_nthRoot_and_mul_nthRoot_le {k s e c p : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) (hse : s ^ k ≤ e)
+    (hes : e ≤ c * s ^ k) (hc : c * p ^ k ≤ (p + 1) ^ k) :
+    s ≤ Nat.nthRoot k e ∧ p * Nat.nthRoot k e ≤ (p + 1) * s := by
+  calc p ^ k * Nat.nthRoot k e ^ k ≤ p ^ k * (c * s ^ k) :=
+    _ = c * p ^ k * s ^ k := by ring
+/-- **Enough copies**: `(1 + 1 / p) ^ p ≥ 2`, so `(1 + 1 / p) ^ (m p) ≥ 2 ^ m`, that is
+  -- Bernoulli's inequality: `p ^ p + p ^ p ≤ (p + 1) ^ p`
+  have h : 2 * p ^ p ≤ (p + 1) ^ p := by
+    rwa [mul_one, Nat.cast_id, mul_pow_sub_one hp, ← two_mul] at this
+variable {ι : ℕ → Type*} [∀ j, Fintype (ι j)] {X : Type*} {Y : ℕ → Type*} [∀ j, Fintype (Y j)]
+/-- The relative estimate of `#S` from hashing: the integer `k`-th root of `16 E`, where `E` is
+Stockmeyer's estimate (`hashEstimate`) of the size `#S ^ k` of the Cartesian power `S ^ k` from
+the hash families `h j` on `k`-tuples, the targets `y j` and the seeds `ω`. The factor `16` makes
+`16 E` an over-estimate of `#S ^ k` whenever `E` is at least `#S ^ k / 16`. -/
+def relativeHashEstimate {k : ℕ} (h : ∀ j, ι j → (Fin k → X) → Y j) (y : ∀ j, Y j)
+    (S : Finset X) (ω : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Fin (2 * r) → ι j) : ℕ :=
+  Nat.nthRoot k (16 * hashEstimate h y (Fintype.piFinset fun _ => S) ω)
+/-- **The failure probability of Stockmeyer's estimate**: if every `h j` is a pairwise independent
+hash family into a set of `2 ^ j` elements, with seeds from a nonempty type `ι j`, and
+`#S ≤ 2 ^ n`, then for `2 r` independent uniform seeds per level `j ≤ n`, the estimate from the
+majority answers fails to lie between `#S / 16` and `8 #S` with probability at most
+theorem dens_filter_not_hashEstimate_le (h : ∀ j, ι j → X → Y j) (y : ∀ j, Y j) (S : Finset X)
+    (hh : ∀ j, IsPairwiseIndependentHash (h j)) (hY : ∀ j, Fintype.card (Y j) = 2 ^ j)
+    dens {ω : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Fin (2 * r) → ι j |
+      ¬ (hashEstimate h y S ω ≤ 8 * #S ∧ #S ≤ 16 * hashEstimate h y S ω)} ≤
+  refine (dens_le_dens fun ω hω => ?_).trans (dens_filter_not_answersCorrect_le h y S hh hY)
+  simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at hω ⊢
+  exact fun ha => hω ⟨ha.estimate_le, ha.le_estimate hS⟩
+/-- **Approximate counting with relative error**: if every `h j` is a pairwise independent hash
+family on `k`-tuples into a set of `2 ^ j` elements, with seeds from a nonempty type `ι j`,
+`#S ^ k ≤ 2 ^ n`, and `128 ≤ (1 + 1 / p) ^ k`, then for `2 r` independent uniform seeds per level
+`j ≤ n`, the relative estimate fails to lie between `#S` and `(1 + 1 / p) #S` with probability at
+theorem dens_filter_not_relativeHashEstimate_le {k p : ℕ} (h : ∀ j, ι j → (Fin k → X) → Y j)
+    (y : ∀ j, Y j) (S : Finset X) (hh : ∀ j, IsPairwiseIndependentHash (h j))
+    (hY : ∀ j, Fintype.card (Y j) = 2 ^ j) (hS : #S ^ k ≤ 2 ^ n)
+    dens {ω : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Fin (2 * r) → ι j |
+        p * relativeHashEstimate h y S ω ≤ (p + 1) * #S)} ≤ (n + 1) * (8 / 9) ^ r := by
+  have hcard : #(Fintype.piFinset fun _ : Fin k => S) = #S ^ k := Fintype.card_piFinset_const S k
+  simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, hcard] at hω ⊢
+  refine fun ⟨hle, hge⟩ => hω (le_nthRoot_and_mul_nthRoot_le hk hge ?_ hp)
+/-- **Approximate counting with relative error and small failure probability**: under the
+seeds per level `j ≤ n`, the relative estimate lies between `#S` and `(1 + 1 / p) #S` with
+    (h : ∀ j, ι j → (Fin k → X) → Y j) (y : ∀ j, Y j) (S : Finset X)
+    (hh : ∀ j, IsPairwiseIndependentHash (h j)) (hY : ∀ j, Fintype.card (Y j) = 2 ^ j)
+      #S ≤ relativeHashEstimate h y S ω ∧ p * relativeHashEstimate h y S ω ≤ (p + 1) * #S} := by
+  have hbad := (dens_filter_not_relativeHashEstimate_le (r := 6 * (n + 1 + t)) h y S hh hY hS
+  rw [tsub_le_iff_right, ← dens_univ (α := ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Fin (2 * (6 * (n + 1 + t))) → ι j),
+      (fun ω => #S ≤ relativeHashEstimate h y S ω ∧
+        p * relativeHashEstimate h y S ω ≤ (p + 1) * #S)]
+/-- **Approximate counting with affine hashes and relative error**: for a set `S` of vectors in
+`(ZMod 2) ^ m` and a precision `p ≠ 0`, with `7 p` copies, the affine hash families
+`x ↦ A x + b` into `(ZMod 2) ^ j` applied to `7 p`-tuples of vectors read as vectors in
+`(ZMod 2) ^ (7 p × m)`, for the levels `j ≤ 7 p m`, target `0`, and `12 (7 p m + 1 + t)`
+independent seeds per level, the relative estimate lies between `#S` and `(1 + 1 / p) #S` with
+        Matrix (Fin j) (Fin (7 * p) × Fin m) (ZMod 2) × (Fin j → ZMod 2) |
+      #S ≤ relativeHashEstimate (fun _ A x => affineHash A (Function.uncurry x)) (fun _ => 0) S ω ∧
+        p * relativeHashEstimate (fun _ A x => affineHash A (Function.uncurry x)) (fun _ => 0) S ω
+  have hh : ∀ j, IsPairwiseIndependentHash fun (A : Matrix (Fin j) (Fin (7 * p) × Fin m) (ZMod 2) ×
+      (Fin j → ZMod 2)) (x : Fin (7 * p) → Fin m → ZMod 2) => affineHash A (Function.uncurry x) :=
+  have hY : ∀ j, Fintype.card (Fin j → ZMod 2) = 2 ^ j := fun j => by
+  have hS : #S ^ (7 * p) ≤ 2 ^ (7 * p * m) := by
+      simpa only [Fintype.card_fun, ZMod.card, Fintype.card_fin] using card_le_univ S
+    calc #S ^ (7 * p) ≤ (2 ^ m) ^ (7 * p) := Nat.pow_le_pow_left this _
+      _ = 2 ^ (7 * p * m) := by rw [← pow_mul, mul_comm]
+  have hp' : 128 * p ^ (7 * p) ≤ (p + 1) ^ (7 * p) := two_pow_mul_pow_le_add_one_pow 7 hp
+    (ι := fun j => Matrix (Fin j) (Fin (7 * p) × Fin m) (ZMod 2) × (Fin j → ZMod 2))
+    (Y := fun j => Fin j → ZMod 2) _ _ _ hh hY hS hp' t

title: feat(Circuit): sparse corrections and square-root continuity of circuit complexity

lines: +Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Let `f` and `g` be Boolean functions with `m` outputs on `n` inputs that differ only on the
+inputs in a set `s`, and only in the outputs selected by `select : Fin k → Fin m`. A circuit for
+`g` is corrected into one for `f` as follows. Compute the indicator of `s` once, and compute the
+selected outputs of `f ⊕ g` by a single circuit that is only required to be correct on `s`. Mask
+each of these labels with the indicator and add it, by an exclusive or, to the corresponding
+output of `g`; the other outputs of `g` are kept. The mask and the exclusive or cost five De
+Morgan gates per selected output, so with `1_s` the indicator of `s` and `C^s` complexity on `s`,
+`C(f | g) ≤ C(1_s) + C^s((f ⊕ g) ∘ select) + 5 k` (`complexityGiven_le_of_cover`). Correcting
+in both directions bounds `|C(f) - C(g)|` by the same quantity (`dist_complexity_le_of_cover`).
+For a single output, the indicator of the inputs where `f` and `g` differ is `f ⊕ g` itself, so
+The point of keeping the indicator and the labels as two circuits shared by all outputs is that
+both can be much cheaper than the truth tables they encode: when `s` is small, `1_s` is a sparse
+function and the labels form a partial function defined on few inputs. Bounds for the
+complexity of such functions turn these corrections into continuity estimates for circuit
+complexity; see `Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Boolean.SparseSynthesis`. The case of a single
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.xor`: an exclusive or costs four De Morgan gates.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.complexity_xor_le`: the complexity of an exclusive or.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.complexityGiven_le_of_cover`: the cost of a sparse correction, given
+  complexity by at most their cost.
+* [Stasys Jukna, *Boolean Function Complexity: Advances and Frontiers*][Jukna2012], Chapter 1,
+  for circuit complexity over the De Morgan basis.
+/-- The exclusive or `f ⊕ g = (f ∨ g) ∧ ¬(f ∧ g)` costs four gates beyond its arguments. -/
+theorem Synthesis.xor {s : Set (BooleanFunction n)} {f g : BooleanFunction n} {a b : ℕ}
+    (hf : Synthesis interpretation s {f} a) (hg : Synthesis interpretation s {g} b) :
+    Synthesis interpretation s {fun x => f x ^^ g x} (a + b + 4) := by
+  have hf' : Synthesis interpretation {f, g} {f} 0 := of_mem (by simp)
+  have hg' : Synthesis interpretation {f, g} {g} 0 := of_mem (by simp)
+  have heq : (fun x => (f x || g x) && !(f x && g x)) = fun x => f x ^^ g x := by
+    cases f x <;> cases g x <;> rfl
+/-- An exclusive or of two outputs costs four gates. -/
+    complexity interpretation (single fun x => f x ^^ g x) ≤
+      complexity interpretation (single f) + complexity interpretation (single g) + 4 := by
+  have hxor : Synthesis interpretation (inputs 2) {fun y : BitString 2 => y 0 ^^ y 1} 4 :=
+    (fun x => Fin.append (single f x) (single g x)) (single fun y : BitString 2 => y 0 ^^ y 1)
+  have heq : (single fun y : BitString 2 => y 0 ^^ y 1) ∘
+      (fun x => Fin.append (single f x) (single g x)) = single fun x => f x ^^ g x := by
+    exact congrArg₂ (· ^^ ·) (Fin.append_left (single f x) (single g x) 0)
+/-- Correcting a single output: the complexities of `f` and `g` differ by at most the complexity
+of `f ⊕ g`, the indicator of the inputs on which they differ, plus four gates. -/
+      complexity interpretation (single fun x => f x ^^ g x) + 4 := by
+  have hf' : (fun x => g x ^^ (f x ^^ g x)) = f := funext fun x => by
+    cases f x <;> cases g x <;> rfl
+  have hg' : (fun x => f x ^^ (f x ^^ g x)) = g := funext fun x => by
+    cases f x <;> cases g x <;> rfl
+  have hf : complexity interpretation (single f) ≤ complexity interpretation (single g) +
+      complexity interpretation (single fun x => f x ^^ g x) + 4 := by
+    simpa only [hf'] using complexity_xor_le g fun x => f x ^^ g x
+  have hg : complexity interpretation (single g) ≤ complexity interpretation (single f) +
+      complexity interpretation (single fun x => f x ^^ g x) + 4 := by
+    simpa only [hg'] using complexity_xor_le f fun x => f x ^^ g x
+/-- The output wire carrying output `j` of the corrected function, in the inputs of `patch`. -/
+private abbrev oldWire (j : Fin m) : Fin (m + (1 + k)) := Fin.castAdd (1 + k) j
+/-- The input wire carrying the indicator, in the inputs of `patch`. -/
+private abbrev supportWire : Fin (m + (1 + k)) := Fin.natAdd m (Fin.castAdd k 0)
+/-- The input wire carrying label `i`, in the inputs of `patch`. -/
+private abbrev labelWire (i : Fin k) : Fin (m + (1 + k)) := Fin.natAdd m (Fin.natAdd 1 i)
+/-- The final stage of a correction. It reads the outputs of the function being corrected, the
+indicator, and the labels, and adds the masked label of some `i` with `select i = j` to output
+private noncomputable def patch (select : Fin k → Fin m) :
+  fun z j => if h : ∃ i, select i = j then
+    z (oldWire j) ^^ (z supportWire && z (labelWire h.choose)) else z (oldWire j)
+/-- The final stage of a correction costs five gates for each index of `select`. -/
+private theorem exists_computes_patch (select : Fin k → Fin m) :
+      c.Computes interpretation (patch select) ∧ c.size ≤ 5 * k := by
+      Synthesis interpretation (inputs (m + (1 + k))) {fun z => z w} 0 :=
+  have each (j : Fin m) : Synthesis interpretation (inputs (m + (1 + k)))
+      {fun z => patch select z j} (if ∃ i, select i = j then 5 else 0) := by
+    by_cases h : ∃ i, select i = j
+    · simpa only [patch, h, dite_true, ite_true] using
+    · simpa only [patch, h, dite_false, ite_false] using input (oldWire j)
+  have himage : ({j | ∃ i, select i = j} : Finset (Fin m)) = univ.image select := by
+/-- **Sparse correction.** Suppose that `f` and `g` agree outside `s`, and agree on every output
+outside the range of `select`. Given the values of `g`, computing `f` costs at most the
+complexity of the indicator of `s`, plus the complexity on `s` of the outputs of `f ⊕ g`
+selected by `select`, plus five gates for each of the `k` indices of `select`. -/
+theorem complexityGiven_le_of_cover (f g : BitString n → BitString m) (s : Finset (BitString n))
+    (select : Fin k → Fin m) (hs : ∀ x ∉ s, f x = g x)
+    (hselect : ∀ j ∉ Set.range select, ∀ x, f x j = g x j) :
+      complexity interpretation (single fun x => decide (x ∈ s)) +
+        complexityOn interpretation s (fun x i => f x (select i) ^^ g x (select i)) + 5 * k := by
+    (S := (s : Set (BitString n))) (f := fun x i => f x (select i) ^^ g x (select i))
+  let read : Circuit signature (n + m) n := Circuit.wiring signature (Fin.castAdd m)
+  let old : Circuit signature (n + m) m := Circuit.wiring signature (Fin.natAdd n)
+  have hc (x : BitString n) : c.eval interpretation (Fin.append x (g x)) = f x := by
+    simp only [c, old, read, Circuit.eval_comp, Circuit.eval_append, Circuit.eval_wiring,
+    by_cases h : ∃ i, select i = j
+      simp only [patch, h, dite_true, oldWire, supportWire, labelWire, Fin.append_left,
+      · rw [show cl.eval interpretation x = _ from hcl (Finset.mem_coe.mpr hx)]
+        cases f x j <;> cases g x j <;> rfl
+    · simp only [patch, h, dite_false, oldWire, Fin.append_left]
+      exact (hselect j (fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => h ⟨i, hi⟩) x).symm
+  have hle := ecomplexityGiven_le_of_eval f g c hc
+  have hsize : c.size ≤ complexity interpretation (single fun x => decide (x ∈ s)) +
+      complexityOn interpretation s (fun x i => f x (select i) ^^ g x (select i)) + 5 * k := by
+    simp only [c, old, read, Circuit.size_comp, Circuit.size_append, Circuit.size_wiring]
+  exact (by exact_mod_cast hle : complexityGiven interpretation f g ≤ c.size).trans hsize
+/-- **Sparse correction changes complexity little.** If `f` and `g` agree outside `s`, and agree
+on every output outside the range of `select`, then their complexities differ by at most the
+complexity of the indicator of `s`, plus the complexity on `s` of the outputs of `f ⊕ g` selected
+by `select`, plus five gates for each of the `k` indices of `select`. -/
+theorem dist_complexity_le_of_cover (f g : BitString n → BitString m) (s : Finset (BitString n))
+    (select : Fin k → Fin m) (hs : ∀ x ∉ s, f x = g x)
+    (hselect : ∀ j ∉ Set.range select, ∀ x, f x j = g x j) :
+      complexity interpretation (single fun x => decide (x ∈ s)) +
+        complexityOn interpretation s (fun x i => f x (select i) ^^ g x (select i)) + 5 * k := by
+    (Nat.add_le_add_left (complexityGiven_le_of_cover f g s select hs hselect) _)
+    (Nat.add_le_add_left (complexityGiven_le_of_cover g f s select (fun x hx => (hs x hx).symm)
+      fun j hj x => (hselect j hj x).symm) _)
+/-- Computing `k` functions on `s` side by side costs at most the sum of their complexities on
+private theorem complexityOn_pi_le (s : Set (BitString n)) (f : Fin k → BooleanFunction n) :
+    complexityOn interpretation s (fun x i => f i x) ≤
+      ∑ i, complexityOn interpretation s (single (f i)) := by
+  choose c hc hsize using fun i =>
+  have hcongr : Set.EqOn (fun x i => f i x) (fun x i => (c i).eval interpretation x 0) s :=
+    fun x hx => funext fun i => (congrFun (hc i hx) 0).symm
+  refine complexity_le_of_computes (c i) fun x => funext fun j => ?_
+/-- **Sparse correction with separate labels.** If `f` and `g` agree outside `s`, and agree on
+every output outside the range of `select`, then their complexities differ by at most the
+complexity of the indicator of `s`, plus the sum over the indices `i` of `select` of the
+complexity on `s` of output `select i` of `f ⊕ g`, plus five gates for each of the `k` indices
+theorem dist_complexity_le_sum_of_cover (f g : BitString n → BitString m)
+    (s : Finset (BitString n)) (select : Fin k → Fin m) (hs : ∀ x ∉ s, f x = g x)
+    (hselect : ∀ j ∉ Set.range select, ∀ x, f x j = g x j) :
+      complexity interpretation (single fun x => decide (x ∈ s)) +
+        ∑ i, complexityOn interpretation s (single fun x => f x (select i) ^^ g x (select i)) +
+  (dist_complexity_le_of_cover f g s select hs hselect).trans
+      (complexityOn_pi_le s fun i x => f x (select i) ^^ g x (select i)) _) _)

+# Sparse and partial synthesis: the constructions
+This file builds De Morgan circuits, with explicit gate budgets, for two kinds of Boolean functions
+that carry little information: the indicator of a small set of inputs
+(`complexity_indicator_le_indicatorBound`), and a function that only has to be correct on a small
+`Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Boolean.SparseSynthesis` chooses the parameters and shows that,
+for sets of `2 ^ p` of the `2 ^ (2 p)` inputs, the budgets are `(1 + o(1)) 2 ^ p` and
+`(1 + o(1)) 2 ^ p / p`. No asymptotics happen here. The constructions follow Chashkin's account
+[Chashkin, Sections 2 and 3][Chashkin2024] of the methods of Lupanov [Lupanov1965], Nechiporuk
+Split `k + l` input bits into `k` column bits and `l` row bits, and view a truth table as a
+matrix with `2 ^ l` rows and `2 ^ k` columns. Every column minterm and every row minterm is built
+once. Each row is a disjunction of *patterns*, sets of columns that are built once from the
+column minterms and shared by all rows, so beyond a fixed overhead a table costs one gate per
+* A *sparse table* computes the indicator of a set `D`: the true entries of each row are cut into
+  chunks of `K`, and every set of at most `K` columns is a pattern. About `|D| / K` patterns are
+* A *partial table* computes a function given on a set `D`: the given entries of each row are cut
+  into chunks of `J` consecutive entries. On a chunk, the function agrees with some assignment to
+  all columns from a bank of `(2 · 2 ^ k + 1) 2 ^ J` assignments, found greedily, which extends
+  every assignment to at most `J` columns [Chashkin, Lemma 2.1][Chashkin2024]. Masked to the
+  interval of columns spanned by the chunk, that assignment is a pattern and does not interfere
+  with the other chunks [Chashkin, Lemma 2.2][Chashkin2024]. About `|D| / J` patterns are
+A table only has few patterns when it has few columns, so the inputs are first hashed to `k + l`
+bits by a linear map over the field with two elements. Two distinct inputs collide under a
+`2 ^ -(k + l)` fraction of the linear maps, so some linear map makes at most that fraction of any
+given pairs of distinct inputs collide [Chashkin, Lemmas 2.3 and 2.4][Chashkin2024].
+* For a function given on `D`, tabulate it on the image of `D` under one hash, and correct, by
+  explicit minterms, the few inputs of `D` whose hash collides with that of another input of `D`.
+* For the indicator of a set `B` with `|B| ≤ 2 ^ p`, a hash to `k + l = p + a` bits followed by a
+  sparse table for the image of `B` is a *filter*: true on `B`, and on at most a `2 ^ -a` fraction
+  of the other inputs. The conjunction of `t` filters wrongly accepts at most `2 ^ n / 2 ^ (a t)`
+  inputs, which are removed by explicit minterms [Chashkin, Lemma 3.3][Chashkin2024].
+The linear hashing here is the minimal amount needed for these two constructions.
+  of a set of at most `2 ^ p` inputs costs at most `indicatorBound n k l K p a t` gates.
+  of inputs costs at most `partialBound n k l J |D|` gates on `D`.
+* [A. V. Chashkin, *On computing partial Boolean functions*][Chashkin2024]

+* [L. A. Sholomov, *On the realization of incompletely defined Boolean functions by circuits of
+* [A. E. Andreev, *On the complexity of the realization of partial Boolean functions by circuits
+/-- Number the assignments to `k` bits as `0, …, 2 ^ k - 1`. -/
+private def index (k : ℕ) : BitString k ≃ Fin (2 ^ k) :=
+/-- The column of an input of a table: the number of its first `k` bits. -/
+private def column (x : BitString (k + l)) : Fin (2 ^ k) :=
+  index k fun i => x (Fin.castAdd l i)
+/-- The row of an input of a table: its last `l` bits. -/
+private def row (x : BitString (k + l)) : BitString l :=
+/-- The input in row `r` and column `c` of a table. -/
+private def entry (r : BitString l) (c : Fin (2 ^ k)) : BitString (k + l) :=
+@[simp] private theorem row_entry (r : BitString l) (c : Fin (2 ^ k)) : row (entry r c) = r := by
+@[simp] private theorem column_entry (r : BitString l) (c : Fin (2 ^ k)) :
+/-- The columns of row `r` whose entries lie in `D`. -/
+private def rowSupport (D : Finset (BitString (k + l))) (r : BitString l) : Finset (Fin (2 ^ k)) :=
+private theorem mem_rowSupport {D : Finset (BitString (k + l))} {x : BitString (k + l)} :
+    column x ∈ rowSupport D (row x) ↔ x ∈ D := by
+/-- The rows of a table split its entries. -/
+  let e : BitString l × Fin (2 ^ k) ≃ BitString (k + l) :=
+    ⟨fun rc => entry rc.1 rc.2, fun x => (row x, column x), fun rc => by simp,
+      = ∑ rc : BitString l × Fin (2 ^ k), if e rc ∈ D then 1 else 0 := by
+    _ = ∑ x : BitString (k + l), if x ∈ D then 1 else 0 :=
+/-- The function of a table whose rows are disjunctions of column patterns: true at `x` when the
+column of `x` lies in one of the patterns chosen for the row of `x`. -/
+private def table {B : Type*} (pattern : B → Finset (Fin (2 ^ k)))
+    (chosen : BitString l → Finset B) : BooleanFunction (k + l) :=
+  fun x => decide (∃ b ∈ chosen (row x), column x ∈ pattern b)
+/-- A table costs `2 (k + l) + 1` gates for the minterm of every column and every row, `w + 1`
+gates for each of the patterns, of at most `w` columns each, which are built once and shared by
+the rows, one gate per pattern chosen in a row, three gates per row, and a constant. -/
+private theorem synthesis_table {B : Type*} [Fintype B] (pattern : B → Finset (Fin (2 ^ k)))
+    {w : ℕ} (hw : ∀ b, #(pattern b) ≤ w) (chosen : BitString l → Finset B) :
+  let test : Fin (2 ^ k) ⊕ BitString l → BooleanFunction (k + l)
+    | .inl c => fun x => decide (column x = c)
+    | .inr r => fun x => decide (row x = r)
+  have htest : Synthesis interpretation (inputs (k + l)) (Set.range test)
+    have h (t : Fin (2 ^ k) ⊕ BitString l) :
+        Synthesis interpretation (inputs (k + l)) {test t} (2 * (k + l) + 1) := by
+            fun x => decide ((fun i => x (Fin.castAdd l i)) = (index k).symm c) := by
+      | inr r => exact (synthesis_minterm _ r).mono Set.Subset.rfl Set.Subset.rfl (by omega)
+  let bank (b : B) : BooleanFunction (k + l) := fun x => decide (column x ∈ pattern b)
+  have hbank : Synthesis interpretation (Set.range test) (Set.range bank)
+    have h (b : B) : Synthesis interpretation (Set.range test) {bank b} (w + 1) := by
+      have h := Synthesis.exists_mem (pattern b) (fun c => test (.inl c)) (fun _ => 0)
+        fun c _ => Synthesis.of_mem (s := Set.range test) ⟨.inl c, rfl⟩
+  let rowValue (r : BitString l) : BooleanFunction (k + l) :=
+    fun x => test (.inr r) x && decide (∃ b ∈ chosen r, bank b x = true)
+  have hrow (r : BitString l) : Synthesis interpretation (Set.range test ∪ Set.range bank)
+      fun b _ => Synthesis.of_mem (s := Set.range test ∪ Set.range bank) (Or.inr ⟨b, rfl⟩)
+      (Synthesis.of_mem (s := Set.range test ∪ Set.range bank) (Or.inl ⟨.inr r, rfl⟩)).and h
+  have hrows := Synthesis.exists_mem univ rowValue _ fun r _ => hrow r
+  have hall := htest.comp (hbank.mono Set.subset_union_right Set.Subset.rfl le_rfl)
+    (Set.singleton_subset_singleton.mpr (funext fun x => by simp [rowValue, test, bank, table]))
+  simp only [sum_add_distrib, sum_const, card_univ, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool,
+/-- A sum of quotients is at most the quotient of the sum. -/
+private theorem sum_div_le_div_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℕ) (K : ℕ) :
+    ∑ i ∈ s, f i / K ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, f i) / K := by
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos K with rfl | hK
+      (sum_mul s _ K ▸ sum_le_sum fun i _ => Nat.div_mul_le_self _ _)
+/-- The elements named by a tuple of optional elements. -/
+private def tupleSupport {K : ℕ} (v : Fin K → Option (Fin N)) : Finset (Fin N) :=
+private theorem card_tupleSupport_le {K : ℕ} (v : Fin K → Option (Fin N)) :
+    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin K, 1 := sum_le_sum fun i _ => by cases v i <;> simp
+/-- Block `b` of `C` in increasing order: the elements of ranks `b K, …, b K + K - 1`, padded
+private def block (C : Finset (Fin N)) (K b : ℕ) : Fin K → Option (Fin N) :=
+  fun i => if h : b * K + i < #C then some (C.orderEmbOfFin rfl ⟨b * K + i, h⟩) else none
+/-- The first `#C / K + 1` blocks of `C` cover `C`, and nothing else. -/
+private theorem exists_mem_tupleSupport_block_iff (C : Finset (Fin N)) {K : ℕ} (hK : 0 < K)
+    (c : Fin N) : (∃ b ∈ range (#C / K + 1), c ∈ tupleSupport (block C K b)) ↔ c ∈ C := by
+  simp only [tupleSupport, mem_biUnion, mem_univ, true_and, Option.mem_toFinset,
+    obtain ⟨ρ, rfl⟩ : c ∈ Set.range (C.orderEmbOfFin rfl) := by
+    have hρ : ρ.val / K * K + ρ.val % K = ρ.val := Nat.div_add_mod' _ _
+/-- The position of the element of rank `i` of `C`, or the end `N` if `C` has fewer elements. -/
+private def cut (C : Finset (Fin N)) (i : ℕ) : Fin (N + 1) :=
+  if h : i < #C then (C.orderEmbOfFin rfl ⟨i, h⟩).castSucc else Fin.last N
+private theorem cut_le_iff (C : Finset (Fin N)) (i : ℕ) (ρ : Fin #C) :
+    cut C i ≤ (C.orderEmbOfFin rfl ρ).castSucc ↔ i ≤ ρ := by
+/-- The elements of `C` whose ranks lie between `b J` and `b J + J - 1`. -/
+private def rankBlock (C : Finset (Fin N)) (J b : ℕ) : Finset (Fin N) :=
+  ({ρ : Fin #C | b * J ≤ ρ ∧ ρ < (b + 1) * J} : Finset (Fin #C)).map
+private theorem card_rankBlock_le (C : Finset (Fin N)) (J b : ℕ) : #(rankBlock C J b) ≤ J := by
+  calc #({ρ : Fin #C | b * J ≤ ρ ∧ ρ < (b + 1) * J} : Finset (Fin #C))
+        card_le_card_of_injOn Fin.val (fun ρ hρ => by simpa using (mem_filter.mp hρ).2)
+/-- The gate budget of a sparse table on `k + l` inputs with `w` true entries and chunks of `K`
+columns: the shared minterms of the `2 ^ k` columns and the `2 ^ l` rows, every one of the
+`(2 ^ k + 1) ^ K` patterns of at most `K` columns, one gate per chunk, about `w / K` of them, and
+def sparseTableBound (k l K w : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+private theorem sparseTableBound_mono {k l K w w' : ℕ} (h : w ≤ w') :
+    sparseTableBound k l K w ≤ sparseTableBound k l K w' := by
+/-- **Sparse tables.** Split each row of the truth table of the indicator of `D` into chunks of
+`K` true entries; each chunk is one of the shared patterns of at most `K` columns. -/
+private theorem complexity_indicator_le_sparseTableBound {k l : ℕ} (D : Finset (BitString (k + l)))
+    complexity interpretation (single fun x => decide (x ∈ D)) ≤
+  let chosen (r : BitString l) : Finset (Fin K → Option (Fin (2 ^ k))) :=
+    (range (#(rowSupport D r) / K + 1)).image (block (rowSupport D r) K)
+  have h := synthesis_table tupleSupport card_tupleSupport_le chosen
+  have heq : table tupleSupport chosen = fun x => decide (x ∈ D) := by
+    have := exists_mem_tupleSupport_block_iff (rowSupport D (row x)) hK (column x)
+    simp only [table, chosen, exists_mem_image, this, mem_rowSupport]
+  have hsum : ∑ r, #(chosen r) ≤ #D / K + 2 ^ l := by
+    calc ∑ r, #(chosen r) ≤ ∑ r, (#(rowSupport D r) / K + 1) :=
+          simpa using sum_div_le_div_sum univ (fun r => #(rowSupport D r)) K
+variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α] (cover : α → β → Prop)
+  [∀ x b, Decidable (cover x b)] {a : ℕ}
+/-- If every target is covered by at least a `1 / a` fraction of the candidates, then some
+candidate covers at least a `1 / a` fraction of the targets. -/
+    (hs : ∀ b ∈ s, Fintype.card α ≤ a * #{x | cover x b}) :
+    ∃ x, #s ≤ a * #{b ∈ s | cover x b} := by
+  have hsum : ∑ _x : α, #s ≤ ∑ x : α, a * #{b ∈ s | cover x b} := by
+    calc ∑ _x : α, #s = ∑ _b ∈ s, Fintype.card α := by simp [Nat.mul_comm]
+      _ ≤ ∑ b ∈ s, a * #{x | cover x b} := sum_le_sum hs
+      _ = ∑ x : α, a * #{b ∈ s | cover x b} := by
+/-- Greedy covering: after `t` greedy choices, at most a `(1 - 1 / a) ^ t` fraction of the
+    ∀ s : Finset β, (∀ b ∈ s, Fintype.card α ≤ a * #{x | cover x b}) →
+        a ^ t * #{b ∈ s | ∀ x ∈ chosen, ¬cover x b} ≤ (a - 1) ^ t * #s := by
+  | zero => exact fun s _ => ⟨∅, by simp, by simp⟩
+    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := exists_card_le_mul_card_filter cover s hs
+    let rest := s.filter fun b => ¬cover x b
+    obtain ⟨chosen, hcard, hrest⟩ := ih rest fun b hb => hs b (mem_filter.mp hb).1
+    have heq : ({b ∈ s | ∀ y ∈ insert x chosen, ¬cover y b} : Finset β) =
+        {b ∈ rest | ∀ y ∈ chosen, ¬cover y b} := by
+      obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ : ∃ a', a = a' + 1 := ⟨a - 1, by omega⟩
+    calc a ^ t * a * #{b ∈ rest | ∀ y ∈ chosen, ¬cover y b}
+        = a * (a ^ t * #{b ∈ rest | ∀ y ∈ chosen, ¬cover y b}) := by ring
+  have haR : (0 : ℝ) < a := by exact_mod_cast ha
+  have hcast : ((a - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = a * (1 - 1 / a) := by
+  have hfour : (4 : ℝ) ^ L ≤ Real.exp (2 * L) := by
+  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < (a : ℝ) ^ ((2 * L + 1) * a) := by positivity
+      _ < (a : ℝ) ^ ((2 * L + 1) * a) * 1 := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hsmall hpos
+/-- **Greedy covering.** If each of at most `4 ^ L` targets is covered by at least a `1 / a`
+fraction of the candidates, then `(2 L + 1) a` candidates cover every target. -/
+private theorem exists_cover (ha : 0 < a) {L : ℕ} (s : Finset β) (hsL : #s ≤ 4 ^ L)
+    (hs : ∀ b ∈ s, Fintype.card α ≤ a * #{x | cover x b}) :
+    ∃ chosen : Finset α, #chosen ≤ (2 * L + 1) * a ∧ ∀ b ∈ s, ∃ x ∈ chosen, cover x b := by
+  obtain ⟨chosen, hcard, hleft⟩ := exists_pow_mul_card_uncovered_le cover ha _ s hs
+    have h₂ := Nat.mul_le_mul_left ((a - 1) ^ ((2 * L + 1) * a)) hsL
+    have h₃ := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right (a ^ ((2 * L + 1) * a)) (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hU0)
+/-- Every assignment to at most `J` of `N` positions has at least a `2 ^ -J` fraction of the
+private theorem two_pow_le_mul_card_extensions {N J : ℕ} {C : Finset (Fin N)} (hC : #C ≤ J)
+    (v : Fin N → Bool) : 2 ^ N ≤ 2 ^ J * #{e : Fin N → Bool | ∀ i ∈ C, e i = v i} := by

+    ∃ φ : BooleanFunction n, (∀ x ∈ B, φ x = true) ∧
+        (k + l) * (4 * n + 1) + sparseTableBound k l K #B := by

+      exact mem_image.mpr ⟨(x, y), mem_filter.mpr ⟨mem_product.mpr ⟨hxA, hyB⟩, hy.symm⟩, rfl⟩
+    calc #{x ∈ A | φ x = true} * 2 ^ (k + l)

+        (single fun y => decide (y ∈ B.image (linearMap H))) ∘ linearMap H := rfl
+/-- **Repeated filters.** If `|B| ≤ 2 ^ p` and the hashes have `k + l = p + a` bits, then `t`

+    (hkl : k + l = p + a) (hK : 0 < K) (t : ℕ) :
+    ∀ A : Finset (BitString n), Disjoint A B → ∃ φ : BooleanFunction n,

+    refine ⟨fun _ => true, by simp, by simp, ?_⟩

+      calc #{x ∈ rest | ψ x = true} * (2 ^ (a * t) * 2 ^ a)

+/-- The gate budget of the construction for the indicator of a set of at most `2 ^ p` of the

+`2 ^ n / 2 ^ (a t)` inputs that wrongly pass every filter. -/
+def indicatorBound (n k l K p a t : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  t * ((k + l) * (4 * n + 1) + sparseTableBound k l K (2 ^ p) + 1) +
+/-- **Sparse indicators.** The indicator of a set of at most `2 ^ p` inputs costs at most
+`indicatorBound n k l K p a t` gates, whenever `k + l = p + a` and `K > 0`. -/
+theorem complexity_indicator_le_indicatorBound {n p a k l K : ℕ} (B : Finset (BitString n))
+    (hB : #B ≤ 2 ^ p) (hkl : k + l = p + a) (hK : 0 < K) (t : ℕ) :
+    complexity interpretation (single fun x => decide (x ∈ B)) ≤
+      indicatorBound n k l K p a t := by

+    · cases h : φ x <;> simp [R, hx, h]
+/-- The gate budget of the construction for a function on a set of `w` of the `2 ^ n` inputs:

+      have hy : linearMap H x ∈ T := mem_image_of_mem _ hxD

+        ≤ #{z ∈ D.offDiag | linearMap H z.1 = linearMap H z.2} * 2 ^ (k + l) :=

+# Rotation maps and the spectral expansion of regular graphs
+A `D`-regular undirected multigraph on `V`, with parallel edges and self-loops allowed, is presented
+`rot : V × D → V × D`: `rot (v, i) = (w, j)`
+when the `i`-th edge at `v` leads to `w` and is the `j`-th edge at `w`. Following an edge back
+returns to where it started, so `rot` is an involution; conversely every involution of `V × D` is
+the rotation map of a `D`-regular multigraph. Vertices and labels are types rather than numbers
+because graph products build graphs whose vertices and labels are pairs or tuples of those of
+The random walk on `G` moves from `v` along a uniformly random edge. Its action on real functions
+is the walk operator `G.walk`, which averages a function over the neighbors of each vertex; it
+fixes constants, preserves expectations, is self-adjoint for the uniform inner product
+`𝔼 v, f v * g v` and does not increase `𝔼 v, f v ^ 2`.
+The spectral expansion `λ(G)` [AroraBarak09, Section 21.1] is the operator norm of the walk
+operator on the functions orthogonal to the constants: the smallest `c ≥ 0` with
+`𝔼 v, G.walk f v ^ 2 ≤ c ^ 2 * 𝔼 v, f v ^ 2` for all `f` of expectation zero
+(`spectralExpansion_le_iff`). It is the largest absolute value of an eigenvalue of the walk operator
+on such functions, but no spectral theory is needed here: everything below is proved from this
+characterization. `λ(G) ≤ 1` always, and `G` is a good expander when `λ(G)` is small.
+* `Cslib.RotationMap`: a `D`-regular multigraph on `V`, given by its rotation map.
+* `Cslib.RotationMap.interedges`: the edges from one set of vertices to another, as darts.
+* `Cslib.RotationMap.expect_expect_neighbor_comm`: every edge is seen once from each of its ends.
+  `Cslib.RotationMap.expect_walk_sq_le`: the walk operator preserves expectations, is
+  self-adjoint and does not increase the second moment.
+  the second moment of a function of expectation zero by at most `λ(G) ^ (2 t)`.

+/-- `v` is the neighbor of its `i`-th neighbor along the same edge. -/

+/-- The edges from `S` to `T`, as the darts `(v, i)` with `v ∈ S` whose `i`-th edge leads into `T`.

+def interedges (S T : Finset V) : Finset (V × D) :=
+  {p ∈ S ×ˢ univ | G.neighbor p.1 p.2 ∈ T}
+/-- A dart `(v, i)` goes from `S` to `T` when `v ∈ S` and its `i`-th neighbor is in `T`. -/
+theorem mem_interedges {S T : Finset V} {p : V × D} :
+    p ∈ G.interedges S T ↔ p.1 ∈ S ∧ G.neighbor p.1 p.2 ∈ T := by
+/-- No edges leave the empty set. -/
+theorem interedges_empty_left (T : Finset V) : G.interedges ∅ T = ∅ := by
+/-- No edges enter the empty set. -/

+/-- Reversing the darts matches the edges from `S` to `T` with those from `T` to `S`. -/
+theorem card_interedges_comm (S T : Finset V) : #(G.interedges S T) = #(G.interedges T S) := by
+  refine card_nbij' G.rot G.rot (fun p hp ↦ ?_) (fun p hp ↦ ?_) (fun p _ ↦ G.rot_rot p)
+/-- Every edge at a vertex of `S` leads into `T` or into its complement. -/
+    #(G.interedges S T) + #(G.interedges S Tᶜ) = #S * Fintype.card D := by
+variable [Fintype V] [Fintype D] {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℚ≥0 M]
+/-- Every edge is seen once from each of its ends: averaging `F v (G.neighbor v i)` over the darts
+`(v, i)` gives the same as averaging `F (G.neighbor v i) v`. -/

+expected value of `f` after one step of the random walk from `v`. -/
+noncomputable def walk : (V → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] V → ℝ where
+  toFun f v := 𝔼 i, f (G.neighbor v i)
+/-- `G.walk f v` is the average of `f` over the neighbors of `v`. -/
+theorem walk_apply (f : V → ℝ) (v : V) : G.walk f v = 𝔼 i, f (G.neighbor v i) :=
+theorem walk_const [Nonempty D] (c : ℝ) : G.walk (fun _ ↦ c) = fun _ ↦ c :=
+/-- Walks of every length fix constants. -/
+theorem walk_pow_const [Nonempty D] (t : ℕ) (c : ℝ) : (G.walk ^ t) (fun _ ↦ c) = fun _ ↦ c := by
+  | succ t ih => rw [pow_succ, Module.End.mul_apply, walk_const, ih]
+theorem expect_walk [Nonempty D] (f : V → ℝ) : 𝔼 v, G.walk f v = 𝔼 v, f v :=
+/-- Walks of every length preserve expectations. -/
+theorem expect_walk_pow [Nonempty D] (t : ℕ) (f : V → ℝ) : 𝔼 v, (G.walk ^ t) f v = 𝔼 v, f v := by
+  | succ t ih => rw [pow_succ', Module.End.mul_apply, expect_walk, ih]
+/-- The walk operator preserves expectation zero. -/
+theorem expect_walk_eq_zero {f : V → ℝ} (hf : 𝔼 v, f v = 0) : 𝔼 v, G.walk f v = 0 := by
+  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty D with hD | hD
+/-- Walks of every length preserve expectation zero. -/
+theorem expect_walk_pow_eq_zero {f : V → ℝ} (hf : 𝔼 v, f v = 0) (t : ℕ) :
+    𝔼 v, (G.walk ^ t) f v = 0 := by
+  | succ t ih => rw [pow_succ', Module.End.mul_apply, G.expect_walk_eq_zero ih]
+/-- The walk operator is self-adjoint for the uniform inner product. -/
+    𝔼 v, f v * G.walk g v = 𝔼 v, G.walk f v * g v := by
+  exact G.expect_expect_neighbor_comm fun v w ↦ f v * g w
+/-- The walk operator does not increase the second moment. -/
+theorem expect_walk_sq_le (f : V → ℝ) : 𝔼 v, G.walk f v ^ 2 ≤ 𝔼 v, f v ^ 2 := by
+  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty D with hD | hD
+  · simpa [walk_apply] using expect_nonneg fun v _ ↦ sq_nonneg (f v)
